Through secret rituals, she steals a man's vital essence to become a powerful sorcerer. Her dark power manifests as a ghost snake that paralyzes and drains victims.

title: Ash woe
topic_desc: Ash woe is an acute blight disease that severely degrades a victim's willpower and cognitive faculties. It is contracted from corprus beasts and other blighted creatures roaming the Red Mountain region and its surrounding blight storms. Unlike the progressive horror of corprus, ash woe represents one of the acute magical contagions linked to Dagoth Ur's spreading influence, debilitating the mind rather than mutating the body. Its capacity to shatter thought and resolve makes it a persistent danger to travelers and settlers in the blighted ashlands.
topic_desc_basic: Ash woe is an acute blight disease that attacks a victim's will and thought processes. It is caught from corprus beasts and other blighted creatures.

title: Ataxia
topic_desc: Ataxia is a mild common disease that diminishes a sufferer's strength and dexterity. Its primary symptoms include generalized pain and muscle stiffness, impairing physical coordination and movement. The affliction is known to be contracted from slaughterfish, making coastal waters and shoreline activities a common source of infection. Though debilitating, it is not considered life-threatening and responds readily to standard common disease cures or the restorative blessings of shrines.
topic_desc_basic: Ataxia is a mild common disease that saps strength and dexterity. It causes generalized pain and muscle stiffness, and can be contracted from slaughterfish.

title: Brown Rot
topic_desc: Brown rot is a mild common disease that afflicts the victim's physical strength and behavior. Its symptoms include necrosis of the flesh and persistent sleeplessness. The affliction is known to be contracted from undead creatures, specifically bonewalkers, greater bonewalkers, skeletons, and bonelords. As a common disease, it is readily cured through standard restorative temple blessings, potions, or common spells.
topic_desc_basic: Brown rot is a mild common disease causing necrosis, sleeplessness, and diminished strength and behavior. It is contracted from undead such as bonewalkers, skeletons, and bonelords.

title: Chanthrax
topic_desc: Chanthrax is an acute blight disease that severely impairs a victim's dexterity and mobility. Like other blight illnesses, it originates from the infected regions around the Ghostfence and is typically contracted through contact with corprus beasts or other blight monsters roaming the Red Mountain region. The disease's specific assault on motor function renders even simple physical tasks difficult for the afflicted. As a blight disease, chanthrax resists conventional treatments and requires specialized curative magic or potions to eradicate. Its acute onset and debilitating symptoms make it a persistent hazard for anyone venturing into blight-affected territories.
topic_desc_basic: Chanthrax is an acute blight disease that reduces dexterity and mobility. It is typically contracted from corprus beasts or other blight monsters found near the Ghostfence and Red Mountain.

title: Chills
topic_desc: Chills is an extremely dangerous common disease that severely impairs both cognitive function and physical coordination. Afflicted individuals suffer from pronounced clumsiness and mental confusion, rendering even routine tasks hazardous. The disease is transmitted through contact with several varieties of undead, specifically bonewalkers, greater bonewalkers, skeletons, and bonelords. As a common disease, it can be treated with standard temple blessings or readily available curative alchemy.
topic_desc_basic: Chills is a dangerous common disease that impairs coordination and mental clarity, causing clumsiness and confusion. It is contracted from undead such as bonewalkers, skeletons, and bonelords.

title: Collywobbles
topic_desc: Collywobbles is a serious common disease that markedly diminishes a sufferer's physical strength, endurance, and mobility. Its defining symptoms are uncontrollable shaking and chronic weariness, which can severely incapacitate those afflicted. The affliction is known to be contracted from the fiery shalk, a hostile insect native to Morrowind's rugged terrain. Healers classify it as a common disease, meaning it yields readily to standard curative magic and restorative potions.
topic_desc_basic: Collywobbles is a serious common disease that causes uncontrollable shaking and chronic weariness. It drains a victim's strength, endurance, and mobility. The affliction is typically caught from the fiery shalk.

title: Crimson Plague
topic_desc: The Crimson Plague is a virulent disease remembered for spreading easily and acting with alarming speed. Historical records hold that it was stamped out during the Second Age, making any suspected recurrence a grave concern to healers and Temple authorities. Accounts from Mournhold associate transmission with infected rats emerging from old tombs beneath the city and connect the disease with the lich Gedna Relvel. Its rapid contagion and debilitating effects give even isolated cases the potential to become a destructive urban epidemic.
topic_desc_basic: The Crimson Plague is a fast-spreading disease believed eradicated during the Second Age. Mournhold accounts associate it with infected rats from old subterranean tombs and the lich Gedna Relvel.

title: Dampworm
topic_desc: Dampworm is a serious common disease that severely impairs a sufferer's mobility. Its defining symptoms include persistent, uncontrollable muscle spasms and twitching, rendering coordinated movement difficult. The affliction is transmitted by nix-hounds, parasitic creatures native to the ashlands and coastal regions of Morrowind. Contracting dampworm poses a significant risk to travelers, as the ensuing loss of muscular control leaves victims vulnerable to predators and further attacks. Without proper remedial intervention, the relentless convulsions prevent effective travel or defense.
topic_desc_basic: Dampworm is a serious common disease that impairs mobility through uncontrollable muscle spasms and twitching. It is transmitted by nix-hounds.

title: Greenspore
topic_desc: Greenspore is a common disease that seriously degrades a victim's mental stability. Its hallmark symptoms are pronounced irritability and violent outbursts, sometimes progressing into mild dementia. The affliction is transmitted by slaughterfish, making coastal and marshland waters a persistent source of infection. As a common disease, it can be readily cured through standard temple blessings or common curative potions, though untreated cases risk escalating behavioral dangers.
topic_desc_basic: Greenspore is a common disease that alters a victim's behavior, causing pronounced irritability, violent outbursts, and occasionally mild dementia. It is typically contracted from slaughterfish.

title: Helljoint
topic_desc: Helljoint is a mild common disease that impairs mobility and dexterity through persistent irritation and inflammation of the joints. It is known to be contracted from the girdle-tailed cliff racer, a pervasive flying creature in Morrowind. While not typically life-threatening, the resulting stiffness and reduced agility can significantly hinder physical activities and combat effectiveness for the infected.
topic_desc_basic: Helljoint is a mild common disease that reduces mobility and dexterity. It causes persistent joint irritation and inflammation, and can be contracted from cliff racers.

title: Rattles
topic_desc: Rattles is a mild common disease that diminishes a sufferer's willpower and dexterity. Its characteristic symptoms include persistent muscle spasms and a pronounced listlessness. The affliction is known to be contracted from nix-hounds. Like other common ailments, it responds readily to standard curative magic and potions, posing little lasting threat to prepared travelers in the Ascadian Isles and other nix-hound territories.
topic_desc_basic: Rattles is a mild common disease that reduces willpower and dexterity. It causes muscle spasms and listlessness, and is contracted from nix-hounds.

title: Rust Chancre
topic_desc: Rust chancre is a mild common disease that impairs mobility and behavior. Its symptoms include swelling, rash, and painful muscle spasms. The affliction is transmitted by the waste rat, a vermin found throughout Morrowind's sewers and wilderness. While not life-threatening, the muscular spasms and physical discomfort significantly hinder an infected individual's movement and coordination. As a common disease, it is readily cured through standard restorative magic or temple blessings.
topic_desc_basic: Rust chancre is a mild common disease causing swelling, rash, and painful muscle spasms that impair mobility and behavior. It is contracted from waste rats.

title: Serpiginous dementia
topic_desc: Serpiginous dementia is a serious common disease that afflicts both mind and body. Its psychological symptoms manifest as persistent hallucinations, while the physical presentation includes an itchy, unsightly scaling of the skin resembling snake scales—giving the condition its distinctive name. The disease is transmitted by the bull netch and betty netch, creatures prevalent in the Ascadian Isles and other coastal regions of Morrowind. Without treatment, the combination of mental deterioration and physical discomfort proves debilitating. As a common disease, it responds readily to standard curative magic and restorative potions.
topic_desc_basic: Serpiginous dementia is a common disease causing hallucinations and a distinctive scaly skin eruption resembling snake scales. It is contracted from netches—both the bull and betty varieties. Though serious, it responds to standard common disease treatments.

title: vampirism cure
topic_desc: Vampirism is widely considered incurable, its destruction the only certain remedy. However, suppressed texts and rare accounts suggest otherwise. The banned Volume II of 'Vampires of Vvardenfell' and the private papers of the Buoyant Armiger Galur Rithari both hint at a cure involving the Daedra Prince Molag Bal. Though not the creator of vampirism, Molag Bal is said to possess the means to purge it. At his shrine in Bal Ur, the Prince reportedly offers this cure only to the truly desperate, demanding a service in return. Rithari's own documented cure lends credibility to these claims, though the Temple's suppression of such texts leaves the matter steeped in rumor and uncertainty.
topic_desc_basic: Vampirism is widely held to be incurable, save by the afflicted's destruction. Persistent rumors and suppressed texts, however, claim that the Daedra Prince Molag Bal possesses a cure for the truly desperate, though the Tribunal Temple actively suppresses such accounts.

title: Witbane
topic_desc: Witbane is an acute common disease that degrades cognitive function, manifesting through memory loss and disorientation. It is contracted from rats. While rarely fatal, its erosion of memory and thought renders victims vulnerable and confused. The condition responds to standard common disease treatments and divine intervention at shrines, though delayed care risks prolonged mental impairment.
topic_desc_basic: Witbane is an acute common disease causing memory loss and disorientation. It is contracted from rats and can be cured with standard common disease remedies or temple blessings.

title: Wither
topic_desc: Wither is a mild common disease that drains a victim's strength and endurance. Its symptoms manifest as a loss of energy and shortness of breath. The affliction is known to be contracted from dreugh, the dangerous aquatic creatures inhabiting coastal waters and deeper submerged regions. Like other common ailments, it can be reliably cured through standard restorative magic or common potions.
topic_desc_basic: Wither is a mild common disease that saps a victim's strength and endurance, causing loss of energy and shortness of breath. It is typically contracted from dreugh.

title: Yellow Tick
topic_desc: Yellow tick is a mild common disease characterized by a reduction in a sufferer's physical strength and mobility. Its distinguishing symptoms are dark, bruise-like swellings that remain sensitive to touch. The affliction is known to be transmitted by the least kagouti, making encounters with these creatures a common vector for infection. While generally not life-threatening, the resulting weakness and impaired movement render victims vulnerable if left untreated, though standard curative remedies for common diseases are effective.
topic_desc_basic: Yellow tick is a mild common disease that saps a victim's strength and mobility. It causes dark, bruise-like swellings sensitive to the touch, and is typically contracted from the least kagouti.

title: Census and Excise agent
topic_desc: The Census and Excise is the Imperial agency responsible for collecting taxes and tariffs throughout the Empire's provinces. Its agents enforce Imperial fiscal law, investigate smugglers, and pursue tax evaders. They also regulate restricted commerce, including the Empire's bans on unlicensed trade in Dwemer artifacts and raw ebony. In Morrowind, Census and Excise agents are stationed at ports of entry such as Seyda Neen, where they register new arrivals and inspect cargo. Their enforcement activities make them unpopular with smugglers and those engaged in grey-market trade, who view the agents as meddlesome pests threatening their livelihoods.
topic_desc_basic: The Census and Excise is the Imperial agency that collects the Emperor's taxes and tariffs. Its agents investigate smugglers and tax dodgers, and enforce Imperial bans on unlicensed trade in goods like Dwemer artifacts and ebony. They are widely resented by those engaged in smuggling or grey-market commerce.

title: Gentleman Jim Stacey
topic_desc: Gentleman Jim Stacey is the Redguard Master Thief who leads the Thieves Guild on Vvardenfell from a hidden back room in Simine Fralinie's Vivec bookstore. He wages a desperate defense of the Guild against the Camonna Tong and their influence over the Fighters Guild. To operatives of sufficient rank, Stacey entrusts missions reviving the Bal Molagmer, an ancient tradition of thieves who stole from the unjust to aid the oppressed. He is also known to seek the recovery of several missing artifacts.
topic_desc_basic: Gentleman Jim Stacey is the Redguard leader of the Vvardenfell Thieves Guild. Operating from a concealed room in a Vivec bookshop, he struggles to preserve his organization against the ruthless Camonna Tong and their Fighters Guild allies. Stacey is known for reviving the Bal Molagmer, a tradition of robbing from the unjust to help the oppressed.

title: Magister
topic_desc: Within House Telvanni, Magister is a distinctive rank and declaration of ambition. A wizard elevated to Magister formally contests the sitting Archmagister, asserting superior worthiness to lead the Council. Accepting this title commits the claimant to a challenge for ultimate authority; those who refuse it may settle permanently as a Master, forgoing any future claim to the archmagistry. The path from Magister to Archmagister is traditionally resolved through the removal of the current officeholder, reflecting the Telvanni principle that rightful rule stems from demonstrated power rather than peaceful succession.
topic_desc_basic: In House Telvanni, Magister is a rank declaring the holder's intent to claim the position of Archmagister. A wizard who accepts this title commits to challenging the current Archmagister, while those who decline it remain as Masters and permanently renounce any future claim to lead the Council.

title: Mouth
topic_desc: Mouths serve as the designated proxies and spokespersons for the Mage Lords of House Telvanni on the ruling Council. Because the elder Councilors cannot be troubled with mundane administrative affairs—and may also wish to avoid the persistent threat of assassination by rivals—they dispatch their Mouths to the Telvanni Council House in Sadrith Mora. There, a Mouth receives messengers from their patron, voices their patron's positions, and casts their patron's votes. Each Mouth is typically a younger, ambitious Telvanni wizard acting as a protege to their patron. Advancement to the rank of Wizard within the House requires a member to secure a willing Mouth to represent their interests in the Council Hall.
topic_desc_basic: In House Telvanni, a Mouth is a spokesperson and proxy who represents a Mage Lord on the Council. Because the elder Councilors cannot be bothered with mundane affairs, their Mouths attend sessions at the Telvanni Council House in Sadrith Mora, casting votes and delivering messages on their patron's behalf.

title: Sjoring Hard-Heart
topic_desc: In 3E 427, Sjoring Hard-Heart is the Nord Guildmaster of the Fighters Guild in Morrowind, based in Vivec's Foreign Quarter. His leadership is controversial because many members suspect close ties between him and the Camonna Tong, as well as an aggressive campaign against the rival Thieves Guild. Sjoring is also regarded as one of Vvardenfell's strongest warriors and carries a steel warhammer of smiting. He is the brother of Radd Hard-Heart.
topic_desc_basic: Sjoring Hard-Heart is the Nord Guildmaster of Morrowind's Fighters Guild in 3E 427. Based in Vivec, he is a formidable warrior suspected of corrupt ties to the Camonna Tong.

title: Tharsten Heart-Fang
topic_desc: Tharsten Heart-Fang is the leader of the Skaal tribe on Solstheim, residing in the Greathall. He is the oldest of the Skaal, and his prowess in battle is considered legendary. Quick to anger and judge, he is nevertheless revered as a once-great warrior. Accounts hold that Heart-Fang was corrupted by the Adversary, employing dark magic to prolong his life far beyond its allotted span. His current absence from the tribe casts uncertainty over Skaal leadership, leaving the village's shamans to guide the people until the All-Maker reveals a successor.
topic_desc_basic: Tharsten Heart-Fang is the leader of the Skaal tribe on Solstheim, found in the Greathall. He is the oldest among the Skaal and a legendary warrior, though quick to anger. Tales hold that he was corrupted by dark magic used to extend his life, and his current disappearance leaves the Skaal without clear guidance.

title: Aesliip
topic_desc: Aesliip was once a powerful mage who delved in necromancy. As a consequence of these dark arts, he was transformed into a draugr, yet he retains much of his immense power. He inhabits the caverns beneath Solstheim, where he sustains a magical barrier against a rime wraith infestation. Skaal histories record him as a dangerous creature, though his continued warding suggests a more complex purpose than mere malevolence.
topic_desc_basic: Aesliip was a powerful mage who practiced necromancy. His dark arts transformed him into a draugr, though he retains much of his magical power. Skaal histories remember him as a dangerous creature dwelling in the caves of Solstheim.

title: Captain Carius
topic_desc: Captain Falx Carius is the commanding officer of the Imperial Legion garrison at Fort Frostmoth on the island of Solstheim. An Imperial of rigid discipline, he endeavors to maintain the frontier outpost as a model installation despite the low morale and poor discipline prevalent among his troops. His imposition of a strict alcohol ban, intended to enforce order, proved deeply unpopular and was widely viewed as spiteful by the rank and file. Carius has periodically vanished from the fort under unclear circumstances, forcing his soldiers to seek him out and compounding the garrison's difficulties. He resides in the fort's upper southern chambers.
topic_desc_basic: Captain Falx Carius commands the Imperial Legion garrison stationed at Fort Frostmoth on Solstheim. A strict disciplinarian, he strives to maintain order at the remote outpost, though his controversial alcohol ban has fueled significant resentment among the rank and file. His quarters are located on the uppermost floor of the fort.

title: Darius
topic_desc: General Darius is the Imperial Legion commandant of the Deathshead Legion garrison at Gnisis in 3E 427. He operates from the Madach Tradehouse and is respected for preserving morale and discipline among both human and Orc soldiers. Darius serves as the Legion's principal recruiting commander on Vvardenfell and oversees Imperial military interests around Gnisis. His command is complicated by disputes between the garrison, local settlers, and neighboring communities, requiring political judgment as well as military authority.
topic_desc_basic: General Darius commands the Imperial Legion's Deathshead Legion garrison at Gnisis in 3E 427. He is respected for maintaining discipline among its mixed human and Orc soldiers.

title: Eydis Fire-Eye
topic_desc: Eydis Fire-Eye is a Nord master-at-arms and Guardian of the Fighters Guild, operating from the Balmora chapter. She provides official guild admission and assignments, and is widely regarded as one of Vvardenfell's foremost axe trainers. Despite her prominent guild position, Eydis is a pious worshipper of the Daedric Prince Clavicus Vile and secretly serves the Camonna Tong, aligning her with Sjoring Hard-Heart's faction. This corruption places her at odds with the reformist wing of the guild.
topic_desc_basic: Eydis Fire-Eye is a Nord master-at-arms and Guardian of the Fighters Guild based in Balmora. She handles guild admissions and assignments, and is renowned for her skill with axes. She is a worshipper of the Daedric Prince Clavicus Vile.

title: Garisa Llethri
topic_desc: Garisa Llethri is a Dunmer warrior and councilor of Great House Redoran, residing in Llethri Manor within Ald'ruhn's Skar. As one of the House's governing councilors, his support carries significant weight in Redoran political affairs. Llethri is known for his staunch opposition to House Hlaalu's control of the Caldera ebony mines, which he views as a corrupt arrangement undermining Redoran interests. His manor occupies a prominent position in Skar, situated between the Redoran Council Hall and the Archmaster's residence. Llethri embodies the martial traditions and honor-bound principles valued by his House.
topic_desc_basic: Garisa Llethri is a Dunmer warrior and councilor of Great House Redoran who resides in Llethri Manor within Ald'ruhn's Skar. He is known for his opposition to House Hlaalu's control of the Caldera ebony mines, which he considers corrupt and detrimental to Redoran interests.

title: Hlaren Ramoran
topic_desc: Hlaren Ramoran is a Dunmer knight and Councilman of House Redoran, holding the lordship of the town of Gnisis. He resides in the private quarters of Ramoran Manor in Ald'ruhn, near Skar. Alongside the Morvayn and Sarethi families, the Ramoran household has suffered recent financial and political decline. Known for a temperamental disposition—especially toward outlanders—he nonetheless heeds counsel from trusted allies and remains a steadfast, honorable lord to his retainers. He is a prominent figure in Redoran governance whose support is vital for any seeking high office within the House, requiring the completion of practical duties to earn his endorsement.
topic_desc_basic: Hlaren Ramoran is a Dunmer knight and House Redoran Councilor serving as the lord of Gnisis. He resides in Ramoran Manor in Ald'ruhn. Though known for a temper, particularly with foreigners, he is regarded by his retainers as an honorable and noble lord.

title: Jobasha
topic_desc: Jobasha is a Khajiit scholar and the proprietor of Jobasha's Rare Books, located in the Vivec Foreign Quarter's Lower Waistworks. His shop offers an extensive selection of obscure texts and enjoys the protection of an Ordinator dispatched by Duke Vedam Dren. A fervent abolitionist allied with the Twin Lamps and Ilmeni Dren, Jobasha freely voices his staunch opposition to slavery. These passionate political views render both the Khajiit and his establishment polarizing figures within Morrowind's society.
topic_desc_basic: Jobasha is a Khajiit bookseller who runs Jobasha's Rare Books in the Vivec Foreign Quarter. Known for his extensive collection of obscure texts, he is also a fervent abolitionist who openly opposes slavery, making him a polarizing figure in Morrowind.

title: Karrod
topic_desc: Karrod is a Redguard warrior serving as King Hlaalu Helseth's Champion and a member of Mournhold's Royal Guard. Long perceived as deaf and mute, he was found as an orphaned child on the streets of Wayrest after attempting to rob Princess Elysana; Helseth, marveling at his audacity, took him in, earning his fierce lifelong loyalty. Karrod's father gave him a Dwemer longsword, prophesying he would remain undefeated until its rightful owner claimed it. True to this prophecy, he is widely regarded as an unparalleled fighter. He frequents the Winged Guar, favoring Cyrodiilic brandy. His Dwemer weapon is rumored to be a fragment of the legendary Trueflame.
topic_desc_basic: Karrod is a Redguard warrior who serves as King Hlaalu Helseth's Champion in Mournhold. Widely considered the finest fighter in the Royal Guard, he is believed to be deaf and mute. He is fiercely loyal to Helseth, who took him in as an orphaned child in Wayrest. He is often found at the Winged Guar.

title: Korst Wind-Eye
topic_desc: Korst Wind-Eye serves as shaman of the Skaal, the isolated Nordic community of Solstheim. Renowned for his wisdom and potent magic, he acts as both spiritual guide and counselor to his people, dispensing insight on matters of importance from the Shaman's Hut in the Skaal village. The title Wind-Eye reflects his gift for foresight and perception. He frequently traverses the island's harsh wilderness on personal errands, yet remains the foremost authority on Skaal traditions and the natural balance they revere. His counsel is sought by villagers and outsiders alike.
topic_desc_basic: Korst Wind-Eye is the shaman of the Skaal village on Solstheim. Revered for his wisdom and strong magic, he serves as spiritual advisor and counselor to his people. He may typically be found in the Shaman's Hut or wandering the island's wilds.

title: Tienius Delitian
topic_desc: Tienius Delitian is the Captain of King Helseth Hlaalu's Royal Guard in Mournhold. A career soldier who has served Helseth since the monarch's youth at the Imperial Court, Delitian was chosen for his command not solely for his martial prowess but for his shrewd political acumen and excellent judgment of character. Queen Mother Barenziah regards him as a trusted, intelligent advisor despite a rough exterior, and Helseth trusts him implicitly. His prominent position as an Imperial leading the Dunmer capital's royal security draws mixed reactions; some respect his competence, while others, including Temple loyalists, view him with disdain or suspicion. He operates from the Royal Palace throne room.
topic_desc_basic: Tienius Delitian is the Imperial Captain of King Helseth's Royal Guard in Mournhold. A career soldier who has served Helseth since the king's youth in the Imperial Province, he is valued as both a fine warrior and a shrewd political advisor. He can typically be found in the Royal Palace throne room.

title: Varus Vantinius
topic_desc: Varus Vantinius is the Knight of the Imperial Dragon, commanding the Imperial Legion's forces in Vvardenfell from the Grand Council Chambers in Ebonheart. As the highest-ranking Legion officer in the district, Vantinius holds authority over all Imperial military operations and represents the Empire's martial presence alongside the Duke of Ebonheart. His position demands both administrative oversight and personal combat readiness, reflecting the Legion's dual role as garrison and governing force in the province.
topic_desc_basic: Varus Vantinius serves as the Knight of the Imperial Dragon, the highest-ranking Imperial Legion officer in Vvardenfell. He commands the Legions from the Grand Council Chambers in Ebonheart.

title: murder Nerevar
topic_desc: The allegation that the Tribunal murdered Indoril Nerevar is a central dispute between Ashlander and Temple traditions. Ashlander oral histories preserve the account of Alandro Sul, Nerevar's shield-companion, who lived among the Ashlanders after the Battle of Red Mountain and accused the Tribunal of killing Nerevar. The Temple rejects this as false, acknowledging that Sul's narrative contains persuasive details alongside implausible ones, and maintains alternative records of Nerevar's death. The truth remains contested, with Ashlanders viewing the Tribunal's rise as founded on betrayal and the Temple venerating Almsivi as divine and righteous.
topic_desc_basic: Ashlander tradition holds that the Tribunal murdered Indoril Nerevar after the Battle of Red Mountain, based on the testimony of his shield-companion Alandro Sul. The Tribunal Temple denies this accusation and maintains its own accounts of Nerevar's death. The truth remains deeply contested between the two traditions.

title: Tribunal fight Dagoth Ur
topic_desc: The Tribunal's military campaigns against Dagoth Ur and his House Dagoth kin constitute a prolonged conflict centered on Red Mountain. In earlier eras, the Tribunal conducted seasonal expeditions to the region, successfully slaying Dagoth Ur and his ash vampires. However, because Dagoth Ur's essence is bound to the Heart of Lorkhan, these victories proved temporary; the Heart invariably restored him. Recognizing the futility of destruction, the Tribunal shifted strategy, constructing the Ghostfence to contain the blight and Dagoth Ur's forces. This containment held for centuries until a devastating ambush by Dagoth Ur resulted in the capture of the vital tools Sunder and Keening. Since that defeat, Tribunal power has waned while Dagoth Ur's influence has grown.
topic_desc_basic: The Tribunal historically waged seasonal campaigns against Dagoth Ur at Red Mountain, slaying him repeatedly. Because the Heart of Lorkhan always revived him, the Tribunal instead built the Ghostfence to contain his forces. This strategy failed when Dagoth Ur ambushed them, capturing Sunder and Keening, greatly weakening the Tribunal.

title: Ald Redaynia
topic_desc: Ald Redaynia is an ancient ruined wizard's tower on the western tip of a large island off Vvardenfell's northern coast, west of Sheogorad. The isolated Velothi structure dates to the Merethic Era and preserves the character of an early Dunmer settlement. Its surviving upper chambers overlook the northern sea, while a concealed flooded chamber lies beneath the tower. A small fishing community nearby emphasizes the remoteness of the site and its distance from the island's major roads and ports.
topic_desc_basic: Ald Redaynia is a ruined Merethic Era wizard's tower on an island off Vvardenfell's northern coast. The remote Velothi site includes upper chambers and a hidden flooded level.

title: Andasreth
topic_desc: Andasreth is one of Vvardenfell's ancient Dunmer strongholds, standing in a dry pocket of the West Gash north of Khartag Point and Gnaar Mok. Its heavy Velothi construction recalls an era when such fortresses protected regional travel and noble power. The stronghold contains a Propylon Chamber linked to Hlormaren and Berandas, placing it within the old magical transport network that joins the ten Dunmer strongholds. Centuries of abandonment have left its halls dangerous despite their historical and architectural importance.
topic_desc_basic: Andasreth is an ancient Dunmer stronghold in the West Gash north of Khartag Point. Its Propylon Chamber connects the ruin with Hlormaren and Berandas through the old stronghold transport network.

title: Assernerairan
topic_desc: Assernerairan is a hidden Daedric shrine dedicated to Mehrunes Dagon, located in the underworks of Vivec City's St. Olms Canton. The cult operating there draws the ire of the Morag Tong, who claim its leadership harbors figures marked for their brand of execution. Sanguine items are known to be held by the Dagon worshippers within. The sanctuary is guarded by armored zealots, and at least one cultist bears a formidable Daedric longsword. Another follower is reputedly skilled in stealth and light armor. An accursed emerald rests upon the shrine's altar, and a Dark Brotherhood presence has also established itself in the vicinity, creating a layered and dangerous environment beneath the canton's ordinary interiors.
topic_desc_basic: Assernerairan is a Daedric shrine to Mehrunes Dagon hidden in the underworks of St. Olms Canton in Vivec City. The cult occupying the underground sanctuary is known to attract dangerous worshippers and is rumored to share its depths with a Dark Brotherhood presence.

title: Caldera ebony mines
topic_desc: The Caldera ebony mines are an Imperial-chartered ebony extraction operation southwest of Caldera, operated under House Hlaalu's administration. The site features an office, bunkhouse, and guard tower near the mine entrance within a mountain bowl. Notably, the mines rely on slave labor, a practice legal in Morrowind but controversial elsewhere. The mines have drawn scrutiny over alleged corruption; Hlaalu administrators are suspected of smuggling unreported ebony beyond Imperial quotas. This exploitation of Red Mountain's resources has fueled resentment among other Great Houses, particularly House Redoran, who consider the ebony the rightful property of the Dunmer and view Imperial involvement as illegitimate exploitation.
topic_desc_basic: Ebony mines southwest of Caldera, operated by House Hlaalu under Imperial charter. The site extracts valuable ebony ore using slave labor, a practice legal in Morrowind but criticized by outlanders. The operation has attracted controversy over potential smuggling and the question of who rightfully owns the resources drawn from Red Mountain.

title: crater citadels
topic_desc: The crater citadels are five ancient Dwemer strongholds within the Red Mountain crater. By 3E 427 they form the fortified heart of the Sixth House under Dagoth Ur and his ash vampire kin. The citadels are known by the names of their Dagoth Lords: Endusal, Odrosal, Vemynal, Tureynulal, and Dagoth Ur. Ghostgate and Foyada Esannudan provide the principal approach through the Ghostfence, beyond which the strongholds support the Sixth House and the spread of the Blight across Vvardenfell.
topic_desc_basic: Five ancient Dwemer citadels stand inside Red Mountain's crater. In 3E 427 they are strongholds of Dagoth Ur and the Sixth House, approached through Ghostgate and the Ghostfence.

title: Forts
topic_desc: The Imperial Legion maintains garrison forts throughout Morrowind as military and administrative centers projecting Imperial authority. On Vvardenfell, these include Fort Pelagiad in the Pelagiad settlement, Fort Hawkmoth at Ebonheart, Fort Moonmoth outside Balmora, Fort Buckmoth outside Ald'ruhn, and Fort Darius in Gnisis. Fort Frostmoth on Solstheim serves as the island's sole Imperial installation. These forts house Legion soldiers, coordinate regional operations, and often provide services to nearby civilian populations.
topic_desc_basic: Imperial Legion forts serve as military garrisons and administrative centers across Morrowind. Key Vvardenfell installations include Fort Pelagiad, Fort Hawkmoth, Fort Moonmoth, Fort Buckmoth, and Fort Darius. Fort Frostmoth is the sole Imperial garrison on Solstheim.

title: Ihinipalit
topic_desc: Ihinipalit is a shrine to Sheogorath hidden in the sewers beneath the St. Delyn Canton of Vivec City. Its Daedric worship stands in deliberate contrast to the Tribunal Temple institutions occupying the cantons above. The shrine contains a statue through which the Madgod is said to address mortals, often demanding dangerous, absurd, or humiliating acts. Temple authorities regard Ihinipalit as a profane site, while followers of Sheogorath value it as a concealed place of communion with their unpredictable patron.
topic_desc_basic: Ihinipalit is a hidden shrine to Sheogorath in the sewers beneath Vivec's St. Delyn Canton. Its statue is said to let the Madgod address worshippers and impose bizarre demands.

title: Koal Cave
topic_desc: Koal Cave is a coastal grotto south of Gnisis, sacred to the Tribunal Temple as the site where Vivec battled Ruddy Man. It serves as one of the stations on the Pilgrimages of the Seven Graces, housing the Shrine of Valor near its entrance. Pilgrims traditionally offer dreugh wax at the shrine to receive Vivec's blessing. The cave contains kollop beds that attract pearl divers, alongside aquatic creatures including dreugh. Located beyond the Ouada Samsi, the cave entrance sits below a natural arch along the coast.
topic_desc_basic: Koal Cave is a sacred Tribunal pilgrimage site south of Gnisis, marking where Vivec fought Ruddy Man. The Shrine of Valor inside honors this battle, and pilgrims offer dreugh wax there for blessings. The coastal grotto lies across the river from Gnisis.

title: Maelkashishi
topic_desc: Maelkashishi is a ruined Daedric shrine dedicated to Sheogorath, the Daedric Prince of Madness and one of the Four Corners of the House of Troubles. It occupies the bleak wealds of the West Gash along the border with the Ashlands, situated west and slightly north of Maar Gan and roughly southeast of Ald Velothi. The site remains an active center of worship for the Madgod's unpredictable followers. Beyond its main consecrated chamber, the complex extends into the Forgotten Galleries, a deeper section harboring additional Daedric occupants and notable relics. The shrine's cultists are notoriously hostile to outsiders, and the grounds are known to harbor both afflicted worshippers and summoned Daedra.
topic_desc_basic: A ruined Daedric shrine in the West Gash of Vvardenfell, dedicated to Sheogorath of the House of Troubles. It lies west of Maar Gan near the Ashlands border and remains occupied by the Madgod's unpredictable followers.

title: Skar
topic_desc: Skar is the colossal shell of a felled Emperor crab, now serving as the architectural centerpiece of Ald'ruhn. Ashlander oral tradition holds that their ancestors defeated the beast in ancient times, though the identity of the warrior and the exact method of its slaying have been lost to memory. For the Ashlanders, the carcass remains a solemn monument to ancestral strength and a symbol of future glory. In the present day, Great House Redoran has adapted the hollow interior into the Manor District, with the residences and shops of its prominent citizens built securely under Skar.
topic_desc_basic: Skar is the colossal shell of a felled Emperor crab in Ald'ruhn. Great House Redoran has built the homes and shops of its Manor District inside the hollow carapace, while Ashlanders revere the carcass as a monument to their ancestors' victory.

title: Venim Manor
topic_desc: Venim Manor is the residence of the Venim family, situated at the southeast corner of the Ald'ruhn Manor District beneath Skar. It serves as the seat of Bolvyn Venim, the Redoran councilor and Archmaster, housing his family and retainers. The manor comprises five interior sections. As the dwelling of one of House Redoran's most prominent leaders, it stands as a significant landmark in the district.
topic_desc_basic: Venim Manor is the home of the Venim family, located in the Ald'ruhn Manor District beneath Skar. It sits at the southeast corner and houses Bolvyn Venim, his family, and his retainers.

title: birthsign
topic_desc: Birthsigns are the constellations governing the heavens at the moment of a person's birth. Tamrielic astrologers teach that particular celestial conjunctions impress lasting magical influences upon those born beneath them. Such people may be fortunate in their aspects, receiving unusual gifts of body, mind, or sorcery, yet the same influence can impose a corresponding weakness or burden. A birthsign is therefore understood as both an omen and an enduring part of a person's nature, joining astronomy, magic, and fate in a single tradition.
topic_desc_basic: A birthsign is the constellation ruling the sky when someone is born. Its celestial influence may grant remarkable natural abilities, but it can also bring an unusual weakness or curse.

title: ebony
topic_desc: Ebony is a rare, extremely hard volcanic glass found primarily in the lava flows and buried deposits around Vvardenfell's Red Mountain, prized as one of Tamriel's most precious substances. Also known as Godsblood, it is widely believed to be the crystallized blood of Lorkhan, shed after his defeat at Convention. The Dunmer have worked ebony since the time of Boethiah, and the lustrous black material is forged into heavy, highly sought-after weapons and armor through a process of repeated folding. Its scarcity and divine associations make it a cornerstone of Morrowind's wealth and a resource tightly controlled by Great House interests.
topic_desc_basic: Ebony is a rare, extremely hard volcanic glass found mainly in Vvardenfell's Red Mountain lava flows. Also called Godsblood, it is believed to be the crystallized blood of Lorkhan. The dark, lustrous substance is forged into highly prized, heavy weapons and armor, making it one of Tamriel's most valuable materials.

title: enchanters
topic_desc: Enchanters are practitioners of the magical art that binds spell effects into physical objects, producing items that cast spells with reliable consistency. Their craft serves both their own needs and those unskilled in conventional spellcasting, granting magical capability through objects rather than personal aptitude. The simplest enchanted products are scrolls—single-use items that anyone can activate with complete reliability, though the scroll is destroyed in the process. More sophisticated work places permanent enchantments upon weapons, armor, clothing, and ornaments. These enduring items draw power from soul gems integrated during creation; a gem's capacity limits the frequency of use, but expended energy renews over time, rendering such items indefinitely serviceable.
topic_desc_basic: Enchanters bind magical effects into physical objects, creating items that cast spells reliably. They serve both themselves and those who lack spellcasting skill. Scrolls are their simplest products—single-use items destroyed after casting. More complex enchantments are placed permanently on weapons, armor, and clothing, powered by soul gems whose energy renews over time.

title: Argonian neighbors
topic_desc: The Dunmer of Morrowind have long regarded their Argonian neighbors to the south as fit only for servitude. For centuries, the Great Houses have raided Black Marsh's borders and enslaved Argonians, treating them as little better than beasts of burden. Though the Empire formally protects Argonian rights within its domains, it has not abolished the institution of slavery in Morrowind, leaving countless Argonians in bondage. This entrenched exploitation defines relations between the two neighboring peoples.
topic_desc_basic: The Dunmer have long enslaved their Argonian neighbors from Black Marsh, regarding them as animals fit only for servitude. Though the Empire protects Argonian rights elsewhere, it permits slavery to continue in Morrowind, leaving relations between these neighboring peoples defined by exploitation and resentment.

title: Betmeri
topic_desc: The Betmeri, commonly called Beastmen, are the aboriginal inhabitants of Tamriel, predating the arrival of Mer and Men. The term encompasses diverse races including the Khajiit, Argonians, and Orcs, alongside smaller populations like Goblins, Apemen, and Giants. Each Betmeri race possesses distinct physical and cultural characteristics, differing from one another as significantly as they do from Elven and Manish races. While Khajiit and Argonians are the most numerous and culturally advanced, Orc tribes are notable for superior martial prowess and weapon crafting. Smaller Betmeri are largely confined to remote western and northern mountains.
topic_desc_basic: Betmeri, or Beastmen, are the aboriginal inhabitants of Tamriel. This broad category includes diverse races such as Khajiit, Argonians, Orcs, Goblins, Apemen, and Giants, each as culturally and physically distinct from one another as from Elves and Men.

title: Elven ancestry
topic_desc: Elven ancestry, or mer lineage, traces all extant elven peoples to the Aldmer, the ancient progenitor race that settled Tamriel from the vanished continent of Aldmeris. Over millennia, cultural and ideological divergence, alongside varying divine allegiances, splintered the Aldmer into the modern Altmer, Dunmer, Bosmer, and Orsimer. Tracing personal lineage remains deeply significant for many elves, particularly among the Altmer, who prize ancestral purity. Some individuals claim descent from vanished or secluded groups like the Dwemer or Falmer, though verifying such connections proves exceedingly difficult given the scarcity of surviving historical evidence.
topic_desc_basic: All Tamrielic elves share descent from the Aldmer, the ancient progenitor race. Over time, these ancestors diverged into the modern Altmer, Dunmer, Bosmer, and Orsimer. Tracing personal lineage remains culturally significant, and some individuals even claim descent from vanished groups like the Falmer, though firm evidence is scarce.

title: Humans
topic_desc: Humans are short-lived, socially aggressive humanoids, shorter than Elves yet more technologically advanced than Beastfolk. Through martial conquest, human cultures have subjugated Elven and Beastfolk neighbors, synthesizing their subjects' arts, literature, magick, technology, and theology into Tamriel's dominant civilization—the Empire. Obsessed with progress and destiny, human civilization perpetually reinvents itself from materials plundered from conquered cultures and reshaped through human myths and aspirations, making humans the architects of the current era's political and cultural order.
topic_desc_basic: Humans are short-lived, aggressive humanoids shorter than Elves but more advanced than Beastfolk. Their warlike cultures conquered neighboring peoples and forged the Empire that now dominates Tamriel. Driven by obsession with progress and destiny, humans constantly reinvent civilization from conquered knowledge reshaped by their own myths.

title: Aldmeris
topic_desc: Aldmeris is the mythical lost continent from which the Mer peoples are said to have originated, also known as Old Ehlnofey or the Isle of Aldmeris. Its location, environment, and even its existence remain conjecture. Ancient tapestries depict it as an endless city devoid of natural life, built upon itself repeatedly. According to legend, the Aldmer departed during an unspecified crisis, eventually landing on Auridon. A Middle Merethic Era expedition of three ships failed to relocate it. Whether the angry gods sank it, it left Mundus entirely, or was never a physical place at all is fiercely debated. The term also refers to the original Elven language, still spoken by isolated communities and educated Mer.
topic_desc_basic: Aldmeris is the mythical lost continent from which the Mer peoples are said to have originated. Its location and very existence remain conjecture. Ancient accounts describe it as an endless city devoid of natural life. The Aldmer departed during an ancient crisis, eventually settling in Tamriel. The name also denotes the original Elven language, still spoken and written by educated Mer.

title: ash storm
topic_desc: Ash storms are severe meteorological events characteristic of Vvardenfell, carrying dense clouds of volcanic ash from the Red Mountain region across the surrounding landscape. These storms severely reduce visibility, pose a lethal hazard to travelers and trade caravans, and force residents to seek immediate shelter wherever available. The settlements near Red Mountain, such as Maar Gan, frequently endure the most devastating effects. Livestock and goods are routinely lost to the choking, blinding ash, and travelers caught in the open face extreme danger, often becoming trapped in nearby tombs or ruins while waiting for the storm to pass. The Tribunal is frequently invoked for protection from these unpredictable disasters.
topic_desc_basic: Ash storms are severe weather events on Vvardenfell that carry dense volcanic ash from Red Mountain. They drastically reduce visibility and endanger travelers and trade, frequently killing pack animals and ruining goods. Settlers caught in the open must immediately seek shelter in whatever structures are nearby. Towns near the volcano, such as Maar Gan, often bear the worst of these destructive storms.

title: Bal Ur region
topic_desc: Bal Ur is an uninhabitable ash waste region in Molag Amur, named after the ancient Bal Ur Daedric ruins that serve as both a local landmark and a Tribunal pilgrimage site. The terrain consists of rugged highlands broken by lava fields and ash pits. The harsh environment provides no grazing for Ashlander guar herds, though the nomads hunt there. The region's desolation makes it a convenient refuge for outlaws and Ashlander outcasts who seek to avoid settled authority.
topic_desc_basic: Bal Ur is an ash waste region named after the ancient Bal Ur Daedric ruins, a local landmark and pilgrimage site. Its rugged highlands are broken by lava fields and ash pits. Lacking grazing, it sees Ashlander hunters but also serves as a refuge for outlaws and outcasts.

title: Mortrag Glacier
topic_desc: Mortrag Glacier occupies the northwestern coast of Solstheim within the Moesring Mountains, situated west of Castle Karstaag. It is a vast, desolate ice formation widely rumored to be haunted by evil spirits. Local accounts speak of strange occurrences at the glacier, including unsettling reports that portions of the ice have collapsed inward. The glacier's interior conceals a hollowed-out Daedric ruin, a fact largely unknown to the island's general populace. This hidden structure serves as the ritual site for the Hunter's Game during the Bloodmoon Prophecy, where Hircine's werewolf hounds pursue chosen prey through the frozen tunnels. The glacier's remote and hostile nature ensures that very little life inhabits the surrounding area.
topic_desc_basic: Mortrag Glacier is a large, desolate glacier in the northwestern corner of Solstheim, within the Moesring Mountains. Very little lives in the area, and local legends claim the ice is haunted by evil spirits. Strange recent tidings suggest the glacier has collapsed in on itself.

title: ash statue
topic_desc: Small figurines distributed by Sixth House cultists and their smuggler networks, ash statues exert a corrupting magical influence on those who keep them nearby. Placed in dwellings, they induce disturbing, mind-altering dreams and erode the will of their owners, serving as insidious tools for Dagoth Ur's spreading influence. The statues are channeled through hidden shrine cells in settlements, where cultists such as those posing as outcast Ashlanders oversee their distribution to unwitting contacts. Temple and House Redoran authorities recognize the statues as dangerous artifacts linked to the Sixth House and seek to destroy them and root out their sources.
topic_desc_basic: Small figurines used by Sixth House cultists to spread Dagoth Ur's influence. Kept in homes, they cause disturbing dreams and corrupt the minds of those nearby. The Temple and Great Houses consider them dangerous and work to destroy them.

title: Sovngarde
topic_desc: Sovngarde is the storied afterlife of the Nords, said to dwell within Aetherius as a reward for those who die valiantly in honorable combat. Shor created it through his Clever Magic, and at its heart stands the Hall of Valor, a vast feasting hall where mead flows without end and the honored dead know neither pain nor tedium. Tsun guards the Whalebone Bridge, testing new arrivals in combat before they may enter Shor's hall. Kyne, called the Kiss at the End, is believed to guide worthy souls to Sovngarde. Whether the realm truly exists remains debated; some dismiss it as myth, while others cite accounts such as the correspondence between the medium Felga Four-Fingers and the ghost of Rolf the Large, which claims death itself is the entrance Shor intended.
topic_desc_basic: Sovngarde is the legendary afterlife of the Nords, built by the god Shor as a gift to the valiant. Within its Hall of Valor, the honored dead feast eternally on endless mead and test their mettle in ceaseless contest. Kyne is said to guide worthy souls to Sovngarde, though some scholars consider the realm mere myth.

title: The All-Maker
topic_desc: The All-Maker is the supreme deity of the Skaal, the isolated Nord tribe of Solstheim. Unlike the Nine Divines, the All-Maker is conceived as a singular, pervasive force that created and animates the natural world, rather than a distinct personified god. The Skaal believe that all life and the elements are interconnected parts of this entity. To please the All-Maker, the Skaal observe strict nature rituals, taking only what is needed and giving back to the land to maintain a vital balance. Disrupting this harmony offends the All-Maker, risking blight, harsh winters, and the disruption of the hunt. The Skaal also venerate the All-Maker's aspects through ancestral communion and the Greedy Man, their adversarial figure of imbalance.
topic_desc_basic: The All-Maker is the supreme deity worshipped by the Skaal of Solstheim. Unlike the Nine Divines, the Skaal revere a single, all-encompassing force of nature rather than a pantheon of distinct gods. To please the All-Maker, the tribe strictly honors the natural balance, taking only what is necessary from the land and giving back in return. Disrupting this harmony brings blight and harsh winters.

title: the power of the Skaal
topic_desc: The power of the Skaal is the spiritual force derived from the All-Maker, maintained through the Oneness—a harmonious balance between the Skaal people and their land. When this balance is disrupted, the land suffers. Restoration requires the Ritual of the Gifts, a sacred rite performed at six Standing Stones on Solstheim, each representing one of the All-Maker's gifts. Completing these rites restores the Oneness and the Skaal's communal power. The Mace of Aevar Stonesinger is a revered treasure of this faith. The Skaal shaman oversees these traditions, and outsiders who prove their loyalty and wisdom may be permitted to participate in the rituals.
topic_desc_basic: The Skaal draw their spiritual power from the All-Maker, maintained through the Oneness—a sacred balance with the land of Solstheim. When disrupted, this power must be restored through the Ritual of the Gifts, performed at six Standing Stones representing the All-Maker's gifts. The Skaal shaman guides these rites.

title: to be a god
topic_desc: The state of divine existence involves dwelling simultaneously within time and outside it. For a god, the mortal world is experienced like wakefulness, while the god place outside time is like sleep, where all moments occur at once. Death in the temporal world is merely a choice to sleep; returning to life requires only the choice to wake, with no subjective time lost. However, for gods who still walk the mortal plane, this duality demands constant awareness of countless moving threads. The burden of maintaining this divine juggling act grows heavier with time, and even gods may find their touch faltering as they age, dropping the things they strive to sustain.
topic_desc_basic: Divine existence means dwelling both within time and outside it. The god place is outside time, where all moments happen at once. Death in the mortal world is merely sleep; a god returns to life simply by choosing to wake. Yet gods who remain in the mortal world must juggle countless threads of existence, a burden that grows heavier with age.

title: cantons
topic_desc: The cantons are the massive, multi-tiered administrative and residential structures comprising the city of Vivec. Constructed by the Tribunal Temple, which retains ownership and leases space to guilds, shops, and residents, each canton functions as a self-contained district. They are vertically stratified: the upperworks house wealthy manors and exclusive shops; the waistworks contain commercial premises, guildhalls, and apartments; canalside provides cramped housing for the poor; and the underworks consist of submerged sewers navigated only by scavengers and sanitation workers. The interior corridors form notoriously labyrinthine passages. This architectural model reflects both Temple authority and the rigid social hierarchy of Vvardenfell's largest settlement.
topic_desc_basic: The cantons are the massive, multi-tiered buildings that form the city of Vivec. Built and leased by the Tribunal Temple, each canton is vertically divided into the wealthy upperworks, the commercial waistworks, the impoverished canalside, and the subterranean underworks. Their interior corridors are notoriously maze-like.

title: settlements in Morrowind
topic_desc: Morrowind's settlements range from the metropolitan scale of Vivec City to small Ashlander nomadic camps of portable huts. Urban centers follow three broad traditions: the native Dunmer style seen in Ald'ruhn, the Imperial style of newer colonial towns like Caldera, and the metropolitan sprawl of Vivec City. Rural Dunmer villages cluster small huts around Temple compounds. In the sparsely populated Telvanni District, the so-called tower towns function as large villages dominated by monumental wizard tower complexes rather than conventional civic infrastructure. Ashlander camps represent the smallest and most mobile settlements, reflecting the nomadic traditions of the Dunmer ancestral ways.
topic_desc_basic: Morrowind's settlements range from the vast metropolis of Vivec City to tiny Ashlander nomadic camps of portable huts. Urban dwellers inhabit the native Dunmer style of Ald'ruhn, the Imperial colonial style of newer towns like Caldera, or Vivec's metropolitan sprawl. Rural Dunmer cluster huts around Temple compounds, while Telvanni tower towns are large villages dominated by monumental wizard towers.

title: St. Delyn Canton
topic_desc: St. Delyn Canton is a residential canton in Vivec, administered by the Tribunal Temple to provide affordable housing, workshops, and shops for commoners and paupers. Alongside St. Olms Canton, it houses much of Vvardenfell's crafts and light industry. The Temple charges reasonable rents for these accommodations. The Abbey of St. Delyn the Wise occupies the canton's top tier, serving as a religious center. The canton's waistworks and underworks support the daily commerce and infrastructure of its working populace, reflecting the Temple's civic role in maintaining orderly habitation for Vvardenfell's lower and middle strata.
topic_desc_basic: St. Delyn Canton is a residential district in Vivec, operated by the Tribunal Temple. It and neighboring St. Olms Canton provide affordable housing and workshops for commoners and paupers, housing much of Vvardenfell's crafts and light industry. The Abbey of St. Delyn the Wise sits atop the canton.
tags: Abbey of St. Delyn the Wise

title: St. Olms Canton
topic_desc: St. Olms Canton is a residential and industrial district in Vivec City, situated south of the Arena and adjacent to St. Delyn Canton. Along with St. Delyn, it houses Vvardenfell's commoners and paupers, providing affordable workshops, shops, and apartments managed by the Temple at reasonable rents. Most of the region's crafts and light industry operate from these two cantons. St. Olms is structured in tiers from the plaza level down to the underworks. The underworks contain the Assernerairan shrine, while the top tier features a manor belonging to Hlaalu Councilor Yngling Half-Troll. The canton's various halls host specialized guilds of brewers, fishmongers, farmers, laborers, tailors, dyers, tanners, and miners.
topic_desc_basic: St. Olms Canton is a residential and industrial district in Vivec City. Together with St. Delyn Canton, it provides affordable housing and shop space for commoners and paupers, with rents managed by the Temple. The canton hosts much of Vvardenfell's crafts and light industry across its tiered structure.

title: Tear
topic_desc: Tear, also called Dres, is the capital of Great House Dres and a major mainland Morrowind city near the hot, humid borderlands of Argonia. Its wealth comes from vast saltrice plantations and a dominant role in the Dunmeri slave trade, with its notorious slave-pens supplying labor throughout the region. Although House Dres is strongly traditionalist and isolationist, Tear maintains an active harbor and significant commerce. In 3E 427 King Niasth rules this fortified center of agrarian power.
topic_desc_basic: Tear, also called Dres, is the mainland capital of Great House Dres. Its saltrice plantations, harbor, and slave trade make it a wealthy commercial center near the Argonian border.

title: Anu
topic_desc: Anu, or Anu the Everything, is the anthropomorphization of the primal force of Stasis and Order, the eternal counterpart to Padomay's Change and Chaos. In the oldest cosmogenic myths, the brothers entered the Void, and their interplay birthed Nir. After Padomay's violence shattered the twelve worlds of Creation, Anu salvaged their remnants to form Nirn. Grappling his brother outside of Time forever, Anu's spilled blood became the stars, while mingled blood formed the Aedra. Revered across Tamriel under diverse names—Ahnurr to the Khajiit, Satak to the Redguards, and Anui-El to the Altmer—he represents the foundational principle of existence.
topic_desc_basic: Anu, or Anu the Everything, is the primal force of Stasis and Order, eternally opposed to Padomay's Change. After Padomay shattered the twelve worlds of Creation, Anu salvaged their remnants to form Nirn. His blood became the stars, and his mingled blood with Padomay formed the Aedra. He is known across Tamriel by many names, including Anui-El, Ahnurr, and Satak.

title: Padomay
topic_desc: Padomay, called PSJJJJ in Ehlnofex and known by many names including Sithis, is the primal force of change and chaos, the eternal counterpart to Anu's stasis. In the Anuad creation myth, Padomay entered the Void alongside his brother Anu. His bitter jealousy of Nir and subsequent violence against her set in motion the first conflict. Cast outside Time by Anu, Padomay later returned to shatter the twelve worlds of Creation. Their final struggle pulled both brothers beyond Time forever. Padomay's blood became the Daedra, entities unbound by Creation, while his mingled blood with Anu formed the Aedra. He remains central to metaphysical traditions emphasizing change, entropy, and limitation.
topic_desc_basic: Padomay is the primal force of change and chaos, eternally opposed to Anu's stasis. Creation myths hold that his jealousy and violence sparked the first cosmic conflict. His blood became the Daedra, and his mingled blood with Anu formed the Aedra.

title: Nir
topic_desc: Nir, called the world-parent, is a primordial entity from the earliest cosmogonic myths. She emerged from the interplay of Anu and Padomay within the Void. Both brothers were captivated by her, but she loved only Anu. Her pregnancy by Anu provoked Padomay's bitter return; upon her rejection, he assaulted her. Though Anu cast Padomay outside Time, Nir's injuries proved fatal. She perished shortly after giving birth to the twelve worlds of Creation. In her memory, Anu later fashioned the remnants of those shattered worlds into a single realm, naming it Nirn. Nir thus represents the foundational maternal sacrifice underlying the mortal plane.
topic_desc_basic: Nir is a primordial figure from creation myths. She emerged in the Void and loved the deity Anu, spurning Padomay. Padomay attacked her in rage, and though she gave birth to the twelve worlds of Creation, she died from her wounds. The mortal world, Nirn, is named in her memory.

title: Aurbis
topic_desc: The Aurbis is the totality of existence, the imperceptible Gray Maybe born from the intersection of the primordial forces Anu and Padomay. It encompasses all planes of existence—Aetherius, Oblivion, and the mortal center, Mundus—as well as the Void beyond. Often conceptualized as the Wheel, its hub is Mundus, its spokes the Eight Divines, its rim Aetherius, and the empty spaces between Oblivion. The et'Ada, the Original Spirits, emerged within the Aurbis from the interplay of stasis and change, eventually crystallizing into gods and demons. Psijic apologists describe it as a fanciful Unnatural Realm where magical beings lived complex narrative lives before their communal death or transfiguration birthed the mortal plane and its inhabitants. Some Altmeri scholars alternatively envision the Aurbis as a telescope stretching back to the eye of Anui-El, with innumerable Padomaics along its infinite walls.
topic_desc_basic: The Aurbis is the entire cosmos, the Gray Maybe formed between the primordial forces of Anu and Padomay. It encompasses all known planes of existence, including the mortal realm of Mundus, the magical realms of Aetherius, the planes of Oblivion, and the surrounding Void.

title: Mundus
topic_desc: Mundus, also called the Gray Maybe or the Mundex Terrene, is the mortal plane encompassing Nirn and its surrounding structure. Its origin remains deeply disputed. The prevailing traditions hold that Lorkhan convinced or contrived the Original Spirits—the Aedra—to bring about its creation, with Magnus providing designs. To humans, this act constitutes divine mercy, enabling lesser creatures to reach immortality; to most Aldmer, it represents a cruel deception that sundered their connection to the spirit plane. Alternative cosmologies propose radically different origins, suggesting the mortal world is a direct creation of Anu, or that Nirn is a deity born of Ahnurr and Fadomai. In Mundus, conflict and disparity drive change, the most sacred force recognized by certain esoteric orders.
topic_desc_basic: Mundus is the mortal plane of existence, encompassing Nirn. Its creation is widely attributed to Lorkhan's inspiration and the Aedra's sacrifice, though cultures fiercely disagree on whether this act was divine mercy or cruel deception. Alternative origin myths also persist.

title: Aetherius
topic_desc: Aetherius, the Immortal Plane, is the luminous realm of pure magic and origin of the Aedra within the Aurbis. The sun and stars are believed to be wounds in the firmament left by Magnus and the Magna Ge as they fled the creation of Mundus, channeling aetherial light and magicka into the mortal world. Mortal souls, carrying a spark of this Aetherial essence, are said to return there after death. Various cultures envision distinct afterlife realms within its infinite expanse, including Sovngarde, the Far Shores, and the Sands Behind the Stars. Since the conclusion of the Mythic Era, Aedric spirits rarely interfere directly with Nirn, leaving the plane's mysteries largely inaccessible to the living.
topic_desc_basic: Aetherius is the Immortal Plane, a realm of pure magic and the origin of the Aedra. The sun and stars are believed to be holes in the sky left by spirits fleeing the creation of the mortal world, through which magicka flows. It is also widely believed to be the destination of mortal souls after death.

title: Ehlnofey
topic_desc: The Ehlnofey are the mythic progenitors of Mer and Men, Aedric spirits who remained on Nirn after Magnus departed. In elven belief, some of these spirits sacrificed themselves entirely to become the Earthbones, the immutable laws of nature, while others chose to populate the world, diminishing over generations into mortal races. The Annotated Anuad offers a differing cosmogony, claiming the Ehlnofey survived a prior twelve-world creation shattered by Padomay before Nirn's formation. This text divides them into the Old Ehlnofey, who preserved their ancient realm and became the Mer, and the wandering Ehlnofey, who became the Men of other continents. Elven faith reveres the Ehlnofey as divine ancestors, while human religions generally regard them as creators rather than forebears.
topic_desc_basic: The Ehlnofey are the ancient ancestors of all Mer and Men, Aedric spirits who stayed on Nirn during its creation. Some became the Earthbones, the laws of nature, while others diminished over generations into mortal races. Elven tradition reveres them as divine ancestors, a view most humans reject.

title: the Hist
topic_desc: The Hist are a sentient race of giant spore trees inhabiting the innermost swamps of Black Marsh, considered among the most ancient life forms on Tamriel. According to cosmological tradition, they survived the shattering of the twelve worlds alongside the Ehlnofey, remaining bystanders in the subsequent war that destroyed most of their realm, leaving only a small corner that became Black Marsh. All Hist are connected at the root, sharing a single mind, and their roots stretch deep into Nirn's heart. Argonians call themselves people of the root and rely on Hist sap for hatching rituals; separation from this sap proves fatal to the unborn. The Hist acknowledge Sithis as the Original Creator. Some myths suggest they originated from a lush Oblivion realm brought to Tamriel during the Dawn Era.
topic_desc_basic: The Hist are a sentient race of giant spore trees inhabiting Black Marsh's innermost swamps. Among Tamriel's most ancient life forms, they survived the Ehlnofey war that destroyed most of their realm. All Hist share a single mind connected through their roots. Argonians revere them, relying on their sap for vital hatching rituals.

title: Convention
topic_desc: Convention, also called the Moot at the House of We, is the foundational event of the Dawn Era, held at the Adamantine Tower outside aurbic time. At this impossipoint, the et'Ada gathered to determine the physical, temporal, spiritual, and magical laws of Mundus and Nirn. The gathering established the roles of all spirits within the mortal realm. Some traditions equate Convention with the Ehlnofex war, viewing it as the same cosmogenic moment described through a different cultural lens.
topic_desc_basic: The Convention, or Moot at the House of We, was a Dawn Era gathering of the et'Ada at the Adamantine Tower. Occurring outside time, this foundational event established the physical, spiritual, and magical laws governing Mundus and Nirn, defining the roles of all spirits within creation.
aliases: Moot at the House of We

title: the Earthbones
topic_desc: The Earthbones are the Ehlnofey, et'Ada who sacrificed their existence to stabilize the Mundus during creation. When Lorkhan's plan imposed limitation upon the Aurbis, the aspects of the et'Ada began to perish. To prevent the new world from dying entirely, some, such as Y'ffre, willingly transformed into the Ehlnofey, anchoring the laws of nature and mortal existence. Others instead married and produced offspring, growing weaker each generation until the Aldmer emerged. In Altmeri tradition, the Earthbones represent both the tragedy of the Aedra's diminishment and the divine foundation that sustains the mortal realm.
topic_desc_basic: The Earthbones, or Ehlnofey, are et'Ada who stabilized the mortal world during its creation. When the Mundus began to kill its creators, beings like Y'ffre sacrificed themselves, transforming into the Earthbones to preserve existence. Others survived by producing offspring, eventually weakening into the Aldmer.

title: the Lunar Lorkhan
topic_desc: The Lunar Lorkhan is a cosmological treatise by Fal Droon proposing that Masser and Secunda are the two sundered halves of Lorkhan's divine flesh. Unlike the Eight divinities who voluntarily contributed portions of their heavenly bodies to construct Nirn, Lorkhan's plane was cracked apart, and his divine spark fell as a shooting star to impregnate the mortal realm. The moons thus embody the Artaeum's concept of the Cloven Duality—opposing principles such as anima and animus, being and nothingness—serving as Lorkhan's constant reminder to mortal issue of their duty. Adherents consider alternative Heart Stories mythical degradations and likewise observe the hollow crescent theory regarding the moons' nature.
topic_desc_basic: The Lunar Lorkhan is a cosmological theory by Fal Droon proposing that the moons Masser and Secunda are the two halves of Lorkhan's sundered divine flesh. According to this account, Lorkhan's plane was cracked apart during the creation of Nirn, and the moons now embody a Cloven Duality of opposing metaphysical principles, serving as a constant reminder to mortals of their origin and duty.

title: Dragon Break
topic_desc: A Dragon Break is a disruption of linear time, named for Akatosh, the Dragon God of Time. During these events, causality fractures and multiple contradictory timelines may unfold simultaneously before resolving. The most prominent instance is the Middle Dawn, caused by the Maruhkati Selectives' ritual upon White-Gold Tower. Accounts of this era never coincide, save that eight stars fell. The Numidium's activations also triggered temporal fractures. The scholar Fal Droon controversially claims the Middle Dawn is a myth born of a dating error in the Encyclopedia Tamrielica, arguing the Alessian Order lasted merely 150 years rather than a millennium. However, conflicting testimonies and the Amulet of Kings affirm the reality of these temporal schisms.
topic_desc_basic: A Dragon Break is a disruption of linear time named for Akatosh. During these events, causality fractures and contradictory timelines unfold simultaneously. The most famous instance, the Middle Dawn, was triggered by the Maruhkati Selectives. Though some scholars dispute its reality, diverse testimonies confirm these temporal schisms occurred.

title: Aedra
topic_desc: The Aedra are primordial et'Ada who participated in the creation of the Mundus, an act that bound them to the Earth Bones and associated them with cosmic stasis. The Elvish term translates to 'ancestors,' reflecting the belief that they begat the mortal races, in contrast to the Daedra, or 'not our ancestors,' who embody change and cannot create. In common parlance, the designation applies to the Eight great spirits who forged the mortal world, though some theological perspectives argue the term properly encompasses all beings involved in that creation, regardless of their original standing among the Aetherius-aligned et'Ada. As part of the divine contract of creation, the Aedra are mortal in principle and can be killed, as evidenced by Lorkhan, whereas the Daedra can only be banished.
topic_desc_basic: The Aedra are the divine ancestors who created the mortal world and are bound to the Earth Bones. The Elvish term means 'ancestors,' distinguishing them from the Daedra, or 'not our ancestors,' who embody change and cannot create. Associated with cosmic stasis, the Aedra can be killed as part of the divine contract of creation, unlike the Daedra, who can only be banished.

title: realms of Oblivion
topic_desc: The realms of Oblivion constitute the infinite dimension surrounding the mortal plane, serving as the native territory of the Daedra. Rather than a single contiguous landscape, Oblivion comprises numerous distinct principalities, each governed by a Daedra Prince. These realms—such as Coldharbour, Quagmire, and Moonshadow—reflect the sphere and temperament of their ruling Prince. Mortal understanding of these domains remains limited, drawn chiefly from conjuration, scattered First Era accounts, and rare mythological texts. The Daedra themselves resist simple categorization beyond their immense power and extremism, though certain Princes consistently exhibit destructive spheres. Whether mortal passage into Oblivion is practically achievable remains a subject of arcane inquiry.
topic_desc_basic: Oblivion is the dimension surrounding the mortal plane, home to the powerful Daedra. It consists of many distinct realms or principalities, each ruled by a Daedra Prince. These realms, including Coldharbour, Quagmire, and Moonshadow, reflect the nature of their rulers. Mortal knowledge of these dangerous lands comes primarily from ancient accounts and conjuration.

title: Sithis
topic_desc: Sithis is the primordial force of chaos, change, and limitation, often equated with the Void and identified as the soul of Padomay. In Dunmeri theology, Sithis is the true start of the house; before it existed only the nothing of stasis. Sithis sundered this nothing, fashioning myriad possibilities that ebbed and faded. When the demon Anui-El and the Aedra enslaved these creations within everlasting imperfection, Sithis begat Lorkhan to destroy the universe and reintroduce decay. The Dark Brotherhood venerates Sithis as the Dread Father, believing souls killed in its name pass to the Void. Sithis is neither Aedric nor Daedric, existing beyond such classifications.
topic_desc_basic: Sithis is the primordial force of chaos, change, and the Void. Revered by the Dunmer as the true start of creation and by the Dark Brotherhood as the Dread Father, it is neither Aedra nor Daedra. Sithis represents the disruption of nothingness and the inevitable return of all things to the Void.

title: Shezarr
topic_desc: Shezarr is the Cyrodilic expression of Lorkhan, widely honored as the God of Man and the Missing Sibling of the Eight Divines. In early Nedic traditions, he served as a unifier and teacher who revealed Ayleid battle-magic to oppressed humans. Following the Alessian Revolt, Empress Alessia diluted his warrior aspect to appease both Nordic and Aldmeri subjects, recasting him as the beneficent spirit behind all human undertaking. This compromise diminished his prominence, and in the present era of racial tolerance, his once-vital cult is all but forgotten save for a modest following in the Imperial City and the Colovian West, where he is still called Shor.
topic_desc_basic: Shezarr is the Cyrodilic version of Lorkhan, known as the Missing Sibling of the Eight Divines and the God of Man. Once a vital warrior deity who inspired early humans against Ayleid oppression, Alessia later recast him as a peaceful spirit of human endeavor to unite her Nordic and Aldmeri subjects. Today, his worship is largely forgotten.

title: the Velothi exodus
topic_desc: The Velothi exodus was the great migration of the Aldmeri dissidents who followed the prophet Veloth from Summerset to Resdayn. According to orthodox teaching, Boethiah consumed Trinimac, assumed his voice to expose the et'Ada as liars, and revealed the Tri-Angled Truth. Assisted by Mephala, Boethiah instructed the exiles in the Psijic Endeavor, the building of Houses, and the proper ways to wear skin and walk to achieve their departure. Trinimac's remains became the Changed Ones, the Orcs. The exodus founded Velothi civilization and set the religious and cultural foundations of Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: The Velothi exodus was the migration of Aldmeri dissidents led by the prophet Veloth from Summerset to Resdayn. Boethiah revealed the Tri-Angled Truth to them and, with Mephala, taught the foundations of their new culture. This journey established Velothi civilization in Morrowind.

title: Dunmer funerary rites
topic_desc: Dunmer funerary rites center on venerating ancestors whose spirits protect and advise the living. Each household maintains a shrine, the Waiting Door, where families offer prayers and receive blessings. The paramount duty is interring remains at a City of the Dead like Necrom, where spirits find comfort.
