Widely regarded as Vvardenfell's favorite local dish, it is prized for its remarkably tasty flavor as much as its modest magical properties. In alchemy, scuttle is valued for its restorative and fortifying qualities, as well as its utility in altering physical weight and manipulating objects at a distance. Its exact alchemical effects are Restore Fatigue, Fortify Fatigue, Feather, and Telekinesis. The ingredient is commonly available in civilized areas through vendors and food larders rather than direct creature harvesting.
topic_desc_basic: Scuttle is a yellowish, lumpy, cheese-like substance with a greasy sheen, made from the flesh of local beetles. It is considered Vvardenfell's favorite local dish, valued for its taste and modest magical properties. Alchemists use it for its restorative and fortifying qualities, as well as its ability to lighten burdens and manipulate objects at a distance.

title: Shalk Resin
topic_desc: Shalk resin is a rough, amber-colored lump of hardened resin exuded from shalk beetles, slightly translucent and valued at fifty drakes per portion. The tough, soluble substance is extracted from shalk hides and serves practical purposes beyond alchemy: it is widely used as a glue and stiffener in the manufacture of bonemold and chitin armors throughout Morrowind. In alchemical preparations, shalk resin exhibits four distinct properties: Drain Fatigue, Fortify Health, Drain Personality, and Fortify Speed. The combination of restorative and debilitating effects makes it a complex ingredient, valued by apothecaries for its capacity to bolster vitality and swiftness even as it saps endurance and social bearing.
topic_desc_basic: Shalk resin is an amber-colored, slightly translucent lump exuded by shalk beetles. The tough, soluble substance extracted from shalk hides doubles as a glue and stiffener in bonemold and chitin armor crafting. Alchemists prize it for effects ranging from fortifying health and speed to draining fatigue and personality.

title: Sload Soap
topic_desc: A pale, waxy slab of soap bearing a faintly slick surface and rounded edges from uneven hand-molding. It is produced from the immature, non-sentient forms of the Sload, the necromantic slug-folk of Thras. Extremely rare in Morrowind proper due to the absence of local Sload populations, the substance is typically acquired through specialist apothecaries. Healers value it for salves addressing joint ailments and mobility, though its alchemical profile demands careful formulation. Its exact alchemical effects are Drain Personality, Fortify Agility, Fire Shield, and Restore Agility.
topic_desc_basic: A pale, waxy slab of soap bearing a faintly slick surface and rounded edges from uneven hand-molding. This rare substance is rendered from the immature, non-sentient forms of the Sload. It is scarce in Morrowind and typically sourced from apothecary vendors. Alchemists employ it for preparations that bolster agility and provide fire resistance, though it also diminishes personality.

title: Small Kwama Egg
topic_desc: A small, pale ovoid egg with a smooth, slightly translucent shell and faint mottling across its surface. Laid by kwama in the egg mines of Vvardenfell, these eggs are a staple foodstuff throughout the Empire, prized for their nutrition and longevity. While large kwama eggs are more potent, the small variety is far more common, routinely harvested by miners and kept in household larders. In alchemy, its modest magical properties are harnessed to Restore Fatigue.
topic_desc_basic: A small, pale ovoid egg with a smooth, slightly translucent shell and faint mottling. Harvested from kwama in Vvardenfell's egg mines, it is a common, nutritious foodstuff. Alchemists use its modest properties to Restore Fatigue.

title: Snow Bear Pelt
topic_desc: A thick white pelt from a snow bear, showing pale fur over a supple hide. Harvested from the formidable snow bears roaming Solstheim's frozen wilderness, this pelt is valued in alchemy for its diverse properties. Proper preparation yields four distinct effects: Drain Fatigue, Fortify Speed, Resist Common Disease, and Night Eye. The combination of fortifying and resistive qualities makes it a versatile component, though alchemists must account for its draining attribute when formulating mixtures.
topic_desc_basic: A thick white pelt from a snow bear, showing pale fur over a supple hide. Harvested from the snow bears of Solstheim, it is used in alchemy for its varied properties, including the ability to fortify speed and grant night vision.

title: Snow Wolf Pelt
topic_desc: A thick white pelt stripped from a snow wolf, bearing dense pale fur suited to arctic cold. Harvested from the elusive snow wolves roaming the frozen wastes of Solstheim, this hide serves alchemists as a versatile reactive base. When prepared properly, it yields four distinct properties: Drain Fatigue, Fortify Speed, Resist Common Disease, and Night Eye. These combined effects make the pelt particularly valued for crafting warmth and endurance remedies suited to harsh northern survival, while its speed-enhancing and vision-sharpening qualities offer clear tactical advantages in the bleak arctic environment.
topic_desc_basic: A thick white pelt stripped from a snow wolf, bearing dense pale fur suited to arctic cold. Snow wolves of Solstheim yield this ingredient, which alchemists value for its speed-enhancing and vision-sharpening properties alongside its ability to resist common disease and drain fatigue.

title: Spore Pod
topic_desc: A rounded, pale pod covered in small bumps, split open to reveal dark spores within. Spore pods are harvested from the slough fern, a plant found in the shallow pools of the Bitter Coast region. Alchemists value the pod for its diverse properties, though it requires careful handling due to its debilitating qualities. When prepared, it yields the effects Drain Strength, Drain Fatigue, Detect Key, and Paralyze, making it a potent component for both harmful mixtures and utility concoctions.
topic_desc_basic: A rounded, pale pod covered in small bumps, split open to reveal dark spores within. It is harvested from slough ferns growing in the Bitter Coast's shallow pools. Alchemists use it to brew mixtures that can paralyze targets, reveal hidden keys, or drain a subject's strength and fatigue.

title: Stoneflower Petals
topic_desc: Stoneflower petals are harvested from a small flower common to the Ascadian Isles and Azura's Coast, with substantial growths also found throughout the West Gash. The dark blue blooms feature stems that bend toward the ground when in bloom, with leaves that appear folded along their length. The petals themselves are delicate and purple, curling inward from a pale green stem, their surfaces marked by faint white veins. Alchemists value stoneflower petals for their varied properties; when prepared, they can Restore Strength and Fortify Magicka, though practitioners must account for their capacity to Drain Luck while they Fortify Personality.
topic_desc_basic: Stoneflower petals grow on a small, common blue flower found in the Ascadian Isles, Azura's Coast, and the West Gash. The plant's stems bend groundward when in bloom. Alchemists use these delicate purple petals to Restore Strength and Fortify Magicka, though they also Drain Luck and Fortify Personality.

title: Sweetpulp
topic_desc: Sweetpulp is a moist, amber-colored paste produced by mashing the soft, pulpy flesh of a sweetpod. Prized by alchemical practitioners in Mournhold and beyond, its practical applications are remarkably diverse. When properly prepared, sweetpulp manifests four distinct alchemical effects: Paralyze, Levitate, Resist Paralysis, and Restore Health. This unusual combination of immobilizing and liberating properties, alongside restorative and protective virtues, makes it a versatile component in both hostile elixirs and curative preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Sweetpulp is a moist, amber-colored paste made by mashing the soft, pulpy flesh of a sweetpod. Alchemists value it for its diverse properties, which can Paralyze, Levitate, Resist Paralysis, and Restore Health.

title: Timsa-Come-By flowers
topic_desc: Timsa-Come-By flowers grow in small clusters, each bearing pale, rounded petals atop slender green stems of delicate construction. The plant is found in the Mournhold region, where herbalists gather it for its varied alchemical properties. When prepared properly, the blooms yield four distinct effects: Dispel, which strips active enchantments from a subject; Resist Paralysis, offering defense against petrifying afflictions; Drain Magicka, reducing a target's magical reserves; and Restore Endurance, replenishing physical stamina. The combination of restorative and protective virtues makes Timsa-Come-By a practical component for healers crafting remedies against paralysis and fatigue, though the Drain Magicka effect demands careful formulation in restorative mixtures.
topic_desc_basic: Timsa-Come-By flowers are clusters of small, pale blossoms with slender green stems and delicate rounded petals, found in the Mournhold region. Alchemists value them for yielding Dispel, Resist Paralysis, Drain Magicka, and Restore Endurance effects in potion-making.

title: Trama Root
topic_desc: A gnarled, rough-skinned root twists into crooked, branch-like tendrils with a dusty brown exterior. Harvested from the trama shrub, which thrives in the ashy soils of the Ashlands, Molag Amur, and around Red Mountain, the thick, bitter-tasting root is commonly brewed into a calming tea with modest magical properties. In alchemical practice, trama root is valued for its ability to Restore Willpower and confer the power of Levitate, though these benefits come at a cost, as preparations also Drain Magicka and Drain Speed. Its prevalence in Vvardenfell's dry regions makes it a familiar reagent to regional alchemists despite its mixed properties.
topic_desc_basic: Trama root is a gnarled, dusty brown root harvested from the trama shrub, which grows in the ashy soils of Vvardenfell's Ashlands and Molag Amur. It is commonly brewed into a calming, bitter tea and is known to alchemists for its ability to Restore Willpower and cause Levitate, while also carrying the detrimental properties to Drain Magicka and Drain Speed.

title: Treated Bittergreen Petals
topic_desc: Treated Bittergreen Petals are pallid green flower petals, chemically treated and pressed flat into brittle, translucent sheets. They are derived from the common bittergreen plant of Morrowind. Alchemists value the treated form for its distinctive properties: preparations can Restore Intelligence and grant Invisibility, while also inducing Drain Magicka and Drain Endurance. The treatment process renders the petals more potent than their untreated counterpart, making them a sought-after reagent among skilled practitioners.
topic_desc_basic: Treated Bittergreen Petals are pallid green flower petals chemically treated and pressed into brittle, translucent sheets. Derived from Morrowind's bittergreen plant, they are valued by alchemists for properties including Restore Intelligence, Drain Magicka, Drain Endurance, and Invisibility.

title: Unripened Belladonna Berries
topic_desc: Unripened belladonna berries are pale green unripened berries that grow in small, round clusters on thin, dark stems. Found on belladonna bushes across Solstheim, these berries are distinct from their ripened counterparts and are valued in alchemical practice. When prepared, they exhibit a potent magicka affinity, yielding the effects Resist Magicka, Restore Magicka, Fortify Magicka, and Drain Magicka. This unusual combination makes them a sought-after reagent for brews that manipulate an individual's magical reserves and resistance, though the Drain Magicka effect demands careful formulation to avoid unintended consequences.
topic_desc_basic: Unripened belladonna berries are pale green berries growing in small, round clusters on thin, dark stems. Harvested from belladonna bushes on Solstheim, they are used by alchemists for their magicka-affecting properties.

title: Vampire Dust
topic_desc: A small pile of fine, pale ash gathered from the remains of a destroyed vampire. This rare residue is collected solely from the withering corpses of slain vampires and is of particular interest to necromancers and alchemists. Its potent properties make it highly valued in magical research and apothecary. When used in alchemy, vampire dust yields Fortify Health, Fortify Strength, Spell Absorption, and Vampirism. The Vampirism effect is unique to this substance and cannot be combined with other ingredients to produce a viable potion, nor does raw consumption transmit the actual affliction.
topic_desc_basic: A small pile of fine, pale ash gathered from the remains of a destroyed vampire. Prized by alchemists and necromancers, it is collected solely from the withering corpses of slain vampires and occasionally sold by specialized apothecaries.

title: Violet Coprinus
topic_desc: A small violet mushroom with a slender pale stem and a delicate, umbrella-shaped cap. Found abundantly in the Bitter Coast region and within caves, this fungus exhibits modest magical properties. Alchemists value it for its three confirmed effects: Water Walking, Drain Fatigue, and Poison. Its Water Walking property makes raw consumption a practical emergency escape from deep water, while the Poison effect provides a rare and useful tool for toxin brewing alongside luminous russula.
topic_desc_basic: A small violet mushroom with a slender pale stem and a delicate, umbrella-shaped cap. It grows abundantly in the Bitter Coast region and in caves. Healers and alchemists recognize its modest magical properties, which include beneficial and harmful qualities.

title: Void Salts
topic_desc: Dark crystalline salts forming jagged clusters are contained within a small rough clay vessel. Void salts are rare crystalline precipitates collected from the evanescent remains of slain storm atronachs and winged twilights, representing the physical essence of these conjured Daedra as they dissipate back into Oblivion. Highly valued by alchemists, void salts possess potent magical properties. Their exact alchemical effects are Restore Magicka, Spell Absorption, Paralyze, and Drain Endurance.
topic_desc_basic: Dark crystalline salts forming jagged clusters, kept in a small rough clay vessel. These rare precipitates are harvested from the remains of slain storm atronachs and winged twilights. Alchemists prize them for their magical properties.

title: Wickwheat
topic_desc: Wickwheat is a wild Ashland grain growing profusely across the Grazelands of Vvardenfell, making it the region's most abundant plant. It appears as pale golden wheat stalks bearing small clustered kernels, their thin dried husks tightly wrapped around slender grains. For the Dunmer, it serves as a cheap staple for cooking—yielding toast, crackers, and Narsis ale—and as structural thatching for Ashlander yurts alongside hides and sinew. Alchemically, it is a readily accessible reagent. Its known properties are Restore Health and Fortify Willpower, while its latent effects are Paralyze and Damage Intelligence. Mixed with corkbulb, marshmerrow, or saltrice, it yields common healing potions affordable to commoners.
topic_desc_basic: Wickwheat is a wild Ashland grain that grows abundantly in Vvardenfell's Grazelands. It appears as pale golden stalks with small clustered kernels. Dunmer use it widely as a cheap cooking staple and structural material for Ashlander yurts. Alchemically, it possesses modest properties, most commonly used to Restore Health or Fortify Willpower.

title: Willow Anther
topic_desc: A small, pale yellow flower anther from a willow plant, featuring slender filaments and a fine, dusty coating of pollen. Willow plants grow in the Ascadian Isles and on Azura's Coast, bearing reddish, tall flowers with long, thin leaves. The anther is the powdery residue collected from the pollen-bearing parts of these blooms. In alchemy, willow anther is a potent and inexpensive material valued by healers for producing curative mixtures. Its properties include Drain Personality, Frost Shield, Cure Common Disease, and Cure Paralyzation.
topic_desc_basic: A pale yellow, pollen-dusted anther harvested from the tall, reddish willow flowers of the Ascadian Isles and Azura's Coast. Healers prize this inexpensive ingredient for its curative properties, particularly its ability to cure paralysis and common disease, though it also provides frost shielding and drains personality.

title: Wolf Pelt
topic_desc: A coarse, grayish pelt stripped from a wolf, retaining the thick fur and leathery hide of the beast. Wolves roam the wilds of Solstheim and parts of Skyrim, and their pelts are traded widely by hunters and trappers. Alchemists value the pelt for its diverse properties: it can be prepared to yield Drain Fatigue, Fortify Speed, Resist Common Disease, and Night Eye effects. The combination of enhancing agility and vision while sapping stamina makes it a curious but useful reagent in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: A coarse, grayish pelt taken from a wolf, preserving the thick fur and tough hide. Wolves are common across Solstheim and Skyrim. Alchemists prepare wolf pelts to produce several effects, including enhanced speed and night vision, alongside resistance to common disease and fatigue reduction.

title: Wolfsbane Petals
topic_desc: Wolfsbane petals are delicate purple petals plucked from the wolfsbane flower, bearing faintly veined surfaces and curled, papery edges. The flower grows in the wilds of Solstheim, where it is gathered for alchemical preparations. Despite its fragile appearance, the petals produce a potent and mixed spectrum of effects: Restore Intelligence and Invisibility alongside Drain Endurance and Drain Magicka. This combination makes the ingredient valuable to practitioners seeking restorative or concealment properties, though the draining side effects demand careful formulation. Healers value it chiefly for its restorative qualities, while alchemists exploit the full range for complex multi-effect preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Wolfsbane petals are delicate purple petals plucked from the wolfsbane flower, bearing faintly veined surfaces and curled, papery edges. The plant grows on Solstheim. Alchemists prize the petals for yielding Restore Intelligence and Invisibility, though preparations also produce Drain Endurance and Drain Magicka, requiring careful use.

title: Chitin equipment
topic_desc: Chitin equipment comprises armor and weapons fashioned from the lacquered exoskeletal plates of Morrowind's large insects. Craftsmen shape reddish-brown shell segments into cuirasses, greaves, pauldrons, gauntlets, boots, and helms—including a masked variant—binding the plates with sinew over dark leather backings. The same material yields slender arrows with chitin heads and feather fletching, short carving daggers with segmented organic hilts, and knobby laminated clubs with wrapped grips. Chitin gear is light and affordable, favored by Ashlander clans and common travelers who cannot procure metalwork. Its construction reflects deep adaptation to Vvardenfell's fauna, turning the island's giant insects into practical martial equipment without dependence on imported steel or bonemold.
topic_desc_basic: Chitin armor and weapons are crafted from the lacquered shells of Morrowind's large insects. Artisans bind reddish-brown chitin plates with sinew over leather to form cuirasses, greaves, pauldrons, gauntlets, boots, and helms. The material also yields arrows, daggers, and clubs. Lightweight and inexpensive, chitin gear is common among Ashlander clans and provincial travelers.

title: Bonemold equipment
topic_desc: Bonemold equipment comprises armor and weaponry manufactured from finely ground bone and resilient resin, shaped and lacquered into rigid plates. This medium-weight composite forms the customary armament of House Dunmer retainers and guards, balancing protection with the mobility demanded by Morrowind's rugged terrain. Armor pieces include reinforced cuirasses, layered pauldrons, sturdy greaves, and helms, all typically finished in dark brown lacquer. The Armun-An style distinguishes itself with rounded torsos, wide shoulder flanges, and a rough reddish-brown stain over layered chitin-shaped plates. Bonemold also extends to martial ranged implements; fletched arrows and bolts of carved bone and resin composite, as well as reinforced long bows, complement the Dunmer martial tradition.
topic_desc_basic: Bonemold equipment is a traditional Dunmer armament fashioned from ground bone and resin, shaped into lacquered plates. Favored by House retainers and guards across Morrowind, it offers reliable protection without excessive weight. Common pieces include cuirasses, pauldrons, greaves, and helms, alongside bone-tipped arrows, bolts, and long bows. The Armun-An style features a distinctive reddish-brown lacquered finish.

title: Netch leather equipment
topic_desc: Netch leather equipment comprises light armor crafted from the boiled hide of the domesticated netch, a large floating beast native to Morrowind. The leather is worked into flexible, mottled brown panels with segmented, overlapping construction secured by sturdy strapping, offering modest protection with excellent mobility. Standard pieces include the close-fitting Netch Leather Helm with its short nose guard, the flexible Netch Leather Cuirass with broad shoulder flaps, matching greaves, gauntlets, pauldrons, boots, and both round and tower shields. A distinct hardened variant, the Boiled Netch Leather Cuirass and Helm, features darkened, rigid hide shaped into a dome or torso-covering shell for greater resilience. This affordable armor is culturally ubiquitous among Dunmer, favored by scouts, hunters, and travelers.
topic_desc_basic: Netch leather equipment is a common Dunmer light armor fashioned from the boiled hide of the native netch. The flexible, mottled brown leather provides modest protection and good mobility. Standard pieces include helms, cuirasses, greaves, gauntlets, pauldrons, boots, and shields. Hardened boiled variants offer a darker, rigid shell for improved defense.

title: Dreugh equipment
topic_desc: Dreugh equipment comprises arms and armor shaped from the hardened, chitinous shell of dreugh, aquatic creatures of Morrowind's coastal and deep waters. The material's natural rigidity and organic ridges lend themselves to distinctive, segmented construction. Armor pieces such as the Dreugh Cuirass, Dreugh Helm, and Dreugh Shield feature overlapping carapace plates, curved ridges, and angular bosses that echo the creature's form, while weapons like the heavy Dreugh Club and the two-handed Dreugh Staff employ the shell's knobby, pitted texture for formidable striking surfaces. Though uncommon, dreugh gear is valued by Dunmer warriors and smiths for its exotic resilience and the cultural significance of harvesting from a dangerous aquatic predator.
topic_desc_basic: Dreugh equipment consists of arms and armor crafted from the hardened chitinous shells of dreugh, dangerous aquatic creatures. The organic, ridged carapace is shaped into distinctive protective gear and heavy weapons. Examples include the Dreugh Cuirass, Dreugh Helm, Dreugh Shield, Dreugh Club, and Dreugh Staff.

title: Iron equipment
topic_desc: Iron equipment constitutes the most widespread and affordable family of arms and armor across Tamriel, forged from common smelted ore. Armor pieces such as cuirasses, boots, and greaves are formed from dark metal plates riveted to thick leather with buckled straps, offering substantial weight for reliable protection. Weaponry ranges from slender rust-flecked arrows and bolts to heavy two-handed battle axes with thick double blades on long wooden hafts, broadswords with simple crossguards, and imposing claymores. Iron arms serve as the standard kit for provincial militias, mercenaries, and common adventurers. Representative examples include the iron broadsword, iron claymore, iron halberd, iron battle axe, iron dagger, iron club, iron arrow, iron bolt, iron fork, iron cuirass, iron boots, and iron greaves.
topic_desc_basic: Iron arms and armor are the most common and affordable equipment across Tamriel, forged from standard smelted ore. The armor employs dark metal plates riveted to leather, while the weapons range from simple daggers and arrows to heavy two-handed battle axes and claymores. This equipment serves militias, mercenaries, and common travelers.

title: Steel equipment
topic_desc: Steel equipment comprises a widespread family of heavy arms and armor forged from carbon-hardened iron. Segmented plate construction predominates, balancing protection with articulation through overlapped plates, reinforced cuffs, and articulated joint guards. The Empire widely issues steel panoplies to its legions, and Imperial variants like the Imperial Steel Helmet, Imperial Steel Boots, and Imperial Steel Greaves form the backbone of the Legion's heavy infantry kit. Ancient steel examples such as the Ancient Steel Cuirass, Ancient Steel Helm, and Ancient Steel Tower Shield survive with darkly oxidized, pitted surfaces and corroded finishes, bearing witness to considerable age while retaining their segmented plate construction. Such relic pieces occasionally surface on Solstheim. Steel weapons complement these defenses as standard military sidearms across Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: Steel equipment is a common family of heavy arms and armor forged from carbon-hardened iron. The Empire widely issues steel panoplies to its legions, with standardized pieces like the Imperial Steel Helmet, boots, and greaves equipping heavy infantry. Ancient steel variants, recognized by their darkly oxidized and pitted surfaces, also survive from earlier eras.

title: Silver equipment
topic_desc: Silver equipment comprises arms and armor forged from precious silver, valued primarily for its efficacy against undead and magical creatures immune to ordinary steel. Imperial legionnaires employ polished silver cuirasses built with segmented plates over dark leather straps and helms featuring broad nasal guards with fitted cheek plates. Nordic silver weaponry follows traditional northern aesthetics: curved one-handed axes on carved hafts, two-handed battleaxes and claymores mounted on pale wooden grips, tapered daggers with wrapped leather handles, alongside longswords, shortswords, and maces. Ranged options include silver arrows and bolts. Though softer than steel, silver's supernatural efficacy ensures its enduring place in professional arsenals.
topic_desc_basic: Silver equipment encompasses arms and armor crafted from precious metal, prized for harming undead and magical beings that resist ordinary steel. The Imperial Legion fields polished silver cuirasses and helms, while Nordic smiths produce traditional silver axes, claymores, daggers, maces, and swords. Silver arrows and bolts also see regular use against supernatural foes.

title: Imperial equipment
topic_desc: Imperial equipment encompasses the standardized arms and armor issued to the legions of the Septim Empire. Construction prioritizes functional steel and sturdy leather, dyed in the deep red associated with Imperial legionnaires. The core armor comprises interlocking steel chain—coifs with draped mantles, segmented greaves with hanging metal skirts, and riveted pauldrons—designed for versatile provincial garrison duty. Specialized cuirasses include the Imperial Newtscale, fashioned from treated aquatic hide, the Imperial Silver cuirass for resistance to magical foes, and the elite Imperial Dragonscale helm and cuirass. Standard weaponry features the steel Imperial Broadsword, with its straight double-edged blade and leather-wrapped crossguard grip, alongside the Imperial Shortsword. A simple iron-buckled leather belt completes the legionnaire's kit.
topic_desc_basic: Standardized arms and armor of the Septim Empire's legions are built from functional steel and sturdy leather dyed deep red. The kit includes interlocking steel chain coifs, greaves, and pauldrons, alongside specialized newtscale, silver, and dragonscale cuirasses. Legionnaires wield steel broadswords and shortswords, wearing a simple iron-buckled belt.

title: Nordic equipment
topic_desc: Nordic equipment encompasses the weaponry and armor traditionally crafted by the Nordic peoples of Skyrim and their colonial kin. Weapons such as the Nordic Broadsword, Claymore, and Battle Axe feature robust steel blades mounted on cross-guarded hilts or sturdy wooden hafts, built for powerful two-handed strikes or versatile single-hand use. Armor relies heavily on cured leather and thick, shaggy pelts lined with fur to fend off harsh northern cold, epitomized by the Nordic Bearskin Cuirass and the full range of fur helms, greaves, gauntlets, bracers, pauldrons, and boots. The Ancient Nordic Pick Axe represents a weathered iron variant with a double-headed blade, reflecting older mining and survival tooling. These arms and hides are favored by Nordic warriors, sailors, and smiths across the northern territories.
topic_desc_basic: Nordic equipment is the traditional arms and armor of the Nordic peoples, built to endure Skyrim's harsh climate. Weapons like the Nordic Broadsword, Claymore, and Battle Axe employ sturdy steel blades on cross-guarded hilts or long hafts. Armor relies on thick fur and leather, ranging from full fur suits to the heavy Nordic Bearskin Cuirass.

title: Dwemer equipment
topic_desc: Dwemer equipment encompasses the surviving arms and armor of the ancient Deep Elves, forged from their distinctive brass-colored Dwemer metal. The alloy's secret is lost, making existing pieces irreplaceable relics scavenged from ruins. The family includes heavy two-handed weapons such as the broad-bladed Dwarven Claymore, the curved Dwarven Battle Axe, the socketed Dwarven Halberd, and the stout Dwarven Warhammer, alongside one-handed variants like the flanged Dwarven Mace and Dwarven Shortsword. Distinctive ranged options include the sturdy mechanical Dwarven Crossbow and the unusual Dwarven Dart, featuring a perforated spherical head. Defensive pieces like the Dwemer Battle Shield and Dwemer Boots complete the assemblage, all exhibiting the same squared, angular construction. Prized by warriors and merchants for its durability, the equipment is heavy and requires considerable strength.
topic_desc_basic: Dwemer equipment consists of arms and armor forged by the ancient Deep Elves from a distinctive, durable brass-colored metal. The secret of working this alloy is lost, so existing pieces are scavenged from ruins. The heavy, angular designs include weapons like the Dwarven Claymore, Dwarven Battle Axe, and Dwarven Crossbow, alongside armor such as Dwemer Boots. Valued for resilience, the gear demands great strength.

title: Glass equipment
topic_desc: Glass equipment is a prestigious family of light armaments and protective gear renowned for its exceptional balance of agility and defense. Constructed from rare, faintly translucent green glass forged with dark leather and angular bronze hinges, the crystalline material yields sharply tapered blades and articulated plating. This equipment is favored by Dunmer and High Elf warriors who value mobility. Representative pieces include the sharply pointed Glass Arrow, the two-handed Glass Claymore, the tapered Glass Dagger, the Glass Halberd, and the polished Glass Cuirass with its matching pauldrons, greaves, and boots.
topic_desc_basic: Glass equipment comprises light armor and weapons forged from translucent green glass, dark leather, and bronze fittings. Valued for combining agility with strong protection, the crystalline construction yields sharply tapered blades and angular plating. Representative examples include the Glass Dagger, Glass Claymore, Glass Cuirass, and Glass Boots.

title: Ebony equipment
topic_desc: Ebony equipment comprises arms and armor forged from a dense, dark, lustrous volcanic glass prized across Tamriel. Dunmer tradition holds that ebony is the crystallized blood of the gods, lending it profound cultural weight. Armorers work the material into heavy, sculpted plate armor featuring fluted surfaces, articulated joint guards, and full-faced helms, as exemplified by the Ebony Cuirass and Ebony Closed Helm. Weaponsmiths produce heavy, broad-bladed implements such as the Ebony Broadsword and Ebony Longsword, alongside blunt instruments like the Ebony Mace and ranged projectiles including the Ebony Arrow and Ebony Dart. A Carved Ebony Dart represents a finely crafted variant of such throwing weapons. The rarity and difficulty of working ebony confines its use to elite warriors and wealthy nobles.
topic_desc_basic: Ebony equipment is forged from a heavy, dark volcanic glass considered sacred by the Dunmer. The rare material is crafted into fine plate armor and powerful weapons, including broadswords, maces, and arrows. Its expense restricts such arms and armor to elite warriors and nobles.

title: Daedric equipment
topic_desc: Daedric equipment is among the rarest and most formidable material families known on Nirn, forged by binding Daedric essence into ebony using a Daedra heart. The process demands a master blacksmith and enchanter; folk claims regarding lunar conditions are likely myth. The resulting dark metal features glowing red veins and jagged, angular protrusions, an aesthetic some attribute to the Daedra's inability to truly create, instead exaggerating familiar Tamrielic shapes with otherworldly, corrupted forms. Due to its extraordinary rarity and value, Daedric arms and armor are typically restricted to the upper echelons of Great House nobility, passed down through generations, and reserved for the most powerful enchantments. The Dunmer also craft distinctive Daedric helms venerating sacred figures, such as the Faces of Inspiration, Terror, and God. Representative examples include the heavy, segmented Daedric Cuirass, the sweeping Daedric Battle Axe, the red-veined Daedric Claymore, and barbed Daedric Arrows.
topic_desc_basic: Daedric equipment is a rare and formidable family of arms and armor forged by binding Daedric essence into ebony with a Daedra heart. Characterized by dark metal with glowing red veins and jagged, angular shapes, these items are extraordinarily valuable and typically owned only by wealthy nobles. Examples include the Daedric Cuirass, Claymore, and Battle Axe.

title: Adamantium armor
topic_desc: Adamantium armor is a heavy armor family forged from adamantium, a rare and exceptionally resilient silvery metal. The constituent pieces feature polished surfaces, segmented horizontal plates, articulated joints, and reinforced flanges, balancing robust protection with mobility. The full panoply encompasses a cuirass with smooth rounded contours, greaves with overlapping plates and fluted ridges, a rounded helm with a narrow face guard, pauldrons covering the shoulders, and bracers guarding the forearms. Due to the metal's scarcity and the skill required to work it, adamantium armor is highly prized by elite warriors and commands a premium from merchants. Master smiths occasionally accept commissions for custom-fitted pieces, a lengthy process reflecting the material's demands.
topic_desc_basic: Adamantium armor is a heavy armor family forged from rare, resilient silvery metal. Highly valued by warriors and merchants, the polished plate features articulated joints and reinforced flanges for robust protection. The set includes a cuirass, greaves, helm, pauldrons, and bracers. Master smiths sometimes accept commissions for custom pieces.

title: Indoril armor
topic_desc: Indoril armor is the ornate golden-bronze plate worn by the Ordinators of the Tribunal Temple. Constructed from layered chitin plates and segmented bronze with sweeping organic curves, the suit features dark indigo leather trim, flared cuffs, and tall flared collars. The tall elliptical shield bears ornate scrolling copper fittings. The distinctive helmet, cuirass, pauldrons, gauntlets, and boots together signify the Ordinators' sacred authority. Enchanted variants include the Spirit of Indoril and Succour of Indoril shields. Wearing the helmet or cuirass outside official duties provokes lethal wrath from the Ordinators.
topic_desc_basic: Indoril armor is the ornate golden-bronze plate worn by the Ordinators of the Tribunal Temple. Constructed from layered chitin and segmented bronze with dark leather trim, the distinctive suit includes a helmet, cuirass, pauldrons, gauntlets, boots, and an elliptical shield. Wearing the helmet or cuirass without authorization provokes lethal retaliation from the Ordinators.

title: Dark Brotherhood armor
topic_desc: Dark Brotherhood armor is a matched set of black leather armor fashioned for the assassins of the Dark Brotherhood. Each piece is constructed from close-fitting dark leather with reinforced panels, segmented plates, and angular contours, balancing protection with silent movement. The cuirass features subtle reinforcement; the greaves use segmented plates for quiet articulation; the boots bear reinforced soles and dark stitching for noiseless tread. The helm carries a narrow face guard with pointed cheek protectors, while the gauntlets cover reinforced knuckle plates secured by forearm buckles, and the pauldrons present layered, ridged shoulders. The uniform's stark hue and sleek profile reflect the Brotherhood's culture of secrecy and murder. No piece bears intrinsic enchantment; the set's value lies in craftsmanship and the dread its appearance evokes.
topic_desc_basic: Dark Brotherhood armor is a matched set of sleek black leather armor worn by the assassins of the Dark Brotherhood. Constructed from close-fitting dark leather with reinforced panels and segmented plates, the full set includes cuirass, greaves, boots, helm, gauntlets, and pauldrons. Each piece is crafted for stealth and silent movement, reflecting the Brotherhood's murderous trade.

title: Royal Guard armor
topic_desc: Royal Guard armor is the distinctive heavy plate worn by the elite soldiers safeguarding King Helsetth Hlaalu and the royal seat in Mournhold. Crafted from polished dark metal and lavishly accented with gilded trim, each piece projects martial authority and royal prestige. The full harness comprises a crested helm with a narrow face guard, a cuirass bearing an ornate royal insignia across the chest, segmented pauldrons displaying the Royal Guard crest, reinforced greaves fitted with knee plates, and flared gauntlets lined with dark leather. Though undeniably ceremonial in its opulence, the armor provides substantial battlefield protection, reflecting the Guard's dual role as both palace sentinels and the personal sword of the Dunmer monarchy.
topic_desc_basic: Royal Guard armor is the ornate dark plate worn by the elite soldiers protecting Mournhold's monarchy. Featuring gilded trim and royal insignia, the harness includes a crested helm, an insignia-marked cuirass, segmented pauldrons, reinforced greaves, and flared gauntlets. It serves as both functional heavy protection and a symbol of royal authority.

title: Nordic mail
topic_desc: Nordic mail is a traditional heavy armor family forged by the Nord smiths of Solstheim, combining riveted steel rings with supplementary iron and steel plates. The cuirass and greaves consist of interlocking dark mesh, while pauldrons cap the shoulders with rounded plates over dark leather. The helmet features a narrow nasal guard and chainmail aventail, and the gauntlets employ articulated finger plates beneath flared, mail-covered cuffs. Thick leather boots reinforced with rings and broad iron shin plates complete the panoply. This robust construction reflects the harsh northern climate and the martial heritage of the Skaal and island Nords, offering comprehensive protection against the severe cold and formidable predators of the region.
topic_desc_basic: Nordic mail is a heavy armor style crafted by the Nords of Solstheim from riveted steel rings and reinforcing iron plates. The family includes a cuirass, greaves, helmet with nasal guard and aventail, pauldrons, gauntlets, shield, and reinforced leather boots. It provides sturdy protection suited to the harsh northern environment.

title: Nordic fur armor
topic_desc: Nordic fur armor is a practical cold-weather equipment family crafted from thick, pale animal fur stitched over flexible leather frameworks and reinforced with iron where rigid support is needed. The cuirass layers brown fur panels over leather, while greaves and bracers employ rigid or strip leather bases lined with shaggy interior fur. The distinctive helm stretches stitched fur over a rounded iron frame with ear flaps, and calf-high boots feature laced fronts and deep interior cuffs. This construction prioritizes insulation against Skyrim's bitter northern climate over heavy battlefield protection. The complete set includes cuirass, helm, greaves, boots, bracers, gauntlets, and pauldrons.
topic_desc_basic: Nordic fur armor is a practical cold-weather family built from thick, pale fur stitched over flexible leather, with iron reinforcing the helm frame. Designed to insulate against Skyrim's bitter cold rather than withstand heavy combat, the set includes cuirass, helm, greaves, boots, bracers, gauntlets, and pauldrons.

title: Bear armor
topic_desc: Bear armor is a family of rugged hide equipment crafted from shaggy brown bear pelts stretched over shaped leather frames. The coarse fur remains attached across the outer surface, and pieces feature crude stitching, reinforced leather panels, and heavy leather soles. The distinctive helmet incorporates the beast's hollowed skull and lowered ears over a leather cap. This construction yields substantial protection against the harsh northern cold, making it customary among Nord warriors and hunters in Skyrim and Solstheim. Representative pieces include the Bear Cuirass, Bear Greaves, Bear Shield, and Bear Helmet. Specialized variants include the Nordic Bearskin Cuirass, the enchantment-bearing Helm of Bear Scent, and the Snow Bear Boots.
topic_desc_basic: Bear armor is a heavy hide set favored by Nordic warriors, crafted from thick, shaggy brown bear pelts stretched over reinforced leather frames. The distinctive helmet incorporates the beast's hollowed skull. The family includes standard slots like the cuirass, greaves, and boots, alongside cultural variants such as the Nordic Bearskin Cuirass.

title: Wolf armor
topic_desc: Wolf armor is a barbarian panoply fashioned from grey wolf pelts and tanned hide, worn by the warriors of Solstheim. Each piece stretches rough fur over a shaped leather frame, fastened with bone toggles and leather straps. The helmet is carved to resemble a wolf's head, complete with pointed ears, elongated snout, and protective face guard. Gauntlets and pauldrons reinforce the limbs with dark fur and hardened leather finger guards. The full complement includes cuirass, greaves, boots with claw details, paired gauntlets and pauldrons, and a shield. Notable enchanted examples include the Helm of the Wolf's Heart, the Paws of the Wolf-Runner, and Snow Wolf Boots. The craft reflects Nordic reverence for the wolf as both prey and spirit guardian.
topic_desc_basic: Wolf armor is a rugged hide-and-pelt panoply associated with the Nordic warriors of Solstheim. Crafted from grey wolf pelts stretched over leather frames and fastened with bone toggles, it includes cuirass, greaves, boots, gauntlets, pauldrons, helmet, and shield. The distinctive wolf-head helmet and fur-lined construction reflect the barbarian traditions of the island's northern folk.

title: Stalhrim weapons
topic_desc: Stalhrim weapons are arms carved from stalhrim, a rare pale blue crystalline substance found in Solstheim's ancient Nordic tombs. The frost-edged material requires specialized knowledge to work, and only a few Skaal smiths possess the craft to shape it. Each weapon exhibits a translucent, ice-like quality, from the jagged flanges of the mace to the broad curved blade of the war axe. The dagger and longsword feature tapered double-edged profiles. Because raw stalhrim is scarce and culturally sensitive, these weapons are highly prized. Enchanted variants, such as the Stalhrim Longsword of Flame, bear etched flame patterns, pairing frost-rimed steel with destructive magic.
topic_desc_basic: Stalhrim weapons are arms carved from a rare pale blue crystalline substance found in Solstheim's Nordic tombs. Exhibiting a translucent, ice-like quality, they include daggers, longswords, maces, and war axes. Their creation requires specialized craft, and the scarcity of raw stalhrim makes them highly prized.

title: Telvanni equipment
topic_desc: Telvanni equipment comprises distinctive armor and shields crafted for House Telvanni's retainers and guards. Constructed from shaped chitin, bonemold, and creature shells reinforced with dark resin, these pieces reflect the House's isolationist wizard-lord culture and its mastery of Morrowind's indigenous materials. Representative items include the Cephalopod Helm, a domed helmet with textured tentacles framing the face; the Dust Adept Helm, a tall segmented brown helm with a narrow visor and shoulder guards; the Mole Crab Helm, a close-fitting shell retaining its natural reddish-brown ridged texture; and the Guard Shield, a tall bonemold tower shield of layered chitin plates reinforced along the central spine. Such equipment is customary for Telvanni settlements, where wizard retainers require functional protection suited to the harsh eastern coastal environment.
topic_desc_basic: House Telvanni equips its guards and retainers with distinctive armor fashioned from chitin, bonemold, and creature shells. Representative pieces include the Cephalopod Helm with its tentacle-framed face opening, the tall segmented Dust Adept Helm, the ridged Mole Crab Helm, and the layered chitin Guard Shield. These items reflect the House's reliance on indigenous materials and its isolationist wizard-lord culture.

title: Redoran equipment
topic_desc: Redoran equipment is the martial armament tradition of Great House Redoran, the staunchest defender of Dunmer heritage and Temple orthodoxy. Constructed primarily from bonemold and chitin, these arms reflect both Ashland resourcefulness and the noble house's martial pride. Redoran shields are tall, rectangular bonemold tower shields painted in deep crimson and bearing the house heraldic insect emblem, as seen in the Redoran Banner Shield and Redoran Guard Shield. Helmets denote rank and duty: the chitin Redoran Watchman's Helm features dark red lacquered shell plates with a reinforced visor for patrol, while the bonemold Redoran Master Helm and Redoran Founder's Helm display prominent face guards and ridged crests signifying high authority. This equipment is customary for Redoran retainers and house honor guards across their western Vvardenfell holdings.
topic_desc_basic: House Redoran arms its warriors and retainers with distinctive bonemold and chitin equipment. Their tall, crimson-painted bonemold tower shields bear the house heraldic insect emblem. Helmets indicate rank, ranging from the dark red lacquered chitin Watchman's Helm to the crested bonemold Founder's Helm and Master Helm. This armament reflects Redoran's martial traditions and Dunmer cultural pride.

title: Hlaalu equipment
topic_desc: Hlaalu equipment encompasses the arms, armor, and personal adornment produced for or by House Hlaalu, reflecting the Great House's mercantile character and cosmopolitan tastes. Hlaalu Guard Shields exemplify their martial production: tall bonemold tower shields painted in Hlaalu colors, featuring a prominent central ridge and rounded top. These shields equip the House's retainers and guards, balancing traditional Dunmer bonemold craftsmanship with the House's distinctive heraldry. In personal ornamentation, Hlaalu nobles favor costly jewelry signaling wealth and influence, such as polished gold circular amulets centered with small green gemstones, as exemplified by Methas Hlaalu's Amulet. Hlaalu equipment thus ranges from practical guard armaments to the luxurious accessories worn by councilors and merchants.
topic_desc_basic: House Hlaalu equips its guards with distinctive bonemold tower shields painted in Hlaalu colors, featuring a rounded top and prominent central ridge. Hlaalu nobles and merchants favor costly personal adornments, including polished gold amulets set with green gemstones.

title: Long blades
topic_desc: Long blades encompass the most widely used edged weapons across Morrowind and the wider Empire, spanning both one-handed and two-handed forms. Western smiths produce broadswords, sabers, longswords, and claymores—straight-bladed arms suited to Imperial legionaries and noble retainers alike. Akaviri-style katanas and dai-katanas, with their curved single edges, are prized by Dunmer gentry and foreign collectors. Two-handed claymores and dai-katanas trade speed for reach and power, while one-handed types remain versatile sidearms. Masterwork examples range from Dwarven claymores of recovered Dwemer metal to Daedric weapons forged from blackened ebony under arcane binding, their blades traced with crimson veins. Glass longswords and claymores, light and deadly, reflect High Elf metallurgy, while adamantium and ebony pieces represent the pinnacle of mainland craft.
topic_desc_basic: Long blades are the most common edged weapons in Morrowind, including both one-handed and two-handed forms. Western types—broadswords, sabers, longswords, and claymores—differ in form from Akaviri-style katanas and dai-katanas. Two-handed claymores and dai-katanas are heavier and slower but offer greater reach. They are forged in materials ranging from steel to glass, ebony, and Daedric metal.

title: Short blades
topic_desc: Short blades are a family of light, one-handed weapons encompassing daggers, tantos, shortswords, and wakizashis. Daggers and shortswords are Western Imperial designs, while the tanto and wakizashi reflect Akaviri styling. Light and fast, they excel against lightly armored foes, though a skilled user can outlast heavily armored opponents. Daggers, tantos, and shortswords serve as thrusting weapons, whereas the wakizashi chops and slashes. General effectiveness increases from the dagger through the tanto and shortsword to the wakizashi. Materials range from common iron and regional chitin—such as the laminated Chitin Dagger and leather-wrapped Chitin Shortsword—to Dwarven, glass, ebony, and adamantium. Daedric examples, including the jagged Daedric Dagger and curved Daedric Wakizashi, feature dark ebony with crimson edges and sweeping ornamentation.
topic_desc_basic: Short blades are light, one-handed weapons including daggers, tantos, shortswords, and wakizashis. Imperial daggers and shortswords are thrusting weapons, while Akaviri-styled tantos thrust and wakizashis chop and slash. They are fast and effective against light armor, crafted from materials ranging from common iron and chitin to rare ebony and Daedric.

title: Axes
topic_desc: Axes across Morrowind take two principal forms: the one-handed war axe and the two-handed battle axe. War axes permit a shield in the off-hand, while battle axes deliver greater force with both hands on a long reinforced haft. Common iron examples are ubiquitous, and chitin war axes reflect native Ashlander craft, binding shaped chitin blades to segmented hafts with visible joint bindings. Dwarven axes of brass-colored Dwemer metal feature broad curved blades on thick hafts, recovered from ruins across the island. Ebony and glass war axes represent elite Dunmer smithing traditions, while Daedric axes of blackened obsidian-like metal bear jagged ornamentation and sweeping angular blades. Nordic Huntsman axes serve Solstheim woodsmen, the ancient Nordic pick axe endures as a weathered iron tool, and the adamantium axe is a rare silvery two-handed specimen.
topic_desc_basic: Axes across Morrowind come in two principal forms: the one-handed war axe, suited to shield use, and the two-handed battle axe, favored for maximum striking force. Common iron and chitin examples serve soldiers and hunters, while Dwemer, ebony, glass, and Daedric specimens represent progressively rarer and more formidable smithing traditions.

title: Blunt weapons
topic_desc: Clubs and staves are inexpensive, easily mastered arms commonly carried by travelers and militias. Maces and morningstars serve as one-handed professional arms, while the warhammer is a slow, heavy two-handed implement. Construction varies widely by material and culture: laminated insect chitin forms rough knobby clubs with wrapped grips in Morrowind, while Dwemer smiths forged distinct maces from their lost metal. Dreugh clubs and staves are shaped from the carapaces of the aquatic beasts. High-end examples include polished adamantium maces with heavy flanged heads, ebony maces and staves, and glass staves. The rarest and most devastating are Daedric pieces—ebon clubs with thick textured heads, maces with red-veined curved flanges, and tall staves capped with heavy curved prongs of dark red Daedric metal.
topic_desc_basic: Blunt weapons include clubs, staves, maces, morningstars, and warhammers. Clubs and staves are cheap, easily mastered arms favored by travelers and militias. Maces and morningstars are one-handed professional weapons, while warhammers are heavy two-handed arms. They are crafted from diverse materials ranging from chitin and dreugh shell to dwarven metal, ebony, and rare Daedric iron.

title: Spears
topic_desc: Spears are two-handed thrusting polearms prized for their exceptional reach against heavily armored or encumbered opponents. The family divides into two principal styles: the spear and the more formidable halberd. Common among militias and light irregulars, the spear is also refined into a martial art by the Bosmer, while Ashlanders favor elegant variants featuring a shaft-foot spike. Construction spans from segmented chitin and sturdy wooden hafts to heavy socketed blades on stout shafts. Representative examples include the chitin spear, the golden Dwarven spear with its leaf-shaped blade, the barbed Daedric spear, and the bronze Dwarven halberd. Though devastating in massed formations, halberds require considerable skill and prove unwieldy in close quarters.
topic_desc_basic: Spears are two-handed thrusting weapons offering the longest melee reach. The family includes standard spears and the more powerful halberds. Favored by militias, Bosmer martial artists, and Ashlanders—who often add a foot spike—spears range from simple chitin and iron to ornate Dwarven and Daedric designs. Halberds are devastating against armored foes but prove unwieldy in close quarters.

title: Marksman weapons
topic_desc: Marksman weapons encompass bows, crossbows, and hand-hurled projectiles, offering ranged attack capability at the cost of reduced damage compared to melee arms. Bows and crossbows are two-handed and more effective, firing arrows and bolts respectively, while throwing stars and darts permit swift one-handed assaults. Morrowind's archers commonly employ chitin and bonemold constructions; chitin short bows and throwing stars are lightweight and traditional, whereas bonemold long bows and bolts use resin-reinforced bone composite for sturdier arms and shafts. Corkbulb root furnishes readily available arrow and bolt shafts. Rarer materials include dense ebony, yielding finely carved darts, and Daedric forging, producing exceptionally lethal arrows and darts. Auriel's Bow, an ebony longbow of legendary provenance, represents the pinnacle of such craft.
topic_desc_basic: Marksman weapons are ranged arms divided into two-handed bows and crossbows, which fire arrows and bolts, and one-handed thrown weapons like darts and throwing stars. Bows and crossbows deal greater damage, while thrown weapons allow faster strikes. Common regional materials include chitin, bonemold, and corkbulb, with rare ebony and Daedric variants prized by elite warriors.

title: Shields
topic_desc: Shields in Morrowind come in two basic styles: the standard shield and the much larger, heavier tower shield. They are crafted from a wide range of materials reflecting local cultures and resources. Ashland Dunmer favor lightweight chitin shields formed from laminated insect segments bound by resin, while settled House Dunmer employ bonemold—shaped bone resin arranged in overlapping layers or prominent ridges. Nordic warriors use round wooden shields reinforced with iron and covered in hide, such as the Bear Shield. Rarer specimens include the Dreugh Shield, Dwemer Battle Shield, and the formidable Daedric Shield and Daedric Tower Shield. Ancient steel tower shields survive from earlier eras, and legendary artifacts like Auriel's Shield, an ornate ebony piece bearing a sunburst emblem, are highly prized. A warrior's effectiveness with a shield depends on their training in the appropriate armored fighting style.
topic_desc_basic: Shields in Morrowind come in two styles: the standard shield and the larger, heavier tower shield. They are crafted from various materials, from lightweight chitin and shaped bonemold resin to iron-reinforced wood, steel, and rare metals like Dwemer brass and Daedric ebony. A warrior's effectiveness with a shield depends on their training in the appropriate armored fighting style.

title: Robes
topic_desc: Robes are full-length, often hooded garments worn across Morrowind by mages, priests, scholars, and nobles. They range from coarse, thick wool weaves like the Common Robe to luxurious, finely tailored constructions of rich fabric, as seen in the Expensive, Exquisite, and Extravagant variants. Specialized enchanted robes provide elemental protection, including the Flameguard, Flameeater, Flamemirror, Frosteater, and Frostguard robes, the latter featuring deep blue velvet with silver clasps and a fur-trimmed high collar. The Glenmoril Witch Robe represents a plain, coarse black variant associated with the covens of Solstheim.
topic_desc_basic: Robes are full-length garments favored by mages, priests, and nobles throughout Morrowind. They are crafted in a wide range of materials, from simple coarse wool to luxurious tailored fabrics, and frequently serve as a practical base for protective enchantments against elemental hazards.

title: Morrowind clothing
topic_desc: Morrowind clothing encompasses the diverse garments worn across the province, ranging from humble common apparel to ornate extravagent dress. Common items include plain metal amulets, simple belts, unadorned rings, and basic robes, typically crafted from inexpensive materials for everyday utility. Finer construction employs supple leather and elaborate fabric, yielding tailored brocade shirts with ornate stitching along the collared neckline, or broad gold rings bearing intricate filigree patterns. Distinct cultural and faction identifiers are woven into such apparel; the Morag Tong marks its black leather gloves with a stitched insignia, while the Aundae bloodline displays its engraved sigil upon an extravagant gold band. These garments serve both practical and social functions, signaling rank, affiliation, and regional identity throughout Dunmer society.
topic_desc_basic: Clothing in Morrowind ranges from practical common garments like simple belts, plain metal amulets, and unadorned rings to elaborate attire. Finer pieces feature tailored brocade shirts with ornate stitching and gold rings with intricate filigree. Specific apparel also signals faction identity, such as the Morag Tong's stitched insignia on black leather gloves or the Aundae bloodline's engraved sigil on an extravagant gold ring.

title: Alchemy apparatus
topic_desc: Alchemy apparatus comprises four specialized tools essential for potion preparation: the mortar and pestle for grinding and mixing, the alembic for purifying harmful properties, the calcinator for intensifying all effects through heat, and the retort for distilling beneficial virtues. Crafted from stone, glass, brass, and bronze, these instruments range from plain apprentice wares—such as simple stone mortars and shallow brass calcinators on stubby legs—to grandmaster pieces featuring fine glass alembics with domed lids and wide bronze calcinators on tripods. Healers, apothecaries, and mages across Morrowind rely on these devices, with higher-quality construction yielding more potent and refined results.
topic_desc_basic: Alchemy apparatus includes four tools needed to brew potions: a mortar and pestle for grinding, an alembic to reduce harmful effects, a calcinator to intensify all properties, and a retort to strengthen beneficial effects. These instruments are crafted from stone, glass, brass, and bronze, ranging from simple apprentice wares to finely made grandmaster pieces.

title: Lockpicks
topic_desc: Lockpicks are slender metal implements designed to open locked doors and containers without a key. Legitimate locksmiths employ them when owners have misplaced their keys, while thieves and other covert operators use them for less honorable purposes. The craft ranges from simple unadorned shafts with gently curved tapered tips, through journeyman's tools with wrapped grips and bent working ends, to finely forged master's picks with polished hooked tips. The secret master's lockpick represents the pinnacle of the form: a dark-hued, exquisitely tapered instrument with a smooth unadorned grip. Construction quality directly governs durability and effectiveness against complex mechanisms.
topic_desc_basic: Lockpicks are slender metal tools used to open locked doors and containers without keys. Locksmiths employ them for legitimate purposes, while thieves favor them for covert entry. They range from simple apprentice's picks to finely crafted master's and secret master's implements, with construction quality determining effectiveness against increasingly complex locks.

title: Probes
topic_desc: Probes are specialized tools used to detect and disarm traps on doors and containers. While locksmiths employ them for legitimate mechanism work, thieves and agents more frequently rely on them for illicit infiltration. Constructed from metals such as steel or brass, they range from crude bent shafts to intricate folding tines and ornate mechanical grooves. Representative examples include the simple Bent Probe, the folding Journeyman's Probe, the polished Master's Probe with its ribbed brass grip, and the exceptional Grandmaster's and Secret Master's Probes, which feature fine hooked tips for delicate manipulation.
topic_desc_basic: Probes are slender metal tools used to detect and disarm traps on doors and containers. While locksmiths have legitimate uses for them, thieves and agents more commonly employ these instruments. They range from crude bent shafts to polished, intricately grooved designs like the Master's and Grandmaster's Probes.

title: Armorer's hammers
topic_desc: Armorer's hammers are specialized steel-headed tools used to repair damaged metal armor and bladed weapons. Crafted in graded qualities to suit varying skill levels, they range from lightweight apprentice models with narrow peen heads and plain wooden handles to heavy master and grandmaster variants featuring broad faces and reinforced hardwood shafts for demanding metalwork. Journeyman hammers occupy the middle tier, sized for moderate repairs. Essential for maintaining battlefield readiness, these implements are standard kit for professional armorers, soldiers, and traveling merchants who must keep their wares functional.
topic_desc_basic: Armorer's hammers are essential steel-headed tools used to repair dented armor and chipped blades. They come in several grades of quality and durability, from lightweight apprentice tools to heavy grandmaster implements, allowing warriors and traders to maintain their equipment in the field.

title: Amulet of Unity
topic_desc: The Amulet of Unity is a First Era artifact once held by a mainland sorcerer. It is reputed to possess significant magical properties, though its precise capabilities remain a matter of esoteric speculation rather than common knowledge. The amulet is known to be kept under heavy guard, and its retrieval demands considerable magical preparation. Following its recent theft from its owner, the artifact's current whereabouts are tied to the thief's efforts to secure it from its original, well-defended location.
topic_desc_basic: The Amulet of Unity is a First Era magical artifact from the mainland. It is known to be kept under heavy guard by a sorcerer, and its precise capabilities remain a matter of esoteric speculation.

title: The Guarherder's Art
topic_desc: A treatise on guar herding by Ralen Teneran, who argues that Imperial influence has degraded traditional Dunmer practices. Teneran dismisses frightening guar with screams or command spells as ineffective, advocating conditioned feeding instead: gradual befriendment, auditory association with a call or whistle, or fenced containment for the impatient. He details safe diets, warning that saltrice, fungi, and kreshweed are poisonous, while bittergreen, wickwheat, and trama root provide necessary nutrition. Marshmerrow and comberries are recommended as rare loyalty rewards. The text outlines training for caravan labor, riding, and domestic tasks, differentiating between roped and command-driven pack guar. It also catalogs the uses of guar hides, bones, and offal, with noted disdain for Ashlander consumption of innards.
topic_desc_basic: Ralen Teneran's treatise on traditional Dunmer guar herding, which critiques Imperial-influenced methods and advocates conditioned feeding and dietary care over coercion.

title: Mole Crab
topic_desc: Mole crabs are crustaceans bred for practical yield. A large shell covers the cephalothorax and is shaped for helms, greaves, and pauldrons, while a smaller shell fits bracers, boots, and cups; a large shell from a young crab can substitute for the small variety. Remaining chitin from legs, mandibles, pincers, and damaged shells is ground into powder and mixed with resin to produce bonemold. Their durable, lightweight shells form the traditional light armor of Telvanni guards. Their meat substitutes for mudcrab meat in alchemy. Unfertilized eggs are gathered from breeding pits for cooking and alchemical use; kept cold and wet, they remain viable for later fertilization to replenish stock.
topic_desc_basic: Mole crabs are hardy crustaceans bred for useful shells, meat, and eggs. Their light shells are used in traditional Telvanni armor.

title: Hlaalu Company Scrip
topic_desc: Hlaalu Company scrip consists of clay tokens issued as wages in place of Imperial gold septims. Each token carries a stated value of one septim but can be spent only at Hlaalu-owned establishments, principally the company store tied to a given mine. The arrangement lets House Hlaalu pay workers without dispersing hard currency while capturing their spending internally. The chief risk to laborers is that saved scrip becomes worthless when a mine and its company store close, leaving holders with tokens no longer redeemable anywhere. The practice is a recognized feature of Hlaalu-controlled mining operations, where the gap between nominal value and practical liquidity falls squarely on the worker.
topic_desc_basic: Hlaalu Company scrip is a clay token currency issued by the Hlaalu Council Company in place of gold septims. Each piece holds a nominal value of one septim but is accepted only at Hlaalu-owned establishments on the mainland, not on Vvardenfell. The tokens are chiefly used to pay miners and new retainers at company stores near Hlaalu mines.

title: Almalexia's faithful
topic_desc: Almalexia's faithful are members of an Indoril guard post on a road in Morrowind, described by a Merihayan vampire as followers of Almalexia who murdered the vampire's clan brethren. The guard post is staffed by two of Almalexia's faithful and is located near Indoril territory. The term appears in the context of the vampire's account of the slaughter of the Merihayan clan and the ongoing presence of Almalexia's followers at a nearby outpost.
topic_desc_basic: Almalexia's faithful are followers of the Tribunal god Almalexia who staff an Indoril guard post on a road in Morrowind, near House Indoril territory.

title: Alandro Sul
topic_desc: Alandro Sul served as Lord Nerevar's shield-companion and fought alongside the Hortator at the Battle of Red Mountain. Following Nerevar's death, Sul bore his body from the mountain on his tower-shield, a relic still venerated in Temple shrines. He then brought word of Nerevar's death and Dagoth Ur's betrayal to the Tribunal. However, Ashlander tradition holds that Sul subsequently joined their ancestors and revealed a different account of events at Red Mountain, one that implicated the Tribunal in Nerevar's demise. This testimony became the foundation of Ashlander rejection of the Tribunal's divinity and the root of the Dissident Priest schism. Temple doctrine consequently regards Sul's Ashlander narrative as heretical lies. Sul's spirit has not spoken to the Ashlanders in living memory, and accounts of his testimony remain deeply contested between Temple orthodoxy and Ashlander tradition.
topic_desc_basic: Alandro Sul was Lord Nerevar's shield-companion at the Battle of Red Mountain. Temple tradition honors him for bearing Nerevar's body away on his tower-shield and reporting Dagoth Ur's betrayal to the Tribunal. Ashlander tradition, however, credits him with revealing that the Tribunal murdered Nerevar, a claim the Temple condemns as heresy.

title: Armistice
topic_desc: The Armistice is the treaty that joined Morrowind to the Empire under Tiber Septim, granting the Tribunal Temple autonomy and allowing Morrowind to retain its native laws and governance in exchange for imperial sovereignty.
topic_desc_basic: The Armistice is the treaty that joined Morrowind to the Empire under Tiber Septim. It allows Morrowind to retain its native laws, Great House governance, and Tribunal Temple autonomy in exchange for imperial sovereignty.

title: Daedric ruins
topic_desc: Daedric ruins are the remnant structures of Daedric worship scattered across the landscape. Within the Roth Roryn region, two major Daedric ruins stand. Veranzaris is dedicated to Sheogorath, and Ossurnashalit is dedicated to Molag Bal. These sites serve as enduring monuments to the Daedric Princes they venerate.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Daedric ruins is.

title: origin of vampirism
topic_desc: The origin of vampirism is a matter of disputed theological claim rather than settled doctrine. Among Orc vampire bloodlines in Morrowind, particularly the Orlukh, some assert that their condition originates with the Daedric Prince Namira, whose spheres of darkness and decay are said to explain the vampire's aversion to sunlight, hunger for mortal blood, and exemption from natural aging. These adherents reject alternative attributions to Molag Bal, Vaermina, or Clavicus Vile, dismissing them as belittling or as Temple propaganda. Other Orc vampires, however, profess indifference to the question of origin, maintaining that Malacath alone tests their worth in life and undeath alike. The Temple's own teachings, which these vampires deride, attribute vampirism to Molag Bal. No consensus exists among the undead themselves, and the disagreement reflects broader tensions between rival bloodlines and their respective Daedric allegiances.
topic_desc_basic: The origin of vampirism is disputed. The Tribunal Temple attributes the condition to Molag Bal, while some Orc vampire bloodlines claim Namira as their progenitor. Other Orc vampires disregard the question entirely, caring only that Malacath tests their worth.

title: Alfiq
topic_desc: The Alfiq are the smallest of the Khajiit forms, resembling the housecats of Cyrodiil. Quick, cunning, and capable of navigating tight spaces, they are often underestimated. Despite their inability to speak the common tongue—understanding it while only vocalizing the Khajiiti language, Ta'agra—they are known as tricksters, mages, and skilled rapier duelists. They possess beautiful singing voices and are sometimes seen wearing hats and vests. Alfiq are uncommon in Morrowind, where most Khajiit are Suthay-raht, though some serve at the Ebon Tower mission.
topic_desc_basic: The Alfiq are the smallest form of Khajiit, looking much like the housecats of Cyrodiil. Though they cannot speak the common tongue, they understand it perfectly while speaking only Ta'agra. They are clever, quick, and known for their magical skill.

title: Aanthirin
topic_desc: Aanthirin is a lush, orange-green region in the Mournhold District of Morrowind, centered around the Thirr River Valley. It contains Lake Andaram, Morrowind's largest lake, and is divided by the Thirr River as it flows to the Inner Sea. Historically significant as the path crossed by Veloth, the land was later shattered by the creation of the Inner Sea, which linked the river to the Sea of Ghosts. Today, Aanthirin's status as Morrowind's central crossroad makes it the focus of a bitter territorial and trade dispute between the dominant House Indoril and the ascendant House Hlaalu. Imperial trade interests and Tribunal Temple authority further complicate the region's divided loyalties. The Temple stronghold of Almas Thirr spans the Thirr River and regulates most of the province's trade, while Old Ebonheart serves as the main Imperial hub. Despite its gentle river and abundant farms, Aanthirin remains a contested land.
topic_desc_basic: Aanthirin is a lush region in the Mournhold District of Morrowind, divided by the Thirr River as it flows toward the Inner Sea. It contains Lake Andaram and serves as a major crossroad for the province, making it a focal point of trade and territorial disputes between House Indoril and House Hlaalu.

title: Almas Thirr
topic_desc: Almas Thirr is a large Tribunal Temple city and pilgrimage site spanning the Thirr River in the Aanthirin region. Built upon Veloth's Path, the route Saint Veloth is said to have taken through Morrowind, it connects Indoril lands to Hlaalu and holds the only road linking western and eastern Morrowind north of Narsis. The Temple-owned canton derives wealth from tolls on river traffic and the constant flow of pilgrims. Its strategic location places it amid rising tensions between Great House Hlaalu and Great House Indoril. Though the Temple professes neutrality, the Indoril maintain a garrison on the eastern bank, while Hlaalu agents operate within the city. The Majordomo of the Crossing governs Almas Thirr on behalf of the Temple, striving to preserve its independence amid these pressures.
topic_desc_basic: Almas Thirr is a large Tribunal Temple city and pilgrimage site spanning the Thirr River in the Aanthirin region. It sits on the only road connecting western and eastern Morrowind north of Narsis.

title: Akamora
topic_desc: Akamora, also called Draloris, is the largest Indoril settlement in the Mephalan Vales. Built into a mountainside surrounded by waterfalls, its high cliffs and narrow paths provide natural defenses. The city lies near the border between Indoril and Telvanni territory, serving as a vital travel stop to the northern reaches of Morrowind. Despite its size, internal scheming among noble factions prevents any from consolidating power and claiming a befitting council seat. The current lord is Novas Senim, though his rule is contested by factions led by Seras Indaren and Telera Parys. Akamora hosts highly productive egg-mines, numerous noble manors, a Tribunal Temple, and guildhalls for the Fighters Guild, Mages Guild, and Morag Tong. It is reachable by silt strider, Almsivi Intervention, and Mages Guild guide.
topic_desc_basic: Akamora, or Draloris, is a mountain city in the Mephalan Vales and the largest Indoril settlement there. It lies near the Telvanni border and is reachable by silt strider, Almsivi Intervention, or Mages Guild guide. Imperial maps call it Dragon Glade.

title: Gortwog gro-Nagorm
topic_desc: Gortwog gro-Nagorm is the Lord of Orsinium and chieftain of the Minat Orc tribe. He founded the current Orcish nation of Orsinium, providing the Orsimer people a recognized homeland. His establishment of this state represents a pivotal moment in Orcish history, formally realizing their long-sought ambition for a sovereign territory rather than existing solely in dispersed strongholds or imperial servitude.
topic_desc_basic: Gortwog gro-Nagorm is the Lord of Orsinium and chieftain of the Minat Orc tribe. He founded the Orcish nation of Orsinium, giving the Orsimer people a true home.

title: Shinathi
topic_desc: The Shinathi are nomadic Dunmer clans inhabiting the red canyons of the Shipal-Shin highlands. Claiming descent from the Red Khans, they have occupied the region since the early settlement of Resdayn. Unlike the Ashlanders, the Shinathi are devout followers of the Tribunal Temple, and most established camps include Tribunal priests for spiritual guidance. Their pastoral lifestyle revolves around herding sharai hoppers and riding kwoom through the canyons. While they maintain a distinct nomadic identity, many Shinathi integrate into House Hlaalu society as traders, craftspeople, and highly valued mercenaries, scouts, and local guides. Accounts of their livelihood differ: Shinathi themselves emphasize hunting, foraging, and herding, while outside observers claim smuggling and extortion of traveling merchants fund much of their existence. The founders of Shipal-Sharai are rumored to belong to a Shinathi clan. They prefer isolation but share common ground with settled Dunmer through Tribunal worship.
topic_desc_basic: The Shinathi are nomadic Dunmer clans of the Shipal-Shin highlands. Unlike the Ashlanders, they are devout followers of the Tribunal Temple. Many integrate into House Hlaalu society as traders, craftspeople, and valued mercenaries or guides.

title: Boethiah's Spine
topic_desc: Boethiah's Spine is a mountainous region in the Telvannis District of mainland Morrowind, stretching north-to-south through the eastern peninsula. Its treacherous ridges and deep valleys feature rugged rocks twisted into strange shapes by erosion. The south is dominated by deep Lake Boethiah, whose shores host the Telvanni tower-settlements of Alt Bosara and Tel Mothrivra. In the north, the Spine separates into several ridges that cut through the flat plains of Molagreahd. The region borders Sunad Mora to the north, Dagon Urul to the west, Molag Ruhn and the Mephalan Vales to the south and southwest, and the Padomaic Ocean to the east. Though largely rocky and barren, steep cliffs conceal several lushly forested valleys. The region holds Daedric ruins, Dwemer ruins, Velothi towers, and ancestral tombs among its rugged terrain.
topic_desc_basic: Boethiah's Spine is a mountainous region in the Telvannis District of mainland Morrowind, stretching north-to-south through the eastern peninsula. It is named for its treacherous ridges and deep valleys, and is largely rocky and barren.

title: Hierophants
topic_desc: The Niben Hierophants are elite battlemage aristocrats who preside over the complex governmental hierarchy of the Nibenay. Their magocratic system traces its origins to the administrative reforms enacted during the Second Era's Akaviri Potentate, though the modern Heartlands hierarchy is now fully integrated with the Third Empire and its institutions.
