The most powerful among the Hierophants hold the rank of vizier, each administering one of the eight Circuits; these viziers report directly to the Emperor and the Elder Council.
topic_desc_basic: The Niben Hierophants are an elite class of battlemage aristocrats who rule the Nibenay's complicated governmental hierarchy. This magocratic system originated with the Akaviri Potentate's reforms in the Second Era but is now fully integrated with the Third Empire. The most powerful Hierophants serve as viziers, governing the eight Circuits and reporting directly to the Emperor and the Elder Council.

title: Winterhold
topic_desc: Winterhold is the queen city of the North, mistress of the Sea of Ghosts. While the wind and snow blow endless about the ancient arcology walls, its people thrive in warmth and splendor within.
topic_desc_basic: Winterhold is a major city on the northeast coast of Skyrim, capital of the eponymous hold. Called the queen city of the North, it is an ancient arcology whose inhabitants thrive within its walls despite the endless wind and snow. It is home to the College of Winterhold, Skyrim's premier school of magic.

title: Evermore
topic_desc: Evermore is a kingdom and settlement situated in the West Reach of High Rock. Its people claim a legacy extending to Ebonarm as their founder and take pride in being home to exceptionally talented mages. The kingdom presents itself as a peaceful power, seeking stability across High Rock and Tamriel, and declares friendship with Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: Evermore is a kingdom and trading city in the West Reach of eastern High Rock, situated on the Bjoulsae River near the Hammerfell border. Its people claim Ebonarm as their founder, take pride in their talented mages, and seek peace and friendship across Tamriel.

title: skylamp
topic_desc: Skylamps are hovering creatures related to the netch, though smaller and more agile. Their thin hide renders them unsuitable for tanning, leaving passenger and small cargo transport as their primary use. House Redoran domesticates them extensively; garrisons at Ald Iuval and Ald Marak employ skylamps to patrol Lake Coronati and cross its waters. Wild skylamps inhabit regions further north and can become aggressive if diseased or injured. While generally placid, riding one is considered a precarious experience, with some fearing their riders might fall and drown.
topic_desc_basic: Skylamps are hovering creatures related to netches, used to carry passengers and small cargo. House Redoran domesticates them to patrol Lake Coronati. Wild skylamps live further north and can become aggressive if diseased or injured.

title: Shipal-Shin
topic_desc: Shipal-Shin is a region of red cliffs and canyons in the Narsis District of Morrowind, stretching along the borders with Cyrodiil and Black Marsh. Within Morrowind, it borders the Velothi Mountains, Othreleth Woods, and Coronati Basin to the north, the Deshaan Plains to the northeast, and the Salt Marsh and Arnesian Jungle to the east. Its largest settlement is Narsis, the capital of House Hlaalu, which prospers by supplying Imperial settlements in Black Marsh; nearly all goods passing through Stormhold move through Narsis first. The region hosts isolated Hlaalu settlements tilling the red soil, Shinathi tribal camps, numerous sapphire mines, and Imperial garrisons at Septim's Gate Pass and Stormgate Pass. The Purple Road traverses the region, connecting its settlements and ruins.
topic_desc_basic: Shipal-Shin is a region of red canyons in southern Morrowind, forming a natural border with Cyrodiil and Black Marsh. Its largest settlement is Narsis, the capital of House Hlaalu.

title: Bad Daedra
topic_desc: The Tribunal Temple designates four Daedric Princes as Bad Daedra, also called the Rebel Daedra, Dark Daedra, or the Four Corners of the House of Troubles: Molag Bal, Malacath, Sheogorath, and Mehrunes Dagon. Temple doctrine holds that, unlike the Three Good Daedra—Azura, Boethiah, and Mephala, who recognized the Tribunal's divinity and paid homage—the Bad Daedra refused in arrogance and pride to keep faith with the Tribunal. They are regarded as sources of heresy and dark worship, continually tempting the unwary. Temple teaching associates each with specific lesser Daedric servants: the daedroth serves Molag Bal, the ogrim serves Malacath, the scamp, dremora, and clannfear serve Mehrunes Dagon, and the golden saint serves Sheogorath.
topic_desc_basic: The Tribunal Temple calls four Daedric Princes the Bad Daedra or Rebel Daedra: Molag Bal, Malacath, Sheogorath, and Mehrunes Dagon. They are also known as the Four Corners of the House of Troubles. Temple doctrine holds they arrogantly refused to recognize the Tribunal's divinity and continually tempt the unwary into heresy and dark worship.

title: Narsis District
topic_desc: Narsis District is one of the six administrative divisions of the Imperial province of Morrowind, situated in the southwestern hills. It borders both Cyrodiil and Black Marsh. While the Velothi Mountains persist along its Cyrodiilic border, they are less pronounced here than in the Velothis District. The region is dominated by Imperial-friendly Great House Hlaalu. Its key settlement is the city of Narsis, which serves as the Hlaalu capital and hosts the Imperial Proconsul.
topic_desc_basic: Narsis District is one of the six administrative districts of Morrowind, located in the southwestern hills and bordering both Cyrodiil and Black Marsh. It is dominated by House Hlaalu, and its key city is Narsis, the Hlaalu capital and residency of the Imperial Proconsul.

title: Woodhearth
topic_desc: Woodhearth is a major city on the southwestern coast of Valenwood, overlooking the Blue Divide. It was once a beautiful port where lush green canopies sank into the ocean, serving as the premier trade port between the Summerset Isles and Valenwood. During the Imperial Simulacrum, war broke out between the Summerset Isles and Valenwood. Though brief, the conflict devastated the region: the Summerset Isles seized several Valenwood islands, half of Haven's Altmeri population was executed, and Altmeri war-wizards engulfed Woodhearth in flames. Survivors described fireballs descending from Aetherius and Oblivion alike, Bosmer burning in the streets, and a siege that starved the remnants. The attackers slaughtered Bosmer herds and cornered the population within the ashen ruins of the city.
topic_desc_basic: Woodhearth is a major city on the southwestern coast of Valenwood, overlooking the Blue Divide. Once the premier trade port between the Summerset Isles and Valenwood, famed for its lush canopies reaching the ocean, it was devastated by Altmeri war-wizards during the Imperial Simulacrum.

title: Cathnoquey
topic_desc: Cathnoquey is an archipelago in the Padomaic Ocean east of Morrowind. Annexed by the Empire over a century ago, it remains the homeland of the Quey civilization, whose culture endures despite Imperial subjugation. The Wasabi Run, a prominent island chain within the territory, yields more wasabi than the rest of the known world combined. The region is characterized by fair weather, calm waters, and abundant fish and game.
topic_desc_basic: Cathnoquey is an Imperial island territory and archipelago in the Padomaic Ocean east of Morrowind. Annexed by the Empire over a century ago, it remains the homeland of the Quey civilization and is known for the Wasabi Run, an island chain that produces more wasabi than the rest of the known world combined.

title: Yneslea
topic_desc: The Yneslea archipelago lies southeast of Cathnoquey. It is a beautiful and ancient realm, but a troubled one.
topic_desc_basic: The Yneslea archipelago lies between Tamriel and Akavir, southeast of Cathnoquey. It is a beautiful and ancient realm, but a troubled one.

title: Kogotel
topic_desc: A Kogotel is a Redoran fortress-within-a-fortress, serving as the innermost redoubt of a major House Redoran fortification. When outer defenses fall, defenders retreat into the Kogotel, which is well-provisioned and designed to sustain a small garrison for months or even years against besieging forces. The concept is central to Redoran military architecture. Notable examples include the Star Hearth in Blacklight and Skar in Ald-ruhn. At Ald Marak, the Kogotel is burrowed deep into the island's rock and crowned by a tower commanding the strait between the Horns of Lake Coronati. Access is controlled by a drawbridge, and its sheer cliffs and layered defenses make assault extraordinarily difficult. Ald Marak has fallen only once in its history, to an attacking force that used water-breathing magic to bypass its defenses.
topic_desc_basic: A Kogotel is a Redoran fortress-within-a-fortress, serving as the innermost redoubt of a major House Redoran fortification. Well-provisioned, it allows a small garrison to hold against besiegers for months or years. Every major Redoran fortification has one, with famous examples including the Star Hearth in Blacklight and Skar in Ald-ruhn.

title: Tur Julan
topic_desc: Tur Julan is an extensive ruined Indoril chapel in the Aanthirin region, situated on a ridge northwest of the Oran Plantation on the western side of the Thirr River. Formerly a House Indoril stronghold, its priests performed a grand invocation ritual, surrendering the fortress to Daedra to prevent its capture by encroaching House Hlaalu forces. The complex comprises fifteen distinct zones—including the Hall of Invocation, Warriors' Hall, Statesmen's Hall, Servants' Hall, and Spire—and is heavily infested with diverse Daedra, many of which are not immediately hostile. The ghosts of the Indoril who once governed the site linger within the Crossing of Wings' Hall of Judgment, maintaining spectral tribunals over lesser Daedra. The Spire is guarded by the Daedric Guardian Xerhet Hitai and holds significant material wealth, while the Statesmen's Hall contains ceremonial apparatus and alchemical equipment.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Tur Julan is.
aliases: Tur Julan, Crossing of Wings: Hall of Judgment
Tur Julan, Crossing of Wings: Waiting Door

title: Queen Morgiah
topic_desc: Queen Morgiah is the firstborn child of Barenziah and the sister of King Hlaalu Helseth of Morrowind. Formerly a princess of Wayrest, she became the first Dunmeri Queen of the Altmer kingdom of Summurset, marrying King Karoodil. Accounts of their union differ sharply: some describe a love at first sight, while others suspect unnatural manipulation, alleging that such instant devotion is not natural and citing her non-Altmer birth as a source of provincial unease. She is widely recognized as cunning and a natural leader and strategist. Her Dunmer heritage affords her a perceived loyalty among House Dunmer, who expect her to continue prioritizing House interests in her decisions.
topic_desc_basic: Queen Morgiah is the first Dunmeri Queen of the Altmer kingdom of Summurset. She is the firstborn child of Barenziah and the sister of King Hlaalu Helseth of Morrowind, having married King Karoodil to secure her position.

title: Firewatch
topic_desc: Firewatch is a fortified Imperial city on the Inner Sea coast within the Dagon Urul region, serving as the seat of Imperial power in northeast Morrowind. Founded shortly after the Treaty of the Armistice over four centuries ago, it was constructed in the Imperial style to house the offices and infrastructure of the Empire. The city is divided into several districts: the Old Fortress, which includes Ember Keep, the Drakelight Beacon lighthouse, the Dustmoth Legion Garrison, and the docks; the Market Quarter; the affluent Vaynth Quarter, home to the College of Firewatch and the Guild of Mages; and Uriel's Quarter, slums built to house veterans of Uriel Septim V's disastrous Akavir invasion. Duchess Perulia Jandacia rules from Ember Keep. The city maintains busy maritime trade and hosts three separate garrisons, including the notoriously corrupt Dustmoth Legion.
topic_desc_basic: Firewatch is a fortified Imperial city on the Inner Sea coast in the Dagon Urul region of northeast Morrowind. Founded after the Treaty of the Armistice, it serves as the seat of Imperial power in the area and features a tall lighthouse, an impressive keep, and a rich college.

title: Cuirass of Olms' Valor
topic_desc: The Cuirass of Olms' Valor is a blessed cuirass venerated by the Tribunal Temple's Order of War. It was interred with a War Ordinator in Ovam Ancestral Tomb to honor his service. The Order considers its recovery a sacred duty; vampires who defiled the tomb were cleansed to retrieve it. The cuirass is notably durable, exceeding standard Indoril armor, and bears a useful enchantment. Ordinators bestow it upon those who prove worthy, honoring past bearers and reaffirming the wearer's duty to defend the Tribunal and the faithful.
topic_desc_basic: The Cuirass of Olms' Valor is a blessed cuirass venerated by the Tribunal Temple's Order of War. It surpasses standard Indoril armor in durability and carries a useful enchantment. Ordinators bestow it upon the worthy to honor past bearers and reaffirm the wearer's sacred duty to defend the Tribunal and the faithful.

title: St. Ino's Caravanserai
topic_desc: St. Ino's Caravanserai is a remote East Empire Company trade outpost situated in the desert along the route to Narsis. The facility manages commercial caravans and maintains a guar herd for transport. Despite its Company designation as an independent operational command, personnel stationed there regard it as an isolated and undesirable posting, characterized by spartan accommodations and a reliance on hired mercenaries for security. Tensions exist between Company staff and local guild operatives, and the caravanserai draws labor from nearby farmsteads, including former workers from Seles-owned estates. The surrounding open desert terrain contrasts sharply with the crowded conditions reported in Narsis.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where St. Ino's Caravanserai is.

title: connection to Molag Bal
topic_desc: The connection to Molag Bal refers to a dissolved historical pact between a specific clan and the Daedric Prince, which the group is actively seeking to restore. Lord Molag Bal recently communicated with the clan through a vision to Kashshaptu, declaring that one final step remains to regain their former influence: the creation of new clan amulets to reforge the old agreements. The reestablishment of this connection is understood by the clan as the direct return of their former glory and power, recognized by the Dreaded Lord himself.
topic_desc_basic: The connection to Molag Bal refers to a dissolved historical pact between a specific clan and the Daedric Prince. The clan believes that reforging this agreement through new amulets will restore their former glory and influence.

title: Demons of Veloth
topic_desc: The Demons of Veloth are figures referenced within certain traditionalist Morrowind circles, invoked in aphoristic warnings such as 'Ever they deceive,' 'Ever they vex us,' 'Ever they try us,' and 'Ever they test us.' These refrains reflect a cultural apprehension of malevolent spirits or Daedric forces that perpetually threaten the Dunmer people. The phrase also serves as a covert code among those conducting discreet business with outlanders; speaking of the Demons of Veloth signals illicit dealings to traditionalist peers who would otherwise condemn such associations. This dual usage underscores the tension between orthodox Temple morality and the pragmatic realities of commerce in Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: The Demons of Veloth are malevolent figures in traditionalist Dunmer belief, invoked in the aphoristic warnings 'Ever they deceive,' 'Ever they vex us,' 'Ever they try us,' and 'Ever they test us.' These phrases also serve as a covert code among orthodox Dunmer to signal discreet business with outlanders.

title: Sentinel
topic_desc: Sentinel is a major city of Hammerfell situated along the shores of the Iliac Bay near the Alik'r Desert. It serves as a prominent base for desert expeditions. The city is renowned for its opulence, featuring grand temples, rich palaces, unbreachable forts, and beautiful gardens. Its markets are characterized by the scent of spices and herbs, while streets fill with music, acrobats, and artisans. Some Hammerfell natives favor other cities such as Hegathe, but Sentinel remains a celebrated jewel of the region.
topic_desc_basic: Sentinel is a major city in Hammerfell on the shores of the Iliac Bay near the Alik'r Desert. It is renowned for its opulent palaces, grand temples, unbreachable forts, and beautiful gardens. Its markets offer spices and herbs, while its streets feature music, acrobats, and artisans.

title: Velothis District
topic_desc: Velothis District is one of the six administrative districts of the Imperial province of Morrowind. It encompasses the mountainous northern and western reaches of Morrowind along the borders with Skyrim and Cyrodiil, and contains the bulk of the Roth Roryn and Armun Ashlands regions. Blacklight, the district's capital, is the largest city in northwestern Morrowind and serves as the seat of the Duke.
topic_desc_basic: Velothis District is one of the six administrative districts of Morrowind, occupying the mountainous northwestern frontier along the borders with Skyrim and Cyrodiil. Its capital is Blacklight, the largest city in northwestern Morrowind and the seat of the Duke. The district includes much of the Roth Roryn and Armun Ashlands.

title: Old Ebonheart
topic_desc: Old Ebonheart is the largest Imperial city in Morrowind and the province's Imperial capital, set on the eastern banks of the Thirr River delta. It stands on the ruins of the original city of Ebonheart, also known as Khalaan, which House Indoril burned rather than surrender to Tiber Septim's forces. Rebuilt in the Colovian style, the city has prospered for centuries as a beacon of Cyrodilic civilization. Its great citadel, the Ebon Tower, houses the Morrowind Imperial Legion headquarters, the Imperial Curia's Hall of Justice, courtrooms, and provincial offices, controlling the route between Vivec and Almalexia. The plaza hosts the Grand Chapel of Talos, Fighters Guild, East Empire Company, and the Imperial Archaeological Society. The Imperial Navy maintains its headquarters at the docks. The Imperial Cult reigns supreme within the walls, and the Emperor's law is the only law.
topic_desc_basic: Old Ebonheart is the largest Imperial city in Morrowind and the province's Imperial capital, located on the eastern banks of the Thirr River delta. Built on the ruins of the original Ebonheart, it was rebuilt in Colovian style and has served as a center of Imperial administration for centuries. Boat and Guild Guide transport connect it to major settlements across the region.

title: Stories of Lorkhan
topic_desc: Stories of Lorkhan are diverse mythological accounts explaining the creation of the mortal world and the fate of its architect, the trickster deity Lorkhan. Dunmeri traditions, including the book "Sithis," frame Lorkhan as a figure who tricked the Aedra into transforming pre-creation nothingness into a living world, for which they destroyed him. Nordic accounts know him as Shor and hold that his heart landed beneath Red Mountain, a claim supported by the longstanding belief that a great power lies buried there. The Altmer, by contrast, venerate the pre-creation void and view Lorkhan's act as destructive. Key texts preserving these narratives include the Monomyth, Sithis, and the Five Songs of King Wulfharth.
topic_desc_basic: Stories of Lorkhan are mythological accounts of the mortal world's creation and the fate of its trickster architect. Dunmer revere him for tricking the Aedra into making a living world from nothingness, for which they destroyed him. Nords know him as Shor and believe his heart landed beneath Red Mountain. Altmer view his act as destructive, revering the pre-creation void instead.

title: Velothi Mountains
topic_desc: The Velothi Mountains form a mountainous natural border between Morrowind and Skyrim, and extend along much of the Cyrodiil frontier, within the Velothis District. Riddled with dangerous passes, only a few serve as viable passage between the provinces, guarded by remote outposts. The region is largely unsettled, save for the tiny Redoran village of Uman and encampments of Malahk Orcs. Its harsh, frequently foggy and overcast terrain conceals numerous caves, ancestral tombs, and Velothi towers. Ancient Dwemer ruins like Hendor-Stardumz and Ngelfltingth lie within its bounds, alongside Daedric shrines dedicated to Malacath and Sheogorath. The mountains border Uld Vraech to the north, the Grey Meadows and Roth Roryn below, and the Othreleth Woods and Shipal-Shin to the south.
topic_desc_basic: The Velothi Mountains form a mountainous natural border between Morrowind and Skyrim, and extend along much of the Cyrodiil frontier. Riddled with dangerous passes, only a few serve as viable routes between the provinces.

title: Hlaalu Council Company
topic_desc: The Hlaalu Council Company is a pan-Tamrielic chartered trading firm founded by the Hlaalu Council to consolidate and advance House Hlaalu's mercantile interests beyond Morrowind. Ostensibly an independent entity, it functions in practice as an arm of the Hlaalu government, establishing exclusive foreign contracts, managing external enterprises, and controlling the House's monetary policy. Its board and Director are selected by Council vote and remain subject to Council oversight. Headquartered at the Mesa Exchange in Narsis's Market Quarter, adjacent to the Sixth Family Manor, the company maintains branch offices in Kragenmoor, Haafingar, Wayrest, Firsthold, and the Imperial City. While founded by and aligned with Hlaalu interests, not all Factors are House members; its current Director is the Altmer Cyrtumir. The East Empire Company views the firm as a direct and aggravating rival, accusing it of leveraging political influence to obstruct competing shipments while securing favorable treatment for its own.
topic_desc_basic: The Hlaalu Council Company is a pan-Tamrielic trading firm founded by the Hlaalu Council to advance House Hlaalu's mercantile interests beyond Morrowind. Though nominally independent, it operates in close alignment with House Hlaalu. Its headquarters sit at the Mesa Exchange in Narsis's Market Quarter, with branch offices across the Empire including Kragenmoor, Wayrest, and the Imperial City.

title: Roth Roryn
topic_desc: Roth Roryn is a region of rocky canyons and hills in the Velothis District of Morrowind. It is bordered by the Clambering Moor to the north, the Velothi Mountains to the west, the Armun Ashlands to the south, and Aanthirin to the east, with a small stretch of Bitter Coast coastline. The Pryai River flows through its terrain. Its largest settlement is Bal Foyen, a House Hlaalu trade entrepot on the Inner Sea. Other notable sites include the Hlaalu towns of Bodrum, Menaan, Omaynis, and the Imperial colony of Teyn, overseen by Fort Ancylis. The region holds monasteries dedicated to Saints Aralor and Felms, Daedric and Dwemer ruins such as Bthuangthuv and Leftunch, and the fallen Indoril castle of Bahrund. Scattered farms, egg mines, and dwellings occupy the canyon walls and riverbanks.
topic_desc_basic: Roth Roryn is a rocky canyon region in the Velothis District of Morrowind, bordered by the Clambering Moor, Velothi Mountains, Armun Ashlands, and Aanthirin. Its largest settlement is the House Hlaalu trade city of Bal Foyen on the Inner Sea.

title: Face of Veloth
topic_desc: The Face of Veloth is a legendary, possibly divine apparition associated with Saint Veloth. Long ago, a saint directed House Hlaalu to seek it, prompting the Council to dispatch a massive fleet led by the ship Seyda Neen eastward. An unnatural storm wrecked the fleet; the Seyda Neen's wreckage built the town's lighthouse. Survivors implanted washed-up shards in their foreheads to commemorate the disaster. The Face's exact nature remains uncertain, with skeptics dismissing it entirely. Accounts claim an outlander later performed the Ritual of St. Veloth in Necrom and beheld a divine presence that directed them further east toward Akavir, though Temple scribes continue to debate whether it was truly Veloth.
topic_desc_basic: The Face of Veloth is a legendary apparition associated with Saint Veloth. Long ago, a saint directed House Hlaalu to seek it, prompting a massive fleet led by the ship Seyda Neen. An unnatural storm wrecked the fleet, and the Seyda Neen's wreckage built the lighthouse of the town bearing its name. Its exact nature remains uncertain, and skeptics dismiss it entirely.

title: Gorne
topic_desc: Gorne is a verdant and peaceful island in the Inner Sea, situated between Tel Branora and Darvonis, contrasting sharply with the harsh landscape of the nearby Sundered Scar. Its southern end hosts an Indoril settlement and pilgrimage site serving as the seat of Councillor Indoril Sandil. The town is divided into two districts: an upper town dominated by Sandil House, where retainers train at the Warrior's Hall, and a lower waterfront. Isolated from the mainland, the island is accessible only by sea.
topic_desc_basic: Gorne is a verdant island in the Inner Sea between Tel Branora and Darvonis. Its southern end holds an Indoril town and pilgrimage site that is the seat of Councillor Indoril Sandil.

title: halls of our Emperor
topic_desc: The Halls of our Emperor is an Imperial faction associated with Casimor, which its members describe as a proud bastion of Imperial power. At least one warrior within the faction reports having been prohibited from projecting that power during a period he calls the long wait, and seeks news of the war and of the Emperor. The faction's precise relationship to broader Imperial military or administrative structures in the region is not clearly documented in available sources.
topic_desc_basic: The Halls of our Emperor is an Imperial faction based at Casimor. Its members regard the site as a bastion of Imperial power in the region.

title: Narsis Watch
topic_desc: The Narsis Watch is the original guard force of the city of Narsis, formed shortly after the founding clans consolidated under Tharel Hlaalu. In peacetime, its duties are restricted to the Council Quarter and Hlaalu family manors. In war, it forms House Hlaalu's elite core, maintaining armories and drilling the militia. The Bailiff of Narsis, Thelama Salandys, commands the Watch and its subordinate Canyon and River Watches, which police the rest of the city; a subordinate handles daily Watch operations. Most manor guards belong to the Watch, though the Grandmaster maintains a personal bodyguard and high-security areas are guarded by a Colovian mercenary company.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Narsis Watch is.

title: Deshaan District
topic_desc: The Deshaan District is the southeastern and southernmost of the six administrative districts comprising the Imperial province of Morrowind. Primarily controlled by House Dres, the district is defined by its largely agrarian economy and its proximity to Argonia, which fuels a great influx of slaves into Dres plantations. The geography transitions from the fertile Deshaan Plains in the north, through the salty, mountainous Ilumat Highlands—a wasteland where shade and water are scarce—to the treacherous southern swamps of Arnesia and the wet marshes of Urush-Nal. The major settlement of Silnion sits near the Ilumat Highlands' eastern border, while only smaller plantations like Hairab and Bashipal brave the highland interior. Disputed border claims with Argonia remain a persistent feature of the region.
topic_desc_basic: The Deshaan District is the southernmost administrative district of the Imperial province of Morrowind, primarily controlled by House Dres. Its proximity to Argonia supplies a great influx of slaves for the region's agrarian society. The landscape transitions from the fertile Deshaan Plains in the north to the treacherous southern swamps of Arnesia, with the salty, mountainous Ilumat Highlands lying in between.

title: pilgrimage
topic_desc: Pilgrimages are devotional journeys undertaken by faithful of the Tribunal Temple to sacred sites, shrines, and cantons. They commemorate divine acts of Almalexia, Vivec, and Sotha Sil, honor the sacrifices of Temple defenders, and mark events of spiritual significance. The Ghostgate shrine, for instance, honors the Tribunal's creation of arcane barriers against Dagoth Ur and memorializes the Ordinators, Buoyant Armigers, crusaders, and pilgrims who died defending Morrowind. Another recent pilgrimage marks the site where an incarnation of a saint was rescued from a daedra before leading the faithful to the Face of Veloth in Necrom.
topic_desc_basic: Pilgrimages are devotional journeys to sacred Tribunal Temple sites. They commemorate divine acts of Almalexia, Vivec, and Sotha Sil, honor fallen Temple defenders, and mark spiritually significant events across Morrowind.

title: On Elemental Daedra
topic_desc: On Elemental Daedra is a somewhat rare magical tome concerned with the study of elemental Daedra. The work is uncommon enough that it is not typically available in ordinary bookshops. Copies are known to be held in the collections of major Mages Guild halls on the mainland, including Old Ebonheart and Bal Foyen, and may also be found among the libraries of Telvanni tower masters or within Daedric ruins. The text is generally absent from Vvardenfell, necessitating travel to the mainland for those who seek it. Its subject matter makes it of particular interest to scholars of Daedric studies and conjuration.
topic_desc_basic: On Elemental Daedra is a somewhat rare magical tome concerned with the study of elemental Daedra. It is not typically found in ordinary bookshops or on Vvardenfell. Scholars suggest seeking copies in major mainland Mages Guild halls, Telvanni towers, or Daedric ruins.

title: The Origin of Vampires
topic_desc: A rare and controversial text that disputes the commonly accepted origin of vampirism. The Tribunal Temple considers it heretical and systematically destroys any copy it obtains.
topic_desc_basic: A rare book that disputes the Temple's teaching that vampirism comes from Molag Bal. The Tribunal Temple considers it heretical and burns any copy it finds.

title: Montagnard
topic_desc: Montagnards are the Breton inhabitants of the Wrothgarian and Kurallian mountain ranges in High Rock. As the most insular Breton cultural group, they have minimal contact with the wider world. Their settlements face persistent threat from Orcs and goblinken roaming the uplands, compelling Montagnards to construct fortified villages within stout fortress walls perched in high mountain valleys for protection.
topic_desc_basic: Montagnards are the Breton mountain-dwellers of the Wrothgarian and Kurallian ranges in High Rock. They are the most insular Bretons, having little contact with outsiders, and their villages are fortified against persistent threats from Orcs and goblinken.

title: King Moraelyn
topic_desc: King Moraelyn of House Raathim was a Chimer
topic_desc_basic: King Moraelyn of House Raathim was a First Era Chimer “witch-king” who ruled Khalaan, now Old Ebonheart. He is famous for driving the Nords out of Morrowind.

title: Ohmes-raht
topic_desc: Ohmes-raht are a breed of Khajiit said to resemble tall Bosmer or men. Unlike other Khajiit, they walk on their heels. They are often refined and poised, and serve as ambassadors like Prince Ji'Morashu-ri.
topic_desc_basic: The Ohmes-raht are a breed of Khajiit who resemble tall Bosmer or men. Unlike other Khajiit, they walk on their heels. They bear tails and thin fur, and paint their faces to suggest a feline appearance. Known for refinement and poise, they sometimes serve as ambassadors.

title: Chimeri-Quey
topic_desc: The Chimeri-Quey are a seafaring people inhabiting the Padomaic Ocean region of Cathnoquey. Distinguished from mainland cultures by their maritime nomadism, they reside aboard great flotilla cities that move freely across the waves. Tamrielic observers apply the ethnonym Chimeri-Quey, though the people themselves consider Cathnoquey to encompass both the islands and their population, believing their vessels bring Cathnoquey wherever they travel. Their social organization includes distinct groups; one such group is represented by the counterpart Imequol Miveo, suggesting internal cultural divisions among the flotilla-dwelling population.
topic_desc_basic: The Chimeri-Quey are a seafaring people of the Padomaic Ocean around Cathnoquey. They live aboard great flotilla cities that move freely across the waves, believing their vessels bring Cathnoquey wherever they travel.

title: Port Telvannis
topic_desc: Port Telvannis is the largest city in the Telvanni holdings and the administrative center of all Telvanni business, hosting the Parliament of Bugs and Tel Thenim. Situated in the Telvanni Isles, it holds the distinction of being the most northeastern city in Tamriel. The settlement offers extensive services, including alchemists, enchanters, blacksmiths, and spellmakers, alongside a local slave market. Transport is facilitated exclusively by River Strider to destinations such as Tel Ouada, Llothanis, Sadas Plantation, and Gah Sadrith; no boat services operate from the city. Non-members of House Telvanni must purchase Hospitality Papers to access the city's services. The architecture is tiered, with key residences and shops situated across multiple elevated levels.
topic_desc_basic: Port Telvannis is the largest city in House Telvanni's holdings, located in the Telvanni Isles. It serves as the center of all Telvanni business and hosts the Parliament of Bugs. It is the most northeastern city in Tamriel. River Striders provide transport to nearby settlements, though boat services are unavailable. Non-Telvanni must purchase Hospitality Papers to use city services.

title: dreugh man o'war
topic_desc: A dreugh man o'war is an especially large and dangerous aquatic dreugh. Whether man o'wars metamorphose from mighty land dreugh returning to the water, or skip the land stage entirely, remains unobserved and debated. They frequently serve as guardians and consorts to dreugh queens, though many also command hives independently. Certain specimens are reported to cast spells.
topic_desc_basic: A dreugh man o'war is an especially large and dangerous form of aquatic dreugh found in the sea. They often guard or consort with dreugh queens, though many command hives on their own.

title: ancestors
topic_desc: Ancestor worship is central to Dunmer religion. The Dunmer believe the spirits of the dead persist in the mortal world, capable of knowing and affecting the future, communicating with other spirits, and working great magic. The living honor, gift, and petition these spirits for aid and protection. Recently dead spirits remain close to their living kin, offering quick guidance despite their relative weakness. The strongest spirits endure long after death as Heroes and Wise Women, preserving the race's wisdom and honor. Conversely, the worst spirits become evil and harmful, known as Ghosts, Devils, and Daemons; the living must beg their kinder ancestors for protection from these malevolent dead. The oldest and greatest ancestor spirits are the Daedra—powerful and cunning, but dangerous, distant, and hard to understand.
topic_desc_basic: Dunmer believe the spirits of the dead persist in the mortal world. The living honor and petition these ancestors for aid and protection, while fearing the evil spirits of the wicked dead.

title: King Edward
topic_desc: King Edward is the central figure of a long fictional historical series bearing his name. At least five volumes exist, with the fifth being notably rare and unlikely to be found in conventional bookshops. References to the work in mainland Tamriel occasionally surface in the context of rare book searches and private collections. While the narrative details of his reign and deeds remain within the pages of the series itself, the character's cultural footprint is defined by the scarcity and collectability of the texts rather than established historical fact.
topic_desc_basic: King Edward is the central figure of a long fictional historical series. At least five volumes exist, with the fifth being notably rare and unlikely to be found in conventional bookshops.

title: war-pilgrimage of St. Felms
topic_desc: The war-pilgrimage of St. Felms is a militant Temple rite commemorating Saint Felms' stand against the warriors of the frozen west. Pilgrims are tasked with facing the bitter cold to slay a vicious frost troll, a manifestation of the harsh Velothi mountains, in the Saint's footsteps. The target creature lurks northwest of Bodrum; the route follows the river west from the outpost into the mountains, where a trail near the northern bank leads to snowy foothills and a wooden staircase built by House Redoran. Completing the trial by slaying the troll cleanses the pilgrim's weapon and fulfills the sacred duty.
topic_desc_basic: The war-pilgrimage of St. Felms is a militant Tribunal Temple rite commemorating Saint Felms' stand against the warriors of the frozen west. Pilgrims must face the bitter cold of the Velothi mountains to slay a vicious frost troll northwest of Bodrum, fulfilling the sacred duty and cleansing their weapon.

title: chaos of the Interregnum
topic_desc: The Chaos of the Interregnum denotes the prolonged dissolution of the Second Empire following the Akaviri Potentate's collapse. Cyrodiil fractured as the ruling council's Nibenese house guards proved insufficient to hold the province. Western kings withdrew their militias to independent splinter territories, each aspiring to restore the Empire yet lacking the capacity to do so. This protracted fragmentation persisted until the First Reman emerged from among these rival claimants, ultimately reuniting the fractured provinces.
topic_desc_basic: The Chaos of the Interregnum was a period of fragmentation after the Akaviri Potentate's collapse, when Cyrodiil broke apart. Western kings each tried to restore the Empire but could not, until the First Reman arose to reunite the provinces.

title: Rihad
topic_desc: Rihad is a grand mercantile city-state and republic on Hammerfell's southern coast, sharing the mild climate of Cyrodiil's Strident Coast. Shielded from Alik'r Desert brigands, it prospers as a major trade hub between Hammerfell and Cyrodiil. The city features a prominent fire tower. Historically subjected to repeated Cyrodiilic conquests, Rihad presently harbors strong anti-Imperial sentiment despite its substantial Imperial presence. Reconciling this hostility with the Empire remains a persistent diplomatic challenge.
topic_desc_basic: Rihad is a grand mercantile city-state and republic on Hammerfell's southern Abecean coast. Shielded from the Alik'r Desert, it prospers as a major trade hub between Hammerfell and Cyrodiil, sharing the mild climate of Cyrodiil's Strident Coast. The city features a prominent fire tower.

title: spider daedra
topic_desc: Spider Daedra are arachnid Daedra recognized as among the most dangerous daedra encountered in Morrowind. They possess blinding and burdening magical abilities, and a paralytic threat significant enough that the Mages Guild produces specific potions to counter it. They are known to congregate in packs led by a Matriarch and establish nests in rocky, labyrinthine terrain. While they may superficially resemble spiders, their Daedric nature makes them formidable; seasoned advisors recommend engaging them at range with projectiles or spells rather than in melee, and emphasize the necessity of protective armor and antidotes.
topic_desc_basic: Spider Daedra are dangerous arachnid Daedra found in Morrowind's rocky, labyrinthine terrain. They congregate in packs led by a Matriarch and possess blinding, burdening, and paralytic magical abilities. The Mages Guild produces specific potions to counter their paralysis.

title: lake of sulphur
topic_desc: Sulphur lakes are found in the Sundered Scar region of mainland Morrowind. The most notable is Lake Dolosamsi, situated beside the stronghold of Morandano. Reports indicate that powerful daedra have been seen just outside the stronghold's vicinity, making the area hazardous. The sulphur lakes are a distinguishing geographic feature of the Sundered Scar, a region whose terrain and dangers are known to scouts familiar with the mainland's interior. The relationship between these lakes and the presence of daedra near Morandano remains unexplained by available accounts.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where lake of sulphur is.

title: Sanguine
topic_desc: Sanguine is a Daedric Prince recognized as a patron of the Morag Tong. Through his craftsmanship, he created the Threads of the Webspinner at the Forge of Inferndere. Accounts differ on the forge's location, placing it either directly at the site or on Vounoura. These relics were subsequently gifted to Mephala, who in turn granted them to the order's most devoted members. Any Morag Tong member possessing a Thread holds a sacred gift from this divine patronage.
topic_desc_basic: Sanguine is a Daedric Prince of hedonistic revelry and debauchery, known to worshippers as the Lord of Revelry. He is recognized as a patron of the Morag Tong, having crafted the Threads of the Webspinner, sacred relics later gifted through Mephala to the order's devoted members. His summoning day falls on Heart's Day, the 16th of Sun's Dawn.

title: Laws Determined
topic_desc: The Laws Determined constitute the absolute and unchanging principles established by the Tribunal for their followers. Considered foundational to Tribunal doctrine, many of these laws are profoundly complex, requiring decades of study to fully comprehend. Humility is recognized as one such law. To assist adherents in fulfilling these strictures, chapel-councilors provide practical guidance by establishing the Laws Ordained, which serve as accessible directives rooted in the overarching Laws Determined.
topic_desc_basic: The Laws Determined are the absolute and unchanging principles set by the Tribunal for their followers. Many are highly complex, requiring decades of study; humility is one recognized example. Chapel-councilors help adherents follow these strictures by establishing the more accessible Laws Ordained.

title: Veloth's Path
topic_desc: Veloth's Path is a sacred pilgrimage route believed to retrace Saint Veloth's journey leading the Chimer to their new homeland. It runs from Shadowgate Pass in the Velothi Mountains to the holy city of Necrom, passing Kragenmoor, Hlan Oek, Almas Thirr, and Almalexia. Pilgrims, chiefly Dunmer but occasionally outlanders, travel in great numbers, supported by the Tribunal Temple. Wayfarers pay respects at ancestral tombs and temples, sometimes undertaking side pilgrimages like the Bloodstone Shrine. Gourd harps line the path; these wind-powered instruments attract wayward spirits toward Necrom, and locals leave bones at them for pilgrims to carry onward. The Chimeri-Quey of Cathnoquey hold that Veloth continued east out to sea rather than ending at Necrom, and some Chimer traveled to the Padomaic archipelagos seeking him.
topic_desc_basic: Veloth's Path is a sacred pilgrimage route retracing Saint Veloth's journey leading the Chimer to Morrowind. It runs from Shadowgate Pass through major settlements like Kragenmoor, Almas Thirr, and Almalexia, ending at the holy city of Necrom. Dunmer pilgrims travel it in great numbers, supported by the Tribunal Temple.

title: Poison Song
topic_desc: Poison Song is a work of fiction by the author Bristin Xel, rooted in the tragic history of Morrowind. Its central motif is a refrain called the poison song, which the author describes as ringing in concert with the heartbeat of the land. Xel researched the novel among House Indoril and House Redoran, focusing on the betrayal of House Dagoth as a tragedy that lingers beneath the surface of Dunmer society. A sequel exploring the blossoming of that dormant tragedy was planned. Critical reception among Dunmer is sharply divided: some dismiss the work as dreadful, rife with historical inaccuracies and insulting stereotypes, while others tolerate it as a keepsake. The first volume is known to circulate in Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: Poison Song is a multi-volume work of fiction by Bristin Xel, described as a historically inaccurate epic set in the aftermath of the war with the Dwemer and House Dagoth. The first volume circulates in Morrowind, where Dunmer opinion of it is sharply divided.

title: Ja-Natta Syndicate
topic_desc: The Ja-Natta Syndicate is Morrowind's youngest significant criminal enterprise, alongside the Thieves Guild and Camonna Tong. Its chief purpose is manufacturing and distributing greydust, an alchemical solution catering to spiritual yearnings. Operating covertly due to official disapproval, the Syndicate maintains trading posts in Narsis, Ald Iuval, and Ald Horak, with significant activity along the Thirr region and canyons east of a local plantation. Observers characterize the gang as violent and profit-driven, lacking the codes of the Guild or the communal ideals of the Tong. The Syndicate's uneasy, non-hostile stance with both organizations remains fragile. Its structure and origins remain unknown, and its very existence is officially unconfirmed.
topic_desc_basic: The Ja-Natta Syndicate is a criminal gang operating in Morrowind, chiefly known for manufacturing and distributing greydust, an alchemical solution. Active around Narsis and the Thirr region, the group is widely regarded as violent and profit-driven, lacking the codes of the Thieves Guild or the communal ideals of the Camonna Tong.

title: Mephalan Vales
topic_desc: The Mephalan Vales are a humid, rocky, mountainous region in the Mournhold District that extends the Boethiah's Spine southward. This complex maze of fog-wreathed canyons forms a natural northern border for House Indoril's territories. The treacherous terrain remains largely impenetrable to the Tribunal's influence, allowing ancient forces to operate unseen in hidden valleys and ruins like Dun Akafell. Local Indoril rulers feud among themselves, lacking a unified vision, while outlaws and ghosts dwell in the winding paths connecting fortresses such as Ammar and Akamora, the region's largest settlement. Bordered by the Sacred Lands, Nedothril, Lan Orethan, Alt Orethan, the Sundered Scar, and the Inner Sea, the Vales host numerous Daedric shrines, Dwemer ruins, and ebony mines.
topic_desc_basic: The Mephalan Vales are a humid, rocky, mountainous region in the Mournhold District of Morrowind. This maze of fog-wreathed canyons forms a natural northern border for House Indoril's territories.

title: Dhaunayne Aundae
topic_desc: Dhaunayne Aundae is an ancient Altmer vampire and the leader of the Aundae vampire clan. The Aundae were a lesser noble family of the Summerset Isles largely wiped out during the Siege of Alinor. Dhaunayne's survival and transformation into a vampire ancient went unknown until a recent publication identified her as heading a vampiric bloodline bearing her family name. Under her leadership, the Aundae clan established Ashmelech, their lair built within a desecrated tomb on an island southwest of Dagon Fel between Sheogorad and Vvardenfell. Mages Guild researchers studying vampirism, including Skink-In-Tree's-Shade, recognize her as a figure of significant academic interest regarding the vampiric condition.
topic_desc_basic: Dhaunayne Aundae is an ancient Altmer vampire who leads the Aundae clan. Her family were Summerset Isles nobles largely killed during the Siege of Alinor. The Aundae clan lair is Ashmelech, a desecrated tomb on an island southwest of Dagon Fel.

title: Armun Ashlands
topic_desc: The Armun Ashlands is the largest ash-covered region on the Morrowind mainland, situated within the Velothis District. It borders Roth Roryn to the north, the Velothi Mountains to the west, Othreleth Woods and Thirr Valley to the south, and Aanthirin to the east. Local inhabitants offer differing explanations for why this region alone possesses ash to rival Vvardenfell. The largest settlement is the Hlaalu outpost and caravan stop of Arvud. The region hosts numerous traditionalist Ashlander tribes, alongside scattered Velothi towers, ancient Indoril ruins, and imposing Dwemer edifices. Daedric shrines dedicated to Princes such as Molag Bal, Mehrunes Dagon, Sheogorath, and Malacath dot the landscape. The hostile terrain is garrisoned by House Redoran's Eighth Watchman Patrol at Ramaniran and troubled by vampire covens, bandit gangs, and necromancers.
topic_desc_basic: The Armun Ashlands is a large, hostile region of dust and ash in the Velothis District of mainland Morrowind, bordering Roth Roryn, the Velothi Mountains, Othreleth Woods, Thirr Valley, and Aanthirin. Its largest settlement is the Hlaalu caravan stop of Arvud.

title: Tosh Raka
topic_desc: Tosh Raka, called the Tiger-Dragon, is the immortal god-king of Ka Po' Tun. Regarded as the largest dragon on Nirn, he commands a realm the Empire considers equal in standing to the Emperor of Tamriel. Diplomatic relations with Ka Po' Tun remain impossible to establish. Accounts allege that Tosh Raka intends to invade Tamriel after conquering Tsaesci.
topic_desc_basic: Tosh Raka, the Tiger-Dragon, is the immortal god-king of Ka Po' Tun in Akavir. Regarded as the largest dragon on Nirn, he is the only foreign ruler the Empire considers equal to the Emperor of Tamriel, though diplomatic relations with his realm remain impossible to establish. Accounts allege he intends to invade Tamriel after conquering Tsaesci.

title: Forebear
topic_desc: The Forebears are a major Redguard cultural and political bloc in Hammerfell, descended from the Ra Gada warriors who first settled the province's frontier for Yokudan migrants. In the Second Era, they rebelled against what they deemed a tyrannical Crown republic, winning self-governance. During the Tiber War, Forebears fought alongside the Empire and Crowns, securing victory and embracing free trade. Today, they maintain their proud martial traditions while sharing Hammerfell's peace and prosperity alongside the Crowns as brothers in arms.
topic_desc_basic: The Forebears are a major Redguard cultural and political group in Hammerfell, descended from the Ra Gada warriors who first settled the province. They are known for their liberal traditions, cosmopolitan trade, and worship of Imperial deities, contrasting with the traditionalist Crowns. Major Forebear strongholds include Sentinel, Rihad, and Taneth.

title: Telvannis District
topic_desc: Telvannis District is one of the six administrative divisions of the Imperial province of Morrowind, encompassing the entire northeastern sweep of the territory. Its official borders stretch from the southern foothills of Boethiah's Spine north of Necrom to Althoa in the Sea of Ghosts. In practice, however, Imperial authority is tenuous; the interior remains hostile and effectively beyond Imperial control, with actual governance rarely extending far beyond the walls of the settlements of Firewatch, Helnim, and Nivalis.
topic_desc_basic: Telvannis District is one of the six administrative districts of Morrowind, covering the province's entire northeastern sweep from the foothills of Boethiah's Spine north of Necrom to Althoa in the Sea of Ghosts. Imperial authority is weak, rarely extending beyond the walls of Firewatch, Helnim, and Nivalis.

title: Keptu-Quey
topic_desc: Keptu-Quey is the Cyrodilic term for the Quey people of the Cathnoquey islands. The Quey identify themselves as the People of the Bull, described as an ancient and hardy folk. Cyrodiils apply the compound designation to distinguish them as a people both Keptu and Quey, though the Quey themselves emphasize their bull heritage and their identity as Quey. The precise relationship between the Keptu and Quey elements of this name remains a matter of cultural distinction that the Quey themselves are best positioned to clarify.
topic_desc_basic: The Keptu-Quey are the people of the Cathnoquey islands. They call themselves the People of the Bull, an ancient and hardy folk, though Cyrodiils use the compound term to distinguish them as both Keptu and Quey.

title: Deshaan Plains
topic_desc: The Deshaan Plains are a flat, salty, and hostile region forming the heartland of the Deshaan District in Morrowind. Claimed by House Dres as their homeland, the plains serve as a base from which the House extends its influence east and north. The terrain is riddled with crevasses and sinkholes, and the region is home to vicious skyrenders and the xenophobic Dres. Despite its hostile conditions, the river valley is fertile and produces the majority of the saltrice consumed in Morrowind. The region borders Aanthirin to the northwest, the Coronati Basin to the west, Dejasyte to the southwest, the Shalimar Highlands to the southeast, the Mudflats to the east, and Orethan and Amber Forest to the north. Its largest settlement is Ald Horak.
topic_desc_basic: The Deshaan Plains are a flat, salty, and hostile region in the Deshaan District of Morrowind. Claimed by House Dres as their homeland, the area produces the majority of the saltrice consumed in Morrowind.

title: Bosmora
topic_desc: Bosmora is a wealthy Indoril settlement in the Lan Orethan region, deriving its abundant trade wealth from close proximity to Almalexia. The town maintains its own vault stacked with riches on behalf of House Indoril. Mercantile activity concentrates at the base of the cliff, featuring an indoor marketplace with six merchants, one serving as an enchanter, alongside additional outdoor market stalls. The markets terminate at the Starlight Inn. Ramps provide access to the town's upper level. Bosmora is well-connected, reachable from Sailen and Almalexia, with silt strider transport to Sailen and nix-mount rickshaw services from Enamor Dayn. The settlement hosts a Tribunal Temple offering spellmaking and healing services. Nearby landmarks include the Dwemer ruins of Alencheth, the Sassur-Dari Mine to the northwest, and old Indoril ruins at Dulandos to the east and Veremmu to the north.
topic_desc_basic: Bosmora is a wealthy Indoril settlement in the Lan Orethan region near Almalexia. It features a large indoor and outdoor marketplace, an inn, and a Tribunal Temple. The town is reachable from Sailen and Almalexia via silt strider.

title: Bal Foyen
topic_desc: Bal Foyen, sometimes called Stonefalls, is House Hlaalu's largest city on the Inner Sea, situated on the western side of the Thirr River delta. Unlike neighboring Old Ebonheart, Bal Foyen governs its own trade without Imperial oversight. The city occupies the site of Almalexia's cataclysmic victory over the Akaviri army of Ada'Soom Dir-Kamal; much of it is built over the resulting crater, where waterfalls cascade from the high rim into a sea-filled bay. The Temple stands on a central island, and local tradition holds that so long as it endures, Bal Foyen will never fall. The city is a Hlaalu stronghold: manors line the western cliffs, the Hlaalu Council Manor rises above eastern shops, the port stretches north, and the Andas Estate overlooks all from the southern cliff. The Camonna Tong is entrenched among Hlaalu nobility, and the Temple struggles to provide for the poor.
topic_desc_basic: Bal Foyen is House Hlaalu's largest city on the Inner Sea, located on the western side of the Thirr River delta. It is a major trading port built upon the site of Almalexia's legendary victory over the Akaviri invaders. The city governs its own affairs without direct Imperial oversight.

title: Ordinator of Doctrine
topic_desc: The Ordinators of Doctrine are a specialized branch of the Ordinators, the military-orders of the Tribunal Temple primarily associated with Great House Indoril. Tasked with safeguarding religious orthodoxy, they investigate and suppress heretical texts, unauthorized teachings, and doctrinal deviations among the faithful. Their duties include conducting inspections of Temple libraries and repositories to ensure no proscribed or heretical writings are held. While all Ordinators enforce Temple law, the Doctrine Ordinators focus specifically on intellectual and theological purity, distinguishing them from counterparts who guard temples or enforce general ecclesiastical discipline. Their authority to inspect and seize materials makes them a feared instrument of the Temple's inquisitorial apparatus.
topic_desc_basic: The Ordinators of Doctrine are a branch of the Tribunal Temple's Ordinator orders, tied to Great House Indoril. They investigate heretical writings and enforce theological orthodoxy, inspecting Temple libraries and repositories for proscribed texts.

title: Jehanna
topic_desc: Jehanna is a kingdom situated on High Rock's eastern border. It is characterized by a superstitious and primitive peasantry, making it an environment more conducive to raising fighters than scholars.
topic_desc_basic: Jehanna is a Breton kingdom on High Rock's eastern border, along the icy Northern Coast. Its superstitious peasantry makes it a place more suited to raising fighters than scholars.

title: Telvanni Isles
topic_desc: The Telvanni Isles constitute the northeasternmost archipelago in Tamriel, forming the isolated heartland of Great House Telvanni within the Telvannis District of Morrowind. The region consists of three main islands: Vahn Isle, the largest and site of the House capital; the Isle of Arches, a desolate island sacred to the Tribunal Temple; and Hlavan Isle, dominated by the town of Gah Sadrith. The terrain appears inhospitable at first glance, characterized by barren hills and damp fungal groves, yet these isles produce the great sadrith fungi from which the Telvanni construct their iconic towers. The sprawling capital of Port Telvannis anchors the archipelago, surrounded by subordinate settlements and plantations. The isles border the Padomaic Ocean to the south and east, the Sea of Ghosts to the northwest, and the regions of Boethiah's Spine and Sunad Mora across a narrow channel to the southwest.
topic_desc_basic: The Telvanni Isles are the northeasternmost archipelago in Morrowind, serving as the isolated heartland of Great House Telvanni. The terrain consists of barren hills and damp fungal groves that produce the great sadrith fungi used to construct Telvanni towers. The region's largest settlement is Port Telvannis.

title: the rift
topic_desc: The Rift is a tear in the fabric of Nirn, described as a circumpenetration forming a stable portal to a pocket realm. This aperture allows celestial travelers to move through the shadows between worlds. The pocket realm itself is hostile and devoid of air, requiring visitors to find means to breathe. The Rift was opened through a ritual employing three esoteric texts—Introduction to Hermaean Logic, Hyperagonal Media Theorem, and Transpontine Circumpenetrations—which also serve as the key to sealing it. Ralam Othravel's experiment in opening the Rift was deemed a threat before the aperture was closed. Raryn Girando investigated the disturbance from beyond but perished during the passage.
topic_desc_basic: The Rift is a tear in the fabric of Nirn forming a stable portal to a hostile, airless pocket realm. It allows celestial travelers to move through the shadows between worlds.

title: Quey
topic_desc: The Quey are the collective people of Cathnoquey, encompassing both Men and Mer who share a single cultural identity across the islands and surrounding seas.
topic_desc_basic: The Quey are the people of Cathnoquey, islands northeast of Morrowind. They include both Men and Mer under one shared identity, which many Tamrielics find unfamiliar.

title: Arnesian War
topic_desc: The Arnesian War was a conflict fought roughly thirty years ago between the Dunmer and the Argonians of Black Marsh. It was preceded by a brutal massacre at Arnesia, which led to the martyrdom of St. Roris and prompted the onset of hostilities. Fighting took place across the region south of Lake Andaram, though the Argonians never crossed the lake itself. The war caused widespread suffering and left many Dunmer orphaned; the Temple has since directed significant charity toward these survivors, known as the Orphans of Arnesia. The Dunmer ultimately waged war successfully in Argonian territory.
topic_desc_basic: The Arnesian War was a conflict fought roughly thirty years ago between the Dunmer and the Argonians of Black Marsh. It began as a slave revolt in House Dres lands after the massacre at Arnesia and the martyrdom of St. Roris. The Dunmer ultimately won, expanding their territory southward. The Temple now aids the surviving Orphans of Arnesia.

title: heresy
topic_desc: Heresy, as defined by the Tribunal Temple, encompasses any belief or practice that undermines the tenets established by the Tribunal. Specific transgressions include challenging the divinity of the Three, glorifying spirits deemed unworthy, and exhibiting irreverence toward the ancestors. The Temple identifies such deviations as direct threats to orthodox doctrine and spiritual order. Standard Temple texts like 'Fellowship of the Temple' and 'The House of Troubles' provide orthodox overviews of these dogmas.
topic_desc_basic: In the Tribunal Temple, heresy is any belief or practice that undermines the tenets laid down by the Tribunal. It includes challenging the divinity of the Three, glorifying unworthy spirits, and showing irreverence for the ancestors.

title: Archmagister of House Telvanni
topic_desc: The Archmagister is the traditional supreme leader of House Telvanni. Ordinarily, only one Archmagister holds authority at a time. Succession is typically resolved through a formal duel against the sitting Archmagister, though peaceful transitions have occurred rarely. The Parliament of Bugs recognizes legitimate authority; self-proclaimed claimants who avoid challenging the incumbent hold no real power. Rilvin Dral currently serves as Archmagister. The mage Gothren previously declared himself a rival Archmagister and fled to Vvardenfell rather than challenge Dral, rendering his title insignificant. Dral considered the matter beneath his notice, leaving the House with a de facto sole but uncontested Archmagister.
topic_desc_basic: The Archmagister is the supreme leader of House Telvanni. Succession is traditionally settled by formal duel against the incumbent, though peaceful transitions rarely occur. The Parliament of Bugs only recognizes claimants who legitimately challenge the sitting Archmagister; self-proclaimed rivals hold no actual power.

title: Imperial Navy
topic_desc: The Imperial Navy's Far East Fleet, colloquially known as the Sea Serpent Fleet, maintains its headquarters at the docks of Old Ebonheart in Morrowind. Under the command of Lord Admiral Potemus Marolus, the fleet patrols the Inner Sea for raiders and smugglers while monitoring the eastern coast for threats crossing the Padomaic Ocean from Akavir. Despite its strategic mandate, the fleet's Morrowind detachment faces local criticism; detractors dismiss it as a modest force confined to the narrow Inner Sea, questioning its stature compared to grander naval commands.
topic_desc_basic: The Imperial Navy is the Empire's aquatic military force, complementing the Imperial Legion. It operates out of its home port of Anvil and maintains fleets across the provinces, including the Far East Fleet headquartered at Old Ebonheart in Morrowind.

title: Laws Ordained
topic_desc: The Laws Ordained comprise the body of statutes established by House Indoril's councilors to clarify and contextualize the Laws Determined, the more abstract foundational principles of Indoril jurisprudence. Where the Laws Determined set forth broad doctrinal frameworks, the Laws Ordained address practical specifics—most notably the detailed mechanisms of the demesne governance system through which House Indoril administers its territories. Outsiders referencing House Indoril's laws typically mean the Laws Ordained, as these concrete provisions are more visible and comprehensible than the philosophical underpinnings of the Laws Determined. Together, the two tiers form a layered legal tradition: the Determined establishing principle, the Ordained establishing application.
topic_desc_basic: The Laws Ordained are the practical statutes enacted by House Indoril's councilors to clarify and contextualize the abstract foundational Laws Determined. They cover specific applications such as the demesne governance system and are the provisions outsiders typically mean when referring to House Indoril's laws.

title: High Court of Narsis
topic_desc: The High Court of Narsis is the supreme legal body within House Hlaalu's western-style justice system, functioning as a local implementation of the Imperial court model that nonetheless operates under the umbrella of House law. This interlocking arrangement grants House Hlaalu considerable efficiency in both legal and commercial matters, allowing the Court to adjudicate trade disputes and questions involving western institutions that would prove unwieldy under traditional House legal structures. The courtroom itself sees relatively limited use, as traditional House law mechanisms persist alongside the western system, with most major traditional matters resolved through tribunals convened at council meetings. The Court accordingly finds its greatest application in trade disputes and complex questions of Imperial law, with House Hlaalu represented before it by the Chief Justice and Chief Inquisitor. Supporters contrast its flexibility with the more rigid traditionalist systems maintained by House Redoran and House Indoril.
topic_desc_basic: The High Court of Narsis is the supreme legal body of House Hlaalu's western-style justice system, located in the city of Narsis. It is a local implementation of the Imperial court model that operates under House law, primarily adjudicating trade disputes and complex matters of Imperial law.

title: Lake Andaram
topic_desc: Lake Andaram is a large, deep lake situated on the hotly contested Thirr River, with the river's entrance located at the lake's western end. It is encircled by the Aanthirin region, though loosely on its southern and eastern sides, bordering the Coronati Basin to the southwest and the Deshaan Plains to the southeast. Three Great Houses maintain settlements along its shores: House Hlaalu controls Nav Andaram, guarding the outflow into the Thirr River; House Indoril holds the small fishing port of Aimrah on the northeastern shore; and House Dres occupies Dres Horak on the southeastern shore. The lake hosts a heavy dreugh presence, including the deep labyrinth known as Paruddma's Maw. Its submerged grottos contain pearl beds, dreugh colonies, and at least one flooded ancestral tomb. The partly flooded Daedric ruin of Andarannipal stands on the southern shores.
topic_desc_basic: Lake Andaram is a large, deep lake on the Thirr River, encircled by the Aanthirin region. The Hlaalu, Indoril, and Dres Great Houses all maintain settlements on its shores, and its waters host a heavy dreugh presence.

title: the Towers
topic_desc: The Towers is a collective designation for the large apartment blocks at the center of St. Veloth's Quarter, specifically Brevur Heights and the Velothi Tower. These imposing structures serve as the seat of Camonna Tong influence in southern Morrowind, where the Tong's regional bosses, including Mervis Llarel, maintain their operations. The extent of Camonna Tong control over the Quarter through these towers is regarded as considerable, reflecting the organization's deep entrenchment in the region's power structure. The towers' foundations have reportedly been subject to destabilization efforts by rival interests seeking to undermine that hold. Beyond their functional role as residential and organizational strongpoints, the Towers stand as notable examples of large-scale Velothi urban architecture, dominating the city's central district.
topic_desc_basic: The Towers are the large apartment blocks at the center of St. Veloth's Quarter, comprising Brevur Heights and the Velothi Tower. They serve as the seat of Camonna Tong influence in southern Morrowind, housing the organization's regional bosses.

title: Shipal-Sharai
topic_desc: Shipal-Sharai is a House Hlaalu town in the Shipal-Shin region, situated west of Narsis along the Purple Road, the Imperial highway running toward Cyrodiil. The settlement lies within a narrow canyon, with many buildings carved directly into the rock walls. It was reputedly founded by an unnamed Shinathi Dunmer clan, and its governor claims descent from those founders. The town's prosperity has declined: the sapphire mine that once enriched it is disused, and trade along the Purple Road has diminished due to troubles affecting the nearby Cyrodiilic city of Mir Corrup. Order is maintained by Hlaalu guards, while the Imperial Legion maintains an outpost. A caravanserai still hosts passing caravans, and the cornerclubs see steady patronage. The Camonna Tong, Ja-Natta Syndicate, and Twin Lamps each maintain a presence.
topic_desc_basic: Shipal-Sharai is a House Hlaalu town in the Shipal-Shin region, west of Narsis along the Purple Road to Cyrodiil. It sits in a narrow canyon with buildings carved into the rock walls. Once enriched by a sapphire mine now disused, the town has declined but remains a stop for caravans. Hlaalu guards and the Imperial Legion both maintain a presence.

title: Muatra
topic_desc: Muatra, the sacred spear of Vivec, holds profound theological significance in Morrowind. Accounts of its origin differ: Temple doctrine holds it was fashioned from Molag Bal's vices turned virtues, while an alternative folk tradition claims a fisherman recovered it after it drifted down the Thirr. The sanctioned relic rests in Narsis at Eight-Bones Temple, drawing pilgrims who venerate it beneath the dome. Conflicting narratives also surround its wieldings; Temple orthodoxy credits it with slaying the monstrous offspring of Chimer and demons—including Vivec's own progeny, GULGA MOR JIL, whose bones reportedly form Narsis' bedrock—while a Hlan Oek tradition claims it vanquished Kognchuft, last god-king of the Dwemer. Devotion holds that to speak its name lightly invites spiritual sterility and that its touch brings death. The spear is thus revered as scripture made weapon.
topic_desc_basic: Muatra is the sacred spear of Lord Vivec, housed beneath the dome of Eight-Bones Temple in Narsis. Pilgrims travel from across Morrowind to venerate the relic, which Temple doctrine credits with slaying the monstrous offspring of Chimer and demons.

title: Peninsula of Veloth
topic_desc: The Peninsula of Veloth is a coastal geographic projection in Morrowind bearing a named pilgrimage site. Accessible via trails south and west from the Teriviel Ancestral Tomb, the route requires navigating a specific series of forks and paths near the coast before ascending rough stone steps to reach the destination. The site's name honors Saint Veloth, the Prophet of the Dunmer, indicating the peninsula's religious significance within the Tribunal faith.
topic_desc_basic: The Peninsula of Veloth is a coastal projection in Morrowind named for Saint Veloth, the Prophet of the Dunmer. It bears a pilgrimage site of religious significance to the Tribunal faith, accessible via coastal trails south and west of the Teriviel Ancestral Tomb.

title: Four Score War
topic_desc: The Four Score War was a conflict fought between Morrowind and the Second Empire of Man at the end of the First Era. Most of the fighting occurred in western Morrowind, suffering extensive destruction. The ancient House Hlaalu council seat of Narsis was sacked by the Second Empire. The war ultimately ended in a truce. No evidence of the sacking of Narsis remains today; House Hlaalu has rebuilt and expanded the city as a trade hub that has not seen war since.
topic_desc_basic: The Four Score War was an eighty-year conflict between Morrowind and the Second Empire of Man at the end of the First Era. Most fighting occurred in western Morrowind, causing extensive destruction. The House Hlaalu council seat of Narsis was sacked. The war ended in a truce, and Narsis has since been rebuilt as a trade hub.

title: Malacath
topic_desc: Malacath is a Daedric Prince worshiped as the keeper of the Sworn Oath and the Bloody Curse. The Orcs are his oldest followers and are considered his people. His worship is maintained at dedicated Daedric shrines, where adherents honor these sacred and cursing aspects. As the patron of the Orcs, his veneration is deeply intertwined with their cultural identity and devotion.
topic_desc_basic: Malacath is a Daedric Prince worshiped as the keeper of the Sworn Oath and the Bloody Curse. The Orcs are his oldest followers and are considered his people. His veneration is maintained at dedicated Daedric shrines.

title: The Empress Katariah
topic_desc: Empress Katariah Septim, a Dunmer consort who ascended to the Ruby Throne and ruled the Third Empire during the third century of the Third Era. She is widely regarded as one of the most capable and effective monarchs in the Septim dynasty's history.
topic_desc_basic: Empress Katariah Septim was a Dunmer who ruled the Third Empire during the third century of the Third Era and is remembered as one of the most capable monarchs in the Septim dynasty.

title: Tremor March
topic_desc: The TEM Tremor March is a vessel of the Imperial East Navy that lost contact with its command while conducting an undisclosed mission. The ship later wrecked under unknown circumstances. Its logbook constitutes classified material, and Admiral Potemus Marolus at Fort Pelagius actively seeks its recovery, offering considerable unofficial compensation. Evidence within the logbook reportedly documents the illegal smuggling of an ash ghoul from Vvardenfell to the mainland, posing a severe risk of spreading the Blight. The Imperial East Navy refuses to officially comment on any rumors surrounding the vessel and actively suppresses public disclosure of the incident and its implications.
topic_desc_basic: The TEM Tremor March is an Imperial East Navy ship that wrecked after losing contact with its command. Admiral Potemus Marolus at Fort Pelagius seeks information regarding the vessel and offers unofficial compensation for its recovery.

title: Reign of the Septims
topic_desc: Reign of the Septims is a mnemonic song enumerating many of the historical Emperors of the Septim Dynasty. Numerous versions circulate throughout Tamriel, ranging from vulgar verses muttered by common folk to refined recitations taught by governesses to noble children. The song commemorates pivotal figures and events of the dynasty: Tiber Septim, first of the line, who rose from humble origins to be hailed by the people of Tamriel as Talos and Ysmir, the Dragon of the North; the Grey Empress Katariah of House Raathim, called the Empress with Ruby Eyes, slain by a stray Argonian arrow and entombed beneath Old Ebonheart; and Uriel V, who sailed to Akavir and fell on the fields of Ionith, ambushed by serpent swords. The song endures as both popular entertainment and a vehicle for preserving dynastic memory across social strata.
topic_desc_basic: Reign of the Septims is a popular mnemonic song listing many of Tamriel's historical Septim emperors. Versions range from coarse peasant verses to refined recitations for noble children. Bards and street performers commonly sing it for coin.

title: Daggerfall
topic_desc: Daggerfall is a major city and the capital of the eponymous kingdom within the Iliac Bay region of High Rock. Renowned as the jewel of the Bay, it stands as a prominent splendor at the gates of the west. As a leading power among the Breton kingdoms, the city commands significant political and economic influence throughout the region.
topic_desc_basic: Daggerfall is the capital of the Kingdom of Daggerfall in southwestern High Rock. Known as the jewel of the Iliac Bay, it is the largest city in the Glenumbra region and commands significant political and economic influence throughout the region.

title: Mournhold District
topic_desc: Mournhold District is one of the six administrative districts of the Imperial province of Morrowind. Occupying the heartland of the province, it houses the capital city of Mournhold-Almalexia, which also serves as House Indoril's capital. Largely under Indoril control, the district features a striking juxtaposition of verdant river valleys, particularly around the Aanthirin, and the scattered Mephalan Vales. It is home to the most holy city of the Tribunal Temple, Necrom, and its surrounding Sacred Lands. The Imperial bastion of Old Ebonheart, perhaps Morrowind's greatest Imperial city and seat of the Lord General of the Imperial Legion, also lies within its borders. The district is officially governed by the King of Morrowind, Hlaalu Helseth. The famed Dwemer ruins of Kemel-Ze are situated here as well.
topic_desc_basic: Mournhold District is one of the six administrative districts of Morrowind, occupying the provincial heartland. It contains the capital city of Mournhold-Almalexia, the holy city of Necrom, the Imperial bastion of Old Ebonheart, and the Dwemer ruins of Kemel-Ze. The district is officially governed by King Hlaalu Helseth.

title: Padomaic Isles
topic_desc: The Padomaic Isles are a collection of islands dotting the vast Padomaic Ocean. Cathnoquey, Yneslea, and Esroniet comprise the three largest archipelagos among them. Over a century ago, during his invasion of the Uttermost East, Uriel Septim V conquered each of these territories for the Empire.
topic_desc_basic: The Padomaic Isles are a collection of islands in the Padomaic Ocean. Their three largest archipelagos are Cathnoquey, Yneslea, and Esroniet, all of which were conquered for the Empire by Uriel Septim V over a century ago.

title: Velothi Tower
topic_desc: The Velothi Tower is one of two large apartment towers in St. Veloth Quarter, Narsis City, housing much of the city's lower-class population. The smaller of the quarter's two residential towers, it is owned by the Second Hlaalu Family.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Velothi Tower is.

title: Mysteries of the Worm
topic_desc: Mysteries of the Worm is a rare tome concerning advanced soul trap techniques and the raising of ancestral spirits who achieved great power in life. Copies have historically circulated among those dabbling in necromancy, prompting the Ordinators to hunt them down for destruction. Temple ordinance protects the book, and only the highest-ranking Temple masters in Necrom are permitted to possess and use it, and only on rare occasions. A copy is known to be stored in the vaults beneath the Council House in Port Telvannis. The Temple priests of Necrom guard the book's secrets closely, and those who have sought copies from unauthorized sources are reportedly not heard from again.
topic_desc_basic: Mysteries of the Worm is a rare tome on advanced soul trap techniques and raising powerful ancestral spirits. Temple ordinance forbids unauthorized possession; Ordinators hunt copies for destruction, and only the highest-ranking Temple masters in Necrom may use it.

title: Tel Thenim
topic_desc: Tel Thenim is a massive Telvanni tower dominating Port Telvannis.
