It serves as the residence of Archmagister Rilvin Dral, head of Great House Telvanni, though the Council House remains the seat of the faction's governance. The tower is divided into three sections: the Lower Tower, containing halls and a dining room accessible without levitation; the Upper Tower, featuring bedrooms and central halls with its highest reaches requiring levitation; and the Grandmaster's Chambers at the summit. Tel Thenim houses numerous powerful wizards and offers extensive magical services, including alchemists, spellmakers, a spell merchant, and an enchanter. The Archmagister's private quarters occupy the pinnacle of the tower.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Tel Thenim is.

title: Ayleid
topic_desc: A long-extinct race of mer that dominated central Tamriel for centuries. Their ruins are most densely concentrated in Cyrodiil, with sparse outliers located in western Morrowind and Black Marsh. Cyrodiil is considered the primary center for scholarly study of their civilization.
topic_desc_basic: The Ayleids, also called Heartland High Elves, were an ancient elven people whose ruined cities are found chiefly in Cyrodiil.

title: Reman
topic_desc: The name Reman denotes both the founding emperor of the Second Empire and the dynasty he established. Reman I, a Western Colovian king, united Cyrodiil and ended the Interregnum late in the First Era; he remains worshipped as a god-hero within the Empire. The Reman Dynasty persisted for two centuries, with Reman II expanding dominion westward and Reman III turning imperial ambition eastward. The assassination of Reman III by the Morag Tong terminated the dynasty and inaugurated the Second Era, after which Akaviri Potentates assumed rule. The Old Elvish epithet 'Light of Man' attaches to the name, and historical contention surrounds additional claimants to the title.
topic_desc_basic: The Reman Dynasty founded the Second Empire of Cyrodiil late in the First Era. Its founder, Reman I, united Cyrodiil and ended the Interregnum; he is still worshipped as a god-hero within the Empire. The dynasty lasted two centuries before the assassination of Reman III by the Morag Tong ended their rule and began the Second Era.

title: Malahk-Bazul
topic_desc: Malahk-Bazul is a large, isolated highland valley in the Velothi Mountains, situated at the tripoint where the borders of Morrowind, Skyrim, and Cyrodiil meet. A caravan route is said to pass through it, offering a theoretical overland passage toward Cyrodiil. In practice, the route is essentially impassable due to the presence of Malahk Orcs, making the valley far more notable for its danger than its utility as a trade corridor.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Malahk-Bazul is.

title: land dreugh
topic_desc: The land dreugh is a mature phase of the dreugh lifecycle, representing individuals that have migrated from deep aquatic habitats onto dry land. The exact evolutionary purpose of this transition remains uncertain, as dreugh reproduction apparently occurs entirely underwater. Scholars theorize the terrestrial period serves to harden the dreugh's carapace and strengthen its musculature. The phase may also act as a natural culling mechanism; while land dreugh possess sturdier shells than their aquatic counterparts, they are significantly more vulnerable to hunters on shore, allowing the elimination of weaker specimens.
topic_desc_basic: The land dreugh is a mature stage of the dreugh lifecycle. Dreugh begin life in deep water and eventually migrate onto dry land, where they grow larger and develop sturdier shells. They are more easily hunted on shore than in their aquatic phase.

title: Princess Morgiah
topic_desc: The Princess Morgiah is a three-masted Imperial Navy warship currently anchored at the docks of Ebonheart. Its sails bear the Navy's sea dragon symbol. The vessel serves as a notable presence in the waters of Morrowind's Inner Sea, representing the Empire's maritime military strength in the region.
topic_desc_basic: The Princess Morgiah is a three-masted Imperial Navy warship anchored at the Ebonheart docks. It bears the Navy's sea dragon symbol on its sails.

title: Treaty of the Four Score War
topic_desc: The Treaty of the Four Score War is a historical accord signed at the fortress of Ald Lambasi near Fervinthil during the First Era conflict between Morrowind and the Cyrodiilic Empire. Brokered between Prince Juilek and the Tribunal, it bears the signatures of all three Almsivi. Despite its divine provenance, the treaty failed to end the war; fighting continued until a later agreement was signed by Vivec in the Imperial City, following the deaths of Juilek, Indoril Dorom, and Emperor Reman III. Because it followed the Imperial capture of Ald Marak and preceded continued bloodshed, many Dunmer ascribe it little historical significance. Nevertheless, it is venerated as a holy relic proving the Tribunal walk among their people. The treaty is preserved beneath the dome at the Temple of Ald Iuval, seat of the Waters March.
topic_desc_basic: The Treaty of the Four Score War is a First Era accord between Morrowind and the Cyrodiilic Empire, signed at Ald Lambasi near Fervinthil. Though it failed to end the war, it is venerated as a holy relic bearing the signatures of all three Tribunes. It is preserved at the Temple of Ald Iuval.
tags: Treaty of the Four Score War

title: Office of Intercession
topic_desc: The Office of Intercession is a Tribunal Temple institution that receives pleas from those who believe they were wronged by Temple members or that Temple dogmas were misinterpreted or abused. Located in the canton plaza, it is headed by Andor Orothi, Canon of the Crossing. The Office examines whether actions accord with the sacred texts and decrees of the Almsivi and punishes the guilty where necessary, functioning as an internal doctrinal and disciplinary body within the Temple hierarchy.
topic_desc_basic: The Office of Intercession is a Tribunal Temple institution in the canton plaza. Headed by Canon Andor Orothi, it receives pleas from those who believe they were wronged by Temple members or that Temple dogmas were misinterpreted or abused, examining matters against the sacred texts and decrees of the Almsivi.

title: Wayrest
topic_desc: Wayrest is the trade capital of High Rock and its greatest city, situated on the shores of the Bjoulsae River. Renowned for its canals and cathedrals, it is the heart of Boullard culture and the Breton ideal. The city's ancient institutions provide enduring stability, even as Queen Elysana steers the realm toward imperial ambition and potential calamity. Wayrest's prominence extends across the Iliac Bay; a prince of Wayrest notably fought alongside northern warriors during the War of the Bend'r-mahk, subsequently facilitating a knighthood for a Jehanna companion through his brother, the king. The city's wealth and influence make it a destination for those seeking to capitalize on wartime fortunes.
topic_desc_basic: Wayrest is the trade capital of High Rock and its greatest city, located at the mouth of the Bjoulsae River on the Iliac Bay. Renowned for its canals and cathedrals, it is the heart of Breton culture and a destination for those seeking wealth.

title: Ebonarm
topic_desc: Reymon Ebonarm, a First Era mortal warrior who achieved godhood and is still worshipped in the present day.
topic_desc_basic: Reymon Ebonarm is the God of War and protector of warriors. A First Era mortal who achieved godhood through legendary deeds, he is worshipped at shrines called Anvils of Ebonarm throughout the Iliac Bay region.

title: Sundered Scar
topic_desc: Sundered Scar is a marshland region along the southern coastline of the Inner Sea within the Mournhold District. Historically known as the Inlet Bog, it borders the Mephalan Vales to the north and east, Lan Orethan to the south, and Aanthirin to the west. Under Tribunal rule, the Indoril transformed Morrowind, but the seat associated with House Mora remained empty by tradition, filled only in name by the spirit of Indoril Nerevar. Left neglected while neighboring regions flourished, the land became an unacknowledged scar in the heart of Morrowind. Today, it is a dangerous bog where packs of beasts prey on lost travelers. Despite its perilous wilderness, the Scar holds scattered settlements like the fishing village of Darvonis, alongside submerged Dunmer strongholds, Dwemer ruins, and Daedric shrines.
topic_desc_basic: Sundered Scar is a marshland region along the southern coast of the Inner Sea in the Mournhold District. Once called the Inlet Bog, it is a neglected and dangerous bog where packs of beasts prey on lost travelers.

title: Clavicus Vile
topic_desc: Clavicus Vile, the Child-God of the Morningstar, is a Daedric Prince whose spheres encompass mockery, oath-breaking, and wish fulfillment. Worshipped in Cyrodiil since the Mythic Age, he serves as patron of merchants and traders, and his cult holds considerable influence over the East Empire Company's board of directors. The Little Key Cult, a powerful merchant religion, exerts substantial sway over Cyrodiil's trade routes and emphasizes serenity through wealth. Imperial marketplaces traditionally bear the sign of the dog in his honor. In Summerset Isle, where Imperial mercantilism has made little headway, Vile is regarded as an enemy god who has tested the Altmer people's resolve repeatedly. The Direnni merchant house stands as a notable Altmer exception, having produced summoners who sought profitable negotiation with the Lord of License.
topic_desc_basic: Clavicus Vile is a Daedric Prince of mockery, oath-breaking, and wish fulfillment. Widely venerated in Cyrodiil as a patron of merchants and traders since the Mythic Age, his cult wields significant influence over the East Empire Company.

title: Ebon Tower
topic_desc: The Ebon Tower is the castle at the heart of Old Ebonheart, serving as the Imperial Legion's headquarters in Morrowind. It formerly housed the seat of the Duke of Vvardenfell prior to the island's opening for colonization, and remains home to numerous Imperial and Dunmer authorities overseeing Vvardenfell affairs. Constructed as one of the first buildings after Indoril Raathim burned Ebonheart to the ground, its layout deliberately mimics the Imperial City. The tower's prominent bell calls the faithful to service and is audible far beyond the city, while the structure itself is visible across the region on clear days. Subterranean sewers connect to the Legion prison and the Duke's treasure chamber; trespassing in these passages is a capital offense.
topic_desc_basic: The Ebon Tower is the castle in Old Ebonheart, visible across the region and audible from even further via its prominent bell. It serves as the Imperial Legion's Morrowind headquarters and formerly housed the seat of the Duke of Vvardenfell before the island's colonization.

title: Cathay-raht
topic_desc: Cathay-raht are a breed of Khajiit, widely regarded as among the most powerful of their kind. They serve the Mane as warriors and guards. Other races commonly refer to them as the jaguar-men.
topic_desc_basic: Cathay-raht are a powerful breed of Khajiit from Elsweyr, commonly called the jaguar-men by other races. They serve the Mane as warriors and guards.

title: Kragenmoor
topic_desc: Kragenmoor is a major settlement and one of the largest holds of House Hlaalu, second only to Narsis in size. It is situated in the northwest Othreleth Woods, south of the Morrowind interior, near the Shadowgate Pass on the border to Cyrodiil.
topic_desc_basic: Kragenmoor is one of the largest holds of House Hlaalu, second only to Narsis. It lies in the northwest Othreleth Woods, near the Shadowgate Pass on the border to Cyrodiil.

title: Death Mask of Empress Katariah
topic_desc: The Death Mask is a funerary artifact interred with Empress Katariah I upon her death, when her remains were returned to the city of her ancestors. It was sealed within her burial chamber in the Raathim Ancestral Tomb beneath Old Ebonheart. The tomb is protected by a stone guardian that denies entry to those lacking Raathim blood, and the sarcophagus is secured by a mechanism that can trap intruders. The mask holds significant value to the Empire; its recovery is considered a matter of prestige, sufficient to warrant pardons for serious crimes in exchange for its return. It is destined for display in the Palace of the Ebon Tower.
topic_desc_basic: The Death Mask of Empress Katariah I is a funerary artifact sealed with her remains in the Raathim Ancestral Tomb beneath Old Ebonheart. The Imperial government considers it a prestigious relic of considerable value to the Empire.

title: Ebony Blade
topic_desc: The Ebony Blade is a Daedric artifact associated with Mephala, the Daedric Prince of lies, secrets, and murder. Also called Mephala's Blade, it is a weapon deeply tied to deception and betrayal. The blade's power is not static; it can diminish during prolonged periods without a wielder. Devotees of Mephala can commune with the Prince to restore the weapon to its true potency, a process that strengthens the artifact for those Mephala's web holds a greater purpose. It is wielded in Mephala's name, serving as an instrument of her will.
topic_desc_basic: The Ebony Blade, also called the Vampire or the Leech, is a Daedric artifact created by Mephala. Resembling an ebony katana, it steals the life essence of those it strikes and is widely feared as a weapon of great evil that corrupts and drives its wielders insane.

title: Helnim
topic_desc: Helnim is an Imperial settlement in the Dagon Urul region of Telvannis District, situated on Zafirbel Bay. Founded as an entrepôt of the Zafirbel Bay Company, it serves as the Empire's principal trading connection with House Telvanni, exploiting the relative openness of the neighboring Tel Gilan councilor to outlander commerce. The Census and Excise Office at the docks regulates the outflow of Telvanni goods, bug musk in particular. Regular boat traffic connects Helnim to Firewatch, Marog, Sadrith Mora, and Darvonis. The town maintains a Legion garrison at Fort Servas, Mages and Fighters Guild chapters, an Imperial Cult chapel dedicated to Kynareth, and an Imperial Archaeological Society presence. The Zafirbel Bay Company's local Factor wields considerable civic influence alongside the Telvanni lord of Tel Gilan, whose reach extends across the settlement. The cyclopean ruins of Kemel-Ze lie across the bay, with several Dwemer sites clustered nearby.
topic_desc_basic: Helnim is an Imperial trading town on Zafirbel Bay in Telvannis District, serving as the Empire's main commercial link to House Telvanni. Founded by the Zafirbel Bay Company near the Telvanni tower of Tel Gilan, it handles the export of Telvanni goods such as bug musk. Boat services connect it to Firewatch, Marog, and Sadrith Mora.

title: War of Lies
topic_desc: The War of Lies was a military conflict between Firewatch and Old Ebonheart roughly three decades ago. Casik, then the head of all Imperial Legions in Morrowind, committed treason by marshaling a large navy and invading the territory of the Duchess of Firewatch. The campaign proved devastating; the Duchess and most of the Order of Firewatch perished, and significant casualties occurred at Nivalis, whose damage remains visible. Following the war's conclusion, Commander Rufus restored order to Firewatch. The conflict's lingering aftermath continues to affect the region.
topic_desc_basic: The War of Lies was a war between Firewatch and Old Ebonheart some thirty-odd years ago. The conflict caused lasting issues for the region and left visible damage at Nivalis.

title: The Silvenar
topic_desc: The Silvenar serves as the de facto High King and spiritual ruler of Valenwood, acting as a physical manifestation of the Bosmeri people. This unique bond means the Silvenar literally embodies the collective will and temperament of all Bosmer, from Yokuda to Akavir; if the people are loyal, the Silvenar is loyal, and if treacherous, the Silvenar is treacherous. This profound connection creates inherent challenges when the population's attitudes are divided, forcing the Silvenar to rely upon advisors and lesser kings to navigate hard decisions during such periods of internal fracture. The city of Silvenar shares the ruler's name. Despite the office's exalted nature, administrative records from the capital note the Silvenar's notoriously poor penmanship.
topic_desc_basic: The Silvenar is the spiritual king and de facto High King of Valenwood, serving as a physical manifestation of the Bosmer people. He embodies their collective will and temperament, and the city of Silvenar shares his name.

title: blighted queen
topic_desc: A kwama queen at the Tel Gilan eggmine, northwest of the settlement, that has contracted blight disease. The affliction has halted the mine's egg production, as miners refuse to work near the infected creature. The condition can be remedied by application of a cure blight effect, restoring the queen to health and allowing normal operations to resume. The queen is named Disela in some accounts, though this may conflate the creature with the Director who commissioned its treatment. The blight's origin is attributed to contact from Vvardenfell. The creature's survival is essential to the mine's economic function, as the queen is the sole source of kwama eggs for the operation.
topic_desc_basic: A kwama queen at the Tel Gilan eggmine that has contracted blight disease. The infection has halted egg production, as miners refuse to work near the creature. The queen is the sole source of eggs for the mine.

title: King of Worms
topic_desc: The King of Worms is the self-appointed title of Mannimarco, who claims both necromantic mastery over decomposition and a form of temporal authority over worm-kind. Sload tradition holds that Mannimarco aided the Empire in sinking Thras during the First Age, after which the surviving Sload allegedly swore him fealty—a claim regarded as doubtful. He is acknowledged as king or god of some worms, though not all. His titles remain self-proclaimed rather than universally recognized.
topic_desc_basic: The King of Worms is the self-proclaimed title of Mannimarco, a notorious lich and the founder of the Worm Cult. Expelled from the Psijic Order for necromancy, he became Tamriel's most powerful necromancer and a lasting enemy of the Mages Guild.

title: Othreleth Woods
topic_desc: The Othreleth Woods form the autumn-like western highlands that serve as the heartlands of House Hlaalu within the Narsis District. The region is characterized by great mushroom forests and the downpour of the Kanit River, which—along with other tributaries—flows south and east to meet the Thirr River at Lake Coronati in the Coronati Basin. Its largest settlement is Kragenmoor in the northwest. The woods border the Armun Ashlands to the north, the Velothi Mountains to the northwest, Shipal-Shin to the south, and the Coronati Basin to the east. The landscape hosts hackle-lo plantations, small farms, ancestral tombs, and shrines to Daedric Princes such as Molag Bal and Malacath.
topic_desc_basic: The Othreleth Woods are an autumn-like region in the western highlands of Morrowind's Narsis District. Serving as the heartlands of House Hlaalu, the area is known for its great mushroom forests and the Kanit River. It lies south of the Armun Ashlands and east of the Velothi Mountains, with Kragenmoor as its largest settlement.

title: Nedothril Coast
topic_desc: The Nedothril Coast is a stretch of grassland and cliffs along the Sea of Ghosts in eastern Mournhold District, lying between the Lan Orethan and the sea. Less vegetated than the Lan Orethan but fertile, it serves as a transitional zone where most seaborne commerce bypasses its shores in favor of the Orethan river system or House Dres ports. The island of Nan Iban is its most notable landmark. Main settlements include the villages of Seitur and Enamor Dayn, with Sailen located near its northern extent. Paths from the coast lead north toward Necrom and Telvannis District, and south toward Bosmora. Despite its location within Great House Indoril territory, the coast is a sparsely populated rocky expanse; the true Indoril heartland lies further west along the Orethan river system.
topic_desc_basic: The Nedothril Coast runs along the Sea of Ghosts in eastern Mournhold District, a fertile but sparsely settled strip between the Lan Orethan and the ocean. Small villages such as Seitur and Enamor Dayn lie along its shore. The island of Nan Iban is its chief landmark.

title: the Armistice
topic_desc: The Armistice is the treaty that ended hostilities between Morrowind and the Empire at the close of the Second Era, signed by Vivec and Tiber Septim. Because both signatories are revered as gods—Vivec by the Dunmer and Talos by the Imperial cult—the pact carries divine authority for both peoples. The document displayed in Imperial custody is alleged by some to be a forgery, its text illegible, giving rise to disputes over the treaty's true wording and authenticity.
topic_desc_basic: The Armistice is the divine pact that ended hostilities between Morrowind and the Empire at the end of the Second Era. Signed by the living god Vivec and Tiber Septim, who became Talos, it holds divine authority for both the Dunmer and the Empire.

title: Elysana
topic_desc: Elysana is the ruling Queen of Wayrest, governing through corruption and deceit, and is widely feared in the courts of High Rock. Known as the Queen of the Boulland, her ambition has only grown since the Warp in the West. She is suspected of maintaining an extensive intelligence network with eyes in Morrowind, extending her influence beyond the borders of her kingdom.
topic_desc_basic: Elysana is the ruling Queen of Wayrest, widely known as the Queen of the Boulland. She governs through corruption and deceit and is greatly feared throughout the courts of High Rock. Her ambition has only grown since the Warp in the West, and she is suspected of maintaining an extensive intelligence network with eyes even in Morrowind.

title: The Blue Divide
topic_desc: The Blue Divide is the oceanic strait separating the Summerset Isles from mainland Tamriel. This maritime expanse forms a natural barrier between the Altmer's insular homeland and the continental coastlines, historically shaping the naval and political dynamics of the western seas.
topic_desc_basic: The Blue Divide is the strip of sea separating the Summerset Isles from mainland Tamriel, lying between the Abecean Sea and the Southern Sea.

title: Syffim
topic_desc: The Syffim was the Akaviri predecessor to the Fighters Guild, founded by Dinieras-Ves, who established the tenets of Syffa Temet Kai. Formed as hired arms for noble lords following a ban on private armies, the organization evolved into the modern guild. Its legacy persists most strongly in old Cyrodiilic chapters, particularly in Nibenay, where high-ranking members of the old guard value Akaviri serpent blood and political influence in their hierarchy. Serpent Hall in Cyrodiil City serves as their headquarters, with major chapters in Bravil and Cheydinhal. The Tsaesci word denotes a warrior. Traditionalist Syffim philosophy overvalues the counsel of noble patrons, creating friction between chapters whose clients oppose one another—a practice some guildhalls, like Narsis, deliberately reject.
topic_desc_basic: The Syffim was the Akaviri predecessor to the Fighters Guild, formed as hired arms for nobles after a ban on private armies. Its traditions endure in old Cyrodiilic chapters, particularly in Nibenay, where high-ranking members value Akaviri heritage and noble patronage.

title: Temple law
topic_desc: Temple law encompasses the religious statutes and legal codes upheld by the Tribunal Temple across its sphere of influence in Morrowind. It governs spiritual practice, social rites, and civic order, strictly prohibiting practices such as necromancy. Temple priests confer blessings that legitimize significant social contracts, including lawful marriage, which can alter political alignments and override secular House authority. However, its jurisdiction is not absolute; Imperial law supersedes it within districts governed by the Empire, such as Old Ebonheart, creating a complex dual legal framework. This duality allows practices forbidden under Temple doctrine to operate legally under Imperial protection, though adherents often express respect for Temple beliefs to avoid offense.
topic_desc_basic: Temple law is the religious and legal code upheld by the Tribunal Temple in Morrowind. It governs spiritual and civic order, strictly forbidding practices like necromancy. Temple priests bless significant social contracts, such as marriages that can override secular House authority. However, Imperial law supersedes Temple law in Empire-governed districts like Old Ebonheart.

title: Coronati Basin
topic_desc: The Coronati Basin is a region in the Narsis District of Morrowind characterized by a distinct yellow-orange landscape. Lake Coronati fills the valley's center, fed by the Thirr River flowing north from Narsis. The lake's shallow edges are choked with mangrove parasols, and its relatively rich shoreline soil supports numerous plantations. This fertility quickly gives way to drier grasslands and increasingly rocky, cliff-cut slopes further from the water. The basin borders Aanthirin to the north, the Armun Ashlands to the northwest, the Othreleth Woods to the west, Shipal-Shin to the south, and the Deshaan Plains to the east. Its largest settlements are Othmura and Hlerynhul. The region contains diverse sites including Daedric shrines, Dreugh hives, Dunmer strongholds, and Redoran ruins, reflecting a long and varied habitation history.
topic_desc_basic: The Coronati Basin is a yellow-orange region in the Narsis District of Morrowind. Lake Coronati sits in its center, with the Thirr River flowing north from Narsis. The lake's shores feature mangrove parasols and fertile soil that supports many plantations, though the land grows drier and rockier further from the water.

title: Icebreaker Keep
topic_desc: Icebreaker Keep is an Imperial Navy fortress situated along the Sea of Ghosts. The small Imperial colony of Nivalis shelters in its shadow. The keep serves as a strategic maritime outpost, housing a garrison under the command of Tibera Rone. It also hosts a Mages Guild outpost headed by Dagmund Wind-Whisker, providing guild guide services to the remote installation. The fortress features a dock tower and curtain wall defenses befitting its naval alignment, alongside a smithy to support its operations.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Icebreaker Keep is.

title: Dremora Lord
topic_desc: A high-ranking Kyn, the proud and warlike Dremora who serve the Daedric Princes of Oblivion. Organized into rigidly stratified clans, Dremora Lords command lesser ranks and possess formidable martial and magical power. Their souls are exceptionally potent, making them prized offerings in Daedric rituals; summoners seeking to bridge planes specifically require the energy only a Lord can provide. Dremora Lords occasionally manifest on Nirn by inhabiting mineral deposits, sometimes emerging from precious stones or at void-shrines to torment mortals. Summoning or confronting one demands great strength, as they disdain weak opponents.
topic_desc_basic: A high-ranking Dremora serving the Daedric Princes. Dremora Lords command lesser Kyn and wield formidable martial and magical power. They occasionally manifest on Nirn by inhabiting mineral deposits or emerging at void-shrines to torment mortals.

title: Aalmu Ouradas' Shack
topic_desc: Aalmu Ouradas' Shack is a small molecrab farmstead in the Aanthirin region, located southeast of Gol Mok. The shack serves as the dwelling of Aalmu Ouradas, a Dunmer herder, and is accompanied by an adjacent molecrab paddock. The interior stores numerous molecrab shells along with components of Telvanni molecrab armor. The paddock outside houses the farm's molecrab population.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Aalmu Ouradas' Shack is.

title: Abammu Grotto
topic_desc: Abammu Grotto is a small cave in the Dagon Urul region of Molag Amur, situated a short distance east of Tel Oren. The grotto consists of a single chamber containing a deep pool. A solitary blue beetle inhabits the cave. The remains of a dead adventurer, still burdened with armor and equipment, lie within, and a chest rests submerged in the pool. The grotto otherwise holds no particular historical or cultural significance.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Abammu Grotto is.

title: Abandoned Egg Mine
topic_desc: The Abandoned Egg Mine, formally recorded as Turan-Habinat Egg Mine, is a disused kwama egg mine situated in the Lan Orethan region. While largely unremarkable, its tunnels still contain standard kwama egg sacs and active kwama. A notable flooded section of the mine has breached a buried Dunmer ruin. An exposed pillar within this submerged area holds a gold dagger, and a skeleton resting at the bottom of the underground lake clutches a dreugh club and a pearl, suggesting a violent or fateful encounter in the depths.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Abandoned Egg Mine is.

title: Abandoned Shack
topic_desc: A small, isolated shack on a hill in the Molag Ruhn region, far from any settlement. Its last inhabitant never departed, but remains inside as a corpse resting in a hammock. Scattered ingredients and a repair hammer are the only contents of note.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Abandoned Shack is.

title: Acre of Saint Meris
topic_desc: The Acre of Saint Meris is a small farm situated in the Sacred Lands region. It serves as the home of Indrys and Sathys Norvayn, two Tribunal Temple initiates. Indrys practices alchemy on the grounds, while Sathys resides inside the dwelling. The site's dedication to Saint Meris reflects the religious character of its inhabitants and its situation within the Temple's sphere of influence.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Acre of Saint Meris is.

title: Adadpaliki
topic_desc: Adadpaliki is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Molag Bal in the Sunad Mora region. The ruin serves as a haven for vampires, who have used contaminated provisions to covertly spread their affliction among the unsuspecting populace. You do not know where Adadpaliki is.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Adadpaliki is.

title: Adammuburtu
topic_desc: Adammuburtu is a cavern in the Roth Roryn region notable for its exposed veins of ruby ore. The cave currently serves as the headquarters of the Ruby Pond Boys, a band of rogues who exploit the site's mineral wealth. The gang's activities include impersonating Imperial Legion soldiers; they wear uniforms stripped from two Legion corpses now present within the cavern, using the disguise to extract fraudulent tolls from travelers. The cave is inhabited by nix-hounds and the gang's members, including the Imperial Bossman Colennus and the Dunmer Nalus. The presence of the slain Legion personnel makes the site a matter of concern for Imperial forces.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Adammuburtu is.

title: Adanibi Grotto
topic_desc: Adanibi Grotto is a sizable coastal cave situated on the south shore of a larger island northeast of Aegondo Point, within the Sea of Ghosts. The surrounding waters host numerous small islands. The grotto interior holds little of notable value, sheltering only sea creatures and four pearl-bearing kollops. A solitary skeleton within the cave lies beside a wooden buckler and an iron broadsword, suggesting a past maritime fatality. Potions facilitating underwater navigation rest inside, though the site offers no other significant features.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Adanibi Grotto is.

title: Adavrin Egg Mine
topic_desc: Adavrin Egg Mine is the kwama egg mine serving Adavrin Plantation, situated in the Shipal-Shin region just across the road from the plantation gate. Like many Hlaalu-owned mining operations, it relies heavily on slave labor, with Argonian and Khajiit captives providing the bulk of the workforce alongside paid Dunmer miners. The mine's day-to-day Hlaalu administration is overseen by retainers and lawmen of the House. As an active egg mine, it produces kwama eggs for the plantation's commercial export.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Adavrin Egg Mine is.

title: Adavrin Plantation
topic_desc: Adavrin Plantation is a large agricultural estate in southern Shipal-Shin, situated on the main road running east from Stormgate Pass. It is owned by Ilethi Adavrin of House Hlaalu. The arid climate of the region precludes extensive crop cultivation, so the plantation's wealth derives primarily from netch ranching and the nearby Adavrin Egg Mine. The estate includes a manor, workers' housing, and slave quarters, reflecting a substantial Dunmer agricultural operation. The Adavrin family holds several positions within House Hlaalu, indicating the plantation's role as a seat of a minor Hlaalu-aligned noble household.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Adavrin Plantation is.

title: Addai Mine
topic_desc: Addai Mine is an ebony mine situated deep within the Armun Ashlands, lying east of the Daedric ruin Balititashpi along the road connecting Bodrum and Kragenmoor. The operation relies on slave labor, and its entrance is secured by armed bear traps and a locked door, though it remains unclear whether these measures are intended to keep intruders out or to prevent the enslaved miners from escaping. Despite these precautions, the mine's security is compromised: bandits from the nearby cave of Marananit have excavated a connecting passage into the rear of the mine, enabling them to siphon off ebony ore undetected by the front guard.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Addai Mine is.

title: Adhuhartis
topic_desc: Adhuhartis is a small cave situated on the southern shore of the island directly south of the Mundrethi Plantation slave market in the Aanthirin region. The cave serves as a smugglers' hideout, currently holding captive slaves. A copy of the skill book Last Scabbard of Akrash rests beneath a table near the bedrolls, alongside a slave key.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Adhuhartis is.

title: Adosi Rothari's Shack
topic_desc: Adosi Rothari's Shack is an isolated dwelling in the Molag Ruhn region, near Ranyon-ruhn. The structure belongs to a local guar herder, though its owner typically remains outside tending to crops rather than occupying the interior. The shack holds little of note; its storage sacks and baskets contain only common foodstuffs and basic ingredients, reflecting the modest subsistence of its inhabitant.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Adosi Rothari's Shack is.

title: Adryn Ancestral Tomb
topic_desc: Adryn Ancestral Tomb is a small Dunmer ancestral burial site situated in the Aanthirin region, south-southwest of Indal-ruhn. Its original entrance has become buried beneath the earth, leaving the tomb accessible only through the cave of Kanasami. The tomb contains no treasure of note, yet its ancestral guardians remain fiercely vigilant over the interior. Whatever living descendants the Adryn lineage retains have permitted the original entry to remain obstructed, though the undead protectors continue their eternal watch within the sealed halls.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Adryn Ancestral Tomb is.

title: Adunji
topic_desc: Adunji is a smugglers' cave located in the Sunad Mora region, south of Baldrahn and the Dwemer ruins of Nchazdrumn, with its entrance situated on a low hillside. The cave serves as a secure lair for a band of three outlaws who enforce their claim ruthlessly; the pinned and impaled remains of a past trespasser serve as a grim warning. The interior holds typical contraband, including plentiful moon sugar and Cyrodiilic brandy, alongside assorted weapons and armor stored in crates.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Adunji is.

title: Adursaranit
topic_desc: Adursaranit is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Molag Bal, situated in the Othreleth Woods west of the Thirr River's westernmost bend. The ruin consists of two distinct zones: the Outer Shrine and the Inner Shrine. The site is occupied by Molag Bal's cultists and summoned Daedra. The Inner Shrine houses notable arms, including an ebony dagger, and holds the remains of the crusader Dralnas Virian.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Adursaranit is.

title: Aegondo Point
topic_desc: Aegondo Point is a cape at the northern tip of Sunad Mora, northeast of Tel Ouada, jutting into the Sea of Ghosts. It is revered as the site where the Tribunal defeated the Underking in battle, making it an ancient place of worship. A Daedric ruin dedicated to Boethiah and Sheogorath stands on the cape, and the pilgrimage site lies at its south side. The Shrine of Foresight is situated there, where pilgrims traditionally offer gravedust. The cape also contains Dim-Dai, a grotto beneath a waterfall on the eastern coastline. Daedric creatures roam the ruin's exterior, and bandits frequent the area.
topic_desc_basic: Aegondo Point is a cape at the northern tip of Sunad Mora, northeast of Tel Ouada, jutting into the Sea of Ghosts. It is a traditional pilgrimage site associated with the Tribunal's defeat of the Underking.

title: Age of Peace
topic_desc: The Age of Peace is a trading vessel currently docked at Hlerynhul in the Coronati Basin for provisions. The ship is divided into three interior zones: a cabin, a lower level, and an upper level. Its cargo consists primarily of food and clothing, offering little of value to thieves. The vessel's crew is led by Shipmaster Vasesius Lannus. The resupply effort has been hindered by the disappearance of two sailors dispatched to procure goods.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Age of Peace is.

title: Aharnat
topic_desc: Aharnat is a cavern situated at the southern edge of the Othreleth Woods, where the tree line gives way to the deserts of Shipal-Shin. The cave serves as a refuge for a small band of outlaws, including Khajiit, Wood Elf, and Imperial members, who eke out a marginal existence within. Its proximity to the Daedric Shrine of Kalkusara, southwest of Edalvel Plantation, marks its general vicinity. The occupants are poorly equipped and share their dwelling with rats, suggesting the site holds no notable wealth or strategic importance. Aharnat remains a minor, obscure hideout of little consequence beyond its role as shelter for those evading civilized authority in the region.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Aharnat is.

title: Ahhepu
topic_desc: Ahhepu is a cave in the Shipal-Shin region that serves as a Camonna Tong base of operations. Situated east of Narsis, its entrance lies along a narrow canyon between the Old Dren and Vedas plantations, northeast of the Daedric shrine of Ebamasharisus. The Tong maintains a garrison of Dunmer rogues, assassins, nightblades, and sorcerers within its single zone, alongside a modest cache of equipment.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ahhepu is.

title: Ahhesha
topic_desc: Ahhesha is a small cave situated in the region of Boethiah's Spine, in the lands surrounding Necrom. The cave lies north of the Dwemer ruins of Mzungleft. Its interior branches into three passages: one leading to a slave pen, another descending into a submerged section where pearl-bearing kollops dwell and providing a connecting route to the cave's northern reaches, and a third opening onto a bandit encampment. Beyond these features, the cave holds little of notable value.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ahhesha is.

title: Aimmund
topic_desc: Aimmund is a crystalline cavern in the Aanthirin region, situated atop the hill west of Idathren. The cave's numerous sparkling crystals suggest past magical usage, though the only evidence of mortal habitation is a lone skeleton and its remaining supplies. A Storm Atronach currently lairs within the cavern, posing a significant hazard to any who enter.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Aimmund is.

title: Aimrah
topic_desc: Aimrah is a small Velothi town on the northern shore of Lake Andaram in the Aanthirin region, paying fealty to Indoril Beroth of Nanaav. Despite its humble size, it serves as a vital Great House Indoril trade hub, handling goods shipped to and from the Dres lands across the lake. Most residents work in fishing or shipping. The atmosphere is notoriously chilly and unwelcoming to outsiders, a suspicion perhaps rooted in memory of the Arnesian War, when Argonian rebels ravaged the lands south of the lake. Fog frequently shrouds the settlement, though clear days offer views across waters concealing a high density of Dreugh. Services are limited to the Sailors' Inn, a few street stalls, and a potions shop. Transport connects Aimrah to Almas Thirr and Vhul via silt strider, and to the Maar-Bani Crossing by boat.
topic_desc_basic: Aimrah is a small Velothi town on the northern shore of Lake Andaram. It serves as a Great House Indoril trade hub for goods shipped to and from the Dres lands across the lake. Most residents work in fishing or shipping. The town is connected to Almas Thirr and Vhul by silt strider, and to the Maar-Bani Crossing by boat.

title: Aimur Grotto
topic_desc: Aimur Grotto is a submerged cavern in Lake Andaram, situated within the Aanthirin region. Its entrance rests on the lakebed between the settlements of Aimrah and Nav Andaram, lying closer to the latter's shore. The grotto is a known habitat for Dreugh and kollops, alongside slaughterfish, and yields plentiful pearls. Several air pockets within the cave system permit divers to surface briefly, making exploration of the depths reasonably manageable for well-prepared swimmers.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Aimur Grotto is.

title: Akuband
topic_desc: Akuband is a Dwemer ruin concealed within the cavern of Mansurabi in the Alt Orethan region. The site is distinguished by its second zone, designated the Test of Disorder, which features a complex mechanical puzzle. This apparatus requires sustaining a continuous chain reaction of moving blocks to unlock a sealed door. The architecture demonstrates the Dwemer propensity for intricate kinetic mechanisms and protective sealing systems. Beyond the puzzle-locked barrier lies a substantial repository of cached goods, including the unique Prismatic Shield, while a smaller side chamber secured by a conventional lock holds additional stores. The ruin's interior is devoid of active constructs or other guardians.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Akuband is.

title: Alayepi's Tent
topic_desc: Alayepi's Tent is a dwelling in the Shipal-Shin region, situated east of Ussiran Camp and connected to it by a rope bridge. It serves as the home of Alayepi, a Dark Elf barbarian of the Shinathi culture who holds the rank of Hearthfriend within the Ussiran clan.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Alayepi's Tent is.

title: Ald Balaal
topic_desc: Ald Balaal is a sprawling Daedric ruin dedicated to Molag Bal, situated in the Armun Ashlands. The site comprises three interconnected interior zones: the Shrine, the Halls of Woe, and the Vault, alongside the cavern system of Verenabi. The exterior features a southwestern tower; its upper entrance leads directly into the Shrine, while the ground-level entrance accesses the Halls of Woe. Verenabi connects to the interior from the west. The ruin is infested with numerous Daedra. Its vaults contain notable treasures, including a Daedric Scimitar, an Adamantium Staff, and rare skill texts such as 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 18 and Palla, Book II.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ald Balaal is.

title: Ald Erfoud
topic_desc: Ald Erfoud is a complex of ruins reflecting Arvud's Redoran heritage, situated beneath Uvayn Manor and accessible through the nearby Nan-Assali cave. The site dates to at least the First Era, as it is referenced in historical accounts of Reman III's reign. Relics of the Second Empire, including a Reman Legion helmet and coins, attest to its occupation during that period. The ruin's last known ruler, Firolen Ervanys, persists in spectral form; in life, he was noted for his hatred of vampires and kept the ashes of a Baluath clan ancient. Undead, including skeletal champions and war-wizards, currently inhabit the chambers. A vault at the northern end holds notable arms and armor, including an ebony shield, ebony halberd, and a Redoran ceremonial blade.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ald Erfoud is.

title: Ald Iuval
topic_desc: Ald Iuval is the dilapidated capital of the Waters March and one of the last House Redoran settlements in the Coronati Basin. It stands on the shores of Lake Coronati, northeast of Hlerynhul, and alongside its twin settlement Ald Marak guards the Thirr River where it exits the lake. The capital's influence and economy have long been in decline, and surrounding lands now fall largely under House Hlaalu sway. The settlement is filled with ruins of abandoned houses and paupers made destitute through economic displacement or rejection by House Hlaalu. Prouder traditions persist: the local Tribunal Temple still provides ministry, and a Morag Tong branch still accepts writs. The settlement retains a Redoran Council Hall and is governed by the acting Lord of the Waters March.
topic_desc_basic: Ald Iuval is a declining House Redoran town on the shores of Lake Coronati in the Coronati Basin, northeast of Hlerynhul. It is the capital of the Waters March and, with its twin Ald Marak, guards the Thirr River. The surrounding lands have largely fallen under House Hlaalu influence.

title: Ald Khan
topic_desc: Ald Khan is a holy site of the Tribunal Temple commemorating a union between Vivec and Molag Bal. The shrine looms over the headwaters of the Thirr River, situated halfway between Stormgate Pass and Shipal-Sharai in the Shipal-Shin region. Despite its dedication to a Daedric Lord, Ordinators and Temple members staff the interior, maintaining the complex and providing services to pilgrims. The site consists of at least two distinct zones: the Outer Halls and the Shrine. Though occupied by the Temple, the shrine retains traces of its Daedric origins, including unclaimed Daedric artifacts on the shrine's highest level.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ald Khan is.

title: Ald Marak
topic_desc: Ald Marak is the smaller twin settlement of Ald Iuval, together forming the remnant of the Waters March—a once vast territory under Great House Redoran's control. Though still commanded by Redoran lords, the march's influence has waned; a silver mine that once fed its coffers has been lost to bandits, and Ald Marak is now considered a backwater. The settlement retains its traditional role of guarding the horns, the entrance to Lake Coronati, periodically inspecting ships such as the Thirrine Lily. Ald Marak's commander, Delis Llethri, is more willing than her superior in Ald Iuval to antagonize House Hlaalu and actively reclaim lost territory. Nearby landmarks include the mage tower of Rallabala and the Daedric shrine of Bessarnamidan.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ald Marak is.

title: Ald Mirathi
topic_desc: Ald Mirathi is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Mehrunes Dagon, standing on the western shore of Lake Boethiah in the Boethiah's Spine region of mainland Morrowind. The shrine lies a short distance south of Hla Bulor. Within its interior, a statue of the Daedra Prince dominates the main chamber, and offerings are arrayed upon an altar before it. The site draws Daedra and their cultist worshippers, who maintain devotions to the Prince of Destruction. The shrine's contents are typical of Daedric sanctuaries across Morrowind, including ritual offerings of precious stones and daedric components left in tribute before Dagon's likeness.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ald Mirathi is.

title: Ald Niripal
topic_desc: Ald Niripal is a Daedric shrine dedicated to the Prince Azura, situated within the Alt Orethan region. The complex consists of three distinct zones: the Outer Halls, the Shrine, and the Flooded Chamber. As a site of Daedric veneration, it hosts both Daedra and cultists within its confines. The shrine's architecture and flooded lower areas reflect the typical construction and enduring nature of such Daedric sites of worship devoted to Azura.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ald Niripal is.

title: Ald Uman
topic_desc: Ald Uman is a Daedric shrine dedicated to the Prince Malacath, situated beneath the small House Redoran village of Uman on the edge of the Velothi Mountains. The site consists of two interior zones: the Shrine and the Inner Shrine, which includes a Sepulcher and an Antechamber. The shrine is occupied by a band of Orcish worshipers and their undead servants. A statue of Malacath stands within the Sepulcher, and a Glass Shardsword rests upon its altar.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ald Uman is.

title: Ald Uran
topic_desc: Ald Uran is a Daedric shrine dedicated to the Prince Mephala, situated in the Lan Orethan region. The complex consists of three distinct zones: the Outer Halls, the Ruined Passages, and the Shrine of the Webspinner. As a site devoted to the Webspinner, it serves as a locus for Mephala's cultists and summoned Daedra. The structural division into ruined passages and an inner shrine suggests a site of considerable age, where active worship persists alongside decayed architecture.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ald Uran is.
aliases: Ald Uran, Shrine of the Webspinner

title: Ald Verya
topic_desc: Ald Verya is an ancient Indoril ruin located in the Alt Orethan region. The site comprises at least two distinct interior zones, including a tower section. Like many such structures, its original purpose is obscured by time, and it currently serves as a refuge for smugglers.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ald Verya is.

title: Ald Virak
topic_desc: Ald Virak is an ancient Velothi tower situated in the hills of Roth Roryn, southwest of Menaan. The structure has suffered severe collapse over the centuries; its floors have crumbled into a central pit, exposing small ebony veins. Only fragments of the upper level endure, housing the tower's original shrine alongside the Holy Blade of Ald Virak, a dagger possessing properties to turn and burn undead. The ruin is currently infested with skeleton guardians. These sentinels protect Ald Virak's most significant secret: the tower was constructed atop Romayon, an even older Dunmer stronghold now inhabited by Daedra and other profane entities. A bandit camp occupies the immediate eastern approach, while the abandoned iron mine of Anbarsud lies to the west.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ald Virak is.

title: Ald Volos
topic_desc: Ald Volos is a Velothi tower situated in the Aanthirin region, northeast of Aimrah. The tower serves as the residence of the wizard Ralam Othravel, who is often found near the waterfalls forming the source of the river flowing north of the structure. The tower's interior holds sparse items of note, though a grand soul gem rests on the top floor bookshelf.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Ald Volos is.

title: Alencheth
topic_desc: Alencheth is a small, partially-flooded Dwemer ruin situated in the Lan Orethan region, northwest of Bosmora. Its entrance is unconventional, accessible only via a door at the end of a Dwemer pier extending over the water. The interior consists of at least two distinct chambers. A northern dry chamber houses standard Dwemer automata, including a Centurion Sphere and a Dwarven Spectre, which guard the site's mechanisms and a Dwemer chest. A separate eastern chamber remains flooded and secured behind a locked door, containing additional Dwemer chests that hold caches of Dwemer coins. The site's unusual waterside entry and the presence of spectral guardians make it a point of interest for scholars of Dwemer engineering and necromantic remnants.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Alencheth is.

title: Alendu Plantation
topic_desc: Alendu Plantation is a muckspunge farm situated in the Sunad Mora region, east of Tel Ouada. The estate is dominated by a two-level manor belonging to the Dunmer farmer Ralnym Alendu. Behind this structure, amidst the muckspunge patches, sits a slave shack housing the laborers who work the marshy fields. The environment is notoriously damp and saturated with muck, a defining characteristic noted by those who reside there.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Alendu Plantation is.

title: Alnadribi
topic_desc: Alnadribi is a cave situated in the Mephalan Vales region of mainland Morrowind. It currently serves as a lair for a coven of necromancers and mages, including practitioners of witchcraft. The presence of these spellcasters renders the cavern a hazardous site for unprepared travelers.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Alnadribi is.

title: Alt Bosara
topic_desc: Alt Bosara is a small House Telvanni settlement situated on the southern shore of Lake Boethiah within the Boethiah's Spine region. The town is dominated by a vast waterfall and crowned by Tel Vaerin, the tower of Telvanni Councilor Master Vaerin. Tel Vaerin is an expansive four-story structure navigated internally by levitation, housing the master's chamber, an apothecary, and a mage's curio shelf. Despite its humble size, the town offers a diverse array of services, including enchanting, clothier, weaponsmithing, and general trade, spread among commoner housepods flanking the waterfall. Alt Bosara maintains transport links via River Strider to Tel Mothrivra and Llothanis, and by carriage to Necrom and Llothanis. A separate barracks houses the local guard.
topic_desc_basic: Alt Bosara is a small House Telvanni town on the southern shore of Lake Boethiah in the Boethiah's Spine region. A vast waterfall dominates the settlement, which is crowned by Tel Vaerin, the tower of Telvanni Councilor Master Vaerin. The town provides diverse trade services and transport links via River Strider and carriage to nearby settlements.

title: Alt Orethan
topic_desc: Alt Orethan is a region in the Mournhold District of Morrowind, encompassing the rocky scrubland situated between the city of Almalexia and the Lan Orethan forest. Owned by House Indoril, the area directly surrounding Almalexia is green and full of life, featuring significant pilgrimage sites. It is a relatively safe territory patrolled by Ordinators. Alt Orethan borders Aanthirin to the west, the Sundered Scar to the north, the Mephalan Vales to the northeast, Lan Orethan to the east, and the Deshaan Plains to the south. The landscape contains ancient Indoril ruins, Velothi towers, Daedric shrines, and ancestral tombs, alongside active diamond, gold, iron, and kwama egg mines. Its largest settlement is Almalexia, with the town of Meralag serving as the primary hub in the developed area.
topic_desc_basic: Alt Orethan is a green, rocky scrubland region in the Mournhold District of Morrowind, lying between the city of Almalexia and the Lan Orethan forest. Owned by House Indoril and patrolled by Ordinators, it contains significant pilgrimage sites.

title: Alta Vathor
topic_desc: Alta Vathor is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Azura, situated north of Narsis. The outer chamber serves as the research area of Lord Mhas Vathor, a Dremora, containing numerous books and scrolls. The inner shrine holds an altar bearing the Book of Dawn and Dusk, a black rose, and a small chest. Winged Twilights guard the precinct. The shrine reflects the enduring presence of Daedric veneration in the Morrowind interior, where servants of the Princes maintain their own apparatus of study and ritual apart from Temple authority.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Alta Vathor is.

title: Althoa
topic_desc: Althoa is a large, elongated island in the Sea of Ghosts situated north of the Dagon Urul region and just northeast of Bal Oyra. The land tapers to a narrow point in the southeast, broadens across its center, and narrows slightly toward the northwest. It hosts three distinct settlements: the small fishing village of Bahrammu in the interior, the Imperial colony of Nivalis at the northernmost point, and the Telvanni tower of Tel Rivus in the southeast, which grows from the foundations of an ancient Dunmer stronghold.
topic_desc_basic: Althoa is a large, elongated island in the Sea of Ghosts located northeast of Bal Oyra, north of the Dagon Urul region. It hosts a small fishing village, an Imperial colony, and a Telvanni tower built atop an ancient Dunmer stronghold.

title: Alumawia
topic_desc: Alumawia is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Malacath, situated in the Alt Orethan region. The site consists of two distinct zones: the Shrine and the Sepulcher. It is inhabited by Daedra and Malacath-worshipping cultists, including Orcs and others drawn to the Daedric Prince's sphere.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Alumawia is.

title: Alver Farmhouse
topic_desc: Alver Farmhouse is a farmstead in the Roth Roryn region, situated adjacent to the Savrethi Distillery. The property is owned and occupied by the Dunmer couple Mirea and Nols Alver. Its fields are worked by an enslaved Argonian and yield a variety of crops including corkbulb, comberry, ash yam, and hamum root. The farmhouse basement holds a copy of the mercantile treatise The Buying Game.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Alver Farmhouse is.

title: Alvor-Vidran Egg Mine
topic_desc: Alvor-Vidran Egg Mine is a remote kwama egg mine situated in the Dagon Urul region. It is worked for its yield of kwama eggs, a staple trade good of Morrowind. The mine contains a working colony of kwama, from which miners harvest the eggs. Its isolated location in the rugged terrain of Dagon Urul makes it a modest and seldom-visited operation, contributing to the local economy rather than to broader commerce.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Alvor-Vidran Egg Mine is.

title: Amanil Gratis' Shack
topic_desc: Amanil Gratis' Shack is a modest farmer's dwelling situated in the Lan Orethan region, southwest of Nethril Plantation. The structure serves as the home and operational base for a Dark Elf wickwheat farmer, with adjacent fields where the owner typically labors. It represents the humble agrarian lifestyle common among the rural Dunmer of the area.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Amanil Gratis' Shack is.

title: Ammar
topic_desc: Ammar is an Indoril clifftop fortress situated on the mainland coast of the Mephalan Vales, directly opposite the Shrine of Azura on Vvardenfell. It serves as the northernmost Indoril settlement before Telvanni-held territory begins. The garrison is widely recognized for maintaining peace throughout the western Mephalan Vales, making the fort a common rest stop for southbound travelers in need of supplies and equipment repairs. The fortress is led by the Indoril noble Tavrene Indalas, who resides in Indalas Manor at the fortress summit alongside family members. Service providers within the entrance hall include an alchemist, a smith, and a trader. A guard tower with a small prison sits across a covered walkway from the manor. The settlement was formerly known as Ayemar.
topic_desc_basic: Ammar is an Indoril clifftop fortress on the mainland coast of the Mephalan Vales, directly opposite the Shrine of Azura on Vvardenfell. It is the northernmost Indoril settlement before Telvanni territory and a common rest stop for southbound travelers. The garrison is known for keeping the surrounding region safe and peaceful.

title: Amthuandz
topic_desc: Amthuandz is a Dwemer ruin situated in the Boethiah's Spine region, northeast of Tel Muthada. The site is currently under excavation by a team of archaeologists and miners. According to one of the researchers present, the bridge outside the fortress once served as the sole passage through Boethiah's Spine, rendering the stronghold of considerable strategic importance in antiquity. The interior retains active Dwemer constructs and spectral guardians, alongside a notable concentration of Dwemer artifacts and salvage. The excavation team does not contest removal of recovered materials from the premises. The ruin comprises a single known zone. Its remote mountainous situation, accessed by steps cut into the rock above a nearby farmstead, reflects the characteristic Dwemer preference for defensible, elevated construction in rugged terrain.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Amthuandz is.

title: Amurbal Peninsula
topic_desc: The Amurbal Peninsula is a long promontory in Dagon Urul that reaches west from the mainland into the Sea of Ghosts. It is dominated by Tel Oren, an isolated Telvanni tower at its northern tip that serves as the study of Mistress Faruna. The peninsula also contains Zatamushi, a small cave leading to a ruined Daedric shrine.
topic_desc_basic: The Amurbal Peninsula is a long promontory in Dagon Urul that extends west into the Sea of Ghosts. It is dominated by the Telvanni tower of Tel Oren at its northern tip.

title: Anashbibi
topic_desc: Anashbibi is an ice-covered Daedric shrine dedicated to Sheogorath, situated within a glacier in the Velothi Mountains. A recent glacial collapse exposed the ruin, which consists of an Outer Shrine and an Inner Shrine. Frost atronachs inhabit the frozen complex. The enchanted blade Shard of the Borealis lies proffered before Sheogorath's statue in the Inner Shrine. The Daedra Ishil-Mahon has established itself within the shrine, drawing cultist interest to the site.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Anashbibi is.

title: Anbarsud
topic_desc: Anbarsud is a dilapidated iron mine in the Roth Roryn region of mainland Morrowind, situated in the hills west of Menaan. The complex comprises three zones: the Mine, a Shrine, and a Forge. The Shrine contains a statue of Malacath with Orcish arms placed as offerings, and the Forge holds a working anvil. Anbarsud serves as the lair of the Orlukh Clan, an Orcish vampire bloodline. The mine connects subterraneously to the nearby ruins of Ald Virak and Romayon, linking it to broader networks of abandoned sites in the region. The presence of Daedric and Ebony armaments within the Forge suggests long occupation or deliberate curation by the clan. The site's association with Malacath worship and Orcish undead distinguishes it from typical vampire lairs.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Anbarsud is.

title: Andar Mok
topic_desc: Andar Mok is a small, isolated farming and fishing settlement on the shores of Lake Boethiah in the Boethiah's Spine region, aligned with House Telvanni. Formerly called Adurin-Ouaka, meaning 'shipwreck village' in the Dunmer tongue, the community supplements its livelihood by looting the numerous wrecks on the treacherous lakebed. The inhabitants are notably xenophobic and isolationist. The village consists primarily of shacks and is governed by a local hetman. Its sole commercial establishment is the Andalas Tradehouse. Reaching Andar Mok overland requires a long trek through the surrounding mountains, while water routes from the nearest fast-travel town at Tel Mothrivra still necessitate swimming, water walking, or levitation.
topic_desc_basic: Andar Mok is a small, isolated farming and fishing village on the shores of Lake Boethiah in the Boethiah's Spine region. Aligned with House Telvanni, the settlement is known for its xenophobic inhabitants and its former name, Adurin-Ouaka, meaning 'shipwreck village,' derived from the numerous wrecks on the treacherous lake.

title: Andarannipal
topic_desc: Andarannipal is a partly flooded Daedric ruin on the southern shores of Lake Andaram, situated in the Aanthirin region. Dedicated to Mehrunes Dagon, the shrine maintains an active cult of worshipers within its interior. A grounded vessel, the Overrun Shipwreck, rests against the ruin's northern side; its breached hull penetrates the structure and remains visible from the inner shrine, a testament to the crew's destruction at the hands of the Daedra. The site holds significance for the Tribunal Temple, which suspects the Dagon cultists of possessing a sacred artifact of the Hlan Oek temple.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Andarannipal is.

title: Andasamsi Grotto
topic_desc: Andasamsi Grotto is a cavernous grotto in Lake Andaram, in the Aanthirin region. Dreugh inhabit its depths, and pearls and Dreugh wax may be found within. The entrance lies a short distance southwest of Aimrah.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Andasamsi Grotto is.

title: Andathril Ancestral Tomb
topic_desc: Andathril Ancestral Tomb is the family burial site of the Indoril lords of Tur Julan, former rulers of much of Roth Roryn prior to the Armistice. The underground complex is notably vast, befitting the tomb of a noble lineage that once held regional authority. The Andathril family retains an ancestral connection to the Andas family, which presently controls much of Bal Foyen. The tomb lies in the Roth Roryn region, southwest of Ossurnashalit and accessible via the great rock arch spanning the Pryai River near the Monastery of St. Felms. As with many Dunmer ancestral tombs, the site is inhabited by undead guardians. Its scale and contents reflect the wealth and standing of the Indoril house in the pre-Armistice era.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Andathril Ancestral Tomb is.

title: Andrani Farmhouse
topic_desc: Andrani Farmhouse is a small guar farm situated in the northern Coronati Basin. It lies along the path running southwest up the hill from Idathren. The farmhouse is owned and operated by the Andrani family, who raise guar for their hide and meat.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Andrani Farmhouse is.

title: Andrelo Ancestral Tomb
topic_desc: Andrelo Ancestral Tomb is a small Dunmer burial site located across the Kanit River from Hlerynhul, with its entrance lying south of the settlement's docks. The tomb houses the honored dead of the Andrelo family. Redoran weapons and armor interred within indicate the family's history of service to House Redoran, though this connection reflects a period when that Great House held authority over these lands—a rule that has since lapsed. Like many ancestral tombs, it is inhabited by undead guardians.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Andrelo Ancestral Tomb is.

title: Andresian Dreugh
topic_desc: The Andresian Dreugh is a shipwreck lying in the deep waters immediately north of Almas Thirr in the Aanthirin region. The vessel appears to have been Telvanni-associated, as a Telvanni guard shield rests in the captain's cabin. Its cargo consisted of various beverages. Though the wreck sits at considerable depth, the interior has not fully flooded; air pockets persist on the upper deck, while the lower deck remains partially blocked by wreckage. Slaughterfish infest the surrounding waters.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Andresian Dreugh is.

title: Anmu-Shaddr's Yurt
topic_desc: Anmu-Shaddr's Yurt, also known by the settlement name Inuibbisa, is a small Ashlander dwelling located in the Roth Roryn region. It lies north of the Savrethi Distillery. The yurt serves as the home of the hunter Anmu-Shaddr. It was originally intended to form part of a larger Ashlander community named Inuibbissa Camp, though currently only the single yurt occupies the site.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Anmu-Shaddr's Yurt is.

title: Anthelasa Ancestral Tomb
topic_desc: Anthelasa Ancestral Tomb is a Dunmer ancestral tomb located in the Mephalan Vales region. Like other ancestral tombs of Morrowind, it serves as a sealed burial site for a particular Dunmer lineage, housing the remains of generations bound to that family name. The tomb is occupied by undead guardians, a common condition of ancestral crypts whose protective wards and funerary rites sustain the dead in unlife. The Mephalan Vales setting places it within the rugged interior reaches of Morrowind's Telvanni-controlled mainland, a region of isolated valleys and scattered settlements. Beyond its existence as a family crypt, no widely circulated historical or cultural significance is recorded for the Anthelasa tomb specifically. The practices it represents—lineage veneration, sealed interment, and the restless vigil of the honored dead—reflect enduring Dunmer funerary tradition.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Anthelasa Ancestral Tomb is.

title: Antirrhinum
topic_desc: The Antirrhinum is a vessel operating as a floating alchemy store, presently docked at the Narsis waterfront in the Shipal-Shin region. The ship's owner, an Argonian alchemist named Pylameda, claims to have purchased the craft in Thorn thirty years ago. Since then, the Antirrhinum has sailed to distant ports including Senchal and Anvil; its current berth up the Thirr River marks its first journey into Morrowind. The vessel is divided into two primary zones: the cabin, where Pylameda offers alchemical wares, and the hold, which houses the ship's crew. The complement includes sailors, a cook, and a warrior, reflecting the practical requirements of operating a merchant vessel on long oceanic voyages.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Antirrhinum is.

title: Aranyon Pass
topic_desc: Aranyon Pass is a sinister, haunted canyon cutting through the Boethiah's Spine mountain range. Running north-south for most of its length before curving northwest-southeast at its southern end, it begins east of Sarvanni and emerges near Ranyon-ruhn. The canyon is large enough to generate its own weather system, frequently cloaked in fog and overcast skies. Both entrances bear warning signs, and with good reason: the pass harbors unique undead not found elsewhere in Morrowind, often concentrated near Erushara Ancestral Tomb roughly two-thirds of the way south. A former tunnel connecting west to Ashamul has largely collapsed. Despite the dread it inspires in nearby residents—who report hearing ghostly voices and faint screams—the pass remains a tempting shortcut, halving the travel distance between Ranyon-ruhn and Tel Ouada compared to the coastal road via Sunad Mora and Ashamul.
topic_desc_basic: Aranyon Pass is a haunted canyon through the Boethiah's Spine mountains, running between the areas of Sarvanni and Ranyon-ruhn. Locals avoid it due to its undead inhabitants and eerie sounds, but travelers sometimes use it as a shortcut between Ranyon-ruhn and Tel Ouada.

title: Archtumz
topic_desc: Archtumz is a small, recently discovered Dwemer ruin situated within the Palisnabat glass mine in the Sunad Mora region. New Dwemer ruins in this part of Morrowind are rare, lending the site significance to both the Mages Guild and nearby locals. Because the ruin was uncovered only recently, much of its architecture and contents may remain in their original state, and numerous Dwemer artifacts—weapons, armor, and tomes—still rest within its chambers. The interior features a vertical shaft requiring levitation to exit and a tower that presently shelters an Imperial savant studying the site. Access to the ruin lies through the mine, which is guarded.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Archtumz is.

title: Aren Eggmine
topic_desc: Aren Eggmine is a Hlaalu-operated egg mine situated in the Aanthirin region, owned by Orns Aren. The mine entrance lies immediately south of Aren Manor's wall. It comprises two zones: the upper mine and a lower level accessible by two routes, one behind a securely locked door. The lower passages lead above the kwama queen's chamber. The mine is worked by miners tending kwama for egg production. Little else of note distinguishes the site at present.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Aren Eggmine is.

title: Aren Farmhouse
topic_desc: Aren Farmhouse is a small agricultural settlement in the Coronati Basin, situated west of Sarys Plantation. The farm's economy centers on Hamum Root cultivation worked by two Argonian slaves and guar rearing for meat. Hervil Aren sells the farm's produce and potions outside, while his wife Gariru remains inside the farmhouse.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Aren Farmhouse is.

title: Aren Manor
topic_desc: Aren Manor is a secluded clifftop estate in the Aanthirin region, situated south of Indal-ruhn. The manor governs an adjacent kwama eggmine from which it appears to draw its wealth. The approach is steep and difficult, lending the site the character of a fortress. The manor is governed by Orns Aren, a Bosmer and adopted son of a Hlaalu nobleman. The presence of free Khajiit and Argonian residents suggests an attitude toward slavery that differs from the larger Hlaalu plantations to the east. References within the manor to a place called 'Neen,' together with a guarded door, hint at an undisclosed secret associated with the locale, though its nature remains unknown.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Aren Manor is.

title: Areno Varo's House
topic_desc: Areno Varo's House is a comberry farmstead in the Lan Orethan region, situated northwest of Bosmora across the river. It is one of several isolated homesteads scattered through that rural stretch of Morrowind's interior. The property consists of a locked house and surrounding comberry fields worked by the occupant, Areno Varo. The house itself contains little of note. The farm represents the pattern of small, dispersed agricultural settlements typical of Lan Orethan's settled margins.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Areno Varo's House is.

title: Arkgnthleft
topic_desc: Arkgnthleft is a Dwemer ruin situated in the Mephalan Vales. The site comprises three distinct architectural zones: the Upper Levels, the Lower Levels, and the Towers. Like many extant Dwemer strongholds, its deep chambers and corridors now serve as a refuge for smugglers operating in the region. The ruin's original Dwemer designation and specific historical purpose remain uncertain.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Arkgnthleft is.

title: Armun Pass Outpost
topic_desc: Armun Pass Outpost is a fortified settlement guarding the pass between the Armun Ashlands and the Othreleth Woods. Situated along the road south of Arvud, it serves as a waystation for travelers continuing toward Hlan Oek and Andrethis. The outpost provides essential services for expeditions into the ashlands, including an outfitter's shop and a tavern called The Guar With No Name, which offers lodging. A garrison commanded by House Hlaalu maintains order at the site.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Armun Pass Outpost is.

title: Arnesian Jungle
topic_desc: The Arnesian Jungle is a shifting, deceptive region forming the northern reaches of Black Marsh. Its terrain closely resembles the neighboring Argonian homeland. Thirty years ago, the Arnesian War resulted in the annexation of this territory into the lands of House Dres, placing it within the Deshaan District of Morrowind. The region borders Shipal-Shin to the west, the Salt Marsh to the north, and the Mudflats to the east. Its largest known settlement is the village of Taj'Xa'thaxi, and the landscape also holds the ruins of Fort Arnesia. The jungle is characterized by persistent dampness, with fog, overcast skies, and rain dominating the climate.
topic_desc_basic: The Arnesian Jungle is a shifting, deceptive region forming the northern reaches of Black Marsh. It was annexed by House Dres following the Arnesian War thirty years ago and is located in the Deshaan District of Morrowind.

title: Arvel Ancestral Tomb
topic_desc: Arvel Ancestral Tomb is a Dunmer ancestral burial site located in the Roth Roryn region, southeast of Teyn. The tomb features a main chamber concealing a secretive walled room. Access to this hidden chamber is mechanically linked to the skulls within the primary hall. The sealed interior houses the tomb's greater wealth and serves as the prison for the vampire Ilvaalmu.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Arvel Ancestral Tomb is.

title: Arvethu Ancestral Tomb
topic_desc: Arvethu Ancestral Tomb is a small Dunmer ancestral tomb located in the Dagon Urul region, east of Bthalag-Zturamz. Like many such sites, it serves as a resting place for the honored dead, though it has become populated by undead. Skeletons cram the interior chambers, including a Skeleton Champion that guards a glass longbow resting upon a sarcophagus in a hidden chamber opposite the entrance to the tomb's largest room.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Arvethu Ancestral Tomb is.

title: Arvs-Nalor
topic_desc: Arvs-Nalor is a Velothi tower situated in the Dagon Urul region, housing a Great House Telvanni alchemist and an assistant. The tower serves as a modest seat of Telvanni magical study, offering training to members holding the rank of Oathman or higher within the House. It stands along the northern road from Tel Gilan, accessible by taking the left fork where the path turns sharply before the coast. The tower itself holds little in the way of material wealth, its primary value lying in the alchemical expertise of its occupants.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Arvs-Nalor is.

title: Arvs-Shadan
topic_desc: Arvs-Shadan is a Velothi tower in the Armun Ashlands, situated along the hilly border with Roth Roryn opposite the Daedric shrine of Essarnartes. It serves as a base for a Telvanni sorcerer's research into vampirism. The tower holds imprisoned vampires within its cells. The resident Telvanni wizard oversees the facility from her top quarters, assisted by an apprentice and guarded by a warrior.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Arvs-Shadan is.

title: Arvud
topic_desc: Arvud is a House Hlaalu-run outpost and caravan stop in the Armun Ashlands, serving as an oasis of civilization amid desolate surroundings. The settlement occupies the site of Ald Erfoud, a Redoran stronghold abandoned two millennia ago; the ruins of the old fortress remain accessible beneath the current town. Hlaalu governance centers on Uvayn Manor, from which the governor administers the holding. The Lucky Shalaasa's Caravanserai provides lodging, while a bazaar, an alchemist, a clothier, and a blacksmith support travelers and residents. A slave market operates near the entrance. Silt strider transport connects Arvud to Menaan, and roads link it to Hlan Oek, Andrethis, and Kragenmoor. Nearby landmarks include the Ishanuran Ashlander camp to the west, the Daedric shrine of Hummurushtapi to the north, and the vampire-infested Indoril ruin of Khirakai to the east-northeast.
topic_desc_basic: Arvud is a House Hlaalu-run outpost and caravan stop in the Armun Ashlands. It occupies the site of Ald Erfoud, an ancient abandoned Redoran stronghold. Silt strider service connects it to Menaan, and roads link it to Hlan Oek, Andrethis, and Kragenmoor.

title: Ashamul
topic_desc: Ashamul is a small, traditional Velothi cave settlement located in the Molkadh Mountains of the Boethiah's Spine region, within House Telvanni territory. The community inhabits a vast cavern hewn into the rock, with several small dwellings formed out of hollows in the cavern walls. A network of wooden platforms and landings links the interiors together, though some walkways are narrow and precarious. The cavern lies at the end of a short east-west canyon, its eastern end joining the road between Ranyon-ruhn and Tel Ouada. Outside the cave entrance sits a guar pen; Ashamul is known for selling the creatures as beasts of burden. The settlement offers no other services and remains remote, with the Erushara Ancestral Tomb and other landmarks situated some distance away across the surrounding mountains.
