Above the waterline, the cavern serves as a base for a smuggler gang trading in skooma, wine, and pillows, with numerous skooma bottles stored within. This illicit activity along the Thirr has drawn the attention of Hlan Oek's governor, Feldril Sathis.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yadamsi is.

title: Yalamalkus
topic_desc: Yalamalkus is a cave in the Armun Ashlands serving as a haunt of the restless dead. It is guarded by skeletons both within and without. The cave lies in the hills above the entrance to Puman, reachable by following the path leading up from the left side of that entrance, west of Ishanuran Camp. Notable relics within include the Water Spear, found on a rocky ledge in the chamber beneath the entrance, and the Short Blade skill book Unnamed Book, located in the passage leading to that chamber.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yalamalkus is.

title: Yamandalkal
topic_desc: Yamandalkal is an Althoa Daedric shrine dedicated to Mehrunes Dagon, situated in the Sea of Ghosts region. The site comprises two interior zones: the Crying Chambers and the Sanctum. A powerful Xivilai lord holds dominion over the shrine, attended by hostile cultists and lesser Daedra in its service. The ruin's interior contains various scattered armaments and texts, though some are warded, summoning hostile guardians when disturbed.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yamandalkal is.

title: Yamniban
topic_desc: Yamniban is a small, remote cavern situated in the Aanthirin region, southeast of Roa Dyr. Its isolation makes it a suitable refuge for outlaws, and the cave is currently inhabited by a group of bandits. The cavern consists of a single zone that terminates in a final chamber. Within this deepest recess lies a copy of the treatise How to Break in a Set of Armor, which details the magical principles behind the destructive spell known as Fracture Armor.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yamniban is.

title: Yamuninisharn
topic_desc: Yamuninisharn is a Daedric ruin dedicated to the Princes Boethiah and Sheogorath, rising above Aegondo Point in the Sunad Mora region. Its exterior spans nearly the entire peninsula, though the interior is significantly restricted; a cave-in renders the northwest area inaccessible. The shrine remains an active site of worship, guarded by Daedra and devoted followers. A modest offering of gems, potions, scrolls, and an ebony broadsword is maintained within.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yamuninisharn is.

title: Yanashpi
topic_desc: Yanashpi is a large, well-defended cave in the Velothi Mountains, situated east of the Dwemer ruin Hendor-Stardumz. The lower cavern walls expose Dwarven architecture, a likely consequence of this proximity. The cave's bandit occupants maintain strong fortifications, including a palisade and an archer in the first chamber, likely due to the nearby goblin stronghold of Kharom further up the mountain slope. The site is divided into upper and lower levels, with the lower chambers containing the primary stronghold and exposed ebony veins near a lava pit.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yanashpi is.

title: Yandaran
topic_desc: Yandaran is the main camp of the Nasar Shinathi clan, situated in the southern Shipal-Shin region. The Nasar have held this site since the Four Score War, using it as a base from which to attack the invading forces of the Second Empire. The settlement spans multiple zones, including an upper and lower level, a scouts' dome, a drillmaster's hut, and a hunters' tent. It offers clan services such as alchemy, smithing, and training. Tame Sand Kwoom and Sharai Hoppers are kept in the underground section. The site includes a propylon chamber linking to Indomarano and Kaladryon, though its index is stored elsewhere. The clan is led by Saharkhan Diruabanam.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yandaran is.

title: Yanimmu Mine
topic_desc: Yanimmu Mine is an iron ore mine situated in the Alt Orethan region. The site yields iron from mineral veins and operates with a small workforce of miners. Its proximity to Fort Umbermoth provides a degree of security, and the settlement of Sailen serves as the nearest point for Almsivi Intervention. The mine's output contributes to the regional supply of raw iron.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yanimmu Mine is.

title: Yanishanabi
topic_desc: Yanishanabi is a single-chambered Daedric shrine dedicated to Mehrunes Dagon. It stands upon the border of the Mephalan Vales and the Sacred Lands, directly east of Akamora. Cultists occupy the site. A statue of Dagon forms the shrine's focal point; the gems placed before it—save for a pearl and an emerald—are cursed, summoning Dremora to defend the offerings when disturbed. Beyond these trapped offerings and a few magical scrolls, the shrine holds little of material value. Despite its diminutive size, Yanishanabi has drawn the enmity of Mephala, marking it as a site of inter-Daedric friction.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yanishanabi is.

title: Yansumanmus Mine
topic_desc: Yansumanmus Mine is a rich sapphire mine operated by House Hlaalu in the Shipal-Shin region, situated a short walk southwest of Riverkeep near Narsis. The site yields abundant sapphire ore veins worked by a labor force of Dunmer and outland miners, alongside Khajiiti and Orcish slaves, all overseen by a Hlaalu foreman and guarded by Hlaalu retainers. Beyond its gem extraction, the facility holds no other significant features.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yansumanmus Mine is.

title: Yansurashmi
topic_desc: Yansurashmi is a cave situated at the edge of the Armun Ashlands, north of the old Indoril ruin of Khirakai. It serves as an animal den, inhabited by wild creatures. The cave's walls feature exposed veins of raw glass, a valuable material for light armor crafting and enchantment. Its interior extends to a waterfall chamber containing a secured chest that holds an Orcish helm. A suspended rope bridge marks the surface entrance above the cave mouth.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yansurashmi is.

title: Yashazmus
topic_desc: Yashazmus is a large Daedric ruin in the Telvanni Isles, dedicated to Mehrunes Dagon. The shrine is crumbling under the weight of rogue Telvanni roots, which have caused significant structural damage to its many towers. The complex comprises four zones: the Outer Halls, the Shrine, the Flooded Halls, and the Pit of Sacrifice. The Shrine centers on a massive excavated cavern housing a huge Daedric citadel crowned by a giant statue of Dagon. The Flooded Halls contain a lesser shrine to the Daedric Prince. The Pit of Sacrifice features a deep corpse-disposal pit and suspended cages for prisoners awaiting sacrifice. A Dremora Lord named Drekhva Yashaz is bound to the shrine's unique spear, Anarchy, and emerges to defend the offering if the weapon is disturbed.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yashazmus is.

title: Yaztaramz
topic_desc: Yaztaramz is a Dwemer ruin situated on the coast between Helnim and Firewatch in the Dagon Urul region, northwest of the Daedric shrine of Onimushili and the Dwemer ruin of Ratharzak. The site currently serves as the residence and research base of a Telvanni wizard studying Dwemer artifacts and mechanisms. A significant number of functional Dwemer centurions remain active within the ruin, serving as sentinels that bar passage through its interior. The wizard occupies the uppermost chamber of the ruin's tower.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yaztaramz is.

title: Yenashpi
topic_desc: Yenashpi is a small cave situated in the Roth Roryn region, lying east of the settlement Omaynis. The cavern currently serves as a hideout for a pair of Dunmer bandits who deal in illicit Dwemer goods. Their accumulated contraband includes various Dwemer artifacts, among them a Dwarven dagger and the notable Ring of Euphoria.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yenashpi is.

title: Yenidan
topic_desc: Yenidan is a small cave situated in the Boethiah's Spine region along the main road between Helnim and Firewatch. Its entrance lies west of Mzankh and a considerable distance east of Sadrith Mora, with no other notable landmarks in the immediate vicinity. The cave's main passageway is notable for an abundant growth of bloatspore plants. Nix-hounds inhabit the cave alongside a solitary Orcish resident.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yenidan is.

title: Yenmmend Grotto
topic_desc: Yenmmend Grotto is a submerged cavern in the Aanthirin region, its entrance located on the riverbed northeast of the village of Idathren. The interior is characterized by dense kelp growth and waters inhabited by slaughterfish. A submerged chest in the southeastern chamber holds a Glass Jinkblade, marking the grotto as a site of some interest to those willing to navigate its dangers.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yenmmend Grotto is.

title: Yennakiblis Camp
topic_desc: Yennakiblis Camp is a hostile Shinathi outpost situated among the mesas of the Shipal-Shin region, south of Adavrin Plantation and southeast of Stormgate Pass. The camp comprises several structures, including a communal tent and individual shelters. Its inhabitants are exclusively Dunmer aligned with the Shinathi, a nomadic Ashlander group known for their hostility toward outsiders. The camp's layout reflects a traditional Ashlander communal arrangement, with shared and private spaces.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yennakiblis Camp is.
aliases: Yennakiblis Camp, Emul-Danba and Hashuzul's Tent
Yennakiblis Camp, Kaupi and Manenumsu's Tent

title: Yeva Gahne's Shack
topic_desc: Yeva Gahne's Shack is a modest dwelling situated in the Lan Orethan region of mainland Morrowind, southwest of the Nethril Plantation. It serves as the home of the Dark Elf commoner Yeva Gahne. The structure is a typical example of the humble vernacular architecture found throughout rural Morrowind, reflecting the modest living conditions of the local working class.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yeva Gahne's Shack is.

title: Yfrac Farmhouse
topic_desc: Yfrac Farmhouse is a combined netch ranch and hackle-lo farm situated in the northeast portion of the Coronati Basin. The settlement lies along the road running northeast from Sarys Plantation, serving as a local agricultural outpost engaged in the herding of netches and cultivation of hackle-lo leaf.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yfrac Farmhouse is.

title: Yrgjol Steelfist's Shack
topic_desc: Yrgjol Steelfist's Shack is a small, isolated dwelling situated on a lonely island in the Boethiah's Spine region, southeast of Bal Oyra. The shack is inhabited by a Nord smith who operates as an arms salesman. Accessible only by water, the location lies past the vessel The Northern Wind along the route out of Bal Oyra.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Yrgjol Steelfist's Shack is.

title: Zabamallit
topic_desc: Zabamallit is a cave in the Roth Roryn region serving as a lair for members of the Orlukh vampire clan. The undead inhabitants keep mortal cattle within its chambers. Little of value resides inside beyond the Legion uniforms worn by the Orcish undead.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zabamallit is.

title: Zainissour Hive
topic_desc: Zainissour Hive is a skyrender nest carved into a mesa in the Shipal-Shin region, northeast of Narsis. Unlike many similar colonies, the cave system is distinguished by having fewer vertical passages. An Ebonweave Right Bracer lies within a dead-end cavern passageway in the southern reaches of the nest.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zainissour Hive is.

title: Zainna
topic_desc: Zainna is a medium-sized coastal cave situated in the Sunad Mora region, northeast of Tel Oren. The cavern currently serves as a hideout for a bandit gang, which includes the wanted Redguard rogue Jalian. The group is well-guarded, hosting several warriors, mages, and archers. Despite its occupation, the cave holds no notable wealth, containing only modest supplies, basic weapons, a small quantity of skooma, and common clutter. Slaughterfish inhabit the surrounding waters.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zainna is.

title: Zalitalan
topic_desc: Zalitalan is a cave in the Boethiah's Spine region of mainland Morrowind, situated across the channel from Dragonhead Point, east of Alt Bosara. The cave serves as a dwelling for a coven of witches drawn from multiple races of Tamriel, indicating a gathering bound by shared arcane practice rather than common origin. Daedra and undead also inhabit the cave, likely bound or summoned by the coven's sorceries. The remains of a slain witchhunter within the cave attest to the perils confronting those who would challenge the coven directly. Zalitalan stands as one of the more dangerous witch-holds in the remote eastern reaches of Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zalitalan is.

title: Zanammu
topic_desc: Zanammu is a sprawling, multi-tiered ruin of House Indoril situated in the Alt Orethan region, northwest of Dreynim. The cause of its downfall remains uncertain, though the presence of a plaguebearer lich and plaguebearer skeletons suggests a virulent corruption. Local Ashlanders consider the site cursed, a reputation well-earned by its diseased inhabitants, which are capable of transmitting afflictions even in death. The ruin comprises six distinct zones, including an ancient crypt and collapsed corridors. Within its depths lie ruined Indoril structures, statues of Almalexia, and scattered armaments such as an adamantium staff, an ebony bardiche, and a full set of Indoril armor. The enchanted staff Alchurnod is also found here. Architectural features include false floors and illusionary passages connecting the tiers.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zanammu is.

title: Zarathil
topic_desc: Zarathil is a smugglers' cave situated on the promontory north of Ald Marak's Skylamp tower in the Coronati Basin, its entrance marked by a wall of wooden stakes. The cave serves as a hold for escaped slaves whom the smugglers attempt to ransom back to House Hlaalu. The presence of these slaves and the ransom scheme make the site a point of concern for the Great House.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zarathil is.

title: Zatamushi
topic_desc: Zatamushi is a small cave situated in the Dagon Urul region, leading to a ruined Daedric shrine. The entrance lies southeast of the shrine's Daedric tower, accessible by traveling south-southeast along the islands stretching out from Tel Oren. The cave itself holds little of note beyond its connection to the ruined shrine and a modest guarded cache of gold, scrolls, and texts.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zatamushi is.

title: Zeddan
topic_desc: Zeddan is a small cave in the Aanthirin region, situated southeast of the river fork between Indal-ruhn and Hlan Oek. The cavern serves as a base for a smuggler band, which holds captives in its northern chamber. The interior contains pitfalls, though levitation potions permit escape from these depressions. Notable resources within include raw ebony deposits and magical scrolls. The site is known to the Morag Tong, which has issued a writ targeting the smuggler Ilmeni.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zeddan is.

title: Zeral-Pan Mine
topic_desc: Zeral-Pan Mine is a long, winding sapphire mine situated in a narrow canyon north of Casimor and the Purple Road in the Shipal-Shin region, separated from the Chimer stronghold of Teloseras by a single mesa. The excavation is overrun by goblins of the Blind Stalker tribe, alongside cave rats and durzog. It comprises two zones, with the Lower Tunnels connecting to the depths of Kalkusara, the likely origin of the goblin infestation. The mine contains abundant sapphire veins, making it a potentially lucrative, if dangerous, site.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zeral-Pan Mine is.

title: Zernital
topic_desc: Zernital is a Velothi tower situated in the Coronati Basin, north of Narsis. Currently occupied by outlaws and summoned Daedra, it serves as a hostile conjurer's stronghold. The tower's remote position and dangerous inhabitants make it a notable landmark for travelers navigating the region north of the city.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zernital is.

title: Zirconia
topic_desc: The Zirconia is a vessel of the Imperial Census and Excise office, moored at Narsis in the Shipal-Shin region. It serves as a floating extension of the local C&E authority, its hold storing confiscated contraband. A brig occupies the aft section for holding prisoners.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zirconia is.

title: Zuldassur Ancestral Tomb
topic_desc: Zuldassur Ancestral Tomb is the ancestral tomb of the family that inhabited the ill-fated Zuldassur Manor. Located in the Lan Orethan region, west of Bosmora, the tomb is inhabited solely by ancestor ghosts. Within its single zone stands a Shrine of Almalexia's Mercy, and an Amulet of Health rests among its otherwise modest contents.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zuldassur Ancestral Tomb is.

title: Zuldassur Manor
topic_desc: Zuldassur Manor is a ruined estate in the Lan Orethan region, plagued by undead. The site comprises three zones: an entryway, the main manor, and a basement. The main hall holds bedrolls indicating a bandit group once camped there before being slain by the resident undead. The basement ruins contain further undead and a pit descending into a flooded cavern. A concealed passage in the cavern ceiling leads to a hidden hideout occupied by an Argonian enforcer named Ruul, who stores magical trinkets, Cyrodiilic brandy, and potions of rising force among his crates. The manor's original purpose and the origin of its undead inhabitants remain uncertain.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zuldassur Manor is.

title: Zunawi Egg Mine
topic_desc: Zunawi Egg Mine is a small Tribunal Temple-owned kwama egg mine in the Shipal-Shin region, situated just south of the Number Rooms Temple at the source of the Thirr River. The mine is diminutive, comprising only three chambers. Buoyant Armigers of the Tribunal Temple guard the interior, while Dunmer miners work the kwama colony. The Temple's direct ownership and the posting of its holy warriors suggest the operation holds some institutional importance beyond mere commercial output, though the mine's small size limits its overall productivity.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zunawi Egg Mine is.

title: Zurindi Grotto
topic_desc: Zurindi Grotto is a sizable cavern den situated in the Coronati Basin, east of Ald Marak. Its entrance lies within the regional mangroves, near the Overgrown Shipwreck. The grotto serves as a major habitat for swamp trolls, which infest its interior. A sunken pit in the southern portion of the cave harbors a dreugh man o'war and the remains of an ill-fated Argonian diver named Tej-Na, alongside the fabled Benthic Mail, a notable piece of armor.
topic_desc_basic: You do not know where Zurindi Grotto is.

title: 16 Accords of Madness, v. VI
topic_desc: The sixth volume of the Sixteen Accords of Madness, known as Hircine's Tale, recounts a wager between Sheogorath and Hircine set among the peaks of Skyrim. Sheogorath proposes that each Prince groom a champion beast to meet in fatal combat three years thence. Hircine breeds a lycanthropic Daedroth of peerless ferocity; Sheogorath brings a diminutive songbird. The monstrous beast destroys itself in blind fury pursuing the oblivious bird, and a humiliated Hircine withdraws. The narrative illustrates the series' broader project of cataloguing the Daedric Princes' rivalries, here demonstrating how Sheogorath's cunning and love of absurdity overcome Hircine's martial pride and brute strength.
topic_desc_basic: A volume of the Sixteen Accords of Madness recounting a contest between Sheogorath and Hircine in Skyrim's peaks. Each Prince prepared a beast for combat; Sheogorath's tiny songbird triumphed over Hircine's fearsome lycanthropic Daedroth, which destroyed itself in frustrated rage. The tale demonstrates the Mad Prince's cunning prevailing over brute force.

title: 16 Accords of Madness, v. XII
topic_desc: The twelfth volume of the Sixteen Accords of Madness, subtitled Malacath's Tale, recounts a pre-Orsinium legend demonstrating Sheogorath's cruel cunning. It follows Emmeg Gro-Kayra, a noble Orsimer champion who receives the cursed blade Neb-Crescen from a disguised stranger. The weapon drives Emmeg into a frenzied bloodlust, compelling him to brutally murder an Orc woman. Sheogorath summons Malacath to the corpse, feigning shared outrage and directing him to slay the killer using Neb-Crescen. Malacath agrees and beheads the cloaked murderer, only to discover he has killed his own mortal son, Emmeg. By the terms of their agreement, Malacath's own strike damns his offspring to Sheogorath's realm, illustrating the Mad God's mastery of humiliation and deceit over his fellow Prince's wrath.
topic_desc_basic: A volume of the Sixteen Accords of Madness recounting a legend of Sheogorath tricking Malacath. The tale describes the Mad God using a cursed blade to drive a noble Orc champion to murder, then manipulating Malacath into unwittingly killing his own mortal son.

title: 36 Lessons of Vivec, Sermon 0
topic_desc: Sermon Zero is a cryptic preamble to the Thirty-Six Lessons of Vivec, presenting an alternative or concealed origin for the god Vehk. The text names the netchiman Irdri and Berahzic as his parents and describes a journey to the Dwemer king Kagrenac at Bthuangthuv, who provides a thrice-secret word encoded in an unreadable cipher. The sermon claims that the true key lies within this cipher, declaring Vivec himself the lesser or false key. It invokes multiple Daedric Princes alongside ALMSIVI and concludes with three contradictory statements on the primordial Word. Its esoteric content and deliberate obfuscation make it a deeply contested work among Tribunal theologians.
topic_desc_basic: Sermon Zero is a cryptic preamble to the Thirty-Six Lessons of Vivec. It claims an alternative origin for the god Vehk through the netchiman Irdri and Berahzic, describes a meeting with the Dwemer Kagrenac, and presents an unreadable cipher said to contain the true key to understanding, calling Vivec the false key.

title: A Bandit's Alchemical Work
topic_desc: A Bandit's Alchemical Work is a personal worksheet authored by an outlaw alchemist. The document records the practitioner's protracted difficulty in formulating a viable water breathing potion, noting that a prior attempt produced a lethal mixture. The writer identifies kwama cuttle and luminous russula as the correct ingredients but refuses to self-test the new concoction, instead designating enslaved individuals as test subjects. The alchemist's ultimate objective is to employ a successful brew to extract gold ore from flooded tunnels. The note also speculates that the previously failed, deadly potion might retain utility should the mining operation succeed. The work provides insight into the unscrupulous experimental practices and economic motivations driving illicit alchemy.
topic_desc_basic: A Bandit's Alchemical Work is an outlaw alchemist's worksheet detailing the difficult formulation of a water breathing potion. The writer identifies kwama cuttle and luminous russula as the correct ingredients, plans to test the concoction on enslaved people, and intends to use a successful brew to mine gold from flooded tunnels.

title: A Biography of Arkhonius Lim
topic_desc: This biographical work by Ormellia Lim chronicles the life of Arkhonius Lim, a Second Era noble who forsook his Nibenese heritage to join the Mages Guild. Rising from Apprentice in Mir Corrup to Magician in Cheydinhal, his career was defined by wit, magical ingenuity, and extensive travels through southern Cyrodiil and Black Marsh. Recognizing his talents, the Guild appointed him Archmagister and tasked him with establishing their first presence in the newly-conquered province of Morrowind. Arriving in Almalexia, he successfully negotiated Dunmeri skepticism, catalogued ancestral tomb wards, and explored Dwemer ruins before dying in a potions accident at age fifty-two. The biography frames his foundational work in Morrowind as a continuation of Vanus Galerion's legacy.
topic_desc_basic: A biography by Ormellia Lim detailing the life of Arkhonius Lim, the Archmagister who established the Mages Guild in Morrowind during the Second Era.

title: A Caution to Disciples
topic_desc: A Caution to Disciples is a Temple doctrinal text warning the uninitiated against heretical writings preserved within the Repository of Saint Veloth. It explains that such dangerous texts are kept solely for study by the Orders of Doctrine and Inquisition to protect the faithful. The work identifies specific threats: followers of Alandro-Sul who reject the Tribunal, Cyrodiilic scholars who sow doubt, the Sixth House and the Sharmat who present dreams as fact, House Dwemer whose logic is deemed inferior to the Tribunal's light, and the children of Padhome who make false promises of power. It instructs devotees to find ALMSIVI's words on the central dais, pay homage to Veloth at the back wall, and avoid heretical texts kept away from the center. The text serves as both a spiritual warning and a practical guide for navigating the Repository.
topic_desc_basic: A Caution to Disciples is a Temple text warning the uninitiated against heretical writings kept in the Repository of Saint Veloth. It identifies several groups whose teachings are considered dangerous, including followers of Alandro-Sul, Cyrodiilic scholars, the Sixth House, House Dwemer, and the children of Padhome.

title: A Commentary on the Covenants
topic_desc: A theological treatise dictated by Primate Dierem of the Temple-School of Julianos, examining the nature of Divine Covenants. The work posits that a Covenant—also termed an Illustrious Pact or Diathaka—is a spiritual commitment between a mortal and a Divine, representing the sole true path to sainthood and the only direct interface with the unknowable Divines. It argues that the mortal world is a Divine engine designed to reforge unworthy spirits, and that Covenants are initiated by exceptional mortals rather than the distant Divines, allowing the gods to directly influence the world through signs and wonders. The text warns that unworthy individuals who enter into Covenant may break under the strain, becoming violent Un-Saints or fading as spirits of nill. It concludes by urging meditation on the lives of Cyrod's saints to learn the path to sainthood.
topic_desc_basic: A theological work by Primate Dierem of the Temple-School of Julianos. It examines the Covenant of Saints, a spiritual pact between a mortal and a Divine that is considered the one true path to sainthood and direct communion with the Divines.

title: A Dubious Tale...
topic_desc: A humorous work attributed to Bibenus Geon, framed as a story passed among neonate students of the Crystal Tower on Summerset. The author recounts a tale told by an older student, presenting it as deliberately untrustworthy. It describes a destitute bard hired by a Tower Magister to impersonate a rare white ape for a visiting royal party from Firsthold after the actual specimen died. The bard's increasingly theatrical performance captivates the crowds until an acrobatic mishap lands him in an adjacent cell with a Snow Wolf. When the bard cries for help, the wolf whispers a warning to stay quiet lest they both lose their positions. The narrative serves as a comedic academic anecdote, its punchline implying the wolf is another disguised performer.
topic_desc_basic: A humorous tale by Bibenus Geon about a bard hired to impersonate a rare white ape in the Crystal Tower's animal pens for visiting royalty, only to discover the neighboring Snow Wolf is another disguised performer.

title: A Dunce in Morrowind, vol. 1
topic_desc: A Dunce in Morrowind, vol. 1 is a comedic work collected and edited by Frolja Silver-Blood for the Sneezing Horker Historical Society in Winterhold. Originally a skit by the late Ferana Adrethi, it was performed by Society members to introduce Nordic newcomers to Dunmer culture through satire. The narrative follows an oblivious Nord who claims to be an educated Winterhold noble but proves profoundly ignorant, misreading maps, misunderstanding directions, and falling prey to a witch while insisting on his own intellect. The publisher's note explains that such blustering, would-be nobles are a common sight in Winterhold, often lingering as prospective College students. The work uses this caricature to highlight and mock the mutual cultural ignorance between Nords and Dunmer in a cosmopolitan border setting.
topic_desc_basic: A comedic book edited by Frolja Silver-Blood, originating from the Sneezing Horker Historical Society in Winterhold. It features a satirical skit about an ignorant Nord traveling in Morrowind, written to help Nordic newcomers learn about Dunmer lands.

title: A Dunce in Morrowind, vol. 2
topic_desc: A satirical travelogue by Frolja Silver-Blood, chronicling an ignorant Nord's journey to Ald'Ruhn with a Hlaalu guide. The narrator confidently misidentifies Dunmer gods, conflates Nordic and Imperial divines, and reduces the Great Houses to simplistic gimmicks. A blight storm forces the pair into the Fighters' Guild alongside stranded House delegates, who argue and mock the narrator's foolishness. A publisher's note reveals the Sneezing Horker Historical Society adapted the original mainland setting to Vvardenfell, capitalizing on the Imperial Geographics Society's notoriously inaccurate maps and confusing settlement names.
topic_desc_basic: A satirical book by Frolja Silver-Blood about an ignorant Nord's misadventures in Morrowind, confidently misunderstanding Dunmer religion, the Great Houses, and Nordic traditions while traveling to Ald'Ruhn.

title: A Dunce in Morrowind, vol. 3
topic_desc: The third volume of the comedic travel series 'A Dunce in Morrowind,' authored by Frolja Silver-Blood and attributed to the late Ferana Adrethi. The narrative follows a bumbling Nord protagonist and his Dunmer companion Remyn through a series of misadventures in Morrowind, including imprisonment in Ald'Ruhn on suspicion of murdering a Telvanni woman, a jailbreak via Divine Intervention, and a disastrous Mages' Guild teleportation that strands them in the Dejasyte, a poisonous salt wasteland off Vvardenfell. The work satirizes Great House politics, cultural tensions between Nords and Dunmer, and the hazards of provincial travel. A publisher's note records that Ferana Adrethi perished during a bar brawl provoked by her characters' remarks about House Dres, leaving the series unfinished at volume four.
topic_desc_basic: A comedic travel narrative by Frolja Silver-Blood following a bumbling Nord's misadventures in Morrowind. The third volume recounts his imprisonment in Ald'Ruhn on suspicion of murder, a magical jailbreak, and a botched teleportation that strands him in a poisonous wasteland. The series satirizes Great House politics and Nord-Dunmer cultural tensions.

title: A Dunce in Morrowind, vol. 4
topic_desc: The fourth volume of the travel narrative compiled by Frolja Silver-Blood, continuing Ferana Andrethi's account of a bungling Nord's journey through Morrowind. This installment depicts the narrator and his Dunmer companion Remyn Sadrethi surviving the toxic Dejasyte salt plains of the southern Deshaan. Rescued by a Zoar-hide trader, the Nord is knocked unconscious and wakes imprisoned in Ald Horak, a Dres settlement that strictly forbids outlander entry. The narrative satirizes Dunmer xenophobia through a relentlessly ranting guard, and provides observations on local survival adaptations such as Salt Beetle water packs, Zoarskin buckled clothing, and the use of striped guar by local guards. The Sheezing Horker Historical Society published this continuation using accounts from sailors near Tear and Ald Horak.
topic_desc_basic: A satirical travel narrative by Frolja Silver-Blood chronicling a foolish Nord's disastrous journey through the toxic Dejasyte salt plains of southern Morrowind and his imprisonment in the strict Dres settlement of Ald Horak.

title: A Dunce in Morrowind, vol. 5
topic_desc: The fifth volume of Frolja Silver-Blood's comedic travel series, recounting the Nord narrator's misadventures in Morrowind. After being expelled from Fort Lutemoth due to the overwhelming stench of the Deshaan salt plains, the narrator and his long-suffering companion Remyn find themselves at Savos Manor in Akamora. There, they encounter Ovar Savos, an overeager young retainer of House Indoril desperate to perform an act of charity to advance in his House. When the travelers refuse his aid, Ovar threatens them with a crossbow to force his generosity upon them, only to be thwarted by the narrator's oblivious literalism. A publisher's note identifies Ovar as an adaptation of the traditional eastern Skyrim comedic skit character Ovar Sandos.
topic_desc_basic: A comedic travelogue by Frolja Silver-Blood detailing a Nord's bungling misadventures in Morrowind, featuring an encounter with an overzealous House Indoril retainer near Akamora.

title: A Dunce in Morrowind, vol. 6
topic_desc: The sixth volume of Frolja Silver-Blood's comedic travelogue, recounting the Nord narrator's encounter with Tholas, a forgetful House Telvanni magister. Tholas hosts the narrator and his companion Remyn in a Telvanni mushroom tower, expressing gratitude for a murder in Ald'Ruhn that eliminated a rival's staff member and advanced his political standing. The magister's eccentricity extends to an obsessive fascination with Nordic culture and an inability to recall his own schemes. Through farcical dialogue, the narrator's profound ignorance is showcased as he unknowingly admits to a Morag Tong assassination, dismisses Akavir as fictional, and conflates Trinimac with Orkey, all while Tholas celebrates these absurdities as profound insights. The work satirizes both Nordic obliviousness and Telvanni eccentricity.
topic_desc_basic: A comedic travelogue by Frolja Silver-Blood, following a dim-witted Nord's misadventures in Morrowind. This volume recounts his encounter with an eccentric House Telvanni magister who celebrates the narrator's unwitting involvement in an assassination.

title: A Dunce in Morrowind, vol. 7
topic_desc: The seventh volume of Frolja Silver-Blood's travel narrative, continuing the misadventures of the self-proclaimed scholar and his Hlaalu companion Remyn. Aboard a ship from Port Telvannis, the two are captured by an Argonian agent of the Dark Brotherhood. The Argonian reveals he has pursued them from Ald'Ruhn, believing they interfered with a contracted assassination of a Telvanni councillor—a writ he claims the Morag Tong improperly usurped from the Brotherhood. Central to the dispute is Frolja's enchanted axe, Niptickler, which the Argonian insists is proof of their involvement. The volume explores the fraught intersection of the two assassin guilds and Telvanni bodyguard practices, while the Argonian remains convinced that Frolja's buffoonish persona is a calculated disguise.
topic_desc_basic: A travel narrative by Frolja Silver-Blood recounting his capture at sea by an Argonian Dark Brotherhood agent. The assassin accuses Frolja and his companion of stealing a contracted kill from the Brotherhood, a dispute involving the Morag Tong and a Telvanni councillor.

title: A Dunce in Morrowind, vol. 8
topic_desc: The concluding volume of Frolja Silver-Blood's comedic travel series, recounting a self-important Nord scholar's misadventures in Morrowind. As the narrator prepares to depart for Skyrim via silt strider from Balmora—which he insists on calling 'Stoneforest'—his Dunmer companion Remyn confronts him about rumors that he is a Morag Tong assassin who killed a Telvanni councillor. The narrator deflects with characteristic obtuseness. A woman from outside Khuul returns his stolen belongings, revealing herself not as the suspected witch but as a necromancer devoted to Mehrunes Dagon. The publisher's note discloses that the late Ferana Adrethi planned to conclude the series with a 'find the Morag Tong' mystery, and that the Sneezing Horker Historical Society of Winterhold continues to generate sequels. The work satirizes Nord provincialism and scholarly pretension through its narrator's comical ignorance.
topic_desc_basic: A comedic travel narrative by Frolja Silver-Blood, a self-proclaimed scholar of the College of Winterhold, recounting his bumbling journey through Morrowind alongside his Dunmer companion Remyn. This final volume sees the narrator departing for Skyrim while Remyn questions whether he is secretly a Morag Tong assassin.

title: A Dunmer's Guide to The Reach
topic_desc: A Dunmer's Guide to The Reach is a travel guide written by Giras Daroso for Dunmer journeying to the Reach in Skyrim. Daroso corrects the common Dunmer assumption that all of Skyrim resembles the cold northern lands of House Redoran, noting the Reach's temperate climate, deciduous forests, and mesas reminiscent of Vvardenfell's foyadas. He advises traveling by boat from Blacklight to Haafingar, then by river barge down the Karth to Markarth. For the pious, he warns that Temple facilities are scarce, recommending travelers bring their own prayer books, though he notes a hostel and house temple in Markarth run by Vadas Marvani. Daroso cautions that while western Nords are preoccupied with harassing Breton and Redguard communities, the native Reachmen are dangerous and their villages harbor marauders. He also records ongoing Yokudo-Nordic unrest in Dragonstar at the time of writing.
topic_desc_basic: A travel guide by Giras Daroso advising Dunmer on traveling to the Reach in Skyrim, covering transportation to Markarth, scarce Temple resources, and the dangers posed by local Reachmen and ongoing unrest in Dragonstar.

record_links.display_name: A Dunmer's Guide to The Reach

title: A History of Almalexia
topic_desc: Alym Feneru's historical treatise chronicles the city of Almalexia, formerly Mournhold, framing it as the enduring center of Dunmer civilization. The account traces the capital from its Chimer founding and golden age under Lord Nerevar, through the devastation of the War of the First Council and Mehrunes Dagon's destruction of the old city, to its meticulous reconstruction by Sotha Sil and renaming after the Tribunal god. The narrative presents a staunchly orthodox Tribunal Temple perspective: it reveres the Tribunal's ascent, praises Vivec's truces with invading Empires as salvation, and dismisses the Dwemer founding rumor as disrespectful. It concludes by celebrating the current order under King Llethan and Lady Almalexia, omitting or reframing controversies to affirm divine stewardship over the capital.
topic_desc_basic: Alym Feneru's treatise chronicles the city of Almalexia, formerly Mournhold, as the enduring center of Dunmer civilization. Tracing the capital from its Chimer founding through devastation and reconstruction, it presents a staunchly orthodox Tribunal Temple perspective that reveres the Tribunal's ascent and praises Vivec's imperial truces as salvation.

title: A History of Saturalia
topic_desc: Eadwyn Arkidge's treatise traces the evolution of the wintertide festival Saturalia from its pagan-Nedic origins to its modern Imperial form. The work details how the early midwinter feast honored Sadhuill, a now-forgotten Bjoulsae and Wayrest Nedic deity of merriment later identified with Sanguine or Dibella. Arkidge attributes the holiday's transformation to Governor Saturio, Tiber Septim's early Third Era interim governor of Wayrest. By deliberately adopting Sadhuilli practices—distributing gifts and communal drinking—Saturio integrated himself into local tradition while substituting the Imperial gods Dibella, Mara, and Arkay for the heathen deity. Within three years, Sadhuill vanished from celebrations, and Saturio himself was posthumously declared a saint of the Imperial Cult. The work remains a significant account of religious syncretism and cultural assimilation in High Rock.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly work by Eadwyn Arkidge tracing the wintertide festival Saturalia from its origins as a midwinter feast for the Nedic god Sadhuill in Wayrest to its modern Imperial celebration, detailing how Governor Saturio replaced the pagan deity with Imperial gods and was himself later venerated as Saint Saturio.

title: A Million Eyed Insect Dreaming
topic_desc: A Million Eyed Insect Dreaming is a fragmentary Ashlander account of Veloth's spiritual conquests. It denounces the Tribunal as a hermaphroditic shapeshifter demon, Almsivi, born as a dreamborn doppelganger of Sul-Alandro. The text claims this entity murdered Hortator Nerevar, blasted Alandro's memories into the Wraithmail, and later kidnapped and shattered the prophet Veloth, imprisoning him within Lie Rock at the heart of Vivec. The narrative follows the mabrigash Bar-Ziah Sul, who, guided by her ancestor's whispers, sought to free Veloth. At a transdimensional crossing, an apparition of the Emperor awaited; Bar-Ziah sacrificed Veloth to save him, trading history and honor. Upon entering the opened Lie Rock, her host found only golden footprints dissolving into nix-mongrel images. The tale is recorded by Bar-Ziah's nix companion, the titular dreaming insect.
topic_desc_basic: A Million Eyed Insect Dreaming is an Ashlander text denouncing the Tribunal as a demon that murdered Nerevar and imprisoned the prophet Veloth within Lie Rock. It recounts the mabrigash Bar-Ziah Sul's attempt to free Veloth by making a sacrifice to an Emperor apparition, only to find his prison empty.

title: A Most Unfortunate Party
topic_desc: Ardarlunwe of Sunhold, an Altmer mage, authored this satirical account of attending a royal party in Wayrest at the invitation of the King. The narrative chronicles a disastrous journey from Alinor, during which Ardarlunwe's companion perishes, pirates attack the vessel, and the passengers nearly starve. Upon arriving in Wayrest, Ardarlunwe finds the city and its Breton inhabitants crude and culturally inferior. The party itself proves catastrophic: a hanged boy is discovered in the entrance hall, and guards begin slaughtering guests as entertainment. Ardarlunwe escapes by magical recall. The work serves as a vehicle for extreme Altmer cultural supremacism, using the derogatory term 'nemer' for humans and expressing unrelenting disdain for Breton architecture, customs, and hospitality.
topic_desc_basic: A satirical travelogue by the Altmer mage Ardarlunwe of Sunhold recounting a disastrous journey from Alinor to attend a royal party in Wayrest. The narrative showcases extreme Altmer cultural supremacism, depicting Breton society as crude and barbaric, and culminates in the party's violent collapse.

title: A Murder of Crows
topic_desc: A Murder of Crows is a martial narrative recounting a night assault by Imperial resistance fighters upon a Bosmer encampment at the ruins of Crowhaven during the Camoran Usurper's campaigns across Colovia. The tale follows Aemilius, a survivor of the sack of Kvatch, whose fighters ambush the Wood Elf camp only to face reanimated corpses conjured by an Altmer necromancer allied with the Camoranite forces. The story culminates in Aemilius slaying the necromancer, collapsing the undead, and preparing to execute surrendered prisoners out of personal vengeance. The work blends battlefield action with themes of grief, loss, and the dehumanizing effects of prolonged conflict, reflecting the suffering inflicted upon Colovian communities by the Camoranite horde. Its significance lies in dramatizing a turbulent chapter of western Tamrielic history through the perspective of common soldiers rather than generals or nobles.
topic_desc_basic: A Murder of Crows is a popular tale of Imperial resistance fighters battling Wood Elf forces and undead at the ruins of Crowhaven during the Camoran Usurper's rampage across Colovia. The story follows soldiers driven by revenge for losses suffered in the Camoranite invasion, including the sack of Kvatch.

title: A Noble's Best Tricks
topic_desc: A guide by Sir Dorthan Moros offering ten pieces of advice for nobles on personal habits, social influence, and leveraging aristocratic status.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Sir Dorthan Moros outlining ten practical tips for nobles, covering daily habits, social charm, and the advantages of wealth and rank.

title: A Nobleman's Garden
topic_desc: A Nobleman's Garden by Neril Sevuro is a treatise on the spiritual and philosophical significance of horticulture within House Indoril tradition. Sevuro presents his prayer garden as a microcosm of the world and a tool for cultivating noble duty. Each planting embodies a spiritual lesson: sweetbarrels represent the progression from painful resistance to numinous vision; timsa flowers, descended from Saint Timsa-of-the-Long-Hours, symbolize faith's triumph over profane sorcery; fireferns, nurtured by hearth-ash of holy offerings, demonstrate how divine law fosters enduring citizens; and noble sedge, grown from Second Era cuttings, embodies continuity and eternal harmony. A central inscribed stone serves as his legacy. Sevuro frames the Indoril lord's birthright and burden as the wise stewardship of both garden and world, interpreting horticultural discipline as essential to guiding descendants along righteous paths.
topic_desc_basic: A Nobleman's Garden by Neril Sevuro is a treatise in which an Indoril lord explains the spiritual purpose of his prayer garden. Sevuro presents the cultivation of specific plants as allegories for noble duty, spiritual progression, and the endurance of faith, framing the garden as a microcosm of the world that an Indoril lord is bound to wisely steward.

title: A Nord's Summary of the Reach
topic_desc: A Nord's Summary of the Reach is a pro-Nord account of western Skyrim's Reach hold, celebrating its recent conquest from Bretons and Redguards while warning travelers of ongoing dangers. The author characterizes the region as an unusually fertile, warm land of mesas and diverse populations under Nord governance, contrasting it with Skyrim's frozen interior. The work details the Reach's three jarldoms—Midkarth under Jarl Barda, the Sundered Hills under Jarl Horir, and the Karthwasten Cession under Jarl Jona—while acknowledging persistent threats from Reachmen bandits, Redguard guerrillas, and hostile creatures.
topic_desc_basic: A Nord's Summary of the Reach is a book describing Skyrim's western Reach hold from a Nordic viewpoint, covering its warm climate, diverse populace, and the recent Nordic reconquest of the territory from Bretons and Redguards.

record_links.display_name: A Nord's Summary of the Reach

title: A Pearl Betwixt Empires, vol. 1
topic_desc: A Pearl Betwixt Empires, Volume I is the first part of a survey of the island of Cathnoquey, adapted from the journals of Clavus Temperian, a scholar who voyaged to the archipelago in 3E 414. The work describes the Chimeri-Quey, descendants of the ancient Chimer who live aboard flotilla cities on the Padomaic Ocean. These settlements consist of ancient Greatships connected by bridges and kelp-net farms, supplemented by diverse outer vessels of foreign origin. The Chimeri-Quey venerate St. Veloth and the Good Daedra, reject settled life as decadent, and govern through elected Wave Councils led by a Shore-Khan. The volume also notes the Keptu-Quey as Cathnoquey's co-existing culture. The text reflects the Imperial Geographical Society's renewed interest in the Empire's eastern territories during Uriel Septim VII's era of consolidation.
topic_desc_basic: A Pearl Betwixt Empires, Volume I is a scholarly survey of the island of Cathnoquey, an Imperial territory in the Padomaic Ocean. It describes the Chimeri-Quey, seafaring elves who live aboard floating flotilla cities, and the Keptu-Quey, their co-existing human neighbors. The work is adapted from the journals of a scholar who visited the archipelago in 3E 414.

title: A Pearl Betwixt Empires, vol. 2
topic_desc: A Pearl Betwixt Empires, vol. 2 is the second volume of an Imperial geographical and ethnographic survey of the Cathnoquey Territory in the Padomaic Ocean. It details the archipelago's bleak, volcanic terrain and natural resources, noting Imperial difficulties exploiting sulphur and glass deposits due to Keptu-Quey resistance. The work examines the Keptu-Quey people, whose origins remain disputed; scholars variously propose Nedic-Keptic, Akaviri, or mixed ancestry, citing their bull heraldry and physical traits as evidence. It describes their mysterious conical citadels—rock fortresses claimed to be shaped by ancestral sacrifice rather than masonry—and their matriarchal, inter-generational family structures. The volume also contrasts the land-bound Keptu-Quey with the seaborne Chimeri-Quey, documenting their deepening social ties, and notes the Imperial quarantine of the southern island of Llénnöcöcönnéll since 3E 289.
topic_desc_basic: The second volume of an Imperial survey of the Cathnoquey archipelago, covering the territory's geography, resources, and the disputed origins, mysterious citadels, and family structures of the Keptu-Quey people.

title: A Scholar's Guide to Nymphs
topic_desc: Vondham Barres's personal account challenging the scholarly neglect of nymphs. A former Imperial University scholar, Barres argues that prejudice reduces these shy beings to objects of lust, ignoring their profound wisdom. After mastering the melodious nymph tongue with assistance from the School of Julianos in Sentinel, he spent months gaining the trust of a nymph named Ayalea in a coastal Hammerfell grotto. She instructed him in deep woodland lore and an experiential approach to knowledge. Following the manuscript's submission, an editor notes Barres abandoned his university position and vanished from the civilized world, his current whereabouts unknown.
topic_desc_basic: Vondham Barres's account challenging the scholarly neglect of nymphs. The former Imperial University scholar documents mastering the nymph language and learning woodland lore from a nymph named Ayalea off the coast of Hammerfell. He deposited the manuscript and subsequently vanished.

title: A Short History of Karthwasten
topic_desc: This historical treatise by Nerus Lalrav, steward to Jarl Jona of Dragonstar, chronicles Karthwasten from its late Merethic origins as an Aldmeri farming settlement through its absorption into the Nordic hold of the Reach under King Vrage. It details centuries of frontier conflict against Nedic tribes, Rourken Dwemer, and Yokudan warriors, the town's sack and annexation by Dragonstar forces in 3E 136 following its alliance with Potema during the War of the Red Diamond, and its reconquest by Nordic forces during the War of the Bend'r-Makh in 3E 396. The Treaty of Chorrol returned Karthwasten to Nordic governance under Jarl Jona the Ansei-Ender. Written from a pro-Nordic administrative perspective, the work celebrates the restoration of Nordic rule and the city's revitalization while acknowledging the displacement of Redguard inhabitants to the poor quarter.
topic_desc_basic: A historical account by Nerus Lalrav, steward to Jarl Jona of Dragonstar, tracing Karthwasten from its Merethic-era settlement through its incorporation into the Nordic Kingdom of the Reach after the War of the Bend'r-Makh. The work covers the town's role as a fortified border settlement and its shifting governance between Nordic and Redguard powers.

title: A Short History of the Empires
topic_desc: A historical work surveying the successive empires that have ruled Cyrodiil and Tamriel, from the Ayleid Hegemony through the Third Empire of the Septims. The author presents a distinctly pro-Imperial and devoutly Divines-worshipping perspective, framing the Alessian Rebellion as a recognition that Ayleid divine mandate had passed, and venerating Tiber Septim's ascension as Tiber Imperator. The narrative traces the cyclical pattern of imperial rise and fragmentation, attributing collapses to religious heresy, dynastic assassination, or foreign misrule, while praising the administrative innovations of the Reman dynasty and the enlightened guidance of Uriel VII. The text notably dismisses the Marukhati faith as blasphemous and characterizes the Akaviri Potentates' governance as unfit for Tamriel despite their wisdom.
topic_desc_basic: A historical book chronicling the major empires that have ruled Cyrodiil, from the Ayleid Hegemony through the First and Second Empires to the current Third Empire of the Septim dynasty.

record_links.display_name: A Short History of the Empires

title: A Study of the Locked Novel
topic_desc: A scholarly treatise by Maros Quinnus examining the Altmer literary tradition of locked novels—obscure Second Era works written for specific aristocratic circles, deliberately devoid of exposition, and used as coded communication between clan members. Quinnus traces how these novels served as tools of group identity and secrecy, citing House Vilyas and their novel Stinging, the Obtuse Barb in Dragonflesh Ripped as a key example. He argues that reliance on such opaque communication may have weakened Altmer resistance to external threats, while noting that modern diaspora communities have repurposed surviving locked novels with new interpretations, inadvertently repeating their original social function.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise by Maros Quinnus on the Altmer locked novels of the late Second Era. These deliberately obscure works were written for specific aristocratic circles and used as coded communication between clan members, a practice Quinnus argues may have weakened Altmer resistance to the Maormer and Sload.
tags: Stinging the Obtuse Barb in Dragonflesh Ripped

title: A Study on Guar
topic_desc: Gidiron Yoiua's travelogue and naturalist study of the common guar, written following Vvardenfell's reorganization opening the island to Imperial scholarship. The work contrasts the domesticated common guar with the larger, ferocious tiger guar of the Deshaan plains, which Tiber Septim famously misidentified. Yoiua observes the common guar's regional behaviors: their avoidance of the swampy Bitter Coast, their foraging and territorial habits in the Ascadian Isles, and their vital role as beasts of burden in the ashlands, where thick skin and protected eyes allow them to endure blight storms. The author notes Redoran mounted patrols and Ashlander herding, and provides practical advice for travelers, emphasizing that despite a wild guar's capacity to trample, the species is meek and easily demoralized.
topic_desc_basic: Gidiron Yoiua's naturalist study of the common guar, contrasting it with the larger, ferocious tiger guar of the Deshaan plains. The travelogue details the common guar's regional behaviors across Vvardenfell and its vital role as a beast of burden in the ashlands.

title: A Traditional Sload Tale
topic_desc: A Traditional Sload Tale is a cautionary narrative presented by an elder Sload to larvae, recounting the fate of a young, ambitious Sload named K'tala. Enticed by the wealth of a reclusive soul merchant, K'tala employed banshees, rusalka, and phantasms to locate the hidden treasury on the northern coast of Pankor. After a painstaking infiltration past reanimated sharks, K'tala discovered not riches but the skeletal remains of previous seekers. The cave was a soulsnare trap, and K'tala's soul was claimed by the very merchant whose fortune was sought. The tale serves as a catechism for Sload young, emphasizing patience, cunning, and the dangers of hotheadedness in Sload society, where greed and deception are paramount.
topic_desc_basic: A Traditional Sload Tale is a cautionary story told by an elder Sload to larvae about a young Sload named K'tala, who sought the hidden treasury of a wealthy soul merchant on Pankor, only to fall victim to a soulsnare trap, reinforcing Sload cultural values of patience and cunning.

title: A Treatise on Calcinator Use
topic_desc: This treatise outlines an Argonian alchemical tradition holding that calcinator alignment must follow the lunar phases. It asserts that during a full moon the device should face due south, oriented toward the Southron pole star, with precise adjustments made from star charts to account for the star's offset from true south. As the moon wanes, the calcinator is rotated by one twenty-eighth of a circle per night—clockwise in the northern hemisphere and counter-clockwise in the southern. The device must be positioned so moonlight falls across half of it, or fully exposed during a new moon. The author claims this regimen yields a marginal increase in distillate purity, acknowledging the effect is slight. The work preserves a distinctive Black Marsh practice linking astronomical observation to alchemical apparatus configuration.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise detailing an Argonian alchemical method for positioning calcinators according to the lunar phases and the Southron pole star, intended to marginally increase the purity of distilled preparations.

title: Advances in Lock Picking
topic_desc: A practical manual on lockpicking written by a self-described experienced thief. The author advocates carrying bent lockpicks to counter angled keyholes and recommends copper picks for their malleability, cautioning that their fragility demands care. To address locks with irregular springs, the author advises holding a torch near the mechanism; the applied heat normalizes the springs' tension, making them easier to manipulate. The work reflects an empirical, tradesman-like approach to security rather than a theoretical one.
topic_desc_basic: A practical guide on lockpicking written by an experienced thief. It covers techniques for dealing with angled keyholes using bent picks, the advantages and fragility of copper picks, and a method for using a torch's heat to normalize irregular lock springs.

title: Aebis Feathers
topic_desc: Aebis feathers are white and blue plumage harvested from porcelain aebises. These elegant birds are known to circle the inland skies near Cyrodiil's Strident Coast.
topic_desc_basic: Aebis feathers are white and blue feathers taken from the porcelain aebis, an elegant bird that circles the inland skies near Cyrodiil's Strident Coast.

title: Aetherial Ephemeris
topic_desc: The Aetherial Ephemeris and Astrological Almanac is a technical reference published by the Imperial Astrological Society—also identified as the Guild of Astrologers—for mariners, surveyors, mages, and travelers. It provides detailed tabular data on the positions of significant aetherial bodies at regular intervals, alongside predicted trajectories, eclipses, and occultations. The almanac covers Masser, Secunda, the Thirteen Patrons, and various natural and artificial astronomical objects. Crucially, it includes instructions for observing and recording the unpredictable movements of the Serpent constellation, enabling navigators to avoid ill-omened headings. Each printed copy also incorporates localized tide tables and lunar phase readings relevant to the issuing office.
topic_desc_basic: The Aetherial Ephemeris and Astrological Almanac is a navigational and astronomical reference published by the Imperial Astrological Society. It provides tables tracking the positions and predicted trajectories of celestial bodies like Masser, Secunda, and the constellations, alongside tide readings and warnings about the unpredictable Serpent constellation.

title: Ahzirr Trajijazaeri
topic_desc: Ahzirr Trajijazaeri is the public manifesto of the Khajiiti insurgent organization known as the Renrijra Krin. Written to explain the group's philosophy to sympathetic non-Khajiiti, the text outlines six guiding principles it terms 'thjizzrini'—foolish concepts—since the Ta'agra language lacks a word for rules. These tenets advocate bravery against the Empire, pragmatic retreat, the enjoyment of life's pleasures, ruthless combat, generosity toward displaced Khajiiti, and the forceful reclamation of territory seized by the Count of Leyawiin. The work frames the Renrijra Krin's struggle as a political war for the return of ancestral lands around Lake Makapi and the River Malapi, prioritizing popular support and sabotage over conventional warfare. It presents a worldview that embraces contradiction, viewing the group's derogatory moniker as a weapon of psychological defiance.
topic_desc_basic: Ahzirr Trajijazaeri is the public manifesto of the Renrijra Krin, a Khajiiti group fighting to reclaim lands taken by the Count of Leyawiin. The book outlines the organization's guiding principles, advocating bravery, pragmatic retreat, enjoyment of life, ruthless combat, generosity to displaced Khajiiti, and the forceful reclamation of territory.

title: Alchemist's Globe
topic_desc: An alchemical ingredient of uncertain natural origin. Its properties and common applications remain poorly documented in standard herbal and alchemical references, leaving its precise alchemical character a matter of specialist study rather than common knowledge.
topic_desc_basic: An uncommon alchemical ingredient of uncertain natural origin, valued by practitioners of the alchemical arts.

title: Alit Meat
topic_desc: Alit meat is the flesh of the two-legged predator of the same name. It is bitter and chewy, but it has modest magical properties.
topic_desc_basic: Hunters and travelers in Morrowind sometimes carry the flesh of the alit, a two-legged predatory beast. Though tough and bitter to eat, it is known to hold minor magical virtue.

title: Alkanet Flower
topic_desc: Alkanet flowers are small blue blooms native to Cyrodiil. Alchemists value them as a common reagent for their solutive properties, and hunters occasionally gather the flower for practical field preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Alkanet flowers are small blue flowers that grow in Cyrodiil.

title: Almalexia Speaks to Children
topic_desc: A recorded address by Almalexia to the people of Mournhold at the close of the Second Era, responding to widespread anxiety following the Armistice and the fall of Khalaan. The Goddess rebukes those who question the Tribunal's judgment, contrasting the Dunmer's former wretchedness under Daedric deception and foreign predation with their present civilization, which she credits entirely to the Almsivi. She catalogues the Tribunal's martial triumphs over the Remanite legions, Mehrunes Dagon, the Kamal, and the Dwemer, asserting that the gods' deeds and wisdom place them beyond mortal scrutiny. Almalexia frames her condescension as maternal love, warning that while mortal voices are easily silenced, she has chosen to listen and demands no further dissent. She subsequently ordered her Archcanon to distribute the transcription throughout Morrowind, ensuring her authoritative justification for the Treaty reached every settlement.
topic_desc_basic: A transcription of Almalexia's address to the people of Mournhold at the end of the Second Era. The work records her defense of the Tribunal's decision to sign the Armistice with the Empire, asserting that the Dunmer owe their civilization and safety entirely to the gods and possess no right to question their judgment. Copies were ordered distributed and read across Morrowind.

title: Aloe Vera Pulp
topic_desc: Aloe vera pulp is a thick paste obtained by crushing the entire aloe vera plant rather than harvesting its leaves alone. While the leaves themselves possess alchemical properties, the whole-plant pulp exhibits more potent qualities. It is widely employed in remedies against diseases and poisons, making it a valued and common import from Cyrodiil. The aloe vera plant grows naturally in Colovia, Hammerfell, and Elsweyr.
topic_desc_basic: Aloe vera pulp is a thick paste made by crushing the whole aloe vera plant. Used in many remedies against diseases and poisons, it is a common import from Cyrodiil. The plant grows in Colovia, Hammerfell, and Elsweyr.

title: Alphyn Claw
topic_desc: Alphyn claws are harvested from alphyns, large predatory beasts that inhabit remote areas of the Strident Coast in Cyrodiil. The claw serves as an alchemical ingredient, though acquisition requires sourcing from one of the region's more dangerous predators. Because alphyns favor isolated terrain far from settled districts, their claws seldom reach markets beyond the Strident Coast, remaining a regional reagent familiar chiefly to alchemists and hunters who operate along Cyrodiil's southwestern shores.
topic_desc_basic: Alphyn claws are an alchemical ingredient taken from alphyns, large predators that roam remote stretches of the Strident Coast in Cyrodiil. Their distant habitat keeps them scarce in markets far from that coast.

title: Amber
topic_desc: Amber is a rare gemstone of non-mineral origin, formed from ancient fossilized tree resin rather than crystalline geological processes. Valued for its beauty and interesting magical properties, it serves alchemists as a reagent capable of conferring resistance to fire. While of limited practical use to most of Tamriel beyond this alchemical application, amber smithing is an ancient and secretive craft in the Shivering Isles. There, master smiths of Bliss forge amber into weapons and armor, passing the tradition to a chosen apprentice and hiding matrices throughout the realm before their death. Amber is common in the Shivering Isles, where it forms in vast quantities within the root tunnels beneath the surface; severe trauma to the root walls triggers amber deposits as a natural defense mechanism. Gnarls, the animated plants tending these tunnels, clear away the deposits and occasionally bring them to the surface.
topic_desc_basic: Amber is a rare and valuable gemstone formed from fossilized tree resin rather than mineral origins. It possesses interesting magical properties useful to alchemists.

title: Ambergris
topic_desc: Ambergris is a solid, waxy substance produced within the digestive system of whales. As an alchemical ingredient of marine origin, it is uncommon in much of Tamriel, where whales are rarely encountered along the coasts. Its waxy consistency and unusual provenance distinguish it from more common reagents gathered from plants and land-dwelling creatures.
topic_desc_basic: Ambergris is a solid, waxy substance that forms in the digestive system of whales. It serves as an alchemical ingredient, though its marine origin makes it a rarity in much of Tamriel.

title: Amberwing Butterfly Wing
topic_desc: The wing of the amberwing butterfly, valued by alchemists and hunters for its properties. It is harvested from the amberwing butterfly, a creature of natural origin. As a specialized ingredient, it is not commonly found in guaranteed stock, typically appearing only in randomized supplies associated with the Reach.
topic_desc_basic: A wing taken from an amberwing butterfly, used in alchemy.

title: Amethyst
topic_desc: Amethyst is a purple crystal found in geodes near volcanic rock. Valued for decoration, it is commonly fashioned into jewelry and adorns temples and tombs. In Argonian tradition, a wedding proposal band features three flawless amethysts representing the couple and the Hist. When crushed, amethyst yields alchemical preparations that cure common diseases and resist poison, though it induces weariness. Notable mining sites include Dak'fron, Kulati, and Zareth M'Kai in Hammerfell.
topic_desc_basic: Amethyst is a purple gemstone with modest magical qualities, commonly used in jewelry and decoration.

title: Ametrine
topic_desc: Ametrine is a crystalline mineral substance valued as an alchemical ingredient. It occurs as a gem-quality stone, likely forming within geological deposits rather than deriving from any flora or fauna. Its specific alchemical properties and applications remain a subject for specialist study, as the stone is not commonly encountered in general trade or standard alchemical supply. Unlike many common reagents, it does not circulate through typical merchant stock or randomized loot, making it a relatively rare curio. Its scarcity and mineral nature suggest it holds particular interest for alchemists and hunters seeking uncommon reagents for specialized preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Ametrine is a rare crystalline mineral used in alchemy. It is not commonly found in trade or general merchant supplies.

title: An Alchemist's Guide to Skooma
topic_desc: A treatise on skooma production and alternative alchemical ingredients by Jeannot Lapage, a producer for the Mane's Court.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly work by Jeannot Lapage detailing the production of skooma from moon sugar and nightshade, and exploring alternative ingredients across Tamriel.

title: An Illustrated Guide to Fire
topic_desc: An Illustrated Guide to Fire, authored by Abraxas K'Eje, is a specialized alchemical reference work cataloging the distinctive flame colors produced when various substances burn. The text systematically pairs common and rare reagents—including metals such as copper, iron, and quicksilver, alongside rarer materials like dragonbone, adamantium, and heartwood—with their corresponding flame hues. Its significance lies in providing alchemists and scholars a practical observational tool for identifying reagents through combustion, a method useful for verifying material purity or distinguishing between visually similar substances.
topic_desc_basic: An Illustrated Guide to Fire by Abraxas K'Eje is a reference work that catalogs the distinct colors of flame produced by burning various substances, from common metals to rare materials like dragonbone.

title: An Indoril's Garden
topic_desc: An anonymous tollmer's account of a young, non-verbal Indoril mer named Dorvon, whose physical and behavioral differences led his family to fear a Temple-ordered execution as impure. The work reflects on Molag Bal as a tester who prunes flaws to nurture essence, and reveals that Dorvon's fastidious tending of fire orchids ultimately brought prosperity to House Indoril through a prized perfume trade.
topic_desc_basic: A reflective account by an anonymous Indoril tollmer concerning a young mer named Dorvon, whose perceived impurities nearly led to his execution by Temple authorities, and whose unusual sensitivity to flowers ultimately benefited his House's perfume trade.

title: Analysis on the Asurani Writing
topic_desc: Eredictus Facilicius, an Imperial scholar, authored this analytical treatise examining the Dark Elf folktale Of Fire Ants and Hooms by Shissal Asurani. Written from a Western perspective and supplemented by Altmer collaborators, the work attempts to decode the text's layered metaphors and cultural significance. Facilicius identifies Asurani as a Buoyant Armiger and proposes that the folktale mirrors the multilayered teachings of Vivec, serving as a digestible spiritual allegory for Dunmer. He surveys existing theories, including Cantur Caelmoryn's popular argument that the tale is a metaphorical autobiography of Asurani's spiritual journey and relationship with his deity. Facilicius ultimately concludes the narrative functions as a Buoyant Armiger's instructional text, embedding heretical or esoteric meanings beneath a seemingly simple story of Ashlander-outlander friendship, much like the Thirty-Six Lessons of Vivec.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly treatise by Eredictus Facilicius analyzing the Dark Elf folktale Of Fire Ants and Hooms. It attempts to decode the story's layered metaphors and cultural significance from a Western perspective.

title: Ancestor Moth Wing
topic_desc: Ancestor Moth Wings are the delicate wings harvested from Ancestor Moths, uncommon insects native to Cyrodiil. Valued by alchemists and hunters, these wings possess distinct alchemical properties that make them a sought-after ingredient. The moths are active during both day and night, allowing for collection at any hour, though their uncommon nature keeps the wings from being readily abundant. As with other lepidopterans, a single moth typically yields a pair of wings.
topic_desc_basic: Ancestor Moth Wings are alchemical ingredients taken from Ancestor Moths, uncommon insects found in Cyrodiil.

title: Ancestral Tombs
topic_desc: Ancestral tombs are Dunmer burial vaults maintained by clan families to inter and venerate their departed kin, a tradition rooted in the ancient Velothi tribes of Resdayn. Cremated remains are housed in burial urns alongside ritual altars and significant possessions. Tombs range from single chambers to spacious, multi-roomed vaults. The Dunmer guard their sacred relationship with their ancestors intensely, rarely permitting outsiders entry. Spirits of the dead often linger as animated sentries; while foreigners mistake this for necromancy, the Dunmer despise conventional necromancy and emphasize the distinct nature of their ancestor worship. Open tombs receive regular visits for meditation and rites, though families must sometimes hire mercenaries to clear infestations of Daedra or vampires. Abandoned tombs, long haunted by the spirits of extinct lines, provide most of the limited Western knowledge of these practices.
topic_desc_basic: Ancestral tombs are Dunmer burial vaults used to inter and venerate clan ancestors. The Dunmer intensely guard these sacred sites and rarely allow outsiders inside. The spirits of the dead often remain as guardians, a practice foreigners sometimes mistake for necromancy.

title: Anchor of the Crimson Storm
topic_desc: The Anchor of the Crimson Storm is one of two immense anchors belonging to the TEM Crimson Storm, the flagship of Emperor Uriel V during his invasion of Akavir. The five-decked vessel reached Ionith but was severely damaged and scuttled on an isolated sandbar in 3E 289 during the Fleet's return to Tamriel. The loss of the flagship contributed heavily to the faltering supply lines that doomed the Legions wintering in Akavir. The wreck remained lost until 3E 377, when a Quey fishing vessel discovered it on a remote Padomaic sandbar. A Navy team dispatched from the Temaris garrison found only a crumbling hulk, but recovered the anchor. It was held at Temaris until 3E 389, the centennial of the Ionith disaster, when it was transferred to the Museum.
topic_desc_basic: The Anchor of the Crimson Storm is a massive relic from the TEM Crimson Storm, Emperor Uriel V's flagship during the Akavir invasion. Recovered from a Padomaic sandbar in 3E 377, it is currently displayed in the Museum.

title: And We Ate It To Become It
topic_desc: The Tsaesci creation myth, recounting a cosmogony structured around successive acts of the Striking, Biting, Slithering, Shedding, Reaching, and Laying. The narrative frames existence as a sequence of name-eggs, edible communications, and calculations, where naming generates reality and consumption preserves it. It describes the fragmentation of an original Egg into twelve worlds, the destruction of foreign alphabets, and the Tsaesci gift of a dead language to other beings. Through consuming the alphabet-virus and all source-information from the first serpents, the Tsaesci claim immortality. The myth culminates in the final name Tsaescence, which the Tsaesci ate to become, ending all variation. The work's alien vocabulary and logic make it a significant but difficult primary source for understanding Akaviri cosmology.
topic_desc_basic: A Tsaesci creation myth describing the origin of the world through a sequence of cosmic events centered on serpents, naming, and consumption. It explains how the Tsaesci achieved immortality and their final state, called Tsaescence, by consuming source-information.

record_links.display_name: And We Ate It To Become It

title: Anemic Twinstipe
topic_desc: Anemic Twinstipe is a botanical ingredient harvested from its namesake plant. Alchemists and hunters value it for its alchemical properties, though it remains a relatively uncommon find. Specimens are typically gathered from the wild rather than cultivated, appearing in the flora across certain Velothi regions.
topic_desc_basic: Anemic Twinstipe is a wild-growing plant ingredient valued by alchemists and foragers. It is found scattered across Velothi lands rather than cultivated.

title: Angelfish
topic_desc: Angelfish are a species of fish bearing distinctive blue and yellow coloration. They inhabit both freshwater and coastal marine waters within Cyrodiil and are valued as an alchemical ingredient.
topic_desc_basic: Angelfish are blue and yellow fish found in both freshwater and seawater in Cyrodiil. They are used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Anise Seeds
topic_desc: Anise seeds are a spice originating from the Summerset Isles. They are primarily valued as a culinary flavoring for desserts and liquor. In alchemical practice, they are recognized as a botanical ingredient, though their specific alchemical properties require personal experimentation or specialist knowledge to determine. Their exotic origin makes them a sought-after commodity outside their native province.
topic_desc_basic: Anise seeds are a spice originating from the Summerset Isles, widely used to flavor desserts and liquor.

title: Antimony Ore
topic_desc: Antimony ore is a mineral substance occasionally sought for alchemical work. Its properties and full alchemical character remain obscure, as it is not commonly encountered in standard trade or widely cataloged in typical apothecary references. The ore is not found among standard leveled supply lists, making it an uncommon and specialized reagent. You do not know where Antimony Ore is commonly found.
topic_desc_basic: Antimony ore is a mineral substance occasionally sought for alchemical work. It is not found among standard leveled supply lists, making it an uncommon and specialized reagent.

title: Antler Moth Wing
topic_desc: Antler Moth Wings are alchemical ingredients harvested from the Antler Moth, a creature native to Skyrim. The wings are obtained from the insect's remains and are valued by alchemists for their properties. As with other moth and butterfly parts, a typical specimen yields two wings. The ingredient circulates among apothecaries and suppliers through regional trade lists catering to Skyrim's alchemical markets.
topic_desc_basic: Antler Moth Wings are alchemical ingredients taken from the Antler Moth, a creature found in Skyrim. A single moth typically provides two wings for harvesting.

title: Aquamarine
topic_desc: Aquamarine is a form of beryl recognized by its clear, turquoise-blue hue. The gemstone occurs naturally within granite outcroppings. Beyond its ornamental value, aquamarine possesses notable alchemical properties; it is of particular interest for its magical qualities effective against poison.
topic_desc_basic: Aquamarine is a clear, turquoise-blue beryl gemstone valued for its magical qualities against poison.

title: Aquilegia Root Pulp
topic_desc: Aquilegia root pulp is a botanical preparation derived from the aquilegia plant. The root is processed to yield a usable alchemical substance. It grows in Cyrodiil, where foragers and hunters gather it from the wild. Alchemists value the pulp for its inherent properties, which become apparent when the substance is combined with other reagents. The plant's specific habitat and full alchemical character remain subjects of specialist study rather than common knowledge.
topic_desc_basic: Aquilegia root pulp is a prepared substance derived from the root of the aquilegia plant. It grows in Cyrodiil and is gathered as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Arcana and the Sciences
