topic_desc: A classification of magical and mundane disciplines documented by the College, encompassing classical schools, obscure fields, and the sciences.
topic_desc_basic: A College classification covering the classical schools of magic, obscure fields like divination and thaumaturgy, and mundane sciences such as botany and physics.

title: Arcturianism For Beginners
topic_desc: A treatise by Claude Telling examining the Arcturian Heresy, which claims Tiber Septim is a fabricated identity maintained by a secret society rather than a genuine god. The work frames Arcturianism as a radical offshoot of Numidianism, a historical theory defending the Numidium construct's role in the Tiber Wars. While traditional scholarship long dismissed Numidium, the Warp in the West vindicated historical Numidianism and revitalized Arcturianist thought, which now spreads among provincial populations as anti-Imperial sentiment. Telling notes that many self-described Arcturianists are political firebrands rather than philosophical adherents, though some exhibit disturbing compulsions like brass-fever. The author observes that Talos's divine presence is nonetheless tangible, raising unsettling theological questions if the Arcturianist fraud thesis holds true.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Claude Telling about the Arcturian Heresy, a conspiracy theory claiming Tiber Septim, or Talos, is a fabricated identity used by a secret society to rule Tamriel through deceit. The theory is a radical wing of Numidianism and has spread among anti-Imperial factions since the Warp in the West.

title: Argonian Skulls
topic_desc: A Dunmer account of two Argonian shaman skulls taken as war trophies during the Arnesian War. The first shaman fell to House Redoran at the battle of Han Hloadal, while the second was slain by House Dres hunters in the war's final days. The work presents the shamans as heathen leaders of Argonian assaults on Dunmer lands and frames their preserved skulls as symbols of Morrowind's ultimate victory and the shamans' refusal to submit.
topic_desc_basic: A record of two Argonian shaman skulls taken as trophies during the Arnesian War. One was captured by House Redoran at Han Hloadal, the other by House Dres late in the conflict. The text presents them as symbols of Dunmer victory.

title: Arithmetic for Barbarians
topic_desc: A humorous arithmetic primer cast as a cautionary tale between two barbarians, Gorg and Ulf, who share a hoard of coins. The text presents simple problems in addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, with each answer rendered in reversed spelling. Gorg persuades Ulf that counting will ensure a fair division, but the closing reveals that Gorg's numerical cunning leaves Ulf neither clever nor happy, implying violence follows regardless. The work satirizes the notion that arithmetic can civilize brute disputes, suggesting cunning merely redirects bloodshed rather than preventing it.
topic_desc_basic: A humorous instructional text presenting basic arithmetic through a story of two barbarians dividing a hoard of coins. It covers addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, but satirizes the idea that counting alone can settle disputes peacefully.

title: Ark'ay the God
topic_desc: Mymophonus the Scribe's work presents a mythic account of Ark'ay's apotheosis, proposing that the Divines were once mortal. It describes Ark'ay as a shopkeeper consumed by a book on existence's secrets. As plague claimed him, he prayed to Mara for time to study, arguing that birth and death allow souls to learn in the physical world. Mara offered him a choice: accept death or become the God of Birth and Death, eternally balancing the two and agonizing over the correctness of each decision. Ark'ay accepted the burden. The text is significant for advancing the theological view that the gods are not inherently different from mortals, and for framing divine duty as an eternal, uncertain sacrifice rather than a privilege.
topic_desc_basic: A religious text by Mymophonus the Scribe recounting the legend that Ark'ay was once a mortal shopkeeper. After a plague struck him while he studied a tome on existence, Mara offered him the choice to die or ascend as the God of Birth and Death, eternally balancing mortal souls.

title: Armies of the Usurper
topic_desc: Baeralorn's treatise on the Camoran Usurper's invasion of western Colovia, examining his unprecedented deployment of mass necromancy. The work details the fall of Anvil and Sutch, the raising of defeated rulers as mummified champions, and the necromancer corps that occupied conquered territory. It argues that while masterless undead and scattered necromancers still plague the region, the remaining lieutenants are too divided to reconstitute the threat, and western preparedness now makes such an invasion unlikely.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Baeralorn recounting the Camoran Usurper's invasion of western Colovia using mass necromancy, the destruction of Anvil and Sutch, and the lasting regional stigma and danger posed by remnants of his undead armies.

title: Arrow Moth Wing
topic_desc: Arrow moth wings are the wings of the arrow moth, a nocturnal insect native to Cyrodiil. Alchemists value these wings for their properties, and hunters typically harvest two wings from each specimen. The moths emerge only at night, making their collection a dusk-tide endeavor.
topic_desc_basic: Arrow moth wings are harvested from the arrow moth, a nocturnal insect found in Cyrodiil.

title: Arrowroot
topic_desc: Arrowroot is a botanical ingredient derived from the root of its namesake plant. Alchemists and hunters value the harvested root for its alchemical properties, incorporating it into various preparations. The plant grows in the wilds of Tamriel, with foragers most commonly encountering it across the temperate and tropical forests of Valendiil and Cyrodiil. As a naturally occurring flora, it is gathered in the field rather than cultivated or widely stocked by merchants.
topic_desc_basic: Arrowroot is a wild-growing plant root valued as an alchemical ingredient. Foragers harvest it from the wilderness, primarily across the forests of Valenwood and Cyrodiil.

title: Arrowroot Flower
topic_desc: The arrowroot flower is a botanical ingredient valued in alchemical practice. While its specific alchemical properties are documented by practitioners, the precise appearance and favored climate of the plant that yields it remain subjects of specialized study rather than common knowledge. The flower is recognized among alchemists and hunters for its contributions to potion-making, though its virtues are not widely known to the general populace.
topic_desc_basic: The arrowroot flower is a plant ingredient used in alchemy.

title: Arthorn Berry
topic_desc: The arthorn berry is a botanical ingredient gathered for both culinary and alchemical purposes. It circulates among general food provisions and ingredient stocks across various regions. Its dual presence in food and alchemical ingredient collections indicates it serves as common sustenance as well as a component in alchemical preparations. Beyond its identity as a berry and its circulation in general provisions, detailed documentation of its specific appearance, natural habitat, or alchemical character remains limited.
topic_desc_basic: The arthorn berry is a berry used for food and alchemy, found among general provisions and ingredient stocks in various regions.

title: As Shokhahn Am Jabikaam
topic_desc: As Shokhahn Am Jabikaam is a two-chapter text written in the Dunmer language. It presents a religious and historical account of the Chimer exodus from Summerset, the transformation of Trinimac into Malacath and his followers into the Orsimer, and the prophet Veloth's covenant with the Good Daedra—Azura, Boethiah, and Mephala. The work frames this schism as a deliberate rejection of Altmer ancestor worship and rigid tradition in favor of Daedric guidance, detailing the foundational mythos that separates the Chimer from their Aldmeri origins and the cursed Orsimer. It remains a significant, if esoteric, Dunmeri scripture on the origin of their covenant.
topic_desc_basic: As Shokhahn Am Jabikaam is a Dunmer-language text recounting the prophet Veloth's exodus from Summerset, the transformation of Trinimac into Malacath, and the Chimer's covenant with the Good Daedra.

title: As Shokhahn Am Morfijin
topic_desc: As Shokhahn Am Morfijin is a Dunmeris-language text recounting the early history of the Chimer. It narrates the Chimer's divergence from the Altmer and Orsimer, following the prophet Veloth and the Daedric Prince Mephala. The work details the Chimer warlord Aldis's conflict with a neighboring kingdom, his capture, and his subsequent betrayal of Mephala's secrets under duress. It further describes the kingdom of Relsear, the Bosmer's role in the conflict, and Veloth's journey to guide the Chimer away from these wars. The text emphasizes Mephala's web of manipulation and Veloth's ultimate decision to lead his people on an exodus to find a new homeland, framing this departure as a necessary severance from a corrupted web of conflicts.
topic_desc_basic: As Shokhahn Am Morfijin is a Dunmeris historical text. It recounts the Chimer's early divergence from other mer, the warlord Aldis's capture and betrayal of Mephala's secrets, and the prophet Veloth's decision to lead the Chimer on an exodus away from these ancestral conflicts.

title: Ash and Blood: Volume I
topic_desc: Sila Merilia's historical work examines the upheaval in Morrowind during Jagar Tharn's usurpation. Volume I details Tharnite agents' systematic destabilization of Almalexia City through arson, assassinations, and falsified orders, which provoked famine and civil unrest. Merilia recounts Queen Barenziah's departure for the Imperial City, the peasant riot of First Seed 391 led by the agitator Zirik, and the death of King-consort Symmachus at the hands of the mob. The narrative covers Almalexia's public intervention to restore order, Barenziah's subsequent exile, and the Elder Council's acknowledgment of Athyn Llethan as King of Morrowind. Merilia's account is significant for its critical assessment of both Tharnite treachery and provincial leadership failures, and for noting Almalexia's conspicuous silence on Imperial loyalty.
topic_desc_basic: A historical account by Sila Merilia covering the Imperial Simulacrum's impact on Morrowind. It details Jagar Tharn's destabilization of Almalexia City, the famine and riots of 391, the death of King-consort Symmachus, and the ascension of Athyn Llethan to the throne of Morrowind.

title: Ash and Blood: Volume II
topic_desc: A historical study of the Imperial Simulacrum's impact on Morrowind, focusing on the War of Lies between Ebonheart and Firewatch.
topic_desc_basic: A historical volume by Sila Merilia examining the War of Lies, a civil conflict in Morrowind during the Imperial Simulacrum.

title: Ash and Blood: Volume III
topic_desc: A scholarly work by Sila Merilia examining the Imperial Simulacrum's impact on Morrowind, specifically the Arnesian War.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Sila Merilia about the Arnesian War during the Imperial Simulacrum.

title: Ash Fowl Meat
topic_desc: Ash Fowl Meat is a food ingredient obtained from the ash fowl, a bird associated with Morrowind's ash-covered regions. It circulates through trade networks and general supply lists across multiple regions, including Mournhold, Telvannis, and the Velothi Highlands. Categorized among meat provisions, it serves primarily as sustenance. Hunters encounter ash fowl in the course of their trade, and the meat reaches alchemists and merchants through general ingredient distribution channels.
topic_desc_basic: Ash Fowl Meat is the edible flesh of the ash fowl, a bird of Morrowind. It is commonly traded as a foodstuff and appears in provisions across the eastern and Velothi regions.

title: Ash-Fowl Tongue
topic_desc: Ash-Fowl Tongue is an ingredient harvested from the ash fowl, a creature of the ashlands. Alchemists value the tongue for its alchemical properties, and hunters often collect the part from their quarry. The substance circulates through common ingredient supplies and apothecary stock across Morrowind and its surrounding regions.
topic_desc_basic: Ash-Fowl Tongue is an ingredient taken from the ash fowl. It is used in alchemy and can be found in general ingredient supplies across Morrowind.

title: Ash Moth
topic_desc: Ash moths are insects native to the volcanic ashlands of Morrowind. Their wings and bodies are adapted to the ashen environment, providing camouflage among the dark soils and scorched rock. They are commonly encountered in the blighted and ash-covered regions where they flutter near the ground. For travelers and hunters, ash moths serve as a recognizable feature of the harsh terrain, and their presence is a standard indicator of the local ecosystem. Their durable chitinous parts are occasionally gathered for use in regional crafts and alchemical practices.
topic_desc_basic: Ash moths are insects found in the ashlands of Morrowind. They are recognized by their ashen camouflage and are commonly seen fluttering near the ground in volcanic regions.

title: Ash Moth Wing
topic_desc: Ash moth wings are the membranous wings of the ash moth, a lepidopteran insect native to Morrowind. Ash moths are active during both daylight and nighttime hours, making their wings a readily obtainable ingredient for alchemists and foragers. The wings are gathered directly from living specimens and are known to circulate in general alchemical supply stocks across the province. Their properties make them a staple component in common potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Ash moth wings are gathered from ash moths, insects native to Morrowind that are active during both day and night. The wings serve as a common alchemical ingredient available through general supply channels.

title: Ashdew
topic_desc: Ashdew is a fungus associated with environments of death, thriving in places such as ancestral tombs. It is not native to Morrowind but was introduced from Thras. The Ja-Natta Syndicate cultivates ashdew specifically for brewing greydust, a potent narcotic. Its affinity for morbid surroundings and its role in illicit alchemical production make it a noteworthy ingredient among those familiar with underground trade and fungal cultivation.
topic_desc_basic: Ashdew is a fungus that grows in places associated with death, such as ancestral tombs. It was brought to Morrowind from Thras and is used in brewing greydust, a potent narcotic.

title: Aspis Venom Gland
topic_desc: The aspis venom gland is an alchemical ingredient harvested from the diamond aspis, a serpent indigenous to the Dasek Marsh and the Strident Coast of Cyrodiil. Prized by practitioners of the venomous arts, the gland contains the snake's potent natural toxin. Alchemists value these organs for their essential properties, which make them a staple component in the synthesis of deadly poisons and specific curative concoctions. Sourcing the gland requires hunting the diamond aspis in its native swamp and coastal habitats, making it a regional specialty of those Cyrodiilic territories.
topic_desc_basic: An alchemical ingredient obtained from the diamond aspis snake. It is native to the Dasek Marsh and Strident Coast regions of Cyrodiil.

title: Aspyr Tea Leaves
topic_desc: Aspyr tea leaves are a botanical ingredient harvested from the aspyr tea plant. They are valued in alchemical practice and culinary traditions for their distinctive properties. The plant thrives in the Reach region of Skyrim, where the leaves are commonly gathered for use as a seasoning and brewing material. Alchemists prize the foliage for its stable alchemical character, while hunters and travelers in the region recognize the plant as a familiar resource. The leaves appear in various regional ingredient supplies and spice collections, reflecting their established role in Reachfolk and broader Skyrim trade.
topic_desc_basic: Aspyr tea leaves are a plant ingredient gathered from the Reach in Skyrim. They are commonly used as a brewing tea and seasoning spice, and are familiar to alchemists and travelers in the region.

title: Assa Tea Cake
topic_desc: Assa tea cakes are compressed bricks of herbal tea mixtures originating from the Summerset Isles. The name derives from the Altmer term 'assa,' meaning 'unwilted,' which refers to the specific state of the tea shrub's leaves at the time of harvest. This preservation method allows the herbal properties of the freshly picked foliage to endure within the compacted form. Alchemists value these cakes as a stable, transportable source of botanical essence for their preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Assa tea cakes are compressed bricks of herbal tea from the Summerset Isles. The name means 'unwilted,' referring to the state of the tea shrub's leaves when harvested.

title: Astral Jellyfish
topic_desc: Astral Jellyfish are a species of bright blue and purple jellyfish found in the seawater areas of Cyrodiil. As an aquatic creature, they serve as a source of alchemical ingredients for practitioners and hunters familiar with coastal fauna. Their distinct coloration makes them visually recognizable in their natural marine habitat.
topic_desc_basic: Astral Jellyfish are bright blue and purple jellyfish found in the seawater areas of Cyrodiil.

title: Astral Vapors
topic_desc: Astral vapors is an acute disease contracted from magical creatures such as undead or golems. It produces no physical symptoms but adversely affects the victim's magicka while increasing their vulnerability to the magical attacks of others. Healers and alchemists familiar with acute ailments of magical origin recognize it among the category of diseases that drain and destabilize arcane reserves rather than manifesting bodily corruption.
topic_desc_basic: Astral vapors is an acute disease contracted from magical creatures such as undead or golems. It has no physical symptoms but drains magicka and makes the afflicted more vulnerable to magical attacks.

title: Atavistic Eye
topic_desc: The atavistic eye is an alchemical ingredient harvested from the rare blind slaughterfish, a creature found in the waters of Morrowind. Prized by alchemists, these eyes are known to circulate through regional ingredient supplies across the Deshaan, Mournhold, Narsis, Telvannis, and Velothis districts, indicating a steady if uncommon demand for their properties.
topic_desc_basic: The atavistic eye is an alchemical ingredient harvested from the rare blind slaughterfish that inhabits Morrowind's waters.

title: Atop a Tower on Moridunon
topic_desc: An essay by the Colovian poet Pallav Valernius, written during the Tiber Wars while he toured the Aldmeri Dominion recording oral traditions. It recounts a dialogue with an Altmeri scholar atop a beacon tower near Firsthold as Numidium approaches across the sea. The Altmer dismisses the Empire of men as childish and ephemeral, wielding a mere brass puppet rather than true power, and condemns the mortal cycle of rebirth as a breaking wheel that strips the soul of identity—a prison antithetical to hope. The city of Moridunon is destroyed below them. The editor notes the backdrop of destruction remains dubious, the Altmer's bleak cosmology is contested by Imperial and elven scholars, and rumors of Valernius acting as an Imperial spy are undermined by his perilous proximity to the Brass Golem.
topic_desc_basic: An essay by the poet Pallav Valernius describing a dialogue with an Altmer scholar near Firsthold during the Tiber Wars. As Numidium approaches, the Altmer dismisses the Empire of men as fleeting and condemns the mortal cycle of rebirth as a cruel prison, offering a bleak elven perspective on death and existence.

title: Axe of Boethiah
topic_desc: The Axe of Boethiah is a Daedric artifact associated with Boethiah, the Daedric Prince of Plots and Deceiver. The weapon embodies the sphere of its patron, reflecting the deceptive and subversive nature characteristic of the Prince. While recognized among esoteric traditions as a genuine Daedric relic, its present location remains unknown to Tamrielic scholars.
topic_desc_basic: The Axe of Boethiah is a Daedric artifact associated with the Prince of Plots. Embodying its patron's deceptive sphere, the weapon is recognized as a genuine relic, though its present location remains unknown to Tamrielic scholars.

title: Ayleid Cities of Valenwood
topic_desc: A scholarly excerpt by the historian Homfrey of the University of Gwylim, dated 2E 455, surveying the Ayleid settlement of southern Tamriel. Homfrey examines the prosperity of cities such as Ceyatatar, Haven, Woodhearth, Silvenar, and Elden Root following the establishment of the White-Gold Tower, attributing their growth to expanded trade. He gives particular attention to Elden Root, where Ayleids built around the Elden Tree, revered as the First Tree that seeded all Valenwood. The text chronicles the destruction of Haven and Woodhearth by Maormer raiders, who also plundered Elden Root and the Great Tree itself. Homfrey speculates that Maormer savagery stemmed from intermingling with indigenous Pyandonean tribes, reflecting a pronounced pro-Aldmer bias. The work stands as a valuable, if partisan, record of Ayleid civilization's reach into Valenwood and its eventual decline.
topic_desc_basic: A historical excerpt by University of Gwylim historian Homfrey, dated 2E 455, surveying Ayleid settlement in southern Tamriel. It describes the prosperity of cities including Haven, Woodhearth, Silvenar, and Elden Root following the White-Gold Tower's establishment, and their subsequent destruction by Maormer raiders.

title: Ayleid Inscriptions
topic_desc: A scholarly compilation by Raelys Anine, preserving Ayleid phrases and their translations transcribed and interpreted over many years. The work records several notable Ayleid aphorisms, including the fundamental magical principle that life emerges from fire and magic from light, and the martial admonition to wear lore as armor. The inscriptions reflect a worldview valuing wisdom gained through suffering, the ancestral exile of the Elves, and the pursuit of truth within obscure depths. Anine provides literal translations for certain idioms, such as clarifying that wisdom learned by pain literally denotes terrible wisdom that never betrayed loremasters, and that the term for exiled ancestors literally means driven from home. The collection stands as a significant record of Ayleid thought and linguistic heritage.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Raelys Anine that records and translates several Ayleid phrases and proverbs. It preserves notable Ayleid sayings concerning magic, wisdom, ancestral exile, and the pursuit of truth.

title: Ayleid Ruins
topic_desc: Glories and Laments Among the Ayleid Ruins by Alexandre Hetrard is a travelogue recounting the author's visit to Ceyatatar, Ayleid ruins near Delodiil on the Gold Road between Skingrad and the Imperial City. Hetrard describes the underground temple dedicated to Magnus, its magical pools, and still-pulsing Welkynd stones. He expounds on Ayleid elemental philosophy, noting that the Ayleids recognized earth, water, air, and light rather than fire, regarding fire as a corrupt form of light tied to primary magical principles. The work warns of deadly mechanisms still active in the ruins. Hetrard's central thesis attributes the fall of the Ayleid civilization not to slave revolts or beast peoples, but to the arrogant pride and complacency of the Ayleids themselves. The work serves as both architectural record and philosophical meditation on imperial decline.
topic_desc_basic: Glories and Laments Among the Ayleid Ruins by Alexandre Hetrard is a travelogue describing the author's visit to the Ayleid ruins of Ceyatatar near the Imperial City. The work details Ayleid architecture, their elemental philosophy of light over fire, and reflects on the civilization's decline, attributing it to arrogant pride rather than external conquest.

title: Ballad of a Dead Man
topic_desc: A poem composed by a condemned criminal awaiting execution. The author confesses to a life of drinking, thieving, and violence, though identifying capture as the gravest sin. The verses denounce the harsh treatment received from Legion captors and close with a spiteful postscript directed at a rival named Horatio Gargonath, whose own poetry is dismissed as rubbish. The ballad offers a grim, sardonic glimpse into the final thoughts of a doomed outlaw in Imperial custody.
topic_desc_basic: A condemned criminal's final poem, written shortly before execution. The author confesses to a villainous life, complains of mistreatment by the Legion, and insults a rival poet.

title: Baluath Clan
topic_desc: The Baluath Clan, archaically known as Baalvayn, is a gathering of vampires primarily found within the Armun Ashlands. Reputedly the first great vampiric clan in Morrowind, their origins lie east of the Thirr River. According to the vampire historian Sathram Volos, the Baluath once strove to bring down the Tribunate in its infancy, an effort that failed and left the bloodline scattered and broken into small groups and lone hunters. The clan historically migrated to Armun under the leadership of Turon Baluath. Another notable figure, the Elder Vunal, called the Ageless Apprentice, died by suicide several years ago. Currently, the largest splinter group is led by the vampire Ofelia from the Indoril ruin of Khirakai, while another leader, Kashshaptu, seeks the clan's reunification. The Baluath are ancient rivals of the newborn Orlukh Clan and are hostile toward the other vampire bloodlines and mainstream Dunmer factions.
topic_desc_basic: The Baluath Clan is an ancient vampire bloodline scattered across the Armun Ashlands. Reputedly the first great vampiric clan in Morrowind, they are now broken into small groups following their failed historical opposition to the Tribunal.

title: Banker's Bet
topic_desc: A humorous tale by Porbert Lyttumly set at the Bank of Daggerfall, illustrating the lengths to which greed drives people. An elderly gambler named Petuva Smethworthy deposits a vast fortune and wagers the bank's president twenty-five thousand gold that his testicles will be feathered by morning. The president obsessively monitors himself and, confident he has won, drops his breeches to prove it. Smethworthy then reveals she wagered her son one hundred thousand gold that she would have the president of the Bank of Daggerfall by the balls, winning the larger sum through his own vanity.
topic_desc_basic: A humorous tale by Porbert Lyttumly about a wealthy elderly woman who visits the Bank of Daggerfall and uses an outrageous wager to trick the bank president, demonstrating what people will do for money.

title: Bark Heart
topic_desc: Bark Hearts are organic materials harvested from adult Koglings, creatures native to Skyrim. Elder Koglings are known to reliably yield these specimens. The ingredient's rarity places it among scarce alchemical components, valued for its uncommon properties and limited availability outside its northern habitat.
topic_desc_basic: Bark Hearts are ingredients taken from Koglings, creatures found in Skyrim.

title: Bark Scale
topic_desc: Bark Scales are bodily growths harvested from koglings, creatures native to Skyrim. Their alchemical character remains a subject of specialist study rather than common knowledge, and they yield no guaranteed samples, making them a somewhat uncommon reagent. Hunters and alchemists occasionally acquire these scales from the creatures' hides, though their specific properties are obscure to lay practitioners.
topic_desc_basic: Bark Scales are harvested from koglings, creatures found in Skyrim.

title: Barracuda Tailfin
topic_desc: Barracuda tailfins are the severed tails of the Padomaic Barracuda, a predatory fish inhabiting the waters surrounding the Padomaic Isles. Valued by alchemists and hunters familiar with exotic maritime ingredients, the tailfin is harvested from its aquatic source and employed in various alchemical preparations. As the barracuda is not native to Vvardenfell or mainland Morrowind, the ingredient remains an import, typically procured through trade or chance encounters rather than reliable local supply.
topic_desc_basic: Barracuda tailfins are harvested from the Padomaic Barracuda, a fish found in the waters around the Padomaic Isles. They are used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Barristers Guild
topic_desc: The Barristers Guild is an officially sanctioned Imperial organization employing barristers from across the Empire. Established under the Guild Act sanctioned by Versidue-Shaie in 2E 321, it operates protected by the Empire of Cyrodiil, though it must pay the Empire to expand its influence. The guild functions within Tamriel's universal legal system, which follows the Prophet Marukh's credo that all are guilty until proven innocent, while accommodating provincial rules and decrees. By the late Third Era, legal counsel became restricted to the Imperial City, leaving the provinces without such support; the impact of this shift on the guild remains unknown. Despite this, the guild maintains practices in Dunmer lands, including the city of Narsis, and counts Archmagister Nelos Otheri of House Telvanni among its prominent patrons. The guild holds an adversarial relationship with several vampire clans.
topic_desc_basic: The Barristers Guild is an officially sanctioned Imperial organization that employs legal professionals across Tamriel. Chartered under the Guild Act of 2E 321, it operates under Imperial protection. The guild practices law within the Empire's universal legal framework, which dictates that all are guilty until proven innocent. It maintains a presence in Morrowind, including the city of Narsis.

title: Bearclaw Flower
topic_desc: The Bearclaw Flower is a botanical ingredient valued in alchemical practice. It grows in forested regions and is notably associated with the flora of the Reach and Skyrim, where it is gathered as a random ingredient of the wild. Its specific alchemical properties and precise appearance remain subjects of specialist study rather than common knowledge, though its utility in potion-making ensures steady demand among apothecaries and hunters familiar with the northern wilds.
topic_desc_basic: The Bearclaw Flower is a wild blossom found in forested regions, particularly in Skyrim and the Reach. It is gathered for use in alchemy.

title: Beautyberry
topic_desc: Beautyberry is a botanical ingredient harvested from its namesake shrub. While the precise alchemical virtues of the berry remain subject to specialist study, it is recognized in compounding traditions and appears in general ingredient stock. The plant grows in select regions of Tamriel, and the fruit is gathered for use in alchemical preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Beautyberry is a small fruit harvested from a flowering shrub. It is gathered in the wild and used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Beef
topic_desc: Beef is meat harvested from cows, common livestock herded in Cyrodiil and Skyrim. As a foodstuff, it provides sustenance and is widely circulated through regional markets and supply lists. In alchemical practice, beef possesses inherent properties that practitioners can extract, though its primary cultural and economic significance remains culinary. Its prevalence in the agricultural economies of the Imperial Province and the northern holds ensures steady availability across those regions.
topic_desc_basic: Beef is meat harvested from cows, common livestock herded in Cyrodiil and Skyrim. It is widely eaten as food throughout those regions.

title: Beetle Resin
topic_desc: Beetle resins are tough, soluble substances extracted from the hides of blue, brown, green, and horned beetles. Like shalk resin, they serve as glues and stiffeners in manufacturing bonemold and chitin armors, though they are considered second rate for this task. Alchemically, the substance simultaneously drains fatigue and endurance while restoring health. The resin is commonly harvested from wild beetles or herded beetles kept by farmers in settlements such as Old Ebonheart's Market Quarter.
topic_desc_basic: A tough, soluble substance extracted from the hides of various beetles. It is used as a glue and stiffener in making bonemold and chitin armors, and has alchemical properties that affect endurance, fatigue, and health.

title: Before the Ages of Man
topic_desc: Aicantar of Shimerene's scholarly chronicle, the first volume of the Timeline Series, which synthesizes the prehistoric Dawn and Merethic Eras. The work frames the Dawn Era as the period of divine acts before mortal time, concluding with the convention at the Adamantine Tower, the departure of Magic, and the exile of Lorkhan. It then traces the Merethic Era using a reverse Nordic calendar, detailing the displacement of aboriginal beastpeoples by Aldmeri colonists from the lost continent of Aldmeris, the rise of Ayleid and Direnni civilizations, and the Chimer exodus under Prophet Veloth. The text further chronicles the subsequent decline of Velothi culture into Ashlander tribes and Great Houses, alongside the arrival of Nedic peoples from Atmora led by Ysgramor. It remains a significant compilation of mythic and historical traditions regarding Tamriel's earliest inhabitants and the formation of the mortal plane.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly chronicle by Aicantar of Shimerene that surveys Tamriel's prehistory. It divides early history into the Dawn Era, covering the creation of the mortal plane and the gods' departure, and the Merethic Era, detailing the Aldmeri colonization, the Chimer exodus, and the first human migrations from Atmora.

title: Before the Gates of Valsar
topic_desc: Before the Gates of Valsar is a historical narrative recounting the arrival of the Velothi in Cyrod. It describes a group of pilgrims from New Aldmeris, hardened by their journey through the great southern forests, arriving at the city of Valsar. A high preacher among them denounced the inhabitants' unending lifecycles and ancestral worship as lies, promising instead an escape from the folly of birth through hardship and survival. Despite the city watch's initial suppression of such preachers and the governor's inaction, the pilgrims' creed prevailed. After a siege of three days and seven nights, Valsar's gates were opened, and the pilgrims were accepted. Following a four-day rest, the pilgrims—described as twice their number but of the same sum—departed, leaving Valsar abandoned. The text serves as an account of the transformative early Velothi migration and the ideological shift from Aldmeri ancestral tradition to the exodus philosophy.
topic_desc_basic: Before the Gates of Valsar is a historical account of the early Velothi migration into Cyrod. It describes pilgrims from New Aldmeris arriving at the city of Valsar, preaching against unending lifecycles and ancestral lies in favor of hardship and survival. The city ultimately accepted them before being abandoned as the pilgrims departed.

title: Beggar Prince
topic_desc: Beggar Prince recounts the First Era legend of Wheedle, the thirteenth child of a Valenwood king who sought fortune and encountered the Daedric Prince Namira. After persistently following Namira for thirty-three days seeking an apprenticeship, Wheedle received three gifts: the power to bear any disease at will, the power to evoke pity, and the power of disregard. Though Wheedle initially considered these curses, the combined boons proved remarkably effective. The power of pity made Wheedle an irresistible beggar, while the power of disregard allowed Wheedle to overhear secrets unnoticed. The tale concludes that Wheedle became legendary among beggars, and it offers the folk wisdom that beggars, being overlooked, know the hidden affairs of every city.
topic_desc_basic: Beggar Prince is a legendary tale of Wheedle, a royal child of Valenwood who received three gifts from the Daedric Prince Namira and became a legendary beggar. The story claims that beggars know the secrets of every city because they are universally overlooked.

title: Belt of St. Olms
topic_desc: The Belt of St. Olms is a precious Temple relic currently held in the Eight-Bones Temple in Narsis, where it is considered the holiest artifact in that sanctuary, second only to Muatra. The belt bears an enchantment that fortifies mercantile and hand-to-hand aptitude. Recently, an Ordinator absconded with the belt and fell to apostasy, joining a Dagonite cult at the Daedric ruin of Naemunbatashpi north of Othmura. Temple authorities attempted to locate the artifact discreetly through informants monitoring the black market, but the effort failed. The theft and the Ordinator's apostasy remain sensitive matters; Temple leadership considers the belt's desecration by Daedra worshippers unacceptable and seeks its immediate recovery.
topic_desc_basic: The Belt of St. Olms is a precious Temple relic held in the Eight-Bones Temple in Narsis, valued second only to Muatra. It fortifies mercantile and hand-to-hand skill. An Ordinator recently stole the belt and fled to a Dagonite cult at Naemunbatashpi, prompting Temple efforts to recover it.

title: Benighted Cortinar
topic_desc: Benighted Cortinar is a harvestable ingredient of uncertain natural origin. Its alchemical properties and common uses remain largely undocumented in standard herbalist texts, leaving its specific effects a matter for specialist experimentation rather than common knowledge.
topic_desc_basic: Benighted Cortinar is a little-known harvestable ingredient. Its specific origin and alchemical properties are obscure, known primarily to specialist alchemists and experienced hunters rather than the general public.

title: Bertpod Slice
topic_desc: A bertpod slice is a prepared section of the bertpod plant, valued by alchemists as a botanical reagent. Its specific alchemical properties are known to practitioners, though the ingredient remains relatively uncommon in the wild. It is not typically found in guaranteed supply, instead appearing sporadically among randomized foraging yields, requiring deliberate search or chance encounters to harvest.
topic_desc_basic: A bertpod slice is a botanical ingredient harvested from the bertpod plant. It is used in alchemy, though it is uncommon and not reliably found in any particular location.

title: Bezoar Stone
topic_desc: A bezoar stone is a rare alchemical ingredient valued for its property of evading physical attacks. Alchemists combine it with other ingredients, such as kagouti hide, to brew potions of sanctuary. Its scarcity makes specimens highly sought, with some practitioners trading considerable favors or equivalent reagents to acquire one for their work.
topic_desc_basic: A bezoar stone is a rare alchemical ingredient. Alchemists prize it for brewing potions that help the drinker evade physical attacks.

title: Big Mole Crab Shell
topic_desc: The big mole crab shell is a durable yet lightweight carapace harvested from mole crabs, creatures native to Morrowind. The shell's combination of toughness and low weight makes it valued beyond its alchemical properties. House Telvanni craftsmen work the material into various forms of light armor, exploiting its protective qualities without encumbering the wearer. The shells circulate among alchemists and hunters familiar with Morrowind's fauna, appearing both in general ingredient trade and in Telvanni-specific markets.
topic_desc_basic: Big mole crab shells are harvested from mole crabs found throughout Morrowind. The shells are tough but light, and the Telvanni use them to craft light armor.

title: Bird's Nest Egg Spore
topic_desc: A fungal spore harvested from bird's nest fungi, valued by alchemists and hunters for its properties.
topic_desc_basic: A fungal spore gathered from bird's nest fungi, used in alchemy.

title: Biscuit
topic_desc: Biscuits are small baked pastries enjoyed across Tamriel. They come in a variety of flavors, are quickly prepared, and keep for a long time without going stale. Their convenience makes them popular with travelers, who eat them on the road to recover energy lost to journey's fatigue. Alchemists classify them among food-grade ingredients valued more for practical sustenance than for arcane properties.
topic_desc_basic: Biscuits are small baked pastries found across Tamriel. They come in various flavors, keep well without going stale, and are favored by travelers for eating on the road to recover energy.

title: Bitter Heart
topic_desc: Bitter Heart is a Nord tale recounting the tragedy of Skali, a renowned Solstheim hunter. After a black wolf seemingly kills his young son, Skali's wife perishes from grief. In despair, Skali invokes the Trickster—whom the Dark Elves call Clavicus Vile—and receives a dark, twisted spear to slay the beast. Upon throwing the weapon and piercing the wolf's heart, he discovers his son's body in the animal's place. The story serves as a cautionary account of Daedric deception and cruel bargains, ending with the broken hunter renouncing his craft and taking the name Skali Bitter-Heart before sailing east into exile.
topic_desc_basic: Bitter Heart is a Nord tale about Skali, a Solstheim hunter who loses his son to a wolf and makes a desperate pact with the Trickster, only to be deceived into killing his own child.

title: Bitterstar Seeds
topic_desc: Bitterstar seeds are a floral ingredient of uncertain natural origin. Alchemists and hunters encounter them only sporadically, as the plant is not reliably cultivated or harvested in any known region. Their alchemical character remains a subject of specialist study rather than common practice, owing to the scarcity of guaranteed samples. The seeds appear in varied regional ingredient supplies, suggesting a dispersed habitat across Tamriel, though specific growth conditions are not well documented.
topic_desc_basic: Bitterstar seeds are a scarce floral ingredient occasionally found in regional supplies, though their specific origin and habitat remain poorly documented.

title: Bitterstone Ore
topic_desc: Bitterstone ore is a mineral ingredient of uncertain natural origin. Its alchemical character and common uses remain largely undocumented in standard references. The ore is known to appear sporadically among randomized mineral yields, suggesting it is an uncommon discovery rather than a staple alchemical supply.
topic_desc_basic: Bitterstone ore is a mineral substance occasionally found among random mineral yields. Its specific properties and common uses are not widely known.

title: Bjoulsae Rose
topic_desc: The Bjoulsae Rose is a floral ingredient of alchemical interest. Its common name suggests an origin in the lands adjoining the Bjoulsae River, where it presumably grows as part of the regional flora. Alchemists and hunters value the plant for its useful properties, and it circulates in trade through general and rare ingredient supply channels across Hammerfell, High Rock, and Skyrim. Specific alchemical effects remain a matter for specialist determination.
topic_desc_basic: The Bjoulsae Rose is a flowering plant valued as an alchemical ingredient. As its name implies, it grows in the Bjoulsae River region.

title: Black Bear Pelt
topic_desc: A pelt taken from the black bears native to Skyrim. Hunters and furriers value these hides as a source of durable fur and bone, and alchemists prepare the pelts for their useful properties. The creatures are primarily found throughout Skyrim's wilderness, and the pelts are commonly traded among those who work with hides and animal parts.
topic_desc_basic: A pelt taken from the black bears native to Skyrim, valued as a source of fur and hide.

title: Black Pearl
topic_desc: Black pearls are exceptionally rare, notably huge pearls distinguished by their glossy black sheen. They possess enormous value and certain magical properties, making them prized alchemical reagents. In Morrowind, they are practically never harvested from native kollops and must typically be imported. In Cyrodiil, black pearls are occasionally found in clams along the seafloor, though such yields remain uncommon.
topic_desc_basic: Black pearls are exceptionally rare, huge pearls with a glossy black sheen. They hold enormous value and some magical properties. They are usually imported into Morrowind, as the native kollops practically never yield them.

title: Black Rose
topic_desc: A late-blooming flower with a spicy smell, the black rose is native to Morrowind. Artists and nobles have often used it to symbolize the province. The plant possesses potent magical qualities valued in alchemical practice. A specimen of particular significance, described as a special flower from the gardens of Moonshadow, is known to exist, though such Daedric origins are extraordinary and atypical for the common provincial flower.
topic_desc_basic: A late-blooming flower with a spicy smell, the black rose is native to Morrowind. Artists and nobles often use it to symbolize the province.

title: Black Spore Cap
topic_desc: Black Spore Caps are a type of mushroom found growing in the wilds of Tamriel. As a fungal ingredient, they are recognized and gathered by alchemists and hunters for their useful properties. They occur naturally across various regions and are commonly sourced from the wild by foragers.
topic_desc_basic: Black Spore Caps are a type of mushroom gathered for alchemical use.

title: Blackberries
topic_desc: Blackberries are small dark fruits that grow on creeping vines. They serve as a common foodstuff across Tamriel and are occasionally utilized by alchemists for their inherent properties. The fruits are broadly distributed, appearing in general and regional produce supplies.
topic_desc_basic: Blackberries are small dark fruits that grow on creeping vines. They are a common food found throughout Tamriel.

title: Blacknettle
topic_desc: Blacknettle is a flora-derived ingredient of alchemical interest. Its specific properties and appearance remain poorly documented in standard herbalist references, and it holds no widespread commercial significance. The plant is known to grow in Skyrim, where it appears in regional ingredient stocks. Alchemists and hunters who encounter it value it for its alchemical potential, though its scarcity prevents common use.
topic_desc_basic: Blacknettle is a plant ingredient found growing in Skyrim.

title: Bleak Bell
topic_desc: Bleak Bells are the blue, drooping blossoms of Bleakbell Hay, a flowering plant native to the Druadach Highlands and Grey Plains of Skyrim. Alchemists and gatherers familiar with northern flora recognize them by their distinctive pendulous shape and pale blue hue. The plant thrives in the harsh, windswept terrain of Skyrim's western reaches, where it is collected for use in alchemical preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Bleak Bells are blue, drooping flowers that grow on Bleakbell Hay, a plant found in the Druadach Highlands and Grey Plains of Skyrim. They are known to herbalists and alchemists as a gatherable ingredient.

title: Bleakstar Stalk
topic_desc: Bleakstar stalk is a botanical ingredient valued in alchemical practice. The plant yields a slender stalk, though its precise appearance and favored climate remain obscure to general record. It is not cultivated and grows sparsely across Tamriel, encountered unpredictably by foragers rather than in any guaranteed harvest. Its alchemical properties are known to practitioners, though its scarcity renders it a secondary subject in common herbalism.
topic_desc_basic: Bleakstar stalk is a scarce plant ingredient. It grows unpredictably across Tamriel and is not found in any reliable quantity, making it unfamiliar to common foragers.

title: Bleeding Heart
topic_desc: Bleeding Heart is a floral ingredient harvested from the plant of the same name. Alchemists value the flower for its properties, and it sees common use in potion-making. Hunters and herbalists also encounter the plant in the wild, where it is gathered for regional ingredient supplies and trade.
topic_desc_basic: Bleeding Heart is a flowering plant valued by alchemists as an ingredient.

title: Blight Moth
topic_desc: The Blight Moth is a large, ash-gray lepidopteran adapted to the blighted environments of Morrowind. Its wings and body carry the distinctive ruddy discoloration characteristic of Corprus infection, blending with the ashen terrain. These creatures inhabit the volcanic slopes and blight-stricken regions near Red Mountain, where they have developed a tolerance for the hostile conditions that kill lesser fauna. Blight Moths are territorial and aggressive when provoked, using their corrupted physiology as a defense. Their durable significance lies in their status as a visible marker of blight corruption and their adaptation to the most hostile ecologies of Vvardenfell.
topic_desc_basic: The Blight Moth is a large, ash-gray moth found in the blighted regions near Red Mountain. It is recognizable by the ruddy discoloration of Corprus infection on its wings and is known for its aggressive behavior when threatened.

title: Blight Moth Wing
topic_desc: Blight Moth Wings are the wings of blight moths, insects found throughout Morrowind that are active during both day and night. As an alchemical ingredient, the wing is valued by practitioners for its inherent properties. Because each moth yields two wings, the ingredient is relatively accessible to those who gather from live specimens, though loose samples are not known to be reliably found in any particular location. The wings are commonly distributed through general moth-wing supply lists.
topic_desc_basic: Blight Moth Wings are taken from blight moths, insects found across Morrowind active during day and night. Each moth provides two wings, making them a readily gathered alchemical ingredient, though loose samples have no known reliable location.

title: Blind Stalker Amulet
topic_desc: The Blind Stalker Amulet is an artifact renowned for its powerful Command Creature enchantment. The amulet is associated with the Blind Stalker tribe of goblins and is currently in the possession of Garth, the Goblin King. Garth resides within Kalkusara, a goblin stronghold.
topic_desc_basic: The Blind Stalker Amulet is an artifact with a powerful Command Creature enchantment. It belongs to the Blind Stalker goblin tribe and is held by their king, Garth, in the stronghold of Kalkusara.

title: Blister Spore
topic_desc: Blister Spores are the spherical caps of the Blister Spore mushroom, a fungus native to the Othreleth Woods in Morrowind. As an alchemical ingredient, the spore caps are harvested for their properties. They are commonly gathered by foragers and hunters familiar with the southwestern woodlands, and they circulate in general ingredient supplies throughout the region.
topic_desc_basic: Blister Spores are the spherical caps of the Blister Spore mushroom, which grows in the Othreleth Woods of Morrowind.

title: Blistering Fomentarius
topic_desc: Blistering Fomentarius is a fungal ingredient harvested from a variant of the fomentarius fungus. Prized by alchemists and hunters for its distinctive properties, it yields potent alchemical characteristics typical of its species. The fungus thrives in damp environments and is recognized by its blistered, inflamed appearance, which distinguishes it from common strains. It appears in randomized ingredient supplies across the Hlaalu region, particularly around Narsis, and features in alchemical and floral supply distributions.
topic_desc_basic: Blistering Fomentarius is a fungus used in alchemy. It is found in the Hlaalu lands around Narsis.

title: Blood Lily Flower
topic_desc: Blood Lily Flowers are the bright red blooms of the Blood Lily plant. They grow on Stirk Isle and on smaller islands throughout the Abecean Sea in Cyrodiil. Alchemists and hunters value them as an ingredient for their distinct properties.
topic_desc_basic: Blood Lily Flowers are bright red blooms harvested from Blood Lily plants. They grow on Stirk Isle and smaller islands throughout the Abecean Sea in Cyrodiil.

title: Blood Lily Pod
topic_desc: The blood lily pod is the prickly seed pod of the blood lily plant, a flora known to grow on Stirk Isle and smaller islands scattered throughout the Abecean Sea. As an alchemical ingredient, it is recognized by harvesters and apothecaries for its distinctively barbed casing. Its restricted island habitat in the Cyrodiilic waters makes it a regional commodity rather than a mainland staple, valued by practitioners for the properties it contributes to mixtures.
topic_desc_basic: The blood lily pod is a prickly seed pod harvested from blood lily plants, which grow on Stirk Isle and smaller islands throughout the Abecean Sea.

title: Blood Lung
topic_desc: Blood Lung is a mild disease carried by ornada and parastylus; rats are also frequently infected. Its symptoms include painful swelling in the trachea and a heavy, bloody cough. The affliction saps endurance, potentially leaving the infected too weak for physical labor.
topic_desc_basic: Blood Lung is a mild disease carried by ornada, parastylus, and rats. It causes painful swelling in the trachea and a heavy, bloody cough, and saps endurance.

title: Blood Rot
topic_desc: Blood rot is a serious disease transmitted by the bite of muck leeches. The bite provokes an inflammatory reaction alongside the infection. The disease drains an infected person's personality, willpower, and health, and can prove fatal.
topic_desc_basic: Blood rot is a serious, sometimes fatal disease spread by muck leeches. It drains a person's personality, willpower, and health.

title: Blood Stone
topic_desc: Bloodstone, also called heliotrope, is a semiprecious crystal of chalcedony containing jasper. It possesses modest magical virtues valued in alchemical practice. In the West, the stone carries a sinister reputation; vampires are said to employ it in profane rituals to curse those who hunt them.
topic_desc_basic: Bloodstone, or heliotrope, is a semiprecious crystal of chalcedony containing jasper with modest magical virtues. It is infamously said to be used by western vampires in profane rituals.

title: Bloodgrass
topic_desc: Bloodgrass is a red grass that grows in the planes of Oblivion. Accessible realms where it is known to flourish include Khalaan and the Subfuscous Cupola. Its extraplanar origin and distinct crimson appearance make it a subject of interest in alchemical and planar studies. As a reagent, it is valued by specialists familiar with the properties of Daedric flora, though its precise alchemical character demands practical experimentation to harness fully.
topic_desc_basic: Bloodgrass is a red grass that grows in the planes of Oblivion.

title: Bloodstone Pilgrimage
topic_desc: The Bloodstone Pilgrimage is a Tribunal Temple rite reenacting Saint Veloth the Pilgrim's crossing of the Thirr River and honoring Sharai the Herder, whose sacrifice made the crossing possible. The destination is the Bloodstone Shrine within the Monastery of Saint Veloth on the eastern bank of the Thirr at Almas Thirr. Pilgrims must wear ceremonial cloth wrappings on their feet from the journey's start until reaching the shrine; removing them constitutes failure. The rite demands physical and mental fortitude, intended to instill empathy for Veloth's hardships. Hetman Llothro of Almas Thirr administers the undertaking.
topic_desc_basic: The Bloodstone Pilgrimage is a Tribunal Temple rite reenacting Saint Veloth's crossing of the Thirr River and honoring Sharai the Herder's sacrifice. Pilgrims travel to the Bloodstone Shrine inside the Monastery of Saint Veloth at Almas Thirr, wearing ceremonial foot wrappings for the journey's duration.

title: Blue Chalk Butterfly Wing
topic_desc: The wing of the Blue Chalk Butterfly, a diurnal insect native to Cyrodiil. Alchemists and hunters value these wings for their inherent properties, harvesting them from the living butterflies which frequent the Cyrodiilic countryside during daylight hours. As a standard preparation, each specimen yields a pair of wings for reagent use.
topic_desc_basic: The wing of a Blue Chalk Butterfly, a common daytime insect found in Cyrodiil. It is used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Blue Diamond
topic_desc: The blue diamond is an incredibly rare variant of diamond, noted for its distinctive sea-blue coloration. It shares some magical properties with the common diamond, making it of interest to practitioners of alchemy. Its exceptional scarcity renders it a prized commodity; a single specimen can serve as proof of professional skill among thieves. Alchemists such as Nevusa Falen in Bal Foyen are known to keep these gemstones.
topic_desc_basic: A blue diamond is an incredibly rare, sea-blue variant of diamond valued as a gemstone and alchemical ingredient.

title: Blue Felt Lichen
topic_desc: Blue Felt Lichen is a fungal growth harvested for its alchemical properties. As its name suggests, the lichen possesses a distinctive blue, felt-like texture. It grows naturally in cold, northern climes such as Skyrim, where foragers and hunters gather it from the wild. Alchemists value the lichen as a reagent, though its specific alchemical effects remain a subject of specialized study rather than common knowledge. It is often collected alongside other mushrooms and lichens, appearing in varied regional ingredient stocks.
topic_desc_basic: Blue Felt Lichen is a blue, felt-like fungus that grows in the wilds of Skyrim. It is gathered by foragers and used in alchemy.

title: Blue Flax Flowers
topic_desc: Blue flax flowers are blue blossoms harvested from the flax plant. They serve as an alchemical ingredient, utilized by apothecaries and practitioners of the craft for their inherent properties. The flowers are gathered directly from the living plant rather than derived from animal or mineral sources. Their widespread availability through general ingredient supplies and flora-specific collections attests to a recognized utility in common alchemical practice across the regions where the flax plant grows.
topic_desc_basic: Blue flax flowers are blue blossoms harvested from the flax plant. They are commonly gathered for use as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Blue Kanet
topic_desc: Blue Kanet is a blue-flowered plant native to Morrowind, commonly found growing in the Aanthirin region. It is recognized by alchemists and hunters for its alchemical properties.
topic_desc_basic: Blue Kanet is a common blue flower native to Morrowind, found growing in the Aanthirin region.

title: Blue Lichen
topic_desc: Blue lichen is an uncommon fungal growth found in southern Morrowind. Distinguished from common lichen by its bluish hue, it is sought by alchemists and foragers for its specific alchemical properties. It thrives in the regional conditions of the south, and its harvest is often associated with the Narsis area.
topic_desc_basic: Blue lichen is an uncommon lichen variety that grows in southern Morrowind.

title: Blue Pearl
topic_desc: Blue Pearls are rare pearls occasionally found within clams on the sea floor. They possess highly useful magical properties, making them particularly valued by mages. Their scarcity and potent alchemical character distinguish them from ordinary pearls, ensuring they remain a sought-after ingredient for magical preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Blue Pearls are rare pearls sometimes found inside clams on the sea floor. They are valued for their useful magical properties, especially by mages.

title: Blue Topaz
topic_desc: Blue topaz is a blue variant of the topaz gemstone valued as an alchemical ingredient. Unlike many minerals, it possesses no dedicated mine nor is it harvested from any known creature; specimens are instead recovered from ancient tombs and Daedric shrines scattered across Morrowind, or acquired through specialized merchants. Its presence in such ruins suggests cultural or ritual significance to past inhabitants, though the stone itself yields only its inherent alchemical properties when processed.
topic_desc_basic: Blue topaz is a blue gemstone used in alchemy. It is not mined or carried by creatures, but is found in old tombs and Daedric shrines throughout Morrowind or sold in shops.

title: Bluefoot
topic_desc: Bluefoot is a common mushroom growing in Telvanni lands and across southern Morrowind. It thrives in dark, damp environments. Alchemists value the fungus as a frequent ingredient in water-walking potions.
topic_desc_basic: Bluefoot is a common mushroom found in Telvanni lands and southern Morrowind. It thrives in dark and damp places, and is a frequent ingredient of water-walking potions.

title: Boar Meat
topic_desc: Boar meat is a cut of flesh harvested from wild boars. These beasts roam the woodlands and heaths of western Skyrim, including Vorndgad Forest, Midkarth, and Lorchwuir Heath. The meat serves as a common foodstuff and holds utility in alchemical practice.
topic_desc_basic: Meat taken from wild boars, commonly found in the wilds of western Skyrim. It is used as food and as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Boethiah's Proving
topic_desc: An anonymous account of a fatal summoning of Boethiah, detailing how the Daedric Prince tests her followers' worth through destruction and survival.
topic_desc_basic: An anonymous account of a fatal summoning of Boethiah, in which the Daedric Prince destroys followers who fail to prove their existence and spares the one who demonstrates the will to survive.

title: Bog Beacon Cap
topic_desc: Bog Beacon Cap is a variety of mushroom found in marshy environments. Alchemists value it as an ingredient for its distinct properties, and hunters and foragers also gather the fungus. Its cap is the primary portion harvested for alchemical preparation.
topic_desc_basic: Bog Beacon Cap is a type of mushroom gathered for use in alchemy.

title: Bondman's Creed
topic_desc: This Dunmer creed frames existence as a proving ground where adversity forges strength. It dismisses the Aedra as complacent beings who abandoned their descendants when Lorkhan introduced the Arena, praising the Daedra as stronger ancestors who nurtured and challenged the foundlings of Veloth. The work recounts how weaker ancestors fled to lick salt from rocks, only to be hardened by the skyrenders. Using metaphors of whetstones, hagglers, and rivals, it argues that worth requires testing and that both ancestors and descendants need each other. It exhorts followers to seek out discord, overcome it, and rule, identifying its audience as Daedric foundlings, seekers of Veloth, and brothers of the Hive who till salt fields and war with trees without fleeing.
topic_desc_basic: A Dunmer creed teaching that adversity is essential to forge true strength. It reveres the Daedra as nurturing ancestors who challenged Veloth's foundlings, unlike the Aedra who abandoned theirs, and urges followers to actively seek out and overcome discord.

title: Bonebreak Fever
topic_desc: Bonebreak fever is a mild disease transmitted by the parastylus and the rat. Its symptoms include fever, muscle pains, and a queasy sensation that one's bones have become brittle like a scrib's shell and will fracture from vigorous movement. This unsettling symptom causes those afflicted to unconsciously refrain from exerting their full physical strength.
topic_desc_basic: Bonebreak fever is a mild disease carried by rats and parastyluses. It causes fever, muscle aches, and a feeling that one's bones are brittle and might break from strenuous movement, leading sufferers to hold back their strength.

title: Bones of Hlur'Matta
topic_desc: A Dunmer religious text expounding the sacred nature of the physical form. The work argues that the living body is itself a temple, its breath, tears, and blood the root of being. It extends this metaphor to physical structures of worship, claiming they are built with the congregation's throats, minds, and lives. The treatise contrasts Dunmer ancestral veneration with the practices of men and Altmer, asserting that outsiders cannot comprehend the relationship between the living and the dead. It condemns the use of ash in funerary rites, instead advocating for the curation of the deceased's bones into cairns and effigies of power. These bone monuments mirror the internal temple of the body and serve as markers of Dunmer sacred lands and ancestral abodes.
topic_desc_basic: A Dunmer religious text teaching that the living body is a sacred temple. It explains that the Dunmer shape the bones of their dead into cairns and effigies, rather than using ash, and that these bone markers signify the presence of ancestral lands.

title: Book of Nordic Proverbs
topic_desc: The Book of Nordic Proverbs is a compilation of traditional Nord sayings reflecting the pragmatic and fatalistic worldview shaped by Skyrim's harsh environment. Its aphorisms address themes of mortality, vigilance, and the inevitability of change, frequently employing imagery of wolves, crows, winter, and battle. The proverbs counsel resilience and caution, observing that power is transient—one day the wolf hunts, the next it feeds the crows—and that strength lies in wisdom and endurance rather than mere arms or armor. The collection serves as a significant record of Nordic cultural values and folk philosophy.
topic_desc_basic: The Book of Nordic Proverbs is a collection of traditional Nord sayings. It reflects the pragmatic and fatalistic worldview of the Nordic people, offering wisdom on survival, mortality, and the transient nature of power through imagery of wolves, winter, and battle.

title: Book of the Master
topic_desc: The Book of the Master chronicles the tenure of a Morag Tong Grandmaster, recording their decisions and their consequences for the guild. It catalogs all Writs of Execution performed under their rule, listing the responsible agents, execution dates, the Great House leaders who contracted each assassination, and the fees paid. The account concludes by naming the agent who killed the Grandmaster to assume leadership, in accordance with the Morag Tong's traditional succession practice.
topic_desc_basic: A Morag Tong record that chronicles a Grandmaster's tenure, cataloging their decisions, the Writs of Execution carried out under their rule, and the agent who ultimately killed them to take their place.

title: Books of Sand v1
topic_desc: The Books of Sand constitute the first division of a five-part anthology compiled by Khajiiti and Imperial scribes shortly after Tiber Septim's conquest. Commissioned to help the Emperor understand the Khajiit, the project failed but preserved literature that would otherwise be lost. The Books of Sand focus on personal poetry and nursery rhymes, while companion volumes cover erotic tales (Sugar), maxims and fables (Meat), pseudo-historical and practical discourses (Rain), and mysticism (Dust). Later volumes appended to each series reflect more recent origins, with the earliest pre-dating the Third Era. Translated by Cassolar Draebo for Black Moon Publishing, the work demonstrates the challenges of rendering Ta'agra's alliterative, internally rhyming verse into Cyrodiilic, requiring creative pronoun substitutions and imposed titles for originally untitled poems.
topic_desc_basic: The Books of Sand are the first volume of a Khajiiti literary anthology compiled by Imperial-era scribes. They preserve personal poetry and nursery rhymes from Elsweyr that might otherwise have been lost.

title: Boots of Peace
topic_desc: The Boots of Peace are an enchanted pair of armored boots possessing properties that fortify a broad range of skills. Despite their name, they are presently held by the Dremora Lord Drekhva Yashaz within the Daedric shrine of Yashazmus, located in the Telvanni Isles.
topic_desc_basic: The Boots of Peace are an enchanted pair of armored boots known to fortify a broad range of skills. They are associated with the Daedric shrine of Yashazmus in the Telvanni Isles.

title: Boots of the Savior's Hide
topic_desc: The Boots of the Savior's Hide are an artifact of the Daedric Prince Hircine. They form a component of the Savior's Hide set, completing the ancient armor alongside the cuirass, greaves, pauldrons, gauntlets, and helm. As with the broader set, the boots are associated with Hircine's sphere of the hunt and lycanthropy.
topic_desc_basic: The Boots of the Savior's Hide are an artifact of Hircine. They are part of the Savior's Hide armor set and can be found in Helnim.

title: Boreal Hydnum
topic_desc: Boreal Hydnum is a fungus harvested for its alchemical properties. As a wild specimen, it is not cultivated or commonly stocked by merchants, requiring foragers to rely on chance encounters in appropriate terrains rather than guaranteed harvests. Its specific alchemical characteristics are known among practitioners, though its scarcity demands deliberate effort to procure in useful quantities.
topic_desc_basic: Boreal Hydnum is a wild fungus gathered for its alchemical properties. It is not cultivated or commonly sold, so foragers must find it in the wilderness.

title: Bottomweed
topic_desc: Bottomweed is an aquatic plant that grows beneath the waters of Skyrim. As a submerged flora, it is harvested for its alchemical properties by those with the skill to locate it in its natural environment.
topic_desc_basic: Bottomweed is an underwater plant found growing in the waters of Skyrim.

title: Bow of Heaven's Hail
topic_desc: The Bow of Heaven's Hail is a legendary weapon of immense destructive power, counted among the deadliest in Tamrielic legend by the Compendium of Lost Artifacts. It saw use during the invasion of the Battlespire in the Imperial Simulacrum. The bow is currently in the possession of the Dremora Lord Kraatas Zathan, who holds court near the Daedric Shrine of Anashbibi in Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: A legendary weapon of great destructive power. It is currently held by the Dremora Lord Kraatas Zathan near the Daedric Shrine of Anashbibi in Morrowind.

title: Brain Fever
topic_desc: Brain fever is an acute disease which provokes sometimes-lethal fevers, terrible headaches, and strong discoloration of the skin tissue on the brow and temples. It affects a patient's health, personality, and willpower. Fortunately, it is quite rare and only transmitted by white rats.
topic_desc_basic: Brain fever is a rare acute disease transmitted only by white rats. It causes severe fevers, intense headaches, and visible discoloration of the skin on the brow and temples. The illness can prove lethal.

title: Brain Rot
topic_desc: Brain Rot is a mild disease transmitted by mummies and muck leeches. It afflicts the victim's intelligence and strength. Physical symptoms include anemia and occasional fungal infestations of the scalp. Healers and alchemists possess the means to treat the condition.
topic_desc_basic: Brain Rot is a mild disease carried by mummies and muck leeches that saps a victim's strength and intelligence, causing anemia and sometimes scalp fungus.

title: Brass Ore
topic_desc: Brass Ore is a metallic mineral substance occasionally encountered in its raw form. The ore yields alchemical properties when processed, though its specific characteristics remain a subject for specialist study. As a natural resource, it holds potential utility in metallurgical and alchemical practices alike.
topic_desc_basic: Brass Ore is a raw metallic mineral. It is a relatively uncommon find, valued by those with skill in alchemy and metallurgy.

title: Bravil: Daughter of the Niben
topic_desc: A historical and cultural study of the Cyrodiilic town of Bravil, written by Destri Melarg. The work traces the region's Ayleid heritage, the Alessian conquest led by the centurion Teo Bravillius Tasus, and the origins of the Lucky Old Lady statue. Melarg recounts how the local Ayleid community resisted Imperial occupation through collective mastery of Alteration magic—levitation and water-breathing—concealing themselves after each siege until Tasus discovered their methods. The author further suggests that southern Ayleids developed Alteration as a formal magical school independently, paralleling the Psijic origins of Mysticism. The text also preserves the folk legend of the Lucky Old Lady, an illegitimate child blessed by a priest of Stendarr, whose generosity to a cursed prince brought prosperity to Bravil. The work stands as both local history and a meditation on the enduring cultural character of a Nibenese settlement.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Destri Melarg chronicling the history and character of Bravil, a town on the Niben River in southern Cyrodiil. It covers the region's Ayleid past, its conquest during the Alessian Rebellion by the centurion Teo Bravillius Tasus, and the legend of the Lucky Old Lady statue.

title: Bridethorn Berries
topic_desc: Bridethorn berries grow on the bridethorn, a thorn-bearing plant whose fruits are collected as a foodstuff and ingredient. They appear among Skyrim's wild flora, gathered by foragers and travelers in the region. Alchemists and hunters value them as a basic ingredient, though detailed accounts of their alchemical properties remain uncommon in standard references.
topic_desc_basic: Bridethorn berries are edible fruits gathered from thorny shrubs. They are found in Skyrim and used as both a foodstuff and an alchemical ingredient.

title: Broken Diamonds
topic_desc: Ryston Baylor's personal reflection on the Broken Diamonds holiday observed in Glenumbra Moors on the 19th of Frost Fall. The observance commemorates the murder of Empress Kintyra II on the 23rd of Frost Fall, 3E 123, ordered by her cousin and usurper Uriel III. Baylor recounts how locals silently circle a ruined castle each year to sing the Sephavre, an Old Bretic dirge whose meaning has faded over generations. The translated lyrics express ancestral guilt for failing to aid their imprisoned ruler, a shame that still afflicts the region. The holiday's name derives from the torn Red Diamond flags of the Septim family that littered the snow after the populace belatedly tried to block the killer's escape.
topic_desc_basic: Broken Diamonds is a sorrowful holiday in Glenumbra Moors commemorating the murder of Empress Kintyra II in 3E 123. Locals gather at a ruined castle to sing the Sephavre, mourning their ancestors' failure to aid their imprisoned ruler.

title: Brown Book of 3E 426
topic_desc: The Brown Book of 3E 426 is the annual yearbook of Great House Telvanni, documenting the council's membership, representatives, and significant actions for the year. It records Archmagister Dral governing the Telvannis District from Port Telvannis alongside Archmagister Gothren in Vvardenfell, and lists the Mouths who speak for the Mage Lords in the Parliament of Bugs and the Sadrith Mora Council Hall. The chronicle notes Mistress Eldale's elevation to the council after prolonged deliberation. It also formally reiterates the Telvanni stance on two contentious issues: the House refuses to constrain its members' exploration and colonization of Vvardenfell's wildernesses despite protests from Duke Dren and other Great Houses, and it firmly rejects any proposals to abridge the right to own and trade slaves, citing the Treaty of the Armistice.
topic_desc_basic: The Brown Book of 3E 426 is the annual yearbook of Great House Telvanni, recording the council's membership, their towers, and their representatives for the year. It also documents the House's refusal to restrict its members' colonization of Vvardenfell's wildernesses and its firm rejection of any challenges to the right to own and trade slaves.

title: Buck Moth Wing
topic_desc: Buck moth wings are harvested from the buck moth, a diurnal insect native to Skyrim. Two wings are typically recovered from each specimen. Alchemists value them for their innate properties, and hunters encounter the moths during daylight hours. Supply is unpredictable, as the wings are not cultivated or reliably stocked; instead, they enter circulation as random finds from the region's wilderness.
topic_desc_basic: Buck moth wings are taken from the buck moth, a daytime insect found in Skyrim. They serve as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Bug Shield of Vivec
topic_desc: The Bug Shield of Vivec is an artifact personally gifted by Lord Vivec to a Buoyant Armiger garrison. It is displayed in the Number Rooms Temple, where pilgrims travel from across Morrowind to look upon it. Commander Reloth serves as its sole custodian, strictly forbidding others from touching it. Vivec granted the shield as a safeguard against potential emergencies involving the Theologians and the Philosopher's Armor below, intended to prevent a catastrophe akin to the rampage of Ruddy Man. Some question the strategic wisdom of Vivec leaving both his shield and spear on the mainland while threats persist on Vvardenfell.
topic_desc_basic: The Bug Shield of Vivec is a sacred artifact gifted by Lord Vivec to a Buoyant Armiger garrison. It is displayed at the Number Rooms Temple, where it draws pilgrims from across Morrowind.

title: Burial of the Moths
topic_desc: Machil Coridale's treatise, commissioned by the Imperial Seminary, details the Nibenese practice of moth-burial. Ancestor Moths lay eggs in the recently deceased; the hatched larvae absorb the dead's essence before spinning blood-red cocoons. Nibenese silk-weavers harvest this silk, weaving it into ancestor cloth embroidered with genealogies, serving as a spiritual nexus. Silkhouses maintain withering-crypts for this process before final interment. Rural populations rely on wild moths and local weavers. Ancestor silk, distinct from common moth-silk, possesses superior durability and enchantment capacity. Trade in old silk from forgotten families is accepted, but stealing silk from the recently deceased is considered theft of history and essence. Destroying ancestor silk, termed ancestralcide, is a heinous crime met with severe retribution.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise by Machil Coridale on the Nibenese funerary custom of moth-burial. It describes how Ancestor Moths consume the dead and produce silk imbued with their essence, which weavers craft into genealogical ancestor cloth. The text also covers the silk trade and the severe crime of ancestralcide.

title: Cabbage Leaf
topic_desc: Cabbage leaves are the layered foliage of the cabbage, a common crop vegetable known to grow in Skyrim. They serve as a readily available botanical ingredient for alchemical preparation, valued as much for their agricultural accessibility as for their useful properties. While primarily cultivated as food, alchemists employ cabbage leaves for their inherent virtues in compounding.
topic_desc_basic: Cabbage leaves are the outer layers of the cabbage, a common crop vegetable grown in Skyrim. They are widely recognized as both a foodstuff and a basic alchemical ingredient.

title: Cairn Bolete Cap
topic_desc: The Cairn Bolete is a fungus that grows in subterranean and marshland environments, including the Dasek Marsh of Cyrodiil. Its cap is harvested as an alchemical ingredient valued by practitioners of potion-craft. The mushroom thrives in damp, dark conditions, making it familiar to those who frequent caves and wetland regions. Herbalists and alchemists recognize it as a useful component, and hunters who traverse such terrain often encounter it during their travels.
topic_desc_basic: A type of mushroom found growing naturally in caves and marshy regions of Cyrodiil, including the Dasek Marsh. Its cap is gathered for use as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Cake
