topic_desc: Cake is a baked sweet treat originating from Cyrodiil, where it is a recognized culinary confection. As an ingredient, it holds no known alchemical properties of interest to practitioners, functioning instead as a straightforward foodstuff. It is not gathered from the wild nor taken from game, placing it outside the typical purview of the hunter. Its preparation requires baking rather than butchery or harvest, and it remains a provincial specialty unfamiliar to Morrowind's native environment.
topic_desc_basic: Cake is a baked sweet treat usually found in Cyrodiil.

title: Caliron's Curse
topic_desc: Caliron's Curse is a serious disease that drains a sufferer's agility, speed, and strength. Those afflicted describe a sensation akin to being immersed in scrib jelly. The affliction can be contracted from eyestars, as well as from magical creatures such as golems and undead. Healers and alchemists recognize it as a persistent magical malady requiring dedicated curative treatments to resolve.
topic_desc_basic: Caliron's Curse is a serious disease that drains agility, speed, and strength, and causes a sensation like being immersed in scrib jelly. It is contracted from eyestars and magical creatures like golems or undead.

title: Camaraderie
topic_desc: A compilation of writings exploring companionship and bonding, featuring a soldier's lament on the cost of Imperial conquest, a commander's journal on training and unit cohesion, and a Redguard oral account of desert survival through mutual aid.
topic_desc_basic: A compilation of writings on companionship and bonding, including an Imperial soldier's reflections on war, a commander's thoughts on unit cohesion, and a Redguard oral history of survival.

title: Canah Feather
topic_desc: Plucked from the canah, a rare avian species endemic to the Summerset Isles, this feather is a scarce alchemical ingredient. Outside the isles, acquiring a specimen is exceptionally difficult; they appear on mainland Tamriel only through Altmer expatriates, who demand exorbitant sums for them. Their rarity and cost make them prized curiosities for specialist practitioners, though they remain virtually absent from typical supply chains.
topic_desc_basic: A feather taken from the canah, a rare bird found only in the Summerset Isles. They are occasionally sold on mainland Tamriel by Altmer expats at incredibly high prices.

title: Canis Root
topic_desc: Canis root is a botanical ingredient harvested from its namesake plant. Alchemists prize the root for its properties, which typically manifest in fortifying and restorative preparations. The plant grows in Skyrim's harsher climates, and the root is commonly gathered by hunters and herbalists who recognize its alchemical value. It appears in various regional ingredient stocks and random root harvests across the northern provinces.
topic_desc_basic: Canis root is an alchemical ingredient gathered from a plant found in Skyrim. It is valued by alchemists and hunters for its useful properties.

title: Canyon Thresher
topic_desc: Canyon Threshers are giant, horned, mer-eating insects that serve as the apex predators of the Shipal-Shin region. They stalk the canyons and caves of the area, preying upon local kwoom herds. Among the Shinathi people, defeating a thresher is a recognized mark of honor. The creatures are highly prized for Arena combat in Narsis due to their lethal nature. Frost magic is their only known weakness.
topic_desc_basic: Canyon Threshers are giant, horned, mer-eating insects that stalk the canyons and caves of Shipal-Shin, preying on kwoom herds.

title: Caput Mortuum
topic_desc: Caput Mortuum is a rare alchemical ingredient of uncertain natural origin. Its name, meaning 'dead head' in the old tongue, suggests it is a residual substance—perhaps a mineral remainder or necrotic byproduct—rather than a harvest from a living creature. It is not commonly found in the wilds, nor does it appear in the standard stocked supplies of most apothecaries or the loot of common game. Because of its scarcity and absence from typical leveled sources, it remains largely unknown outside specialist alchemical circles. Its properties are obscure, valued by dedicated practitioners for its unique characteristics rather than any widespread utility.
topic_desc_basic: Caput Mortuum is a rare alchemical ingredient. It is not found on common creatures or in typical merchant stock, making it difficult to obtain without specialist knowledge.

title: Cardamon Powder
topic_desc: Cardamon powder is a spice produced by grinding the seeds of the cardamon plant. Originating from the Summerset Isles, it serves as a valued culinary and alchemical ingredient. It is notably recognized as one of the spices featured in the preparation of Colovian Battlewine.
topic_desc_basic: Cardamon powder is a spice made from ground cardamon seeds. It originates from the Summerset Isles and is used in recipes like Colovian Battlewine.

title: Carline Thistle Seeds
topic_desc: Carline Thistle Seeds are the seeds of the carline thistle plant. They are recognized as an alchemical ingredient by apothecaries and hunters familiar with Skyrim's regional flora. The seeds are typically harvested from their thistle host and utilized in potion-making for their inherent properties. Their alchemical character and specific effects remain a matter for specialist study, requiring further experimentation or consultation of advanced botanical texts to determine their full potential in mixtures.
topic_desc_basic: Carline Thistle Seeds are an alchemical ingredient harvested from the carline thistle, a plant found in Skyrim's wilds.

title: Carrot
topic_desc: Carrots are purple root vegetables native to Cyrodiil, where they grow occasionally. While commonly harvested as food, alchemists value them for their properties. Their natural occurrence is largely limited to Cyrodiilic regions, making them a familiar but regionally characteristic specimen.
topic_desc_basic: Carrots are purple root vegetables that grow occasionally in Cyrodiil. They are commonly eaten as food.

title: Cathay
topic_desc: The Cathay are a bipedal furstock of Khajiit distinguished by their plantigrade stance, walking flat on their feet with a skeletal structure much more similar to that of Men and Mer. Like the Suthay-raht, they possess upright pointed ears, full fur, and long tails, though the Cathay are slightly larger and stronger, standing around the size of most Men and Mer. This robust, upright build places them among the most commonly seen Khajiit throughout Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: The Cathay are a common bipedal Khajiit furstock found throughout Tamriel. They are around the size of most Men and Mer, slightly larger and stronger than the Suthay-raht, and walk flat on their feet rather than on their toes.

title: Cave Bear
topic_desc: Cave bears are large, robust creatures found in cavernous and mountainous regions. Distinguished by their substantial bulk and thick fur, they are formidable omnivores capable of formidable aggression when provoked or defending their territory. While they typically forage for sustenance, their raw physical power makes them dangerous predators. Encounters with cave bears pose significant risk to travelers traversing rocky terrain, and their durable pelts are valued by hunters for warmth and trade.
topic_desc_basic: Cave bears are large, powerful beasts that inhabit mountainous and cavernous regions. They are highly aggressive when provoked and pose a significant threat to travelers and hunters alike.

title: Cave Troll Ear
topic_desc: Cave Troll Ears are ears taken from cave trolls, creatures found throughout Tamriel. They serve as an alchemical ingredient, and specimens circulate among apothecaries and hunters familiar with the beasts.
topic_desc_basic: Cave Troll Ears are ears harvested from cave trolls, creatures found throughout Tamriel. They are used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Census and Excise Office
topic_desc: The Census and Excise Office is an Imperial organization responsible for managing population counts, tax assessment, and excise collection throughout the Empire. Imperial taxation relies on head counts of citizens, making the office essential for provincial revenue. Beyond tax collection, its officers administer various Imperial licenses, including those for importation and mercenary company incorporation. The office maintains a presence in major ports across Tamriel, such as Seyda Neen in Vvardenfell, facilitating the oversight of trade and population movement.
topic_desc_basic: The Census and Excise Office is an Imperial organization that counts citizens for taxation and collects excise duties. It also administers Imperial licenses for imports and mercenary companies, and operates in ports across Tamriel, including Seyda Neen.

title: Cephalopod Shell Fragment
topic_desc: Cephalopod shell fragments are durable remnants shed by Telvanni cephalopods. Among seafarers, these shells serve as prized trophies and are frequently kept as good luck charms by superstitious fishermen and shipmasters. Beyond their talismanic value, the fragments possess useful alchemical properties appreciated by skilled practitioners, who employ them as an ingredient in various preparations.
topic_desc_basic: These shells come from Telvanni cephalopods. Superstitious sailors and fishermen often carry them as good luck charms, while alchemists value them as a useful ingredient.

title: Chalk
topic_desc: Chalk is a soft, white mineral substance occasionally gathered for alchemical use. Its natural origin and specific properties remain poorly documented in standard references, and it is not widely traded or encountered in common alchemical practice. As a reagent, it holds limited circulation among apothecaries and is notably absent from conventional supply channels, suggesting either a highly specialized application or a rarity that restricts its study to dedicated practitioners.
topic_desc_basic: Chalk is a soft, white mineral occasionally used in alchemy. It is rare and not commonly found in standard merchant supplies.

title: Charcoal
topic_desc: Charcoal is the lightweight black residue left after organic material, typically wood, has been burned in the absence of air. It retains the shape and grain of its source material but is reduced almost entirely to carbon. Miners and laborers gather it from controlled burns and from deposits encountered in excavation. Beyond its common use as fuel for fires and smelting, charcoal is valued by alchemists, who grind it down as a reagent in the preparation of potions. Its alchemical character derives from its concentrated carbon, produced through incomplete combustion rather than from any living creature or mineral vein.
topic_desc_basic: Charcoal is the black carbon residue left after wood or similar organic matter is burned without sufficient air. It is widely used as fuel for fires and smelting, and alchemists also grind it for use as a potion ingredient.

title: Charity and Leadership
topic_desc: A treatise by Serjo Indoril Daris Varen articulating House Indoril's self-conception as Morrowind's rightful spiritual and temporal authority. Varen argues that Indoril's intimacy with ALMSIVI confers a duty to extend charity toward lower-born Dunmer, drawing them into Temple grace and service. The work contrasts Indoril piety against Hlaalu's embrace of Imperial commerce, which it frames as spiritually ruinous. Varen attributes to Indoril lineage the qualities of healing after Ayem, mystic discernment after Seht, and martial resolve after Vehk, presenting these alongside iron will and endurance against the House of Troubles as essential leadership traits. The text functions as an ideological declaration of Indoril supremacy within Dunmer society and a defense of the House's traditional role.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Serjo Indoril Daris Varen setting forth House Indoril's claim to be Morrowind's holiest Great House and rightful leader. It argues that the House's closeness to ALMSIVI obliges its members to practice charity toward common Dunmer and guide them into Temple service, while criticizing Hlaalu for adopting Imperial, commerce-driven ways.

title: Cheese
topic_desc: Cheese is a dairy product made by fermenting and pressing milk from various mammals into a solid food. It is produced across Skyrim, Cyrodiil, Hammerfell, and High Rock, each culture yielding its own variants. The milk may come from cows, goats, sheep, echatere, mammoths, giant bats, or even rodents. Cheese appears in forms ranging from truckles known as cheese wheels to liquid cheese dips, and is commonly stored in barrels and crates. It features in simple meals alongside soup, bread, and tea, or in more refined settings paired with wine. Giant rats are drawn to its scent and may infest stores of it. Alchemically, cheese exhibits properties useful in potions and poisons alike, though its effects vary by variety and specimen.
topic_desc_basic: Cheese is a dairy food made by fermenting and pressing milk from mammals such as cows, goats, and sheep. It is produced across Skyrim, Cyrodiil, Hammerfell, and High Rock, each with its own variants, and commonly stored in wheels, barrels, or crates.

title: Chicken Leg
topic_desc: A chicken leg is a cut of meat harvested from chickens, domesticated fowl raised on farms throughout Cyrodiil and Skyrim. As a common foodstuff, it is widely recognized for its nutritional value rather than any alchemical potency. Within the practice of alchemy, the ingredient is classified among mundane animal parts, typically yielding only the most basic of properties when subjected to refinement, and is generally considered a staple of provincial larders rather than a reagent of significance to serious practitioners.
topic_desc_basic: A chicken leg is a cut of meat from chickens, domesticated fowl raised on farms throughout Cyrodiil and Skyrim. It is a common foodstuff.

title: Chokeberry
topic_desc: Chokeberry is a small fruit harvested from the chokeberry shrub. Alchemists value the berry for its toxic properties, and hunters occasionally employ it as a natural poison.
topic_desc_basic: Chokeberry is a small, poisonous berry. It grows on shrubs and is commonly used by alchemists and hunters for its toxic properties.

title: Chrondiasis
topic_desc: Chrondiasis is a mild disease that attacks a sufferer's magicka and intelligence. Its primary symptom is a clouded mind, diminishing both arcane capacity and mental acuity. The affliction can be transmitted through contact with liches and mud golems. As a relatively minor condition, it is within the scope of standard healing and alchemical practice to diagnose and treat.
topic_desc_basic: Chrondiasis is a mild disease that drains magicka and clouds the mind, reducing intelligence. It can be caught from liches and mud golems.

title: Cinnabar Polypore Red Cap
topic_desc: A red-capped variety of cinnabar polypore mushroom bearing a distinctive reddish cap. As a fungal ingredient, it is collected from the wild and employed in alchemical preparations. The cinnabar polypore family is recognized among herbalists and alchemists as a source of useful reagents, with the red-capped form representing one of its known varieties.
topic_desc_basic: A red-capped mushroom known to alchemists as a variety of cinnabar polypore, gathered from the wild for use in alchemy.

title: Cinnabar Polypore Yellow Cap
topic_desc: The yellow-capped variety of cinnabar polypore is a distinct mushroom prized for its alchemical properties. Like other polypores, it grows upon wood, though its exact habitats remain loosely documented. Alchemists and hunters value the cap for its contributions to potion-making, differentiating it from related polypore species by its distinctive coloration.
topic_desc_basic: Cinnabar Polypore Yellow Caps are a variety of mushroom valued as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Citrine
topic_desc: Citrine is a crystalline mineral ingredient. Its alchemical properties remain a subject for specialist study, as its practical applications in potion-making are not widely documented in common circles. The stone is occasionally unearthed in regions such as Cyrodiil and Hammerfell, where it is valued alongside other precious gems.
topic_desc_basic: Citrine is a crystalline gemstone and mineral ingredient occasionally unearthed in Imperial and Redguard territories.

title: Clam Meat
topic_desc: Clam meat is the edible flesh harvested from clams, bivalve mollusks found resting on the seafloor. Prized as a form of seafood, it is a guaranteed yield when foraging from these coastal beds. Alchemists value clam meat for its intrinsic properties, while hunters and coastal foragers gather it as a staple maritime foodstuff. It is commonly traded and distributed through general seafood provisions.
topic_desc_basic: Clam meat is edible flesh harvested from clams on the seafloor. It serves as a common seafood and alchemical ingredient.

title: Claw of Nafaalilargus
topic_desc: The Claw of Nafaalilargus is a powerful artifact associated with the Imperial red dragon Nafaalilargus. This short sword is kept alongside the Scales of Nafaalilargus within a secret stone safe concealed in the private quarters of Caecalia Victrix, the Imperial Legion Lord General of Morrowind, at the top of the Imperial Legion Headquarters in Old Ebonheart. The safe is accessed via a switch hidden behind a locked painting of the dragon.
topic_desc_basic: The Claw of Nafaalilargus is a powerful short sword associated with the Imperial red dragon Nafaalilargus. It is kept in a secret safe within the Imperial Legion Headquarters in Old Ebonheart.

title: Clearwing Moth Wing
topic_desc: Clearwing Moth Wings are the delicate wings harvested from the clearwing moth, an insect native to Skyrim that is active during both day and night. As an alchemical ingredient, the wing is valued by practitioners for its inherent properties. Because the moths are relatively common throughout their native range, the wings are a familiar sight in apothecaries' inventories and foraging supplies, often gathered by hunters and alchemists traversing Skyrim's wilderness.
topic_desc_basic: Clearwing Moth Wings are alchemical ingredients taken from the clearwing moth, a creature found in Skyrim that is active day and night.

title: Cloud Flutterling Wing
topic_desc: The Cloud Flutterling Wing is an alchemical ingredient harvested from the Cloud Flutterling, a species of butterfly native to Skyrim. These diurnal insects are active only during daylight hours, requiring hunters to seek them by sun. As with other butterflies, each specimen yields two wings. The wings are valued by alchemists for their properties, though they are not commonly found as loose samples and must typically be gathered directly from the living creatures.
topic_desc_basic: A butterfly wing harvested from the Cloud Flutterling, a diurnal insect found in the skies of Skyrim during daylight hours.

title: Clouded Funnel Cap
topic_desc: Clouded Funnel Caps are a variety of mushroom found across Tamriel. Mycologists and alchemists value these fungi for their organic properties, which make them a useful reagent in potion-making. As a common woodland growth, hunters and foragers often gather them alongside wild game, while alchemists seek them out as a staple ingredient for experimental or restorative mixtures.
topic_desc_basic: Clouded Funnel Caps are a type of mushroom used in alchemy.

title: Cloudy Corn
topic_desc: Cloudy corn is a grain cultivated as a dietary staple throughout Skyrim, with extensive farming particularly concentrated across the Reach. Its hardy cultivation sustains the region's population, and it serves as a common agricultural product and ingredient in local foodstuffs.
topic_desc_basic: Cloudy corn is a grain widely farmed across the Reach in Skyrim, where it serves as a dietary staple.

title: Coal
topic_desc: Coal is a dark, combustible mineral substance. It is primarily valued as a fuel source for hearths and forges, though alchemists occasionally employ it as a reagent. Its precise alchemical properties remain poorly documented in standard texts. The mineral is widely sourced from mining operations across Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: Coal is a dark, combustible mineral used mainly as fuel for forges and hearths, though it also sees use as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Cod
topic_desc: Cod is the flesh of the cod fish, a saltwater species prevalent in the seas around Skyrim. Harvested for its meat, it serves as a common foodstuff and is frequently preserved through salting to extend its viability for trade and travel. Beyond its culinary role, cod is recognized in alchemical practice for its intrinsic properties, making it a staple ingredient for practitioners processing marine materials. Hunters and fishermen routinely procure the fish from northern waters to supply both the table and the apothecary.
topic_desc_basic: Cod is the meat of a saltwater fish found in the seas around Skyrim. It is commonly eaten and often preserved in salted form.

title: Codified Law, Vol. I
topic_desc: Codified Law, Vol. I is an excerpt-book of the Alessian Doctrines written by the prophet Marukh. Though the Doctrines are now considered heretical, certain Marukhati principles—such as the presumption of guilt until innocence is proven—remain foundational to Imperial law. Due to the Doctrines' condemned status, their promulgation is strictly limited; excerpt-volumes like this one are permitted only among authorized students and practitioners of law. The text itself is encrypted using legal ciphers, with the decryption keys closely guarded by the Guild of Barristers, ensuring that the full Doctrines remain inaccessible to the general populace.
topic_desc_basic: Codified Law, Vol. I is an encrypted excerpt-book of the Alessian Doctrines by the prophet Marukh. Though the Doctrines are now considered heretical, some Marukhati principles remain foundational to Imperial law. Access to these texts is restricted to authorized legal practitioners, and the Guild of Barristers guards the cipher keys required to read them.

title: Codified Law, Vol. II
topic_desc: An excerpt-book of the Alessian Doctrines written by the prophet Marukh, encrypted by legal ciphers controlled by the Guild of Barristers. Though the Doctrines are considered heretical today, certain Marukhati principles, such as the presumption of guilt until innocence is proven, remain foundational to Imperial law. Such volumes are permitted only for authorized legal scholars.
topic_desc_basic: An encrypted excerpt of the Alessian Doctrines by the prophet Marukh, restricted to authorized legal scholars. Certain Marukhati principles within remain foundational to Imperial law despite the Doctrines' heretical status.

title: Codified Law, Vol. III
topic_desc: Codified Law, Vol. III is an excerpt-book of the Alessian Doctrines, the founding edicts of the Alessian Order written by the prophet Marukh. Though the Doctrines are now considered heretical, certain Marukhati principles remain foundational to Imperial Law. This volume is one of the few sanctioned ways the Doctrines are permitted to be promulgated, restricted to authorized students and practitioners of law. Its contents are encrypted using legal ciphers, with the keys closely guarded by the Guild of Barristers, ensuring the esoteric legal precepts remain inaccessible to the uninitiated.
topic_desc_basic: Codified Law, Vol. III is an encrypted excerpt-book of the Alessian Doctrines. Though the Doctrines are now considered heretical, some of their principles remain foundational to Imperial Law. Access is restricted to authorized legal practitioners, and the contents are encrypted by the Guild of Barristers.

title: Colovian Bread
topic_desc: Colovian Bread are loaves of bread baked in the Colovian style of western Cyrodiil. Those baked in other provinces are adapted to use locally grown wheat and are often considered inferior, if still enjoyable, compared to genuine loaves. The bread is found in whole and half loaf variants. As a staple foodstuff, it serves primarily as sustenance rather than a potent alchemical reagent, though its regional variations in grain composition may yield minor properties of interest to practitioners.
topic_desc_basic: Colovian Bread is a loaf baked in the Colovian style of western Cyrodiil. Provincial loaves adapted to local wheat are considered inferior to genuine ones. It comes in whole and half loaves.

title: Colovian Cheese
topic_desc: Colovian Cheese is a common foodstuff originating from the Colovian regions of Cyrodiil. As a staple provision, it reflects the pastoral and agricultural character of western Imperial territory. While widely consumed as nourishment, alchemists recognize it as an ingredient with distinct, if modest, alchemical properties. Its specific animal origin and full alchemical profile remain subjects of specialist study rather than common knowledge.
topic_desc_basic: Colovian Cheese is a common food item imported from Cyrodiil.

title: Colovian Grapes
topic_desc: Colovian Grapes are a variety of grape cultivated in eastern Colovia, Cyrodiil. Primarily farmed for winemaking and other beverages, they also serve as a common food item within the province. Though imported to Skyrim and Morrowind, they reach these markets only in small quantities. Alchemists value them for their properties, which stem from their natural fruit composition.
topic_desc_basic: Colovian Grapes are a variety of grape grown in eastern Colovia, Cyrodiil. They are primarily farmed for making wine and other beverages, and are a common food item there. Small amounts are imported to Skyrim and Morrowind.

title: Comatus Corpinus
topic_desc: Comatus corpinus is a rare botanical ingredient of uncertain specific origin, known primarily to alchemists and skilled hunters through scattered foraging rather than cultivated or guaranteed sources. The plant's appearance and the precise nature of its harvestable matter remain poorly documented in standard herbalist references. Its alchemical character is recognized by specialists, though its properties are seldom discussed outside circles that regularly process uncommon flora. The ingredient is encountered unpredictably in the wild, associated with the temperate and harsh climes where such elusive plants compete for survival, and it occasionally appears in the randomized botanical stocks gathered by travelers from Skyrim's wilderness.
topic_desc_basic: Comatus corpinus is a rare plant ingredient occasionally gathered from the wilderness, most notably in Skyrim. It has no known cultivated or reliable sources, making it unfamiliar to the general public.

title: Compendium of Lost Artifacts
topic_desc: A compilation of research notes on legendary items once possessed by mortals or lost to the ages. The anonymous author asserts that the cataloged artifacts genuinely exist and are actively pursued, including by high-ranking Imperial officials. The work surveys over two dozen renowned relics, detailing their attributed powers, known histories, and rumored locations. Subjects range from Aedric items like Auriel's Bow and Shield, to Daedric gifts such as Azura's Star, Hircine's Ring, and the Oghma Infinium, alongside historically significant pieces like the Flask of Lillandril and the Necromancer's Amulet. Several entries note artifacts associated with the Imperial Battlespire or exhibiting a notorious tendency to vanish and reappear across Tamriel. The compendium serves as a significant scholarly reference for artifact hunters and researchers studying Tamriel's most elusive and powerful objects.
topic_desc_basic: A book of research notes describing legendary artifacts from across Tamriel, including Auriel's Bow, the Necromancer's Amulet, and the Oghma Infinium. It details the powers and histories of these renowned relics, many of which are said to vanish and reappear throughout the ages.

title: Confessions and Last Resort
topic_desc: Salar Nydendan's autobiographical testament chronicling his descent into madness after participating in a Tribunal Temple raid against a Sheogorath shrine. A former Ordinator of House Indoril, Salar details how the destruction of the Mad God's statue brought insidious whispers that gradually eroded his sanity, costing him his family and dignity. Abandoned and alone, he wrote these confessions after Sheogorath himself appeared, offering to claim him for mindless oblivion. The work stands as a grim account of Daedric retribution and the peril of opposing the Prince of Madness.
topic_desc_basic: Salar Nydendan's autobiographical account of his descent into madness after helping destroy a Sheogorath shrine during his service as a Tribunal Temple Ordinator.

title: Confessions of a Thief
topic_desc: An anonymous first-person account defending the profession of theft and the role of the Thieves Guild within the Empire. The author argues that regulated crime benefits the economy and that rulers tacitly rely on the Guild to suppress amateur thieves. The narrative details the author's recruitment during the Imperial Simulacrum, driven by destitution after their family farm failed, and describes the Guild's coercive enrollment methods, professional training, and capacity for retaliation against hostile authorities. The work serves as a primary source on Guild operations and the socio-economic rationalizations of its members.
topic_desc_basic: An anonymous first-person account that defends theft as a legitimate profession and explains the Thieves Guild's role in regulating crime across the Empire.

title: Constant Invocation
topic_desc: Constant Invocation is a liturgical text that presents the Nine Divines as an interdependent cycle. Each divine's domain flows into the next: Kynareth's rain nurtures Dibella's flowers, whose beauty softens Arkay's mortality, recorded by Julianos, forged by Zenithar, wielded by Tiber Septim against foes who fall on Mara's fields, yielding fruit for Stendarr's wine, whose mercy is seen by Akatosh, whose judgment returns the cycle to Kynareth. The verse repeats endlessly, varying only the adjective for Akatosh's judgment—eternal, immortal, unchanging, constant—emphasizing the unbroken, perpetual nature of the divine order. The work serves as a meditative invocation, reinforcing the theological view that the Divines are not isolated patrons but a unified, self-sustaining cosmic circuit.
topic_desc_basic: A devotional text presenting the Nine Divines as an endless, interdependent cycle where each god's domain flows into the next, reinforcing their unity.

title: Copper Ore
topic_desc: Copper ore is a mined mineral used as an alchemical ingredient. It appears among mineral collections and mining supplies across several regions of Tamriel, including those associated with Direnni mineral holdings.
topic_desc_basic: Copper ore is a common metallic mineral mined from deposits across Tamriel and used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Cornflower Sprig
topic_desc: Cornflower sprigs are cuttings of the cornflower plant, a flora native to the province of High Rock. Recognized by alchemists and hunters for their reliable alchemical properties, these sprigs serve as standard reagents in potion-crafting. The plant's prevalence in its home province ensures a steady supply for practitioners familiar with High Rock's vegetation.
topic_desc_basic: Cornflower sprigs are cuttings of the cornflower plant, a flower native to High Rock. They are commonly gathered for use as alchemical ingredients.

title: Corprus: The Divine Disease
topic_desc: A scholarly treatise by Dralas Therayn examining corprus, the affliction Divayth Fyr terms the
topic_desc_basic: A treatise by Dralas Therayn cataloguing corprus, the incurable affliction called the

title: Courtesans Guild
topic_desc: The Courtesans Guild is an Empire-wide association that sets standards for courtesans and affiliated businesses across Tamriel. Its members are protected by Imperial law and the organization's reputation; clients who mistreat Guild courtesans face blacklisting from every recognized Guild brothel, from Daggerfall to Thorn. Establishments operating outside Guild oversight are typically shabby and exploitative, lacking the protections and quality the Guild enforces. The Guild favors skills in Hand-to-hand, Speechcraft, Sneak, Unarmored, and Athletics, reflecting both the social grace and personal resilience expected of its members. It holds an adversarial relationship with several vampire clans.
topic_desc_basic: The Courtesans Guild is an Empire-wide association that sets standards for courtesans and their businesses. Members are protected by Imperial law and the Guild's reputation; clients who behave badly are blacklisted from Guild brothels across Tamriel. Establishments outside the Guild's oversight are generally shabby and exploitative.

title: Cow
topic_desc: Cows are large domesticated farm animals widely kept as beasts of burden across agricultural settlements. They are a common and significant source of dairy and meat products for the populace.
topic_desc_basic: Cows are large farm animals commonly raised for dairy, meat, and labor as beasts of burden.

title: Cowbell Flower
topic_desc: Cowbell flowers are pale yellow flowers that grow in Skyrim. Their alchemical properties are of interest to practitioners, though their specific effects require specialist knowledge to detail. As mountain flora, they are typically gathered by those familiar with Skyrim's rugged terrain and are distributed through general regional ingredient supplies.
topic_desc_basic: Cowbell flowers are pale yellow flowers that grow in Skyrim.

title: Cracker
topic_desc: Crackers are little discs of baked dough prepared from flour, water, and olive oil. Originating in Cyrodiil, they serve as a common staple food and provision. Their simple, durable composition makes them suitable for travel and storage, and they circulate widely as a standard ration throughout the Imperial province.
topic_desc_basic: Crackers are little discs of baked dough made from flour, water, and olive oil, commonly found in Cyrodiil.

title: Crag Beetle Shell
topic_desc: Crag beetle shells are harvested from the chitinous forewings of crag beetles, a fauna native to Morrowind. The shells serve a dual purpose in local craft and alchemy. Armorsmiths grind and dissolve the shells, mixing the resulting compound with bone shards and resin to produce bonemold and aena armors and weapons. Beyond their material utility in smithing, crag beetle shells also possess distinct alchemical virtues, making them a valued reagent among alchemists.
topic_desc_basic: Crag beetle shells come from the chitinous forewings of Morrowind's crag beetles. They are commonly ground and dissolved with bone shards and resin to craft bonemold and aena equipment, and also hold alchemical value.

title: Crown of Ushu-Dimmu
topic_desc: The Crown of Ushu-Dimmu is an ancient crown found upon the head of the mummy Ushu-Dimmu. Its origins and specific enchantments remain obscure, though its enduring presence on an undead sovereign suggests potent magical properties. The relic is associated with a curse tied to its bearer, marking it as an artifact of considerable arcane and historical significance.
topic_desc_basic: The Crown of Ushu-Dimmu is an ancient crown found upon the head of the mummy Ushu-Dimmu.

title: Crowned Kagouti Hide
topic_desc: Crowned Kagouti Hide is the pelt of the Crowned Kagouti, a distinctive beast native to the Armun Ashlands of western Morrowind. The hide is valued by alchemists and hunters familiar with the region's fauna. It circulates through general ingredient trade networks across Morrowind, appearing in varied regional supply lists from Narsis to Velothi lands.
topic_desc_basic: Crowned Kagouti Hide is a pelt taken from the Crowned Kagouti, a creature of the Armun Ashlands in western Morrowind. It is traded as an alchemical ingredient throughout the region.

title: Crusader's Ring
topic_desc: The Crusader's Ring is a ring that enhances certain skills associated with the Crusader class when worn. It is presently kept within a chest belonging to Duchess Perulia Jandacia, located in the Ducal Chambers of Ember Keep in Firewatch. The chest is concealed behind a hidden door covered by a wall hanging.
topic_desc_basic: The Crusader's Ring is a ring that enhances skills associated with the Crusader class. It is kept in a hidden chest within Duchess Perulia Jandacia's chambers in Ember Keep at Firewatch.

title: Cultural Eras of the Nords
topic_desc: A scholarly treatise by Elonwe of Lillandril proposing a six-era framework for Nordic history based on cultural evolution rather than the Standard Era calendar. The work traces Nordic development from the oral totemic traditions of Atmora through the Falmer conflicts and the anthropomorphization of the pantheon, into the record-keeping of Harald's First Empire, the internecine Broken Sky and Way of the Voice, the cultural dilution under Cyrodiilic vassalage, and finally the Talos Period's revival of traditional myth and song under the Septim Empire.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly work by Elonwe of Lillandril proposing a six-era framework for Nordic history based on cultural evolution rather than the Standard Era calendar, tracing Nordic development from early Atmoran totems through the First Empire, the Way of the Voice, and the current Talos Period.

title: Cunning, Contempt, Confusion
topic_desc: Cunning, Contempt, Confusion is a political treatise written for the conservators of House Dres. It outlines three paths of governance, each framed as an anticipation of one of the Tribunal: cunning for Almalexia, contempt for Sotha Sil, and confusion for Vivec. The Way of Cunning advocates incremental, concealed advancement through mechanical metaphors like the ratchet and flood. The Way of Contempt teaches the cultivation and controlled release of disdain to manipulate both subordinates and rivals, using clockwork imagery. The Way of Confusion promotes deliberate contradiction between words and actions, prioritizing personal loyalty and secret machinations over formal titles. The work argues that laws should be secret and ambiguous, motivations obscured, and power maintained through webs of obligation and deceit.
topic_desc_basic: Cunning, Contempt, Confusion is a political treatise written for House Dres conservators. It outlines three paths of governance—cunning, contempt, and confusion—each associated with one of the Tribunal, advocating manipulation, controlled disdain, and deliberate deception as tools of rule.

title: Cured Siyat
topic_desc: Cured Siyat is a prepared ingredient derived from siyat through an unspecified curing process. Its alchemical properties and precise origin remain poorly documented in standard references. As it does not circulate through common trade channels or appear in leveled merchant stock, it is primarily of interest to specialist alchemists and hunters familiar with obscure regional preparations. The specific qualities that distinguish it from uncured siyat are not widely recorded.
topic_desc_basic: Cured Siyat is a prepared form of siyat, created through a curing process. It is not commonly traded or found in regular merchant supplies.

title: Cusp Moth Wing
topic_desc: Cusp Moth Wings are harvested from the Cusp Moth, a relatively uncommon moth native to Cyrodiil. The insect is nocturnal, appearing only under cover of darkness, which constrains collection to nighttime hours. The wings are recognized as alchemical ingredients and circulate among apothecaries and ingredient traders familiar with Cyrodilic fauna. Their relative scarcity compared to more common moth species lends them a modest but steady demand in alchemical practice.
topic_desc_basic: Cusp Moth Wings are the wings of the Cusp Moth, a relatively uncommon moth native to Cyrodiil that flies only at night. The wings are gathered for use as alchemical ingredients.

title: Daedra Silk
topic_desc: Daedra Silk is a rare alchemical ingredient harvested from Spider Daedra and their stronger variants. Woven from these Daedric creatures, the silk possesses notable magical properties valued by alchemists and hunters who dare to face such dangerous prey. Its alchemical character is distinctive, yielding rare effects that include the capacity to impair physical endurance and to bend light around the subject to achieve chameleon-like concealment. These uncommon properties make the substance sought after for specialized preparations, though its origin ensures it remains difficult to obtain.
topic_desc_basic: Daedra Silk is a rare ingredient obtained from Spider Daedra. It is prized by alchemists for its unusual magical properties.

title: Dagi-raht
topic_desc: The Dagi-raht are a less common bipedal furstock of the Khajiit, bearing lynx-like facial features and a diminutive, skeletal frame. They are slightly larger than the Dagi, though the difference is the slightest among all Khajiit furstocks. Dagi-raht prefer an arboreal existence, dwelling in the higher jungle branches of the Tenmar Forest that cannot support a Bosmer's weight. Their light build and natural agility make them nimble acrobats who always land on their feet, and they possess exceptionally sharp claws for physical combat. While outsiders stereotype Khajiit as lacking magical aptitude, the Dagi-raht are suspected of greater magical talent, particularly in Mysticism, making them effective spellcasters, thieves, assassins, and nightblades. Their unsettling appearance often engenders distrust from other races and even fellow Khajiit.
topic_desc_basic: The Dagi-raht are a less common bipedal Khajiit furstock with lynx-like features and a slight, skeletal frame. They live in the high jungle branches of the Tenmar Forest and are known for their agility, sharp claws, and magical talent, particularly in Mysticism.

title: Danswyrm Venom Gland
topic_desc: A venom gland harvested from a danswyrm, yielding a potent alchemical substance. Its properties make it a valued component among apothecaries and poisoners who work with beast-derived reagents. The gland's toxic nature requires careful handling during extraction and preparation.
topic_desc_basic: A venom gland taken from a danswyrm. It is used in alchemy for its poisonous properties.

title: Dark Elf Craftsmanship
topic_desc: Dark Elven craftsmanship encompasses a range of material traditions shaped by resource availability and devotional practice. Stone was historically common for ordinary household vessels, though modern Dunmer frequently use limeware, clay, or glass for such purposes. Distinctive Tribunate craftsmanship is identified by intricate Velothi patterns featuring the scarab—a holy symbol since the First Era—and stylized holy figures common to Temple art, often adorning decorative bowls rather than practical storage. Certain ornate turquoise containers, recovered from abandoned Telvanni towers, are employed by House Indoril in obscure inner-nobility rituals. Archaeological finds at Firewatch confirm pre-Armistice settlements, while the region's borderlands yield remnants of abandoned Telvanni holdings. The oldest known artifacts, such as an enigmatic carved stone possibly serving as a primitive spokeshave, remain difficult to identify.
topic_desc_basic: Dark Elven craftsmanship traditionally favored stoneware for everyday vessels, though modern Dunmer commonly use limeware, clay, or glass instead. Signature Tribunate styles feature intricate Velothi patterns, the holy scarab, and stylized Temple figures, primarily as decoration rather than storage. House Indoril also crafts ornate ritual containers.

title: Dark Sage Petals
topic_desc: Dark Sage Petals are the petals of the Dark Sage plant, found in Skyrim. Dark Sage is also dried and hung from rope for use in cooking. There are no guaranteed samples. However, they are found in the following leveled lists: T_Sky_Random_FlorDarkSage T_Sky_Random_Ingredient
topic_desc_basic: Dark Sage Petals are the petals of the Dark Sage plant, found in Skyrim. Dark Sage is also dried and hung from rope for use in cooking.

title: De Rerum Dirennis
topic_desc: A genealogical and anecdotal chronicle by Vorian Direnni, an Altmer wizard claiming six centuries of life, recounting the lesser-known magical ancestors of his clan. The work centers on Asliel Direnni, an early Summurset farmer from the village of Tyrigel who, through herb expertise and necessity, formulated alchemy into a systematic art and science. Vorian traces a lineage of Direnni mages including Raven Direnni, credited with creating enchantment before the Psijic Order; Pelladil Direnni, who encouraged the Guild Act; Jovron Direnni, Imperial Battlemage to Empress Katariah; and Medora Direnni, court sorceress to King Lysandus of Daggerfall. The text blends family pride with historical claim, asserting that these magical ancestors shaped Tamriel's destiny as profoundly as the clan's celebrated warriors and rulers.
topic_desc_basic: A chronicle by the Altmer wizard Vorian Direnni recounting the magical ancestors of his clan. Its central figure is Asliel Direnni, an early Summurset farmer credited with formulating alchemy into a formal art and science. The work also profiles several Direnni mages who served as imperial battlemages and court sorcerers.

title: De Sphaera Nirni
topic_desc: A scholarly treatise by Deniel Juris detailing the cosmological structure of the Mundus, arguing that Nirn is the immovable center of the celestial spheres and explaining the arrangement of the Divines, Principalities, elements, and stars.
topic_desc_basic: De Sphaera Nirni is a scholarly work by Deniel Juris concerning the shape and cosmological structure of the Mundus, arguing that Nirn is the immovable center of the celestial spheres.

title: Dead Magic
topic_desc: A lecture by Archmagister Xodores, delivered at the Anticlere Mages Guild in 3E 422, arguing against the classification of magic as a stable science. Xodores contends that magic is fundamentally change and cannot be permanently classified or understood, warning that mages who forget this risk destruction. He cites the fate of the eastern mage Barilzar, whose Mazed Band artifact violently malfunctioned and consumed him, as well as the loss of Passwall and the Warp in the West, as evidence that arcane rules shift unpredictably. A publisher's note records that Xodores has not been seen publicly since delivering this lecture.
topic_desc_basic: A lecture by Archmagister Xodores delivered in 3E 422 arguing that magic is inherently unstable and cannot be treated as a science, citing historical instances of arcane rules shifting unpredictably.

title: Death Bell
topic_desc: Death Bells are bright purple flowers that grow in Skyrim. They are recognized in alchemical practice for their distinct properties and are considered a rare ingredient, typically gathered from the harsh northern climates rather than cultivated.
topic_desc_basic: Death Bells are bright purple flowers found growing in Skyrim.

title: Death by Water
topic_desc: Death by Water is a scholarly treatise by Machil Coridale, composed by order of the Imperial Seminary as part of the broader work Funerary Rites of Cyrodiil. It examines the ancient Nibenese custom of river-burial, tracing its presumed Nedic origins—where moth-embalmed bodies were cast in hako skiffs down the Niben toward Topal Bay—and its modern evolution. The treatise details the Order of the Psychopompoi, an Arkay sub-cult whose skiffmen transport the dead to stone catacombs built along the Niben and its tributaries. Coridale also addresses the ritual's decline: the Niben's role as a busy trade artery has rendered water-burial impractical, and the Elder Council's harsh tax now restricts the practice to affluent castes. The text further notes the interrelation of water-burial with moth-burial, persistent rumors of vampires and wreck-haunts inhabiting the catacombs, and traditionalist objections that the catacombs pervert the original rite.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly work by Machil Coridale, part of Funerary Rites of Cyrodiil, examining the ancient Nibenese custom of river-burial. It describes how moth-embalmed bodies were cast in skiffs down the Niben River and the modern practice involving Arkay's Psychopompoi sub-cult and stone catacombs along the river's shores.

title: Defense of Morrowind Volume I
topic_desc: The Practical Defense of Morrowind Volume I: Island Strongholds, by Apelle Laecinnius, is an Imperial military assessment of Morrowind's island fortifications. Intended for Imperial authorities, it evaluates defensive positions and vulnerabilities against foreign invasion, dismissing internal threats like the Twin Lamps as insignificant. The report deems Solstheim indefensible and recommends abandoning Fort Frostmoth. It identifies the unaffiliated town of Dagon Fel as a strategic early warning post, proposing the use of local criminals as expendable defenders. Vvardenfell is assessed as nearly impregnable if Great Houses cooperate, owing to the impassable Red Mountain interior and layered coastal defenses, including ancient Dunmer fortresses, inland cities, and the formidable Ebonheart citadels. The east coast's Telvanni towers are highlighted for their natural and magical defensibility. The work identifies the Firemoth Archipelago as a critical vulnerability, currently held by the lich Grurn, and recommends its immediate covert recapture to prevent enemy staging.
topic_desc_basic: An Imperial military report by Apelle Laecinnius assessing the defensive strengths and vulnerabilities of Morrowind's islands, including Vvardenfell, Solstheim, and the Telvanni Isles, against foreign invasion.

title: Desert Rose Petals
topic_desc: Desert rose petals are the gathered blooms of the desert rose, a flora native to southern Morrowind. Prized by alchemists for their inherent properties, these petals are a recognized ingredient in potion-making. The plant's adaptation to arid southern climes makes its flowers a regional specialty, typically acquired through harvesting wild specimens or via supply networks that deal in southern Morrowind's botanical resources.
topic_desc_basic: Desert rose petals are alchemical ingredients harvested from the desert rose, a plant native to southern Morrowind.

title: Disaster at Ionith
topic_desc: An official Imperial commission report authored by Lord Pottreid, Chairman, examining the catastrophic failure of Emperor Uriel V's invasion of Akavir beginning in 3E 288. The work traces the campaign from its planning stages in the 270s through the landing at the Tsaesci port renamed Septimia and the establishment of headquarters at Ionith upriver. The Commission finds the Emperor's preparations sound given available intelligence, but identifies the decision to delay reinforcing legions in favor of transporting colonists as pivotal. The account details deteriorating conditions: severe winter storms that crippled the Far East Fleet, a Tsaesci assassination attempt disguised as peace negotiations, an anomalous drought that dried the river and destroyed crops, and growing magical interference that severed communication with Tamriel. The Commission concludes the entire Expeditionary Force was lost and that the invasion exceeded Imperial strength, leaving the Empire dangerously weakened relative to its provinces.
topic_desc_basic: An Imperial commission report by Lord Pottreid documenting Emperor Uriel V's failed invasion of Akavir in the late Third Era. The Expeditionary Force landed in 3E 288, established colonies at Septimia and Ionith, and was ultimately destroyed by Tsaesci resistance, severe weather, and supply failures. The loss left the Empire militarily weakened.

title: Djulighana's Role
topic_desc: A Yokudan mythological account explaining how the spirit Djulighana became the watchman who provides ideas and guidance to mortal spirits. The work describes Sep the Snakewise convincing other spirits to roll Satakal's shed skins into an enormous ball, promising an easy home free from the World Snake's teeth. The ball grows uncontrollably, devastating the world-skins and stranding the spirits in a sea of Nothing. Pursuing the runaway sphere, Djulighana fashions two helpers from shed skins and torn holes: Sheogog, who proves mad and flees, and the sane but apathetic Hermonga Mora. When Paparuptga arrives and rebukes Sep, he commissions Djulighana to watch over the trapped spirits, offering them ideas to find their way to the Far Shores. The narrative thus establishes Djulighana's enduring role as a beneficent counselor and the origin of two other enigmatic entities.
topic_desc_basic: A Yokudan myth explaining how the spirit Djulighana became the watchman who provides mortals with ideas and guidance, after Sep the Snakewise trapped spirits on a runaway ball of Satakal's shed skins.

title: Dolphin Meat
topic_desc: Dolphin meat is the flesh of dolphins, aquatic mammals inhabiting the Abecean Sea off the coast of Cyrodiil. It is recognized as a foodstuff and ingredient by alchemists and hunters familiar with the region's marine fauna.
topic_desc_basic: Dolphin meat is the flesh of dolphins, aquatic mammals found in the Abecean Sea off the coast of Cyrodiil. It serves as a foodstuff and ingredient.

title: Donkey Hide
topic_desc: Donkey Hides are the pelts taken from donkeys, beasts of burden native to Cyrodiil. Hunters and alchemists value these hides for their alchemical properties, and they circulate commonly through regional trade and leveled supply stocks.
topic_desc_basic: Donkey Hides are pelts taken from donkeys, beasts of burden native to Cyrodiil.

title: Dragonscales
topic_desc: Dragonscales are purportedly harvested from dragons, though the creature's scarcity renders the ingredient exceptionally rare. Alchemists and hunters value the scales for their distinctive properties, but the near-mythic status of dragons in the modern era means genuine samples are scarcely encountered. The specific alchemical characteristics of dragonscales remain known primarily to specialist practitioners.
topic_desc_basic: Dragonscales are rare alchemical ingredients obtained from dragons. You do not know where Dragonscales are commonly found.

title: Dragynia Blossom
topic_desc: Dragynia blossoms are large red-orange flowers distinguished by their fern-like leaves. They grow wild in the Reach and throughout High Rock, where alchemists and hunters value them for their properties.
topic_desc_basic: Dragynia blossoms are large red-orange flowers with fern-like leaves that grow in the Reach and High Rock.

title: Draketail Webbing
topic_desc: Draketail webbing is a rare alchemical ingredient harvested from draketail plants. Its properties remain a subject of specialist study among alchemists and hunters familiar with uncommon regional flora. The ingredient is not widely cultivated or traded, and its alchemical character is known primarily through experimentation rather than established herbal tradition.
topic_desc_basic: Draketail webbing is an uncommon ingredient gathered from draketail flora. It is known to alchemists and hunters but is not a staple of common trade.

title: Drakewing Butterfly Wing
topic_desc: The Drakewing butterfly wing is harvested from the Drakewing butterfly, a diurnal insect native to Cyrodiil. As with other lepidopterans, each specimen yields two wings. The ingredient circulates through regional supply lists, though it possesses no guaranteed presence in any known location or habitat, making it an unpredictable harvest dependent entirely on the creature's sporadic appearance.
topic_desc_basic: The Drakewing butterfly wing is an alchemical ingredient harvested from the diurnal Drakewing butterfly of Cyrodiil. Each butterfly yields two wings.

title: Dres Armor
topic_desc: A memorial account of the armor of Giladis Rothan, a Dunmer warrior of Great House Dres born in Silnim. The text commemorates Rothan's service during the Arnesian War, noting his role in quelling Argonian slave uprisings on Dres plantations and his leadership of a detachment against Argonian forces. Rothan was killed by Argonian poisons at the height of a victorious battle. The narrative emphasizes the joint triumph of House Dres and House Indoril forces, who overran the enemy encampment to secure the war's greatest victory. The Rothan family subsequently permitted his ashes to be interred in Necrom, where the armor serves as a memorial to Dunmer who died fighting for the Tribunal during the conflict.
topic_desc_basic: A memorial text detailing the armor of Giladis Rothan, a Great House Dres warrior killed by Argonian poisons during the Arnesian War. It commemorates his service and the final victory won by House Dres and House Indoril, noting his ashes were interred in Necrom as a tribute to Dunmer who died for the Tribunal.

title: Dres Cremation Practices
topic_desc: A Hlaalu-published missive documenting House Dres funerary customs, drawn from a Dunmer boatman's account. Because the Tribunal requires bones for the Ghostfence, the Dres cremate their dead entirely rather than sending remains along Veloth's Way to Necrom. The body is desiccated in salt plains under clan guard, seated in a lotus position, and reinforced with bone stakes—often from slaves—chitin, and at least one metal piece, which survives the fire as a keepsake. Saturated in insect tallow, the corpse is placed atop a pillar and ignited, producing the beacon fires visible across the plains. The wind from Lake Andaram is said to carry the ashes toward Necrom. The work emphasizes Dres thoroughness in preventing necromancy and their hostility to outsider inquiries about their dead.
topic_desc_basic: A published account describing how House Dres cremates its dead. Rather than sending bones to Necrom for the Ghostfence, the Dres fully burn corpses on tall pillars, producing beacon fires visible across the salt plains.

title: Dres Slave Trade
topic_desc: A scholarly treatise by Nurcius Punitus, a student at the Imperial Library, analyzing the slave trade within Great House Dres and its economic and political effects on the house. Punitus examines House Dres's reliance on slave labor for saltrice cultivation, which has sustained the house's economy for at least six centuries, and describes the capital city of Tear as purpose-built for slave control and transport, featuring immense concrete-reinforced slave pits. The work details the sources of slaves through raids into Black Marsh and trade with outlaws in Elsweyr, the brutal conditions within the pits, and the systematic cruelty inflicted upon Argonian and Khajiit captives. Punitus argues that slavery forms the very foundation of House Dres's existence, and notes that the treaty incorporating Morrowind into the Empire legally permits the practice, exempting the province from the Imperial abolition law. The treatise concludes with an expressed hope for universal abolition.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly work by Nurcius Punitus of the Imperial Library examining Great House Dres's dependence on slavery. The treatise analyzes how slave labor sustains Dres saltrice cultivation and describes the capital Tear as built for slave control and trade, with slaves sourced through raids on Black Marsh and commerce with Elsweyr outlaws. Punitus notes that Morrowind's Imperial treaty legally permits slavery within the province.

title: Dreugh Queen
topic_desc: The dreugh queen is the largest and most dangerous of all dreugh. Sightings are exceptionally rare, and killings even rarer; perhaps no more than a dozen exist in all Tamriel. Survivors of encounters report that queens are powerful spellcasters. A stuffed queen carapace is said to be on display in Dawnstar, Skyrim. While some claim every dreugh is the progeny of a queen, this remains unverified.
topic_desc_basic: The dreugh queen is the largest and most dangerous dreugh. Perhaps no more than a dozen exist in all Tamriel. They are exceptionally rare, and survivors report them to be powerful spellcasters.

title: Dried Fig
topic_desc: Dried figs are figs that have been left in the sun to prolong their shelf life. Figs are commonly grown in Cyrodiil, and the drying process makes the fruit easier to export to other provinces.
topic_desc_basic: Dried figs are sun-preserved figs grown in Cyrodiil, dried to prolong their shelf life and facilitate export across the provinces.

title: Dried Hibiscus
topic_desc: Dried hibiscus consists of the preserved petals of the tropical hibiscus flower, a flora native to Elsweyr. Valued in alchemical practice and culinary preparation alike, the spice is cultivated from the arid province's warmer regions and traded across Tamriel. Its alchemical properties make it a staple reagent for apothecaries, while its distinct floral character renders it a sought-after commodity in spice markets.
topic_desc_basic: Dried hibiscus is a spice prepared from the petals of the tropical hibiscus flower, a plant native to Elsweyr.

title: Dried Slaughterfish
topic_desc: Dried slaughterfish is a preserved foodstuff prepared from various slaughterfish species. The curing process yields a lightweight, durable provision valued by travelers. While regional varieties exist—some sourced from Morrowind's coastal waters, others from Cyrodiil, and at least one trade variant crossing both provinces—all known types share a common alchemical property: restoring stamina. Alchemists and hunters appreciate the fish for this reliable, if limited, virtue.
topic_desc_basic: Dried slaughterfish is a preserved food made from slaughterfish. It is a common travel ration, and different varieties are sourced from the waters of Morrowind and Cyrodiil. It is known to restore stamina.

title: Dried Whitepoppy Pod
topic_desc: A dried seedpod of the whitepoppy plant. It holds a singular distinction in alchemical practice: its primary property is a Drain Sneak effect. Because this effect appears alone among all known ingredients, no synergistic combination exists to yield a potion of Drain Sneak; the effect manifests only when the pod is consumed raw. Beyond this unusual characteristic, the pod is otherwise unremarkable in alchemy. Whitepoppy plants grow in Cyrodiil, and the dried pods circulate among alchemists and hunters familiar with the region's flora.
topic_desc_basic: A dried seedpod harvested from the whitepoppy plant. It is known among alchemists for its unusual primary property, which drains the consumer's ability to move unseen.

title: Drift Puff Flower
topic_desc: Drift Puff Flower is a flowering plant valued as an alchemical ingredient. It is encountered among general ingredient collections and floral stocks, suggesting it is gathered from the field and circulated to practicing alchemists.
topic_desc_basic: Drift Puff Flower is a flowering plant gathered for use as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Drumpear Seeds
topic_desc: Drumpear seeds are large seeds harvested from the drumpear, a plant native to the Shipal-Shin region of Morrowind. They are commonly ground into a rough powder and used as a culinary spice. Market Quarter farmers in Hlaalu lands cultivate the drumpear specifically for this spice trade, and whole seeds are occasionally available from merchants before grinding.
topic_desc_basic: Drumpear seeds are large seeds from the drumpear plant, native to the Shipal-Shin region. They are widely ground into a rough powder and used as a spice.

title: Dry
topic_desc: In this scholarly treatise, the Argonian author Dr. Nak Bur-za challenges the prevailing critical assumption that dryness in Saxhleel literature merely metaphorizes death or despair. Arguing instead that aridity and thirst function as distancing terms for the "other" and the uncanny, she traces how sophisticated writers deploy desiccation imagery to evoke foreignness and alienation. She supports her thesis with close readings of two novels by Paxhan Dar Uush ("Long Strong-eye"): "The Saltrice Broker," where a drought-blasted canal signals an alien land and misadventure, and "The Eye in the Mask," where a character's physical thirst signals cultural estrangement and bigotry. Bur-za distinguishes this literary trope from the colloquial, mildly pejorative term "dry skin" for non-Argonians, showing that writers who avoid that shorthand still exploit dryness for its evocative power.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly treatise by Dr. Nak Bur-za arguing that, in Saxhleel literature, dryness and thirst serve as metaphors for foreignness and the "other" rather than simply for death or despair.

title: Dryad's Saddle Polypore Cap
topic_desc: Dryad's saddle polypore caps are shelf mushrooms that grow on tree trunks. They are native to the Strident Coast and the Brennan Bluffs regions of Cyrodiil. Alchemists value the fungus for its usable properties, and hunters encounter it while traversing these wooded territories.
topic_desc_basic: A shelf mushroom that grows on tree trunks in the Strident Coast and Brennan Bluffs regions of Cyrodiil.

title: Dunmer Law: A Primer
topic_desc: Galothis Omeyn's scholarly overview of the diverse legal traditions of Morrowind's Great Houses, written to guide outlanders through the province's competing jurisdictions. The work details Hlaalu's Imperial-style courts, Redoran trial by combat, Telvanni wizard-lord autocracy, Dres ancestor-spirit adjudication, and Indoril's all-encompassing philosophical code derived from Aldmeri algorithmic doctrine. It also examines the Court of Waters, a religious conclave resolving inter-House disputes that carries both Tribunal and Imperial sanction, and notes the tensions arising from the implementation of the Juris Imperator Tamrielicus alongside traditional customs.
topic_desc_basic: A guide by Imperial scholar Galothis Omeyn introducing outlanders to Morrowind's varied legal systems, explaining that each Great House maintains its own distinct laws and judicial customs.

title: Durata
topic_desc: Durata is a vegetable cultivated in Hammerfell and Colovia, recognized by its tiny red kernels. Though botanically a vegetable, it serves as a staple grain substitute; the kernels are routinely dried and ground into meal for culinary use. Alchemists and hunters value durata as a common ingredient, though its specific alchemical properties require specialist preparation to harness effectively.
topic_desc_basic: Durata is a vegetable grown in Hammerfell and Colovia. It produces tiny red kernels that are commonly dried and ground into meal like a grain.

title: Durzog Hide
topic_desc: Durzog hide is the skin taken from a durzog, a beast kept and bred by goblins as guards and war animals. The pelt's coarse, durable character makes it a recognized alchemical ingredient, though its specific properties remain a subject for specialist study. As durzogs are uncommon and largely confined to goblin-held territories, the hide is difficult to obtain and does not circulate through standard trade or alchemical supply networks.
topic_desc_basic: Durzog hide is the skin taken from a durzog, a beast kept by goblins. It is a recognized alchemical ingredient, though it is uncommon and difficult to obtain through ordinary trade.

title: Duskbell
topic_desc: Duskbell is a plant distinguished by its red flowers, native to eastern Morrowind. It grows most readily in the Sunad Mora and Molag Ruhn regions, with occasional specimens found in the Sacred Lands and Nedothril. Though somewhat uncommon in the wild, the plant's vibrant appearance has made it a popular choice as an indoor ornamental across Morrowind. Alchemists and hunters value the flower for its properties in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Duskbell is a red flower that grows in eastern Morrowind, mainly around Sunad Mora and Molag Ruhn. Though somewhat uncommon in the wild, it is widely kept as an indoor plant across Morrowind.

title: Dusky Parrotfish
topic_desc: Dusky parrotfish are brightly colored fish recognized by their vivid purple and blue hues. They are a common sight in the Abecean Sea, where they swim in its warm waters. Alchemists and hunters value these fish as an ingredient, though their specific alchemical properties are a matter for specialist study rather than common knowledge. Their striking coloration makes them one of the more easily identifiable marine creatures harvested for their useful properties.
topic_desc_basic: Dusky parrotfish are bright purple and blue fish commonly found in the Abecean Sea. They are harvested as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Dust Beetle Shell
topic_desc: The dust beetle is a lesser cousin of the fiery shalk. Its chitinous forewings yield the dust beetle shell, an ingredient valued both by armorers and alchemists. Ground and dissolved, the shell is combined with bone shards and resin to craft bonemold and aena weapons and armor. In potions, the shell exhibits alchemical virtues that yield potent fortify endurance mixtures.
topic_desc_basic: The dust beetle is a lesser cousin of the shalk. Its shell is ground and dissolved with bone shards and resin to make bonemold and aena armors, and is used by alchemists to brew potent fortify endurance potions.

title: Dwemer Burial Customs
topic_desc: Nedlir Andrethi's treatise compiling secondhand accounts of how the Dwemer handled their dead, contrasting their practices with Chimeri customs and describing tomb architecture, sarcophagus forms, and body preservation methods.
topic_desc_basic: A widely circulated scholarly work by Nedlir Andrethi describing how the Dwemer disposed of their dead. The book explains that common Dwemer were cremated in lava, while notable individuals were interred in sealed, elaborately constructed tombs. Andrethi acknowledges that his findings derive from written accounts and hearsay rather than firsthand observation.

title: Dwemer Collection
topic_desc: A catalog or assemblage of Dwemer artifacts sourced from the Kemel-Ze excavation in the Telvannis District. The collection encompasses parts of defunct automatons, everyday Dwarven items, and a statue of an unidentified Dwarven king, presumably not life-sized. These relics were recovered by the Archaeological Society during their ongoing excavation at Kemel-Ze, a project commissioned by the Elder Council and considered the Society's most important in Morrowind. The Dwarven people, known for ingenious mechanical contraptions, mysteriously went extinct in the eighth century of the First Era.
topic_desc_basic: A collection of Dwemer artifacts from the Kemel-Ze excavation in the Telvannis District, including automaton parts, everyday items, and a statue of an unidentified Dwarven king.

title: Ebonheart: A History
topic_desc: A historical treatise by Imperial scholar Qualia Tarvix examining the city of Ebonheart, commonly called Old Ebonheart. The work traces the settlement from its mythic First Era origins as Khalaan, a probable site of Shezarr veneration, through its rivalry with Mournhold and subsequent suppression under the Tribunal Temple. It details the city's governance by House Raathim, including Sotha Sil's legendary silencing of the city and the resulting silent language still used by Dark Elf agents. Tarvix recounts Ebonheart's surrender and destruction during Tiber Septim's conquest, its Western-style rebuilding as the Imperial military headquarters following the Armistice, and its elevation to a special administrative zone. The narrative culminates in the city's contemporary role as the organizational center for Vvardenfell's colonization under Duke Vedam Dren, reflecting an Imperial perspective on Morrowind's political transformation.
topic_desc_basic: A historical work by Qualia Tarvix chronicling the city of Old Ebonheart. It covers the settlement's ancient origins as Khalaan, its long rule by House Raathim, its destruction and rebuilding as the Imperial military headquarters in Morrowind, and its present role administering the Vvardenfell colonization effort.

title: Edryon's Poetry
topic_desc: Edryon's Poetry is a romantic verse composed by an Indoril Dunmer named Edryon, addressed to a woman named Folvalie. The poem expresses Edryon's desire to cross the Av Orethan and bring Folvalie to a place he calls 'Azura's bosom,' where they might defy local spirits. The work is widely regarded as poorly written by Dunmer familiar with it; critics note its shallow focus on Folvalie's foreign qualities rather than her personal traits, arguing it conveys only superficial affection. Folvalie's associates consider the verse an embarrassment that tarnishes Edryon's standing. The phrase 'Azura's bosom' is speculated to refer to a valley near a shrine of Azura across the Av Orethan, though the passage to the shrine has been blocked by a rockslide.
topic_desc_basic: A poorly regarded romantic poem by the Indoril Dunmer Edryon, expressing desire for a woman named Folvalie and referencing a place called 'Azura's bosom' near the Av Orethan.

title: Effects of the Elder Scrolls
topic_desc: A scholarly thesis by Justinius Poluhnius, dictated in 2E 126, cataloguing the physical and mental effects suffered by those who read Elder Scrolls. Poluhnius groups readers into four categories based on training and mental discipline. The untrained, or Naifs, perceive only odd symbols and suffer no harm. Unguarded Intellects possess enough knowledge to read the Scrolls but lack the discipline to withstand a glimpse of infinity, and are struck immediately and irrevocably blind, though they receive a fragment of hidden knowledge. The Cult of the Ancestor Moth alone has developed the fortitude for Mediated Understanding: their monks suffer only gradual vision loss and gain knowledge through prolonged meditation. At the highest stage, Illuminated Understanding, a monk reaches a Penultimate Reading that signals the next will be the last, after which total blindness follows. Poluhnius acknowledges that a unified theory of these effects still eludes him.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly thesis by Justinius Poluhnius, dictated in 2E 126, cataloguing the hazards of reading Elder Scrolls. It groups readers into four categories based on training and mental discipline, ranging from the untrained, who suffer no ill effects, to the Moth priests, who gradually lose their sight over years of readings in exchange for prophetic knowledge.

title: Egg
topic_desc: Eggs, specifically chicken eggs, are a common ingredient found on farms in Cyrodiil and Skyrim. They serve as a staple foodstuff and are widely used in cooking. In alchemy, the egg is valued as a basic reagent. It is regularly harvested from domestic poultry and appears in general food supplies and simple provisions across these provinces.
topic_desc_basic: Chicken eggs are a common food and ingredient found on farms in Cyrodiil and Skyrim.

title: Elf Cup Cap
topic_desc: Elf Cup Cap is a variety of mushroom valued as an alchemical ingredient. Foragers and apothecaries recognize it by its distinctive cup-shaped cap, which lends the fungus its common name. It grows in Cyrodiil's woodlands and is routinely gathered by hunters and herbalists for its stable alchemical properties. The fungus is common enough to appear in regional supply stocks and random ingredient shipments, ensuring its availability to practiced alchemists.
topic_desc_basic: Elf Cup Cap is a type of mushroom commonly gathered in Cyrodiil. Foragers and alchemists prize it as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Embalming Paste
topic_desc: Embalming Paste is a preparation associated with the preservation of the dead. Alchemists value it for its properties, and hunters occasionally encounter it among the remnants of barrows and crypts. Its specific alchemical character remains a matter of specialist knowledge, as its use is tied to funerary practices rather than common commerce.
topic_desc_basic: Embalming Paste is a substance used in the preservation of corpses. It is typically found in barrows and other crypts.

title: Emeralds
topic_desc: Emeralds: Applications in Alchemy by Whertold the Blackened is a reference work and primer on the alchemical properties of emeralds. The text recounts Elsweyr folklore claiming emeralds are the tears of Akatosh before detailing practical recipes. It provides instructions for a costly health-restoring potion combining ground emerald with corkbulb root, marshmerrow, wickwheat, or corprus weepings, and a magicka-fortifying potion using saltrice, stoneflower petals, or belladonna berries. Whertold cautions that fortifying magicka depletes the user's natural reserves once the effect ends, and warns that careless combinations yield harmful results, such as draining agility and endurance with black anther, or inducing exhaustion and clumsiness with other ingredients. The author stresses that alchemical success depends entirely on the practitioner's skill and equipment quality.
topic_desc_basic: Emeralds: Applications in Alchemy by Whertold the Blackened is a reference work detailing the alchemical uses of emeralds. It provides recipes for health and magicka potions while warning of the dangers of improper ingredient combinations and unskilled practice.

title: Emetic Russula Cap
topic_desc: Emetic russula caps are a variety of mushroom found growing in Cyrodiil. As their name suggests, these fungi possess purgative properties, making them a recognized ingredient in alchemical practice. Alchemists and foragers harvest the caps for their useful properties, which are commonly employed in the preparation of curative and cleansing concoctions.
topic_desc_basic: Emetic russula caps are a type of mushroom known for their purgative properties, making them useful in alchemy.

title: Ensis Tea Cake
topic_desc: Ensis Tea Cakes are bricks of herbal tea mixtures originating from the Summerset Isles. The name derives from the Altmer term for 'wilted,' referring to the required state of the tea shrub's leaves at the time of harvest. These compressed cakes preserve the prepared foliage for transport and steeping, reflecting a distinctive Altmer approach to botanical preparation and cultivation.
topic_desc_basic: Ensis Tea Cakes are bricks of herbal tea mixtures from the Summerset Isles, made from the wilted leaves of a tea shrub.

title: Ephialtic Nightkiss Wing
topic_desc: Ephialtic Nightkiss wings are harvested from the Ephialtic Nightkiss, a rare butterfly native to Cyrodiil. The insect is notably elusive, emerging only during the brief twilight hours at dusk. As with other lepidoptera, each specimen yields a pair of wings. Alchemists value the wing for its distinct properties, though its scarcity and the creature's narrow window of activity make consistent collection a considerable challenge.
topic_desc_basic: Ephialtic Nightkiss wings are taken from a rare Cyrodiil butterfly that only emerges at dusk. Each specimen provides two wings, prized by alchemists despite the difficulty of harvesting them during their brief twilight appearance.

title: Essence of Being a Thief
topic_desc: A cautionary tale by Thralos Devneri about a boastful thief's fatal lapse in discretion.
topic_desc_basic: A story by Thralos Devneri illustrating that secrecy is the core of thievery, following a thief who brags to a stranger and pays with his life.

title: Etiquette With Rulers
topic_desc: Erystera Ligen's practical guide to addressing and conversing with Breton nobility, cataloging the peerage hierarchy of High Rock's eight kingdoms and the regional variations in noble titles, forms of address, and conversational decorum.
topic_desc_basic: A guide by Erystera Ligen on properly addressing Breton nobility in High Rock.
