It explains the hierarchy of titles from Kings and Queens down to Lords and Ladies, the correct forms of address such as 'Your Majesty' and 'Your Grace,' and regional variations in peerage customs across High Rock's kingdoms.

title: Expanding Magicka: Revised
topic_desc: Esling Serrenan's treatise on magical properties and applications, revised with an editor's corrective annotations. Serrenan argues that subterranean crystals are magicka sources akin to the sun and stars, that conjuration and necromancy share identical binding principles differing only in method, and that destruction, restoration, and alteration fundamentally operate as a single school. The editor refutes several claims: the crystals absorb rather than emit magicka, soulstones derive from them, and prolonged exposure damages reason. The editor also notes a competing theory that conjuration amalgamates ambient Daedric particles rather than opening Oblivion rifts. Despite acknowledged errors, the work remains a foundational text for understanding modern magical practice.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise by Esling Serrenan on magical properties and applications, widely read by apprentice wizards. An editor's annotated revision corrects several of the author's disproven hypotheses while affirming the work's foundational role in contemporary magical understanding.

title: Eyestar
topic_desc: The eyestar is a pale, starfish-like creature bearing a large, prominent eye on its body. Immobile, it rests on the seabed and lake floors, functioning more like flora than fauna. These creatures inhabit the waters of the Inner Sea and the oceans surrounding Morrowind. The distinctive eyes are harvested from the living eyestar and are sought after by alchemists for their properties.
topic_desc_basic: The eyestar is a pale starfish with a large eye on its body. Eyestars can be found in the Inner Sea and the oceans surrounding Morrowind, and their eyes are sought after by alchemists.

title: Fall of Vitharn
topic_desc: A historical account chronicling the rise and destruction of Keep Vitharn in Dementia across three generations of rulers. The work attributes the keep's doom to accumulated heresy and dysfunction: the founder's blasphemous denial of Sheogorath, Count Csaran's incestuous paranoia that drove his Argonian bride to madness, the sickly sadism of their incest-born heir Cesrien, and finally the crippling cowardice of Cesrien's son Cirion. Cesrien's marriage to a Manic peasant further inflamed their Demented Fanatic vassals, who ultimately besieged the keep when the terrified Cirion failed to placate them. The author claims personal memory of Cesrien's reign and records local myth that the spirits of the defenders and attackers remain cursed to replay their final battle in perpetuity.
topic_desc_basic: A history detailing the destruction of Keep Vitharn in the Shivering Isles. It traces the ruling family's decline through blasphemy, incest, and madness, culminating when cowardly Count Cirion failed to prevent a vassal rebellion. Local myth holds the fallen keep is haunted by spirits endlessly replaying the siege.

title: Fascicle 0
topic_desc: Fascicle 0 is the opening section of the religious text known as the Testament of the Church-Mothers. It presents a creation myth focusing on the spirit Shezarr, characterizing him as ambitious and dissatisfied with the stasis permitted by Akatosh. The account describes Shezarr's journey beyond the boundaries of the Beginning Place, where he conceives a greater shape called the World Entire. This realm is envisioned as a crucible for growth and creation, allowing a soul to surpass all prior existence. The text frames this vision as the catalyst that will end the Beginning Place, bringing both joy and sorrow. The work offers a distinctive theological perspective on the origins of mortal creation and the divine impulse that disrupted primordial stillness.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 0 is the opening portion of the Testament of the Church-Mothers. It recounts the creation myth of the spirit Shezarr, who, dissatisfied with the stasis of the Beginning Place, conceives a greater realm called the World Entire to serve as a crucible for growth, an act that will end the primordial era.

title: Fascicle 13-16
topic_desc: A section of The Testament of the Church-Mothers addressing the origin of knowledge. It recounts that as the Beginning Place sharpened under Mara, new thoughts overwhelmed the spirits until Julianos emerged from the whispered word to govern wisdom and teach all spirits. Julianos raised two pupils: Has-Mora, who craved knowledge beyond boundaries, invented the Lie, and was banished to the Outer Darkness, later returning to hoard forbidden things; and Magnus, who pursued abstract formulae over substance, ultimately overshadowing his master. The text presents a distinct theological viewpoint on knowledge, explaining both its gift and its perilous divergences.
topic_desc_basic: A section of The Testament of the Church-Mothers describing the origin of knowledge. It recounts the birth of Julianos as a spirit of wisdom, and the fall of his two pupils, Has-Mora and Magnus, who pursued forbidden knowledge and abstract idealism respectively.

title: Fascicle 17-20
topic_desc: Fascicle 17-20 of the Testament of the Church-Mothers is a theological text subtitled "The Roar of the Void." It details a creation myth in which the crowded, airless Void prompts the emergence of Kynareth from the divine roar. Kynareth provides air, sound, and the sky, and imbues creation with majesty. However, her restlessness breeds nightmares and madness, from which the spirits Vaer-Em and Shegg-Et are born and subsequently cursed.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 17-20 is a section of the Testament of the Church-Mothers. It recounts the origin of Kynareth from the Void and her establishment of the sky, and attributes the birth of the spirits Vaer-Em and Shegg-Et to her restless madness.

title: Fascicle 1-4
topic_desc: Fascicle 1-4 of the Testament of the Church-Mothers, a theological text recounting the Song of the Abyss. It describes the pre-creation state of darkness and formlessness, termed the Beginning Place, from which Akatosh emerged as the First and King of Spirits. Upon realizing the joy of existence, Akatosh birthed the Hours and Minutes, whose labors formed the Waters and the space of Days. The fascicle emphasizes that before time was ordered, creation was chaotic, with no sequence or order among the Days. This work provides a distinct mythic lens on the genesis of time and the transition from primordial void to structured existence.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 1-4 is part of the Testament of the Church-Mothers. It recounts the Song of the Abyss, describing how the dragon Akatosh emerged from primordial darkness and birthed the Hours and Minutes to bring time and order to the void.

title: Fascicle 21-24
topic_desc: Fascicle 21-24 is a segment of the Testament of the Church-Mothers, a mythic text detailing the acts of early spirits. This portion focuses on Dibella, who declares the emerging world and its creators things of Beauty. Her mystery births subordinate spirits of shadow and fading light. Magnus seeks her favor by crafting an abstract concept of lines and symmetry to shape pleasing patterns; Dibella grants him fire in return, though this light will later desert his sphere to become a tyrant. Crucially, Dibella perceives the flaw in the Beginning Place before Shezarr's intervention, recognizing that creation implies motion and decay. She curses her peers for failing to conceive of loss and the end, puzzling the other spirits who cannot yet comprehend mortality.
topic_desc_basic: A section of the Testament of the Church-Mothers covering early creation myths. It details the spirit Dibella blessing the world as Beauty, granting fire to Magnus, and foreseeing the inherent decay and end of creation, a concept the other spirits cannot yet grasp.

title: Fascicle 25-27
topic_desc: Fascicle 25-27 of the Testament of the Church-Mothers is a theological text detailing the genesis of Zenithar within the primordial Beginning Place. It recounts how the spirits, guided by Dibella's Beauty, learned to discern worth and value, from which Zenithar emerged as the spirit who knows all estimation. The work portrays Zenithar measuring the Void and recognizing its fundamental limitation: in the absence of places, no growth, labor, or earned reward can occur. Though displeased with the Void's sterility and the serenity of his peers, Zenithar cannot yet conceive a solution, retreating into reclusive denial until the Hour of Creation reveals his true worth. The fascicle emphasizes Zenithar's intrinsic connection to work, commerce, and the value of things gained through effort, contrasting his desire for productive substance with the static tranquility of the pre-creation void.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 25-27 of the Testament of the Church-Mothers is a religious text explaining the origin of Zenithar. It describes how he emerged from the concept of value derived from Dibella's Beauty, and how he measured the primordial Void, only to find it incapable of supporting growth, labor, or earned reward.

title: Fascicle 28
topic_desc: Fascicle 28 of *The Testament of the Church-Mothers*, titled "Enter, Mercy," addresses the origins and nature of Stendarr. It describes him as the last of the great spirits, defined entirely by compassion, and assigns him the sphere of mercy. The text notes that while Stendarr pitied lesser spirits who could not grow, his role in the earliest hours of creation was minor, as mercy had little application then. He preserved his voice for later ages, when regret and mortal suffering would drive the afflicted to call upon his aid. The work presents a theological viewpoint framing Stendarr's mercy as a force that developed purpose alongside the suffering of mortals.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 28 of *The Testament of the Church-Mothers* addresses Stendarr's origin, characterizing him as the last of the great spirits and defining his sphere as mercy and compassion.

title: Fascicle 29-31
topic_desc: Fascicle 29-31 is a section of The Testament of the Church-Mothers, a doctrinal text addressing the nature of spirits beyond the Divines. It identifies the Dmath as encompassing both Daedric and Elven spirits, whose laws and will are said to be obscured from humanity. The fascicle distinguishes Daedric spirits—originating from the workings of the Divines, the Outer Darkness, or strange angles forbidden by Akatosh's edict—as dwellers in darkness who command respect but hold no claim over mortals. Elven spirits are condemned as dissatisfied entities who would lead humanity back to the Void of the Beginning, a timeless, lifeless stasis. The text frames both categories as fundamentally alien to human experience and warns against submission to either. The Church-Mothers' testament thus articulates a distinctly human theological perspective, positioning mortalankind between divine masters and obscured spirits whose influence is to be acknowledged but resisted.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 29-31 is part of The Testament of the Church-Mothers, a religious text that teaches about spirits beyond the Divines. It describes the Dmath—Daedric and Elven spirits—whose laws do not apply to humanity. Daedric spirits are to be respected but not obeyed, while Elven spirits are condemned as evil beings who would lead mortals back to the Void.

title: Fascicle 32-40
topic_desc: Fascicle 32-40 is a segment of The Testament of the Church-Mothers, a theological text chronicling the spirits' awakening in the Void. It recounts how the restless Shezarr proposed the creation of a virtuous world, attracting Kynareth, Zenithar, Stendarr, and Dibella to the endeavor, while Julianos, Mara, and Arkay hesitated. Akatosh, the First Spirit, rebuked the plan, warning that breaking the natural order risks long oblivion. Shezarr then revealed a profound metaphysical insight glimpsed from the Outer Darkness: the world is simultaneously wheel, tower, and king, and shares identity with both Akatosh and Shezarr. Confronted with this revelation, Akatosh acquiesced. The passage is significant for its synthesis of Cyrodilic creation theology, its depiction of divine dissent and consensus, and its cryptic articulation of the metaphysical structure of existence.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 32-40 is a section of The Testament of the Church-Mothers. It recounts the primordial debate among the gods when Shezarr proposed creating the world, detailing how the Divines divided over the plan and how Akatosh ultimately acquiesced after Shezarr revealed a profound metaphysical truth about the nature of existence.

title: Fascicle 41-45
topic_desc: Fascicle 41-45 is a section of the religious text known as the Testament of the Church-Mothers, subtitled "Consent of the Unwilling Spirits." It records the responses of various divine and spiritual entities to a proposed cosmic course. Mara consents on the condition that creation and growth incur hardship, making their value self-evident. Arkay agrees, acknowledging that joy in creation must be balanced by grief and loss. Akatosh consents without explanation, asserting his will as inherent in all transpiration. The gods of the Elves voice opposition, warning against Daedric deception, while the Daedric spirits declare they will only observe and dismiss Elven divine wisdom. The fascicle thus preserves a foundational theologic dialogue on the nature of mortal existence, divine consent, and the contested relationship between Aedra, Daedra, and Elven gods.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 41-45 is a portion of the Testament of the Church-Mothers recording the consent and objections of various gods and spirits—including Mara, Arkay, Akatosh, Elven gods, and Daedric spirits—to a proposed cosmic plan for creation.

title: Fascicle 46-49
topic_desc: Fascicle 46-49 is a segment of The Testament of the Church-Mothers, titled Song for the Architect. It recounts the role of Magnus in the creation of the Mundus, describing how Shezarr persuaded him to design the world by promising a throne of power. Magnus is depicted as the Architect who sketched the world's form with the aid of a legion of spirits, yet the text also brands him a coward and traitor for abandoning the Mundus and nearly robbing it of light and heat. Despite this condemnation, the fascicle exhorts praise for Magnus in three aspects—Architect, Transmittal, and Warden—calling for forgiveness of celestial betrayal. The work reflects a distinctive theological tradition that simultaneously reveres and condemns the divine beings who shaped and then departed the mortal realm.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 46-49 is a portion of The Testament of the Church-Mothers, a religious text addressing Magnus's role in designing the Mundus. It describes how Shezarr persuaded Magnus to plan the world, then condemns him for abandoning it and nearly depriving it of light, while still urging praise for his architectural contribution.

title: Fascicle 50-53
topic_desc: Fascicle 50-53 is a portion of the Testament of the Church-Mothers, a theological text addressing the creation of the mortal world. It presents a cosmogony in which gods and spirits sacrificed their own flesh and blood to build existence, with Zenithar laboring over the world's engine. The passage explains the origin of the sun and stars as wounds torn in the firmament when Magnus, fearing to sacrifice himself, fled creation; his departure and the subsequent flight of lesser spirits caused a moment of primordial darkness. During this darkness, the Divines faltered, allowing evil spirits to enter the world's root. Arkay's ordinance that all things pass eventually ended this uncertainty, though the Divines resumed their work in a diminished, half-wake state, convening in fear of the moment they had endured.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 50-53 is a section of the Testament of the Church-Mothers detailing the creation of the world. It describes the gods sacrificing flesh and blood to build existence, Magnus fleeing and tearing the sun and stars in his haste, and a subsequent moment of darkness that allowed evil spirits to enter the world before Arkay's law restored order.

title: Fascicle 54-59
topic_desc: Fascicle 54-59 is a portion of the Testament of the Church-Mothers, a religious text recounting the Divine Convention at the dawn of creation. It describes Akatosh descending as a spire to convene the gods, the willing sacrifice of the Divines who became earth, air, and waters, and the despair of the elven gods who had opposed creation yet submitted to it. The passage culminates in the assault upon the spirit Shezzar, whom the gods called liar and deceiver for speaking great truth. His blood, spilled upon the ground, produced the first flowers and constituted the first murder. The text frames this violence as foreknown and inevitable, with the gods averting their eyes. The fascicle thus presents a mythic account of creation's cost, the tension between merish and mannish divine figures, and the origin of sacrifice and bloodshed in the mortal world.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 54-59 is a section of the Testament of the Church-Mothers, a religious text describing the Divine Convention. It recounts Akatosh descending to convene the gods, the Divines sacrificing themselves to form the world, and the assault on the spirit Shezzar, whose blood produced the first flowers and the first murder.

title: Fascicle 5-12
topic_desc: Fascicle 5-12 of the Testament of the Church-Mothers is a theological text detailing the nascence of Arkay and Mara. It presents Arkay as the offspring of Akatosh's will and Mara's thought, who imposes cosmic order by establishing the Circle—the cyclical cause and consequence of life, death, and rebirth via the Waters. Mara emerges as Arkay's twin, born of growth and Akatosh's love, but she rejects the Circle's repetition, instead fostering the earth as a static refuge and resting place. The work frames the tension between Arkay's relentless cycle of mortality and Mara's nurturing but ultimately impermanent earthly solace, counseling that the wise follow the Waters to renewal rather than seek permanent shelter in the earth.
topic_desc_basic: Fascicle 5-12 of the Testament of the Church-Mothers is a religious text recounting the origins of Arkay and Mara. It describes Arkay establishing the cyclical nature of life and death, while Mara creates the earth as a resting place away from this cycle.

title: Father of the Niben
topic_desc: A scholarly translation and study by Florin Jaliil of the fragmented Aldmeri epic Udhendra Nibenu, which chronicles the Middle Merethic Era voyage of Topal the Pilot. Sent from Firsthold with two other ships to find a passage back to Old Ehlnofey, Topal followed a northeast-pointing waystone across the Abecean Sea to mainland Tamriel. The surviving verses describe his encounters with orcs in southern High Rock, a giant bat-lizard near Morrowind's coast, and Argonian swamps, before his fateful decision to navigate north up a river—now the Niben—rather than south around a peninsula. There, he discovered eight islands in a crystalline lake, home to feathered folk he taught to write, who yielded their home to him. Jaliil's commentary explores the mystery of the other two ships, the nature of the waystones, and the controversial implication that orcs inhabited the mainland before the Aldmeri diaspora, challenging traditional accounts of their origin.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly translation of the fragmented Aldmeri epic Udhendra Nibenu by Florin Jaliil, chronicling the Middle Merethic Era voyage of Topal the Pilot. It details his expedition from Firsthold to find Old Ehlnofey, his circumnavigation of Tamriel, and his discovery of the Niben River and the eight islands of Lake Rumare.

title: Fearstruck
topic_desc: Fearstruck is a Daedric artifact created by Boethiah, taking the form of a shield. The Prince granted it to the First Era hero Lyrisius, who led a military campaign against Akaviri slave-traders in Akavir. After his army was routed, Lyrisius encountered a wyrm; its fiery breath utterly melted and destroyed the shield. This destruction possibly accounts for a residual weakness to fire afflicting those who bear it. Though the original was lost millennia ago, replica shields styled after Fearstruck have been sighted. These replicas depict it as an ebony shield emblazoned with Boethiah's symbol: a fist surrounded by wrrit golden snakes.
topic_desc_basic: Fearstruck was a Daedric shield created by Boethiah and given to the First Era hero Lyrisius. It was famously destroyed by the fiery breath of a wyrm after his army was routed in Akavir.

title: Feeble Limb
topic_desc: Feeble Limb is a mild disease transmitted by cave rats. Afflicted persons feel weak and weary.
topic_desc_basic: A mild disease spread by cave rats that causes weakness and weariness.

title: Fennel Seeds
topic_desc: Fennel seeds are the seeds of fennel plants. They grow naturally in Cyrodiil's Brennan Bluffs and Strident Coast regions, as well as on certain islands in the Abecean Sea. Alchemists and hunters value these seeds for their useful properties in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Fennel seeds are the seeds of fennel plants. They grow in Cyrodiil's Brennan Bluffs and Strident Coast, and on some islands in the Abecean Sea.

title: Fig
topic_desc: Figs are the fruit of the fig tree, a plant common throughout Cyrodiil. The fruit is also preserved and consumed in a dried form. As a common foodstuff, it is widely gathered and traded, appearing regularly among regional fruit supplies and the broader ingredient markets of Mournhold.
topic_desc_basic: Figs are the fruit of the fig tree, commonly found growing around Cyrodiil. They are also widely eaten in dried form.

title: Fire Agate
topic_desc: Fire Agate is a mineral ingredient, a variety of agate stone known to alchemists. It is uncommon and rarely encountered in general trade or circulation. Detailed accounts of its specific alchemical properties and applications remain scarce in widely available texts.
topic_desc_basic: Fire Agate is a mineral ingredient, a variety of agate stone. It is uncommon and rarely seen in general trade.

title: Fire and Darkness
topic_desc: Fire and Darkness: The Brotherhoods of Death by Ynir Gorming is a scholarly examination of the Morag Tong and the Dark Brotherhood. Gorming argues that the earliest Morag Tong venerated Sithis alongside Mephala, citing coded poetic fragments in First Era writs. Following the Tong's brazen assassinations of Emperor Reman and Potentate Versidue-Shaie, the order was outlawed across Tamriel but survived in Morrowind by securing Tribunal sanction, likely abandoning Mephala for Vivec. This schism birthed the Dark Brotherhood, which, Gorming contends, continues to revere Mephala as the Night Mother. Consequently, the two orders remain locked in perpetual, irreconcilable conflict.
topic_desc_basic: Fire and Darkness by Ynir Gorming examines the history and schism between the Morag Tong and the Dark Brotherhood, arguing that the Brotherhood originated when the Tong abandoned Mephala for Tribunal sanction in Morrowind.

title: Fire Opal
topic_desc: Fire Opal is a mineral ingredient valued in alchemical practice. Sourced from gemstone deposits, it possesses distinct alchemical properties that make it useful for crafting potions. As a precious stone, it also holds worth beyond its alchemical utility, often traded as a valuable commodity.
topic_desc_basic: Fire Opal is a precious gemstone with alchemical uses, sourced from mineral deposits.

title: Firewatch: A History
topic_desc: Savri Hlervu's historical work chronicles Firewatch, the Imperial capital of Telvannis District. Founded by General Symmachus after Telvanni intransigence prevented using Port Telvannis, the city grew from a grim shore-fort into a major staging base for Uriel V's Akavir invasion. The fleet's catastrophic failure ushered in paranoia, fortification, and the Chapel of the East Empire Everlasting. Firewatch survived the 306 siege by the Telvanni rebel Turimal, whose captured staff Oathrung became a civic treasure. Subsequent peace enabled Duchess Bredami Vaynth to charter the College of Firewatch in 379, attracting scholars until the Imperial Simulacrum devastated the city and claimed the Duchess. Though Duchess Perulia Jandacia restored order in 400, Firewatch remains shadowed by past anxieties.
topic_desc_basic: A historical work by Savri Hlervu chronicling Firewatch, the Imperial capital of Telvannis District. It details the city's founding after Telvanni resistance, its growth as a staging base for the Akavir invasion, survival of a Telvanni siege, and the establishment of the College of Firewatch.

title: Flashgrit
topic_desc: Flashgrit is a strange, soap-like alchemical substance derived from leachlye that explodes violently when friction is applied. Its primary utility lies in excavation and demolition. The Redguard So-Mitana Company holds the exclusive charter to manufacture and sell it, making it uncommon in the east. Flashgrit is heavily controlled; it is completely illegal to trade, sell, or buy secondhand, and merchants will generally refuse to associate with anyone possessing it.
topic_desc_basic: Flashgrit is a soap-like substance derived from leachlye that explodes under friction. Used for excavation and demolition, it is heavily regulated and illegal to trade secondhand, with a Redguard company holding the sole manufacturing charter.

title: Flat Bread
topic_desc: Flat bread is a simple, unleavened staple common throughout Skyrim, crafted from grain and baked into thin rounds. It serves as hearty, portable sustenance for travelers and hunters, valued for its keeping properties and restorative qualities. Alchemically, it is a mild curative ingredient, though its properties are modest compared to specialized reagents.
topic_desc_basic: Flat bread is a simple, unleavened bread common throughout Skyrim, baked into thin rounds. It serves as a staple food and offers mild restorative properties when eaten.

title: Floater Sac
topic_desc: A floater sac is an alchemical ingredient harvested from a floater, an airborne creature. The sac's specific alchemical properties remain a subject of specialist study, though it is collected for use in potion-making. Hunters and alchemists acquire these specimens through general foraging and fauna-derived ingredient channels.
topic_desc_basic: A floater sac is an ingredient harvested from the airborne creature known as a floater.

title: Flora of Skyrim, Volume I
topic_desc: Arielle Jurard's practical alchemical reference detailing Skyrim's native flora and the formulae that employ them. The work instructs practitioners on combining common foodstuffs like witherwheat flour and honey to restore fatigue, and provides recipes using regional ingredients for health restoration, curing Wormmouth diseases, lessening bodily weight, replenishing magicka, and enhancing night-vision. Notable plants covered include the Reach's honey lily and vicar herb, the rare shadowfly, and the forsythia tromja, whose wiry roots harbor a mild paralyzing poison requiring an alembic to process safely.
topic_desc_basic: A guide by Arielle Jurard on the alchemical uses of Skyrim's native plants. It records practical potion formulae employing regional ingredients such as honey lily, shadowfly, and vicar herb.

title: Flour
topic_desc: Flour is a powder obtained from the grinding of grain. As a staple product of agriculture, it is especially common in Cyrodiil and Skyrim, where milled grain forms the foundation of regional food supplies. In alchemical practice, flour is classified as a basic ingredient, though its properties are modest compared to rarer reagents. Its widespread availability ensures steady supply for both culinary and alchemical use.
topic_desc_basic: Flour is a powder obtained from grinding grain. It is a common staple, especially in Cyrodiil and Skyrim.

title: Fly Amanita
topic_desc: Fly amanita is a mushroom prized for its levitation properties, making it a sought-after alchemical ingredient for flight mixtures. It appears occasionally in ingredient shops, primarily throughout Cyrodiil, and grows wild in select caverns such as Berjodhre in Skyrim. While valuable for achieving levitation, the mushroom demands careful formulation; when combined with other common levitation sources like green stain mushrooms or racer plumes, it tends to produce adverse side effects, requiring alchemists to exercise caution in their mixtures.
topic_desc_basic: Fly amanita is a mushroom valued for making levitation potions. It is sold in shops mostly in Cyrodiil and grows in caves such as Berjodhre in Skyrim. It carries a risk of negative side effects when mixed with other common levitation ingredients like racer plumes or green stain mushrooms.

title: Fool's Gold
topic_desc: Fool's Gold is a mineral ingredient of uncertain natural origin. Its alchemical properties remain largely undocumented due to its exceptional rarity; it does not appear in standard leveled supplies or guaranteed deposits, leaving its character and common uses a matter of speculation rather than established practice.
topic_desc_basic: Fool's Gold is a rare mineral ingredient. It is exceptionally uncommon and not found in typical supply stocks or standard deposits.

title: Fools' Ebony, Part I
topic_desc: A comedic play by Frincheps, set in Daggerfall during the Third Era. The first part depicts a Dunmer adventurer conversing with two dissolute Akatosh priests at the Dead Daedra Inn. The priests recount the High Rock peasant myth of Nackles, a gaunt, unsettling Dark Elf spirit who rides subterranean Dwarven mine carts and climbs into homes to terrorize misbehaving children, sometimes substituting their sweets with lumps of Fools' Ebony. The work satirizes priestly hypocrisy while introducing the eponymous Fools' Ebony, a mysterious substance rumored to hold potential for vast profit, cultural upheaval, or death.
topic_desc_basic: A comedic play by Frincheps in which a Dark Elf adventurer and two disreputable Akatosh priests discuss the High Rock folk myth of Nackles, a sinister elven spirit who punishes naughty children, and the mysterious substance called Fools' Ebony.

title: Fools' Ebony, Part II
topic_desc: The second installment of Frincheps' comedic play, staged as a tavern conversation between a Dunmer adventurer and priests of the Imperial cult. The priests reveal that the Temples secretly collaborate and share funds while maintaining a facade of rivalry, and they discuss Fools' Ebony—a worthless rock resembling raw ebony that dupes inexperienced miners. The adventurer claims this substance burns longer and hotter than wood, making it valuable for heating and smithing. Conspiring to monopolize rumored surface deposits in the Wrothgarian Mountains, the priests advance the adventurer seed money from their temple coffers. An epilogue explicitly reminds the audience that Fools' Ebony is fictitious and that the play's depiction of ebony mining is inaccurate, framing the work as a satirical farce on clerical corruption and gullibility.
topic_desc_basic: The second part of Frincheps' comedic play about a Dunmer adventurer and corrupt Imperial priests. The characters conspire to monopolize a fictitious substance called Fools' Ebony, which the epilogue explicitly declares is not real.

title: Fools' Ebony, Part III
topic_desc: Fools' Ebony, Part III is the third installment of Frincheps' comedic play concerning a Dunmer adventurer's scheme involving the fictitious substance Fools' Ebony. In this act, the protagonist visits the Mages' Guild and encounters two mages both named Shub. Feigning knowledge of priests seeking the material, the adventurer learns the mages know its supposed location in the Wrothgarian Mountains but refuse to travel there. The adventurer volunteers to retrieve it and establish a supply line, receiving five hundred gold in advance while plotting to mislead the rival priests. The play's Prologue and Epilogue highlight the work's ironic humor and question whether the seemingly incompetent mages are truly as foolish as they appear.
topic_desc_basic: Fools' Ebony, Part III is the third part of Frincheps' comedic play about a Dunmer adventurer manipulating both priests and mages in pursuit of the fictitious substance Fools' Ebony.

title: Fools' Ebony, Part IV
topic_desc: The fourth installment of Frincheps' comedic play Fools' Ebony, subtitled Mercantile Dealings, The Armorers Involve Themselves. The Dark Elf Adventurer and the merchant Nephron conspire to monopolize a newly discovered cache of Fools' Ebony in the Wrothgarian Mountains. They scheme to undermine the Akatosh Chantry by exploiting a missing Royal Contessa, while cooperating with the School of Julianos and Mages. Five Armorers then ambush the Adventurer, forcing him to share the venture under threat of violence, and assign the monosyllabic apprentice Ortho as his coerced escort. The play satirizes Daggerfall's guild rivalries and mercantile corruption through farcical intrigue.
topic_desc_basic: A comedic play by Frincheps following a Dunmer adventurer's schemes to control a cache of Fools' ebony in the Wrothgarian Mountains while manipulating Daggerfall's competing guilds and temples.

title: Fools' Ebony, Part V
topic_desc: Fools' Ebony, Part V is the fifth installment of Frincheps's comedic play concerning a Dunmer Adventurer's schemes surrounding the titular substance. This portion depicts the Adventurer, seemingly cornered by armorers, manipulating priests of Akatosh and Julianos. Exploiting a scandal involving a priest named Komon and a Contessa, the Adventurer secures funding for an expedition by leveraging the Akatosh Chantry's resulting tax crisis and arranging for the School of Julianos to absorb its debts and personnel. The priests, distracted by baser pursuits, remain unaware that the Adventurer and the merchant Nephron retain control of the operation. The work satirizes clerical hypocrisy and mercantile cunning in the Iliac Bay region.
topic_desc_basic: Fools' Ebony, Part V is part of Frincheps's comedic play about a Dunmer Adventurer scheming over the valuable substance Fools' Ebony. In this installment, the Adventurer manipulates corrupt priests of Akatosh and Julianos to fund an expedition.

title: Fools' Ebony, Part VI
topic_desc: The sixth installment of Frincheps' comedic play Fools' Ebony, set in the Iliac Bay region during the early Third Era. The narrative follows a Dunmer rogue known as the Adventurer as he schemes to control a lode of Fools' Ebony, a miraculous burning mineral, while duplicity entangles rival mages, priests, and armorers. In this segment, the Adventurer encounters Contessa Aveet Videspreed, a cunning noble and illusionist from the Court of Daggerfall who blackmails her relatives and seeks to join his expedition for profit. Employing seduction and the aid of former alchemists at Minnie's Inn, she neutralizes the armorers' spy, Ortho, and plots to eliminate their remaining escorts. The work is heavily bawdy; a prologue narrator frequently interrupts to note censorship by the Guild of Playwrights, Actors, and Dramatists, offering uncensored copies for a fee.
topic_desc_basic: A bawdy comedic play by Frincheps, the sixth part of Fools' Ebony. It follows a Dunmer rogue's schemes to acquire a miraculous burning mineral called Fools' Ebony, and his encounter with a cunning noblewoman who joins his expedition.

title: Forsythia Root
topic_desc: Forsythia root is harvested from the Forsythia Tromja, a hardy bush growing amid the rocky terrain of Skyrim's Sundered Hills. Its robust nature makes the plant a reliable source of alchemical material for those traversing the region. Alchemists and gatherers value the root for its practical utility in their craft.
topic_desc_basic: Forsythia root is gathered from the hardy Forsythia Tromja bush, which grows in the rocky Sundered Hills of Skyrim.

title: Foxglove Nectar
topic_desc: Foxglove nectar is drawn from the foxglove, a cultivated flower commonly grown in pots and gardens across Tamriel. Alchemists prize the nectar as a reagent for its distinct alchemical properties, while hunters and herbalists gather it from domestic plantings rather than wild specimens. Its widespread horticultural presence makes it a familiar and accessible ingredient throughout the provinces.
topic_desc_basic: Foxglove nectar is drawn from the foxglove, a flower commonly grown in pots and gardens across Tamriel.

title: Fragments of an Altmer Guide
topic_desc: A scholarly Altmeri rebuttal to the Pocket Guide to the Empire, written by the royal court scholar Ariyael in 2E 870. The work systematically contests the Imperial account of the Aldmeri Dominion, framing it not as a conquest but as a willing reaffirmation of ancient Altmeri suzerainty over Valenwood. Ariyael provides an Altmer-centric racial taxonomy of the merish peoples, defends Altmeri culture against accusations of eugenics, and portrays the Bosmer as kin rescued by Y'ffre from Azura's cruelty. The text is a significant example of Second Era Summerset propaganda, seeking to legitimize the Dominion as a merish alliance against Imperial tyranny while downplaying its military occupation of Valenwood.
topic_desc_basic: An Altmeri treatise written in 2E 870 by the scholar Ariyael, intended to correct the perceived lies of the Imperial Pocket Guide to the Empire. It defends the Aldmeri Dominion as a voluntary merish alliance and offers an Altmer-centric view of the elven races.

title: Fragments on General Talos
topic_desc: A fragmentary text venerating General Talos, depicting him as a martial paragon of the Red Legions. The surviving passages describe brutal discipline under King Cuhlecain before the siege of Sancre Tor, where soldiers pre-emptively adorned themselves with carmine mud and nooses to defy desertion orders. Talos is portrayed as the fiercest among them, a singular figure cast by the dragon god. The work espouses a messianic viewpoint, prophesying that a god of war will descend in flesh and iron, chosen by camaraderie and proven in battle, acting from love for the Red Legions. The text functions as martial hagiography, framing Talos not merely as a historical general but as a divinely forged champion intrinsically bound to the Imperial soldiery.
topic_desc_basic: A fragmentary work venerating General Talos. It portrays him as the fiercest soldier of the Red Legions and a divinely chosen god of war who fights out of love for his troops, framing his martial deeds during the siege of Sancre Tor as the acts of a messianic figure.

title: Frog Eyeball
topic_desc: Frog Eyeballs are alchemical ingredients harvested from the bullfrog, an amphibian native to the province of Cyrodiil. As a regional faunal extract, the eyeballs are gathered by hunters and alchemists for use in potion-making. Their specific alchemical properties are of interest to practitioners of the alchemical arts, though the ingredient remains a provincial specialty tied to Cyrodiil's wetland fauna.
topic_desc_basic: Frog Eyeballs are ingredients harvested from the bullfrog, an amphibian native to Cyrodiil.

title: Frost Troll Pelt
topic_desc: A frost troll pelt is the hide harvested from a frost troll, a creature found throughout Tamriel. Valued by hunters for its hardiness and by alchemists as a source of rare properties, the pelt serves as a distinctive ingredient in alchemical preparations.
topic_desc_basic: A frost troll pelt is a hide taken from a frost troll, a creature found throughout Tamriel. It is used by alchemists and hunters.

title: Fruitbearer Butterfly Wing
topic_desc: Fruitbearer butterfly wings are delicate alchemical ingredients harvested from the fruitbearer butterfly, a rare diurnal insect native to Cyrodiil. The wings are valued by alchemists and hunters for their inherent properties. As with other lepidopteran specimens, a single butterfly typically yields a pair of wings when collected.
topic_desc_basic: Fruitbearer butterfly wings are alchemical ingredients taken from the rare fruitbearer butterfly, a daytime insect found in Cyrodiil.

title: Fungal Pod
topic_desc: Fungal Pods are fungal growths valued as alchemical ingredients. Their appearance and precise properties are poorly documented in standard references, though they are recognized among alchemists and ingredient gatherers as a distinct and usable reagent. They are known to occur in regions of Tamriel where appropriate fungal flora thrives, and they circulate in alchemical trade through random ingredient collections. Beyond their identification as a fungal ingredient suitable for alchemical preparation, detailed scholarly description of their morphology, specific effects, and natural habitat remains scarce in available sources.
topic_desc_basic: Fungal Pods are fungal growths gathered as alchemical ingredients. They are recognized among herbalists and alchemists as a distinct, usable reagent found in regions of Tamriel where fungal flora grows.

title: Game of Thirty-Six
topic_desc: The Game of Thirty-Six is a dice game of chance played for wagers. On each turn, participants roll both dice and add the result to a running total. A participant may roll repeatedly or stand; the winner is the one whose total comes closest to thirty-six without exceeding it. A total above thirty-six loses, while a tie returns both wagers.
topic_desc_basic: The Game of Thirty-Six is a dice game of chance played for wagers. Participants roll two dice, adding the result to a running total, and may roll repeatedly or stand. The winner is the one whose total comes closest to thirty-six without exceeding it; exceeding thirty-six loses, while a tie returns both wagers.

title: Garlic
topic_desc: Garlic is a pungent herb cultivated in Cyrodiil and Skyrim. Valued as a common foodstuff and culinary seasoning across these provinces, it is also gathered by alchemists and hunters for its inherent properties. The plant thrives in temperate regions and is routinely harvested for both sustenance and alchemical experimentation.
topic_desc_basic: Garlic is a pungent herb commonly grown in Cyrodiil and Skyrim, widely used as a food seasoning.

title: Garnet
topic_desc: Garnet is a semi-precious gemstone occasionally employed as an alchemical ingredient. While its specific alchemical properties remain a matter of specialist study rather than broad doctrine, the stone is widely gathered from mineral deposits across Tamriel. It circulates readily through trade, appearing among the standard gem and ore yields of both Morrowind and the western provinces. Beyond its ornamental appeal, alchemists value the stone for its inherent virtues in the mortar, treating it as a staple mineral reagent alongside more common ores.
topic_desc_basic: Garnet is a semi-precious gemstone used in alchemy and ornamentation, commonly mined and traded across Tamriel.

title: Ghost
topic_desc: Ghosts, also known as spirits, are the disembodied souls of the deceased classified as the Returned. They remain on Nirn due to unfinished business, guilt, or because they are prevented from entering the afterlife through curses or necromantic binding. Unresolved emotions may crack a soul, creating a Void within it; self-forgiveness can heal this wound. Conversely, spirits may willingly answer summons to aid the living, resolving their affairs. Their forms vary widely, from degraded upper bodies or skeletal shapes to exact reflections of their living selves. In combat, they perceive invisible foes, inflict chilling touches, drain magicka at a distance, and can become virtually invisible in shadow. Slaying a ghost does not truly kill it; it merely disperses the energy holding it to the world. Professional hunters actively pursue these entities.
topic_desc_basic: Ghosts are non-corporeal undead that haunt all of Tamriel. They are the souls of the dead unable or unwilling to pass on, often remaining due to unresolved affairs or necromantic binding. They appear in varied forms and can chill their foes, drain magicka, and strike from shadows.

title: Ghost Laurel
topic_desc: Ghost laurel is a bright blue flower native to Morrowind, occasionally cultivated in provincial gardens. Its striking hue makes it recognizable to alchemists and hunters familiar with the region's flora, who value it as an ingredient in various preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Ghost laurel is a bright blue flower native to Morrowind that sometimes grows in gardens.

title: Ghost Ring
topic_desc: This artifact dates to the era of the Chimer and was once possessed by a noted sorcerer of that people. It confers a Chameleon effect upon the wearer and significantly enhances Conjuration skill. A Mages Guild researcher has spent fifteen years searching for the ring, and its enchantments have proven instrumental in accelerating the development of new Conjuration spells. The ring is believed to lie somewhere deep within the Dunmer stronghold of Vandirelyon.
topic_desc_basic: The Ghost Ring is a powerful magical artifact once owned by a noted Chimer sorcerer. It is said to lie somewhere deep within the Dunmer stronghold of Vandirelyon.

title: Ghraewaj and the Harpies
topic_desc: Tidasus's scholarly treatise examines the traditional Redguard play Ghraewaj, performed annually at the Riglametha festival in the Hammerfell barony of Lainlyn. The play recounts the transformation of a wicked sisterhood of Daedra worshippers into harpies through a magical robe. Their leader, the temptress Noctyr-a, is turned into a giant black bird, slain, and unwittingly devoured by her followers, who are then themselves transformed into harpies. Tidasus notes that the story shifts considerably across versions: in some, Noctyr-a is an innocent seamstress blessed by Dibella, while the baroness is the villain; during the reign of Viana the Pure (2E 120–148), the baron was cast as Noctyr-a's willing conspirator. The author observes that harpies common to the Iliac Bay possess their own tongue but seem ignorant of their own origins, and draws an etymological connection between Noctyr-a and the Daedra Prince Nocturnal, who is depicted holding two black crows.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly work by Tidasus examining the traditional Redguard play Ghraewaj, performed at the Riglametha festival in Lainlyn, Hammerfell. The play tells how a sisterhood of Daedra worshippers were transformed into harpies through a magical robe, and explores how the story has shifted across versions, with the name Noctyr-a possibly linked to the Daedra Prince Nocturnal.

title: Gift of the Deceiver
topic_desc: A preserved Chimer text from the High Velothi period, attributed to Indoril Dorom. The work recounts the Prophet Veloth's despair after leading the Chimer to Resdayn, only to find his people warring among themselves. Seeking peace, Veloth petitions Boethiah and Azura, whose cryptic prophecies he cannot comprehend. He then descends into a subterranean darkness to parley with Mephala, the Deceiver. Mephala offers peace through her unseen daughters, demanding Veloth's life as tribute. When Veloth hesitates, fearing his people will perish without him, Boethiah's voice emerges from Mephala's darkness, and Veloth finally understands the divine lesson: peace requires the sacrifice of the old warring self. The narrative is a foundational theological allegory for the Anticipations' interconnected roles and the Chimer transition from exile to settled society.
topic_desc_basic: A Chimer account of the Prophet Veloth's prayers for peace after reaching Resdayn. The text describes his encounters with Boethiah, Azura, and Mephala, culminating in his realization that lasting peace demands personal sacrifice.

title: Gilan Llarethi's Speech
topic_desc: A recorded oration by the Dunmer Gilan Llarethi, delivered to fellow House Telvanni on the 19th of Hearthfire, 3E 424. The speech addresses a community displaced for a decade following an Imperial seizure of their settlement, Bal Oyra. Llarethi announces that a coerced treaty will compel the local Imperial governor, Meritius Vinnus, to return the town. By exploiting Vinnus's vulnerable position—his superiors in Firewatch remain ignorant of his tyrannical and immoral conduct—Llarethi secures the concession without bloodshed. The oration frames the impending repossession as a pivotal step toward the broader expulsion of all foreign powers from Morrowind, reflecting persistent Dunmeri resistance to Imperial authority.
topic_desc_basic: A speech by Gilan Llarethi delivered to House Telvanni in 3E 424, announcing the imminent return of the seized town of Bal Oyra. Llarethi reveals that the local Imperial governor, Meritius Vinnus, is being coerced into signing a treaty surrendering the settlement back to its displaced Dunmer inhabitants.

title: Ginseng
topic_desc: Ginseng is a common root found growing on the Strident Coast of Cyrodiil. It is valued by alchemists and herbalists for its properties as an ingredient.
topic_desc_basic: Ginseng is a common root that grows on the Strident Coast of Cyrodiil. It is known to herbalists and alchemists as a useful ingredient.

title: Glass in Morrowind
topic_desc: An Imperial study commissioned by General Warhaft investigating Morrowind's glass mining industry, the material's unique properties, and the security of Imperial supply lines. The report details how Red Mountain's volcanic activity produces a hard yet flexible glass unlike common obsidian, valued for luxury goods and lightweight Dunmer armor and weapons. It surveys major Vvardenfell mines—Yassu, Dunirai, and Halit—alongside smaller mainland sites like Palinisbat and Bodrem, noting transportation hazards from blight, Daedra, and hostile tribes. The authors warn that Imperial control over these operations is tenuous and vulnerable to Dunmer monopolization. They conclude that fielding glass-armored Imperial legions is financially prohibitive, as Dunmer artisans guard their craft and quoted exorbitant sums per armor set.
topic_desc_basic: An Imperial report surveying Morrowind's glass mines and the material's military and economic value. It details the unique properties of Red Mountain glass, profiles major mining sites on Vvardenfell and the mainland, and warns that Dunmer unrest threatens the Empire's tenuous hold on this rare resource.

title: Glasswort Sprig
topic_desc: A glasswort sprig is a botanical specimen harvested from the glasswort plant. Its alchemical properties make it a reagent of interest to practitioners of the craft, though its precise effects remain a matter of specialized study. The plant is known to grow in the Deshaan region, where it is gathered for use in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: A glasswort sprig is a plant cutting gathered from the Deshaan region. It serves as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Gloomtears
topic_desc: Gloomtears are the flowers of the gloomtear plant, a flora native to High Rock. As a botanical ingredient, they hold alchemical value and are sought by practitioners for their inherent properties. The plant's growth habits make it a relatively uncommon harvest, and it typically reaches alchemists and hunters through regional randomized floral collections rather than reliable cultivation.
topic_desc_basic: Gloomtears are flowers harvested from the gloomtear plant, which grows naturally in High Rock.

title: Goat Fur
topic_desc: Goat fur is the pelt harvested from goats, domesticated or wild beasts common to the provinces of Hammerfell and Skyrim. A light-colored variant of the creature, known as the Weald goat, inhabits Cyrodiil. Hunters and trappers harvest these pelts as a common material, while alchemists value the fur for its properties in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Goat fur is a pelt taken from goats, hardy animals found across Hammerfell and Skyrim, with a light-colored Weald goat variant native to Cyrodiil.

title: Goat Meat
topic_desc: Goat meat is a common foodstuff harvested from the various breeds of goats found across Cyrodiil, Hammerfell, and Skyrim. As a staple provision drawn from widely domesticated and wild herds, it serves primarily as sustenance rather than a refined alchemical reagent. While hunters regularly cull these animals for their meat, the substance holds little significance in formal alchemy, lacking the potent magical properties characteristic of rarer ingredients. Its availability is subject to the natural distribution of goat herds rather than guaranteed supply.
topic_desc_basic: Goat meat is a common food harvested from goats across Cyrodiil, Hammerfell, and Skyrim.

title: Gold Ore
topic_desc: Gold ore is a large chunk of gold obtained from veins of ore-bearing rock. Mined in Cyrodiil and Morrowind, it is quite valuable and can be shaped into everyday objects such as coins.
topic_desc_basic: Gold ore is a chunk of gold obtained from ore-bearing rock veins. It is quite valuable and can be shaped into everyday objects such as coins, with mines found in Cyrodiil and Morrowind.

title: Gold Tantha Beak
topic_desc: The Gold Tantha Beak is an alchemical ingredient harvested from the Gold Tantha, a monkey-like creature native to Cyrodiil. As the creature's hardened facial structure, the beak is collected for its alchemical properties and finds use among practitioners of the craft. The ingredient circulates through Cyrodiilic supply channels, occasionally appearing in randomized merchant stock.
topic_desc_basic: The beak of the Gold Tantha, a monkey-like creature found in Cyrodiil. It is used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Golden Watcher Seed
topic_desc: The valuable seeds of the Golden Watcher cactus, a plant that typically grows in the Brennan Bluffs of Cyrodiil. Prized by alchemists and hunters for their useful properties, these seeds are a noteworthy regional harvest.
topic_desc_basic: The valuable seeds of the Golden Watcher cactus, which typically grows in the Brennan Bluffs of Cyrodiil.

title: Goldenlock
topic_desc: Goldenlock is a rare botanical ingredient harvested from the maidenhair plant. Its scarcity across Tamriel makes guaranteed samples virtually unknown, and it is typically encountered only by chance through randomized foraging or harvesting. The herb possesses distinct alchemical properties valued by practitioners, though its elusive nature confines its steady use largely to dedicated specialists who actively seek it out in the wild. For the general populace, goldenlock is recognized as an uncommon and difficult-to-procure floral reagent.
topic_desc_basic: Goldenlock is a rare botanical ingredient harvested from the maidenhair plant. It is notoriously difficult to find, with no reliable sources known to harvesters.

title: Goldenrod Seed Pod
topic_desc: Goldenrod Seed Pods are the seeds harvested from the Goldenrod plant, a flora commonly found growing on Stirk Isle and the Strident Coast of Cyrodiil. Valued by alchemists and hunters for their botanical properties, these seed pods serve as a regional alchemical ingredient sourced from the western Cyrodiilic coast.
topic_desc_basic: Goldenrod Seed Pods are seeds from the Goldenrod plant, commonly found growing on Stirk Isle and the Strident Coast of Cyrodiil.

title: Gooseberries
topic_desc: Gooseberries are small edible berries gathered from the wild. They appear among common foodstuffs and general ingredient collections across Morrowind and surrounding regions. Alchemists recognize them as a mundane culinary ingredient with no notable arcane properties beyond their basic nourishing qualities. Hunters and foragers encounter them as part of the natural bounty of the land, typically collected alongside other wild fruits and edible plants. They hold no particular cultural or religious significance among the peoples of Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: Gooseberries are small edible berries found growing wild across Tamriel. They are commonly gathered as food and appear among general provisions and ingredient supplies.

title: Gorapple
topic_desc: Gorapples are large fruits that grow in clustered bunches upon gorapple trees, a species found in the Alt Orethan region of Morrowind. The fruit constitutes the harvestable portion rather than the tree itself, and individual trees may bear varying quantities of bunches. Gathered as a foodstuff and alchemical ingredient, gorapples are recognized among those who work with the region's flora. Their clustered growth habit allows collection of the bunches without destruction of the tree.
topic_desc_basic: Gorapples are sizable fruits borne in bunches by gorapple trees throughout Alt Orethan in Morrowind. They are gathered as a foodstuff and ingredient by those familiar with the local flora.

title: Goujian
topic_desc: Goujian is a mighty and highly valuable sword. It currently rests within the Entrenched Shipwreck, located northwest of the Sadas Plantation. The blade is reputed to be a weapon of exceptional quality, significant enough to draw the attention of those seeking a perfect sword.
topic_desc_basic: Goujian is a mighty and very valuable sword. It lies within the Entrenched Shipwreck, northwest of the Sadas Plantation.

title: Grapes
topic_desc: Grapes are a cultivated fruit grown in Cyrodiil and High Rock. Valued as a common foodstuff, they are also recognized by alchemists and hunters for their useful properties when prepared in the proper manner. Their widespread cultivation in these provinces ensures a steady supply for both culinary and alchemical purposes.
topic_desc_basic: Grapes are a fruit grown in Cyrodiil and High Rock, commonly eaten as food.

title: Grass Pod
topic_desc: Grass Pods are plant-derived alchemical ingredients of uncertain specific origin. Their natural growth habits and regional distribution remain largely undocumented in standard herbalist references. Within the practice of alchemy, the pod is recognized for its distinct alchemical character, though its precise properties and interactions in synthesis are subjects of specialist study rather than common knowledge. The ingredient circulates through general supply channels and is gathered by hunters and foragers, yet it remains a comparatively obscure material.
topic_desc_basic: Grass Pods are plant-derived ingredients used in alchemy. Their specific origin and growth habits are not widely documented.

title: Great Harbingers
topic_desc: A historical chronicle by Swyk the Long-Sighted recording notable Harbingers of the Companions. It clarifies that the Harbinger is not a true leader but an advisor on honor, a role unoccupied since Ysgramor. The work profiles several pivotal figures: Jeek of the River, who founded Whiterun; Mryfwiil the Withdrawn, who ended the Companions' involvement in wars; Cirroc the Lofty, the first non-Atmoran Harbinger; Henantier the Outsider, the first elven Harbinger; Macke of the Piercing Eyes, whose disappearance remains unexplained; and Kyrnil Long-Nose, who overthrew false Harbingers and established the Circle. The text emphasizes the steady evolution of the Companions' traditions of honor over lineage.
topic_desc_basic: A chronicle by Swyk the Long-Sighted recording notable Harbingers of the Companions. It explains the Harbinger's advisory role and profiles key figures who shaped the Companions' traditions of honor.

title: Great House Dres
topic_desc: Great House Dres is one of the five Great Houses of Morrowind, governing the Dres District of southeastern Morrowind from its ancestral capital of Tear. Founded in the First Era by Grandmaster Thalthil Dres following a slave-raid over Thorn, the House maintains a wealthy agrarian society built upon vast saltrice plantations and the mass trade of Argonian and Khajiit slaves. House Dres is distinguished by its staunch support of Great House unity, persistent traditions of Daedra worship and ancestor reverence, and patronage of Saint Llothis the Pious. Unlike other Great Houses, it holds no territory on Vvardenfell, though ancient Dres cadet branches once resided there. It maintains close ties with the Camonna Tong and House Telvanni, while fiercely opposing the Imperial Legion, Imperial Cult, and abolitionist movements.
topic_desc_basic: Great House Dres is one of the five Great Houses of Morrowind, governing the southeastern Dres District from its capital of Tear. A wealthy agrarian society, it operates vast saltrice plantations and dominates the regional slave trade. The House holds no territory on Vvardenfell.

title: Great House Indoril
topic_desc: Great House Indoril is one of the five Great Houses of the Dunmer, governing the Mournhold District of east-central Morrowind from the capital city of Almalexia. Alongside House Dres, it maintains no holdings on Vvardenfell. Indoril prides itself as the holiest of the Great Houses, claiming the closest communion with the Tribunal and asserting spiritual authority over Morrowind. The house views itself as the nation's rightful leadership, staunchly opposing Imperial assimilation and the secular, mercantile values championed by House Hlaalu. Major settlements within Indoril territory include Akamora, Bosmora, Gorne, and Roa Dyr.
topic_desc_basic: Great House Indoril is one of the five Great Houses of the Dunmer. It governs the Mournhold District of east-central Morrowind from the capital city of Almalexia and has no holdings on Vvardenfell. The house is known for its devout adherence to the Tribunal Temple and its staunch opposition to the Empire.

title: Greaves of the Savior's Hide
topic_desc: The Greaves of the Savior's Hide constitute the lower body segment of the fabled Savior's Hide, a renowned artifact associated with the Daedric Prince Hircine. The complete armor is celebrated in legend for conferring total resistance to magic upon its wearer. As a component of this legendary set, the greaves share in its profound enchantments and historic significance within Daedric lore.
topic_desc_basic: The Greaves of the Savior's Hide are part of the legendary Savior's Hide, an artifact of the Daedric Prince Hircine. The complete set is famed for granting total resistance to magic.

title: Green Stain Mushroom
topic_desc: Green Stain Mushrooms are uncommon fungi that grow on fallen tree logs and occasionally at the base of living trees in the Strident Coast region of Cyrodiil. In alchemy, they are valued as a source of levitation, though they carry a notable risk of adverse side effects when combined with other inexpensive levitation ingredients such as fly amanita and trama root.
topic_desc_basic: Green Stain Mushrooms are uncommon fungi found on fallen logs and tree bases in the Strident Coast region of Cyrodiil. Alchemists value them for brewing levitation potions, though mixing them with cheaper levitation ingredients often causes harmful side effects.

title: Gremlin Earwax
topic_desc: Gremlin earwax is a yellow waxy substance harvested from gremlins. Alchemists and hunters value it as an alchemical ingredient, and it circulates in regional trade through random ingredient supplies across Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: Gremlin earwax is a yellow waxy substance obtained from gremlins. It serves as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Grey Tick Powder
topic_desc: Grey Tick Powder is an alchemical ingredient derived from the Grey Tick Polypore, a species of mushroom. This fungus grows naturally within the Grey Meadows of Morrowind. The powder is sought after by alchemists and hunters for its properties in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Grey Tick Powder is an ingredient taken from the Grey Tick Polypore, a mushroom that grows in the Grey Meadows of Morrowind.

title: Ground Drumpear Seeds
topic_desc: Ground Drumpear Seeds are crushed seeds of the drumpear, employed as a culinary spice to season food. Drumpears are a common crop extensively grown in the Shipal-Shin region of Morrowind. In alchemical practice, the ground seeds are recognized for their spice properties, though their precise alchemical effects remain a matter of specialist study rather than common knowledge.
topic_desc_basic: Ground Drumpear Seeds are a food seasoning made by crushing drumpear seeds. Drumpears are a common crop grown throughout the Shipal-Shin region of Morrowind.

title: Guar Meat
topic_desc: Guar meat is flesh harvested from guar, the domesticated pack beasts and livestock common throughout Morrowind. When butchered by skilled hands, the cuts yield nourishment valued not only as a staple food but also for its intrinsic alchemical properties. The meat is known to fortify the consumer against the harsh cold snaps characteristic of the Morrowind climate, making it a practical provision for travelers and hunters braving the elements. Its presence in general food supplies and regional ingredient stocks reflects its widespread culinary and alchemical utility.
topic_desc_basic: Guar meat is flesh harvested from guar, the common domesticated beasts of Morrowind. It is a staple food source, and when properly butchered, it is known to help withstand the cold.

title: Guide to Ancestral Tombs
topic_desc: A blasphemous, satirical Dunmeri text that ironically instructs outlanders on looting ancestral tombs while condemning Imperial authority for permitting the desecration.
topic_desc_basic: A satirical Dunmeri guide that ironically instructs outlanders on looting ancestral tombs while condemning the practice and Imperial tolerance of it.

title: Guide to Telvanni Construction
topic_desc: Clagius Galenus's treatise explaining the methods and principles behind Great House Telvanni's organic architecture. The work details how Telvanni towers and pod-houses are not built but grown from fungal spores, forming interconnected colonies rather than separate structures. Galenus outlines the multidisciplinary expertise required—construction, architecture, magic, and mycology—and describes the critical role of grand soul gems filled with powerful souls as catalysts to spur the fungus's remarkable growth. The text also covers the transformation of spent soul gems into purplish crystals within mature towers, the advantages of fungal dwellings such as low maintenance and saltwater desalination, and the use of levitation-exclusive shafts to restrict access. Notable examples cited include the mainland town of Ranyon Ruhn and the capital Port Telvannis, dominated by the massive Tel Thenim.
topic_desc_basic: A guide by Clagius Galenus explaining how Great House Telvanni grows its fungal towers and pod-houses from spores rather than constructing them from traditional materials. The work covers the magical and practical requirements for cultivating these organic structures, including the use of soul gems as growth catalysts.

title: Guide to the Guild Guides
topic_desc: Hroka's essay examines why teleportation remains limited despite advances like the Celaudine method and Suma Prenja's framework for transportive enchantments. It identifies three primary inhibitors: location, as a mage must establish a "spiritual anchor" at a previously visited destination and maintaining multiple anchors is extremely difficult; distance, because magicka and concentration requirements rise exponentially per the Lucevarius Curve, making interprovincial teleportation impractical and long-range attempts perilous; and specialization, since Guild Guides require lifelong, intensive study to overcome the Celaudine method's inherent caster-transport bias and manage multiple destinations safely. The essay also notes that powerful magical fields or anti-teleportation frequencies can block transit, and dismisses unverified tales of inter-planar teleportation to Oblivion via spiritual anchors as myth.
topic_desc_basic: Hroka's essay explains why teleportation is not more widespread despite modern arcane advances. It details three main limitations: the need to establish a "spiritual anchor" at a previously visited location, the exponential magicka costs over long distances, and the intensive lifelong specialization required to train Guild Guides who can safely transport others.

title: Hagiographa: Saints of the East
topic_desc: A hagiographic text cataloguing saints venerated across the eastern provinces of the Empire, including Morrowind, Black Marsh, and the trade routes connecting them to Cyrodiil. The work profiles figures such as Saint Ino, a First Era merchant who charted Shipal-Shin trade passes; Saint Cheltesses, an Argonian guide martyred atop Chixathe Mesa; Saint Taldeus, a shipwreck survivor of Uriel V's Akaviri invasion; Saint Stend, who founded the first Stendarr order in Black Marsh; Saint Symmachus, the long-lived king-consort of Barenziah martyred during the Imperial Simulacrum; Saint Tarjelius, an Argonian Consultor who ended an Archon uprising by reason alone; and Saint Moraelyn, the mythic king of Ebonheart. The collection reflects an Imperial Synodic tradition of elevating figures who embodied civic virtue, mercantile courage, faith, and loyalty across the eastern frontier.
topic_desc_basic: A hagiographic text profiling saints venerated across the eastern Imperial provinces, including Morrowind and Black Marsh. The work catalogues figures such as merchants, guides, healers, and rulers celebrated for virtues of courage, faith, and civic loyalty.

title: Hagiographa: The Animal Saints
topic_desc: A hagiographic text cataloging animal saints venerated in Colovian and Imperial tradition, detailing their deeds and patronages.
topic_desc_basic: A hagiographic work cataloging animal saints venerated in Imperial tradition, including a prophetic pig, a martyred donkey, a cunning crab, a vigilant goose, and the first Mananaut dog.

title: Hagiographa: The Emperor Saints
topic_desc: A hagiographic text venerating nine Imperial rulers recognized as Emperor-Saints, detailing their deeds and the patronages assigned to them. It covers figures from the early Cyrodilic and Septim dynasties: Ami-El, patron of Emperor-worship and the Dragonfire rituals; Belharza the Man-Bull, who confirmed pacts between men and minotaurs; Goreath, a penitent wanderer; Hestra, patron of road-builders; Pelagius the Pious, who formalized the recognition of Tiber Septim as Talos; Kintyra the Dancer, patron of Nibenese performers; Uriel the Lawmaker, whose Lex Imperii remains the basis of Imperial law; Kintyra the Infant, a martyr of the War of the Red Diamond; and Cephorus, patron of generals and peace by force. The work reflects the Imperial Cult's tradition of elevating exemplary rulers to sainthood and assigning them as intercessors for specific vocations and virtues.
topic_desc_basic: A hagiographic work venerating nine Imperial rulers recognized as Emperor-Saints. It profiles figures from the Alessian, Reman, and Septim dynasties, recording their deeds and the specific vocations and groups they patronize within the Imperial Cult tradition.

title: Hagiographa: The Strident Coast
topic_desc: Hagiographa: The Strident Coast is a devotional text venerating eight saints venerated along the Abecean coast and in Colovia. It records the shield-maiden Naharine, protector of Anvil's waterways; Aberdar, patron of the Gold Road; Bendu Olo, the First Era West King who united the All Flags Navy against the Sload; Milica the Careful, guardian of the inner Abecean; the western Nedic warrior Al-Khered, patron of Nibenese merchants in Colovia; Laeca, who witnessed an incarnation of Dibella and became patron of sculptors and painters; and Admiral Amiel Richton, patron of the Imperial West Navy. The work reflects the region's syncretic traditions, blending Alessian-era Nedic heritage, Colovian kingship, and Imperial naval history into a distinct coastal hagiography.
topic_desc_basic: Hagiographa: The Strident Coast is a devotional text profiling eight saints venerated along the Abecean coast and Colovia, including Anvil's shield-maiden Naharine, the All Flags Navy's King Bendu Olo, and Admiral Amiel Richton of the West Navy.

title: Hagraven Feathers
topic_desc: Hagraven feathers are plucked from the arms and shoulders of hagravens, blending avian and witch-like qualities inherent to the creatures. As ingredients, they are valued by alchemists and hunters who understand their rare and potent nature. Because hagravens are uncommon and often solitary, named denizens found only in specific haunts, acquiring their feathers is difficult. Guaranteed samples are scarce, typically found only on the hagravens themselves or in rare ingredient distributions, making these feathers a specialist resource.
topic_desc_basic: Hagraven feathers are taken from the arms and shoulders of hagravens. Because hagravens are uncommon and typically found only in specific locations, their feathers are a scarce and prized alchemical ingredient.

title: Ham
topic_desc: Ham is a cut of processed pork derived from swine, commonly prepared as a preserved foodstuff. It is a recognized culinary ingredient in Skyrim and Cyrodiil, where it serves as a staple provision. While valued as nourishment, its alchemical properties remain unremarkable, and it is not typically employed in formal potion-making or gathered through general foraging and hunting channels.
topic_desc_basic: Ham is processed pork from swine, commonly eaten as food in Skyrim and Cyrodiil.

title: Hammer of Lord Storig
topic_desc: The Hammer of Lord Storig is an enchanted war hammer and relic of the Four-Score War, once wielded by Storig of Farrun. It currently rests in the Monastery of St. Felms in Morrowind, laid before the top-floor shrine in the Tower of Contemplation.
topic_desc_basic: The Hammer of Lord Storig is an enchanted weapon and relic of the Four-Score War, once wielded by Storig of Farrun. It rests in the Monastery of St. Felms in Morrowind.

title: Hamum Root
topic_desc: Hamum root grows from the hamum root plant, appearing as a tiny yellow sprout. It is a staple crop cultivated along the Thirr River and also grows wild in the Aanthirin, the less swampy parts of the Sundered Scar, and Roth Roryn. Alchemists value the root for its beneficial properties, which include restoring health and improving reflexes.
topic_desc_basic: Hamum root is a tiny yellow sprout valued by alchemists for raising health and improving reflexes. It grows wild in the Aanthirin, Sundered Scar, and Roth Roryn regions.

title: Hardtack
topic_desc: Hardtack is a dense, dry cracker prized for its exceptionally long shelf life. This resilience makes it an ideal provision for long journeys, widely carried by travelers, sailors, and campaigning forces across Tamriel. As a comestible ingredient, it offers sustenance rather than notable alchemical properties, though its durability occasionally sees it included in alchemists' and hunters' practical stores.
topic_desc_basic: Hardtack is a dense, dry cracker that keeps for a very long time, making it a common travel ration for long journeys.

title: Harrada
topic_desc: Harrada is a root that grows exclusively in the planes of Oblivion, such as Khalaan and Subfuscous Cupola. Its extraplanar origin makes it a rare and valuable specimen for alchemical study in Tamriel, typically procured only through interplanar contact or specialized trade. Alchemists and hunters value harrada for its intrinsic properties, which reflect the alien nature of the realms from which it is harvested.
topic_desc_basic: Harrada is a root found only in the planes of Oblivion, such as Khalaan and Subfuscous Cupola. It is a rare alchemical ingredient in Tamriel.

title: Harvesting By The Heavens
topic_desc: Harvesting By The Heavens is a farmer's almanac published by the Imperial Astrological Society, also known as the Guild of Astrologers. The lengthy tome correlates agricultural practices with celestial phenomena, listing crops and botanicals alongside tables of their preferred growing conditions and the astrological Patron governing each. It provides weather predictions for the coming year derived from historic trends and readings of the signs within Kynareth's domain. An appendix collects reader-submitted recipes, folklore, and advertisements. The Society includes a prominent disclaimer advising that the almanac's contents are educational rather than instructional, urging farmers to adapt its guidelines to local conditions. Crucially, it warns that the constellation of the Serpent exerts an unpredictable influence over all things, and that planting, harvesting, and alterations to conditions must be strictly avoided during its appearance in the heavens.
topic_desc_basic: Harvesting By The Heavens is a farmer's almanac published by the Imperial Astrological Society. It lists crops and their preferred growing conditions under astrological Patrons, offers weather predictions based on the signs of Kynareth's domain, and includes folk recipes. The almanac strongly warns farmers to avoid planting or harvesting whenever the unpredictable constellation of the Serpent appears in the heavens.

title: Head of Cabbage
topic_desc: A head of cabbage is a leafy green vegetable commonly cultivated as a crop. Extensive farming of this produce is characteristic of Skyrim, though the vegetable is also widely kept in homes and taverns across Cyrodiil. While primarily recognized as a staple foodstuff, alchemists and hunters value it for its stable properties as an alchemical ingredient.
topic_desc_basic: A head of cabbage is a leafy green vegetable commonly farmed in Skyrim and widely found in homes and taverns across Cyrodiil.

title: Heartseeker
topic_desc: Heartseeker is an ancient artifact sword sacred to Dibella, last documented during the Four-Score War. It confers upon its wielder boons identical to those of the Lady birthsign. The blade is traditionally carried by the Knight of Dibella, a champion who swears to fight with beauty, honor, justice, and love. Centuries ago, a Redoran warrior named Terer Drurel slew the reigning Knight in battle. Moved by his fallen foe's grace, Drurel claimed the weapon and swore himself to Dibella as its next bearer. The sword eventually passed to the Drurel family. The Imperial Cult seeks the blade to counter Tribunal Temple claims that its existence is fabricated, while the Temple denounces the story as libel.
topic_desc_basic: Heartseeker is an ancient magical sword sacred to Dibella, traditionally wielded by the Knight of Dibella. It was last seen during the Four-Score War.

title: Hellebore Pollen
topic_desc: Hellebore pollen is a fine particulate harvested from the hellebore flower. Prized by alchemists for its intrinsic properties, the ingredient is gathered from wild hellebore blooms rather than cultivated sources. Specimens are notably scarce, with no guaranteed yields known to harvesters; the pollen appears only sporadically among the flora of certain northern regions, particularly within Skyrim's randomized ecological distributions. Its alchemical character renders it a component of interest in professional circles, though its unpredictable availability demands diligent foraging.
topic_desc_basic: Hellebore pollen is a fine substance gathered from hellebore flowers. It is a known alchemical ingredient, though it is relatively scarce and found sporadically in the wilds of Skyrim.

title: Helm of the Savior's Hide
topic_desc: The Helm of the Savior's Hide is a component of the Savior's Hide artifact set. When worn alongside the other pieces of the set, it confers total resistance to magicka. The helm currently rests within the Treasure Chamber of Firewatch's Ember Keep.
topic_desc_basic: The Helm of the Savior's Hide is a piece of the Savior's Hide set. It is kept in the Treasure Chamber of Firewatch's Ember Keep.

title: Hemlock Seeds
