topic_desc: Hemlock seeds are harvested from the hemlock plant, a species grown in Cyrodiil. The plant carries a sinister reputation and is most commonly sought for the creation of deadly poisons. Under ordinary circumstances, ingesting the seeds is lethal, making them a dangerous substance handled with caution. However, unusual magical phenomena can alter their fundamental nature; in at least one documented instance of anomalous alchemical reversal within a Mages Guildhall, locally cultivated hemlock seeds temporarily exhibited curative properties, counteracting poison rather than causing it. This aberration aside, the seeds remain firmly associated with their toxic character.
topic_desc_basic: Hemlock seeds come from a Cyrodiilic plant with a sinister reputation. They are widely known as a deadly poison, and cautious folk avoid them entirely.

title: Heretical Thoughts
topic_desc: A manifesto of the so-called Heretics of the Shivering Isles, rejecting the divinity of Sheogorath. The text denounces the Madgod as a mortal despot driven insane by foul magic and Daedric consorting, denying the existence of Daedric Princes entirely and claiming only vile servitors like Hungers inhabit those realms. It accuses Sheogorath of perverting the teachings of Arden-Sul and calls for his violent overthrow, detailing a gruesome execution and the destruction of New Sheoth. The author envisions a purified society living in the wilderness, united by heretical robes, that will hail the rebels as saviors for exposing the truth.
topic_desc_basic: A manifesto by the Heretics of the Shivering Isles, claiming Sheogorath is a mortal madman rather than a Daedric Prince. The text calls for his violent overthrow and the destruction of New Sheoth, advocating a return to wilderness living.

title: Hero of the Indoril
topic_desc: A biographical work by Elam Indoril recounting the life and military career of General Indoril Triffith, a prominent First Era commander of House Indoril. The text presents an Indoril-centric perspective on the War of the First Council, portraying Triffith as the pragmatic leader of the united Chimer forces and a steadfast servant of Lord Nerevar and the Tribunal. It emphasizes his strategic role at the Battle of Red Mountain and argues that his initial judgment to entirely exterminate House Dagoth was vindicated when his adopted Dagoth heir, Tay, succumbed to ancestral madness and led a brief, violent revolt. The narrative frames Triffith's ruthlessness toward enemies as virtuous necessity, reflecting orthodox Temple historiography. His spirit is said to have later been devoted to the Ghostfence.
topic_desc_basic: A biography by Elam Indoril detailing the life of General Indoril Triffith, a First Era military leader of House Indoril who commanded Chimer forces during the War of the First Council and the Battle of Red Mountain.

title: High King's Vedda Book Four
topic_desc: The fourth volume of the High King's Vedda presents a Nordic creation account centered on Kyne's five Breaths, which raised the World-Throat, carved the valleys, filled the rivers, brought life, and birthed the Children of the Sky. It frames the World as a sustained Shout filling the void of Alduin's permissive ignorance. The text characterizes elves and their frigid demons as the greatest evil, claiming they watched the World's building with jealous admiration and responded to each of Kyne's acts with escalating despair, self-harm, and horror. The fifth Breath provoked the elf-demons to swear oaths of destruction, and the snowy elves marched to bring War into the World. The volume concludes with a meditative instruction to measure one's own Breath, teaching that great works are wrought from such discipline.
topic_desc_basic: The fourth volume of the High King's Vedda recounts the Nordic creation myth of Kyne's five Breaths, which formed the world and birthed the Children of the Sky. It describes how jealous elf-demons responded to creation with despair and ultimately marched to bring War into the World.

title: Hirv Hide
topic_desc: Hirv Hide is an ingredient obtained from the hirv, a creature native to Morrowind. Alchemists and hunters value the hide for its alchemical properties, which are extracted through standard preparation techniques. It circulates in trade through random faunal supplies and is a recognized material in the region's alchemical practices.
topic_desc_basic: Hirv Hide is an ingredient harvested from the hirv, a creature found in Morrowind. It is used in alchemy.

title: His
topic_desc: A didactic tale recounting Vehk's subjugation of the Nordic warlord Bhag during the Chimer's early conflicts with the men of the north. Through three stratagems, Vehk claims Bhag's domain: first by turning the warlord's retainers to his service, then by fathering heirs who intermarry with Bhag's kin to seize the holding's future, and finally by destroying Bhag's ancestral records and rewriting them as his own. Having thus claimed Bhag's people, progeny, and past, Vehk slays him and presents the head to the Hortator Nerevar, declaring it too is 'his.' The narrative serves as a parable of Vivec's philosophy of acquisition and dominion, illustrating how mastery is achieved through loyalty, lineage, and the appropriation of history.
topic_desc_basic: A legendary tale of the god Vivec, then known as Vehk, who conquers a Nordic warlord named Bhag not through open warfare but by gradually claiming the warlord's retainers, heirs, and history as his own.

title: History of Daggerfall
topic_desc: Odiva Gallwood's historical work tracing the Daggerfall city-state from pre-settlement through the Third Era, examining its enduring rivalry with Sentinel and Wayrest for dominance over the Iliac Bay.
topic_desc_basic: A historical work by Odiva Gallwood chronicling the Daggerfall city-state and its long rivalry with Sentinel and Wayrest for control of the Iliac Bay.

title: History of Lock Picking
topic_desc: A treatise on the evolution of security mechanisms in Cyrodiil, from primitive door bars to modern spring-loaded pin locks. It traces the recorded origins of lock design to the trapped sliding-bar mechanism at Castle Anvil and credits the Dwemer Mzunchend with inventing the pin lock. The work notes that lockpicking only emerged after the blacksmith Orenthal mass-produced affordable pin locks, creating widespread demand to subvert them. It explains the principles of modern multi-pin locks, which reset all pins if any single pin is improperly manipulated, and describes the skill required to tension and set spring-loaded pins, contrasting the many broken picks of novices with the economy of masters.
topic_desc_basic: A book chronicling the development of locks and lockpicking in Cyrodiil, from early trapped sliding bars to modern spring-loaded pin mechanisms, and explaining the techniques used to subvert them.

title: History of The Oroynyon Family
topic_desc: A concise history of the Oroynyon family
topic_desc_basic: A concise history of the Oroynyon family, a minor Dunmer house in southeastern Indoril formed from the union of Houses Dreynyon and Oronis after the Nordic expulsion from Resdayn.

title: History of the Second Empire
topic_desc: A scholarly work published under the authority of the Imperial Geographical Society, examining the Second Empire's two stages: the Reman Dynasty and the Akaviri Potentate. It emphasizes the profound Akaviri influence on Imperial culture and governance following the recruitment of defeated raiders into Reman's service. The text details how Akaviri slaves and advisors established the Empire's administrative structures and restructured the legions with superior discipline, enabling Cyrodiilic dominance over nearly all of Tamriel except Morrowind. It further traces the Akaviri Potentate's rise after the Morag Tong assassinated Reman's last heir during the Four Score War. The work highlights enduring Akaviri legacies in the Third Empire, including daikatana and dragonscale armor craftsmanship, Blades military dress, the Red Dragon banners of the Imperial City, and the prized Akaviri surnames and facial features found among distinguished Cyrodilic families.
topic_desc_basic: An Imperial Geographical Society publication detailing the Second Empire's history under the Reman Dynasty and the Akaviri Potentate, focusing on the lasting impact of Akaviri culture and administration on the Empire.

title: Hlaalu Fine Recipes
topic_desc: Hlaalu Fine Recipes is a culinary text presenting House Hlaalu approaches to regional cooking. It details the preparation of grilled alit meat seasoned with Cyrodiilic garlic and Rihad pepper, served over saltrice and comberries, alongside a fig jam incorporating marshmerrow and drumpear seeds. The work reflects Hlaalu culinary sensibilities that blend native Morrowind ingredients with imported Imperial spices and produce.
topic_desc_basic: Hlaalu Fine Recipes is a cookbook associated with House Hlaalu. It provides instructions for preparing dishes using local and imported ingredients, such as grilled alit meat with saltrice and fig jam with marshmerrow.

title: Hogweed Flowers
topic_desc: Hogweed flowers are a botanical ingredient harvested from the hogweed plant. Alchemists value the blossoms for their inherent properties, which can be extracted and combined with other reagents to produce alchemical mixtures. The flowers are gathered from wild hogweed growth, and practitioners of the alchemical arts routinely seek them out as a staple component in their preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Hogweed flowers are a common botanical ingredient harvested from the hogweed plant. They are widely recognized by alchemists and herbalists for their useful properties.

title: Holidays of the Iliac Bay
topic_desc: A scholarly treatise by Theth-i analyzing the festival calendars of the Iliac Bay to illuminate the cultural divergence between its Breton and Redguard populations. The author argues that Redguard observances—such as the Serpent's Dance and Drigh R'Zimb—are often transposed pre-migration rites honoring homeland deities that largely failed to survive the journey to Tamriel, with their dates and meanings altered to suit Hammerfell's climate. Conversely, Breton holidays like Waking Day and the Moon Festival are presented as near-unchanged survivals of primitive ancestor and nature worship, while newer observances like Tibedetha and Mad Pelagius reflect later political and historical figures. The work treats these traditions as a lens for understanding the broader evolution of both societies.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Theth-i surveying the traditional festivals of the Iliac Bay. It contrasts the ancient Breton celebrations rooted in nature and ancestor worship with the Redguard holidays adapted from their pre-migration homeland.

title: Honey
topic_desc: Honey is a sweet, viscous food substance produced by bees from flower nectar. It is gathered from beehives and is widely recognized across Tamriel as both a foodstuff and an alchemical ingredient. Beekeepers and foragers harvest it from wild and domesticated colonies, and it appears regularly among provisions and trade goods in Cyrodiil, Skyrim, and Morrowind. Its alchemical properties are valued by practitioners who incorporate it into preparations alongside other common ingredients.
topic_desc_basic: Honey is a sweet, golden substance made by bees from flower nectar. It is gathered from beehives and is commonly used as a food and sweetener throughout Tamriel. It is also known to have alchemical properties.

title: Honey Lily Blossom
topic_desc: Honey Lily Blossoms are the flowers of the Honey Lily plant, a flora known to grow in Midkarth and the Vorndgad Forest in Skyrim. As a botanical ingredient, the blossom is gathered for its alchemical properties and is typically sourced from these western Skyrim regions. Its natural occurrence in forested and Reach-adjacent territories makes it a regional resource for practitioners of alchemy.
topic_desc_basic: Honey Lily Blossoms are flowers gathered from the Honey Lily plant, which grows in Midkarth and the Vorndgad Forest in Skyrim.

title: Honey Lily Leaf
topic_desc: Honey Lily Leaves are harvested from Honey Lilies, a flowering plant native to Skyrim. The flower grows in the Midkarth region and the Vorndgad Forest. Alchemists and hunters value the leaf for its properties.
topic_desc_basic: Honey Lily Leaves are taken from Honey Lilies, flowers that grow in Midkarth and the Vorndgad Forest in Skyrim.

title: Hoom
topic_desc: Hooms are large, land-dwelling crustaceans native to Morrowind's Velothi Mountains. As cousins to the desert-dwelling Sand Kwoom, hooms possess thicker fur and shorter legs, adaptations suited to their cold mountain and forest habitats in the north. Wild hooms are mildly territorial and become aggressive if approached, but tamed specimens are passive. Their durable constitution makes them valued as hardy pack animals, and the fellche of House Redoran employ them to pull sleds across the rugged northern terrain.
topic_desc_basic: Hooms are large, land-dwelling crustaceans native to the cold mountains and forests of northern Morrowind. Thicker-furred and shorter-legged than their desert cousins, the Sand Kwoom, they are tamed as hardy pack animals and sled-pullers by House Redoran.

title: Hoom Back Lung
topic_desc: Hoom Back Lungs are organs harvested from the hoom, a creature of Morrowind. Their specific alchemical properties remain a subject of specialist study, though the ingredient circulates through general and regional merchant supply lists, including those serving Velothi communities. The organ's prevalence in these stocks indicates a recognized, if niche, utility in alchemical practice.
topic_desc_basic: Hoom Back Lungs are organs taken from the hoom creature. They are traded as an alchemical ingredient throughout Morrowind.

title: Hoom Egg
topic_desc: Hoom eggs are laid by the hoom, a creature of Tamriel. They circulate through general and specialized egg and ingredient supplies across Morrowind and the Velothi region, appearing in both homogeneous and mixed egg collections as well as broader random ingredient stocks. Alchemists and hunters encounter them as a recognized alchemical component, though guaranteed samples are scarce. Their specific properties and full culinary or alchemical applications remain undocumented in widely available reference texts.
topic_desc_basic: Hoom eggs are laid by the hoom creature. They are a recognized alchemical ingredient found in various general and specialized ingredient supplies throughout Morrowind.

title: Hoom Shell Fragment
topic_desc: A shell fragment derived from a hoom, a creature of Morrowind's wilderness. The chitinous piece is gathered as an alchemical ingredient by hunters and apothecaries familiar with the region's fauna. Its properties make it a modest but recognizable reagent in the preparation of potions, traded and collected alongside other common creature-derived materials.
topic_desc_basic: A shell fragment taken from a hoom creature. It is known among hunters and alchemists as a gatherable ingredient used in potion-making.

title: Hopper Antler
topic_desc: Hopper antler is an ingredient harvested from the hopper, a creature of Morrowind. As a relatively uncommon alchemical reagent, it circulates through regional ingredient supplies and appears in randomized fauna collections, particularly around the Narsis region. Alchemists and hunters value these specimens for their properties in potion-making, though guaranteed sources remain scarce. The antler's specific alchemical characteristics are documented in specialist practice, and its presence in curated ingredient lists suggests recognized utility within the province's apothecary traditions.
topic_desc_basic: Hopper antler is an ingredient obtained from the hopper creature. It is a somewhat uncommon alchemical reagent found in randomized ingredient supplies, especially near the Narsis region.

title: Horker Meat
topic_desc: Horker meat is the edible flesh of horkers, large tusked aquatic mammals that inhabit the cold northern coasts and ice floes of Tamriel. It is consumed as food and traded among coastal communities, particularly in Skyrim and similar northern regions. The meat is also found among general food stores and random provisions carried by travelers and merchants operating in northern lands.
topic_desc_basic: Horker meat is the flesh of horkers, large tusked sea mammals found along Tamriel's northern coasts. It is eaten as food and traded in northern regions.

title: Horker Pup Pelt
topic_desc: Horker pup pelts are the small hides harvested from horker pups, the infant forms of the large marine horkers native to northern Tamriel. The pelts occur in gray, white, and brown varieties. Owing to their origin from young specimens, they are comparatively modest in size. They are not commonly traded through standard mercantile channels, as they do not circulate in typical leveled supply lists, making them a somewhat uncommon alchemical commodity.
topic_desc_basic: Horker pup pelts are small hides taken from horker pups, the young of the large marine beasts. They come in gray, white, and brown varieties.

title: Horn of the Wild
topic_desc: The Horn of the Wild is an enchanted artifact capable of summoning a wolf pack to aid its user in battle. It is currently housed within Inghal Barrow.
topic_desc_basic: The Horn of the Wild is an enchanted horn that can summon a wolf pack to aid its wielder. It is kept inside Inghal Barrow.

title: Horned Beetle Shell
topic_desc: Horned beetle shells are chitinous forewings harvested from the horned beetles native to Morrowind. Beyond their well-known utility in Morrowind's indigenous armors, the shells are ground and dissolved alongside bone shards and resin to form the composite material for bonemold and aena weapons and armor. The shells also possess distinct alchemical virtues, making them a valued reagent among apothecaries and huntsmen familiar with the region's fauna.
topic_desc_basic: Horned beetle shells are the chitinous forewings of horned beetles found in Morrowind. They are commonly ground and dissolved with bone shards and resin to craft bonemold and aena armors and weapons.

title: Horns of Hanugalba
topic_desc: The Horns of Hanugalba is an ancient Nedic weapon interred within the Nedic burial ground at Hattusili in Morrowind. Its presence provides physical corroboration for the theoretical and now-vanished human population of Morrowind described in scholarly accounts such as Frontier, Conquest. As a remnant of this lost Nedic community, the artifact holds significant esoteric and archaeological value, representing the material culture of a people who once inhabited the region before their eventual disappearance.
topic_desc_basic: The Horns of Hanugalba is an ancient Nedic weapon. It rests within the Nedic burial ground at Hattusili in Morrowind.

title: Horse Meat
topic_desc: Horse meat is taken from horses, large animals common to Cyrodiil and Skyrim. In Morrowind, where the creature is scarce, the meat is considered a rare delicacy. Alchemists and hunters value it as an ingredient, and it circulates through trade networks supplying Cyr and Sky regional markets.
topic_desc_basic: Horse meat comes from horses, large animals common in Cyrodiil and Skyrim. It is considered a rare delicacy in Morrowind.

title: Horskva Kongerike, I-VII
topic_desc: A Nordic mirror-for-princes text presenting a dying king's counsel to his heir on ruling the seafaring kingdom of Uld Vraech. The father instructs his son to control the straits between Dunkreath and Solstheim, distrust the Ashen Folk and southern empires, and maintain fealty through taxation and tollships. He identifies the Throat of the World, the serpent hall of Danstrar, and the Dragon Wall as northern marvels, and recounts the overthrow of the Tjaski-men three hundred winters prior. The work advocates raiding eastern Dunmereth and distant islands for wealth, warning against attacking western cousins except in direst need. It frames martial plunder as the truest path to prosperity and a king's standing among Kyne's folk.
topic_desc_basic: A Nordic instructional text in which a dying king advises his heir on ruling the kingdom of Uld Vraech, covering its land, people, enemies, commerce, and the practice of raiding eastern Dunmereth for wealth.

title: House of the Big Walker
topic_desc: A Khajiiti oral account recorded circa 3E 30 by Rodala of the Horse-Men and later restored by Cassolar Drabo from an Alessian palimpsest. Narrated by Dro'Zhani, a Khajiit maimed during the conflict, the work recounts the construction of the 'House'—a tower of 'liar-stones'—by the 'Seizing Men' to house the 'Big Walker.' It describes Alkosh's failed attempts to destroy the structure, the creation of a 'Dragon-in-Flesh' tricked by the 'sly one,' and the activation of the Walker by the 'heart of the buried one.' The narrative culminates in a Dragon Break, where the House is repeatedly blown apart and scattered across time, becoming indistinguishable from the sands of Elsweyr. The text offers a distinct Khajiiti mytho-historical interpretation of Tiber Septim's conquest, the activation of Numidium, and the temporal catastrophe that followed.
topic_desc_basic: A legendary Khajiiti tale recounting the 'Seizing Men' forcing Khajiit to build a great House for the 'Big Walker.' It tells of Alkosh's struggle against the Walker, its activation by a dark heart, and a temporal catastrophe that scattered the House across time until it became indistinguishable from the desert sands.

title: How to Treat Heretics
topic_desc: A doctrinal treatise by Salvas Relas of the Order of Doctrine and Ordination, advising Temple Ordinators on when to show mercy to non-believers. The work categorizes encounters into children of heretics, the misled, the coerced, and the doubters, arguing that reeducation and redemption are preferable to violence. Relas emphasizes that under Temple law, heresy requires a refusal to be corrected, and he urges Ordinators to emulate Almalexia's mercy by prioritizing instruction over execution whenever feasible, reserving lethal force for unrepentant enemies like willing servants of the House of Troubles.
topic_desc_basic: A Temple treatise by Salvas Relas instructing Ordinators on dealing with non-believers. It advocates mercy and reeducation over violence for children, the ignorant, the coerced, and the doubtful, reserving lethal force for unrepentant heretics.

title: How to Tune your Hoom
topic_desc: A treatise by Arvyrin Adrys on the rearing and musical training of the Mountain Hoom. The work recounts the legendary Hoom Daroom, who sang to Dwemer animunculi, and the seven thousand Hoom that greeted Saint Veloth upon his arrival in Resdayn. Adrys advises raising the creature from birth so it imitates its keeper, dismissing the Nord belief that spring mating season improves learning. Fitted reeds and valves broaden the animal's range, and masters engrave sigils upon the carapace; Adrys marks his work with a double-headed Shalk. The author concedes that the ancient art of teaching a Hoom to speak, if it ever truly existed, is now lost, though some hold that the creatures simply chose to sing instead.
topic_desc_basic: A guide by Arvyrin Adrys on rearing and training the Mountain Hoom, a creature of storied Resdayn tradition, to produce musical harmonies.

title: Human Heart
topic_desc: A Human Heart is the visceral organ harvested from a human. Externally, it is indistinguishable from a Daedra's Heart, though the resemblance ends with appearance; its alchemical properties are relatively useless. Apothecaries and hunters recognize it as a mundane anatomical curio rather than a potent reagent, and it yields little of value in standard potion-craft.
topic_desc_basic: A Human Heart is the organ of a human, visually identical to a Daedra's Heart. It is a common anatomical part but possesses relatively useless alchemical properties.

title: Hunting Hound Chitin
topic_desc: Hunting hound chitin is a white shell harvested from the hunting hound, a creature native to the Velothi Mountains of Morrowind. The chitin constitutes a natural carapace for the beast, and a viable alchemical sample is reliably recovered from each specimen. The material is not commonly found as loose stock, requiring direct harvest from the creature itself. Its properties make it a subject of interest for practitioners of alchemy and hunters familiar with the mountainous regions where the hounds roam.
topic_desc_basic: Hunting hound chitin is a white shell taken from the hunting hound, a creature found in the Velothi Mountains of Morrowind. The shell is reliably harvested directly from the hounds themselves.

title: Hyperagonal Media Theorem
topic_desc: The Hyperagonal Media Theorem is a metaphysical treatise challenging the conventional mundiocentric model of the Aurbis as directional creatia moving solely along the axes of IS and NOT. It argues that this framework, limited to parallel and perpendicular transmissions, fails to account for transliminal traversal. The author posits that hyperagonality—the oblique angles beyond mortal perception—cannot be measured by mundane astrolabes or grasped through mathematics alone. The treatise asserts that the Daedric Princes (termed Lords of Misrule) are fundamentally incapable of conveying this concept to mortals, and that cosmological models collapse when pressed for finer detail because mortal minds cannot comprehend the calligraphy of the heavens. Transcending this limitation requires a different gradient of enlightenment beyond mortal conception. The text becomes incomprehensible past its opening passages, inducing severe headaches in readers.
topic_desc_basic: The Hyperagonal Media Theorem is a metaphysical treatise arguing that mortal cosmological models fail to describe transliminal movement. It claims that hyperagonal angles beyond mundane perception are the true medium of the Aurbis, and that Daedric Princes cannot convey this to mortal minds. A copy is known in the possession of Lord Dral of Tel Thenim in Port Telvannis.

title: Ice Crystal
topic_desc: Ice Crystals are extremely rare and notably heavy crystalline ingredients obtained from the remains of Frost Monarchs, a more powerful form of Frost Atronach. As a product of these formidable conjured entities, the crystals are prized by alchemists and hunters familiar with Daedric fauna, though their exceptional weight and scarcity make them difficult to acquire and transport in quantity.
topic_desc_basic: Ice Crystals are extremely rare and heavy crystals dropped by Frost Monarchs, a powerful type of Frost Atronach.

title: Ice Wraith
topic_desc: Ice Wraiths are fey, lucid serpentine nature spirits composed entirely of ice, described as a snaking skeleton of blue flame or a collection of ice bones bound by nature magic, culminating in a sharp-ridged spine and a malcontented jaw of sharp teeth. They inhabit the frozen regions of Tamriel, primarily Skyrim's snow-blown landscapes and mountain ranges, though they also dwell in High Rock, Cyrodiil's reclusive mountains, and the Sea of Ghosts. Masters of ambush, they blend into the snow to become nearly invisible before lunging at unsuspecting prey. They can pass through victims to afflict them with infection, burrow into the ground to burst upward, and attack with frost magic. Witbane is a known infection from their bite. Upon death, their remains combust into large, dangerous spikes of ice. They are immune to paralysis.
topic_desc_basic: Ice Wraiths are serpentine nature spirits made of ice that inhabit frozen regions like Skyrim's mountains and the Sea of Ghosts. Nearly invisible in snow, they ambush prey by lunging or bursting from the ground, and their bites can transmit Witbane.

title: Ice Wraith Teeth
topic_desc: Ice Wraith Teeth are jagged icicle teeth acquired from Ice Wraiths, frozen spirits sometimes found in Skyrim and the icy regions of Morrowind. As an alchemical ingredient, they are valued for their inherent properties, though their extraction requires hunting the elusive spirits that bear them. Their rarity makes them a sought-after component among practitioners of alchemy.
topic_desc_basic: Ice Wraith Teeth are jagged, icicle-like teeth taken from Ice Wraiths, frozen spirits found in Skyrim and cold regions of Morrowind. They are used in alchemy.

title: Icy Shell Fungus
topic_desc: Icy shell fungus is a fungal ingredient valued by alchemists and hunters. As its name suggests, the specimen exhibits a frost-encrusted or hardened exterior. It occurs naturally across Skyrim and is typically gathered from the wild rather than cultivated. The fungus features in regional alchemical supply and foraging collections, indicating recognized utility in potion-making and wilderness survival.
topic_desc_basic: Icy shell fungus is a frost-covered fungus found in Skyrim. It is gathered as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Imga
topic_desc: The Imga, or Great Apes, are intelligent ape-folk native to Valenwood, said to have flourished there long before the Aldmer arrived. They cohabit the forests alongside Bosmer tribes and also inhabit abandoned Second Empire trading posts. Some Imga are found in western and northern Tamriel's mountainous regions, while others have been kept as slaves by the Dunmer, though in lesser numbers than Argonians. Imga clans revere the spoken word, producing remarkable orators, and many find calling in religious orders, law, and commerce. They serve as learned advisors to cult orders, polities, and trading consortiums throughout the Western Empire. Talented acrobats and pugilists, they are also renowned for spiritual innovation. The most notable Imga was Marukh, a First Era prophet of the Camoran Dynasty whose teachings sparked the Alessian Order and the Marukhati Selective.
topic_desc_basic: The Imga, or Great Apes, are ape-folk native to Valenwood. They are known as talented orators and serve as advisors to religious, legal, and commercial interests across the Western Empire.

title: Imperial Archaeological Society
topic_desc: The Imperial Archaeological Society is the oldest archaeological organization in Tamriel, chartered by the Emperor to recover and study the physical remnants of past civilizations. Active since at least the Tiber War, it operates under legal frameworks like the Dwarven Reclamation Act. In Morrowind, the Society focuses on Dwemer ruins, maintaining its Telvannis District headquarters in Helnim and a museum in Old Ebonheart under Dean Decimia Gastoit. Its expeditions include the famous project at Kemel-Ze. The Society enjoys a mutually beneficial relationship with the Mages Guild for investigating Dwemer sites and receives Imperial funding, possibly supplemented by artifact sales through the East Empire Company. It faces opposition from Great House Redoran, Great House Indoril, Great House Dres, and vampire clans, who resent its excavations.
topic_desc_basic: The Imperial Archaeological Society is the oldest organization of archaeologists in Tamriel, dedicated to uncovering and preserving the ancient past. An academic society of the Empire, its scholars can be found across the continent excavating ruins, including the famous Dwemer site at Kemel-Ze. In Morrowind, the Society maintains a headquarters in Helnim and a museum in Old Ebonheart.

title: Imperial Astrological Society
topic_desc: The Imperial Astrological Society is a scholarly organization devoted to the study of the stars and the heavens. As an Imperial institution, it pursues cosmological knowledge and the reading of celestial phenomena across Tamriel. In Morrowind, the Society currently maintains very limited representation, its presence constrained by the province's insular culture and the Tribunal Temple's entrenched cosmological doctrines. While the Society's work flourishes elsewhere in the Empire, its influence in Dunmer lands remains marginal.
topic_desc_basic: The Imperial Astrological Society is a scholarly guild dedicated to studying the stars. It currently has very limited representation in Morrowind.

title: Imperial Census of Daedra Lords
topic_desc: An Imperial scholarly work cataloguing the Daedric Princes, their realms, and their relationships to the Empire. Commissioned under the authority of Emperor Uriel VII, the census describes the domains of the Princes—such as Azura's Moonshadow, Boethiah's Attribution's Share, and Molag Bal's Coldharbour—while noting which realms are currently closed by Elder Council consensus. The text reflects an Imperial bureaucratic and cautionary viewpoint, warning of Princes like Mehrunes Dagon and Molag Bal as enemies of the Empire, restricting propitiation to Hermaeus Mora to an official holiday, and advising only the strongest servants to treat with Clavicus Vile. It also records speculation on the aetherial origins of certain Princes, including Malacath and Meridia, and notes the traditional festival dates for several Daedric Lords.
topic_desc_basic: An Imperial text cataloguing the Daedric Princes, their Oblivion realms, and their relationships to the Empire, compiled under the authority of Emperor Uriel VII.

title: Imperial Geographical Society
topic_desc: The Imperial Geographical Society is a long-standing scholarly organization responsible for outlining and preserving historical accounts across the Empire. Operating on behalf of Imperial authority, it maintains offices in select major cities across Tamriel, though none exist in Morrowind despite the presence of a few individual members. The Society's most renowned commission is the Pocket Guide to the Empire, a broad historical overview first published in 2E 864 under Tiber Septim to educate and reassure inhabitants of the new Empire, though early editions employed propagandist emphasis. Subsequent editions commissioned by Empress Morihatha in 3E 331 and Emperor Uriel Septim VII in 3E 432 abandoned this tone. The Society also produced The Improved Emperor's Guide to Tamriel and Gathering Force in 2E 578, and an apparent branch, the Imperial Geographic Survey, published a census of the Daedra Lords around 3E 432.
topic_desc_basic: The Imperial Geographical Society is a long-standing scholarly organization that preserves historical accounts across the Empire. It maintains offices in select major Tamrielic cities, though none are in Morrowind. The Society is best known for authoring the Pocket Guide to the Empire, a broad historical overview commissioned by Imperial authority.

title: Imperial Heraldry in Morrowind
topic_desc: An illustrated guide written and compiled by Dolemmus Heth-Suurim, documenting the heraldic symbols and coats of arms employed by Imperial institutions and Morrowind's royal house. The work traces each sigil to its origin: the Imperial Dragon, adopted from the Tsaesci by Reman Cyrodiil after Pale Pass in 1E 2703; the Royal Wolf of Symmachus, personal arms of Tiber Septim's general that became the sigil of Morrowind's kings; the Nord-introduced Double-Headed Eagle; the Twin Lions linked to Queen Mother Barenziah's Wayrest heritage; the Vaynth Wyrm of Firewatch, commissioned in 3E 394; and the heraldic achievements of the Fighters and Mages Guilds and the Imperial Navy. The guide is notable for connecting each emblem to its historical and political context, revealing how foreign, provincial, and institutional symbols were layered into the visual language of Imperial authority in Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: A guide written and illustrated by Dolemmus Heth-Suurim documenting heraldic symbols used by the Empire and Morrowind's royal house. It covers the origins and meanings of sigils including the Imperial Dragon, the Royal Wolf of Symmachus, the Double-Headed Eagle, the Twin Lions, the Vaynth Wyrm of Firewatch, and the coats of arms of the Fighters and Mages Guilds and the Imperial Navy.

title: Imperial Knights
topic_desc: The Imperial Knights constitute the militaristic nobility of the Empire, an obscure knightly guild representing the upper echelons of the Imperial Legion. Unlike the Legion's field commanders, the Imperial Knights occupy a distinct social tier where aristocratic standing and martial service converge. The order is referenced in literary works such as *The Wraith's Wedding Dowry* and in colloquial dialogue, though it remains less publicly visible than the Legion's conventional military structure. Their role places them above the rank-and-file Legionnaires in social standing, if not in direct operational authority.
topic_desc_basic: The Imperial Knights are an obscure knightly guild of Tamriel, broadly known as the upper echelons of the Imperial Legion. They serve not as field commanders but as the militaristic nobility of the Empire, a distinction occasionally noted in common dialogue and literature.

title: Imperial Proverbs
topic_desc: A collection of moralizing sayings and aphorisms from across Cyrodiil, illustrating various aspects from the worldview of the common Imperial. The proverbs address themes of law, authority, speech, prudence, and social hierarchy, reflecting a culture that values obedience to the Emperor, the illuminating power of law, and the dangers of careless words. The sayings reveal a pragmatic and sometimes cynical outlook, acknowledging gaps in legal systems and the harsh realities of survival, while cautioning against misplaced trust and foolish friendships. References to hostile jungles and tigers suggest Nibenese origins or broader provincial influences within Imperial culture.
topic_desc_basic: A collection of moralizing sayings and aphorisms from across Cyrodiil. The work illustrates the worldview of the common Imperial through proverbs addressing law, authority, prudence, and the dangers of careless speech.

title: Imperial Purple Dye
topic_desc: Imperial Purple Dye is a costly dark magenta colorant employed in giving vivid hue to paints and textiles. Prized by artisans and dyers, its expense renders it a luxury good beyond common reach. As an alchemical ingredient, it possesses properties of interest to practitioners, though its primary recognized value remains its striking and enduring color.
topic_desc_basic: Imperial Purple Dye is a costly dark magenta dye used to color paints and textiles.

title: In Regards to the Chitin Armor
topic_desc: Roiwra's treatise, published in the Imperial City, examines Dunmeri chitin armor as a product of environmental adaptation. It argues that the Chimer exodus from Aldmeri lands forced the development of indigenous materials like netch leather and insect resin for survival and warfare. The work traces chitin's evolution from early shield-making to its modern layered form, where resinous glues bind carapace plates to provide insulation, padding, and airflow. This design suits light infantry by enabling endurance in heat and against heavier-armed foes. Roiwra presents chitin armor as cost-effective and enduring, suggesting Imperial culture could learn from Dunmer adaptability.
topic_desc_basic: An Imperial military historian's study of Dunmeri chitin armor, arguing that its development from local insect materials was a practical adaptation forced by the Chimer exodus from Aldmeri lands.

record_links.display_name: In Regards to the Chitin Armor

title: Indoril Beroth and the Hermit
topic_desc: A didactic account of an encounter between Indoril Beroth and a faithless hermit along the River Thirr. The hermit, despite twenty years of dutiful and untempted isolation, despairs at feeling no connection to Almsivi. Beroth advises him to abandon the hermitage for city life, arguing that piety is useless if one lacks the corresponding soul; just as an Indoril has an Indoril's soul, the hermit possesses a soul meant for a different noble duty. The hermit relocates to Othrenis, becomes a renowned smith, and attributes his craft to his renewed faith. The work reinforces the orthodox Tribunal view that spiritual fulfillment requires fulfilling one's innate, assigned role rather than imposing an unsuitable ascetic path.
topic_desc_basic: A story in which Indoril Beroth counsels a faithless hermit along the River Thirr to abandon his isolation for city life, arguing that spiritual fulfillment requires one to follow their innate soul's duty rather than an unsuitable ascetic path.

title: Indoril Book of Passing
topic_desc: The Indoril Book of Passing Through the Doors of the Horizon is a doctrinal treatise of Great House Indoril that codifies the few acceptable ways an Indoril mer may die honorably. It establishes five categories of good death: fire, as practiced by the Indoril of Khalaan; sleep, citing Saint Delyn's serene passing; battle, exemplified by Lord Dorom of Almalexia enduring dismemberment by Mehrunes Dagon without yielding expression; house war, framing assassination as martyrdom testifying to the victim's honor; and self-murder, which the work upholds as distinct from treachery. It criticizes Alandro Sul for mourning Lord Nerevar with invocations rather than piercing his own liver with a blessed blade. The text serves as both consolation and strict cultural prescription, reinforcing Indoril standards for mortality and the afterlife.
topic_desc_basic: The Indoril Book of Passing is a Great House Indoril treatise prescribing the few acceptable ways an Indoril mer may die honorably, including fire, sleep, battle, house war, and self-murder.

title: Industries: the Rivermen
topic_desc: A scholarly treatise produced by order of the Conclave of Arts and Artificers, this work examines the fishing and aquaculture industries of the Niben River. It details the catching and processing of chrysophant, slaughterfish, and mudcrab, which form the dietary staple alongside rice. The text describes southern kollop cultivation for food and tinmi pearls, and attributes the fermented fish-sauce mokre to the Keptu tribes. It also notes the economic value of Rumare slaughterfish scales, prized by the Nibenese trader caste as emblems of cunning and traded as symbolic currency among certain Argonian tribes.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise produced for the Conclave of Arts and Artificers examining the fishing and aquaculture industries of the Niben River, detailing the harvesting of fish, mudcrabs, and kollops, the production of the fermented fish-sauce mokre, and the trade in Rumare slaughterfish scales.

title: Industries: the Soap Refineries
topic_desc: Produced by order of the Conclave of Arts and Artificers, this treatise examines the Nibenese Sload soap industry. While true Sload soap is rare and alchemically valuable, the Nibenay produces an abundant, low-grade variant for cosmetics and salves. The industry relies on non-sentient Sload grubs plundered during the Thrassian War, kept in embryonic suspension and fattened on river refuse in great tanks before soap-cutters harvest regenerating tissue from them. Refineries in Bravil, Delodiil, and the Imperial City's industrial islands each use proprietary grubs, making their products traceable and protecting their trade. The author notes the industry's entrenched stagnation: obtaining new grubs is practically impossible without illegal Sload trade, theft, or purchase from firms that never sell. Sabotage—salt can decimate a grub population—and aggressive practices have recently destroyed the Bravil firms and fostered an unpleasant reputation, compounded by rumors of feral Sload escaping into the Imperial City's underground.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise on the Nibenese Sload soap industry, which produces a low-grade cosmetic oil. Unlike true Sload soap, this variant is made from regenerating tissue harvested from non-sentient Sload grubs plundered during the Thrassian War, raised in tanks along Lake Rumare and the Niben Bay.

title: Iniquities of the Current Era
topic_desc: A polemical treatise lamenting the decline of Imperial civilization. The author contrasts the virtue and intellectual ambition of the early Third and Second Empires with the present generation's decadence, arguing that the Heartland lineages have become besotted and incapable of practicing or even appreciating the arts and sciences of their ancestors. Citing the loss of disciplines like astrolothurgy and theosophy, and the abandonment of pious vows to Julianos and Zenithar in favor of vile sanctuary prayers for wealth and murder, the work condemns the era's materialism. It singles out the Elder Council's corruption—employing priests to pray for thirty million drakes annually—as proof that coin is now revered above the masterworks of figures like Morachellis, Selia, and Praxathes.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise lamenting the decline of Imperial civilization. It contrasts the intellectual ambition and virtue of earlier eras with the current generation's decadence, condemning the abandonment of the refined arts and pious vows in favor of materialism and base desires.

title: Ink Cone
topic_desc: Ink cones are harvested from inkwood plants, which grow in the Brennan Bluffs of Cyrodiil. Alchemists value these ingredients for their useful properties, and hunters familiar with the region's flora often gather them for trade or experimentation.
topic_desc_basic: Ink cones come from inkwood plants found in the Brennan Bluffs of Cyrodiil. They are used in alchemy.

title: Inside Almalexia's Tongs
topic_desc: Galasa Sarvu's guide examining the honorable societies, or Tongs, of Almalexia. The work argues that the capital's unique diversity of such fraternities misleads outlanders about broader Great House culture. It categorizes these groups: orthodox societies emphasizing specific Tribunal aspects without challenging doctrine, such as the Galaan and Sorys Tongs; trade guilds rooted in saint veneration; and underground criminal or heretical fraternities like the Camonna and Vel-Osryn Tongs. The author notes that unverified rumors surround the most secretive groups, such as the Issani Tong. The text also outlines the social boundaries of these institutions, observing that most Tongs reject outlander membership and maintain their own laws within their halls, which often operate openly but unmarked.
topic_desc_basic: A guide by Galasa Sarvu detailing the many honorable societies, or Tongs, of Almalexia. The book explains that these fraternities range from orthodox religious groups and trade guilds to criminal organizations, and that most exclude outlanders from membership while enforcing their own rules within their unmarked halls.

title: Insight, Tranquility, Divinity
topic_desc: Insight, Tranquility, Divinity is a poetic work by Fravil Entryne that reflects on the landscapes of Tear and the elevated gardens above the city. The three poems—Divine Tranquility, Visage of Hearts and Souls, and Morbid Serenity—progress from a yearning for solitude amid natural splendor, through anguished contemplation of past transgressions and a desire for redemption, to a fatalistic acceptance of death and subjugation following failed rebellion. The collection frames these themes of enlightenment, despair, and futility as subjective perceptions left to the reader's interpretation.
topic_desc_basic: A collection of three poems by Fravil Entryne inspired by the city of Tear. The verses explore themes of solitude, personal transgression, and the fatalistic consequences of rebellion.

title: Iron Hide
topic_desc: Iron Hide is the tough, segmented outer hide of the Iron Toad, a creature found in Skyrim. Valued by alchemists and hunters for its durable properties, it serves as a regional alchemical ingredient harvested from the beast's natural armor.
topic_desc_basic: Iron Hide is the tough, segmented outer hide of the Iron Toad, a creature found in Skyrim.

title: Iron Ore
topic_desc: Iron ore is the unrefined mineral substance from which pure iron is obtained. Though iron yields cheaper and harder weapons and armor than rarer metals, it serves as the fundamental material for most everyday tools and construction work across Tamriel. Iron mining is far more common in Cyrodiil than in Morrowind; the few iron mines within Morrowind's mainland are overshadowed by Vvardenfell's far more precious ebony and glass deposits. As an alchemical ingredient, iron ore possesses its own distinct properties, though its primary cultural and economic significance stems from its role as a staple of civilized industry rather than from refinement by apothecaries.
topic_desc_basic: Iron ore is the unrefined mineral from which pure iron is obtained. It is a cheap, hard material used for everyday tools and construction. Iron ore is far more common in Cyrodiil than in Morrowind, and no iron mines exist on Vvardenfell, where far more precious minerals like ebony and glass are extracted instead.

title: Ironrye
topic_desc: Ironrye is a grain commonly cultivated in Cyrodiil and Skyrim, where it forms part of the regular agricultural yield. It also grows wild along the Strident Coast and in the Brennan Bluffs, suggesting a hardy constitution capable of thriving both under deliberate tillage and without it. Its widespread presence in both farmed and feral contexts speaks to its adaptability across varied climates. Alchemists and provisioners regard it as a staple foodstuff rather than a rare or exotic reagent, and its ready availability makes it a commonplace component in everyday preparations throughout the regions where it flourishes.
topic_desc_basic: Ironrye is a grain commonly farmed in Cyrodiil and Skyrim. It also grows wild along the Strident Coast and in the Brennan Bluffs.

title: Ironwood Nuts
topic_desc: Ironwood nuts are the seeds of the ironwood tree, valued by alchemists and hunters for their hardy properties. Their alchemical character makes them a sought-after, if uncommon, ingredient in the preparation of various mixtures.
topic_desc_basic: Ironwood nuts are seeds harvested from the ironwood tree. They are an uncommon alchemical ingredient.

title: Ius, Animal God
topic_desc: Buljursoma's treatise examines the deity Ius, God of Animals, whose statues appear throughout Valenwood, Hammerfell, and Elsweyr depicting a misshapen humanoid bearing a rod. The author recounts two traditional tales. In the first, Ius intervenes to save an ox from slaughter by consuming the offending farmer, thereafter carrying scales whose significance worshippers themselves cannot explain. In the second, a wombat sacred to Ius grants a cruel lord's wish by conjuring a permanent equipment store before his palace gate in Rockcreek, driving the royal family to madness. Buljursoma adopts a wry, credulous tone, citing personal acquaintance with a raccoon who conversed with the ox. The work blends folk tradition with eccentric asides, preserving regional animal-god mythology in a form both devotional and satirical.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Buljursoma recounting tales of Ius, God of Animals, whose statues are found throughout Valenwood, Hammerfell, and Elsweyr. The work preserves traditional stories of Ius's interventions on behalf of animals and explores the mysterious scales he is depicted carrying.

title: Ivory
topic_desc: Ivory is a hard, pale material obtained from the tusks of mammoths, large fauna native to Skyrim. Prized by alchemists and hunters alike, it serves as a useful ingredient in alchemical preparations. Its natural origin and distinct properties make it a valued commodity in regions where mammoths roam.
topic_desc_basic: Ivory is a pale, hard material harvested from the tusks of mammoths, which are found in Skyrim. It is commonly used in alchemy.

title: Jade
topic_desc: Jade is a green crystal valued for jewelry and enchantment, particularly in enhancing armor. In alchemy, both jade and jade dust serve as functional reagents. The Bosmer employ jade for practical and sacred objects, including corkscrew handles and statuettes of the Green Lady, while the Silvenar uses jade inkwells to hold the green iridescent ink for official decrees. The Sul-Xan fashion their armors from jade. The legendary Necromancer's Amulet famously incorporates a jade skull.
topic_desc_basic: Jade is a green crystal commonly used in jewelry and to enhance armor enchantments. It also sees use in alchemy.

title: Jadescales
topic_desc: Jadescales are the scales of the Jade Hornfish, an aquatic creature. Alchemists value these scales for their inherent properties, and hunters may procure them from the fish. The ingredient circulates through general trade and randomized supplies rather than from any guaranteed source.
topic_desc_basic: Jadescales are scales harvested from the Jade Hornfish. They are used in alchemy and are typically found through general trade or random supplies rather than from any reliable source.

title: Jarmush Leaves
topic_desc: Jarmush leaves are a botanical alchemical ingredient harvested from the jarmush plant. Their specific alchemical properties are known to practitioners, though the plant is not widely cultivated and yields no guaranteed harvest sites, making the leaves relatively uncommon. They are typically sourced through chance foraging or from randomized ingredient supplies rather than dedicated cultivation.
topic_desc_basic: Jarmush leaves are a plant ingredient used in alchemy. They are not widely cultivated and must typically be foraged or found through chance rather than reliable harvests.

title: Jet
topic_desc: Jet is a rough, dark gemstone born from decaying wood subjected to intense pressure. It possesses a mixed set of alchemical properties. Beyond its alchemical utility, jet holds cultural significance; enchanted specimens occasionally emit a soft weeping sound when exposed to light, a quality that makes them especially favored among worshippers of Nocturnal, the Daedric Prince of darkness, night, and thievery. The common phrase 'jet black' derives from the stone's deep hue, used to describe the shade of materials like ebony and onyx.
topic_desc_basic: Jet is a rough, dark gemstone formed from decaying wood under high pressure. It has a mixed set of alchemical properties and gives its name to the phrase 'jet black.'

title: Jokes!
topic_desc: A ribald collection of jokes by Butha Sunhous that satirizes the cultural stereotypes and rivalries of Tamriel's peoples.
topic_desc_basic: A ribald joke book by Butha Sunhous poking fun at the cultural stereotypes of Tamriel's races.

title: Julianite Number-Spells
topic_desc: Julianite Number-Spells is a mystical treatise that assigns symbolic and cosmological meaning to the numbers one through eight. It presents a numerological framework of existence, beginning with the singular self and progressing through dualities of fear and endeavor, the tripartite nature of fear, and the four striving elements. It catalogs five historical betrayals of mortals, identifies six forces that drive the world's engine, lists seven mysteries that defy the fixed nature of reality, and outlines eight components of mortal inheritance culminating in the word of knowing. The work reflects a Julianite philosophical viewpoint, employing esoteric numerology to explore mortal condition, cosmic mechanics, and the path to understanding.
topic_desc_basic: Julianite Number-Spells is a mystical text that assigns symbolic meaning to the numbers one through eight, outlining a numerological framework of mortal existence, cosmic forces, and esoteric mysteries from a Julianite perspective.

title: Kagouti Meat
topic_desc: Kagouti meat is harvested from the kagouti, a large predatory reptile of Morrowind. The flesh is notably chewy and sinewy, characterized by a strong odor and an acrid taste that limits its culinary appeal. Despite its harsh qualities, a single slain kagouti yields sufficient meat to sustain a family for several days, making it a practical food source. Additionally, kagouti heads serve as prized trophies, ensuring the creature's steady status as a game animal among hunters.
topic_desc_basic: Kagouti meat comes from the kagouti, a large reptilian predator. Though the flesh is chewy, sinewy, and has a strong odor and acrid taste, a single kagouti provides enough meat to feed a family for days, and their heads make good trophies, so they are widely hunted as game.

title: Kamal Bone Fragment
topic_desc: A bone fragment recovered from the colossal skeleton of the Akaviri warlord Ada'Soom Dir-Kamal, who invaded Morrowind during the late Second Era. According to Tribunal legend, Almalexia defeated the Kamal army by summoning the spirit of King Wulfharth, and the receding waters Vivec used to flood the land swept the invaders beneath the earth. The corpse's exact location remains a closely-guarded Temple secret. This fragment was purchased by the College in 392. Many similar fragments exist among mystics, collectors, and Almalexia's cult. While distinguishing fact from myth proves difficult, physical analysis confirms the material originated from a living being of colossal scale.
topic_desc_basic: A bone fragment from the colossal skeleton of the Akaviri warlord Ada'Soom Dir-Kamal, who invaded Morrowind in the late Second Era. The corpse's location is a Tribunal Temple secret, though many fragments circulate among collectors and devotees of Almalexia.

title: Khajiit-Eye
topic_desc: The Khajiit-Eye is a semi-precious, chatoyant gemstone whose cat's-eye luster recalls the Khajiit. Most specimens are recovered from the desert sands of Elsweyr, reinforcing the folk association. Though valued as a minor gem, its principal interest to alchemists lies in its ground form: once reduced to powder, the stone exhibits magical properties of practical use in alchemical preparations. The stone is not known to circulate through common trade channels in any systematic way, and specimens encountered in Morrowind are typically held in private collections, ancestral tombs, or institutional stores rather than openly marketed.
topic_desc_basic: Khajiit-Eye is a semi-precious, chatoyant gemstone found mainly in the desert sands of Elsweyr. Its cat's-eye appearance lends it the name. When ground into powder, it is valued by alchemists for its magical qualities.

title: King Bolete
topic_desc: King Boletes are large brown mushrooms found growing in the Grey Plains region of Skyrim. They are valued as alchemical ingredients by those who gather fungi in the northern wilds.
topic_desc_basic: King Boletes are large brown mushrooms that grow in the Grey Plains region of Skyrim. They are known as a useful alchemical ingredient.

title: King Edward, Part I
topic_desc: An anonymous chronicle of the legendary King Edward's early life. Set before the Septim Empire and the Redguard arrival in Hammerfell, it follows Prince Edward of Daggerfall, the neglected son of King Corcyr I and Queen Aliera of Wayrest. The narrative recounts his encounter with the so-called witch-king Moraelyn, the ArchMagister I'ric Harad Egun, and the dragon Akatosh. These figures, claiming the dragon's sanction, convince the boy to depart his home on the dragon's back to prepare for a royal destiny, promising his return. The tale touches upon questions of Edward's paternity, Aliera's willing departure with Moraelyn, and the role of extraordinary beings in mortal affairs, establishing a foundational myth of the future monarch.
topic_desc_basic: A legendary account of the youth of King Edward, a prince of Daggerfall who departed his home aboard a dragon alongside the elf Moraelyn and the ArchMagister I'ric Harad Egun to prepare for his royal destiny.

title: King Edward, Part II
topic_desc: King Edward, Part II is the second volume of a historical narrative chronicling the life of a long-ago king. This chapter depicts Prince Edward's arrival in the Elven homeland on the dragon Akatosh alongside Moraelyn, the Dark Elf King of Ebonheart. At Firsthold, Edward reunites with his mother, Queen Aliera, who abandoned his father, King Corcyr of Daggerfall. Aliera recounts her arranged marriage, her emotional neglect, and how Moraelyn's diplomatic mission for Wrothgarian ebony mining led to a duel challenge from the drunken Corcyr. She chose to flee with Moraelyn to spare her brother or husband from death, leaving Edward behind because Moraelyn refused to part a father and son. The work explores conflicting perspectives on truth, duty, and the complex familial and political tensions between Bretons and Dark Elves.
topic_desc_basic: King Edward, Part II is the second volume of a story about a long-ago king. It recounts Prince Edward's reunion with his mother, Queen Aliera, in the Elven homeland, where she explains why she left his father for the Dark Elf King Moraelyn.

title: King Edward, Part III
topic_desc: King Edward, Part III is the third installment of the lengthy historical narrative chronicling the life of a long-ago king. This section, titled 'Lessons,' depicts young Prince Edward's time living among Moraelyn's Companions, a diverse band including a Khajiit, Wood Elves, a Nord formerly enslaved, and an Argonian. The work portrays Edward's cultural education as he sheds High Rock aristocratic assumptions about servitude and labor. Through episodes such as carrying hunted game and witnessing Moraelyn's purchase and liberation of the Nord Mats near Reich Parthkeep, the text contrasts Daggerfall's rigid hierarchies with the Companions' egalitarian camaraderie. The narrative also highlights Moraelyn's protective use of magic and the Ebony Blade when Edward provokes a wild sow, reinforcing the bond between the dark elf and the prince.
topic_desc_basic: King Edward, Part III is the third part of a legendary biography of a long-ago king. This chapter, called 'Lessons,' recounts young Prince Edward's time living with Moraelyn and his diverse Companions, where he learns to abandon his High Rock assumptions about servants and labor.

title: King Edward, Part IV
topic_desc: The fourth volume of the lengthy historical romance King Edward, covering the youth of the long-ago King Edward. This chapter presents a conversation between the young prince and the Companion Mith while the two are left behind in Firsthold. Mith recounts his mixed Nord and Dark Elf heritage in Blacklight and the incident in which he first met Moraelyn, involving a stolen pouch and a flight from city guards. Mith also describes Moraelyn's unconventional entry into the Crystal Tower, where he overcame the mages' magical assaults by employing an absorption technique learned from the Wood Elf Willow, ultimately persuading the Archmagister to accept non-High Elf students and specimens into the institution.
topic_desc_basic: The fourth volume of the historical romance King Edward, recounting the youth of a long-ago king. In this part, the young prince converses with the Companion Mith, who shares stories of his origins and how Moraelyn first gained entry for non-High Elves into the Crystal Tower.

title: King Edward, Part IX
topic_desc: The ninth installment of the King Edward series, attributed to an anonymous author. This chapter, titled Luck, continues the journey of the Breton prince Edward and his Dark Elf companion Moraelyn. After a card game, the Nord companion Mats recounts the nature of Sai, the God of Luck, explaining that unlike other deities who reward structured worship, Sai's favor is capricious and finite. Mats describes Sai's Affliction, a destructive compulsion for constant proof of the god's favor that drove his father to ruin, slavery, and suicide. The chapter also begins a tale about a widow named Josea encountering a wolf and a mysterious grey-cloaked figure during a blizzard, illustrating Sai's intervention.
topic_desc_basic: A book in the King Edward series. This chapter follows the Breton prince Edward as his companion Mats explains the nature of Sai, the God of Luck, and the dangers of Sai's Affliction, before beginning a story about a widow in a blizzard.

title: King Edward, Part V
topic_desc: The fifth chapter of the serialized historical romance 'King Edward,' recounting the young Breton Edward's arrival at the Crystal Tower on Summerset Isle in the company of the Dark Elf Moraelyn. The narrative describes the Tower's white luminous interior, its troll guards, caged creatures, and enigmatic talking doors. Edward is received by the Archmagister, who dismisses Moraelyn and begins the boy's magical instruction. The chapter's central concern is philosophical: through dialogue on good, evil, and the nature of the unicorn, the Archmagister challenges Edward's inherited moral assumptions and addresses the boy's profound loneliness. Edward proves adept at fire and shield magic but cannot master healing. The work is attributed to an anonymous author and forms part of a longer cycle treating the life of a long-ago king of Daggerfall.
topic_desc_basic: The fifth part of a serialized tale about a long-ago king named Edward. It recounts the young Edward's entry into the Crystal Tower on Summerset Isle alongside the Dark Elf Moraelyn, his reception by the Archmagister, and early lessons in magic and the nature of good and evil.

title: King Edward, Part VI
topic_desc: Part six of an anonymous multi-volume romance chronicling the life of a long-ago king. This chapter, titled 'Training,' follows young Edward's departure from the Archmagister's Tower after completing his magical novitiate. The elf Moraelyn equips him with gifts including the ebony dagger Tooth and a Companions belt bearing the black rose of Morrowind. During a sparring session Edward lashes out in frustration and nearly severs Moraelyn's wrist, an act that precipitates a discussion on the nature of Daedra. Moraelyn explains that Daedra feed on destructive impulses, connect to all mortals, and grant power that demands disciplined control lest the host lose all will to choose otherwise. The chapter also explores Edward's declaration that Moraelyn is his true father and the moral weight of wielding magical ability. The series circulates widely across Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: A widely circulated Tamrielic romance, part six of an anonymous series on the life of a long-ago king. This chapter depicts the young Edward's departure from magical training, a violent sparring accident with the elf Moraelyn, and a philosophical discussion on Daedra and moral responsibility.

title: King Edward, Part VII
topic_desc: The seventh installment of the King Edward series, an anonymous historical romance recounting the life of a long-ago king. This chapter features Mith recounting to young Edward how Moraelyn, Mats, and he traveled to Fang Lair in Hammerfell's Dragon's Teeth Mountains. Lured by a gambled map promising a legendary healing blade and mithril, the companions instead discovered a live golden dragon hoarding treasure atop an ebony sword. The narrative highlights Moraelyn's composure and cunning as he bargains with the beast, which suffers an abscessed tooth, while Mats demonstrates Nord loyalty by refusing to abandon his companion. The tale provides a romanticized glimpse into the early adventures of Moraelyn's companions and the origins of Edward's dagger hilt.
topic_desc_basic: The seventh part of the King Edward series, an anonymous tale about a long-ago king. In this chapter, Mith tells Edward how he, Moraelyn, and Mats discovered a golden dragon at the Dwarven mine of Fang Lair and how Moraelyn bargained with the beast.

title: King Edward, Part VIII
topic_desc: King Edward, Part VIII is the eighth chapter of an anonymous historical romance recounting the life of a long-ago king. This installment follows Edward, the Dark Elf Moraelyn, and their Companions as they travel northward through Valenwood into Wilderland, a lawless border region where no king's writ runs and all races of Tamriel clash. Denied entry to a human-only town, the party shelters with an elderly woman who reveals that a local baron holds her granddaughter in cruel captivity. Aliera, Moraelyn's wife, interprets a storm and the proximity of the star Zenithar as a divine summons and leads a night raid on the baron's keep to rescue the girl. The chapter explores themes of moral obligation in lawless lands, the limits of vigilante justice, and the interplay of divine guidance with personal action.
topic_desc_basic: King Edward, Part VIII is part of an anonymous saga chronicling the life of a long-ago king. This chapter follows Edward and the Dark Elf Moraelyn's Companions through Wilderland, a lawless region where no king's authority holds. There they shelter with an elderly woman and undertake a raid on a baron's keep to rescue her captive granddaughter.

title: King Edward, Part X
topic_desc: The tenth installment of the *King Edward* series, continuing the tale of the mortal Sai, the god of luck. The chapter recounts how Sai—called Lucky—neglected his divine mandate to distribute fortune across Tamriel after settling with his wife Josea in Skyrim. His prolonged presence brought disproportionate prosperity to the Nords under High King Vrage the Gifted, while Morrowind and High Rock suffered conquest and the ice elves perished entirely. Confronted by Mara, Ebonarm, and the elven god Jephre, Sai is condemned to abandon his mortal family and redress the imbalance. Mara permits him one immaterial night with his descendants each year and grants him the ability to assume wolf form, explaining the Nordic taboo against harming wolves. The narrative also addresses the Dark Elf resistance to Nordic occupation, noting that figures like Moraelyn's father turned to raiding only after being driven from their homeland.
topic_desc_basic: The tenth part of the *King Edward* story, recounting how the god of luck, Sai, neglected his duties to remain with his mortal wife in Skyrim. His inattention caused the Nords to prosper while other peoples suffered, leading the gods to force him to leave and restore balance across Tamriel.

title: King Edward, Part XI
topic_desc: King Edward, Part XI is the eleventh installment of an anonymous historical epic recounting the life of a long-ago king. This chapter follows the Companions as they journey through the Wrothgarian Mountains to a multi-racial settlement founded by the dragon Akatosh. Akatosh explains that he established the village to break the racial stasis and isolation dragons fell into after their futile resistance to the Aurielian gods. The narrative explores how innate behavior patterns particularly hinder long-lived species, with the elf Moraelyn noting that such rigidity makes elves resist change and dragons breed slowly. Akatosh details the settlement's pragmatic economy: elven smiths train Breton settlers, mithril is sold to Nordic nobility, and mining tunnels provide dragons access to their hidden lairs. The chapter highlights the philosophical differences between dragons and humanoids, culminating in their inability to agree on a name for the village.
topic_desc_basic: King Edward, Part XI is part of an anonymous epic about a long-ago king. This chapter recounts the Companions' visit to a multi-racial village in the Wrothgarian Mountains founded by the dragon Akatosh, who seeks to end dragon isolation and stasis. It explores the innate behavioral rigidity of long-lived races and the settlement's integrated economy of elven smiths, Breton miners, and dragons.

title: King Edward, Part XII
topic_desc: The twelfth part of the *King Edward* series records a philosophical discourse among Edward, the dragon Akatosh, Moraelyn, and their companions concerning the nature of divinity. The participants debate whether gods possess inherent natures unlike the Daedra, the necessity of worshippers for divine sustenance, and whether great deeds, innate soul capacity, or localities can produce deities. Moraelyn suggests that establishing a temple cult alone cannot create a god without some preexisting godly essence, while Akatosh questions whether mortals can truly distinguish a god from a powerful being. The dialogue also introduces theological theories on Magicka as the power of existence, which worship converts into divine energy, and touches upon the relationship between gods, Daedra, and mortal magic use.
topic_desc_basic: The twelfth part of the *King Edward* series, presenting a philosophical debate among the story's characters regarding the nature of the gods, the necessity of worshippers, and the origins of divine power.

title: King Helseth, A Biography
topic_desc: A hagiographic biography by Ervil Hlaalu recounting King Hlaalu Helseth's life from his birth in 3E 376 through his coronation, portraying him as a scholarly, cosmopolitan savior of Morrowind while deflecting accusations of political machinations and poisoning rivals in Wayrest.
topic_desc_basic: A biography by Ervil Hlaalu celebrating King Hlaalu Helseth's life and rise to the throne of Morrowind, presenting him as a learned and capable ruler.

title: King of Rats
topic_desc: The King of Rats is a unique enchanted helm associated with Ungolfin, the so-called Rat King, who dwells within Ilu-Shuma Egg Mine. Beyond its magical enchantments, the helm possesses the distinctive property of pacifying ordinary rats, preventing them from attacking the wearer. This ward offers no protection against diseased variants of the creatures, however. The helm's origin and the source of its command over vermin remain obscure, though its connection to Ungolfin suggests a specialized purpose tied to the control of the mine's rodent inhabitants.
topic_desc_basic: The King of Rats is a unique enchanted helm worn by Ungolfin the Rat King in Ilu-Shuma Egg Mine. It magically prevents ordinary rats from attacking the wearer, though diseased variants are unaffected.

title: King Orgnum's Coffer
topic_desc: King Orgnum's Coffer is a legendary magical chest, small and ordinary-looking but weightless, once owned by King Orgnum of Pyandonea. Under his control, it manifested an unlimited supply of gold. King Orgnum lost the coffer in a battle against Emperor Antiochus Septim during the War of the Isle, and without this endless wealth, Pyandonea lost much of its military power. The coffer washed up in the Summerset Isles and has become an elusive artifact ever since. In the absence of its original master, it produces a random number of gold coins once per day. It is said that when found, the coffer always disappears again, though not before generating enormous wealth for its owner; where and why it vanishes remains a mystery. It was last seen in the hands of the Eternal Champion.
topic_desc_basic: King Orgnum's Coffer is a legendary magical chest that once belonged to the King of Pyandonea. It is said to generate gold and is known to vanish and reappear throughout Tamriel.

title: King Thistle Flower
topic_desc: The King Thistle Flower is a botanical ingredient harvested from the king thistle plant. While its specific alchemical properties remain a subject for specialist study, the flower is recognized in botanical and alchemical circles for its utility in potion-crafting. The plant is known to grow in Skyrim and regions sharing similar climates, where it is gathered by hunters and herbalists. It is also distributed in general ingredient supplies.
topic_desc_basic: The King Thistle Flower is a plant ingredient gathered from the king thistle. It grows in Skyrim and similar regions, where it is commonly harvested for use in alchemy.

title: Knowing Your Place
topic_desc: An instructional letter by the guild master Ernestus Abertus, published by the University of Gwylim Press, arguing that magical success depends on understanding the contextual appropriateness of time and place rather than willpower alone. Abertus critiques mages who ignore spatial and temporal propriety—such as performing transformation rituals amid ancient ruins—and illustrates his thesis through Daedric summoning. While traditional summoning dates are widely known, he contends that the specific location and its contextual alignment determine whether a ritual succeeds or ends in catastrophe. Using Sheogorath as an example, he argues that a humble, contextually resonant location like a shoe in a storm may prove more inviting to the Prince of Madness than a grand shrine. The letter concludes with an editor's note observing that Abertus vanished during subsequent travels, leaving his ultimate fate uncertain.
topic_desc_basic: An instructional letter by guild master Ernestus Abertus, published by the University of Gwylim Press, teaching that successful magic and Daedric summoning require understanding the contextual alignment of time and place rather than relying on willpower alone.

title: Kobold Tongue
topic_desc: Kobold Tongue is the severed tongue of the Kobold, a gray-skinned goblinkin race found throughout Tamriel. As an alchemical ingredient, it is harvested from these creatures for its intrinsic properties. Its extraction and preparation require familiarity with the anatomy of goblinkin, making it a specialized resource sought by alchemists and hunters who process such fauna.
topic_desc_basic: Kobold Tongue is an alchemical ingredient taken from the Kobold, a gray race of goblinkin found across Tamriel.

title: Kuj Sprout Pulp
topic_desc: Kuj Sprout Pulp is harvested from Kuj Sprouts, a small plant commonly found both growing wild and cultivated on farms in the Othreleth Woods of Morrowind. The pulp is used as an alchemical ingredient, and its natural availability in the region makes it a familiar resource to local herbalists and gatherers.
topic_desc_basic: Kuj Sprout Pulp is gathered from Kuj Sprouts, a small plant found wild and farmed in the Othreleth Woods of Morrowind. It is used in alchemy.

title: Kwama Chitin
topic_desc: Kwama chitin consists of the hard shell pieces found within molted kwama husks. While commonly encountered by those who work among kwama, such as miners and hunters, the material holds little value for the practiced alchemist. Its intrinsic properties are functionally useless for creating potions, rendering it a mundane byproduct of the kwama life cycle rather than a viable reagent. Consequently, it sees no meaningful application in legitimate alchemical practice.
topic_desc_basic: Kwama chitin is the shell found in molted kwama husks. It is a common but alchemically useless ingredient.

title: Kwama Meat
topic_desc: Kwama meat is obtained from kwama warriors culled from egg mines. When a mine's warrior population grows too large, the oldest and weakest are slaughtered and their meat roasted. It is regarded as a feast treat, prized for its naturally acid and spicy flavor. Beyond its culinary value, kwama meat possesses modest magical qualities that make it of interest to alchemists as well as cooks. The practice of culling excess warriors provides a practical source of sustenance from the kwama mining industry native to Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: Kwama meat comes from kwama warriors slaughtered when egg mines become overpopulated. It is roasted and served as a festive dish, known for its acid and spicy taste.

title: Kwoom Egg
topic_desc: Kwoom eggs are laid by the sand kwoom, a creature native to Morrowind. Foragers discover them within eggsacks, a reproductive structure comparable to those of kwama. As an alchemical ingredient, the egg possesses properties of interest to practitioners, though its occurrence is sporadic and it yields no guaranteed harvest from any particular site.
topic_desc_basic: Kwoom eggs come from the sand kwoom, a creature native to Morrowind. They are found within eggsacks, similar to kwama eggs.

title: Kwoom Fronds
topic_desc: Kwoom Fronds are the fibrous fur strands that grow between the chitin plates of the Sand Kwoom. Among the Shinathi clans of Morrowind, these fronds serve as a practical material and a food source.
