Alchemists value them for their inherent properties, and hunters harvest them from the creatures in the arid regions the Sand Kwoom inhabits.
topic_desc_basic: Kwoom Fronds are the fur strands growing between the chitin plates of the Sand Kwoom. The Shinathi clans of Morrowind use them as a material and food source.

title: Lady's Mantle Leaves
topic_desc: Lady's Mantle Leaves are the green leaves harvested from the Lady's Mantle plant. The flora grows commonly across the Strident Coast, the Brennan Bluffs, and Stirk Isle in Cyrodiil. Alchemists value the leaves for their properties in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Lady's Mantle Leaves are green leaves taken from the Lady's Mantle plant, which grows commonly on the Strident Coast, the Brennan Bluffs, and Stirk Isle in Cyrodiil.

title: Lady's Smock Leaves
topic_desc: Lady's Smock Leaves are gathered from Lady's Smock, a common garden flower cultivated throughout Cyrodiil. The plant's familiar blossoms make it a recognizable sight in both tended gardens and wild growth across the heartland province. Alchemists value the leaves for their properties in potion-making, and the plant's prevalence ensures steady availability for practitioners of the craft. The leaves are also distributed through general ingredient supply channels in Cyrodiilic regions.
topic_desc_basic: Lady's Smock Leaves are taken from Lady's Smock, a common garden flower found throughout Cyrodiil. The leaves are used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Lament for Pelinal
topic_desc: A poetic work attributed to the bull-god Morihaus, mourning his companion Pelinal Whitestrake after a battle during the Alessian Rebellion. Scholars debate whether the text properly belongs within the fragmentary volumes of The Song of Pelinal or Morihaus's own memoir, The Adabal-a, as both works celebrate the deep affection between these immortals. Regardless of its origin, the lament has fallen into relative obscurity, surviving primarily in secondary sources concerning the rebellion. The poem depicts Morihaus arriving at the site where alien kings have left Pelinal partitioned and dying, expressing profound grief and a desperate desire to contain every piece of his fallen companion. Morihaus questions the cosmic forces that set them upon their path, contemplating whether his own sacrifice could restore Pelinal from his pallid state.
topic_desc_basic: A poetic lament attributed to the bull-god Morihaus for his companion Pelinal Whitestrake. Associated with the Alessian Rebellion, it survives in secondary sources as scholars debate whether it belongs to The Song of Pelinal or The Adabal-a.

title: Lamia Hair
topic_desc: Lamia Hair is an alchemical ingredient harvested from the bodies of deceased lamias. These powerful, aquatic creatures inhabit the Abecean Sea, making the hair a resource primarily associated with the western waters of Tamriel. The ingredient's properties make it a subject of interest for practitioners of alchemy, and it circulates in trade through general and regional ingredient supply lists.
topic_desc_basic: Lamia Hair is an alchemical ingredient harvested from dead lamias, powerful aquatic creatures found mostly in the Abecean Sea.

title: Lamp Knight
topic_desc: The Lamp Knights are an order within the Mages Guild tasked with protective and surveillance duties for the faction. Stationed at guild halls, they monitor local threats and track individuals suspected of hostile sympathies, such as worship of Mehrunes Dagon or Tharnite allegiance. Their assignments are considered sensitive; details are typically restricted to guild leadership and withheld from lower-ranking members. A Lamp Knight's mandate includes watching persons of interest and defending guild property, operating under the authority of local guild guides.
topic_desc_basic: Lamp Knights are Mages Guild members who protect guild halls and monitor potential threats. Their assignments are sensitive and typically kept secret from lower-ranking members.

title: Lamplight
topic_desc: Lamplight is a resinous substance harvested from skylamps. Alchemists value it for its peculiar properties, though its availability depends on the collection of resin from these creatures.
topic_desc_basic: Lamplight is a resinous substance harvested from skylamps. It is known among alchemists and hunters as a useful ingredient.

title: Lapis Lazuli
topic_desc: Lapis lazuli is a deep-blue semi-precious stone valued as an alchemical ingredient. The mineral is sourced from subterranean ore deposits and occasionally appears among random gem and mineral collections. Alchemists prize the stone for its properties, though its specific alchemical effects require specialist knowledge to elicit. Its striking color also makes it a recognized ornamental gem.
topic_desc_basic: Lapis lazuli is a deep-blue semi-precious stone and alchemical ingredient obtained from ore deposits.

title: Large Spider
topic_desc: Large spiders are sizable predatory arachnids found across Tamriel. They inhabit caves, mines, and forested regions, spinning webs to ensnare prey. Their venom poses a significant hazard to travelers and hunters traversing their territories. These creatures are recognized for their robust size and aggressive territorial behavior, making them a durable danger in the wilds.
topic_desc_basic: Large spiders are sizable predatory arachnids that inhabit caves and wilderness areas across Tamriel. They spin webs and use venom to subdue their prey, posing a notable danger to travelers.

title: Lavender
topic_desc: Lavender is a purple flower occasionally cultivated in Cyrodiilic gardens. Alchemists prize it as a benign and inexpensive reagent for brewing potions of magicka restoration and spell reflection, offering these properties without the adverse side effects or prohibitive cost associated with rarer ingredients such as frost salts or diamonds.
topic_desc_basic: Lavender is a purple flower occasionally found in gardens in Cyrodiil.

title: Lead Ore
topic_desc: Lead ore is a mineral substance occasionally unearthed through mining across Tamriel. Alchemists value it as an ingredient for its inherent properties, which are drawn out through preparation rather than metallurgical refinement. It is typically sourced from mineral deposits and appears in trade among those who gather such resources.
topic_desc_basic: Lead ore is a mineral ingredient obtained from mining deposits. It is used in alchemy.

title: Leaper Tail
topic_desc: Leaper tails are ingredients harvested from the fringed leaper, a species of freshwater fish native to the Strident Coast and Dasek Marsh in Cyrodiil. Valued by alchemists and hunters alike, the tail possesses distinct alchemical properties that make it a useful component in potion-making. Its availability is tied to the aquatic fauna of the Cyrodiilic wetlands, where the fringed leaper thrives in its freshwater habitat.
topic_desc_basic: Leaper tails are taken from the fringed leaper, a freshwater fish found in the Strident Coast and Dasek Marsh regions of Cyrodiil. They are used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Leek
topic_desc: Leeks are vegetables found growing across Cyrodiil and Skyrim. They serve as common foodstuffs and are occasionally utilized in alchemical preparations, though their alchemical properties remain a matter of specialist study rather than general knowledge.
topic_desc_basic: Leeks are vegetables commonly found across Cyrodiil and Skyrim, widely used as food.

title: Legal Basics
topic_desc: A legal treatise by Anchivius, M.Z.F., summarizing the most universal crimes and their punishments across the Empire. The work covers offenses such as breaking and entering, trespassing, assault, murder, criminal conspiracy, vagrancy, smuggling, high treason, pickpocketing, and theft. Anchivius notes that both definitions and punishments vary by location and situation, observing that legal counsel exists in the Imperial City but not in the provinces. The text concludes by grounding the Tamrielic legal system in the First Era prophet Marukh's maxim that all are guilty until proven innocent.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise by Anchivius, M.Z.F., outlining universal Imperial crimes and their punishments, from trespassing and theft to high treason. It notes that local laws vary and that legal counsel is unavailable outside the Imperial City.

title: Lesser Catechism of Julianos
topic_desc: A catechism of the Julianos faith presenting its core theological principles through a question-and-answer format. The work defines Julianos's domain as Wisdom and Logic, characterizing Wisdom as the perception of true nature and Logic as the path from ignorance to knowledge. It teaches that mortals employ these gifts to establish and maintain Law, which it defines as the functional order of the world. The text asserts that Law permeates all things, governing both natural phenomena and civil authority, and can be determined through observation and the declarations of rulers.
topic_desc_basic: A religious text outlining the domain of Julianos, the god of Wisdom and Logic, and explaining how mortals use these gifts to establish and maintain the Law that governs the world.

title: Lex Imperii I
topic_desc: Lex Imperii I is the foundational legal text of the Cyrodiilic Empire, establishing the sacred and reciprocal bond between Imperial law and the rule of the Emperors Cyrodiil. The code defines the rights and duties of Imperial citizens, explicitly tying the exercise of civil rights to caste, race, and inherent nobility as governed by the Provincial Codices. It grants citizenship to those born across Tamriel and its protectorates upon reaching majority, while extending reciprocal rights to foreign strangers by treaty or grace. Denizens of Oblivion, termed Outsiders of the Principalities, are explicitly excluded from civil rights. The text further outlines how citizenship is forfeited through naturalization, military service, or settlement in foreign or extramundial territories without intent to return, though mercantile activities abroad are protected. The Emperor or ennobled representatives retain the authority to restore lost citizenship.
topic_desc_basic: Lex Imperii I is a foundational Imperial legal code declaring the sacred authority of the Emperors Cyrodiil and defining the rights and duties of Imperial citizens. It establishes that civil rights are governed by caste, race, and nobility, grants citizenship to those born across Tamriel upon reaching majority, and outlines the conditions under which citizenship may be lost or restored.

title: Lex Imperii II
topic_desc: Lex Imperii II is the second part of the Lex Imperii legal codex, governing civil acts and declarations before Imperial authorities. It mandates that Imperial records declare the year, day, and identities of involved parties, and that warrants be glyph-marked for Elder Scroll traceability and deposited in the Concordian Archives. The text regulates nascency, requiring birth declarations within five days, including birthsign and parentage, with provisions for orphans and births at sea or on starlit sojourn. Marriage may proceed by Citizen consent or before a Deity or Spirit of proven Marital Disposition, represented by knowledgeable ecclesiastics, with declarations made within three days. Decease regulations prohibit burial without an Executor's authority, require two witnesses for death acts, and detail procedures for suspicious deaths and the disposal of unclaimed prisoner remains, which may be sold to accredited parties. Separate provisions govern civil acts for the Legion in provincial territories.
topic_desc_basic: Lex Imperii II is a volume of Imperial law governing civil acts and declarations. It codifies procedures for recording births, marriages, and deaths before Imperial authorities, including specific rules for Legion personnel in provincial territories and the proper archiving of legal warrants.

title: Lex Imperii III
topic_desc: Lex Imperii III is the third volume of the Lex Imperii, a multi-part Imperial legal code. It addresses civil law concerning domicile, defining how Imperial citizens establish and change their principal place of establishment, and the classification of property into immovable, movable, and arcane categories. Detailed provisions govern each class: immovable property by nature, destination, or application; movable property by nature or by determination of law; and arcane property, which is neither movable nor immovable by nature but classified by legal determination. The arcane category addresses magical alteration of property, including buildings reduced in size, folded, or transferred to private realms, with classification depending on the method of accession. The code's systematic structure reflects classical civil law traditions applied to the governance of citizens' rights and holdings across Imperial provinces.
topic_desc_basic: Lex Imperii III is the third part of an Imperial legal code addressing civil law. It defines rules for citizens' domicile and classifies all property as immovable, movable, or arcane, with provisions for how magical effects alter property status under Imperial law.

title: Lex Imperii IV
topic_desc: Lex Imperii IV is the fourth volume of the Imperial legal code. It codifies the rights of accession, defining private citizen property, Imperial Executor administration of non-private holdings, and the Emperor's domain over highways, waterways, shores, fortresses, unclaimed estates, and ownerless property. It further establishes the rights of usufruct, commons, and habitation, permitting citizens to enjoy the advantage of another's property—movable, immovable, or arcane—provided the property's substance is preserved. These rights require security and inventory, cannot be ceded or hired without authorization, and restrict commonage exploitation to personal and familial necessity. Wilderness commonage remains subject to particular law or the Emperor's will. The volume is a foundational statement of Imperial property principles.
topic_desc_basic: Lex Imperii IV is part of the Imperial legal code governing property law. It defines the rights of accession, distinguishing private citizen holdings from the Emperor's domain over roads, waterways, fortresses, and unclaimed property, and establishes the rights of usufruct, commons, and habitation over such property.

title: Lex Imperii V
topic_desc: Lex Imperii V is the fifth volume of the Lex Imperii, the legal codex governing the Empire. This installment addresses manorial services and servitude, defining the charges imposed upon one estate for the benefit of another. It establishes that servitude does not confer preeminence and arises from natural conditions, legal obligations, or citizen agreements. The text regulates water rights, stipulating that lower estates must receive natural waterflow, while proprietors may use springs and bordering waterways provided they do not befoul them, diminish their course, or deprive settlements of necessary supply. Prescription is set at thirty years of uninterrupted enjoyment. Provisions also compel neighbors to share boundary-determination costs and state that enclosing an estate forfeits proportional rights to free pasturage and wilderness. The work is significant as a foundational statement of Cyrodiilic property law, balancing individual proprietorship with communal obligations.
topic_desc_basic: Lex Imperii V is the fifth volume of the Imperial legal codex. It covers manorial services and servitude, defining property charges, water rights, boundary disputes, and the forfeiture of common pasturage rights when land is enclosed.

title: Lex Imperii VI
topic_desc: The sixth volume of the Lex Imperii, an Imperial legal treatise codifying Cyrodilic civil law. This section addresses the laws of succession and donation. Succession is triggered by natural or civil death, with the order of inheritance determined by statute, the judgment of an Akatic Authority, or defaulting through natural children and surviving parents to the Emperor. Foreigners are barred from inheriting, and heirs guilty of murdering the deceased, bringing malicious capital charges, or failing to report the death are deemed unworthy. Donation is defined as an irrevocable transfer. Testaments dispose of property when the testator no longer exists upon the Arena Supermundus; permanent residence in the Principalities constitutes such cessation. A living testator may revoke their will, but one communicating through necromantic means may not. Conditions violating law or morality are void.
topic_desc_basic: The sixth volume of the Lex Imperii, which codifies Imperial civil law. It covers the laws of succession and donation, establishing the order of inheritance, barring foreigners from inheriting, and defining the irrevocable nature of gifts. It also regulates wills, noting that permanent departure from the Arena Supermundus triggers execution of a testament, while necromantic communication after death prevents revocation.

title: Lex Imperii VII
topic_desc: Lex Imperii VII is the seventh volume of the Lex Imperii, the legal code of the Empire. This installment codifies the Imperial law of commerce, detailing the binding nature of sales agreements between Citizens and the precise moment property is legally acquired. It distinguishes between absolute and conditional sales, and specifies when transactions are completed based on whether goods are sold in bulk or by weight and measure. The text also addresses the capacity to buy and sell, affirming that all Citizens not under legal interdict may engage in commerce while explicitly forbidding guardians, factors, administrators, and Imperial Executors from purchasing property under their care, on pain of nullity. The volume further establishes that any sale of property owned by another Citizen is void, reinforcing the legal framework governing Imperial trade.
topic_desc_basic: Lex Imperii VII is a volume of the Imperial legal code that codifies the laws of commerce, sales agreements, and the capacity of Citizens to buy and sell property under the Empire.

title: Lich Dust
topic_desc: Lich Dust is a rare alchemical ingredient obtained from the remains of liches. Its specific alchemical properties are known to specialists, though its extreme rarity limits widespread study. As it does not appear in common leveled lists, acquiring it typically requires direct confrontation with these powerful undead sorcerers.
topic_desc_basic: Lich Dust is a rare ingredient harvested from the remains of liches. It is highly valued by alchemists and hunters of the undead.

title: Lichdom: A Trap, an Escape
topic_desc: A scholarly treatise on the metaphysics of lichdom, arguing that traditional lich rituals are corrupted fragments of processes originally intended for attaining godhood. The anonymous author, drawing on Ancient Elven accounts acquired after Imperial library seizures during the Tiber Wars, contends that lichdom carves a metaphysical pattern into the world using a portion of the practitioner's soul. The work distinguishes two outcomes: the Common Lich, whose undirected pattern collapses upon destruction or attempted alteration, rendering immortality a trap; and the True Lich, whose pattern is tied to an external focus, permitting resurrection and the possibility of carving new patterns. The author frames lichdom through the Monomyth and the magicka patterns of Magnus, suggesting that for most practitioners the path is inescapable, while for a curious few it may serve as an escape.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise on the metaphysics of lichdom by an anonymous necromancer. It argues that traditional lich rituals are corrupted fragments of godhood-attainment processes and distinguishes between the Common Lich, whose immortality is a trap, and the True Lich, whose pattern is tied to an external focus allowing resurrection and further growth.

title: Life and the Animate
topic_desc: Saer Vacerit's treatise on Bretonnic golemworking, a magical tradition Vacerit claims is unique to High Rock. The work explains that golems are created by binding a low-level conscious entity, such as a beast animus or minor Daedra, to a construct, then enhancing it with incantations and alchemicals to transfer living energies. Vacerit categorizes golems by material as a measure of the crafter's skill: chilled mud golems, the oldest type attributed to Bjoulsae shamans; stone or clay golems with soft directive cores, first employed against Redguard invaders; and iron golems, pioneered by Gwylim scholar Anton Demerax after studying Dwemer animunculi. Vacerit separately condemns the Haemonculus, a southern witch-coven creation incorporating Daedric matter, as dangerously malicious and beyond respectable practice.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise by Saer Vacerit on the Breton art of golemworking. It explains how Bretons bind low-level entities to constructs to create living servitors, and categorizes the main types of golems by their construction materials: chilled mud, stone or clay, and iron.

title: Light Armor Repair
topic_desc: A practical guide to refurbishing light armor, distinguishing between metallic and non-metallic varieties. The work classifies chainmail, Elven, mithril, and glass as metallic armors, noting that the material called glass bears no resemblance to household window panes but is instead a strong greenish substance with a high melting point. Fur and leather are treated as non-metallic, requiring sewing kits and awls rather than hammers, with the maxim that armor should be discarded once a patch itself requires patching. For metallic armors, the text advises that Elven and mithril repair best when heated, while chainmail is sufficiently malleable cold. Glass presents the greatest challenge; hammer blows struck across the grain risk shattering the armor, so blows must align with the grain. In extreme cases, the work recommends submerging the affected piece in a tub of oil atop an anvil, allowing the oil to absorb vibrations and reduce the risk of fracture.
topic_desc_basic: A practical manual on refurbishing light armor. It divides the subject into metallic types—chainmail, Elven, mithril, and glass—and non-metallic types like fur and leather, detailing the distinct tools and techniques each requires for effective repair.

title: Liminal Bridges
topic_desc: A theoretical and practical treatise on interdimensional travel by Camilonwe of Alinor. It argues that sustained passage between Mundus and Oblivion requires a sigil stone—a pre-Mythic morpholith inscribed with a daedric sigil—to breach the liminal barrier. The work details the ritual preparation of the morpholith, the necessity of Daedric cooperation for inscription, and the activation process for a temporary portal. It emphasizes conjuration as essential and acknowledges the resulting gates are inherently brief, limiting their utility.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise by Camilonwe of Alinor on traveling between Mundus and Oblivion, detailing the theoretical and practical use of sigil stones to open temporary portals across the liminal barrier.

title: Lizardfoot Extract
topic_desc: Lizardfoot Extract is harvested from the Lizards Foot, an aquatic plant rooted in shallow waters. It grows primarily in the Druadach Highlands of Skyrim, where alchemists and hunters gather the extract for its alchemical properties. The plant's preference for marshy, highland shallows makes it a regional specialty rather than a widely distributed ingredient.
topic_desc_basic: Lizardfoot Extract comes from the Lizards Foot, a plant that grows in the shallow waters of Skyrim's Druadach Highlands.

title: Lodestone
topic_desc: Lodestones are metals possessing strong magnetic energy, capable of attracting iron, dust, and debris. They serve as essential navigational compasses for sea travel and can manipulate electricity and associated magics. The Maormer employ them extensively for seafaring and storm magic. Enchanted lodestones focus magicka over distance, form sympathetic links in pairs, and trace each other's locations. In alchemy, lodestones enhance jumping abilities. Storm atronachs occasionally yield lodestones crackling with lightning. Ancient Aldmeri waystones—crystalline spheres attuned to an unknown power that rotate on a directional axis—share a suspected kinship; historians only recently realized their navigational function. The All Flags Navy famously used enchanted lodestones to maintain fleet formation.
topic_desc_basic: Lodestones are magnetic metals that attract iron and debris. They are widely used as compasses for sea navigation and can manipulate electricity and storm magic.

title: Longbread
topic_desc: Longbread is a variety of bread common to High Rock, associated with Breton foodways. Its name denotes an elongated loaf form. As an ingredient, it serves primarily as everyday sustenance rather than a substance of notable alchemical significance. The bread is a staple provision encountered throughout the Breton homeland, representative of the grain-based dietary customs of High Rock's people.
topic_desc_basic: Longbread is a common bread found in High Rock, reflecting Breton culinary traditions. It is a widely available foodstuff throughout the region.

title: Longfin Filet
topic_desc: Longfin filet consists of strips of meat taken from the Abecean Longfin, an ocean fish commonly encountered in the Abecean Sea along Cyrodiil's western coast. The flesh is prepared as a foodstuff and circulates among coastal communities and travelers familiar with the Abecean's bounty. Fishermen regard the longfin as a staple catch, and its filets serve primarily as provisions. The ingredient holds modest alchemical character, though its chief value remains culinary rather than arcane.
topic_desc_basic: Longfin filet is a strip of fish meat cut from the Abecean Longfin, an ocean fish commonly found in the Abecean Sea near Cyrodiil. It is known as a foodstuff along the western coast.

title: Lotus Poppy Head
topic_desc: The lotus poppy head is the flowering portion of the lotus poppy, an aquatic plant native to Morrowind. As a water-dwelling flora, it is harvested for its alchemical properties by practitioners familiar with the region's wetland vegetation. Its occurrence in the wild is unpredictable, making it a somewhat uncommon ingredient for alchemical work.
topic_desc_basic: The lotus poppy head is the flowering part of a water-dwelling plant native to Morrowind, used in alchemy.

title: Lovers Rafflesia Pistil
topic_desc: The Lovers Rafflesia Pistil is the reproductive organ of the lovers rafflesia, a flower native to Morrowind. Alchemists and hunters value the harvested pistil for its intrinsic properties, which are extracted through standard preparation techniques. As the plant grows scattered across the province, the ingredient is gathered opportunistically rather than from any reliable or cultivated source.
topic_desc_basic: The Lovers Rafflesia Pistil is the reproductive organ of the lovers rafflesia flower, a plant native to Morrowind.

title: Lunar Caustic
topic_desc: Lunar Caustic is a mineral reagent valued by alchemists for its distinctive properties. Its name suggests an association with silver or moonlight, and it is typically obtained through mining rather than from flora or fauna. It is not known to circulate through common trade channels or leveled merchant stock, making it a relatively scarce material sought by practitioners of the alchemical arts.
topic_desc_basic: Lunar Caustic is a mineral ingredient prized by alchemists. It is obtained through mining and is not commonly available through general trade or merchant stock.

title: Lute Moth
topic_desc: The lute moth is an insect found in the regions of Morrowind. It is recognized for its broad, rounded wings, which bear a resemblance to the curved body of a lute. These moths are typically encountered in the wild, where they exhibit standard moth behavior, fluttering near flora and resting on surfaces. While not considered particularly dangerous, they are part of the diverse fauna that hunters and travelers encounter. Their distinct wing shape makes them one of the more visually notable moth species in the region.
topic_desc_basic: The lute moth is an insect found in Morrowind, recognized by its broad, rounded wings. It is commonly encountered in the wild by travelers.

title: Lute Moth Wing
topic_desc: Harvested from the lute moth, a winged insect native to Morrowind active during both day and night, this ingredient yields two wings from each specimen. Alchemists value the wing for its properties in potion-making, and it is commonly traded through randomized supply stocks rather than found as loose samples.
topic_desc_basic: An alchemical ingredient consisting of the wings of the lute moth, an insect found throughout Morrowind during both day and night.

title: Lycoae
topic_desc: Lycoae are small, purple vegetables that grow on vines. Cultivated on farms across Cyrodiil, they serve as both a common foodstuff and an alchemical ingredient.
topic_desc_basic: Lycoae are small, purple vegetables grown on vines. They are a common farm crop found across Cyrodiil.

title: Mace Etiquette
topic_desc: A warrior's instructional text on proper mace tactics, written by a veteran instructor. It challenges the common assumption that mace combat relies solely on brute strength and stamina, arguing instead that effective wielding depends on timing and momentum. The work details specific techniques: anticipating an opponent's backward lean to aim behind the head, keeping the ready position shoulder-high with a constrained windup, leading the swing with the elbow before extending the forearm for additional force, loosening the wrist at impact to prevent injury from the bounce, and using the weapon's natural recoil to flow into a quicker second strike.
topic_desc_basic: An instructional text by a veteran instructor on mace combat tactics, teaching that proper wielding relies on timing and momentum rather than mere strength.

title: Mace Fruit
topic_desc: Mace Fruit is harvested from mace shrubs, a plant native to Hammerfell. The fruit serves both as a foodstuff and as a gathered ingredient. While mace shrubs are predominantly associated with the Hammerfell landscape, a small number have been documented growing on Mykoi, an island off the Cyrodiil coast. The fruit's presence in common provisions and ingredient collections throughout Hammerfell reflects its recognized culinary and practical worth.
topic_desc_basic: Mace Fruit is gathered from mace shrubs, plants native to Hammerfell, where it is known as both a food and a useful ingredient.

title: Magic from the Sky
topic_desc: Irlav Jarol's treatise on Ayleid enchanted artifacts crafted from Aetherial fragments, examining Ayleid Wells, Welkynd Stones, and Varla Stones, and arguing that their creators' moral failings, not superior wisdom, enabled their craft.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise by Irlav Jarol examining Ayleid Wells, Welkynd Stones, and Varla Stones, which are enchanted artifacts crafted from fallen Aetherial fragments.

title: Malachite
topic_desc: Malachite, commonly called glass, is a rare, milky translucent green volcanic crystal. Unrelated to common brittle glass, it absorbs magicka under the right conditions and is most commonly found in Morrowind, particularly on Vvardenfell. Extracting raw glass from its hard stone matrix is arduous but profitable labor. In alchemy, raw glass serves as an ingredient. Its primary significance lies in smithing: when smelted into ingots and alloyed with moonstone, it produces lightweight armor and exceptionally sharp weapons. Only skilled glass smiths can work the material, as improper hammer blows risk shattering it. The East Empire Company holds sole Third Era trading authority over raw glass, which Imperial law declares the Emperor's property; smuggling it constitutes treason.
topic_desc_basic: Malachite, commonly called glass, is a rare, milky translucent green volcanic crystal found in Morrowind. Unrelated to common brittle glass, it is primarily smelted and alloyed with moonstone to craft lightweight, strong armor and sharp weapons. Raw glass is also used in alchemy.

title: Malahk Orc
topic_desc: The Malahk Orcs are a larger, stronger, and more aggressive Orcish people dwelling in the isolated mountainous region of Malahk-Bazul, situated between Cyrodiil, Skyrim, and Morrowind. Claiming to be the true blood of Malahk, they fiercely distinguish themselves from other Orcs—whom they dismiss as soft cowards dwelling in the cities of betrayers. Honed by relentless warfare in their rugged homeland, they are capable of entering a frenzied berserk state in combat. Their imposing stature grants formidable resilience and might, making them devastating with axes, blunt weapons, and unarmed strikes. They maintain an unyielding independence, bowing to no one and continuing to harry the betrayers beyond their mountains.
topic_desc_basic: The Malahk Orcs are a larger, stronger, and more aggressive Orcish people inhabiting the isolated mountainous region of Malahk-Bazul between Cyrodiil, Skyrim, and Morrowind. They claim descent from Malahk and fiercely reject other Orcs as soft city-dwellers.

title: Mandrake Root
topic_desc: Mandrake root is the harvested root of the mandrake plant, valued as an alchemical ingredient. It grows wild in the Dasek Marsh region of Cyrodiil and the Roth Roryn region of Morrowind, where it may be gathered by foragers familiar with those lands. Its properties make it a component of interest to alchemists working with regional flora.
topic_desc_basic: Mandrake root is the root of the mandrake plant, gathered as an alchemical ingredient. It grows in the Dasek Marsh of Cyrodiil and the Roth Roryn region of Morrowind.

title: Mannimarco, King of Worms
topic_desc: A poetic biography by Horicles chronicling Mannimarco's descent into necromancy and his war with Vanus Galerion. The work frames both figures as former Psijic students on Artaeum whose opposing philosophies led to catastrophic conflict. It portrays the Psijic Order as aloof, exiling Mannimarco to the mainland rather than ending his threat, which spurred Galerion's departure to found the Mages Guild. The narrative details Mannimarco's transformation into the first lich through accumulated cursed artifacts and foul alchemy, culminating in a devastating mountain battle where Galerion perished stripping the Worm King of his relics. The poem closes warning that Mannimarco, though diminished, survives in undeath. Its dramatic account of the Mages Guild's foundational struggle makes it a culturally significant, if lurid, historical source.
topic_desc_basic: A poetic biography by Horicles about the necromancer Mannimarco. It recounts his fall from Psijic student to the first lich, his spreading corruption across Tamriel, and his catastrophic mountain battle with Vanus Galerion, who died defeating him. The poem warns that the Worm King still lives in undeath.

title: Manual of Armor
topic_desc: The Manual of Armor is an Imperial military reference commissioned by General Warhaft to instruct all officers of the Imperial service on the selection, material, and battlefield application of armor. It categorizes armor into light and heavy types, prescribing light armor for scouts, archers, light cavalry, and skirmishers where mobility is paramount, and heavy armor for frontline infantry, pikemen, heavy cavalry, foot knights, and all officers. The manual ranks materials by quality and expense, from fur through glass for light armor and iron through daedric for heavy armor, noting the common availability of basic materials and the rarity of exotic ones found only in ancient ruins and hoards. It also acknowledges the Mages Guild's role in enchanting armor, observing that rarer materials hold greater enchantments. The text includes a martial anecdote involving the bard Amorous Janus and a Colovian general.
topic_desc_basic: The Manual of Armor is an Imperial military guide commissioned by General Warhaft for officers of the Imperial service. It describes the types of armor available, their materials, and which armor suits different battlefield roles, distinguishing light armor for mobile troops from heavy armor for frontline forces and officers.

title: Manual of Arms
topic_desc: An Imperial military manual commissioned by General Warhaft to guide officers on weaponry and enchanted arms. It categorizes weapons by required combat skill, grouping axes and hammers under blunt proficiency, and reserving bows for marksmen. Two-handed weapons like claymores and battle axes are recommended for heavily-armored knights and flank holders. The text ranks weapon materials from iron to daedric by cost and desirability, noting silver's unique efficacy against ghosts, wraiths, and certain Daedra despite its lesser durability. It also explains bow construction using laminated material cores, the combined armor penetration of bow and arrow quality, and the mechanics of enchanted weapons, detailing how strikes trigger dormant magic, how bows transfer enchantments to arrows, and how soul gems recharge depleted magicka reservoirs.
topic_desc_basic: An Imperial military manual commissioned by General Warhaft to instruct officers on weaponry. It categorizes weapons by combat skill, ranks material quality from iron to daedric, notes silver's effectiveness against spirits, and explains the mechanics of enchanted arms and their recharge via soul gems.

title: Manual of Spellcraft
topic_desc: This introductory text guides beginning spellcasters through the early stages of magical study. It emphasizes that mastery requires years of hard work and mental discipline following initial exposure to magic. The work recommends the Mages Guild as the primary resource for purchasing spells, noting that independent dealers offer less comprehensive selections. It advises novices not to be discouraged by their inability to cast advanced spells such as invisibility, but rather to use such limits as motivation. Through dedicated practice within a chosen school, a mage can eventually master advanced techniques like spell absorption, Daedric and undead summoning for research, and elemental protection. The text strongly encourages Guild membership, explaining that the Council of Mages restricts potentially dangerous services like Advanced Spellcraft and Enchanting to higher-ranked members in good standing. Copies often bear extensive marginal notes from readers requiring frequent reminders on basic casting.
topic_desc_basic: An introductory text for beginning spellcasters, covering the importance of practice and recommending the Mages Guild as the primary source for spells, training, and advanced services restricted to higher-ranked members.

title: Manual of the Red Sword
topic_desc: Cilicus' Manual of the Red Sword is an Imperial treatise advocating the superiority of rhetoric and diplomacy over martial force. It contrasts the physical sword—a tool of last resort that dulls with use and forces its wielder into the compromised role of protector or oppressor—with the metaphorical red sword of the tongue. Properly honed through the Imperial art of Speech, the tongue opens ever-widening avenues of application, allowing a skilled speaker to protect and cultivate prosperity without making enemies of that which they hold dear. The work frames this rhetorical mastery as the definitive path of the Speaker and the Councilman.
topic_desc_basic: Cilicus' Manual of the Red Sword is an Imperial treatise contrasting the physical sword with the metaphorical red sword of the tongue, advocating diplomacy and the Imperial art of Speech over brute force as the path of the Councilman.

title: Mara's Beads
topic_desc: Mara's Beads are small pink flowers cultivated in gardens throughout Cyrodiil, with a small wild population in the Dasek Marsh region. Their delicate appearance and association with the goddess Mara lend them cultural recognition beyond purely alchemical circles. Gardeners and herbalists in the Imperial Province grow them ornamentally as well as for their ingredient properties. The plant's relative scarcity outside Cyrodiil makes wild specimens noteworthy, particularly those found in the marshlands where conditions apparently sustain growth despite the distance from cultivated heartland stock.
topic_desc_basic: Mara's Beads are small pink flowers grown in gardens across Cyrodiil, with a few wild plants found in the Dasek Marsh region. They are known both as ornamental blooms and as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Mara's Tear
topic_desc: A mythological tale by Zhen recounting the origin of the two moons, framed as a bedtime story. It describes two lovers, Mara and Shandar, from rival villages whose forbidden bond ends in tragedy when Shandar rescues Mara from an orc but suffers a mortal wound. The goddess Mara, moved by their devotion, elevates them into the heavens as the moons Mara's Tear and Shandar's Sorrow, ensuring their eternal union and providing light against the darkness. The narrative serves as an aetiological myth explaining the moons' presence and a moral lesson on love transcending enmity.
topic_desc_basic: A children's tale by Zhen explaining the origin of the two moons. It tells of two lovers from rival villages whose tragic deaths prompted the goddess Mara to place them in the sky as the moons Mara's Tear and Shandar's Sorrow.

title: Marsh Stalk Cap
topic_desc: The marsh stalk cap is a variety of fungus that grows in wetland environments. Documented within alchemical compendia as a harvestable ingredient, it is valued by practitioners for its inherent properties. Specimens are typically gathered from their natural habitats rather than cultivated, making them a staple of regional foraging in marshy terrains.
topic_desc_basic: A type of mushroom found in marshy regions, valued as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Meat Honey
topic_desc: Meat honey is a substance produced by skyrenders for their offspring, found within their nests in southwestern Morrowind. The Gan-Ettu Shinathi revere it as a holy gift, believing it to be Lord Vivec's teachings solidified, imparted to the skyrenders so they might become fierce beasts. The Gan-Ettu maintain a millenia-old relationship with the creatures, allowing honey farmers to extract the substance. Through a sacred ritual, spiritually worthy Gan-Ettu consume it to draw closer to Vivec and his gifts; being deemed worthy of this communion is among their highest honors. Alchemists prize meat honey for its properties.
topic_desc_basic: Meat honey is a substance produced by skyrenders for their offspring, harvested from their nests in southwestern Morrowind. The Gan-Ettu Shinathi revere it as a holy substance that solidifies Vivec's teachings, consuming it in sacred rituals to commune with him.

title: Meditations on Determined Law
topic_desc: Meditations on Determined Law is a theological treatise outlining orthodox Tribunal doctrine on the nature of divine law. Through parables involving seeds, environments, mathematics, and social bonds, the work argues that determined laws reside within all things as inherent potentials and restrictions. These laws remain abstract until activated by their specific context, such as a seed requiring soil or a master requiring a slave to actualize the relationship. The author contends that the infinite combinations of these simple orthodoxies create the illusion of chaos, which is dismissed as a heathen error. Instead, the universe is fundamentally ordered, deliberately called from the void by the Tribunes, and all apparent variation is part of their planned design.
topic_desc_basic: Meditations on Determined Law is a Tribunal doctrinal work arguing that divine law resides within all things as potential and restriction, only becoming expressed through context, and that the universe is entirely ordered by the Tribunes rather than chaotic.

title: Memories of the Highlands
topic_desc: Memories on the Western Highlands, their Gods, and their People by Serus Valicus is a reflective essay by a Nibenese writer dwelling in an uneasy eastern city. Writing from memory after years of war and famine, Valicus recalls the Colovian Highlands as a harsh, neglected land — a world within itself, abandoned by the Empire and forgotten by its own sons who die on distant battlefields. He portrays the Colovian people as living today as they did four thousand years ago, their faith bound to a grim vision of distant Divines and butchering Founder-Saints. The essay contrasts Nibenese religious vitality with Highland spiritual emptiness, observing that god-heroes born in Colovia depart for the wealthy east and never return, while eastern gods bypass the windswept summits entirely. Valicus frames the Highlands as a place where evil is anchored in the earth itself, beyond the reach of order or chaos.
topic_desc_basic: Memories on the Western Highlands, their Gods, and their People by Serus Valicus is a Nibenese author's reflective essay on the Colovian Highlands. Valicus describes the region as harsh, neglected by the Empire, and spiritually void, contrasting it with Nibenese religious life. He portrays the Colovian people as unchanged for millennia, living under a grim vision of the Divines.

title: Metamorphosis
topic_desc: Metamorphosis is a scholarly report detailing a research project to transmute base elements into gold for the benefit of Resdayn. The author recounts how early failures forced a methodical shift: rather than creating gold outright, the team identified its constituent properties—durability, hardness, purity, and brilliance—and sought corresponding elements. Scouts gathered resilient white, black, and gray rocks for durability. Philosophers guided the pursuit of hardness and purity, leading the team to excavate deep beneath the land for volatile firewater and to identify water as the tangible essence of purity. The final criterion, brilliance, required exposing the combined elements to the contrasting light and darkness of night. The experiment's success, producing gold on the white rock, is proclaimed as a triumph of science promising immeasurable wealth and technological advancement for Resdayn.
topic_desc_basic: Metamorphosis is a scientific report documenting a successful experiment to transmute base elements into gold. The author describes combining resilient rocks, subterranean firewater, and water under moonlight to achieve the properties of gold, proclaiming the breakthrough a triumph for Resdayn.

title: Midnight Agate
topic_desc: Midnight Agate is a variety of agate, a semi-precious mineral. It possesses alchemical properties, though its specific effects remain a matter for specialist experimentation. As a reagent, it is exceptionally rare and is not found in common leveled supplies or merchant stocks, requiring dedicated search or singular discovery by an alchemist to acquire.
topic_desc_basic: Midnight Agate is a rare semi-precious stone sometimes used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Military Tactics in the New Era
topic_desc: A military treatise published in 3E 26 by the former Legion officer Calonus Cetero, addressing counterinsurgency strategies for the Empire's peacetime threats. Cetero argues that the Legion's institutional commitment, intelligence networks, and discipline can outlast peasant militias, which rely on guerrilla hit-and-run tactics and lack centralized leadership. He identifies the Dunmer as the greatest threat to Imperial security, noting their fervent devotion to the Tribunal, their use of mobile bonemold armor, and their adaptation to Morrowind's climate and terrain, which negates the Legion's cavalry. He advocates forcing pitched battles, capturing the Dunmer's Living Gods to break morale, and exploiting the political divisions among the Great Houses, particularly House Hlaalu's Imperial alignment. For revolutionaries and religious leaders, Cetero warns that their charisma makes them dangerous martyrs, advising early interception and strict isolation from Legion ranks to prevent sedition.
topic_desc_basic: A military treatise by former Legion officer Calonus Cetero, published in 3E 26. It outlines Imperial strategies for managing peacetime threats, analyzing the tactics of peasant militias, the Dunmer, and charismatic insurgents, and how the Legion's discipline and resources can overcome them.

record_links.display_name: Military Tactics in the New Era

title: Milk Thistle Flower
topic_desc: The milk thistle flower is a botanical reagent valued by alchemists. Specimens enter circulation through Cyrodiilic and general Tamrielic trade networks, distributed among randomized shipments of common ingredients. The flower's alchemical character makes it a standard component in the inventory of traveling herbalists and ingredient merchants across provincial trade routes.
topic_desc_basic: A blossom of the milk thistle plant, gathered and traded as an alchemical ingredient throughout Tamriel.

title: Mindcap
topic_desc: Mindcap is a species of mushroom native to High Rock. It grows wild in that province and is valued by alchemists for its properties. As a regional ingredient of the Breton heartland, it is not commonly encountered in Morrowind and must be sought through trade or travel.
topic_desc_basic: Mindcap is a mushroom native to High Rock, valued as an alchemical ingredient. It is not commonly found in Morrowind.

title: Minerals of Morrowind
topic_desc: A treatise by East Empire Company prospector Apelle Dubilius surveying the mineral wealth of Morrowind, assessing the properties, economic viability, and practical applications of the province's resources.
topic_desc_basic: A guide by EEC prospector Apelle Dubilius assessing Morrowind's mineral wealth and the economic potential of its ores.

title: Minotaur
topic_desc: Minotaurs, also called man-bulls or bull-men, are a species of beastfolk native to Cyrodiil possessing the body of a man and the head of a bull. During the First Era, they symbolized the Alessian Empire, though in later eras they are more commonly perceived as savage monsters. They have thick grey, brown, or red hide and fur, and large curved horns. Their attire varies from simple loincloths and shawls to intricate leather armor, nose-rings, or nothing at all. They inhabit the Blackwood, Colovian Highlands, Great Forest, and Gold Coast regions of Cyrodiil, the Reach, and the Scar of Elsweyr, with historical presence in Bangkorai and Valenwood. Some, such as the Kreathi and the larger Trebataur, exhibit distinct regional traits or innate restorative abilities.
topic_desc_basic: Minotaurs, also called man-bulls, are beastfolk with a man's body and a bull's head, bearing thick hide, fur, and large curved horns. Native to Cyrodiil, they are commonly found in regions like the Blackwood and Colovian Highlands, as well as the Reach and the Scar of Elsweyr. Once symbols of the Alessian Empire, they are now widely regarded as savage monsters.

title: Minotaur Horn
topic_desc: A horn harvested from the head of a minotaur. These horns are obtained from the beast itself, with Kreathi minotaurs roaming Skyrim and bare-chested minotaurs inhabiting Cyrodiil. The material circulates among alchemists and hunters, who prize it for its alchemical properties and incorporate it into regional ingredient supplies.
topic_desc_basic: A horn taken from a minotaur's head. Minotaurs are found in Skyrim and Cyrodiil.

title: Mistletoe Berries
topic_desc: Mistletoe berries are harvested from mistletoe plants, a parasitic growth found upon dead trees. The plant is notably prevalent in the Vorndgad Forest of Skyrim, where it draws sustenance from its host timber. Alchemists and hunters value the berries for their properties in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Mistletoe berries grow on mistletoe plants, which are found on dead trees in the Vorndgad Forest of Skyrim.

title: Mixed Unit Tactics v2
topic_desc: A military treatise by Codus Callonus analyzing Bosmer and Khajiiti strategies during the Five Years War, detailing how the Bosmer adapted to Khajiiti terrain tactics but were ultimately outmaneuvered by a strategic diversion.
topic_desc_basic: A military treatise by Codus Callonus examining the Bosmer and Khajiiti strategies of the Five Years War, focusing on how a small Khajiiti force successfully diverted a larger Bosmer army.

title: Mixed Unit Tactics v3
topic_desc: Mixed Unit Tactics in the Five Years War, Volume Three, by Codus Callonus, an Imperial Legion veteran's account of the Bosmer-Khajiit conflict near Dune. Callonus narrates the long-standing border cycle of Khajiit tree-felling and Bosmer replanting, the Bosmer surprise assault on Khajiiti camps using blood-painted warriors, enchanted arrows, and forest beasts, and the subsequent siege of Dune. He describes with evident distaste the Bosmer practice of consuming fallen Khajiiti flesh and the Khajiiti counter-strategy of poisoning their own bodies before suicidal charges, so that the feasting Bosmer would sicken and die. Written from a strongly pro-Imperial viewpoint, the work advocates continued civilizing efforts toward the Bosmer and draws military lessons for the Legions, while acknowledging that the garrison at Fort Sphinxmoth was constrained by orders later attributed to the usurper. The account concludes by noting the siege's outcome is reserved for a fourth volume.
topic_desc_basic: A military memoir by Imperial veteran Codus Callonus covering the Five Years War between the Khajiit and Bosmer near the city of Dune, on the Elsweyr-Valenwood border. It describes the siege of Dune, Bosmer assault tactics using beasts and magic, and Khajiiti poison-based countermeasures.

title: Mixed Unit Tactics v4
topic_desc: Mixed Unit Tactics v4 is the fourth volume of Codus Callonus's military account of the Five Years War between the Bosmer of Valenwood and the Khajiit of Elsweyr. Written from the perspective of an Imperial Legion officer stationed at Fort Sphinxmoth, it details the siege of the Khajiiti city of Dune. The work describes how numerically inferior Khajiit forces used coordinated mixed-unit tactics—heavily armored Cathay-raht and Suthay-raht defending wall breaches, Senche-raht-drawn onager carts firing fire-pots, mounted Alfiq wizards and archers, and small sling-spear units—to rout the larger Bosmer force. Callonus analyzes these tactics' potential threat to Imperial Legion formations and recounts the subsequent fall of Fort Sphinxmoth to Khajiit deception and internal betrayal. The author exhibits strong racial prejudice and advocates restricting non-human Legionaries from border assignments.
topic_desc_basic: Mixed Unit Tactics v4 is the fourth volume of Codus Callonus's account of the Five Years War. Written by an Imperial Legion officer, it details the siege of the Khajiiti city of Dune and analyzes the coordinated tactics by which outnumbered Khajiit forces defeated a larger Bosmer army.

title: Mixed Unit Tactics v5
topic_desc: Mixed Unit Tactics v5 is the fifth volume of Codus Callonus's military chronicle Mixed Unit Tactics in the Five Years War. Written from the perspective of an Imperial Legion prisoner of war in the Khajiiti city of Dune, it details the capture and forced labor of Legion soldiers, the Imperial City's failure to ransom them during the Simulacrum, and the Bosmeri recapture of the city. Callonus describes how a small Bosmer force exploited Khajiiti overconfidence, using tunneling pranks and a decisive champion duel between a Bosmer Knight of the Spider-Wood and the Pahmar-raht Dro'Zaksa. The Bosmer knight's bleeding poison and evasive tactics secured an unlikely victory, winning Dune and Fort Sphinxmoth. The work provides a rare Imperial eyewitness perspective on the unconventional warfare and cultural practices of the Khajiit and Bosmer during the conflict.
topic_desc_basic: The fifth volume of Codus Callonus's chronicle of the Five Years War, recounting his imprisonment in Dune and the Bosmeri recapture of the city through a champion duel and unconventional tactics.

title: Modern Heretics
topic_desc: A scholarly study of Daedra worship within the Empire by Haderus of Gottlesfont, examining the legal status, social perception, and practices of Daedric cults. The work contrasts traditional pious worship with modern power-seeking, and details the author's field research methodology and personal discovery of an Azura shrine in the Jerall Mountains, alongside notes on other Daedric Lords and their associated artifacts.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Haderus of Gottlesfont studying Daedra worship in the Empire. It examines the legal and social status of Daedric cults and recounts the author's discovery of a shrine to Azura.

title: Mokre
topic_desc: Mokre is a fermented fish sauce commonly employed in Nibenese cooking throughout Cyrodiil. Valued as a culinary ingredient, it contributes its distinct properties to alchemical preparations. Its creation through fermentation points to an aquatic origin, aligning its harvest and use with the practices of hunters and alchemists familiar with regional foodstuffs.
topic_desc_basic: Mokre is a fermented fish sauce often used in Nibenese cooking in Cyrodiil.

title: Mole Crab Egg
topic_desc: Mole crab eggs are harvested from egg clutches found in mole crab farms across Morrowind. They are a common foodstuff and alchemical ingredient, appearing in assorted cheap food and egg supply lists throughout the region.
topic_desc_basic: Mole crab eggs are a common food ingredient found across Morrowind. They are harvested from clutches raised on mole crab farms and are widely available in markets and food supplies.

title: Monarda Seeds
topic_desc: Monarda seeds are the seeds of the monarda flower, a plant that grows in the Dasek Marsh region of Cyrodiil. Alchemists and hunters value them for their properties in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Monarda seeds are harvested from the monarda flower, which grows in the Dasek Marsh region of Cyrodiil.

title: Monk's Tonsure Cap
topic_desc: Monk's Tonsure Cap is a floral ingredient of uncertain alchemical character. Its common name suggests a distinctive shape reminiscent of a shorn crown. The plant grows in Hammerfell, where it appears in regional ingredient stocks and may be gathered by herbalists and hunters familiar with the province's flora. Beyond its Hammerfell distribution and general classification as a botanical reagent, its specific properties and applications remain poorly documented in widely available references.
topic_desc_basic: Monk's Tonsure Cap is a plant ingredient found in Hammerfell. Alchemists and hunters sometimes gather it.

title: Monkshood
topic_desc: Monkshood consists of the flowers harvested from the monkshood plant, a flora native to Cyrodiil. The plant's blooms are valued by alchemists and hunters for their useful properties when preparing concoctions. As an ingredient, it sees common use in Cyrodiilic alchemical traditions and appears in regional supply stocks.
topic_desc_basic: Monkshood is a flowering plant native to Cyrodiil, valued as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Monkshood Root Pulp
topic_desc: Monkshood root pulp is the crushed root of the monkshood plant, a flora native to Cyrodiil. Valued by alchemists for its derived properties, the pulp is prepared by macerating the root of the plant. It circulates through Cyrodiil's regional ingredient supplies and is commonly stocked by practitioners familiar with provincial flora.
topic_desc_basic: Monkshood root pulp is the crushed root of the monkshood plant, which grows native to Cyrodiil. It is used in alchemy.

title: Moon Moth Wing
topic_desc: Moon Moth Wings are the wings of the Moon Moth, a nocturnal moth commonly found throughout Cyrodiil. These moths appear only during nighttime hours, and each specimen bears a pair of wings that may be harvested for alchemical use. Moon Moth Wings are recognized as an alchemical ingredient among those familiar with Cyrodilic fauna, gathered by hunters and alchemists who collect them under the night sky.
topic_desc_basic: Moon Moth Wings are harvested from the Moon Moth, a nocturnal insect native to Cyrodiil that appears only after dark. The wings serve as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Moonstone
topic_desc: Moonstone is an ivory-colored metal found in veins throughout Tamriel. It also forms as a rare mineral in volcanic lava flows, exhibiting a soft reflected light caused by internal crystalline reflections. In metallurgy, moonstone is worked to craft elven armor, a process long guarded as a secret by the Altmer of Summerset, and serves as the signature material for Khajiiti-styled armor. Alloying it with quicksilver is common for elven armor, though moonstone's significantly higher melting point makes the combined working difficult; saltwater is required to properly quench the hot metal during the forging process.
topic_desc_basic: Moonstone is an ivory-colored metal found in veins across Tamriel. It is primarily used to craft elven armor and Khajiiti-styled armor.

title: Moosebite Polypore
topic_desc: Moosebite Polypore is a polypore mushroom native to Skyrim. As a fungal ingredient of Nordic origin, it is not commonly encountered in Morrowind's provincial flora. The specific alchemical properties and traditional applications of this mushroom are not widely documented beyond Skyrim's own practitioners, leaving its full character known primarily to alchemists and hunters familiar with the region's fungal varieties.
topic_desc_basic: Moosebite Polypore is a mushroom that grows in Skyrim. It is not commonly found in Morrowind.

title: Morning Glory Flower
topic_desc: Morning glory flowers are harvested from the morning glory, a trailing plant native to Cyrodiil. Alchemists value the blossom for its inherent properties, and the plant's vining habit makes it a recognizable specimen across its provincial range.
topic_desc_basic: Morning glory flowers grow on a trailing plant native to Cyrodiil and are used in alchemy.

title: Morrowind Historia: Bal Foyen
topic_desc: A historical work by Varias Cedas examining the Dunmer city of Bal Foyen and the Dwemer ruins beneath it.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Varias Cedas recounting the history of the Dunmer city of Bal Foyen, situated in a crater along the Inner Sea, and the sprawling Dwemer ruins discovered beneath it.

title: Mosslog
topic_desc: Mosslog is a staff artifact bearing a Command Creature enchantment. It is associated with ambitions to recruit and command creatures, particularly mudcrabs, as a martial force against House Telvanni. The artifact is reportedly found in the pond on the east side of Sadas Plantation. Despite its reputed power, accounts suggest its wielder struggled to control even common mudcrabs, casting doubt on the full extent of its capabilities.
topic_desc_basic: Mosslog is a staff artifact with a Command Creature enchantment. It is said to rest in the pond on the east side of Sadas Plantation.

title: Motherwort
topic_desc: Motherwort is a botanical ingredient consisting of the leaves harvested from the plant of the same name. It grows in the Dasek Marsh of Cyrodiil, where herbalists and alchemists gather it for its useful properties. The plant thrives in the wet, marshy conditions of that region, and the harvested foliage serves as a recognized component in alchemical practice across the province.
topic_desc_basic: Motherwort is a plant whose leaves are used as an alchemical ingredient. It grows in the Dasek Marsh of Cyrodiil.

title: Mountain Damask
topic_desc: Mountain Damask is a flowering plant native to Morrowind. It thrives in the region's terrain and is recognized by alchemists and hunters as a source of usable ingredient material. The flower is gathered for its alchemical properties and features in regional supply networks, including those around Narsis and the Velothi Mountains.
topic_desc_basic: Mountain Damask is a flower native to Morrowind, commonly gathered for its alchemical properties.

title: Mountain Goat
topic_desc: The mountain goat is a sturdy herbivorous creature adapted to Tamriel's steep highlands. It navigates rocky slopes with cloven hooves and a robust frame, foraging on sparse alpine vegetation. Its coarse pelt provides insulation against harsh mountain climates. While normally docile and prone to fleeing from threats, cornered specimens defend themselves with horned charges. The animal's durable hide and meat make it a valued target for hunters traversing elevated terrain.
topic_desc_basic: The mountain goat is a sturdy herbivorous creature found in steep, rocky highlands. It forages on alpine vegetation and navigates difficult slopes with ease. While normally docile, it defends itself with its horns when cornered, and is commonly hunted for its meat and hide.

title: Muck-stained copy of 'Seasons'
topic_desc: A soiled copy of 'Seasons', a poetic work by Horatio Gargonath. The poem comprises four verses, each celebrating the natural splendor of a different season: spring's blossoms and gentle winds, summer's honeysuckle and drowsy warmth, autumn's painted leaves and migrating birds, and winter's icy stillness. The verses reflect a pastoral viewpoint, finding serenity and paradise in the cyclical rhythms of the natural world. The muck staining this particular copy obscures neither its text nor its idyllic appreciation of nature's changing pageantry.
topic_desc_basic: A copy of 'Seasons', a poem by Horatio Gargonath celebrating the natural beauty and tranquility of spring, summer, autumn, and winter.

title: Mummy
topic_desc: Mummies are reanimated, embalmed corpses preserved through cultural rites or necromantic craft across Tamriel. The mummification process—soaking the body in salt or natron, optionally removing organs, and wrapping it in cloth—halts decay and preserves musculature, yielding an undead servant more durable and autonomous than a zombie, though stiffer and requiring stronger necromantic animation. They are liable to rise due to restless spirits or a necromancer's binding. Mummies resist ordinary weapons, requiring silver or better to harm, and often carry horrible diseases; some plaguebearer variants infect victims with a remarkable range of afflictions. Disturbing their remains can invoke a mummy's curse, inflicting nightly hauntings until the undead is destroyed. Their wrappings hold alchemical value. Diverse cultures practice mummification, from Ashlanders using ash salts to honor ancestors, to Redguard and Ayleid traditions, and Imperial necromantic bindings on condemned prisoners. Minotaur barrowguards in Colovian crypts are notably stronger than human mummies.
topic_desc_basic: Mummies are reanimated, cloth-wrapped undead found in tombs and burial sites across Tamriel. They are more durable than zombies but require silver or better weapons to harm. Many carry dangerous diseases, and disturbing their remains can bring a nightly curse of hauntings.

title: Mummy Heart
topic_desc: A dried, shriveled organ harvested from preserved dead, most reliably barrowguards. Mundane mummies in Morrowind typically lack these remains, though loose samples exist. Alchemists prize the organ for its varied magical character.
topic_desc_basic: A dried, shriveled organ taken from preserved dead like barrowguards, valued by alchemists for its varied magical properties.

title: Murudius
topic_desc: A memoir by the retired Imperial General Monious Kathil detailing a disastrous patrol in the Argonian swamps. Kathil recounts how a legionnaire named Murudius was bitten by a lycanthrope and subsequently transformed, slaughtering most of the squad. The general asserts that the Imperial Legion suppresses such incidents, falsely claiming it can control lycanthropes. The account serves as an indictment of this official posture, arguing that the Legion exercises no real control over infected soldiers and that the power of lycanthropes is dangerously underestimated.
topic_desc_basic: A memoir by Imperial General Monious Kathil recounting a disastrous patrol in the Argonian swamps, where a legionnaire transformed into a lycanthrope and killed most of his squad.

title: Muscat
topic_desc: Muscat is a spice valued for its aromatic and flavoring properties in culinary and alchemical preparations alike. While its specific alchemical applications remain a matter of practitioner technique rather than established doctrine, the ingredient is recognized in trade as a standard seasoning commodity. Its natural origin is botanical, harvested for its fragrant qualities that lend distinction to dishes and concoctions. Alchemists and hunters alike encounter muscat as a trade good, though its precise habitat and growth habits are not widely documented in standard herbalist references. Its presence in curated spice collections suggests a recognized, if specialized, role in both kitchen and laboratory.
topic_desc_basic: Muscat is a fragrant spice used as a flavoring in cooking and as an ingredient in alchemy. It is a common enough trade commodity, recognized by cooks and herbalists for its aromatic qualities.

title: Muskrat Fur
topic_desc: Muskrat fur is the pelt of the muskrat, a rodent commonly found in Cyrodiil. It serves as an alchemical ingredient, valued by practitioners for its inherent properties. Hunters and furriers operating in the region routinely collect these pelts from the creatures, making the material a staple resource for local alchemists.
topic_desc_basic: Muskrat fur is the pelt of the muskrat, a common rodent found in Cyrodiil. It is used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Mutton
topic_desc: Mutton is meat harvested from butchered adult sheep. It serves as a common foodstuff across Tamriel, finding its way into regional diets and culinary preparations such as Ornada stuffing. Beyond its nutritional value, mutton possesses alchemical properties that make it suitable as an ingredient in potion-making. The meat is widely distributed through commercial supply channels, appearing in general meat and ingredient vendor stocks throughout Cyrodiil, Hammerfell, and Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: Mutton is meat from butchered adult sheep, commonly eaten as food across Tamriel.

title: Mystery Play
topic_desc: Mystery plays are ancient religious dramas portraying stories of the Divines and Saints, developed as some of the earliest rites of the Nibenese cults. They are as much liturgy as art. Very few were written down, as they originated in the chaos before the rise of Emperor Reman I, and surviving texts are often incomplete. The 'Mystery Play of Old Ebonheart' was composed by the first Nibenese settlers of that city in the style of their ancient cult traditions. In later years the Imperial Cult assumed responsibility for performing it. No performances have been given since the unrest on Vvardenfell began, and hope of reviving the tradition dwindled further when the 426 Balmora tax revolts erupted into violence. The Old Ebonheart chapel has recently been tasked with staging the play again to accompany King Helseth's coronation tournament, suggesting a renewed effort to restore the custom.
topic_desc_basic: The Mystery Play of Old Ebonheart is an ancient religious drama portraying stories of the Divines and Saints, written by the first Nibenese settlers of Old Ebonheart. The Imperial Cult later took over its performance. It has not been performed since the unrest on Vvardenfell began.

title: Mystery Play of Old Ebonheart
topic_desc: The Mystery Play of Old Ebonheart is a dramatic work performed annually during the Ebonheart Festival on the city's fountain square. Written by Nibenese immigrants of the rebuilt city, it has been staged with minimal alteration for over three hundred years. Accounts of its cast and content differ: one version depicts Akatosh, Dibella, and Arkay confronting a three-part Triune representing lost divine attributes—mercy, order, and poetry—that refuse reunification, negotiating instead to reside within the gods without absorption. Another version features Stendarr and Julianos debating justice and law before subduing a three-faced Demon of eastern origin, ultimately demonstrating that mercy tempers the strict wages of law. Both iterations employ symbolic casting—magistrates, cult officials, and reformed criminals—and conclude with costumed actors distributing brass coins to the audience before joining the revelry.
topic_desc_basic: The Mystery Play of Old Ebonheart is a traditional play performed annually during the Ebonheart Festival on the city's fountain square. Written by Nibenese immigrants, it has been staged for over three hundred years. It dramatizes the relationship between the Divines and eastern spirits, exploring themes of law, justice, and mercy.

title: Mystic Path of the Emperor
topic_desc: A Cyrodilic devotional text structured as three liturgical invocations, each addressed to a different aspect of imperial sovereignty. The first honors past emperors—Alessia, Reman, and Tiber Septim—as exemplars of overcoming, will, and conquest. The second offers praise to earlier figures including Hestra, Sidri-Ashak, and Cuhlecain, casting them as waymakers who established law and foresaw the imperial path. The third exalts Cyrod itself, describing the Highlands, the Niben, and the jungle as embodiments of the land's power, culminating in the image of the Emperor enthroned under divine mandate. The work frames imperial rule as both a personal mystical discipline and a sacred bond between ruler, land, and ancestor, reflecting a distinctly Cyrodilic theology of sovereignty that venerates the Emperor not merely as a political office but as a manifestation of the region's divine purpose.
topic_desc_basic: A Cyrodilic devotional text that venerates imperial sovereignty through three invocations. It honors emperors such as Alessia, Reman, and Tiber Septim as exemplars of rulership, praises earlier figures who prepared the imperial path, and exalts the land of Cyrod itself as sacred. The work frames the Emperor's authority as divinely mandated.

title: Myths of Sheogorath
topic_desc: Myths of Sheogorath by Mymophonus is a collection of three tales illustrating the nature and deeds of the Daedric Prince Sheogorath. The work recounts how Sheogorath invented music by dismembering a mortal woman to craft the first instruments, how he cursed the excessively rational King Lyandir's city with madness after the king banned all art and revelry, and how he broke the wizard Ravate's mind through a contest of wills. The tales collectively portray Sheogorath as both Lord of the Creative and Lord of the Deranged, emphasizing that creativity and madness are inseparable gifts, and that those who reject one invite the other. The book serves as both entertainment and cautionary lore regarding the Madgod's capricious influence on mortal affairs.
topic_desc_basic: Myths of Sheogorath by Mymophonus is a widely circulated collection of legends about the Daedric Prince Sheogorath, the Madgod. It presents three stories: the invention of music from a mortal's body, the destruction of the rational King Lyandir through madness, and the breaking of the wizard Ravate's mind. The tales illustrate Sheogorath's dual nature as patron of both creativity and derangement.

title: Names of the Mother Cyrod
topic_desc: A recovered liturgical text, originally titled *Maunr ovn Ulmscyrod* by Saint Orsede, depicting the events in which Alessia received her various names. Discovered in fragments at the monastery of Bed-Geron, the manuscript is contemporary with Alessia but shows significant later editing. An illumination glyph links it to a fellowship of Colovian scribe monks known for Shezarrhic syncretism. The surviving portions describe her enslavement as Perrif at the Ayleid pen of Sard, her communion with Kyne, the possible discovery of the Chim-el Adabal, and her emergence as Mother Cyrod alongside Pelinal Whitestrake. The work frames her accumulating names as gifts splintering outward through the Aurbis, each claimed by the newborn people of Cyrod. It stands as a valuable, if layered, primary source for the Alessian Rebellion.
topic_desc_basic: An ancient liturgical text describing the events in which Alessia received her various names. Recovered in fragments at the monastery of Bed-Geron, it covers her enslavement, her communion with Kyne, and her emergence as Mother Cyrod during the Alessian Rebellion.

title: Namira's Shroud
topic_desc: Namira's Shroud is an artifact associated with the Daedric Prince Namira. It is currently held in the vault of Tholer Andas in Bal Foyen. The Shroud possesses a concealed magical property that shields a vampire wearer from the sun damage typically incurred during daylight travel. This protection comes at a cost, inflicting a significant drain on the wearer's personality and a pronounced vulnerability to fire. The vampire ancient Varos has sought the Shroud to facilitate his journey to the region of his lost clan.
topic_desc_basic: Namira's Shroud is an artifact of the Daedric Prince Namira. It is kept in the vault of Tholer Andas in Bal Foyen.

title: Nandor's Spear
topic_desc: Nandor's Spear is a unique weapon associated with the late Nandor Beraid. The spear and its owner are referenced in the skill book The Armorer's Challenge, which preserves their story. Nandor Beraid's remains rest on the deck of the Flooded Shipwreck, a sunken vessel on the seafloor southwest of Nivalis, while the spear itself lies secured within a chest inside the submerged hull. The circumstances of Nandor's drowning and the spear's presence aboard the ruined vessel remain subjects of the armorer's tale.
topic_desc_basic: Nandor's Spear is a unique weapon associated with Nandor Beraid. Both are referenced in the book The Armorer's Challenge. The spear lies in a chest within the Flooded Shipwreck on the seafloor southwest of Nivalis, where Nandor Beraid's corpse rests on the deck above.

title: Narrative of Yilgamseh XI
topic_desc: The eleventh volume of the Narrative of Yilgamseh recounts the Yokudan flood myth set in the ancient city of Shurrupak. The god Ea warns Yilgamseh of a divine council's plan to unleash a great deluge, instructing him to build a cube-shaped ship carrying the seed of all living creatures. After the devastating flood—even the gods cower at their own destructive work—Yilgamseh emerges to find utter devastation. He is granted immortality by Enlil and removed to the rivers' mouth, yet he remains consumed by grief and a profound sense of littleness before the dead. The volume concludes with Yilgamseh recounting his story to an unnamed listener, reflecting on the futility of seeking eternal life to restore what was lost, and acknowledging the listener's painful freedom to rebuild their own world anew.
topic_desc_basic: The eleventh volume of the Narrative of Yilgamseh, a Yokudan mythological epic. It recounts the survivor Yilgamseh's tale of the great flood sent by the gods upon the ancient city of Shurrupak, his survival by building a great ship, and his subsequent grief and reluctant ascension to immortality.

title: Narrative of Yilgamseh XII
topic_desc: The final volume of the Narrative of Yilgamseh recounts the hero's failure to stay awake for a seven-day vigil at Utnamishem's house, proving unready for eternal life. Utnamishem reveals a thorned river plant that restores youth. Yilgamseh retrieves it, but a serpent consumes the plant while he bathes, shedding its skin. Accepting mortality's limits, Yilgamseh returns to Urkai, where even his lost companion Enduki is forgotten, finding brief solace in his city's enduring walls.
