topic_desc_basic: The final volume tells how Yilgamseh fails a seven-day vigil, loses a life-renewing river plant to a serpent, and returns to Urkai accepting mortality.

title: Narsis: A History
topic_desc: Varian Felannus's historical survey traces the development of Narsis from a Merethic Era tomb-guarding steading founded by Narsara Hla-Alu to its present status as House Hlaalu's commercial capital. It details the High Velothi expansion under Tharel Hlaalu, the First Era conquest by the Red Khans, liberation by Nerevar, sacking by the Second Empire during the Four Score War, and the Interregnum rebuilding that positioned the Hlaalu for the Armistice. Felannus emphasizes how post-Armistice integration of foreign merchants and governance by figures like Duchess Vermothah during the Simulacrum transformed Narsis into a cosmopolitan center of Imperial-Hlaalu cooperation and immense wealth.
topic_desc_basic: A historical work by Varian Felannus chronicling the city of Narsis, the great commercial capital of House Hlaalu in Morrowind, from its ancient founding as a tomb steading to its modern prosperity as a cosmopolitan hub of Imperial-Hlaalu trade.

title: Narsis Arena
topic_desc: The Narsis Arena is a gladiatorial fighting organization headquartered in the city of Narsis. It trains combatants in martial disciplines—marksman, athletics, spear, and various blade and armor skills—valuing strength and endurance above all. Gladiators advance through four ranks: Iron Scale, Silver Scale, Gold Scale, and Ebony Scale, progressing by proving their martial prowess in the arena pit against a variety of challengers. The arena's bouts range from rank advancement duels against warriors and veterans to grudge matches and executions of captured spies. The organization holds deep enmity toward the vampire clans of Vvardenfell and the Sixth House. Under the leadership of Felms, a Gold Scale gladiator, the arena continues to draw fighters seeking fortune and reputation through mortal combat.
topic_desc_basic: The Narsis Arena is a gladiatorial fighting organization based in the city of Narsis. It trains combatants in martial skills and advances them through four ranks—from Iron Scale to Ebony Scale—based on their strength, endurance, and proven prowess in arena combat.

title: Nature of Fire
topic_desc: Nature of Fire is a Temple doctrinal codex that examines flame as a sacred, transformative force identified with Sithis. It attributes the taming of fire to Boethiah as Anticipation of Almalexia and frames the Velothi relationship with fire as a birthright predating the Great Houses. The work balances theological reflection with practical instruction, detailing how fire requires air and magicka to sustain its living nature and warning that its inherent character of revolt causes it to overthrow when overfed. It outlines both fire's degenerative effects and its beneficial applications in refinement, alchemy, and healing when wielded by a deft practitioner. The text also catalogs reactive and resistant substances including alcohol, dried saltrice, cliff racer feathers, fire salt, and fire petal. It concludes by directing those who seek to conjure flame to the Temple rather than the Mages Guild, citing Imperial restrictions on magical instruction.
topic_desc_basic: Nature of Fire is a Temple doctrinal work exploring fire as a sacred, transformative force of Sithis and a birthright of the Velothi. It attributes the taming of fire to Boethiah and balances theological reflection with practical knowledge of fire's behavior, applications, and hazards.

title: Navigational Tools
topic_desc: Navigational tools encompass the antique maritime implements and period maps historically employed by the Imperial Navy. A notable surviving specimen is a well-preserved 3E 283 internal naval map of Emperor Uriel V's Akavir invasion, detailing the 282–289 preparatory operations and the final fleet rendezvous at Black Harbor. This map is currently on loan to the College of Firewatch from the Museum of the Imperial Navy in Thorn, bequeathed by the late Admiral Varus Caro, who commanded the 3rd (Southern) Squadron from 277–285. Accompanying the map are authentic navigational implements from the 280s, formerly owned by Captain Rochar of the light galleon TEM 'Dellese Rain'. These artifacts represent the enduring Imperial interest in its disastrous Uttermost East campaign and the era's maritime cartographic practices.
topic_desc_basic: Navigational tools are the antique maritime implements and maps used by the Imperial Navy. A notable surviving period map of Emperor Uriel V's Akavir invasion, along with authentic era navigational implements, is currently exhibited at the College of Firewatch on loan from the Museum of the Imperial Navy in Thorn.

title: Necromantic Texts
topic_desc: Necromantic texts at the College of Firewatch are restricted to passive academic study under the Headmaster's personal approval. Authorized volumes include the practical guides Corpse Preparation (Volumes I-III), Legions of the Dead, and On Necromancy. The Fourth Book of Dust remains under faculty evaluation and is currently prohibited. Several profane tracts are strictly forbidden on College grounds; possession or study of Arkay the Enemy, N'Gasta! Kvata! Kvakis!, or Saka'Punika! Rahkspondu! Kvata! warrants disciplinary action. Any study of the King of Worms or the Worm Cult results in immediate expulsion.
topic_desc_basic: The College of Firewatch restricts necromantic texts to passive academic study under the Headmaster's personal approval. Permitted volumes include Corpse Preparation, Legions of the Dead, and On Necromancy. Profane tracts and any study of the King of Worms or the Worm Cult are strictly forbidden.

title: Neldrac's Reach
topic_desc: Neldrac's Reach is a long bow of Dwemeri origin. Its precise historical provenance and the identity of its namesake remain obscure, though its construction reflects the sophisticated metallurgical and mechanical traditions of the vanished Deep Elves. As an artifact of Dwemeri craftsmanship, the bow holds esoteric significance for scholars of that lost civilization, though its present whereabouts are unknown.
topic_desc_basic: Neldrac's Reach is a long bow of Dwemeri origin.

title: Nerevar's Axe
topic_desc: Nerevar's Axe is a relic of Saint Nerevar, the Hortator of Resdayn, who was a renowned axemaster. The 36 Lessons of Vivec record that he chose an axe from the Fight Racks to quiet his mind, though the name he gave it remains unknown. The histories do not record what happened to the weapon after the Battle of Red Mountain. An Ashlander legend holds that Nerevar's shield-bearer and closest companion, Alandro Sul, recovered the axe and returned it to the vault of Nerevar's stronghold, Idaverrano. This stronghold was supposedly destroyed in the aftermath of the battle, but the axe is believed to remain in its sunken vault beneath the waters north of the Sundered Scar. The Temple and House Indoril consider the relic too important to remain in private hands, holding that it should be displayed for the benefit of all faithful Dunmer.
topic_desc_basic: Nerevar's Axe is a relic of Saint Nerevar, the Hortator of Resdayn. Its fate after the Battle of Red Mountain is unknown, though Ashlander legend claims his companion Alandro Sul returned it to the stronghold of Idaverrano. House Indoril considers it a sacred relic of the Dunmer people.

title: Nerium Rose Flower
topic_desc: The Nerium Rose is a flowering plant native to Elsweyr, collected and used as an alchemical ingredient. The blossom is valued by practitioners for its properties, and those familiar with the region's flora—including alchemists and hunters—recognize it among the indigenous flowers harvested for potion-making. Its presence reflects the botanical character of Elsweyr's landscape.
topic_desc_basic: Those who know Elsweyr's countryside recognize the Nerium Rose as a native flower gathered for alchemical use. It is one of the blossoms that grows naturally in the province.

title: Newt Scales
topic_desc: Newt scales are alchemical ingredients harvested from newts. They are a recognized component in the apothecary's repertoire, utilized in potion-making for their inherent properties. As a natural animal byproduct, the scales are typically procured by hunters and alchemists who skin or process the small creatures. In the region of Cyrodiil, they are known to circulate among practitioners through randomized alchemical supplies and fauna-derived stock.
topic_desc_basic: Newt scales are alchemical ingredients obtained from newts, commonly used by apothecaries and hunters.

title: Nigella Seeds
topic_desc: Nigella seeds are a spice ingredient of uncertain natural origin. They are not widely distributed and do not appear in common leveled supply, suggesting they are either rare, imported, or gathered by specialist means rather than routinely stocked by general merchants. Their alchemical character is not broadly documented in standard references.
topic_desc_basic: Nigella seeds are a spice known to alchemists and herbalists. They are uncommon and not typically found in general trade supply.

title: Nightshade
topic_desc: Nightshade is a poisonous plant native to Elsweyr and Morrowind, also cultivated as an indoor ornamental across Tamriel. Its toxic nature makes it a staple of the poisoner's art, and alchemists value it for the deleterious properties it imparts. The plant's hardiness in both subtropical and temperate indoor environments ensures a steady, if sometimes dangerous, supply for experimental brews.
topic_desc_basic: Nightshade is a poisonous plant native to Elsweyr and Morrowind, commonly grown indoors across Tamriel.

title: Nirthfly Eye
topic_desc: A Nirthfly eye is the harvested ocular organ of the nirthfly, valued by alchemists and hunters for its intrinsic properties. As a creature-derived ingredient, it sees use in potion-making and trade throughout Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: Nirthfly eyes are ingredients harvested from nirthflies and used in alchemy.

title: Nix-Mount
topic_desc: Nix-Mounts are insect-like animals native to Morrowind, primarily utilized as riding beasts and beasts of burden. Adapted to the region's harsh terrain, they serve as a practical means of transportation for those traversing the province. While generally domesticated for their mounting capability, they remain capable creatures in a fight, defending themselves with melee attacks. Upon death, a Nix-Mount typically yields hound meat and possesses a petty soul.
topic_desc_basic: The Nix-Mount is an insect-like animal native to Morrowind commonly used as a mount.

title: Nodding Streakwort
topic_desc: Nodding Streakwort is a green and yellow flower native to Morrowind. It grows across the region and is recognized by alchemists and hunters for its alchemical properties.
topic_desc_basic: Nodding Streakwort is a green and yellow flower native to Morrowind.

title: Nordic Warhammer
topic_desc: The Nordic Warhammer is a distinctive weapon of Nordic origin, recognized by its unique ornamental craftsmanship. Although its singular appearance once led to its classification as a notable artifact, it bears no enchantments. It is presently understood to be a generic weapon rather than a relic of special cultural or historical significance.
topic_desc_basic: The Nordic Warhammer is a distinctive, unenchanted weapon of Nordic craftsmanship, recognized as a generic arm rather than a true artifact.

title: Oathbound Legionaire
topic_desc: The Oathbound Legionaire is an undead creature, specifically the reanimated remains of an Imperial Legion soldier sworn to the service of the Reman Dynasty. Clad in ancient Imperial legionary armor, these skeletal warriors persist beyond death, bound by oaths of loyalty that survive their mortal demise. They are encountered in Cyrodiil, typically guarding ancient fortifications, tombs, or battlefields associated with the Reman Empire. Their behavior is driven entirely by their enduring martial obligation; they attack intruders who violate the sites they are sworn to protect. The existence of these entities serves as stark evidence of the profound gravity of Imperial military oaths and the enduring power of Reman-era traditions, which bind soldiers to their posts long after life has left them.
topic_desc_basic: An Oathbound Legionaire is an undead Imperial soldier clad in ancient armor, bound to its post by oaths of loyalty to the Reman Dynasty. These skeletal warriors are found in Cyrodiil at old garrisons and tombs, where they attack intruders who disturb their charges.

title: Oathrung
topic_desc: Oathrung is a Dwemer artifact functioning as both a powerful staff and a sort of key. It was originally recovered from the Dwemer ruin of Bthalag-Zturamz by the Telvanni magelord Master Turimal, who later used it in an assault on the city of Firewatch in 3E 306. Turimal was captured and executed during the attack, and Oathrung subsequently fell into the custody of Firewatch. The staff is currently held in the vault of Ember Keep, Firewatch's castle, where it is regarded as the city's crown jewel. The Telvanni mage Mistress Faruna, who discovered Turimal's abandoned research notes on the artifact, seeks its return. According to these notes, Dwemer writings identify Oathrung's key-like properties, which may unlock a secret chamber within Bthalag-Zturamz.
topic_desc_basic: Oathrung is a renowned Dwemer staff and the crown jewel of Firewatch. Seized from the Telvanni magelord Turimal after his failed assault on the city in 3E 306, it is currently kept in the vault of Ember Keep.

title: Ocularis Butterfly Wing
topic_desc: The Ocularis butterfly wing is harvested from the Ocularis butterfly, an uncommon diurnal insect native to Stirk Isle in Cyrodiil. Alchemists and hunters value these wings for their distinctive properties. The creature's daytime habits make collection a daylight endeavor, and each specimen reliably yields a pair of wings. As an ingredient, the wing possesses its own alchemical character, contributing to various mixtures. Its regional scarcity outside its native habitat enhances its worth among practitioners of the alchemical arts.
topic_desc_basic: Ocularis butterfly wings come from uncommon daytime butterflies found on Stirk Isle in Cyrodiil. Each butterfly provides two wings, which alchemists use as ingredients.

title: Ode To The Tundrastriders
topic_desc: An anonymous poem venerating the giants of the northern tundra, whom the author addresses as tundrastriders. The work romanticizes the bond between giant and mammoth as a symbiotic partnership of equals essential for mutual survival. Through a first-person reverie, the narrator imagines joining a giant herd, painting mammoths, carving their tusks, hunting skeevers, sharing campfire songs, eating roasted skeever and mammoth cheese, and sleeping sheltered in mammoth fur. The piece reflects a cultural admiration for the giant way of life and offers insight into observed practices such as tusk-carving and the consumption of mammoth cheese, noted for its foul taste but recognized healing properties.
topic_desc_basic: An anonymous poem dedicated to the giants of the northern tundra and their mammoth herds. The work romanticizes the symbiotic bond between giant and beast, imagining a day spent alongside them hunting skeevers, eating mammoth cheese, and sleeping in mammoth fur.

title: Oelander's Hammer
topic_desc: Oelander's Hammer is a children's instructive tale by Krowle, framing a Redguard legend within a narrative about two youths, Froedwig and Silvanda of Granitsta. During an outing, the siblings encounter an elderly ranger, Hoennig Groevinger, who recounts the fate of a young soldier named Oelander. Following a great battle ended by the warrior god Reymon Ebonarm, Oelander was confronted by a dark wizard who demanded his enchanted war hammer. Oelander struck the wizard just as a spell was cast, triggering an explosion that created a chasm, trapped the hammer's handle beneath impenetrable thorny vines, and vanished both combatants. The tale conveys a moral lesson on merit, claiming only one of tremendous worth may retrieve the fabled weapon.
topic_desc_basic: Oelander's Hammer is a children's tale by Krowle about a Redguard soldier whose enchanted war hammer became trapped in a chasm after he struck a wizard, causing a magical explosion. The legend claims only someone of tremendous merit can retrieve the weapon from its thorny prison.

title: Of Fire Ants and Hooms
topic_desc: A dialogue between the outlander Phand and the Ashlander Shabael-Ilu recounting their shared adventures in the Ashlands and Velothi Mountains. Phand tells a farcical, embellished tale of riding a shalk and outwitting the Ashkhan of the Sennahanib tribe through trickery involving fire ants and the shalk's fire-mixing arts. Shabael-Ilu counters with a more sober memory of tracking a hoom through black snow in the Velothi foothills while gravely ill, emphasizing that Phand's trust and perseverance during that harsh journey proved their bond. The work explores the cultural gulf between an outlander's irreverent humor and an Ashlander's traditional values, ultimately affirming friendship through mutual reliance.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Shissal Asurani recording a conversation between an outlander and an Ashlander who share contrasting stories of their adventures in Morrowind to explain their close friendship.

title: Of Fjori and Holgeir
topic_desc: A Nordic tragic tale recounting the romance and deaths of the huntress Fjori and the warlord Holgeir. The two met as opposing leaders in battle, fought to a standstill, and fell in love, uniting their forest clans in peace. When a snake's venom brought Holgeir to the threshold of Sovngarde, Fjori crossed snow-covered mountains to the coast, obtaining a curative elixir from the Akaviri. She returned and saved him, but was herself bitten by the snake and died from exhaustion and venom. Holgeir subsequently built a tomb for her and took his own life to rejoin her. The narrative emphasizes their equality in combat and the depth of their bond, framing their union and demise through natural and animalistic motifs.
topic_desc_basic: A tragic Nordic tale of the huntress Fjori and warlord Holgeir, two former rivals who fell in love and united their clans. After a snake bit Holgeir, Fjori journeyed to obtain an Akaviri elixir and saved him, only to be bitten by the same snake and die. Grief-stricken, Holgeir built her tomb and took his own life to rejoin her.

title: Of Jephre
topic_desc: An anonymous treatise examining the elven god Jephre, revered as the deity of song and forest. The work synthesizes diverse elven traditions: Bosmer revere him as a Major Sylvan god who blessed them with forest affinity, Altmer hold that he perceives all near water and blessed them with beauty, and Dunmer maintain he sang the stars into motion before the first day. The text attributes the origins of elven ballads and the songs of birds and streams to Jephre's teachings. It emphasizes that his temples in Valenwood and Summerset uphold the natural order, noting his absolute intolerance for its harmful manipulation. The work underscores his broad veneration among elven bards and Wood Elven rangers.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise on the elven god Jephre, worshipped as the god of song and forest. It details how he taught birds and streams to sing, blessed the Wood Elves with forest affinity, and is revered by elven bards and rangers. His faith centers on preserving the natural order, which he fiercely defends from harmful manipulation.

title: Of Unspeakable Volumes
topic_desc: A scholarly catalogue of dangerous esoteric works by the librarian Sigius Vile, warning of the madness-inducing knowledge contained within.
topic_desc_basic: A librarian's catalogue of dangerous esoteric works, warning readers that the knowledge within these volumes drives mortals to madness.

title: Ogre
topic_desc: Ogres are a race of large, strong humanoid Goblin-ken found throughout Tamriel, commonly perceived as primal, dim-witted brutes distinguished by a foul smell. They possess steely blue or greenish skin, pronounced teeth, tapered ears, and shaggy hair, with young called groundlings. The grey-blue coloration's purpose is debated; Phrastus of Elinhir hypothesizes sky camouflage, while Lady Cinnabar disputes this. In colder regions like Wrothgar, thick-furred Snow Ogres exhibit greater advancement and totemic frost magic. Ogres are considered Old Life from a different age. Malacath claims patronage over them as his little brothers, a kinship Orcs acknowledge. While often tribal and savage, some demonstrate shamanic intelligence. They inhabit wilderness areas across Tamriel, including the Wrothgarian Mountains and Cyrodiil, and are sometimes enslaved or employed as brute labor.
topic_desc_basic: Ogres are large, strong humanoid Goblin-ken found across Tamriel, widely regarded as dim-witted, foul-smelling brutes. They have steely blue or greenish skin, pronounced teeth, and tapered ears. The Daedric Prince Malacath calls them his little brothers. Furred Snow Ogres inhabit cold regions like Wrothgar.

title: Ogre's Puffball
topic_desc: Ogre's Puffball is a fungal ingredient encountered among Morrowind's wilderness flora. Its name identifies it as a puffball mushroom, though detailed botanical descriptions and preferred growing conditions remain poorly documented in standard herbalist references. The ingredient circulates through general floral and herbal supply channels in the region, where practitioners may acquire it for alchemical preparation. Its specific alchemical character is not widely recorded in available texts, leaving its practical applications to those with direct field experience.
topic_desc_basic: Ogre's Puffball is a mushroom-type ingredient found in Morrowind's wilderness. It is recognized by alchemists and herbalists as a potion component, though detailed knowledge of its properties is uncommon.

title: Ohmes
topic_desc: The Ohmes are a bipedal furstock of the Khajiit of Elsweyr, born under the phase of a new Masser and full Secunda. They are said to be the only Khajiit furstock not to receive the blessing of fur. Physically, they resemble elves—specifically Bosmer—though they are sometimes shorter, and have occasionally been described as man-like; however, it is the taller Ohmes-raht who more closely resemble the races of men. To avoid being mistaken for elves, many Ohmes paint or tattoo their faces to present a feline aspect. The Imperial Geographical Society claims they are the most common Khajiit encountered outside of Elsweyr, often serving as adventurers, diplomats, or merchants. Their appearance and natural agility make them excellent infiltrators and thieves.
topic_desc_basic: The Ohmes are a furless, bipedal furstock of Khajiit from Elsweyr who closely resemble Bosmer. To avoid being mistaken for elves, many paint or tattoo their faces to appear feline. They are the most common Khajiit encountered outside of Elsweyr, often as adventurers or diplomats.

title: Olaf and the Dragon
topic_desc: A historical study by Adonato Leotelli examining the celebrated Nord legend of Olaf One-Eye and the dragon Numinex, weighing the heroic narrative against skeptical accounts.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Adonato Leotelli examining the Nord legend of Olaf One-Eye and the dragon Numinex, and the controversy surrounding the tale.

title: Old Fjori the Cove
topic_desc: Old Fjori the Cove is a macabre call-and-response oar-song favored by the sailors of Uld Vraech. The verses recount a dialogue with the titular Fjori, a benighted rogue who chased the dreugh-folk to recover his stolen dagger, only to be beheaded in the ocean depths. The song's dark humor culminates when the questioner asks how a headless man can still sing, at which point the performers make exaggerated gurgling noises until they deem the performance concluded. The ballad reflects the perilous maritime folklore surrounding the dreugh and the grim sensibilities of northern seafarers.
topic_desc_basic: Old Fjori the Cove is a call-and-response oar-song popular among the sailors of Uld Vraech. It recounts the darkly comic tale of the titular rogue, who loses his head to the dreugh-folk in the ocean depths, ending with the performers making gurgling noises when asked how a headless man can sing.

title: Old Man of the Ashlands
topic_desc: Old Man of the Ashlands by Horadin is a narrative tale recounting the experiences of Eiler, an elderly Redguard who has taken up netch herding in Morrowind's ashlands. As the only Redguard herder in living memory, Eiler faces resentment from neighboring Dunmer herdsmen. The story follows his solitary confrontation with a giant cliff racer preying on his herd, drawing on his past as a Legion scout and his youth guarding herds in the Alik'r. The tale explores themes of cultural alienation, self-reliance in old age, and the tension between chosen freedom and its consequences. Eiler's prayers to Tu'whacca and Tava, and his keepsakes of Weltan's poems and Alik'r sand, anchor the narrative in Redguard identity amid an alien land. The work circulates widely across Morrowind's settlements.
topic_desc_basic: Old Man of the Ashlands by Horadin is a widely circulated tale about Eiler, an elderly Redguard netch herder living in Morrowind's ashlands. The story recounts his solitary battle against a giant cliff racer threatening his herd, drawing on his past experience as a Legion scout and his youth in the Alik'r desert. It explores themes of independence, cultural alienation, and perseverance.

title: Old Temple Pamphlet
topic_desc: This ancient pamphlet, estimated to be thousands of years old, preserves an exhortation attributed to Lord Vivec addressing the Dunmer. It frames mortality as a continuation of the struggle against the Sharmat, promising that death gilds the faithful spirit with glory. The text urges the fallen to join their kin beneath the Triune banner in the holy city of the dead, adding their undying souls to a barrier of ghosts that safeguards the House of Veloth forevermore. It proclaims that while mortal weapons may break, the spirit remains uncrushable and untainted, allowing the faithful to defy the Sharmat in death just as they did in life. Through spirit, sword, and faith in ALMSIVI, this united pillar of ancestral spirits is promised ultimate victory.
topic_desc_basic: An ancient pamphlet containing a speech from Lord Vivec to the Dunmer. It urges the faithful to embrace death without fear, promising that their undying spirits will join their ancestors in the holy city of the dead to form a barrier of ghosts that defends the House of Veloth against the Sharmat forever.

title: Olive Oil
topic_desc: Olive oil is a vegetable oil produced by pressing olives, a fruit widely cultivated across Cyrodiil. Alchemists value the pressed oil as an ingredient for its stable properties, while cooks employ it in various preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Olive oil is a vegetable oil pressed from olives, a common Cyrodiilic fruit.

title: Olives
topic_desc: Olives are a fruit commonly found growing in Cyrodiil, widely recognized as a provincial staple. Beyond their culinary role, they are familiar to alchemists and hunters as a natural ingredient harvested from the wild or cultivated groves. While their specific alchemical properties demand specialist knowledge to apply, their abundance ensures they remain a routine sight across the central province.
topic_desc_basic: Olives are a common fruit widely found in Cyrodiil, often used as a provincial food staple.

title: On Daedric Design
topic_desc: A treatise by Nelos Llothri, a former Mages Guild member now with the Tribunal Temple, arguing that Daedric shrine architecture is a divine mathematics rather than mere construction or mimicry. Llothri contends that Boethiah taught ancestors theurgic geometries that bend Mundus toward the supranatural, enabling worshippers to physically reach their gods. Each element captures and amplifies prayer, directing it into the Void; well-built shrines preserve these echoes indefinitely, explaining the chanting heard in abandoned ruins. The author warns that these geometries are volatile: structural decay produces unpredictable effects that thin the barrier with Oblivion, inducing psychological effects tied to the shrine's patron Prince. Llothri rejects parallels to Dwemer tonal architecture as blasphemy, urges carrying Almsivi talismans near deteriorated sites like Ald Sotha and Ald Balaal, and asserts that while the living Tribunal renders such mathematical communion obsolete, ancestral echoes deserve understanding.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Tribunal Temple scholar Nelos Llothri on Daedric shrine architecture. It argues that Daedric ruins are built on divine mathematics that channel prayer to the Daedra, and warns that damaged shrines are dangerous, causing harmful effects on visitors.

title: On Hammerfell
topic_desc: Erramanwe of Sunhold's historical study of Tiber Septim's acquisition of Hammerfell, tracing the Forebear revolt against Crown rule, the Empire's opportunistic intervention and harsh occupation, the Redguard uprising that expelled Imperial forces, and the Treaty of Stros M'kai that established Hammerfell as a self-governing provincial ally.
topic_desc_basic: A historical work by Erramanwe of Sunhold chronicling Tiber Septim's conquest and subsequent loss of Hammerfell, culminating in the Treaty of Stros M'kai, which granted the Redguards self-rule as provincial allies rather than subjects.

title: On Lycanthropy
topic_desc: Varnard Karessen's treatise on lycanthropy is a significant scholarly work cataloging the seven documented forms of the disease across Tamriel. Drawing from a traumatic childhood encounter with a werewolf in Falcrenth, Karessen combines personal observation with field research to detail the nature and habits of lycanthropes. He identifies werewolves as the most ubiquitous strain, alongside werebears, wereboars, werelions, werecrocodiles, werevultures, and the unverified wereshark. The work notably observes that lycanthrope claws function as naturally enchanted weapons, capable of harming magical entities, and that slain werewolves do not revert to human form. Karessen documents that lycanthropy is curable only shortly after infection, with full transformation leaving the victim permanently doomed. He further theorizes that lycanthropes do not attack humans out of dietary necessity—stomach contents reveal more plant matter than flesh—leaving their aggressive behavior an unresolved mystery of madness or a drive to propagate the affliction.
topic_desc_basic: Varnard Karessen's treatise studies the disease lycanthropy, cataloging seven documented forms across Tamriel including werewolves, werebears, wereboars, werelions, werecrocodiles, werevultures, and the rumored wereshark. It observes that lycanthrope claws act as enchanted weapons and that the disease is only curable shortly after infection, before the first transformation.

title: On Purity
topic_desc: Nonesirmi of Dusk's treatise defines Altmeri Purity as Immaculate Degradation: maintaining an uninterrupted ancestral lineage to remain detached from the mortal Mundus. Impurity afflicts those who tied themselves to Mundus, Aetherius, or Oblivion. The work categorizes non-Altmer accordingly: Betmer are pitied beings incapable of grasping their loss, Men are derided for upholding Lorkhan's lie, and Aldmeri splinter groups represent Aedric, philosophical, or Daedric corruptions. Bosmer and Falmer suffered forced Aedric corruption; Ayleids and Dwemer embraced destructive philosophical deviations; and the Chimer fell to Daedric corruption. Nonesirmi argues that the Altmer ultimately distinguished themselves from the Aldmer by deliberately maintaining ancestral detachment, ensuring their immutable status. The treatise reflects a conservative Altmeri worldview that frames the Septimian Empire and its Talos cults as dangerous imitators of Merish divine assimilation.
topic_desc_basic: Nonesirmi of Dusk's treatise defines Altmeri Purity as Immaculate Degradation, the practice of maintaining an unbroken ancestral lineage to remain detached from the mortal Mundus. The work categorizes other races and Merish splinter groups as impure for tying themselves to the Mundus, Aetherius, or Oblivion, framing Altmeri identity as uniquely pristine and deliberately detached.

title: On Sericulture
topic_desc: A treatise by Cyso Mesorath on Nibenean sericulture, framing silk production as a pious communion with the fjyron—the will or spirit—of moths. The work classifies five moth spirits by their nature, diet, and ceremonial requirements. The common Gypsy-Moth yields coarse sailor-silk. The obedient Sphinx-Moth produces pliant, dye-friendly silk valued by Totem Societies. The unruly Glyph-Moth feeds on texts; its brittle silk creates powerful magical scrolls. The Luna-Moth, devoted to Dibella, provides silk for sacred vestments. The greatest, the Ancestor-Moth, consumes mortal flesh to absorb ancestral fjyron. Its silk, harvested only by hand with mantras and alchemicals, forms Ancestor-Cloth that channels ancestral aid. The text stresses strict adherence to tradition, recording lineages, and proper mantras to avoid abominable outcomes.
topic_desc_basic: A Nibenean treatise by Cyso Mesorath on the pious production of silk. It classifies five moth spirits—Gypsy, Sphinx, Glyph, Luna, and Ancestor—detailing their ceremonial care, diets, and the magical or practical uses of their silk.

title: On Stirk
topic_desc: On Stirk by Calixta Avidrian is a historical chronicle tracing Stirk Isle from its first Ayleid settlement through the Third Era. The work details the founding of Ayleid sea-fortresses—Wormusoel, Nagaiarelle, and Vabriasel—built to repel naval invasions, and their abandonment after the Alessian Rebellion. It records the island's 1E 343 conquest by Skalgar Half-Scorned, the establishment of the Marshal of the Isles title, and the Thrassian Plague's near-depopulation of the island. Avidrian documents Stirk's strategic role under the Reman dynasty as a forward outpost against Summerset, its service during the Tiber Wars, and the construction of Duskwatch Keep. The chronicle first records the town of Charach and concludes with recent piracy linked to the Imperial Simulacrum and Iliac Bay unrest, expressing confidence in the West Navy's restoration of Imperial order.
topic_desc_basic: On Stirk by Calixta Avidrian is a historical chronicle of Stirk Isle in the Abecean Sea. The work recounts the island's history from Ayleid settlement through the Third Era, covering its role as a trade harbor, its conquest by Colovian forces, the Thrassian Plague's devastation, and its strategic importance as a military outpost under the Reman and Septim empires.

title: On the Definition of Heresy
topic_desc: On the Definition of Heresy is a theological treatise by Indoril Beroth examining the nature and purpose of heresy within Tribunal doctrine. Building upon Saint Olms's early teachings on heretical thinking, Beroth distinguishes between the Laws Determined—immutable decrees of the Tribunal's celestial triune authority—and the Laws Ordained—breakable precepts established in the mundane world and enforced by House Indoril, the Ordination, and the Temple. Heresy, he argues, violates only the Laws Ordained and cannot threaten the Laws Determined, yet is both important and evil: important because the Tribunal created the circumstances for its existence, evil because it transgresses ordained law. The work addresses a dispute between Temple scholars Golsu Farelas and Ulmelyn Llaryn, whose writings have drawn Ordination scrutiny, and seeks to reconcile their views within the strictures of Determined Law. Beroth envisions an eventual end to heresy across Resdayn.
topic_desc_basic: On the Definition of Heresy by Indoril Beroth is a Temple treatise on the nature of heresy under Tribunal law. It distinguishes between immutable divine decrees and breakable worldly laws enforced by House Indoril and the Ordination, defining heresy as violation of the latter. The work seeks to reconcile a scholarly dispute between two Temple writers within orthodox doctrine.

title: On the Evils of Heresy
topic_desc: A polemical treatise by Temple scholar Ulmelyn Llaryn, fiercely rebutting Golsu Farelas's essay on the theological utility of heresy. Llaryn argues that Farelas dangerously legitimizes opposition to ALMSIVI by claiming enemies test the faithful. Llaryn counters that the strong require no testing, while the weak-willed inevitably fail and must be purged. He insists Temple scholars educate to promote general well-being, not merely to counter Dissident Priests. Addressing Ordinator conduct, Llaryn asserts their violence is consecrated by faith in ALMSIVI, not by the evil of the slain. While acknowledging that Inquisitors must understand heresy to combat it, Llaryn stresses that ordinary faithful must shun it entirely. Critics consider the prose lethargic and intellectually dull, though it serves those seeking to demonstrate Temple piety.
topic_desc_basic: A Temple treatise by Ulmelyn Llaryn attacking Golsu Farelas's arguments on the value of heresy. Llaryn insists heresy provides no benefit, that the weak must be purged, and that Ordinator violence is sanctified by faith in ALMSIVI rather than by the evil of heretics. The work is widely regarded as dull but useful for demonstrating piety.

title: On the Importance of Heresy
topic_desc: A theological treatise by Temple scholar Golsu Farelas arguing that heresy is a necessary cornerstone of the Tribunal faith. Farelas contends that without the House of Troubles, the Sharmat, and dissenting voices like the Dissident Priests, the faithful would lack the opposition required to prove their worth and the Ordinators of War would have no heretic's blood to sanctify their deeds. The work asserts a paradoxical holiness in heresy as a necessary evil. Farelas further argues that naming and containing heresy grants mastery over it, which is why the Temple records and imprisons the worst heresies rather than simply destroying them. He cites the so-called First Heresy—images of the Daughter, the Apprentice, the Mortal, and a foul murder—kept under guard in the Necrom vaults as proof of this doctrine. The text opens with the maxim of Saint Olms: to purge the Corners, one must first enter the House.
topic_desc_basic: A Temple treatise by Golsu Farelas arguing that heresy is necessary for the faithful to prove their worth. It claims the Ordinators' holy war requires heretical opposition to be sanctified, and that the Temple contains the worst heresies in secure vaults to master them through naming.

title: On the Lunar Lattice
topic_desc: A Khajiiti oral account transcribed in Leyawiin, explaining the Lunar Lattice through the perspective of a beggar. The speaker contrasts Khajiiti devotion with the static worship of other faiths, describing the moons as a dynamic, guiding force that shapes Khajiit forms and movements. Using the tides and musical variation as analogies, the narrator argues that motion and change—following the moons' dance—define the Khajiit way, while stillness represents stagnation. Moon-sugar is presented as a vital substance connecting Khajiit to this lunar rhythm, its effects misunderstood by outsiders as mere intoxication. The work offers an informal, experiential window into how the Lunar Lattice governs Khajiiti identity and spirituality.
topic_desc_basic: A transcribed account from a Khajiiti beggar in Leyawiin explaining Khajiiti beliefs. It describes the Lunar Lattice as a dynamic lunar force that guides Khajiiti forms and movements, contrasting this living devotion with the static worship of other cultures.

title: On the Perfection of the Guar
topic_desc: A passionate essay arguing that the guar is the only perfect creature in Tamriel. The anonymous author dismisses claims that dragons or liches hold this distinction, instead championing the guar's docile nature, appealing appearance, proportioned form, and soothing purr as evidence of divine gift. The work recounts the author's first encounter with a guar transforming a miserable day into a joyous one, asserting that the creature's universal lovability renders it without enemies. The tract stands as an enthusiastic, if uncritical, celebration of the beast's temperament and form.
topic_desc_basic: A short essay by an enthusiastic guar admirer arguing that the guar is the most perfect creature in Tamriel, citing its gentle nature, pleasing appearance, and calming purr.

record_links.display_name: On the Perfection of the Guar

title: Onion
topic_desc: Onions are vegetables commonly found across Cyrodiil and Skyrim. In Skyrim, the plants are cultivated on farms. As a common foodstuff, onions feature broadly in regional diets and provisioning. Their alchemical properties are modest, and they hold no particular rarity or significance beyond their widespread culinary use.
topic_desc_basic: Onions are common vegetables found across Cyrodiil and Skyrim, cultivated on farms in the latter province. They are widely used as food.

title: Onyx
topic_desc: Onyx is a dark, lustrous mineral valued as an alchemical ingredient. Its precise properties remain a subject of specialist study, with no universally documented effects established in common alchemical practice. The stone is occasionally sourced from mining deposits across Tamriel, though guaranteed specimens are rare and typically confined to specific curated collections or particular geological yields. Alchemists and hunters who encounter the stone prize it for its potential in esoteric preparations, despite its uncommon occurrence in standard apothecary inventories.
topic_desc_basic: Onyx is a dark, lustrous mineral occasionally used as an alchemical ingredient. It is found in mining deposits across Tamriel.

title: Opal
topic_desc: Opal is a valuable teal-colored gemstone, prized for the wide array of lights that appear to emanate from within. It forms naturally when silica and water gel is pressed into fissures between surrounding rocks before solidifying, producing its characteristic internal luminescence. Though chiefly treasured as a precious gem, opal also finds use as an alchemical ingredient, its mineral properties lending it reagent value. The stone circulates through gem trade networks across Cyrodiil and Hammerfell.
topic_desc_basic: Opal is a valuable teal-colored gemstone famous for the play of light that seems to come from within it. The stone forms when silica-rich water gel hardens inside rock crevices. Beyond its worth as a gem, it also serves as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Orange Lichen
topic_desc: Orange lichen is an uncommon fungal growth native to Morrowind, prized by alchemists for its distinct properties. It thrives primarily in the humid environments of the Othreleth Woods and the Aanthirin region, though it occasionally colonizes subterranean caves in Shipal-Shin. Its vibrant coloration makes it a recognizable specimen for harvesters traversing these territories.
topic_desc_basic: Orange lichen is an uncommon fungus native to Morrowind. It grows mainly in the Othreleth Woods and Aanthirin, and occasionally in Shipal-Shin caves.

title: Orange Moss
topic_desc: Orange moss is a variety of moss native to Morrowind, recognized by its distinctive coloration. It grows in the Aanthirin and the Coronati Basin, where it is gathered as an alchemical ingredient. Its properties make it a subject of interest for practitioners of alchemy and a recognizable resource for hunters and foragers familiar with the region's flora.
topic_desc_basic: Orange moss is a variety of moss native to Morrowind. It grows in the Aanthirin and the Coronati Basin and is gathered as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Orc Creation Story
topic_desc: An Orcish mythographic text recounting the pariah folk's origin through the transformation of Trinimac into Malak, authored by a member of the Afterdark Society.
topic_desc_basic: An Orcish text recounting the origin of the Orcs and their transformation from followers of Trinimac into the iron children of Malak.

title: Orc's Blood
topic_desc: Orc's Blood is an alchemical ingredient of uncertain natural origin, presumably derived from orcs. Its specific properties and alchemical character remain poorly documented, and it sees no widespread use in conventional potion-making. The ingredient is exceptionally rare, absent from common merchant stocks and leveled supply lists, leaving its practical applications largely a matter of speculation among specialized alchemists.
topic_desc_basic: Orc's Blood is a rare alchemical ingredient presumably derived from orcs. It is not found in common supply lists.

title: Orcscrown
topic_desc: Orcscrown is a purple flower native to Morrowind. Among alchemists and hunters, it is recognized as a distinct floral ingredient valued for its specific alchemical properties. Its natural growth in the Morrowind region makes it a familiar resource to those harvesting the local flora for potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Orcscrown is a purple flower native to Morrowind.

title: Orcsurance, a One-Act Comedy
topic_desc: A satirical one-act play by Surru Runuril that mocks the East Empire Company. It depicts an EEC insurance salesman, Basilius, attempting to sell a policy to the Orcish chieftain Mullug in his mountain cave. When Basilius explains that the company pays beneficiary gold for violent deaths, Mullug realizes that killing the insured salesman would spare him blood-money owed to the EEC. The farce premiered at the birthday celebration of House Hlaalu councillor Llathsa Indarys in 3E 405, offending the Kragenmar EEC director, who believed one character was modeled on him.
topic_desc_basic: A satirical one-act play by Surru Runuril that mocks the East Empire Company. It depicts an EEC insurance salesman attempting to sell a policy to an Orcish chieftain, who instead exploits the policy's terms to murder the salesman.

title: Ordolane's Bestiary, vol. 11
topic_desc: Ordolane's Bestiary, vol. 11 is an encyclopedic work cataloging Tamrielic fauna, compiled from reports by savants and naturalists across the Empire and dedicated to Emperor Uriel Septim VII. This volume describes the mudcrab, the Tinmi Dragon, the troll, the mockmouth, and the Kohl Frog. It blends naturalistic observation with folklore and superstition, noting Valenwood funerary mudcrab practices, the Tinmi Dragon's reverence for the Slave Queen, the troll's classification as a revenant beast by the Order of Arkay and Meridian cults, the mockmouth's bizarre origins and aversion to courtesy, and the Kohl Frog's wind-dispersed reproductive cycle. It also records regional customs and beliefs, such as the widespread use of trollbone in armor and medicine, Morrowind's kill-on-sight policy toward Kohl Frogs as suspected Argonian spies, and the Nibenese harvest of the frogs for the hallucinogenic drug Kohllano.
topic_desc_basic: Ordolane's Bestiary, vol. 11 is an encyclopedic catalog of Tamrielic fauna compiled from reports across the Empire and dedicated to Emperor Uriel Septim VII. This volume covers the mudcrab, Tinmi Dragon, troll, mockmouth, and Kohl Frog, blending naturalistic observation with regional folklore and superstition.

title: Ordolane's Bestiary, vol. 17
topic_desc: Ordolane's Bestiary, vol. 17 is an Imperial naturalist compendium dedicated to Emperor Uriel Septim VII that catalogs select Tamrielic fauna through a blend of observation, folklore, and mysticism. It argues the Dreugh are sapient remnants of a diminished ancient civilization rather than mere aquatic beasts. It describes the vicious Wormmouth of the High Rock-Skyrim borderlands, whose hides Reachmen wear as armor and whose origin Nords attribute to Shor's corpse. It details the Hare's reputed sex-shifting, prolific breeding, and use in Bosmer disguise and folk cures. It recounts Nordic tales of the Snow Whale as a joy-bringing singer of clouds, and traces all moths to the Luna Moth, whose aurbic migrations map safe currents for mystics and whose connection to the dead underpins the Cult of the Ancestor Moth.
topic_desc_basic: Ordolane's Bestiary, vol. 17 is a naturalist compendium dedicated to Emperor Uriel Septim VII that describes several creatures of Tamriel, including the sapient Dreugh, the Wormmouth, the Hare, the Snow Whale, and the Moth, blending reported fact with folklore and mystic tradition.

title: Ordolane's Bestiary, vol. 9
topic_desc: Ordolane's Bestiary, vol. 9 is a naturalist compendium claiming to catalog Tamrielic fauna through reports from savants and mystics. Dedicated to Emperor Uriel Septim VII, the ninth volume presents a superstitious and mythologized viewpoint, blending ecological observation with folk belief. It describes the dwimmerwort as a Bosmer-related beast that confuses travelers when trodden upon; the carnelian sea-snail of the Niben, whose red dye is mandated for Imperial heraldry and whose captive size is supposedly unlimited; the absurdly fragile bellfrog, which bursts from almost any stimulus; the shalk, a fire-breathing Morrowind beetle whose volatile chitin precludes Dunmer crafting; and the spriggan, claimed to be wooden constructs crafted by invisible spirits in Kynareth's likeness, earning Dibella's hatred. The work's significance lies in its illustration of how Imperial natural history interweaves genuine fauna with credulous folklore.
topic_desc_basic: Ordolane's Bestiary, vol. 9 is a naturalist volume dedicated to Emperor Uriel Septim VII that catalogs Tamrielic fauna, blending creature descriptions with superstitious folklore and myth.

title: Orichalc Grains
topic_desc: Orichalc Grains are a granular form of orichalc ore, valued by alchemists as an ingredient. They are obtained from mining rather than from flora or fauna, distinguishing them from most organic alchemical materials. The grains are not commonly encountered in general trade or leveled supplies, suggesting limited circulation outside specialized circles.
topic_desc_basic: Orichalc Grains are a mineral ingredient derived from orichalc ore. They are obtained through mining rather than gathered from plants or creatures, and are not widely available in general trade.

title: Orichalcum Ore
topic_desc: Orichalcum ore is a metallic mineral sought by alchemists and smiths. Mined from subterranean deposits, its alchemical character remains poorly documented in general scholarship, though specialists recognize it for its distinct metallurgical and arcane properties. The raw ore requires refinement before use in durable craftsmanship.
topic_desc_basic: Orichalcum ore is a metallic mineral harvested from subterranean deposits, valued by alchemists and smiths alike.

title: Origin of the Sload
topic_desc: A scholarly work by Flavius Lupus recounting the Sload creation myth, the K'Grua, as related by a member of the Psijic Order. Set during the Ehlnofex Wars, the myth describes how the necromancer N'Gyre raised fallen comrades as undead, provoking the wrath of Trinimac, Champion of Auri-El. After repeated attempts, Trinimac slew N'Gyre and cast his remains into the Western Sea. From the mingling of sea foam and corpse-sludge emerged the Sload, while fragments too small to sink became the islands of Thras. The text claims necromantic power is innate to the Sload from birth, that they worship N'Gyre alone, and that they make pacts with Daedra Princes including Namira and Peryite toward some undisclosed purpose known only to their leaders. The author notes he does not know this secret end.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Flavius Lupus recounting the Sload creation myth, the K'Grua, as told to him by a Psijic Order member. The myth describes how the necromancer N'Gyre was slain by Trinimac during the Ehlnofex Wars, and from his remains cast into the sea the Sload race and the islands of Thras were born.

title: Origins of the Raki
topic_desc: A scholarly work by Hvaldyth tracing the introduction and proliferation of the raki, deceptive predatory beasts now inhabiting Haafingar's western pine forests. The text attributes their arrival to a diplomatic gift from King Orgnum of Pyandonea to Potema in 3E 110, noting their initial use in hunting and their subsequent association with the Wolf Queen's notorious reign. Following Potema's fall in 3E 137, skaldic legend holds that the creatures turned on their maormer handlers, escaped Castle Solitude, and established a feral population that remains a persistent danger to travelers.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Hvaldyth about the raki, predatory beasts of Haafingar. It claims they were originally given to Potema by King Orgnum of Pyandonea in 3E 110 and went feral after the War of the Red Diamond.

title: Orlukh Clan
topic_desc: The Orlukh Clan is a relatively young vampire bloodline inhabiting the Roth Roryn region. Composed entirely of former Orcish legionaries, the clan formed after the soldiers pooled their wealth near the end of their Imperial service to purchase the Anbarsud mine. The mine proved barren, and an ill-fated excavation breached the ancient stronghold of Romayon, exposing the legionaries to the vampire Varos, who spread his curse to them. The group's former leader, Orlukh gro-Othmog, lends the clan its name and maintains a cordial relationship with Varos. The Orlukh harbor deep resentment toward the anonymous seller who missold them the mine, which now serves as their bloodsoaked lair. As a bloodline, Orlukh vampires exhibit enhanced endurance and skill in axe craft, armoring, and medium armor. They are hostile toward the other vampire clans, Ashlanders, and the Tribunal Temple, and hold particular enmity toward the Great Houses and Imperial factions.
topic_desc_basic: The Orlukh Clan is a vampire bloodline based in the Roth Roryn region. Its members are former Orcish soldiers of the Imperial Legion who were turned into vampires after purchasing and excavating the barren Anbarsud mine.

title: Orlukh's Cleaver
topic_desc: Orlukh's Cleaver is a weapon associated with Orlukh gro-Othmog, an Elder of the Orlukh vampire clan. It is currently found in Anbarsud within the Roth Roryn region.
topic_desc_basic: Orlukh's Cleaver is a weapon belonging to Orlukh gro-Othmog, an Elder of the Orlukh vampire clan, who resides in Anbarsud in the Roth Roryn region.

title: Ornada Egg
topic_desc: Ornada eggs are laid by the ornada queen and serve as a foodstuff commonly consumed by the Dark Elves of Morrowind. As an ingredient, they are familiar to alchemists and hunters who deal with the region's fauna, and they circulate readily through trade and random merchant stocks alongside other common eggs and cheap Dunmer provisions.
topic_desc_basic: Ornada eggs are laid by the ornada queen and are a common foodstuff eaten by the Dark Elves of Morrowind.

title: Ornada Meat
topic_desc: Ornada meat is harvested from the ornada, a species of insect native to Morrowind. These creatures are commonly found along riverbanks, with the greatest concentrations along the Thirr River and smaller populations near the Pryai River, the Kanit River, and Lake Boethiah. The meat serves as a common foodstuff among Dunmer, frequently appearing in cheap provisions and regional ingredient supplies. It is also specifically used in ornada stuffing. Alchemists value it as a readily available ingredient, and hunters familiar with Morrowind's riverine fauna routinely collect it.
topic_desc_basic: Ornada meat comes from the ornada, a riverbank insect found in Morrowind, especially along the Thirr River. It is a common food ingredient in Dunmer cuisine, often used in stuffing.

title: Orphaned Dancer
topic_desc: The Orphaned Dancer was a vessel that sank off the coast of the Sacred Peninsula near Necrom after its cargo hold caught fire. The blaze and subsequent slaughterfish attacks killed most of the crew, including Captain Danir Sildreth. Only one survivor, Travin Benelas, was pulled from the water. Benelas later worked as a clerk in the Necrom harbormaster's office before retiring to Romithren Monastery. The ship's logs are retained by the Temple authorities in Necrom.
topic_desc_basic: The Orphaned Dancer was a ship that sank near Necrom after a fire. Its sole survivor, Travin Benelas, later worked as a clerk in the city before retiring to Romithren Monastery.

title: Oyster Meat
topic_desc: Oyster Meat is the chewy flesh harvested from inside oysters. Oysters thrive in the coastal waters of the Dasek Marsh and Stirk Isle regions of Cyrodiil, where they reliably yield this edible substance. The meat presents in two distinct forms, long and round, and is utilized in regional food supplies and alchemical practices. It circulates through trade via random provisions and sea-food distributions.
topic_desc_basic: Oyster Meat is chewy flesh harvested from oysters, which are commonly found in the Dasek Marsh and Stirk Isle regions of Cyrodiil.

title: Padomaic Sage Leaf
topic_desc: Padomaic sage leaves are harvested from the padomaic sage, a plant endemic to the Padomaic Isles east of Tamriel. The flora is virtually unknown on the mainland, making its leaves a scarce alchemical commodity sourced exclusively from that remote archipelago.
topic_desc_basic: Padomaic sage leaves are taken from the padomaic sage plant, which grows only in the Padomaic Isles east of Tamriel.

title: Painted Peoples
topic_desc: Painted Peoples: Tattooing across the Empire by Vantis Orvilius. The author interviews tattooed individuals across Imperial territories, documenting the cultural and personal significance of their markings. A Reachman veteran describes reclaiming his identity through ancestral patterns after the Legion misregistered his heritage. A Dunmer oathman explains facial tattoos as expressions of ancestral pain and deliverance, and holy words on the feet making each step a prayer. A Nord elder recounts receiving hawk tattoos honoring Kyne's guidance during a perilous hunt. A Nibenese cultist displays serpent coils and Akaviri script as vibrant declarations of faith. The work reveals tattooing as a diverse Imperial practice for asserting identity, devotion, and heritage.
topic_desc_basic: Painted Peoples by Vantis Orvilius is a study of tattooing across the Empire. Through interviews, it explores how various peoples use skin markings to express ancestral heritage, religious devotion, and personal identity.

title: Palm Fruit
topic_desc: Palm fruit is harvested from silver palm trees, a variety known to grow in Lorchwuir Heath and the Druadach Highlands of Skyrim. The fruit serves as a gathered ingredient for alchemists and hunters traversing these Reach-adjacent regions.
topic_desc_basic: Palm fruit is a food and alchemical ingredient harvested from silver palm trees, which grow in parts of Skyrim.

title: Parastylus Meat
topic_desc: Parastylus Meat is the flesh of the parastylus, a large insect that inhabits dark, inaccessible caves. It is valued by alchemists for its paradoxical utility in potions concerning paralyzation, as the meat possesses both paralytic and curative properties for such afflictions.
topic_desc_basic: Parastylus Meat comes from the parastylus, a large cave-dwelling insect. It is useful for brewing potions related to paralyzation.

title: Parastylus Shell Fragment
topic_desc: A parastylus shell fragment is a chitinous piece harvested from the parastylus, a large insect that inhabits dark, inaccessible caves. The creature's robust carapace yields these fragments, which alchemists and hunters value for their properties. The shell's resilient nature makes it a recognized ingredient in preparatory circles, sought for its alchemical character.
topic_desc_basic: A parastylus shell fragment is a piece of the shell of the parastylus, a large insect found in dark, inaccessible caves.

title: Parastylus Venom Sac
topic_desc: A gland harvested from the parastylus creature, valued for its alchemical properties.
topic_desc_basic: A venom sac taken from a parastylus, used in alchemy.

title: Parsleydown
topic_desc: Parsleydown is a botanical ingredient of uncertain specific origin. Alchemists value it for its stable properties and employ it in various preparations. It circulates through trade networks and appears in general ingredient stocks, including those in Mournhold, indicating recognized utility in conventional alchemical practice.
topic_desc_basic: Parsleydown is a botanical ingredient used in alchemy. It is traded through general merchant stocks and can be found in Mournhold.

title: Passion Fruit
topic_desc: Passion fruit is a variety of edible fruit found in Tamriel. While recognized as a foodstuff, its specific alchemical properties remain largely undetermined and are not widely recorded in standard apothecary references. The fruit does not commonly appear in the wild through known gathering routes or leveled harvests, making it a relatively uncommon ingredient for routine potion-making or sustenance. Its natural growing conditions and precise regional origins are not documented in standard botanical surveys.
topic_desc_basic: Passion fruit is an edible fruit found in Tamriel. It is recognized as a foodstuff, though it is relatively uncommon and not typically found through standard harvesting or gathering practices.

title: Pearmain Apple
topic_desc: A variety of red, round fruit harvested from apple trees, widely found across Skyrim.
topic_desc_basic: A common red, round fruit from apple trees found across Skyrim.

title: Penitent's Ring
topic_desc: The Penitent's Ring is a relic of Saint Aralor kept at the Monastery of St. Aralor in Roth Roryn. Used in the pilgrimage rite to the Shrine of Forgiveness, the ring embodies the dual nature of penance. Its enchantment calms humanoids and demoralizes creatures, but inflicts health damage upon the wearer, reflecting the suffering inherent in atonement. The ring is entrusted to pilgrims undertaking the rite and is expected to be returned to the monastery upon completion.
topic_desc_basic: The Penitent's Ring is a relic of Saint Aralor housed at the Monastery of St. Aralor in Roth Roryn. It is worn by pilgrims undertaking the rite at the Shrine of Forgiveness.

title: Pension of the Ancestor Moth
topic_desc: This initiatory pamphlet instructs novitiates of the Order of the Ancestor Moth on their duties and the order's nature. It explains that Ancestor Moths carry the fjyron—an ancestor's will to peace—which can be sung into silk to create wondrous garments. The order's adepts gain prescience through ancestral wisdom, granting them the sole privilege of interpreting the Elder Scrolls, writings that exceed even the gods. This insight exacts a cumulative toll; each reading blinds the priest longer, until a final, sublime understanding leaves them permanently sightless. The monastery's sighted members then serve these blind monks, who dwell underground tending the moths, harvesting silk, and weaving ancestral genealogies. The text also recounts Gudrun, a blinded priest who introduced martial teachings so monks could defend themselves, and charges novitiates to learn her peaceful fist and provide for the order's needs.
topic_desc_basic: An initiatory pamphlet for novitiates of the Order of the Ancestor Moth. It outlines the order's veneration of Ancestor Moths, whose silk carries ancestral power, and explains their exclusive privilege of interpreting the Elder Scrolls—a practice that progressively and permanently blinds its readers. The text also details the sighted members' duty to serve the blinded monks.

title: Peony Seeds
topic_desc: Peony Seeds are small brown seeds harvested from peony flowers. As a botanical ingredient, they are recognized within alchemical practice for their floral origin and modest properties. They are gathered and traded by practitioners of the craft, typically sourced from regions where the parent flower grows naturally.
topic_desc_basic: Peony Seeds are small brown seeds that come from peony flowers. They are used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Peoples of the Reach
topic_desc: Antony Cestus, an Imperial Cartographer, composed this ethnographic account following two visits to western Skyrim's Reach, the first after the War of Bend'r-Mahk in 3E 397 and the second in 3E 417. The work surveys the region's principal inhabitants: the Reachmen, of mixed Breton and High Elf descent, who maintain a distinct shamanic culture despite enduring persecution, though some rebel violently against Nordic rule; Orc tribes, many of which departed for Nova Orsinium following its rebuilding, leaving mostly peaceful holdouts; Nords, whom Cestus finds more combative than their kin elsewhere, singling out the Bear Clan of Karthgad as likely petty criminals rather than the defenders they claim to be; and Redguards and Bretons, who coexist uneasily with Nords, particularly in Karthwasten where a walled Redguard quarter minimizes sectarian violence. Cestus balances personal misadventure with observation, arguing the Reach possesses one of Tamriel's richest cultural mixes.
topic_desc_basic: Antony Cestus, an Imperial Cartographer, authored this account of western Skyrim's Reach and its inhabitants. The work describes the Reachmen, Orcs, Nords, Redguards, and Bretons sharing the troubled region, noting both their peaceful coexistence and the persistent sectarian tensions and violence that plague the area.

title: Peridot
topic_desc: Peridot is a bright green and especially rare gemstone. Daedra worshippers often use precious gems as offerings at their altars, making such shrines potential sources for the stone. It also sees trade among jewelers and alchemists. As an alchemical ingredient, peridot possesses distinct properties valued by practitioners, though its scarcity makes it a costly and uncommon reagent.
topic_desc_basic: Peridot is a bright green and especially rare gemstone. It is sometimes found as an offering at daedric shrines or sold by jewelers and alchemists.

title: Perrif's Lotus Seeds
topic_desc: Perrif's lotus seeds are harvested from Perrif's lotus, a water flower native to the Dasek Marsh of Cyrodiil. The plant also thrives in cultivated fountains and water features within urbanized areas. Alchemists and hunters value the seeds for their alchemical properties.
topic_desc_basic: Perrif's lotus seeds come from Perrif's lotus, a water flower that grows in the Dasek Marsh of Cyrodiil and in urban fountains.

title: Persarine Blossom
topic_desc: Persarine blossoms are flowers harvested from persarine plants, a flora known to grow in Lorchwuir Heath and the Druadach Highlands of Skyrim. Prized for their numerous restorative properties, the blossoms are routinely dried and exported across Tamriel, making them a valued commodity in alchemical practice.
topic_desc_basic: Persarine blossoms are flowers from Skyrim known for their restorative properties. They are commonly dried and exported across Tamriel.

title: Philosophies of Thought
topic_desc: Philosophies of Thought denotes a classified section of scholarly texts encompassing philosophical and religious traditions from across the known world. The collection houses the fundamental scriptures of both the Imperial Cult and Morrowind's Tribunal Temple, alongside diverse tomes on global customs. As an introductory Temple tract tailored for Westerners, Fellowship of the Temple is recommended and held in multiple copies. The collection is strictly curated to comply with Imperial and Temple law; consequently, heretical texts are entirely excluded from its holdings.
topic_desc_basic: Philosophies of Thought is a scholarly collection of philosophical and religious texts. It holds the fundamental scriptures of the Imperial Cult and the Tribunal Temple, alongside tomes on global traditions. The curated selection excludes heretical texts to comply with Imperial and Temple law.

title: Physicalities of Werewolves
topic_desc: Reman Crex's 'Experimentation in the Physicalities of the Werewolf' is a morbid anatomical treatise documenting the author's decades-long vivisection of live lycanthropes. Driven by curiosity and hatred for the unnatural, Crex measured skeletal and muscular changes during transformation—recording significant increases in shoulder width, arm length, and foot size—and observed internal organ shifts, noting the heart swells first. He also tested botanical remedies directly on exposed organs, finding wolfsbane renders bones brittle and belladonna juice shrivels veins, causing fatal cardiac detachment. The work is significant as a rare, if ethically abhorrent, empirical study of lycanthropic physiology and the internal effects of traditional remedies.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise by Reman Crex documenting his morbid vivisection of live werewolves to study their anatomical transformations and test the internal effects of botanical remedies like wolfsbane and belladonna.

title: Pierce Thine Everliving Life
topic_desc: Pierce Thine Everliving Life is a bawdy poem addressed to a warrior named Jalir, celebrating him as both champion and lover. The work employs martial imagery—spears, pikes, and battlefield strikes—as double entendre for intimate acts, juxtaposing the ever-present proximity of death in combat with sensual desire. The title itself carries layered meaning, evoking both martial violence and carnal union against the notion of enduring life. The poem's viewpoint is that of an admiring lover who dreams of Jalir's prowess and beckons him to return from the fray. It stands as an example of erotic warrior verse that deliberately blurs the boundary between the violence of battle and the passion of the bedchamber, a thematic convergence found in martial literary traditions across Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: Pierce Thine Everliving Life is a bawdy poem addressed to a warrior named Jalir, using martial imagery of spears and battle strikes as double entendre for intimate acts. It celebrates Jalir as both champion and lover, blending themes of combat and sensual desire.

title: Pike Meat
topic_desc: Pike meat is flesh harvested from the pike, a species of freshwater fish found in waterways such as the Karth River in Skyrim. As a foodstuff, it serves as common sustenance and an alchemical ingredient. Its properties make it a familiar resource to hunters who catch the fish and alchemists who process its meat for various preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Pike meat is flesh taken from the pike, a freshwater fish found in rivers such as the Karth in Skyrim. It is commonly used as food.

title: Pikeperch Meat
topic_desc: Pikeperch meat is harvested from the pikeperch, a freshwater fish native to the Karth River in Skyrim. Valued as a foodstuff, the flesh is also utilized by alchemists for its inherent properties. The fish's riverine habitat dictates its availability to hunters and fishermen familiar with Skyrim's waterways.
topic_desc_basic: Pikeperch meat comes from the pikeperch, a freshwater fish found in the Karth River in Skyrim. It is commonly eaten as food.

title: Pilgrim's Gel
topic_desc: Pilgrim's Gel is a botanical reagent of uncertain natural origin, occasionally harvested by alchemists and hunters. Its properties suggest a floral or plant-derived exudate, though the specific flora that yields it remains a matter of specialist debate rather than common record. The gel is valued in alchemical practice for its solvent and reactive character. Specimens are rare and no guaranteed sources are known; the substance appears sporadically in the wild, with the most reliable—though still infrequent—yields reported from the region surrounding Mournhold. Its scarcity makes it a reagent sought by practiced alchemists rather than general merchants.
topic_desc_basic: Pilgrim's Gel is a rare botanical reagent occasionally found growing in the Mournhold region. Alchemists value it for its useful properties, though it is difficult to obtain.

title: Pilgrim's Petals
topic_desc: Pilgrim's Petals are a floral ingredient of uncertain specific origin and alchemical character. The sparse surviving records confirm only their existence as a recognizable alchemical reagent; their precise properties, appearance, and natural habitat remain undocumented in standard herbalistic texts. They see circulation in the ingredient trade, particularly within Mournhold's markets.
topic_desc_basic: Pilgrim's Petals are a floral ingredient traded in alchemical markets, notably in Mournhold.

title: Pink Pearl
topic_desc: Pink Pearls are rare pearls occasionally found within clams on the sea floor. Prized by alchemists for their uncommon properties, they are considerably more difficult to obtain than standard pearls, requiring either careful diving or fortunate trade. Their distinct hue distinguishes them from common varieties.
topic_desc_basic: Pink Pearls are rare pearls sometimes found inside clams on the sea floor.

title: Platinum Ore
topic_desc: Platinum Ore is a rare metallic mineral valued as both a precious commodity and an alchemical ingredient. Mined from subterranean deposits across Tamriel, the ore yields a heavy, silvery-white metal sought by smiths and metallurgists for its resilience and luster. In alchemy, practitioners prize the ground mineral for its intrinsic properties, utilizing it in various preparations. Its scarcity ensures that platinum remains a luxury material, with uncovered deposits representing a significant find for any miner or traveling alchemist.
topic_desc_basic: Platinum Ore is a rare and valuable metallic mineral. It is sought after for its silvery-white metal and is used in both smithing and alchemy.

title: Pocket Guide to the Empire
topic_desc: The Pocket Guide to the Empire is an encyclopedic survey of the Empire and its territories, commissioned by the Imperial Geographical Society and first published in CE 864 under the authority of Emperor Tiber Septim. The first edition provides an imperial viewpoint of provincial geography, history, and culture, framing Cyrodiil as the destined heart of Tamrielic human civilization. It details the divergence between the martial, traditional Colovian West and the cosmopolitan, arcane Nibenese East, tracing their cycles of separation and unification from the Alessian Reformation through Reman's Second Empire to Tiber Septim's founding of the Third Empire. As a work of state-sponsored scholarship promulgated during Tiber's conquests, it serves as both geographical reference and ideological justification for Imperial dominion.
topic_desc_basic: The Pocket Guide to the Empire is a geographical and historical survey of the Empire and its surroundings, published by the Imperial Geographical Society in CE 864 under Emperor Tiber Septim's authority. It describes the lands, customs, and history of Imperial territories.

title: Poem for Drolora
topic_desc: A romantic poem addressed to a figure named Drolora, who dwells under the protection of a fearsome Warrior. The speaker confesses a hidden, longing heart and praises Drolora's beauty above jewels and precious metals. The verses question whether love can survive crossing the river of glass that separates them, or if the Warrior will forcibly halt it. The speaker recounts facing this guardian armed but being disarmed by dreadful events, ultimately pleading for Drolora's forgiveness. The work captures the tension between forbidden affection and an insurmountable, protective obstacle.
topic_desc_basic: A poem expressing a speaker's love for Drolora, who is guarded by a Warrior. It questions whether their love can cross a river of glass and survive the guardian, ending with a plea for forgiveness after the speaker is disarmed.

title: Poison Bloom Bulb
topic_desc: Poison Bloom Bulbs are the luminous central growths of Poison Bloom plants, a flora typically found deep within the Othreleth Woods of Morrowind. The bulb emits a visible glow that distinguishes it from the surrounding vegetation, aiding gatherers in its collection. The bulb serves as an alchemical ingredient valued by practitioners familiar with the region's woodland flora.
topic_desc_basic: The glowing center of Poison Bloom plants, gathered from the deep Othreleth Woods of Morrowind and used in alchemy.

title: Polyhedrascope
topic_desc: The Polyhedrascope is a helmet of suspected Daedric origin, distinguished by its otherworldly design. When intact, the artifact grants the wearer the ability to detect numerous types of entities. Its unusual properties make it an object of considerable scholarly interest regarding Daedric craftsmanship and enchantment, though it is typically found in a state of disrepair.
topic_desc_basic: The Polyhedrascope is a helmet of suspected Daedric origin. When intact, it grants the wearer the ability to detect numerous types of entities, making it a notable artifact of Daedric craftsmanship.

title: Polyp Pear
topic_desc: A pear-like growth of uncertain natural origin, valued by alchemists and hunters for its properties.
topic_desc_basic: A pear-like growth of uncertain natural origin, valued by alchemists and hunters.

title: Pomegranate
topic_desc: Pomegranates are a type of fruit growing on shrubs, found in Morrowind and across the Alik'r Desert. They hold deep cultural significance in Hammerfell; the Redguards of Sentinel cultivate them along the green shoreline, and the kingdom celebrates Koomu Alezer'i by eating the fruit in honor of Grandee Yaghoub. Pomegranate wine is the most popular vintage in the Alik'r, and the fruit serves as an ingredient in the native dish seared venomsteaks. In Tribunal mythology, the fruit lends its name to the Pomegranate Banquet, a forced wedding ceremony where Molag Bal summoned his minions, strung pomegranates across the Morrowind badlands, and raised tents to approach Vivec in the ash wastes.
topic_desc_basic: Pomegranates are shrub-growing fruits cultivated in Morrowind and Hammerfell. In the Alik'r Desert, pomegranate wine is the most popular vintage, and the fruit is used in seared venomsteaks. Redguards celebrate Koomu Alezer'i by eating them.

title: Pork
topic_desc: Pork is the flesh of pigs, domesticated animals commonly raised on farms throughout Tamriel. Valued as a staple foodstuff, it serves as a familiar ingredient in both rustic cookery and alchemical practice. Its widespread availability through general provisions and merchant stock makes it a readily accessible material for alchemists and hunters seeking basic reagents.
topic_desc_basic: Pork is meat from domesticated pigs raised on farms. It is a common foodstuff and alchemical ingredient.

title: Porous Exidia
topic_desc: Porous Exidia is a species of mushroom native to Morrowind. It is recognized by alchemists and foragers as a distinct fungal ingredient, though it is not reliably found in any fixed location and must instead be gathered where it sporadically appears in the wild. Its name suggests a perforated or spongy cap structure, consistent with the appearance of certain fungal growths. Alchemists value it for its properties in potion-making, and hunters and gatherers encounter it during excursions through Morrowind's varied terrain. Because it does not grow in predictable abundance, it is considered a somewhat uncommon find rather than a staple reagent.
topic_desc_basic: Porous Exidia is a type of mushroom native to Morrowind. It is known to foragers and alchemists as an ingredient gathered from the wild, though it is not reliably found in any particular place and must be sought where it chance-grows.

title: Potato
topic_desc: The potato is a cultivated root vegetable widely grown across Cyrodiil and Skyrim.
