The artifact's nature and the full extent of its enchantments remain poorly understood by surface-dwelling scholars, as the Dreugh and their holdings are rarely accessible to outsiders. The Scepter's very name suggests properties tied to transgression or the breaking of boundaries, though specific accounts of its powers are scarce in Tamrielic literature. Its association with a Dreugh queen places it within the broader context of Dreugh civilization, a reclusive aquatic species that periodically emerges during specific phases of their life cycle. The weapon's presence in Paruddma's possession underscores the martial authority of Dreugh royalty.
topic_desc_basic: The Scepter of Violation is a powerful morningstar wielded by the Dreugh queen Paruddma. It is located in the depths of Paruddma's Maw, an underwater Dreugh lair.

title: Scone
topic_desc: Scones are baked goods originating from Cyrodiil, where they are commonly produced and consumed as a staple foodstuff. As a culinary ingredient, they serve primarily as nourishment rather than an alchemical reagent, though they are handled by provisioners and food merchants across the region. Their preparation follows traditional baking methods, and they circulate widely through Cyrodiilic trade networks and food supply lists.
topic_desc_basic: Scones are baked goods commonly found in Cyrodiil, widely available as a foodstuff through local trade and provisioners.

title: Scrapling Butterfly Wing
topic_desc: Scrapling Butterfly Wings are delicate membranous wings taken from the Scrapling, a species of butterfly native to Skyrim. These diurnal insects are active only during daylight hours, and each specimen typically yields a pair of wings when harvested. The wings are valued by alchemists for their inherent properties, though they are not commonly stocked in any fixed location and must instead be gathered directly from the field. Scrapling Butterfly Wings circulate through certain regional ingredient collections associated with Skyrim's Reach country, reflecting their availability in that rugged northern landscape. For hunters and alchemists traveling Skyrim's daytime skies, the Scrapling represents a reliable if modest source of reagent material, gathered by catching the living insect rather than by looting static deposits.
topic_desc_basic: Scrapling Butterfly Wings are harvested from the Scrapling, a species of butterfly found in Skyrim. These diurnal insects appear only during daylight hours and yield wings when caught. The wings are used as alchemical ingredients.

title: Scrib Pie
topic_desc: Scrib pie is a baked foodstuff prepared from the flesh of scribs, the larval form of the kwama. Common throughout Morrowind, it features prominently in the Dunmer diet alongside bread and small kwama eggs. As an alchemical ingredient, it exhibits restorative properties that replenish bodily vigor. Its simple preparation and the ready availability of scribs from kwama colonies make it an inexpensive staple among the common populace.
topic_desc_basic: Scrib pie is a common baked dish made from scribs, the young of kwama, widely eaten throughout Morrowind. It is a simple, inexpensive food often found alongside bread and kwama eggs in local markets and pantries.

title: Sea Urchin Meat
topic_desc: Sea urchin meat is the yellow, creamy flesh harvested from sea urchins dwelling on the seafloor along the coasts of Cyrodiil. Prized by alchemists for its distinct properties, the ingredient requires cracking open the spiny marine creature to extract the rich interior. Hunters and beachcombers gather the urchins from their oceanic habitat to supply this provender to apothecaries and markets.
topic_desc_basic: Sea urchin meat is a yellow, creamy flesh harvested from sea urchins found on the seafloor off the coasts of Cyrodiil.

title: Seafarer's Ring
topic_desc: The Seafarer's Ring is a unique enchanted ring that confers a constant Water Walking effect upon its wearer. It is associated with the Unusual Shipwreck, a vessel found curiously stranded high up in the Roth Roryn hills of mainland Morrowind, far from any navigable waters. The ring's origin and how it came to rest in such an improbable location remain unknown.
topic_desc_basic: The Seafarer's Ring is a unique enchanted ring that grants its wearer a constant Water Walking effect. It is found at the Unusual Shipwreck, located high in the Roth Roryn hills of mainland Morrowind.

title: Seagull Egg
topic_desc: Seagull eggs are small blue eggs laid by seagulls. They are found in nests built on rocks and in high places along the Strident Coast and the Abecean Sea in Cyrodiil. Alchemists value them for their properties, and hunters gather them from coastal rookeries.
topic_desc_basic: Seagull eggs are small blue eggs laid by seagulls along the Strident Coast and the Abecean Sea in Cyrodiil. They are found in nests built on rocks and in high places.

title: Sermon of the Saints
topic_desc: A Tribunal Temple doctrinal work expounding the theological significance of the Eleven Saints of ALMSIVI. The text interprets passages from the Sermons of Vivec to argue that the saints are the immortal gates to the divine, replacing the void left by the failed Sharmat. It asserts that the relationship between the Tribunal and the saints is reciprocal: the gods work through the saints, yet also draw inspiration from their sacrifices and suffering. Citing Vivek's description of the number eleven as inelegant, the treatise claims this very inelegance is a blessing, as the saints—drawn from the poor, sick, and troubled—serve as vital intercessors and harbingers of the sacred word, essential for the faithful to reach ALMSIVI.
topic_desc_basic: A Temple text explaining the importance of the Eleven Saints of ALMSIVI, describing them as the gateways to the gods who filled the void left by the traitorous Sharmat.

title: Seven Families, Volume 1
topic_desc: A scholarly study of the first three families of House Hlaalu, tracing their origins from the Velothi exodus through their current political standing in Narsis. Milara Rethan details the First Family's founding by Narsara Hla-Alu as wardens of the dead and keepers of Narsis's ancestral catacombs, a sacred duty that keeps them detached from politics. The Second Family, established by Tharel Hlaalu, vassalized neighboring clans and rose to dominate the Hlaalu Council. Under High Hlaalu Pasoroth, they leveraged mercenary service during the Imperial interregnum to forge lasting Western connections and secure the Grandmastership. Though still the most powerful family under High Hlaalu Athires, their influence is waning amid the rise of Kragenmoor and the opening of Vvardenfell. The Third Family's history is lost, its leaders assassinated by the Second Family during the Age of the Warring Houses.
topic_desc_basic: A historical text by Milara Rethan covering the first three of the Seven Families of House Hlaalu. It details the First Family's role as keepers of Narsis's catacombs, the Second Family's political dominance and Western mercenary connections, and the Third Family's destruction in the Age of the Warring Houses.

title: Seven Families, Volume 2
topic_desc: A historical study by Milara Rethan examining the latter four families of Clan Hlaalu. It details the Fourth Family's submission and relocation as House Hlaalo, the Fifth Family's mercantile resurgence in Kragenmoor, the Sixth Family's inter-provincial trade networks and role in founding the Hlaalu Council Company, and the Seventh Family's origin in the Seyda Neen disaster. The work highlights the diverse paths through which these lineages secured influence, from Elder Council seats to maritime enterprise.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly study of the final four families of Clan Hlaalu, documenting their distinct origins, mercantile ventures, and current influence within and beyond Morrowind.

title: Seven Varieties of Shadows
topic_desc: Seven Varieties of Shadows is an esoteric alchemical treatise by No Loss Red-Hand. The work categorizes seven distinct types of shadow, each produced or manipulated through specific material applications: the direct shadow of sunlight, the oblique shadow bent by dust, the effulgent shadow expanded by bitters, the defensive shadow solidified by burning flowerspice, the numbing shadow applied with ground resin, the imbecilic shadow induced by chewing wickstems, and the everted shadow wrought with hound's flesh. The text frames these alchemical processes as revelations learned at the feet of an unnamed master and concludes with invocations to the Daedric Prince Namira, linking the manipulation of shadow to her sphere of influence.
topic_desc_basic: Seven Varieties of Shadows is a treatise by No Loss Red-Hand detailing seven types of shadow and the alchemical ingredients used to manipulate them, framed as teachings devoted to the Daedric Prince Namira.

title: Shadowfly Blossom
topic_desc: Shadowfly Blossoms are bright purple flowers harvested from the shadowfly plant. The plant grows in the Vorndgad Forest and the Druadach Highlands of Skyrim. Alchemists and hunters value the blossom for its properties in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Shadowfly Blossoms are bright purple flowers harvested from the shadowfly plant, which grows in the Vorndgad Forest and the Druadach Highlands of Skyrim.

title: Shadowfly Stalks
topic_desc: Shadowfly Stalks are harvested from the shadowfly, a flowering plant native to the Vorndgad Forest and the Druadach Highlands of Skyrim. Alchemists and hunters value the stalks for their botanical properties, incorporating them into regional ingredient supplies and preparations drawn from the flora of the Reach.
topic_desc_basic: Shadowfly Stalks come from the shadowfly, a flowering plant that grows in the Vorndgad Forest and the Druadach Highlands of Skyrim.

title: Shakes
topic_desc: Shakes is a mild disease characterized by uncontrollable muscle spasms. The affliction is transmitted through contact with infected ornadas or rats. While the spasms can hinder physical action, the illness is not regarded as severe or life-threatening. Healers and alchemists classify it among the common wild ailments spread by vermin and certain native beasts, typically remedied through standard curative practices for common diseases.
topic_desc_basic: Shakes is a mild disease that causes muscle spasms. It is spread by infected ornadas and rats.

title: Sharai Hopper
topic_desc: Sharai hoppers are ravenous, quick-breeding creatures domesticated by the Shinathi for their sweet, tender meat. They mature rapidly, reaching slaughter age weeks after hatching, and lay eggs that require no tending—though the eggs are completely inedible. Shinathi herders feed them tanna leaves, though the hoppers consume nearly any plant, including species poisonous to mer. Escaped hoppers are a persistent agricultural nuisance; they breed swiftly, strip crops bare, and are too fast and numerous for farmers to easily control. To manage excess eggs, herders crush them, mix the pulp with seeds, and leave the blend behind as fertilizer to accelerate new plant growth for future forage.
topic_desc_basic: Sharai hoppers are fast-breeding creatures herded by the Shinathi for their meat. They eat almost any plant and quickly strip crops if they escape, making them a widespread pest to farmers.

title: Sharai Hopper Meat
topic_desc: Sharai hopper meat is the flesh of the sharai hopper, a distinct fauna. As an ingredient, it holds alchemical value and is sought by practitioners for its intrinsic properties. The meat is not commonly stocked through guaranteed supply; instead, alchemists and hunters primarily acquire it through chance encounters, as it circulates through randomized fauna distributions rather than established mercantile channels.
topic_desc_basic: Sharai hopper meat is harvested from the sharai hopper. It is an alchemical ingredient typically acquired by chance from the creature rather than through reliable commercial supply.

title: Sheggo's Shelf
topic_desc: Sheggo's Shelf is a species of bioluminescent mushroom native to the Othreleth Woods of Morrowind. Prized by alchemists and foragers for its distinct properties, the fungus is recognized by its characteristic glow. It is typically harvested from its natural habitat in the deep southwestern forests, where it grows in the region's damp environment.
topic_desc_basic: Sheggo's Shelf is a glowing mushroom that grows in the Othreleth Woods of Morrowind.

title: Sheogorath Invents Music
topic_desc: A mythological work by Mymophonus attributing the origin of music to Sheogorath. The narrative holds that the Madgod, finding mortal existence dull, resolved to provide them a means to create beautiful sounds after observing their inability to match the calls of birds. Unable to alter their nature, he instead fashioned the first instruments from the body of a woman, creating lutes from her tendons, a drum from her skull and arm bones, and flutes from her bones. The text reflects the cultural understanding of Sheogorath as a patron of artistic inspiration born of madness and brutality, framing music as a divine gift that elevates mortals beyond their mundane state through grotesque transformation.
topic_desc_basic: A myth by Mymophonus claiming Sheogorath created music for mortals. Finding their voices inadequate, the Madgod crafted the first lutes, drums, and flutes from the body of a woman, granting them the tools to make beautiful sounds.

title: Shezarr and the Divines
topic_desc: A theological treatise by Faustillus Junius of the Imperial Library examining how the god Shezarr, called Shor by the Nords, was redefined within the Cyrodilic pantheon. Junius argues that after Alessia's revolt liberated humans from Ayleid slavery, she faced the dilemma of Nordic allies who despised Elven deities and Cyrodilic subjects who had assimilated Aldmeri worship. Her solution was the Eight Divines, a synthesis of both pantheons. Shezarr, originally an anti-Aldmer warlord, could not be discarded without alienating the Nords, yet his militant aspect was incompatible with the new faith. He was recast as a vague, inoffensive patron spirit. Junius speculates that Tiber Septim similarly avoids reviving Shezarr's martial aspect during his Aldmeri Dominion campaigns, fearing association with the Alessian Order's catastrophes.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly work by Faustillus Junius explaining how Empress Alessia's creation of the Eight Divines religion transformed the god Shezarr from a Nordic warlord into a vague, inoffensive spirit to reconcile her Nordic allies with her Elven-worshipping subjects.

title: Shezarr's Song
topic_desc: A mythic account of the Aedra and Daedra's responses to Shezarr's proposal that they sacrifice parts of themselves to create the mortal world.
topic_desc_basic: A mythic text explaining how Shezarr convinced the Aedra to create the mortal world through self-sacrifice, and how this act divided the Aedra and drew the envy of the Daedra.

title: Shield of the Emperor
topic_desc: The Shield of the Emperor is the battle shield borne by Emperor Uriel V during his invasion of Akavir. It accompanied him during the disastrous winter of 289, when he led the Tenth Legion in a desperate night breakout from the besieged Tsaesci town of Ionith. According to Lord Pottreid's report to the Commission, Uriel V was cut down by enemy arrows while rallying the Tenth's shield wall, allowing a remnant of the Fourteenth Legion to reach Septimia. The heavily damaged shield was returned to Tamriel by the reduced Far East Fleet in 290 and held at Firewatch. For a century it rested in the vaults of Ember Keep until the College of Firewatch's museum opened in 389. The College has deliberately refrained from repairing the arrow and blade damage due to the artifact's profound historical importance, preserving it as a testament to the Emperor's final stand.
topic_desc_basic: The Shield of the Emperor is the battle shield of Uriel Septim V, returned to Tamriel after his death in Akavir in 289. It is currently displayed in the College of Firewatch's museum.

title: Shield of the Lord Commander
topic_desc: The Shield of the Lord Commander is a lordly heater shield of distinguished make, far surpassing the protective qualities of an ordinary wooden heater shield. Its association with the title of Lord Commander suggests a high-ranking military or knightly origin, though the specific order or lineage it belongs to remains obscure. The shield's exceptional craftsmanship and enhanced defensive enchantments distinguish it from common arms, marking it as a significant relic of martial authority.
topic_desc_basic: The Shield of the Lord Commander is a lordly heater shield renowned for being much more effective than a typical wooden heater shield. It is associated with the title of a Lord Commander.

title: Shield of the Trickster
topic_desc: The Shield of the Trickster is a unique shield depicting a gnome. Its origins and enchantments remain obscure, though the distinctive gnome motif suggests an association with trickery or cunning. The shield's provenance is unknown, and it is not recorded in any known collection or armory.
topic_desc_basic: The Shield of the Trickster is a unique shield depicting a gnome. You do not know where the Shield of the Trickster is.

title: Shor, son of Shor
topic_desc: Shor, son of Shor is a Nord creation myth recounting the eternal twilight war between the tribe of Shor and the tribe of Ald son of Ald. The narrative portrays the divine figures as tribal chieftains locked in cyclical conflict. Following a defeat orchestrated by enemy skin-magic, Shor descends to the Underworld to consult his dead father. At a prior Moot, Shor endured threefold ransom—banishment, disfigurement, and vomiting his heart to guard his wraith—prophesying that the conflict would spiral into a helix of ghosts. Ald declares the debt paid and warns that Shor's focus on the world below traps him in a cycle. Shor's father mirrors this logic, warning that Ald's focus on the world above does the same. Rejecting both counsels, Shor resumes the fight. The work is significant for its mythopoeic framing of the Ehlnofey war and its recursive, enigmatic structure.
topic_desc_basic: Shor, son of Shor is a Nord creation myth depicting the divine tribes of Shor and Ald locked in an eternal, cyclical twilight war. It portrays gods like Kyne, Dibella, and Trinimac as tribal chieftains and thanes, framing the cosmic conflict through martial and political strife.

title: Shutag Jelly
topic_desc: Shutag Jelly is a viscous substance drawn from shutag pods, a plant native to Morrowind. The pods yield a gelatinous extract valued by alchemists for its properties in potion-making. The plant grows in the Velothi regions of Morrowind, and the jelly is gathered as a standard alchemical ingredient across the province.
topic_desc_basic: Shutag Jelly is a gelatinous substance harvested from shutag pods, a plant native to Morrowind. It is known among alchemists and gatherers as a useful ingredient drawn from the province's local flora.

title: Silver Ore
topic_desc: Silver ore is a mineral ingredient prized for its utility in smithing, particularly in the forging of weapons effective against Daedric entities. The raw ore is traded by armorers and general merchants, though prices vary, and it also appears among natural mineral deposits and salvage from shipwrecks. Alchemists and hunters value the material for its inherent properties.
topic_desc_basic: Silver ore is a mineral used to forge weapons capable of slaying Daedra. It is sold by merchants and can be found in natural deposits.

title: Sixteen Accords of Madness IX
topic_desc: The ninth volume of the Sixteen Accords of Madness recounts a wager between Vaermina and Sheogorath over a Breton poet, Darius Shano. Vaermina claims she can inspire arrogant hatred in the mortal through subtle subconscious horrors, while Sheogorath contends madness breeds greater contempt. For ten years, Vaermina plagues Darius with nightmares of atrocity, producing infamous and reviled art. When Sheogorath's decade begins, he simply withdraws Vaermina's presence; the resulting silence breeds resentment, heresy, and sacrilege in Darius, culminating in his execution for mocking Tiber Septim. Sheogorath claims victory, arguing that depriving a mortal of comfort ripens true madness, thereby proving dreams are subordinate to madness.
topic_desc_basic: A volume of the Sixteen Accords of Madness recounting a wager between Vaermina and Sheogorath over a mortal artist, demonstrating Sheogorath's principle that madness is the foundation of dreams and creation.

title: Sixteen Accords of Madness v 12
topic_desc: Volume twelve of the Sixteen Accords of Madness recounts a mythic contest of cruelty between Sheogorath and Malacath. The tale follows Emmeg gro-Kayra, a noble Orc crusader, who receives the cursed blade Neb-Crescen from a disguised Sheogorath. The weapon drives Emmeg into a frenzy, causing him to gruesomely murder an Orc woman. Sheogorath then summons Malacath to the scene, offering to help avenge the killing if Malacath uses the same blade to wound the culprit and banish him to Sheogorath's realm. Consumed by rage, Malacath decapitates the cloaked murderer, only to discover he has slain his own son, Emmeg. Bound by the agreement, Malacath is forced to leave his son's soul to Sheogorath's torment. The work illustrates the perils of Daedric bargains and the devastating cunning of the Madgod.
topic_desc_basic: Volume twelve of the Sixteen Accords of Madness tells the mythic tale of the Orc champion Emmeg gro-Kayra and the Daedric Princes Malacath and Sheogorath. It recounts Sheogorath's cruel deception, which tricks Malacath into unwittingly killing his own son using a cursed blade.

title: Sixteen Accords of Madness v 6
topic_desc: Volume six of the Sixteen Accords of Madness recounts a contest between Sheogorath and Hircine on a Skyrim peak. Sheogorath challenges Hircine to groom a champion beast for fatal combat after three years. Hircine secretly breeds an ancient Daedroth cursed with lycanthropy, creating an unparalleled hunter. At the appointed time, Sheogorath reveals a tiny songbird. The monstrous Daedroth destroys the bird's perch, but the diminutive champion hops onto the beast, picking at detritus near its eyes. Blinded by its own furious attempts to pluck away the nuisance, the were-beast gradually destroys itself. Hircine burns the ragged corpse and withdraws in shame, while Sheogorath departs with his tiny champion. The work illustrates Sheogorath's domain over madness and trickery, demonstrating how cunning and futility can humble raw ferocity, a common theme in mythological accounts of the Mad Prince.
topic_desc_basic: Volume six of the Sixteen Accords of Madness tells the myth of a contest between Sheogorath and Hircine. Sheogorath defeats Hircine's monstrous lycanthropic Daedroth champion with a tiny songbird, which causes the fearsome beast to blindly destroy itself in frustrated rage.

title: Siyat Leaf
topic_desc: Siyat Leaf is a botanical ingredient gathered from a leaf-bearing plant. Its alchemical properties make it of interest to practitioners of alchemy, and it is known to occur in the wilds of Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: Siyat Leaf is a plant ingredient used in alchemy. It is gathered from leaf-bearing flora found across Tamriel.

title: Skin Deep
topic_desc: A scholarly treatise by Glissie Onmavaren documenting the practice of ritual scarification across Dunmer cultures, including its religious significance, regional variations among the Great Houses, and the stricter traditions observed among the Ashlander tribes.
topic_desc_basic: A book by Glissie Onmavaren documenting the Dunmer practice of ritual scarification. It covers the religious and cultural significance of intentional scarring, describing how different Great Houses and Ashlander tribes approach the tradition.

title: Skull of Corruption
topic_desc: The Skull of Corruption is the signature artifact of the Daedric Prince Vaermina. It functions as a staff capable of creating a duplicate, or clone, of whomever it is cast upon; this clone then attacks the original at the caster's behest. Legends attribute a will of its own to the Skull, claiming it can feed upon the memories of those nearby. A well-known, likely apocryphal tale recounts a Thieves Guild Master who used the Skull on an enemy; after the original was defeated, the clever clone seized the artifact and used it to duplicate the Master, with the two clones jointly ruling the guild for years. The lich Sabine Valtienne currently possesses the Skull within Wavebreaker Keep.
topic_desc_basic: The Skull of Corruption is the signature artifact of the Daedric Prince Vaermina. It is a staff that creates a hostile duplicate of whomever it is cast upon. Legends claim it has a mind of its own and feeds on the memories of those nearby.

title: Skyrender Queen Stinger
topic_desc: A sharp organ harvested from the abdomen of a skyrender queen, a more powerful variant of the common skyrender. These stingers are procured from deep within skyrender nests, which inhabit the mesas of Shipal-Shin in southern Morrowind. Valued by alchemists and hunters for their potent properties, the queen's stinger is a relatively rare ingredient not commonly found in general trade or leveled merchant stocks.
topic_desc_basic: A sharp organ taken from the abdomen of a skyrender queen. It is found deep within skyrender nests on the mesas of Shipal-Shin in southern Morrowind.

title: Skyrender Slumgum
topic_desc: Skyrender slumgum is a thick sludge harvested from the pupal cases found within skyrender nests. It is produced during the skyrender's transitional life stage between larva and adulthood, when the insect grows its limbs and wings. The substance is gathered from colonies situated in the mesas of Shipal-Shin in southern Morrowind. Alchemists value this residue for its properties, and hunters familiar with the region's fauna collect it from the nests as a useful ingredient.
topic_desc_basic: Skyrender slumgum is a thick sludge harvested from the pupal cases in skyrender nests, found in the mesas of Shipal-Shin in southern Morrowind.

title: Skyrender Venom
topic_desc: Skyrender venom is extracted from the poison glands of adult skyrenders and skyrender queens. It is highly toxic, capable of completely paralyzing a victim just like the insect's bite, and can be administered orally or via a poisoned blade. This versatility makes it a favored tool for assassins. However, a skilled alchemist can distill the substance into curative mixtures that both cure and grant resistance to poison.
topic_desc_basic: A highly toxic substance harvested from the poison glands of adult skyrenders and their queens. It causes complete paralysis and is a favored weapon of assassins, though skilled alchemists also use it to brew antidotes and poison-resistance mixtures.

title: Small Mole Crab Shell
topic_desc: The small mole crab shell is a chitinous ingredient harvested from the lesser mole crab, a burrowing crustacean found along Tamriel's coastlines. Alchemists value these shells for their inherent properties, which are extracted through standard calcination or digestion techniques. As a common animal byproduct, the shells circulate readily through apothecary supply channels and are frequently stocked by merchants dealing in common reagents. Their modest size and familiar origin make them a staple introductory component in practical alchemy.
topic_desc_basic: A chitinous shell harvested from the lesser mole crab, a small burrowing coastal crustacean. It is a common alchemical reagent valued by apothecaries.

title: Smear Spores
topic_desc: Smear spores are harvested from smear algae, an aquatic plant that grows in and around dreugh hives across Tamriel. Alchemists and hunters value the spores for their alchemical properties.
topic_desc_basic: Smear spores come from smear algae, a water plant found near dreugh hives. They are used in alchemy.

title: Snow Berries
topic_desc: Snow berries are small red berries that grow on snow berry bushes native to Skyrim. They are recognized by alchemists and hunters for their useful properties and are commonly gathered from the wild.
topic_desc_basic: Snow berries are small red berries that grow on bushes in Skyrim.

title: Snow Blossom
topic_desc: Snow Blossom is an orange flower native to High Rock. Alchemists and hunters value it as an ingredient, though it yields no guaranteed harvest, appearing only sporadically in the wild through the region's randomized flora distributions.
topic_desc_basic: Snow Blossom is an orange flower native to High Rock.

title: Snowray Sting
topic_desc: Snowray sting is the harvested stinger of the snow ray, a flying creature native to Skyrim. Valued by alchemists and hunters for its intrinsic properties, the ingredient is a recognized part of the region's natural fauna. Its alchemical character makes it a sought-after component in potion-making, and it circulates through general and rare ingredient supplies across the province.
topic_desc_basic: Snowray sting is the stinger of a snow ray, a flying creature found in Skyrim.

title: Socatra Nectar
topic_desc: Socatra Nectar is a botanical substance drawn from socatra plants, which are native to Cyrodiil. As a floral-derived ingredient, it circulates among alchemists and herbalists familiar with Cyrodilic flora. Its collection and trade reflect the broader regional commerce in plant-derived reagents from the Imperial Province.
topic_desc_basic: Socatra Nectar is gathered from socatra plants native to Cyrodiil. It is known among herbalists and alchemists as a floral ingredient of the Imperial Province.

title: Somber Widow Blossom
topic_desc: Somber Widow Blossoms are the flowers harvested from the somber widow, a plant native to the Padomaic Isles. As a floral ingredient, the blossom is valued by alchemists for its inherent properties, though its remote island origin makes it an uncommon sight in mainland Morrowind. The plant itself yields these distinctive blossoms, which are gathered for alchemical preparation and study.
topic_desc_basic: Somber Widow Blossoms are flowers taken from the somber widow plant, which grows natively in the Padomaic Isles.

title: Somnalius Frond
topic_desc: Somnalius fronds are leaves harvested from the somnalius, a fern native to Black Marsh. Alchemists value the fronds for their properties, and the ingredient circulates through regional supply lists.
topic_desc_basic: Leaves of a fern native to Black Marsh, used in alchemy.

title: Song for You
topic_desc: A handwritten piece of sheet music composed by Dolvys Teloth, featuring full scales and notations accompanying its lyrical text. The song is a direct, cautionary address to an individual, repeatedly warning them to fear an armed person identified by their profession and race. Its lyrics evoke a communal alarm, urging the listener to don adamantium armor in response to the surrounding outcry. The work's significance lies in its personalized, confrontational nature and its reflection of martial anxieties, using the recipient's own identity markers to heighten the sense of imminent threat.
topic_desc_basic: A handwritten musical composition by Dolvys Teloth. The song's lyrics repeatedly warn its recipient to fear an armed person identified by their profession and race, urging them to don adamantium armor in response to a surrounding outcry.

title: Song of Hrormir
topic_desc: An epic narrative poem recounting the exploits of the mage Hrormir, who becomes the champion of the Daedra Lord Nocturnal to free his ensorcelled companion Darfang. Pledging to serve the Shadowy Hag and divide her kingdom of Aelfendor among her heirs, Hrormir instead exploits a literalist loophole in his vow: he keeps Aelfendor whole while literally dividing the heirs themselves. By stealing Nocturnal's gray cowl while she sleeps, he exposes her hideous face to the light, breaking her power over the land. Acknowledging his cunning, Nocturnal releases his soul and departs. The work is significant for its portrayal of Nocturnal and its theme of mortal wit triumphing over Daedric power through oath-craft.
topic_desc_basic: An epic tale of the mage Hrormir, who outwits the Daedra Lord Nocturnal to free his companion, exploiting a clever loophole in his vow to serve her and stealing her cowl to break her power.

title: Song of the Askelde Men
topic_desc: A traditional Nordic poem translated into common circulation, recounting the disembodied vision of a slain warrior whose spirit lingers after death. Set in Hjaalmarch Hold, the narrator follows a Nord warband called the Askelde Men as they cremate their fallen foes, gather the ash, and smear it upon themselves before continuing their march. The poem invokes Wulfharth—addressed as ancestor, Ash King, and Ysmir—whom the warband credits with inspiring their martial valor. The Askelde Men dedicate their kills to Sovngarde and identify themselves as Children of the Sky. The ghost, unable to warn his doomed comrades, is finally dismissed when a warband elder perceives him and speaks ancient words that end the vision. The work is valued as a record of Nordic funerary and martial customs, ancestor veneration, and the enduring cult of Wulfharth.
topic_desc_basic: A traditional Nordic poem about a ghost haunting a warband. The slain narrator's spirit follows the Askelde Men through Hjaalmarch Hold as they burn their enemies' remains, gather the ash, and wear it as a ritual of martial devotion to Wulfharth and Sovngarde.

title: Songs of Stupor
topic_desc: Songs of Stupor is an anonymous compilation of satirical poems reflecting a deeply inebriated perspective. The work comprises four distinct pieces: a tavern tale about the necromancer Mouth Tharnabi and his unruly undead; a mocking address to a clumsy servant; a traveler's ribald comparison of women across Tamriel, concluding with his exclusion from his own Morrowind home by his knowing wife; and a parody of Morrowind's nightly prayers, where each pious invocation to the Tribunal and saints is immediately followed by a demand for more drink. The collection serves as a vernacular example of irreverent humor, blending conventional religious and social structures with the mundane vices of tavern life.
topic_desc_basic: Songs of Stupor is an anonymous collection of satirical poems written from a drunken perspective. The songs mockingly cover topics such as a bumbling necromancer, a clumsy slave, the women of Tamriel, and a parody of Morrowind's nightly prayers to the Tribunal and saints, where each holy invocation is paired with a demand for more drink.

title: Songs of the Grey Herds
topic_desc: Songs of the Grey Herds is a compiled ethnographic record of the Kafri herders of O-Keffer, assembled by Aung of Lettine. Aung journeyed from the isled East to trade books and goods for the indigenous songs of the Kafri, documenting their oral traditions across work, worship, and myth. The compilation includes field chants like 'Plains of Green' and 'Ooaamm the Census,' the solemn religious hymn 'Mother O-Keffer,' and the significant cultural myth 'Dark Odtsetseg and the Horns of Morning,' which recounts the defeat of the betrayer Odtsetseg by a golden-horned lamb. Aung also records the grueling duel chant 'Goldhorn and Blackwool,' the irreverent 'Song of Directions,' and 'Weird Goat of the South,' a Kafri jest about Aung's own people. The work highlights the Kafri's fierce cultural boundaries and their deeply animistic, herd-centered worldview.
topic_desc_basic: Songs of the Grey Herds is a compilation by Aung of Lettine documenting the oral songs and cultural myths of the Kafri herders inhabiting the rolling plains of O-Keffer, far to the west of the isled East.

title: Songs of the Reaver Clans, vI
topic_desc: The first volume of an Imperial scholarly compilation of the oral song-myths maintained by the Nordic reaving clans of the Sea of Ghosts. Compiled by Johannes Silvanus of the Imperial University, the work seeks to preserve traditions that the literate clans seldom record themselves and to challenge the popular characterization of these groups as mere savages. This volume presents a creation song detailing the gods' arrival at the liminal shore between the clashing realms of above and below. Following Jhunal's guidance, Shor beaches the keel of Sovngarde upon this sideways boundary and claims it as Sky. The divine clan then descends: Kyne the War-Wife, the Shield-Thanes Stuhn and Tsun, Dibella the Bed-Wife, Mara the Brood-Wife, and finally Jhunal the rune-scratcher. The transcribed song employs alliteration and repetition typical of the skaldic tradition, preserving its archaic meter.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly book compiling the oral song-myths of the Nordic reaver clans of the Sea of Ghosts. The first volume records a traditional creation myth in which Shor and the divine clan arrive at the boundary between above and below, claiming the shore as Sky.

record_links.display_name: Songs of the Reaver Clans, vI

title: Songs of the Reaver Clans, vII
topic_desc: The second volume of Songs of the Ghost Sea Reaver Clans, compiled by Johannes Silvanus of the Imperial University, preserves a Nordic oral tradition in which Shor leads his clan from Sovngarde into a new world. The song depicts Jhunal's cleverness being punished, the clan's sideways journey, and an encounter with Alduin, who declares he will devour all creation upon waking. Shor resolves to build the world-hall anyway, raising its first post, Sky-Throat. Silvanus notes the original tune was lost, underscoring the fragility of oral transmission.
topic_desc_basic: The second volume of Songs of the Ghost Sea Reaver Clans, compiled by Johannes Silvanus at the Imperial University, records a Nordic oral song about Shor leading his clan from Sovngarde into a new world, encountering Alduin, and raising the first post of the world-hall, Sky-Throat.

record_links.display_name: Songs of the Reaver Clans, vII

title: Songs of the Reaver Clans, vIII
topic_desc: Songs of the Reaver Clans, vIII is the third and final volume of Songs of the Ghost Sea Reaver Clans, compiled by Johannes Silvanus, Chairman of the Committee for the Transposition of Indigenous Oral Traditions at the Imperial University. The volume presents a reaver clan oral song concerning the introduction of time into Mundus. It depicts Shor as a trickster god who seizes Alduin's tail to bind the world-hall, extending the kalpa through cunning. The song recounts Shor's subsequent betrayal and death at the instigation of elves, ending the eternal world and rendering Man mortal. Silvanus notes the song's blend of pre-Return totemism with an Old Empire understanding of the Nordic mythic cycle, directing readers to Elonwe of Lillandril's Cultural Eras of the Nords for the broader scholarly framework.
topic_desc_basic: Songs of the Reaver Clans, vIII is the final volume of Songs of the Ghost Sea Reaver Clans, compiled by Johannes Silvanus of the Imperial University. It presents a reaver clan oral song depicting Shor as a trickster god who binds time to preserve the world-hall, only to be betrayed and killed through elven malice, ending the eternal world and making Man mortal.

record_links.display_name: Songs of the Reaver Clans, vIII

title: Songs of the Return, Volume 19
topic_desc: The nineteenth volume of the traditional Nordic epic chronicling Ysgramor and the Five Hundred Companions. It recounts the aftermath of a decisive battle at a barren pass, where the crews of the Kaal Kaaz, Sadon Reyth, and Ysgramor's ship Ylgermet parted ways. Pressing eastward, Ysgramor encountered the barrow of his son Yngol, who perished by Kyne's will rather than elven treachery. Renewed with grief, Ysgramor decreed a great city be built at the river's mouth, overlooking Yngol's resting place. Elven captives constructed the city, suffering death in numbers equal to those the Ylgermet crew had slain en route. The great bridge was raised to command the river, and the palace built high to defy the winds. Though a tomb was prepared beneath the city for Ysgramor's passage to Sovngarde, he was ultimately buried on the shore facing Atmora. Thus was Windhelm, the City of Kings, founded.
topic_desc_basic: A volume of the traditional Nordic epic of Ysgramor and the Five Hundred Companions. It recounts Ysgramor's grief at the barrow of his son Yngol and his decree to build a monumental city of elven captives overlooking the site, founding Windhelm, the City of Kings.

title: Songs of the Return, Volume 2
topic_desc: Songs of the Return, Volume 2 is a legendary Nordic text recounting the First Tale of the Darumzu, part of the traditional saga of Ysgramor and the Five Hundred Companions. It chronicles Ysgramor sending his sons, the strategist Yngol and the warrior Ylgar, back to Atmora to muster warriors for the Return. Ylgar commissions two ships at Jyljyrfyk, the Darumzu and the Harakk, and gathers renowned fighters including the Shield-Sisters Froa and Grosta and the war-teacher Adrimk. During the voyage to Tamriel, Kyne sends the Storm of Separation. Ylgar's ship survives, but Yngol's Harakk is lost. Ylgar arrives to find his father grieving, and the Harakk's crew becomes the first casualties among the Companions. Ylgar's grief and rage drive his surviving crew to become the first honored among the Companions' names.
topic_desc_basic: Songs of the Return, Volume 2 is a Nordic legendary text about Ysgramor's sons Yngol and Ylgar gathering warriors for the Return to Tamriel. It tells of the Storm of Separation that scattered their fleet, losing Yngol's ship and crew, and driving Ylgar to seek honor in his brother's memory.

title: Songs of the Return, Volume 24
topic_desc: Volume 24 of the traditional epic chronicling Ysgramor and his Five Hundred Companions, subtitled 'The First Tale of the Krilot Lok.' It recounts the westward voyage of the Krilot Lok, a crew from eastern Atmora devoted to Kyne and the sea, who journeyed into southern Tamriel. The song describes their encounters with unfamiliar kingdoms of men, hostile elves, and great deserts peopled by beast-folk. It focuses on the Shield-Brothers Roeth and Breff the Elder and their war-wives, the Shield-Sisters Britte and Greyf, detailing their ravaging march into the foul-smelling marshes of the snake-men. The narrative foreshadows Roeth's death and Britte's famed war-cry, framing their incursion as the beginning of a brutal campaign against the marsh's inhabitants.
topic_desc_basic: A volume of the traditional Nordic epic of Ysgramor and the Five Hundred Companions. This part recounts the Krilot Lok crew's voyage from Atmora and their campaign into the southern marshes against the snake-men.

title: Songs of the Return, Volume 56
topic_desc: Songs of the Return, Volume 56, subtitled 'The Final Tale of the Chrion,' is the concluding volume of the traditional Nordic epic chronicling Ysgramor and his Five Hundred Companions. The work recounts the aftermath of a battle in the eastern lands near the Red Mountain, where the Chrion's crew under Captain Rhorlak encamps after slaughtering elves who feigned peace. A messenger named Asgeir arrives from the sister crew of the Kall Kaaz to announce Ysgramor's death. The news devastates the Companions; the battle-hardened Rhorlak collapses in grief and never lifts his axe again. As the tidings spread across Tamriel, lights extinguish in silent tribute. The volume marks the end of the Return period and the original glories of the Five Hundred, framing their mortal era as closed and their legacy as the foundation of mankind's habitation in the north.
topic_desc_basic: Songs of the Return, Volume 56 is the final volume of the traditional Nordic epic about Ysgramor and his Five Hundred Companions. It recounts the death of Ysgramor and the profound grief of his followers, marking the end of the Return period and their original legendary deeds.

title: Songs of the Return, Volume 7
topic_desc: Songs of the Return, Volume 7 is an Atmoran epic chronicling the Five Hundred Companions' campaigns after retaking Saarthal. It records Ysgramor's command to drive the Mer from Tamriel and the Circle of Captains' decree that each crew seek its own fate, renewing the Companion oath. The narrative follows the crew of the Jorrvaskr, led by Jeek the River, as they march south and discover a colossal bird monument in an unclaimed valley. Elven captives reveal the statue predates Mer and channels ancient magic from the gods' attempt to forge paradise before Lorkhan's shattering. Unafraid, the Companions claim the site, dismantling their ship to build a shelter, thereby founding the Great City along the White River. The text provides foundational myth for the Companions' structure and early Atmoran settlement, attributing the establishment of this city to Ysgramor's closest companions.
topic_desc_basic: Songs of the Return, Volume 7 is an Atmoran epic recounting Ysgramor's command to the Five Hundred Companions after Saarthal and the crew of the Jorrvaskr's journey south, where they founded the Great City along the White River.

title: Soul Anchor
topic_desc: The Soul Anchor is a Daedric artifact associated with the Prince Molag Bal. It manifests as either a saber or a trident, and is believed to possess the ability to harvest the souls of those it strikes. The weapon rests within the Daedric shrine of Baelkashpitu in the mountains southwest of Tel Ouada. It carries a potent curse; if removed from its shrine, a Daedroth guardian is dispatched to hunt down the thief and reclaim the artifact. Due to this lethal enchantment, the Soul Anchor is considered extremely dangerous to possess and handle.
topic_desc_basic: The Soul Anchor is a cursed Daedric weapon associated with Molag Bal, believed to harvest the souls of its victims. It is housed in the Daedric shrine of Baelkashpitu, located in the mountains southwest of Tel Ouada.

title: Spear of Warchief Ulaqth
topic_desc: The Spear of Warchief Ulaqth is a relic of the Four Score War, once wielded by Ulaqth, a warchief from Lilmoth. It is fashioned from Kothringi silver. The weapon currently rests in the Kogotel Vaults beneath Ald Iuval.
topic_desc_basic: The Spear of Warchief Ulaqth is a Kothringi silver relic of the Four Score War, once wielded by a Lilmoth warchief. It is housed in the Kogotel Vaults at Ald Iuval.

title: Spearmouth
topic_desc: Spearmouth is a saltwater fish commonly found in the Abecean Sea, particularly in waters just off the coast of Cyrodiil. It serves as both a foodstuff and an alchemical ingredient, valued by those familiar with the marine life of the Abecean. The fish is recognized by coastal communities and practitioners of alchemy for its utility in preparations and cuisine alike.
topic_desc_basic: Spearmouth is a saltwater fish commonly found in the Abecean Sea off the coast of Cyrodiil. It is used as a food ingredient by the region's coastal inhabitants.

title: Spellstone
topic_desc: Spellstone is a magical alloy created by the great mage Shalidor, who traveled to multiple Oblivion planes to collect crystals from at least five different realms. Through a highly perilous transmutation spell, he fused these crystals together to create an alloyed spell-focus. It ranks among the most concentrated collections of Padomaic matter known. While a specimen discovered on the isle of Eyevea around 2E 282 was rendered inert by centuries of neglect, properly maintained spellstones retain their formidable magical character. In alchemical practice, the substance is treated as an ingredient, valued for its intrinsic properties and its deep connections to the Daedric planes from which its constituent crystals were harvested.
topic_desc_basic: Spellstone is a magical alloy created by the mage Shalidor by fusing crystals from multiple Oblivion planes. It is a highly concentrated form of Padomaic matter used as an alloyed spell-focus and alchemical ingredient.

title: Spiddal
topic_desc: Spiddal is a floral ingredient of somewhat obscure alchemical character. Its properties and precise natural habitat are not widely documented in standard herbalist references, leaving its common uses and origin a matter of specialist knowledge rather than general consensus.
topic_desc_basic: Spiddal is a plant ingredient used in alchemy.

title: Spider Silk
topic_desc: Spider silk is the signature silk produced by spiders and spun from diverse sources across Tamriel. It is known for its soft ductility and is commonly knitted or woven into clothing, furnishings, utilities, and light armor. It is considered stronger than cotton light armor but weaker than Ebonthread or Kreshweed. Dunmer tailors grade spun spidersilk into three varieties: shimmer, a fine rippling fabric and the most common grade; Azura's-breath, lighter and sometimes translucent yet equally durable, and receptive to enchanting; and contraspun, a dense, impervious weave said to turn a knife blade while retaining ductility. The Dunmer favor light armor made from insect carapace covered in finely woven spidersilk wrapped several times around the torso. Lady Eloisse of House Manteau claimed few varieties compare to Morrowind's spidersilk. Though Imperial silk garments typically use ancestor moth silk, spidersilk is farmed in Cyrodiil.
topic_desc_basic: Spider silk is the signature silk produced by spiders across Tamriel, prized for its soft ductility. It is commonly woven into clothing, furnishings, and light armor. Dunmer tailors grade it into several varieties of differing weight and durability, and Morrowind's spidersilk is regarded as exceptional.

title: Spikeworm Carapace
topic_desc: Spikeworm carapace is the chitinous shell harvested from a slain spikeworm. These creatures inhabit the Reach, the rugged border region between High Rock and Skyrim. The carapace serves as an alchemical ingredient, valued by practitioners for its intrinsic properties. Hunters who track spikeworms through the Reach's harsh terrain and alchemists who process the harvested shells both recognize the substance's utility in their respective crafts.
topic_desc_basic: Spikeworm carapace is a chitinous shell harvested from spikeworms, creatures native to the Reach on the border of High Rock and Skyrim. It is used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Spinel
topic_desc: Spinel is a crystalline mineral valued as both a gemstone and an alchemical ingredient. It occurs naturally as subterranean ore and is recovered through mining. The stone circulates widely among apothecaries and jewelers, appearing in trade inventories across Cyrodiil and Hammerfell. Its alchemical properties make it a staple component in scholarly and practical mixtures alike.
topic_desc_basic: Spinel is a crystalline mineral used as both a gemstone and an alchemical ingredient. It is mined as subterranean ore and traded across Cyrodiil and Hammerfell.

title: Sponge Lotus Seed
topic_desc: Sponge lotus seeds are harvested from the sponge lotus, an aquatic plant found growing along the Thirr River in the Shipal-Shin region and within the Coronati Basin of Morrowind. As a botanical ingredient, the seeds hold alchemical value and are sought after by practitioners for their inherent properties. The plant's restricted habitat along these specific waterways makes its seeds a regional specialty rather than a commonplace reagent.
topic_desc_basic: Sponge lotus seeds are harvested from the sponge lotus, an aquatic plant that grows along the Thirr River in Shipal-Shin and the Coronati Basin of Morrowind.

title: Spotted Gillsieve
topic_desc: Spotted Gillsieve is a type of coral that grows in the Thirr River as it flows through the Coronati Basin and the Shipal-Shin region of Morrowind. Harvested from these aquatic environments, it serves as an alchemical ingredient. Its properties make it of interest to practitioners of alchemy and those who gather such resources from the wild.
topic_desc_basic: Spotted Gillsieve is a type of coral found in the Thirr River, particularly in the Coronati Basin and Shipal-Shin regions of Morrowind. It is used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Squirrel Meat
topic_desc: Squirrel meat is the edible flesh harvested from squirrels, small rodents primarily found in the Vorndgad Forest of Skyrim. Valued as a common game food, it is regularly procured by hunters and recognized by alchemists for its basic properties. Its availability in regional supply lists confirms its status as a standard provision across the province.
topic_desc_basic: Squirrel meat is edible flesh taken from squirrels, small rodents commonly found in Skyrim's Vorndgad Forest. It is a standard game food.

title: St. Jahn's Wort Flowers
topic_desc: St. Jahn's wort flowers are yellow blossoms harvested from the St. Jahn's wort plant. The flora thrives along the Strident Coast and on Stirk Isle in Cyrodiil, where it grows commonly. Alchemists and hunters value the flowers as an ingredient, utilizing their inherent properties in various preparations.
topic_desc_basic: St. Jahn's wort flowers are yellow blossoms harvested from the St. Jahn's wort plant. They grow commonly on the Strident Coast and Stirk Isle in Cyrodiil.

title: St. Rilms' Lesson
topic_desc: St. Rilms' Lesson is a religious text teaching the Dunmeri pilgrims' way. It frames physical pilgrimage as an act of devotion, equating the act of walking with love. The work reveres the Prophet Veloth and the Tribunal, interpreting the journey of the feet as a sacred retracing of the ancestral exodus to Resdayn. It intertwines the physical and spiritual through the metaphor of the sole: scars, blisters, and tattoos mark both body and spirit, reflecting the trials that forge heroic tendencies. The lesson presents each step as a paradoxical act that is both free and predetermined, effecting change while altering nothing, and simultaneously telling past, present, and future stories. By retracing Veloth's pattern, pilgrims strengthen their bond to their heritage and the divine source.
topic_desc_basic: St. Rilms' Lesson is a religious text on the Dunmeri pilgrims' way. It teaches that walking is an act of devotion that retraces the exodus of Veloth, intertwining the physical marks of travel on the feet with spiritual growth and resolve.

title: Staff of the Founder
topic_desc: The Staff of the Founder is the stave associated with Narsara Hla-Alu, the founder of Great House Hlaalu. It is held within the city of Narsis, in Vault 1 of the Second Family Manor.
topic_desc_basic: The Staff of the Founder is the stave of Narsara Hla-Alu, founder of Great House Hlaalu. It is kept in Narsis, within the Second Family Manor.

title: Staff of the Typos Sophia
topic_desc: The Staff of the Typos Sophia is a powerful magical artifact that prevents Daedra from binding mortals through possession and grants spell resistance. It was present during the Battlespire invasion, where it was wielded by the Emperor's chief artificer, Clarentavious Valisious. The Dremora Lord Methats Uldun commanded the invasion, and his legions acquired the staff under covenants of conquest. Another Dremora, Rathine Morgal, later stole the artifact and fled with it. Scholars note that artifacts frequently vanish and reappear across existence due to the fragile nature of their interplanar links, though theft often plays a role. The staff is currently sought to neutralize a liminal tumor threatening Old Ebonheart, requiring its return to Methats Uldun in exchange for the tumor's removal.
topic_desc_basic: The Staff of the Typos Sophia is a powerful artifact that prevents Daedric possession and grants spell resistance. It disappeared during the Battlespire invasion and is presumed lost.

title: Starfish Leg
topic_desc: Starfish Legs are the severed limbs of starfish, bottom-dwelling echinoderms found on the seafloor throughout Tamriel's coastal waters. They come in three varieties distinguished by color—orange, pink, and blue—each bearing distinct alchemical properties. Alchemists and coastal foragers harvest these limbs for use in potion-making, and they circulate in general ingredient trade across the region.
topic_desc_basic: Starfish Legs are severed limbs taken from starfish dwelling on the seafloor throughout Tamriel. They occur in orange, pink, and blue varieties, each with different alchemical properties, and are traded as common alchemical ingredients.

title: Steel Blue Entoloma Cap
topic_desc: The steel blue entoloma cap is harvested from the steel blue entoloma, a fungus native to the Dasek Marsh region of Cyrodiil. Prized by alchemists for its distinct properties, the cap serves as a reliable ingredient in various mixtures. Its marshland origin makes it a regional specialty, typically gathered by those familiar with the humid wetlands of Cyrodiil's border territories.
topic_desc_basic: A mushroom cap harvested from the steel blue entoloma, a fungus that grows in the Dasek Marsh region of Cyrodiil.

title: Stinkhorn Cap
topic_desc: Stinkhorn caps are a type of mushroom originally native to Cyrodiil. In Morrowind, they grow in the Roth Roryn region. Alchemists and hunters value these fungi for their properties, though they remain less common than local varieties.
topic_desc_basic: Stinkhorn caps are a type of mushroom originally from Cyrodiil that also grows in the Roth Roryn region of Morrowind.

title: Strawberry
topic_desc: Strawberries are small, red, sweet fruits gathered from low-growing plants. Valued as a foodstuff across Tamriel, they are commonly collected by hunters and foragers in the wild. Alchemists prize the fruit for its properties, which find use in potion-making. The berries also appear in general merchant stock and random provisions through trade and harvest.
topic_desc_basic: Strawberries are small, red, sweet fruits that grow on low plants. They are commonly eaten as food and gathered in the wild.

title: Strident Runner Egg
topic_desc: Strident runner eggs are harvested from the nests of strident runners, a bird species of the Hammerfell deserts. Alchemists and hunters value them as an ingredient, though they are not commonly traded through standard merchant channels.
topic_desc_basic: Eggs taken from the nests of strident runners, birds native to the Hammerfell deserts.

title: Strident Runner Feathers
topic_desc: Strident Runner Feathers are long plumes harvested from Strident Runners, large avian creatures that inhabit the Strident Coast of Cyrodiil. Alchemists value these feathers for their inherent properties, and hunters commonly procure them from the birds. The ingredient circulates through general alchemical markets and is subject to regional supply variations.
topic_desc_basic: Strident Runner Feathers are long plumes taken from Strident Runners, large birds native to the Strident Coast in Cyrodiil. They are commonly used in alchemy.

title: Stridfish
topic_desc: Stridfish is a freshwater fish native to the Strid River and the Naharine River in Cyrodiil. It is valued as a foodstuff and appears in general provisions and regional faunal collections throughout the province.
topic_desc_basic: Stridfish is a freshwater fish commonly found in the Strid River and the Naharine River in Cyrodiil. It is known as a food ingredient throughout the province.

title: Sturgeon Meat
topic_desc: Sturgeon meat is the flesh of the sturgeon, a long-lived fish found in waters across Tamriel. Valued by hunters and alchemists, the meat serves as a common ingredient harvested from these aquatic creatures.
topic_desc_basic: Sturgeon meat comes from the sturgeon, a long-lived fish found in waters across Tamriel.

title: Sturgeon Roe
topic_desc: Sturgeon roe comprises the eggs harvested from the sturgeon, a long-lived fish species inhabiting waters across Tamriel. Prized as a valuable commodity, these eggs serve as an alchemical ingredient. Their natural origin and widespread availability make them a recognized resource among those versed in the culinary and alchemical traditions of the continent.
topic_desc_basic: Sturgeon roe is the valuable eggs of the sturgeon, a long-lived fish found in waters across Tamriel. It is used as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Su-Diang Qergo
topic_desc: An early one-act play by the prolific Redguard playwright Kambuja, known in Cyrodiil as Cambyses. The work stages a philosophical duel between the swordsman Kaludu and the fabled instructor Mosedesi on the Dak'fron steppes. Through layered combat dialogue and a thought-experiment invoking the Hena-Pishatri Doctrine and the progeny of Tall Papa, Mosedesi reveals the secret of assured victory: the concept of a greater infinity, demonstrating that one who grasps it can surpass anyone forever and cannot be defeated except on their own terms. The play is culturally significant for blending traditional Redguard stage sword-fighting with Yokudan metaphysical numerology and epistemology.
topic_desc_basic: A Redguard one-act play by Kambuja, also known as Cambyses. It depicts a philosophical sword-fight and thought-experiment between a swordsman and a fabled instructor, exploring the concept of a greater infinity to reveal the secret of assured victory.

title: Succulent Pulp
topic_desc: Succulent pulp is harvested from embertip, a plant native to the Padomaic Isles. Visually, the translucent pulp is indistinguishable from aloe vera extracts. Alchemists value the substance for its properties, though it remains a regional specialty seldom encountered on the mainland of Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: Succulent pulp is a plant ingredient harvested from embertip, a flora native to the Padomaic Isles. It closely resembles aloe vera pulp.

title: Sulphur
topic_desc: Sulphur is a mineral ore gathered from deposits found near pools that mar the desolate wastes. It is valued for industrial and alchemical applications, most notably the bleaching of cloth. However, its use carries a severe risk: prolonged exposure to sulphur dims and ultimately steals the sight of those who work with it. Despite this danger, its unique properties make it an irreplaceable component in certain traditional crafts, leaving practitioners to rely on ALMSIVI's mercy or the aid of others once their vision fails. The Temple acknowledges the hardships borne by those who handle sulphur in service of their work.
topic_desc_basic: Sulphur is a mineral ore found in deposits near pools scattered across the wastes. It is commonly used to bleach cloth, though prolonged exposure to the substance causes blindness, forcing workers to rely on others to gather it.

title: Summer Bolete Cap
topic_desc: The summer bolete cap is a mushroom native to Cyrodiil, valued by alchemists and foragers for its alchemical properties. As a regional fungal ingredient, it is gathered from the wild and traded among practitioners of the alchemical arts.
topic_desc_basic: A summer bolete cap is a type of mushroom native to Cyrodiil.

title: Sunkindler
topic_desc: Sunkindler is a crossbow believed to have been wielded in the extermination of two separate vampire clans. It is currently associated with the infamous vampire hunter Darron Marceau, the killer of those clans. Marceau carries the weapon while staying at The Grey Lodge, situated on the border between the Armun Ashlands and Roth Roryn.
topic_desc_basic: Sunkindler is a crossbow infamous for its role in the extermination of two vampire clans. It is carried by the vampire hunter Darron Marceau, who resides at The Grey Lodge on the border between the Armun Ashlands and Roth Roryn.

title: Suthay
topic_desc: The Suthay are a furstock of the Khajiit, native to Elsweyr, born under the phase of a new Masser and Secunda. They closely resemble the Suthay-raht, being bipedal with digitigrade legs, but are distinguished by their lesser stature and pale fur. To most non-Khajiit, the two furstocks are indistinguishable. Early literature ascribes to the Suthay a societal role involving preparation for the end of time. Like other Khajiit, they possess natural claws—which many prefer over weapons—and a noted weakness for sweets, particularly skooma. Renowned for unmatched agility even among their kin, the Suthay are exceptionally acrobatic and make excellent thieves.
topic_desc_basic: The Suthay are a bipedal Khajiit furstock from Elsweyr, born under a new Masser and Secunda. Smaller and paler than the Suthay-raht, they are difficult for non-Khajiit to distinguish. They are renowned for their agility.

title: Swamp Chalice
topic_desc: The Swamp Chalice is a species of fungus native to Skyrim. Prized by alchemists and hunters familiar with the region's flora, it is harvested for its useful alchemical properties. As a relatively uncommon ingredient, it holds steady value among practitioners who know how to exploit its characteristics in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Swamp Chalice is a type of fungus native to Skyrim, impacted by alchemists for its properties.

title: Swamp Rot
topic_desc: Swamp Rot is a serious disease transmitted through the bites or contact of various creatures, including mole crabs, swamp trolls, sky renders, and muck leeches. Its symptoms manifest as severe myalgia, erratic muscular spasms, and mental confusion. Afflicted individuals report chaotic cognitive impulses and extreme tremors, described as muscles straining against the body, alongside profound disorientation and loss of basic motor function. Without intervention, the condition subjects the sufferer to prolonged physical torment and mental instability. Restorative care at a Temple provides effective treatment, allowing the afflicted to recover their cognitive faculties and physical control.
topic_desc_basic: Swamp Rot is a serious disease caught from creatures like mole crabs, swamp trolls, sky renders, and muck leeches. It causes severe muscle pain, erratic spasms, and confusion. The condition is treatable at Temples.

title: Sweedledee
topic_desc: Sweedledees are a harvestable flora of uncertain botanical character. Alchemists and hunters recognize them as a source of usable ingredient material, though their specific properties and natural appearance remain poorly documented in standard references. The plant grows in regions where it appears in common foraging distributions, providing a typical yield of alchemical reagents for practiced harvesters.
topic_desc_basic: Sweedledees are a harvestable plant found in the wilds. They are gathered as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Sweetbread Polypore
topic_desc: Sweetbread polypore is a variety of shelf mushroom that grows upon trees in the Othreleth Woods of Morrowind. Its formation on living or dead wood characterizes it as a typical wood-decaying fungus, offering alchemical value to those who gather it. Like other polypores, it is sought after by practitioners of alchemy and woodsmen familiar with the region's fungal growths.
topic_desc_basic: Sweetbread polypore is a shelf mushroom that grows on trees in the Othreleth Woods of Morrowind.

title: Sweetgrass Stem
topic_desc: Sweetgrass stems are plant-derived alchemical ingredients gathered from sweetgrass flora. The stem is the usable portion of the plant, harvested for its properties in potion-making. Alchemists and herbalists value sweetgrass for its contributions to various concoctions, though detailed records of its specific effects remain limited. The ingredient circulates through general herbal and floral supply channels across Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: Sweetgrass Stem is a plant ingredient gathered from sweetgrass flora. Alchemists and herbalists use the stem in potion-making. It circulates through general herbal supply channels across Tamriel.

title: Sweetroll
topic_desc: Sweetrolls are baked confections found across Tamriel, valued as much for their delightful taste as for their potent alchemical properties. Prepared by bakers who commonly sell them, these treats are characterized by a fluffy, gooey warmth and a distinct drizzled glaze. Beyond their culinary appeal, sweetrolls serve as viable ingredients in alchemical practice, though their specific alchemical effects require specialist knowledge to harness. Their cultural significance is such that they have even inspired devotional prayer-songs, revering the treat with liturgical praise and celebrating its presentation upon fine plates or within dark crates.
topic_desc_basic: Sweetrolls are popular baked treats found across Tamriel. They are known for their sweet, delightful taste and are commonly sold by city bakers. In addition to being eaten, they possess potent alchemical properties.

title: Sweetroll Butterfly Wing
topic_desc: Sweetroll Butterfly Wings are the delicate wings harvested from the Sweetroll Butterfly, a diurnal insect native to Skyrim. As an alchemical ingredient, the wing is valued by practitioners for its inherent properties. The host insect is exclusively active during daylight hours, requiring hunters to gather specimens by day. While the wings are a recognized component in alchemical practice, they are not commonly found as loose samples and must typically be sourced directly from the living creature.
topic_desc_basic: Sweetroll Butterfly Wings are alchemical ingredients harvested from the Sweetroll Butterfly, a diurnal insect found in Skyrim. They must be gathered from the living insect during daylight hours.

title: Sword of Taldeus
topic_desc: The Sword of Taldeus is the weapon of Taldys Orothri, a saint of the Imperial Cult. It is interred within the Orothri Ancestral Tomb in Dagon Urul. As a relic associated with an Imperial saint, the blade holds significance to the Cult's faithful and its recovery is a matter of devotional interest.
topic_desc_basic: The Sword of Taldeus is a relic of the Imperial Cult, belonging to the saint Taldys Orothri. It rests within the Orothri Ancestral Tomb in Dagon Urul.

title: Sword of the Moon Reiver
topic_desc: The Sword of the Moon Reiver is a lethal Daedric blade formed from the pure essence of Mehrunes Dagon. It grants its wielder the ability to manipulate the realms of Oblivion, a power demonstrated when Lord Methats Uldun used it to create the Daedric fortress of Vorthas Uldun, which abuts the ruined city of Khalaan. Historically, the blade was wielded to repel Mehrunes Dagon's own invasion of the Battlespire. It is currently possessed by the Dremora Lord Methats Uldun within his chambers in Vorthas Uldun.
topic_desc_basic: The Sword of the Moon Reiver is a lethal Daedric blade formed from the essence of Mehrunes Dagon. It grants its wielder power over the realms of Oblivion. The weapon is currently held by the Dremora Lord Methats Uldun in his fortress of Vorthas Uldun.

title: Syvvit Tong
topic_desc: The Syvvit Tong is a loose band of merchants operating out of the Velothi town of Vhul. Infamous for swindling outlanders, the Tong is viewed with respect by many locals for bringing prosperity and order to the village tradesmer. However, the organization draws suspicion from the Tribunal Temple and Great House Indoril, who disapprove of commoners accumulating wealth and view the Tong's mercantile practices as dishonorable. Indoril Ilvi suspects the Tong may harbor secret ties to House Hlaalu due to their unusual penchant for fraud and mercantilism; if true, this collusion would threaten Indoril hegemony over the eastern Aanthirin. Despite these allegations, some Vhul residents maintain the Tong does nothing illegal, and Indoril authorities have yet to uncover concrete proof of conspiracy.
topic_desc_basic: The Syvvit Tong is a loose merchant band operating out of the Velothi town of Vhul. Infamous for swindling outlanders, the Tong is respected by many locals for bringing prosperity to village tradesmer. However, Great House Indoril and the Tribunal Temple view their practices as dishonorable and suspect them of colluding with House Hlaalu.

title: Tacca Seeds
topic_desc: Tacca seeds are harvested from the tacca, a species of flower native to Cyrodiil. They serve as an alchemical ingredient drawn from the plant's bloom.
topic_desc_basic: Tacca seeds are harvested from the tacca flower, a plant native to Cyrodiil.

title: Tales of Kieran
topic_desc: A collection of tales attributed to Kieran the Bard, edited by Vegepythicus. A librarian's note classifies the stories into the Woodland Cycle, Castles and Kings, and a destroyed unnamed cycle of lusty tales. The extant narratives follow Kieran's encounters with speaking creatures and interweave with the story of Princess Einlea, transformed into a grub by the vengeful wizard Loziard. The work employs a helical structure typical of hearthside recitation and explores the magical principle that harmful spells are broken by acts of charity. Whether the tales record true events, serve as allegory, or exist purely as entertaining fancy remains deliberately uncertain.
topic_desc_basic: A collection of tales about Kieran the Bard, edited by Vegepythicus. The stories are divided into the Woodland Cycle, Castles and Kings, and a destroyed cycle of lusty tales, blending Kieran's encounters with talking creatures and the magical transformation of Princess Einlea.

title: Tales of the Woven City I
topic_desc: Tales of the Woven City I: The Serpent's Feast is a Nibenese moral fable set in Bravil. It recounts a wealthy soap merchant who encounters a jewel-encrusted serpent in the Niben. The snake reveals it gained its opulence by devouring enemies, and the merchant, adopting this predatory philosophy, beats and consumes the creature. The serpent, actually a cunning spirit, survives from within, consuming the merchant's family, possessions, and soul. Glutted on mortal life, the beast bursts from its stolen skin. Priests and hermits then drive the exposed fiend into the Niben, which tears it apart. The tale concludes with conflicting accounts of the victims' fates, offering a warning about the dangers of unverified prosperity and the river's purifying role.
topic_desc_basic: A Nibenese fable about a Bravil soap merchant who consumes a jewel-encrusted serpent to steal its wealth, only to be devoured from within by the creature's spirit. The beast eventually bursts from its stolen skin and is destroyed by the Niben River, illustrating the peril of ill-gotten prosperity.

record_links.display_name: Tales of the Woven City I

title: Tales of the Woven City II
topic_desc: A Nibenese moral tale recounting the mission of the Hierophant Tiro Coero, dispatched by Emperor Gorieus to dismantle a forbidden tiger cult in the Horvalli lands west of Banadher. Disguised as a local, Coero infiltrated the Temple of Vapor Needles, where the Horvalli fed living and dead to a revered beast. Exploiting the creature's gluttony, the battlemage crafted and animated a false man of pitch and fat; when the tiger consumed the decoy, the materials congealed and ruptured its body, exposing its filth to the worshippers. The narrative reinforces the supremacy of the Aetherial spheres over base mortal appetites and celebrates Hierophantine cunning in service of Imperial religious law, referencing Aleshut's ancient casting down of the tigers and the Kothringi silver mines near the evil jungle of Banadher.
topic_desc_basic: A Nibenese tale describing how the battlemage Tiro Coero destroyed a forbidden tiger cult in the Horvalli lands on Emperor Gorieus's orders. Coero tricked the revered beast into eating a false man of pitch and fat, causing it to burst and revealing its filth to its worshippers.

record_links.display_name: Tales of the Woven City II

title: Talhjolde, Allfathirs Beit
topic_desc: A poetic fable published by the Imperial University Press in 3E 421, preserving an ancient Nordic tale of the All-Maker. The work recounts a contest in which the All-Maker asks His flocks—represented by the Woodland Man, the Snake, and the Fox—who is the cleverest. The Fox claims supremacy by asserting it can throw its cunning voice into another's mouth and claim their words as its own. The All-Maker rebukes the Fox for its arrogance and abuse of patience, banishing it to roam the world. A scholarly footnote notes that while proto-Nords of Atmora likely believed in a singular All-Maker and carried this theology to Tamriel, the tradition has not survived into the modern era. The text offers insight into early Nordic cosmology and the cultural moralizing surrounding cunning and pride.
topic_desc_basic: A book published by the Imperial University Press containing an old Nordic fable about the All-Maker. In the tale, the Fox claims to be the cleverest of all beings by stealing the words of others, but the All-Maker banishes it for its arrogance. A footnote notes that the proto-Nord belief in a single All-Maker has not survived to the present day.

title: Talhjolde, Horsk Olf
topic_desc: A Nordic poem translated and published by the Imperial University Press in 3E 421. It recounts the tale of a frost maid who, finding no single suitor worthy, is counseled by a wolfish voice to marry multiple partners for their individual strengths. The poem employs elemental imagery—clouds obscuring the sun, wind dispersing clouds, mountains blocking wind, and sunlight overwhelming mountains—to illustrate cyclical dominance and interdependence. The accompanying scholarly footnotes address translation difficulties, noting the original term for spouse lacks a precise equivalent and that the final elemental line conveys smothering or drowning. The work reflects Nordic cultural values regarding clan-building and pragmatic marital alliances.
topic_desc_basic: A Nordic poem published by the Imperial University Press in 3E 421. It tells of a frost maid who, unable to choose a single worthy suitor, is advised to marry several for their varied strengths and forge a clan from the collective union.

title: Talhjolde, Hvals Bol
topic_desc: A scholarly edition of an old Nordic fable published by the Imperial University Press in 3E 421. The poem recounts the plight of a Whale who, caught between love and fear after wooing Lord Winter's wife, accepts a coin from a scheming Snake disguised as an amiable Owl. The coin promises to end his torment by severing either love or fear, but the kiss that takes it kills him. The annotated footnotes clarify that 'knowing' serves as a Nordic sobriquet, Snake represents the totem of Orkey adopting the form of an Owl—an old analogue to Julianos—and note the recurring folktale motif of poisoned coins, possibly reflecting a historical regicide.
topic_desc_basic: A Nordic fable published by the Imperial University Press in 3E 421. It tells of a Whale who, tormented by love and fear after wooing Lord Winter's wife, accepts a coin from a disguised Snake to end his suffering, only to die from the poisoned gift.

title: Talhjolde, Modiskva Bern
topic_desc: A scholarly publication by the Imperial University Press presenting a Nordic allegorical poem in which three beasts—the loyal Hawk, the joyous Moth, and the thoughtless, thin-skinned Bear—journey toward the sky. An entity called the Adversary demands one sacrifice themselves to sate its hunger until the Burning. The Hawk and Moth refuse, valuing the dignity and pleasure they provide to Men. The Bear, reacting only with fury, is permitted to survive alone. The Adversary declares that only anger will persist until the end of time. The text includes philological footnotes clarifying translation nuances, such as a term for a mountain spring and a comparative note on 'thin-skinned,' framing the poem for an Imperial academic audience.
topic_desc_basic: A book published by the Imperial University Press in 3E 421 containing a Nordic poem.
