topic_desc: The War-Banner of Prince Bashomon is the tattered personal standard of the Esri lord who resisted the Imperial conquest of Esroniet. Following the fall of Black Harbor in 3E 282, Bashomon waged a guerilla campaign against the Legions for two years. Upon his defeat and execution in 3E 284, the banner was seized. Uriel Septim V prized this captured flag above all other Esri relics, ordering the royal court's treasures melted and sent to Cyrodiil. The banner's survival stands in stark contrast to the vanished wealth of Black Harbor, whose so-called Lost Treasury remains a subject of historical speculation—some scholars argue Bashomon hid his golden regalia, while others dismiss the treasury as myth.
topic_desc_basic: The War-Banner of Prince Bashomon is the captured personal standard of an Esri lord who fought the Imperial conquest of Esroniet. Seized upon his execution in 3E 284, the tattered flag was highly prized by Emperor Uriel Septim V. It is currently held in Imperial custody.

title: War Cuirass of Pasoroth
topic_desc: The War Cuirass of Pasoroth is the surviving torso piece of the armor worn by Hlaalu Pasoroth, the great-grandfather of King Hlaalu Helseth. Pasoroth is credited with accumulating much of Great House Hlaalu's power and was regarded as the greatest warrior of his era. According to Hallgerd's Tale, he was so exceptionally attuned to his armor that he moved more gracefully within it than without, reputedly capable of walking on his hands and performing marital duties while wearing the full suit. The cuirass is currently housed within Vault 3 of the Second Family Manor in Narsis.
topic_desc_basic: The War Cuirass of Pasoroth is the surviving piece of the armor worn by the legendary Hlaalu warrior Hlaalu Pasoroth, great-grandfather of King Helseth. It is kept in Vault 3 of the Second Family Manor in Narsis.

title: War Greaves of Pasoroth
topic_desc: The War Greaves of Pasoroth are the leg armor associated with the figure Pasoroth, known through the account recorded in Hallgerd's Tale. They currently rest in the lower vaults of the Measurehall in the city of Narsis, safeguarded within that Hlaalu stronghold. The text establishes the greaves as a notable relic tied to Pasoroth's martial legacy, though the specific enchantments or historical deeds attributed to them remain subject to the tale's narrative rather than independent confirmation.
topic_desc_basic: The War Greaves of Pasoroth are legendary leg armor described in Hallgerd's Tale. They are kept in the lower vaults of the Measurehall in the city of Narsis.

title: War Helm of Pasoroth
topic_desc: The War Helm of Pasoroth is a named piece of armor forming part of a suit described in Hallgerd's Tale. It is currently held in the Grandmaster Quarters of the Second Family Manor, located within the Council Quarter of Narsis.
topic_desc_basic: The War Helm of Pasoroth is a historic armor piece described in Hallgerd's Tale. It is kept in the Second Family Manor in Narsis.

title: War of Honor
topic_desc: War of Honor is a philosophical work that employs the allegory of a red hornet and a black spider to examine the nature of honor-driven conflict. The text frames such disputes as a 'great game' where honor inevitably outweighs virtue, and where the subtle poison and conspiracy of the spider are pitted against the swift dagger of the hornet. In the allegory, the spider envenoms the hornet's drink before attempting to strangle it, but the hornet manages to sting the spider before succumbing. Both perish, an outcome the author acknowledges as possible but ultimately irrelevant, arguing that the upholding of honor justifies the mutual destruction. The work defends this lethal tradition against accusations of mere murder, insisting it is a pure war of honor where both parties possess ample chance to survive.
topic_desc_basic: War of Honor is a philosophical work using the allegory of a spider and a hornet to explore honor-driven conflict. It argues that honor outweighs virtue and justifies lethal tradition, even when both parties perish.

title: War on the Shore-Dreugh
topic_desc: A Nordic mythic account of the Return, recounting Captain Ralek and the crew of the Norfryk. After Ysgramor's Companions cleared the southern shores of elves, Ralek sought the knowing of Ysmir by exterminating another race. Inspired by navigator Black Gjestr's recitation of Shor diving to battle the Dreugh-King, the crew fashioned sealed horker-skin bubbles using Alteration magic to wage war on the shore-dreugh beneath the Sea of Ghosts. They drove the dreugh from those waters, but Ralek's unchecked ambition led him alone into the Dreugh-King's palace, where his air supply failed. The tale serves as a cautionary account of immoderate ambition, explaining the origin of the Rotting Dreugh Clan descended from the Norfryk's survivors.
topic_desc_basic: A Nordic tale from the Return of Ysgramor, subtitled The Value of Tempered Ambition. It recounts how Captain Ralek and his crew used sealed horker-skin bubbles to wage war on shore-dreugh in the Sea of Ghosts, and how Ralek drowned assaulting the Dreugh-King's palace after his ambition outstripped his reason.

title: Ward of Akavir
topic_desc: The Ward of Akavir is an enchanted tower shield crafted from the skin of a dragon. Its name implies a connection to the continent of Akavir, and Imperial records associate it with Uriel V's invasion. The shield is an emblem of the Imperial Legion's honor and bears a powerful enchantment that fortifies the wielder's luck. The Ward was stored at Fort Firemoth in Morrowind's Inner Sea until an undead horde led by the lich Grurn overran the outpost, claiming the shield and taking it deep underground to a Velothi tomb beneath the fort. Its loss brought shame to the Legion. As of 3E 427, Legion scouts have been unable to confirm the Ward's presence on the archipelago, and records from the Simulacrum may be unreliable.
topic_desc_basic: The Ward of Akavir is an enchanted shield made from the skin of a dragon. It is a treasured emblem of the Imperial Legion's honor, named for the continent of Akavir.

title: Warrior
topic_desc: A fictional story about the thief Eslaf Erol's encounter with the wealthy Suoibud and the warrior Laicifitra.
topic_desc_basic: The third book in the fictional Eslaf Erol series, following the thief's escape from a wealthy man's bedroom with a gem promised to a mercenary general.

title: Wasabi Root
topic_desc: Wasabi root is the pungent, spicy root of a plant native to the island territory of Cathnoquey in the Padomaic Ocean. The root is famously cultivated throughout the archipelago known as the Wasabi Run, which produces more wasabi than the rest of the world combined. The Runner's League, operating out of Skyrim with an outpost in Firewatch, handles much of its transport. Historically, warriors have been documented lining their shield rims with wasabi, biting into it during battle to endure pain through its intense burning sensation and choked throat. Alchemists value the root for its distinctive properties.
topic_desc_basic: Wasabi root is a spicy plant root primarily grown on the island of Cathnoquey in the Padomaic Ocean, especially in the Wasabi Run archipelago. It is commonly transported into Morrowind by the Runner's League.

title: Wasting Consumption
topic_desc: Wasting Consumption is a serious disease characterized by anemia, loss of appetite, fever, and weight loss. Afflicted persons appear to be consumed from the inside as their physical agility, strength, and willpower progressively fade away. The affliction is known to be contracted from black rats, wild guars, and trolls.
topic_desc_basic: Wasting Consumption is a serious disease that causes anemia, loss of appetite, fever, and weight loss. It drains a sufferer's strength, agility, and willpower, and can be contracted from black rats, wild guars, and trolls.

title: Water Hyacinth Nectar Sacks
topic_desc: These small, fluid-filled pouches are harvested from water hyacinths, aquatic flowers rooted in the flooded Dasek Marsh of Cyrodiil. Alchemists value the nectar sacks for their intrinsic properties, and hunters occasionally gather them from the marsh waters. The ingredient's character reflects its watery origins.
topic_desc_basic: Fluid-filled pouches harvested from water hyacinths, aquatic flowers growing in Cyrodiil's Dasek Marsh.

title: Water Lilly
topic_desc: Water lilies are aquatic flowers that grow on the surface of water. They bloom in multiple colors, each possessing distinct alchemical properties. All known varieties share the common trait of granting water walking as their primary effect, making them a reliable reagent for traversing marshes and waterways. Their secondary properties invariably drain physical attributes, requiring careful preparation or combination to neutralize in potions. Alchemists value the plant for its consistent buoyant magic, though the draining aspects demand respect.
topic_desc_basic: Water lilies are aquatic flowers that grow on the surface of water. They come in several colors, all of which share the useful ability to grant water walking as their primary alchemical effect.

title: Waterstrider Egg
topic_desc: Waterstrider eggs are laid by waterstriders, a species of giant insect employed as an alternative to boat travel between Telvanni-ruled settlements in Morrowind. As an alchemical ingredient, the eggs are harvested from these domesticated arthropods. Their properties make them a subject of interest for practitioners of alchemy, who process them alongside other reagents. The creature's integral role in Telvanni logistics ensures that their eggs occasionally enter the trade network of house wizards and traveling alchemists.
topic_desc_basic: Waterstrider eggs are laid by waterstriders, a kind of giant insect used as an alternative to boat travel between Telvanni-ruled settlements in Morrowind. They serve as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Way of the Exposed Palm
topic_desc: Way of the Exposed Palm is a treatise on open-handed combat that rejects crude fist-fighting in favor of precise, disciplined technique. It frames mastery through five interdependent principles—concentration, reaction, equilibrium, speed, and breath control—likening them to the five digits required to form a complete strike. The work's central parable illustrates concentration: a plate shard driven by the same force as the intact plate inflicts far greater harm because the impact is focused into a smaller point. From this, it argues that a single thumb can prove deadlier than a whole fist, provided the fighter possesses sufficient training. Concentration further encompasses mental discipline, enabling a combatant to ignore distractions and even suppress the sensation of pain. The text presents these principles as essential to transforming unarmed combat from a brutish struggle into a sophisticated and lethal art.
topic_desc_basic: Way of the Exposed Palm is a martial treatise advocating open-handed combat over crude fist-fighting. It teaches that mastery requires five principles—concentration, reaction, equilibrium, speed, and breath control—and that focusing a strike into a small point, such as the thumb, makes it far more deadly.

title: Wayrest, Jewel of the Bay
topic_desc: A historical study of the city of Wayrest by Sathyr Longleat, tracing its growth from a First Era fishing village at the Bjoulsae River's mouth into a wealthy Breton kingdom. Longleat attributes Wayrest's enduring prosperity to a unique power-sharing alliance between the crown and merchant princes. The work details the city's survival against Orsinium, Akaviri raiders, and the Thrassian plague, and chronicles its ruling dynasties from the Gardners through the Cumberlands and Horleys to the Third Era Septims. The author contrasts Wayrest's forward-looking commercial culture with Daggerfall's antiquarianism, presenting the divided Wayrest Boulevard as a physical symbol of royal and mercantile equality.
topic_desc_basic: Sathyr Longleat's historical study of Wayrest, chronicling the Breton city's rise from a riverside fishing village to a prosperous kingdom and attributing its enduring wealth to a unique alliance between its monarchs and merchant princes.

title: Weeping Veil
topic_desc: Weeping Veils are luminescent plants native to Morrowind, commonly found growing in the Coronati Basin and near water sources throughout Shipal-Shin. Their distinctive glow makes them recognizable to harvesters in these regions. Alchemists and hunters value the plant as an ingredient, incorporating it into various preparations.
topic_desc_basic: Weeping Veils are glowing plants commonly found in the Coronati Basin and near water sources in Shipal-Shin, Morrowind. They are used in alchemy.

title: Welcome to the Arena
topic_desc: An interview with Arminius Aurix, the editor of the Kragenmoor Arena, discussing the arena's operations, the philosophy of its bloodsport, and the life of its professional fighters.
topic_desc_basic: An interview with Arminius Aurix, editor of the Kragenmoor Arena, discussing the arena's operations and the life of its professional fighters.

title: Welkynd Dust
topic_desc: Welkynd Dust is the residual remains of a defeated Welkynd Spirit. These ethereal guardians haunt Ayleid ruins, and their dissolution leaves behind this fine, luminous dust. Alchemists prize the substance for its arcane properties, though its harvest requires confronting the spirits that dwell within these ancient, perilous sites.
topic_desc_basic: Welkynd Dust is the remains left by a defeated Welkynd Spirit. It is typically found within Ayleid ruins.

title: Welkynd Spirit
topic_desc: Welkynd Spirits are spectral entities that reside in Ayleid dungeons. They are intrinsically tied to ancient Ayleid magical practices, manifesting as potent otherworldly guardians. In combat, they employ melee attacks and exhibit volatile magical traits, discharging Shockbloom and reflecting hostile spells. Uniquely, a Welkynd Spirit instinctively casts Dispel on itself, suggesting an innate resistance to magical binding or containment. Upon dissolution, these spirits leave behind Welkynd Dust, a residual substance presumably linked to the enchanted Welkynd stones that proliferate in Ayleid ruins. Possessing a grand-level soul, they are formidable remnants of the Heartland's forgotten magical heritage.
topic_desc_basic: Welkynd Spirits are spectral creatures that inhabit Ayleid dungeons. They are dangerous magical guardians that attack with melee strikes and strange magic, and leave behind Welkynd Dust when defeated.

title: Wheat
topic_desc: Wheat is a cereal grain harvested from plainwheat and witherwheat plants. Plainwheat commonly grows across Cyrodiil, while witherwheat is characteristic of Skyrim. The grain serves as a staple foodstuff and an alchemical ingredient.
topic_desc_basic: Wheat is a common grain harvested from plainwheat in Cyrodiil and witherwheat in Skyrim.

title: White Bloatroot
topic_desc: White Bloatroot is a plant-derived alchemical ingredient harvested from its namesake root. It grows in Morrowind and is recognized by practitioners for its mundane alchemical properties. The root is commonly gathered by hunters and herbalists, and it circulates in regional trade, appearing among the random ingredient stocks of Mournhold merchants and Velothi settlements.
topic_desc_basic: White Bloatroot is a plant root used as an alchemical ingredient. It grows in Morrowind and is commonly traded in Mournhold and Velothi lands.

title: White Book of 3E 426
topic_desc: The White Book of 3E 426 is the annual yearbook of Great House Indoril, recording the High Council's membership, chapelry assignments, and notable affairs for that year. It lists fourteen councilors and their Mournhold District residences, noting five were absent. The chronicle records the council requesting the Alma Rula to halt Vvardenfell settlement following Balmora taxation riots, and advising King Hlaalu Athyn Llethan to reduce levies on Velothi smallfolk. It also documents Councilor Ilvi's bid for emergency Hortator powers against House Hlaalu's growing influence; though quorum was achieved, the motion failed on a tie after abstentions and the Alma Rula's refusal to break the deadlock. A subsequent High Councillor election failed for lack of quorum.
topic_desc_basic: The White Book of 3E 426 is the annual yearbook of Great House Indoril. It records the High Council's membership and notable affairs for the year, including debates over Vvardenfell settlement, taxation, and a failed bid for emergency Hortator powers.

title: White Lead Dye
topic_desc: White Lead Dye is a cheap white pigment employed in the coloring of paints and textiles. Its alchemical character reflects this mundane role as a basic coloring agent rather than a rare or potent reagent, and it is not typically found among the randomized stock of general merchants or leveled inventories.
topic_desc_basic: White Lead Dye is a cheap white pigment used for giving color to paints and textiles.

title: White Lichen
topic_desc: White lichen is a rare fungal growth found within caves across Morrowind and in the Othreleth Woods region. Its pale coloration distinguishes it from more common cave-dwelling fungi. Alchemists value the lichen for its properties, and it circulates through ingredient supply networks in regions such as Mournhold, Narsis, and Velothis, indicating recognized alchemical merit. Hunters and foragers familiar with Morrowind's subterranean and forested biomes know to seek it in shaded, damp environments.
topic_desc_basic: White lichen is a rare fungus that grows in caves across Morrowind and in the Othreleth Woods region.

title: White Meadowsweet
topic_desc: White Meadowsweet is a floral ingredient utilized in alchemical practice. While its specific properties and natural habitat remain subjects of specialist study rather than common knowledge, the plant is recognized by its characteristic white blossoms. Alchemists value it for its contributions to potion-making, and it circulates through general supply channels, appearing in randomized floral stock.
topic_desc_basic: White Meadowsweet is a flowering plant known for its white blossoms. It is gathered for use in alchemy.

title: Widow Kiss Powder
topic_desc: Widow Kiss Powder is derived from the widow kiss, a striped purple flower found occasionally in the Vorndgad Forest and the Druadach Highlands of Skyrim. The powder is prepared from the flower's blossoms and is known to alchemists for its useful properties. Its relative scarcity in the wild, owing to the flower's infrequent growth patterns in those highland and forested regions, makes it a moderately valued ingredient among practitioners of alchemy.
topic_desc_basic: Widow Kiss Powder is a fine substance prepared from the widow kiss, a striped purple flower that grows in the Vorndgad Forest and Druadach Highlands of Skyrim. Alchemists value it as an ingredient.

title: Widow's Mortar
topic_desc: Widow's Mortar is an orange mushroom that grows upon the branches and roots of trees. It is native to the Othreleth Woods of Morrowind. Valued by alchemists and foragers for its properties, it serves as a botanical ingredient in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Widow's Mortar is an orange mushroom that grows on tree branches and roots in the Othreleth Woods of Morrowind.

title: Winged Twilight Membrane
topic_desc: Winged twilight membrane is an alchemical ingredient harvested from the winged twilight, a Daedric servant of Azura. The thin, leathery substance is taken from the creature's wing. Alchemists value the membrane for its inherent magical properties, which reflect the creature's Daedric origin. As winged twilights are formidable conjured entities, reliably obtaining their membrane is difficult, making it a scarce commodity. It appears in specialized random supplies, indicating its use among practitioners who deal with Daedric materials.
topic_desc_basic: Winged twilight membrane is an alchemical ingredient taken from the wings of the winged twilight, a Daedric creature. It is quite rare, as harvesting it requires slaying these formidable Daedra.

title: Wisp Stalks
topic_desc: Wisp Stalks are clusters of tiny, thin mushrooms that emit a faint glow. They thrive in low-light environments, commonly growing in caves and ruins across Cyrodiil. Their bioluminescent nature makes them a recognizable specimen for foragers and alchemists, who harvest them as an ingredient for potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: Wisp Stalks are tiny, thin, glowing mushrooms found in dark environments like caves and ruins in Cyrodiil. They are gathered for use in alchemy.

title: Witless Pox
topic_desc: Witless Pox is a disease that afflicts the victim's mind and body, degrading mental faculties and causing physical deterioration. It drains the victim's intelligence and willpower, severely impairing cognitive function and magical aptitude. The disease also weakens physical resilience, diminishing endurance and overall vitality. Like other common ailments of its nature, Witless Pox can be contracted from diseased creatures or through exposure to infected sources. Healers and alchemists treat Witless Pox with common restorative potions or spells that cure disease, which neutralize the affliction and restore the victim's diminished attributes.
topic_desc_basic: Witless Pox is a disease that impairs the mind and weakens the body, draining intelligence, willpower, and endurance. It can be cured with standard restorative potions or spells.

title: Wizard Fever
topic_desc: Wizard Fever is a mild disease that afflicts spellcasters. Its symptoms include headache and fever, alongside reduced intellect, drained magicka, and impaired concentration when casting spells. A legend claims it was created during the Second Era by a Telvanni wizard to cripple a rival, though this origin remains unconfirmed. The disease is contracted from eyestars.
topic_desc_basic: Wizard Fever is a mild disease that causes headache, fever, reduced intellect, drained magicka, and limited concentration when casting spells. It is contracted from eyestars.

title: Woad Seeds
topic_desc: Woad seeds are harvested from woad flowers, a plant native to Skyrim. In alchemical practice, they are valued as a specialist ingredient, though their properties remain a matter for trained alchemists and hunters to identify and exploit. As the parent flower hails from the northern province, the seeds are an uncommon sight in Morrowind, typically encountered only through imported or randomized botanical collections rather than reliable local sources.
topic_desc_basic: Woad seeds are taken from woad flowers, a plant native to Skyrim. They are an uncommon alchemical ingredient in Morrowind.

title: Wood Beetle Shell
topic_desc: Wood beetle shells are the chitinous forewings harvested from wood beetles native to Morrowind. While their primary practical application lies in craftsmanship—ground and dissolved, then combined with bone shards and resin to form the composite material used in bonemold and aena armors and weapons—the shells also possess recognized alchemical virtues. Their dual utility makes them a valued resource for both armorers and apothecaries throughout the region.
topic_desc_basic: Wood beetle shells are the chitinous forewings of wood beetles found in Morrowind. They are commonly ground and dissolved with bone shards and resin to craft bonemold and aena armors and weapons, and also hold alchemical uses.

title: Wood Blewit
topic_desc: Wood blewit is a variety of mushroom found growing in the wilds of Tamriel. Its natural properties make it a staple foraging target for hunters and wilderness travelers, while alchemists value the fungus for its characteristic contributions to potion-making. The caps are gathered as an alchemical ingredient, utilized in various preparations depending on the specific properties extracted from the specimen.
topic_desc_basic: Wood blewit is a wild mushroom commonly gathered as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Worm Wheat Incense
topic_desc: Worm Wheat Incense is a botanical preparation derived from worm wheat. Alchemists and hunters value the substance for its aromatic and reactive properties, employing it as an alchemical ingredient in various concoctions. The incense is not commonly stocked by merchants, nor are there any guaranteed repositories; it is typically encountered as a chance finding among randomized botanical or ingredient collections in the wild.
topic_desc_basic: Worm Wheat Incense is an alchemical ingredient prepared from worm wheat. It is not commonly sold by merchants and is typically found only by chance among randomized botanical gatherings.

title: Worm Wheat Tufts
topic_desc: Worm Wheat Tufts are a variety of flora used as an alchemical ingredient. The tufts are harvested from worm wheat plants growing in the wild. As a botanical specimen, they hold recognized value among practitioners of alchemy for their inherent properties, though their precise alchemical effects remain a matter of specialist study. The plant is not commonly cultivated, and specimens must be gathered from chance encounters in the landscape rather than from any guaranteed source.
topic_desc_basic: Worm Wheat Tufts are an alchemical ingredient gathered from worm wheat plants found growing in the wild.

title: Wormmouth Hide
topic_desc: Wormmouth hide is harvested from the wormmouth, a creature native to parts of Hammerfell and Skyrim. Alchemists and hunters value the hide for its alchemical properties, and it circulates as an ingredient in regions where the beast is found.
topic_desc_basic: Wormmouth hide is taken from the wormmouth, a creature found in parts of Hammerfell and Skyrim. It serves as an alchemical ingredient.

title: Wormwood Leaves
topic_desc: Wormwood leaves are harvested from the wormwood plant, a silvery flora known to grow in Cyrodiil and Skyrim. The plant's distinct metallic foliage makes it identifiable to harvesters in these provinces. Alchemists value the leaves for their properties, and the ingredient circulates through regional supply networks via randomized merchant stock and container deposits, rather than from guaranteed static deposits.
topic_desc_basic: Wormwood leaves are harvested from the wormwood plant, a silvery herb that grows in Cyrodiil and Skyrim.

title: Wrothgarian Grapes
topic_desc: Wrothgarian Grapes are a variety of grape cultivated in the Reach region, spanning the borderlands of Skyrim and High Rock. Named for the Wrothgarian Mountains that define much of this rugged terrain, the fruit serves as a regional foodstuff and alchemical ingredient. Their hardy nature reflects the harsh climate of their origin, making them a recognizable product of Reachfolk agriculture and foraging. Alchemists value them for their intrinsic properties, and the grapes circulate among healers and hunters familiar with Reach-region flora.
topic_desc_basic: Wrothgarian Grapes are a variety of grape grown in the Reach region of Skyrim and High Rock, serving as both a local food and an alchemical ingredient.

title: Yam Orb
topic_desc: A yam orb is a kind of glowing root commonly found growing in caves throughout the Shipal-Shin region of Morrowind. Its bioluminescent nature makes it a distinctive harvest in the dark underground. Alchemists value the root for its properties, and it serves as a standard ingredient in regional concoctions. Hunters and foragers familiar with the southwestern Velothi caverns can typically locate the root without undue difficulty.
topic_desc_basic: A yam orb is a kind of glowing root commonly found growing in caves in the Shipal-Shin region of Morrowind.

title: Yellow Flax Flowers
topic_desc: Yellow Flax Flowers are the blossoms of the flax plant. As a botanical ingredient, they are gathered for alchemical preparation. Their properties are of interest to practitioners of alchemy and those who harvest floral components across Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: Yellow Flax Flowers are the blossoms of the flax plant, gathered for use in alchemy.

title: Yellow Lichen
topic_desc: Yellow lichen is a variety of lichen growing in the Othreleth Woods and within caves in the Shipal-Shin region of Morrowind. As an alchemical ingredient, it is recognized by practitioners for its readily harvestable nature in these humid, shaded environments. Foragers and hunters frequent these territories to collect samples for alchemical use.
topic_desc_basic: Yellow lichen is a variety of lichen that grows in the Othreleth Woods and in caves throughout the Shipal-Shin region of Morrowind.

title: Yellow Moth Wing
topic_desc: Yellow Moth Wings are the wings of the Yellow Moth, a common insect found throughout Cyrodiil. Unlike many moths, the Yellow Moth is active during both day and night. Alchemists and hunters value the wings for their properties in potion-making. You do not know where Yellow Moth Wing is.
topic_desc_basic: Yellow Moth Wings are gathered from the Yellow Moth, a common insect found in Cyrodiil that is active during both day and night. They are used in alchemy.

title: Yellow Ochre Dye
topic_desc: Yellow ochre dye is an expensive yellow pigment employed in giving color to paints and textiles. As a colorant, it holds recognized value in artisanal and alchemical practices alike, though its scarcity outside of deliberate acquisition makes it a prized commodity rather than a common find.
topic_desc_basic: Yellow ochre dye is an expensive yellow pigment used to color paints and textiles.

title: Yeth Resin
topic_desc: Yeth resin is an alchemically active substance produced by the yeth-grub, an insect native to Morrowind. Harvested from the creature, the resin serves as a practical ingredient in apothecary and is valued for its useful properties in potion-crafting.
topic_desc_basic: Yeth resin is a substance of alchemical value produced by the yeth-grub, a creature native to Morrowind.

title: Ynesai
topic_desc: The Ynesai are an island race of Men native to the Yneslea archipelago. They trace their origins to the extinct Men of Akavir, preserving traces of that lost culture through millennia-old traditions. A melancholic and isolated people, they prefer small, tight-knit communities in their tropical homeland and are rarely seen in Tamriel. In conflict, Ynesai favor deception and ranged attacks before closing in with knives and fists, and they possess a distinct aptitude for moving unseen.
topic_desc_basic: The Ynesai are an island race of Men native to the Yneslea archipelago. They are rarely seen in Tamriel, preferring their tropical homeland.

title: Ynesai Toro
topic_desc: The Ynesai Toro is a well-preserved native Ynesai stone sculpture, one of numerous similar monuments found across the isles of Yneslea. Its precise cultural significance remains unclear. The artifact is notable for its exceptional craftsmanship; despite being made of stone, it bears no trace of hammer or chisel marks, demonstrating remarkable sculptural skill. Imperial archaeologist Jera Cerunia discovered the Toro on an isle near Craesa in 281 and transported it to Thorn aboard the IAS vessel 'Sungazer'. In 389, the artifact was transferred to Firewatch, where it became an original piece in the Museum's Invasion of Akavir collection.
topic_desc_basic: The Ynesai Toro is a well-preserved native Ynesai stone sculpture, one of many such monuments found across Yneslea. Notable for its exceptional craftsmanship, it bears no trace of hammer or chisel marks. Its precise cultural significance remains unclear.

title: Yngol and the Sea-Ghosts
topic_desc: A Nord tale recounting Ysgramor's first adventure in Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: A Nord tale of Ysgramor's first adventure in Tamriel. It recounts the death of his kinsman Yngol, lost to a storm at Hsaarik Head during the migration from Atmora to Mereth. Yngol is remembered as the first of the Children of the Sky to perish on Tamrielic soil, and his barrow was raised in the Atmoran tradition.

title: Yuin Root
topic_desc: Yuin roots are the pale yellow roots of the yuin plant, a species native to High Rock. The plant's specific alchemical properties remain a subject of specialist study, though the root is recognized among herbalists and hunters as a provincial ingredient gathered from the wilds of the Breton homeland.
topic_desc_basic: Yuin root is a pale yellow root harvested from the yuin plant, which grows in High Rock.

title: Zealotry
topic_desc: Zealotry is a treatise examining the fanatical sect devoted to Sheogorath. The author dismisses the Zealots as mad, detailing their belief that Sheogorath is a living god whose will sustains the realm and that Arden-Sul was his mortal aspect who will return to cleanse it. The work characterizes the Zealots as violently hostile, attacking non-believers on sight and fighting to the death. It also outlines their secretive recruitment: Zealots leave robes in settled areas for aspiring supplicants to don, though leaders purportedly discern false hearts and slay deceivers. Initiates endure painful, potentially fatal rituals to prove fealty. Successful entrants learn sorcerous secrets, most notably the summoning of Flesh Atronachs. The text serves as both a warning and a field guide to understanding and infiltrating this dangerous cult.
topic_desc_basic: Zealotry is a book detailing the beliefs and practices of the fanatical Sheogorath-worshipping sect. It describes their conviction that Sheogorath is a living god and Arden-Sul his mortal aspect, their violent hostility toward non-believers, and their secretive initiation rites involving discarded robes, painful rituals, and the summoning of Flesh Atronachs.
